omnĭpŏtens.opening: adj. omnis-potens , all-powerful , almighty , omnipotent ( poet. and in post-class. prose), Enn. ap. Non. 111, 15 (Trag. v. 202 Vahl.): Juppiter, id. ap. Serv. ad Verg. A. 1, 254 (Ann. v. 446 Vahl.); Cat. 64, 171 :…

omnĭpŏtentĭa.opening: omnipotens , almighty power , omnipotence (post-class.), Macr. S. 1, 16 .

omnĭs.opening: (omnia is freq. a dissyl. in the poets, as Verg. G. 4, 221 ; id. A. 6, 33 ; Lucr. 1, 1106 Lachm.), adj. etym. dub.; perh. akin to ambo and Gr. ἀμφί (syn.: cunctus, universus), all , every : omnium rerum, quas ad beate…

omniscĭus.opening: adj. omnis-scio , omniscient (eccl. Lat.), Ps.- Aug. Spec. 16 .

omnĭsŏnus.opening: adj. omnis-sono , uttering all kinds of sounds (post-class.): harmonia, Paul. Nol. Carm. 24, 81 : mela, Mart. Cap. 9, § 912 .

omnĭtĕnens.opening: adj. omnis-tenens , holding all things , all-swaying (eccl. Lat.), Tert. Carm. adv. Marc. 5, 202 .

omnĭtŭens.opening: adj. omnis-tueor , all-seeing ( poet. and in post-class. prose), Lucr. 2, 942 ; Val. Fl. 5, 247 : sol, App. Mundo, p. 71, 23 .

omnĭvăgus.opening: adj. omnis-vagus , roving everywhere , omnivagant : Diana, Cic. N. D. 2, 27, 68 ; Varr. Atac. in Anth. Lat. 2, p. 337 Burm. dub. (al. omnivomus).

omnĭvŏlus.opening: adj. omnis-volo , willing every thing : omnivoli furta Jovis, Cat. 68, 140 .

omnĭvŏrus.opening: adj. omnis-voro , all-devouring , omnivorous : boves, Plin. 25, 8, 53, § 94 .

omphăcĭum.opening: , = ὀμφάκιον , the oil or juice of unripe olives or grapes , Plin. 12, 27, 60, § 130 ; 14, 16, 18, § 98 .

omphăcŏcarpos.opening: , = ὀμφακόκαρπος , a plant , called also aparine, Plin. 27, 5, 15, § 32 (al. omphalocarpon).

omphăcŏmel.opening: , = ὀμφακόμελι , a sirup made of omphacium, Pall. 9, 13 lemm.

Omphălē.opening: , = Ὀμφάλη , a queen of Lydia , whom Hercules served , Hyg. Fab. 32 ; Prop. 4, 10, 17 ; Ov. F. 2, 305 ; Stat. Th. 10, 646 ; cf. Preller's Gr. Mythol. 2, p. 158.

omphălos.opening: , = ὀμφαλός , the navel (pure Lat. umbilicus); transf. for the centre (in post-class. poetry), Aus. Idyll. 11, 60 .

Onchesmītes.opening: , = Ὀγχησμίτης , a wind blowing from Onchesmus ( Ὀγχησμός ), a harbor of Epirus , Cic. Att. 7, 2, 1 .

Onchestĭus.opening: adj. , of or belonging to the city of Onchestus , in Bœotia , Ov. M. 10, 605 .

onco.opening: v. n. , to bray , like an ass: oncat asellus, Auct. Carm. Philom. 55.

Onoba.opening: f , a city in Hispania Bœtica , Plin. 3, 1, 3, § 10 ; Mel. 3, 1, 3

Oönae.opening: , another form of Oeönae, q. v.

opetis.opening: a plant , called also aristolochia, App. Herb. 19 .

Ophir.opening: (= ), a region in Southern Arabia , Vulg. 3 Reg. 9, 28 ; id. 1 Par. 29, 4 .—Hence, , , of or from Ophir , Plin. 36, 26, 66, § 193 .

ophthalmĭa.opening: , = ὀφθαλμία , an inflammation of the eye , Boëth. ex Arist. Topic. 3, p. 689.

Opĭlĭus.opening: a Roman surname. Aurelius Opilius, a grammarian and author , Suet. Gram. 6 .— Another Aurelius Opilius, a physician , Plin. 28, 4, 7, § 38 .— M. Opilius Severus Macrinus, emperor of Rome , A. D. 218, Eutr. 8, 21 .

oppallesco.opening: ( ), , v. n. inch. [ob-palleo], to turn pale (post-class.): carnifex stupore oppalluit, Prud. στεφ . 1, 92; Coripp. Joann. 6, 156.

oppando.grammar: pandi, pansum, or passum, 3 v. a.
oppando.opening: v. a. ob-pando , to spread or stretch out against or before , to spread out (post-class.): aliquid ad flatus helices, Grat. Cyn. 55 : cornibus oppansis et summā fronte coruscum (of the cross of Christ), Prud. Psych. 410…

oppango.opening: ( ), , v. a. ob-pango , to fasten or fix on , to affix (anteclass. and in post-Aug. prose): ubi savium oppegit, fugit, imprinted, Plaut. Curc. 1, 1, 60 : repagula, quae ... ex contrario oppanguntur, Paul. ex Fest. s. v.…

oppecto.opening: ( ), , v. a. ob-pecto , to comb off; transf., of eating, to pluck or pick off , to pick , to eat : nimio melius oppectuntur frigida, Plaut. Pers. 1, 3, 31 .

oppēdo.opening: ( ), , v. n. ob-pedo , to break wind at any one; trop. for to deride , mock , insult; with dat. : curtis Judaeis, Hor. S. 1, 9, 70 .

oppĕrĭor.opening: ( ), (arch. forms, fut. opperibor, Plaut. Truc. 1, 2, 107 al. ; inf. opperirier, id. ib. 2, 3, 5 ; v. infra ; Ter. Eun. 5, 2, 51 ), v. dep. n. and a. [kindred with experior, from perior, whence peritus]. Neutr. , to…

oppessŭlātus.opening: ( ), , Part. , from the obs. oppessulo [ob-pessulus], bolted or barred (post-class.): januam firmiter oppessulatam pulsare, App. M. 1, p. 112, 11 : januae, Amm. 31, 13, 15 .

oppĕto.grammar: īvi and ii, ītum, 3 v. a.
oppĕto.opening: ( ), , v. a. ob-peto , to go to meet , to encounter (an evil, esp. death; class.; syn.: obeo, occumbo, intereo): malam pestem, Enn. ap. Cic. Tusc. 2, 16, 38 (Trag. v. 15 Vahl.); so, pestem, Plaut. As. 1, 1, 7 —Esp.:…

oppexus.opening: ( ), , oppecto , a sombing , dressing of hair: crinium regalium, App. M. 11, p. 261, 15 .

oppĭco.opening: ( ), , v. a. ob-pico , to smear over or seal up with pitch (anteclass.): corticem oppicato, Cato, R. R. 120 .

oppĭdānĕus.opening: adj. oppidum , of a town (post-class.), Cod. Th. 12, 1, 38 sq.

oppĭdānus.opening: adj. id. , of or in a town other than Rome (since urbanus signifies, of Rome, from the capital); sometimes in a depreciating sense, opp. to urbanus, of or belonging to a small town , provincial (class.): senex quidam…

oppĭdātim.opening: adv. id. , by towns , in the towns , in every town (post-Aug.): ludos oppidatim constituerunt, Suet. Aug. 59 : cum oppidatim victimae caederentur, id. Galb. 18 .

oppĭdō.opening: adv. etym. dub.; cf. ἔμπεδον; v. oppidum , very , very much , completely , exceedingly , exactly , precisely (already obs. in the time of Quint.: oppido sunt usi paululum tempore nostro superiores, Quint. 8, 3, 25 .…

oppĭdŭlum.opening: dim. oppidum , a small town (class.), Cic. Att. 10, 7, 1 ; id. Q. Fr. 2, 12, 1 : mansuri oppidulo, quod versu dicere non est (viz Equus Tuticus), Hor. S. 1, 5, 87 .

oppĭdum.opening: ( gen. plur oppidūm, Sulp. ap. Cic. Fam. 4, 5, 4 ; old abl plur. oppedeis, Lex. Servil.), ob and pedum; Gr. πέδον; Sanscr pada-m, on or over the plain . A town (of towns other than Rome, which was called Urbs; though…

oppignĕrātor.opening: ( ), , oppignero , one who takes a pledge , who lends on a pledge , (eccl. Lat.), Aug. Ep. 215 .

oppignĕro.opening: ( ), , v. a. ob-pignero , to give as a pledge , to pledge , pawn (rare but class.). Lit. : libelli pro vino etiam saepe oppignerabantur, Cic. Sest. 51, 110 : anulum, Mart. 2, 57, 7 .— Trop. : filiam. Ter. Heaut. 4, 5,…

oppīlātĭo.opening: ( ), , oppilo , a stopping up , obstructing (post-class.): narium, Scrib. Comp. 47 .

oppīlo.opening: ( ), , v. a. obpilo , to stop up , shut up (rare but class; syn.: obturo, obstruo, claudo): metretam novam amurcā colluito, oppilato, Cato, R. R. 100 ; Varr. L. L. 5, 31, 135 : ostia, Lucr. 6, 725 : scalis tabernae…

Oppĭus.opening: the name of a Roman gens. C. Oppius, a friend of Cœsar , Cic. Att. 4, 16, 14 al. — L. Oppius, a Roman knight , Cic. Fl. 13, 31 .— P. Oppius, a quœstor , defended by Cicero; v. the fragm. in Orell. p. 444.—In fem. :…

opplĕo.opening: ( ), , v. a. obpleo, plenus , to fill completely , to fill up , fill (class.). Lit. : saucii opplent porticūs, Enn. ap. Cic. Tusc. 2, 16, 38 (Trag. v. 16 Vahl.): ager oppletus imbrium fremitu, Enn. ap. Serv. ad Verg. G.…

opplōro.opening: ( ), , v. n. ob-ploro , to cry or wail at , against , or in any thing: auribus meis, Auct. Her 4, 52, 65.

oppōno.opening: ( ), (in Plaut pŏsīvi), sĭtum, 3 ( sync. : oppostus for oppositus, Lucr. 4, 150 ), v. a. ob-pono , to set or place against , to set or station before or opposite , to oppose (class., cf.: obicio, offero, adversor). Lit.…

opporto.opening: ( ), , to bring : portat, subportat, obportat, Not. Tir. p. 11 .

opportūnĭtas.opening: ( ), , opportunus . In gen., fitness , convenience , suitableness (class.; syn. occasio; cf.: copia, facultas): loci, local advantages, Caes. B. G. 3, 14 : corporis, Cic. Leg. 1, 9, 27 : anuli, id. Off. 3, 9, 38 :…

opportūnus.opening: ( ), , adj. obportus, lit., at or before the port; hence , In gen., fit , meet , convenient , suitable , seasonable , opportune (class.; syn.: commodus, utilis): tempus actionis opportunum, Graece εὐκαιρια , Latine…

oppŏsĭtĭo.opening: ( ), , oppono , an opposing , opposition (class.): disparatum est id, quod ab aliquā re per oppositionem negationis separatur, hoc modo: sapere, et non sapere, Cic. Inv. 1, 28, 42 ; Gell. 6, 1, 4 : scientiae, Vulg. 1…

oppŏsĭtus.opening: (in sing. used only in abl. ) [oppono]. A placing or setting against , an opposing; with obj.-gen. : laterum nostrorum oppositus et corporum pollicemur, Cic. Marc. 10, 32 ; Sil. 10, 212 . —With subj.-gen. : lunae, Cic.…

oppressĭo.opening: ( ), , opprimo . A pressing down , Vitr. 10, 3, 3 ; trop., force , violence (class.), Ter. Ad. 2, 2, 30 .— Violent seizure : occupatio fori, oppressio curiae, Cic. Dom. 3, 5 .— Oppression , overthrow : legum et…

oppressĭuncŭla.opening: ( ), , dim. oppressio , a slight pressing , gentle pressure : papillarum horridularum, Plaut. Ps. 1, 1, 66 .

oppressor.opening: opprimo , a crusher , destroyer : oppressores dominationis, Brut. ap. Cic. Ep. ad Brut. 1, 16 .

oppressus.opening: ( ), , opprimo , a pressing down , pressure ( poet. and in post-class. prose): in oppressu valido, Lucr. 1, 851 : montis, Sid. Ep. 9, 11 .

opprĭmo.opening: ( ), , v. a. ob-premo , to press against , press together; to press down (class.; syn. obruo). Lit. : voluit deus ora loquentis Opprimere, to close, Ov. M. 3, 295 : oculos, to press together , i. e. close the eyes , sc.…

opprō^brāmentum.opening: ( ), , opprobro , a reproach , disgrace (ante-class.): opprobramentum, aut flagitium muliebre, Plaut. Merc. 2, 3, 84 (420 Ritschl).

opprō^brātĭo.opening: ( ), , id. , a reproaching , upbraiding , (post-class.): opprobratione permotus, Gell. 12, 12, 4 : reprehensionis, id. 2, 7, 13 .

opprō^brĭōsus.opening: ( ), , adj [opprobrium], opprobrious (post-class.), Cod. Just. 1, 3, 41 ; Ambros. Cain et Abel, 1, 4, 14.

opprō^brĭum.opening: ( ), i. opprobro , a reproach , scandal , disgrace , dishonor , opprobrium (not in Cic. or Cæs.; syn.: dedecus, probrum, infamia). vereor, ne civitati meae sit opprobrio, si, etc., lest it should be a reproach, Nep.…

opprō^bro.opening: ( ), no perf. , , v. a. ob-probrum , to reproach , taunt , upbraid (ante- and post-class.; syn.: vitupero, objurgo, reprehendo): opprobrare, probrum obicere, Fest. p. 187 Müll.: egone id exprobrem, qui mihimet cupio id…

oppugnantĭa.opening: oppugno , resistance , opposition (late Lat.), Dion. Exig Epist. de Rat. Paschae, p. 513 M.

oppugnātĭo.opening: ( ), , id. , a storming , assaulting , besieging; an attack , assault , siege (class.). Lit. : de oppidorum oppugnationibus, Cic. de Or. 1, 48, 210 : oppugnatio Gallorum, i. e. their method of besieging, Caes. B. G. 2,…

oppugnātor.opening: ( ), , id. , an assaulter , attacker , assailant (class.). Lit. : patriae, Cic. Phil. 12, 3, 8 : oppugnatores, opp. obsessi, Tac. H. 3, 71 .— Trop. : meae salutis, Cic. Planc. 31, 76 .

oppugnātōrĭus.opening: ( ), , adj. oppugnator , of or belonging to a siege (only in Vitr.): res, Vitr. 10, 22 ; id. 10, 19 .

oppugno.opening: ( ), no perf. , , v. a. ob-pugnus , to beat with fists , to buffet (Plautin.): os, Plaut. Cas. 2, 6, 56 .

oppŭto.opening: ( ), , v. a. ob-puto , to prune (post-Aug.), Plin. 17, 21, 35, § 156 .

oppŭvĭo.opening: v. a. , to beat , strike : oppuviat, verberat, a puviendo, id est feriendo, Fest. p. 188 Müll.

ops.opening: ( nom. sing. does not occur; and the dat. perh. only in Front. Ep. ad Verr. 6 fin.; abl. ope, but opi, Varr. L. L. 5, 32, 141 ), Sanscr. ap-nas, gain; Gr. ἄφενος, wealth; cf.: opulentus. copia = co-opia . Power , might…

optābĭlis.opening: adj. opto , to be wished for , desirable (class.): quae expetenda atque optabilia videntur, Cic. de Or. 1, 51, 221 : mihi pax imprimis fuit optabilis, id. Phil. 7, 3, 7 : tempus, Ov. M. 9, 758 : quae ut concurrant…

optātĭo.opening: id. , a wishing , a wish (class.). In gen.: Theseo cum tres optationes Neptunus dedisset, Cic. Off. 3, 25, 94 .— Rhet. fig., the expression of a wish : optatio atque exsecratio, Cic. de Or. 3, 53, 205 ; cf. Quint. 9, 1,…

optātīvus.opening: adj. id. , of or belonging to a wish , expressing a wish , optative (post-class.): modus optativus, the optative, Diom. p. 330 P.: adverbia, Mart. Cap. 3, § 310 .

optātō.opening: adv. , v. opto, P. a. fin.

optātus.opening: Part. and P. a. , from opto.

optĭcē.opening: , = ὀπτική , optics : optices non ignarus, Vitr. 1, 1, 4 .

optĭmas.opening: ( ), , adj. optimus , of or belonging to the best or noblest , aristocratic : res publica, quae ex tribus generibus illis, regali et optumati et populari confusa modice, Cic. Rep. 2, 23, 41 (from Non. 342, 31 ):…

optĭo.opening: id. , a helper whom one chooses for himself, an assistant (anteand post-class.). In gen.: tibi optionem sumito Leonidam, Plaut. As. 1, 1, 88 : fabricae, Dig. 50, 6, 6 .— In partic., in milit. lang., an adjutant , Tac.…

optĭōnātus.opening: 2. optio , an adjutancy (ante-class.), Cato ap. Fest. p. 201 Müll.

optīvus.opening: adj. opto , chosen ( poet. and in post-class. prose): cognomen, Hor. Ep. 2, 2, 101 : optivi vocantur hi (tutores) qui ex optione sumuntur, Gai. Inst. 1, 154 (opp. to dativi).

opto.opening: (optassis for optaveris, Plaut. Mil. 3, 1, 75 ), v. a. root op, whence Gr. ΟΠΤΩ, ὄψομαι; qs. to look out, pick out, = legere, eligere , to choose , select (anteclass. and poet. ; syn. deligo): utrum vis, opta, dum…

optostrōtum.opening: ὀπτόσ-στρωτόν , a brick pavement , Not. Tir. p. 164 .

optūtū.opening: , quod est tuor; et significat video, Fest. p. 186 Müll.

orbātĭo.opening: orbo , a depriving , privation (post-Aug.), Sen. Ep. 87, 35 .

orbātor.opening: id. , one who deprives others of children or parents , a bereaver ( poet. ): nostri orbator, Achilles, Ov. M. 13, 500 .

orbĕfăcĭo.opening: v. a. orbus-facio , to bereave , to make an orphan : orbefacio, ὀρφανίζω , Gloss. Philox.

Orbēlus.opening: ( ), , , = Ὀρβηλός , a mountain on the borders of Macedonia and Thrace : Orbelus, Mel. 2, 2, 2 ; Plin. 4, 10, 17, § 35 .

orbĭcŭlāris.opening: adj. orbiculus , circular , orbicular , an appellation of a plant: herba, App. Herb. 17 ; cf. Marc. Emp. 4 .

orbĭcŭlātim.opening: adv. id. , circularly , in circles or rings (post-Aug.), Plin. 11, 37, 67, § 177 ; Macr. S. 7, 9, 3 .

orbĭcŭlātus.opening: adj. id. , circleshaped , rounded , circular , orbiculate (class.): mala, round apples , an excellent kind of apple, Varr. R. R. 1, 59 ; Col. 5, 10, 19 ; 12, 45, 5 ; Pall. Febr. 25, 18 ; Macr. S. 3, 19, 2 .— Hence,…

orbĭcŭlor.opening: v. dep. id. , to go round in a circle : orbiculatur, κυκλεύει , Gloss. Philox.

orbĭcŭlus.opening: dim. orbis , a small disk; a sheave , roller , pulley , etc. (anteclass. and post-Aug.), Cato, R. R. 3, 6 ; 22, 2 ; Col. 4, 30, 4 ; Vitr. 10, 5 : radix concisa in orbiculos, cut in little disks or slices , Plin. 25, 13,…

orbĭfĭco.opening: v. a. orbus-facio , to bereave , make childless : orbificor liberorum leto, Att. ap. Non. 179, 26 (Trag. Rel. p. 161 Rib.).

orbīle.opening: , a false read. for orbis ... ligneus, Varr. R. R. 3, 5, 15 .

Orbĭlĭus.opening: the name of a Roman gens. So, Orbilius, a grammarian in Rome in the time of Cicero , Hor. Ep. 2, 1, 71 ; Suet. Gram. 9 .

orbis.opening: ( nom. orbs, Ven. Carm. 8, 5. — Abl. regul. orbe; but orbi, Lucr. 5, 74 : ex orbi, Varr. R. R. 3, 5, 16 ; Rutil. ap. Charis. p. 112 P.: orbi terrae, in the meaning in the world , Cic. Sest. 30, 66 ; so, orbi terrarum,…

orbĭta.opening: orbis . A track or rut made in the ground by a wheel. Lit. (class.): impressa orbita, Cic. Att. 2, 21, 2 ; Cic. Verr. 2, 3, 3, § 6 ; Verg. G. 3, 293 ; Liv. 32, 17 .— Trop. , a track , course , path (ante-class. and…

orbĭtas.opening: orbus , bereavement of parents or children, of a husband or other dear person, childlessness , orphanage , widowhood (class.). Lit. : in orbitatem liberos producere, Plaut. Capt. 3, 5, 105 : bonum liberi, misera…

orbĭtōsus.opening: adj. orbita , full of cart-ruts ( poet. ), Verg. Cat. 8, 17 .

orbĭtūdo.opening: orbus , bereavement , orphanhood (ante-class. for orbitas): miseret orbitudinis, Att. ap. Non. 146, 17 ; Pac. and Turp. ib. 18 sq.

orbītus.opening: orbis , circular (anteand post-class.): motu, Varr. ap. Non. 148, 16 ; Arn. 2, 83 (others read orbico; cf. Oehler ad Varr. Sat. Menipp. p. 139 ).

Orbĭus clīvus.opening: a place in Rome , Paul. ex Fest. p. 182 Müll.; the same called Urbius clivus, Liv. 1, 48, 6 ; cf. Becker's Antiq. 1, p. 526.

orbo.opening: v. a. orbus , to deprive or bereave of parents, children, or other dear persons; to make fatherless , motherless , childless , etc. (class.; syn.: privo, viduo). Lit. : filio orbatus, Cic. Off. 1, 10, 30 : mater orbata…

Orbōna.opening: id. , the tutelary goddess of parents bereft of their children , Cic. N. D. 3, 25, 63 ; cf. Plin. 2, 7, 5, § 16 ; Arn. 4, 131 ; Tert. ad Nat. 2, 14 .

orbus.opening: adj. kindr. with Gr. ὀρφανός; cf. Fest. p. 183 Müll. , bereaved , bereft , of parents or children; parentless , fatherless , childless (class.; cf. pupillus). Lit. : senex, Cic. Par. 5, 2, 39 ; cf.: parens liberorum an…

orca.opening: cf. ἄρχαὔρχα , a kind of whale , an orc , Plin. 9, 6, 5, § 12 .— Transf. A large-bellied vessel , a butt , tun (cf.: seria, dolium): orca genus marinae beluae maximum dicitur: ad cujus similitudinem vasa quoque ficaria…

Orca.opening: a Roman surname , e. g. Valerius Orca, Cic. Fam. 13, 4 sq.

Orcădes.opening: islands near Scotland , now the Orkneys , Mel. 3, 6, 7 ; Tac. Agr. 10 ; Plin. 4, 16, 30, § 103 .— Acc. plur. : Orcadas, Juv. 2, 161 .

Orchămus.opening: , = Ὄρχαμος , a king of Babylonia , the father of Leucothŏē , Ov. M. 4, 212 .

orchăs.opening: a kind of edible olive of an oblong shape , Verg. G. 2, 86 ; cf. Macr. S. 3, 20 .

orchēsta.opening: , = ὀρχηστής , a dancer , a pantomime (late Lat.): orchestarum loquacissimae manus, Cassiod. Var. 4, 51 .

orchēstŏpŏlārĭus.opening: , = ὀρχηστόπολος , a juggler , tumbler , dancer (postclass.), Firm. Math. 8, 15.

orchēstra.opening: , = ὀρχήστρα . The place where the Senate sat in the theatre, the orchestra : in orchestrā senatorum sunt sedibus loca destinata, Vitr. 5, 6 ; Juv. 7, 47 ; Suet. Caes. 39 ; id. Aug. 35 ; 44 ; id. Claud. 21 et saep.—…

orchĭon.opening: , = ὄρχις , testiculus, a plant , called also testiculata, App. Herb. 82 .

orchis.opening: , = ὄρχις A plant , a kind of olive , Col. 5, 8, 4 ; id. Arb. 17, 3 ; Pall. Febr. 18, 4 .— Another plant , so called from the shape of its roots, the orchis : mirabilis est orchis herba, sive serapias, gemina radice…

orchīta.opening: or , , , and , , , = ὀρχῖτις , a kind of olive of an oblong shape : albam pauseam, vel orchitam, vel radiolum, Col. 12, 49, 2 ; 12, 50, 1 ; Cato, R. R. 6, 1 ; 7, 4 ; cf. Varr. R. R. 1, 60 ; Paul. ex Fest. p. 180 Müll.

Orchĭus.opening: and , the name of a Roman gens.—So, C. Orchius, a tribune of the people , 572 A.U.C., by whom the Lex Orchia was proposed, Macr. S. 3, 17, 2 ; Schol. Bob. ad Cic. Sest. p. 310, 32 Bait.

Orchŏmĕnus.opening: or , , or (and or , , ), = Ὀρχόμενος . The son of Athamas and Themisto , Hyg. Fab. 1 .— A city in Bœotia , Caes. B. C. 3, 55 ; Plin. 8, 58, 83, § 226 .— A city in Thessaly : Minyius, Plin. 4, 8, 15, § 29 .—Hence, , ,…

Orchus.opening: , = Orcus: Orchi traditus thesauro, Naev. ap. Gell. 1, 24, 2 .

Orcīnĭānus.opening: adj. Orcus , of or belonging to Orcus or to the dead ( poet. ): sponda, i. e. a bier, Mart. 10, 5, 9 .

Orcīnus.opening: adj. id. , of or belonging to the realms of the dead : liberti, set free by the last will of their masters, Dig. 26, 4, 3, § 3 ; ib. 33, 8, 22 ; ib. 40, 5, 30, § 12 al. : senatores, who had got into the Senate by means…

Orcivius.opening: name of a Roman gens; esp. C. Orcivius, Cicero's colleague as prœtor, Cic. Clu. 34, 94 ; 53, 147 ; cf. id. Or. 48, 160 .

orcŭla.opening: dim. 1. orca , a small tun , a cask (ante- and post-class.): oleas in orculam calcato manibus siccis, Cato, R. R. 117 ; Auct. de Limit. p. 253 Goes.

ostentārĭus.opening: adj. ostentum , of or relating to prophetic indications , prophetic (post-class.): ostentaria novitas (al. ostentatoria), Mart. Cap. 2, § 151 .— Subst. : , , , a book of prognostics : Tuscum, Macr. S. 3, 7 : arborarium,…

ostentātīcĭus.opening: or , , adj. ostento , that serves for display , ostentatious (post-class.): virginitas, Tert. Virg. Vel. 3 .

ostentātĭo.opening: id. . In gen., a showing , exhibition , display (very rare). in armorum magis quam togarum ostentatione, Plin. Pan. 56 fin. : cognomen Imperiosi ... ab ostentatione saevitiae ascitum, from an open display, Liv. 7, 4 .—…

ostentātor.opening: ostento , a vain , self-satisfied exhibiter , a displayer , parader , boaster , vaunter : ostentatores meri, Plaut. Curc. 4, 1, 15 : ostentatorem pecuniae gloriosum describere, Auct. Her. 4, 50, 63 : factorum, Liv. 1,…

ostentātrix.opening: ostentator , she that displays or boasts (post-class.). Lit. : immodica sui ostentatrix, App. Mag. p. 323, 11 .— Trop. : pompa ostentatrix vani splendoris, Prud. Psych. 439 .

ostentĭfer.opening: adj. ostentumfero , portentous : ostentiferum, τερατῶδες , Vet. Gloss.

ostento.opening: ( inf. pass. ostentarier, Plaut. Most. 1, 3, 129 ), , v. freq. a. ostendo , to present to view , to show , exhibit (class.). In gen.: alicui jugula sua pro capite alicujus, to present, offer, Cic. Att. 1, 16, 4 :…

ostentus.opening: ostendo . In gen., a showing , exhibiting , display (not in Cic. or Cæs.): corpora extra vallum abjecta ostentui, as a public spectacle, Tac. A. 1, 29 : atrocitatis, Gell. 20, 1, 48 .— In partic. Show , parade ,…

ostes.opening: , = ὤστης , a kind of earthquake , App. de Mundo, p. 65, 30.

Ostĭa.opening: , and , , ostium; cf. Engl. mouth, in Ply-mouth, Yar-mouth, etc. , a seaport town in Latium , at the mouth of the Tiber , built by Ancus Marcius , still called Ostia : Ostiam urbem ad exitum Tiberis in mare fluentis…

ostĭārĭus.opening: adj. ostium , of or belonging to the door : ancilla, portress, Vulg. Johan. 18, 17 ; usu. subst. , , , a door-keeper , porter (syn.: janitor, portitor), Varr. R. R. 1, 13 ; Plin. 12, 14, 32, § 64 ; Vulg. 1 Par. 9, 22…

ostĭātim.opening: adv. id. . Lit. , from door to door , from house to house (class.): ostiatim oppidum compilare, Cic. Verr. 2, 4, 24, § 53 : agere crimen, to enumerate the several houses where a crime was perpetrated, id. ib. 2, 4, 22 ,…

ostīgo.opening: , in the lang. of shepherds, a kind of eruption or scab on lambs , also called mentigo, Col. 7, 5, 21 ; v. mentigo.

ostĭŏlum.opening: dim. ostium , a little door (post-Aug.), Col. 8, 14, 1 : ostiola olitoria, Plin. 19, 8, 38, § 125 : abscondita, Vulg. Dan. 14, 20 .

ostĭum.opening: kindred with Sanscr. oshtha, labium; Slav. ūsta, the same; cf. os , a door (class.; cf.: porta, janua, fores, valvae). Lit. : omnia istaec auscultavi ab ostio, Plaut. Merc. 2, 4, 9 : observare, id. Mil. 2, 3, 81 :…

ostŏcŏpŏs.opening: , = ὀστοκόπος , boneracking , a disease (as if the bones were giving way; post-class.), Ser. Samm. 48, 892 ; Pelag. Vet. 3; 10.

Ostōrĭus.opening: the name of several Romans. Ostorins Sabinus, a Roman knight , Tac. A. 16, 23 ; 16, 30 : quaestor, id. ib. 16, 33 .— P. Ostorius Scapula, proprœtor in Britain , Tac. A. 12, 31 : bello egregius, id. Agr. 14 .— M.…

ostrăcĭas.opening: , and , , , = οστρακίας, ὀστρακῖτις , a semigem , prob. hornstone or chalcedony , Plin. 37, 10, 65, § 177 .

ostrăcītes.opening: , = ὀστρακίτης , a precious stone , otherwise unknown, Plin. 36, 19, 31, § 139 .

ostrăcītis.opening: , = ὀστρακῖτις . Hornstone; v. ostracias.— A kind of cadmia , Plin. 34, 10, 22, § 103 .

ostrăcĭum.opening: or , , , = ὀστράκιον , a mussel , also called onyx, Plin. 32, 10, 46, § 134 .

ostrĕa.opening: , and (rarely) , , , = ὄστρεον , an oyster , mussel , sea-snail (class.). Form ostrea, Enn. Heduph. 2 (p. 166 Vahl.); Lucil. ap. Non. 216, 6 ; Afran.; Turp. and Varr. ib.; Plaut. Rud. 2, 1, 8 ; Cic. Fragm. ap. Non. 216,…

ostrĕārĭus.opening: adj. ostrea , of or belonging to oysters , oyster- (post-Aug.): panis, oyster-bread, bread eaten with oysters, Plin. 18, 11, 27, § 105 .— Subst. : , , , an oyster-bed , Plin. 9, 51, 74, § 160 : in Baiano locare, Macr.…

ostrĕātus.opening: adj. id.; qs. covered with oyster-shells; hence, transf. , rough , scabby : quasi ostreatum tergum ulceribus (i. e. verberibus), Plaut. Poen. 1, 2, 186 .

ostrĕōsus.opening: adj. id. , abounding in oysters : Cyzicus ostreosa, Auct. Priap. 77 ; comp. , Cat. 18, 4 .

ostrĭāgo.opening: a plant , otherwise unknown, App. Herb. 28 .

ostrĭcŏlor.opening: adj. ostrum-color , purple-colored ( poet. ), Sid. Carm. 5, 18 .

ostrĭfĕr.opening: adj. ostrum-fero , containing or abounding in oysters ( poet. ): Abydos, Verg. G. 1, 207 : Geraestus, Val. Fl. 1, 456 : Chalcedon, Luc. 9, 959 .

ostrīnus.opening: adj. ostrum , purple (ante-class. and poet. ): supparum, Varr. ap. Non. 549, 12 : ricula, Turp. ib.: colores, Prop. 4, 12, 7 : torus, id. 1, 14, 20 : tunica, id. 3, 27, 26 .

Ostrŏgŏthus.opening: , or , , , an Ostrogoth : Ostrogothum continere, Sid. Carm. 2, 377 ; id. Ep. 8, 9 : imperium Ostrogothae vastarent, Jornand. Reb. Get. 47 ; Claud. in Eutr. 2, 153 .

ostrum.opening: , = ὄστρεον . Lit. , the blood of the sea-snail , purple (cf.: murex, purpura): ostro Perfusae vestes, Verg. A. 5, 111 ; Vitr. 7, 13 .— Transf. Stuff dyed with purple , a purple dress , purple covering , purple :…

ostrўa.opening: , and , , , = ὀστρύα, ὄστρυς , a tree with hard wood , perh. the common hornbeam , Plin. 13, 21, 37, § 117 .

Othreptē.opening: one of the Amazons , Hyg. Fab. 963 .

Othrўădes.opening: , = Ὀθρυάδης , a male proper name. The son of Othrys , i. e. Panthus : Panthus Othryades, Verg. A. 2, 319 .— A Spartan general , who , in a battle against the Argives , was the sole survivor , Ov. F. 2, 665 ; Val. Max.…

Othrys.opening: , = Ὄθρυς , a mountain in Thessaly , now Ierako : Homolen Othrymque nivalem Linquentes, Verg. A. 7, 675 ; cf. Plin. 4, 8, 15, § 30 : totus, Sen. Herc. Oet. 1168 .—Acc. to the later poets, situated in Thrace, Stat. Th.…

Ovĭdĭus.opening: Ovid , the name of a Roman gens.—So esp.: P. Ovidius Naso, a celebrated Latin poet, Quint. 10, 1, 88 ; Sen. Ep. 79, 5 ; Ov. Tr. 2, 119 .— A contemporary of Martial , Mart. 7, 44, 1 ; 7, 45, 6 .

oxălis.opening: , = ὀξαλίς , a sort of sorrel , garden sorrel , Plin. 20, 21, 85, § 231 .

oxalmē.opening: , = ὀξάλμη , a pickle or sauce made of vinegar and brine , Plin. 23, 2, 29, § 61 (al. oxyalme).

Oxartes.opening: a Persian , the father of Roxana , the wife of Alexander the Great , Curt. 10, 3, 11 .

Oxathres.opening: brother of the Persian king Darius Codomannus, Curt. 3, 11, 8 .

Oxĭmum.opening: a city in Italy , also called Auximum, Liv. 41, 21 .

Oxiones.opening: ( acc. -as), , a people in Sarmatia , Tac. G. 46, 6 .

Oxos.opening: or , , , = Ὦξος , the Oxus , a river in Asia , which rises on the borders of Hyrcania and Sogdiana , and flows into the Caspian Sea , now the Amu or Jihon , Mel. 3, 5, 6 ; Plin. 6, 16, 18, § 48 ; Curt. 7, 4, 5 .

oxўbăphus.opening: , = ὀξυβάφον , lit. a vinegar-cup (pure Lat. acetabulum); hence, a liquid measure containing fifteen drachms (post-class.), Rhem. Fan. Ponder. 75 ; cf. Isid. Orig. 16, 26 .

oxўcĕdros.opening: , = ὀξύκεδρος , a species of cedar with pointed leaves , Plin. 13, 5, 10, § 52 .

oxўgăla.opening: , = ὀξύγαλα, τό (sour milk), the thick part of curdled milk , curds , Col. 12, 8 .—Acc. to the Gr., as a neutr. , Plin. 28, 9, 35, § 134 .

oxўgărum.opening: , = ὀξύγαρον , a sauce of vinegar and garum, Mart. 3, 50, 4 .

oxўlăpăthum.opening: , = ὀξυλάπαθον , a kind of sorrel , sharp-pointed dock , Plin. 20, 21, 85, § 231 .

oxўmĕli.opening: , and , , , = ὀξύμελι , vinegar-honey , a mixture of vinegar and honey , oxymel , Plin. 23, 2, 29, § 60 .—Also written oxymelli: brassica ex aceto oxymelli et sale sparsā (al. oxymelle, al. oxymela), Cato, R. R. 157 ;…

oxўmōrus.opening: adj. , = ὀξύμωρος , acutely silly : oxymora verba, expressions which at first sight appear absurd , but which contain a concealed point; so especially of such apparently contradictory assertions as: cum tacent clamant,…

oxўmyrsīnē.opening: , = ὀξυμυρσινη , the plant prickly-myrtle , butcher's-broom (pure Lat. ruscus), Plin. 15, 7, 7, § 27 .

oxўpaedĕrōtĭnus.opening: adj. , = ὀξυπαιδερώτινος , opal-colored : vestes, Vop. Aur. 46 .

oxўpŏrus.opening: adj. , = ὀξυπόρος , that passes quickly through , penetrating; of food, easily digested; of medicine, that operates quickly : moretum, Col. 12, 56 ; Plin. 20, 7, 26, § 65 ; 20, 23, 96, § 256 ; 24, 8, 36, § 55 ; Stat. S.…

Oxyrrhŏē.opening: or , , , = Ὀξυρρόη , one of Actœon's hounds , Hyg. Fab. 181 .

oxys.opening: , = ὀξύς (sharp). Common wood-sorrel , Plin. 27, 12, 89, § 112 . — A kind of sharp rush , Plin. 21, 18, 69, § 112 .

oxўsacchărum.opening: , = ὀξυσάκχαρον , vinegar-sugar , a drink made of vinegar and sugar , Constant. Afer. 7, 1.

oxyschoenos.opening: , = ὀξύσχοινος , a kind of rush , Plin. 21, 18, 69, § 112 .

oxyzōmus.opening: adj. , = ὀξύζωμος , seasoned with sour sauce (post-class.): pullus, Apic. 6, 9 .

ozaena.opening: , = ὄζαινα . A kind of polypus : ozaena, dicta a gravi capitis odore, Plin. 9, 30, 48, § 89 .— A polypus in the nose : narium ozaenae, Plin. 25, 13, 104, § 165 .

ozaenōsus.opening: adj. ozaena, II. , affected with a polypus of the nose (late Lat.): loca, Pelag. Vet. 16.

Ozŏmĕnē.opening: the wife of Thaumas and mother of the Harpies , Hyg. Fab. 14 .

P.grammar: the fifteenth letter of the Latin alphabet, the character for which is derived from the ancient form of the Greek II
P.opening: (P or P), as is shown by inscriptions and coins, which exhibit the P in these forms.The P -sound, like the K - and T -sounds, was not aspirated in the ancient language; whence the spelling TRIVMPE for triumphe, in the…

Pa.opening: (leg. patre) et po pro potissimum positum est in Saliari carmine, Fest. p. 205 Müll.

păbillus.opening: dim. pabo , a small wheelbarrow (late Lat.), Lampr. Elag. 29 .

păbo.opening: a one-wheeled vehicle , a wheelbarrow : pabo vehiculum unius rotae, Gloss. Isid.

pābŭlāris.opening: adj. pabulum , of or fit for fodder : vicia, Col. 2, 14, 1 ; Pall. 1, 6, 14 ; Plin. 18, 16, 41, § 142 .

pābŭlārĭus.opening: adj. id. , of or belonging to fodder or pasture : PABVLARIORVM COLLEGIVM, perh. the farmers of the public pastures , Inscr. Don. cl. 9, n. 3 and 20.

pābŭlātĭo.opening: pabulor , pasture. Lit. , Varr. R. R. 3, 16 ; Col. 7, 9 fin. — Transf. , in milit. language, a collecting of fodder , a foraging : omnes nostras pabulationes frumentationesque observabat, Caes. B. G. 7, 16 ; 1, 15 :…

pābŭlātor.opening: id. . A fodderer , a herdsman; only according to the gloss: pabulator pastor, qui bubus pabula praebet, Isid. Gloss.— In milit. lang., a forager , Caes. B. C. 1, 55 ; id. B. G. 5, 17 ; Hirt. B. G. 8, 11 ; Liv. 27, 43 ;…

pābŭlātōrĭus.opening: adj. pabulator , of or for fodder : corbis, Col. 6, 3, 5 ; 11, 2, 99 .

pābŭlor.opening: v. dep. n. and a. [pabulum]. Neutr. To eat fodder , to feed , graze (syn. pascor): capella placide et lente pabulatur, Col. 7, 6, 9 ; 8, 15, 6 : pabulantia jumenta, Front. p. 2203 P.— To seek fodder , seek for food;…

pābŭlōsus.opening: adj. id. , abounding in fodder (late Lat.): insula, Sol. 22, 2 .

pābŭlum.opening: from the root pa, whence also pa-sco , food , nourishment. Lit. Of men (only poet. ): dura mundi, Lucr. 5, 944 : dira (of the human food of Polyphemus), Val. Fl. 4, 105 ; Stat. Th. 12, 566 .— Of animals, food , fodder…

pācālis.opening: adj. pax , of or belonging to peace , peaceful ( poet. ): olea, Ov. M. 6, 101 : laurus, peaceful, that betokens peace, id. ib. 15, 591 : flammae, on the altar of the goddess of peace, id. F. 1, 719 .

pācātē.opening: adv. , v. 2. paco, P. a. fin.

pācātĭo.opening: 2. paco , a peace-making , pacification , peace , Front. Strat. praef.

pācātor.opening: id. , a peace-maker , pacificator , subjugator (post-Aug.): gentium, Sen. Ben. 5, 15, 6 : terrarum, id. ib. 1, 13, 3 : orbis, id. Herc. Oet. 1990 : terrae Iberae, Sil. 16, 246 : Nemeae, id. 2, 483 : Rheni, Claud. Laud.…

pācātōrĭus.opening: adj. pacator , peace-promoting , pacific (post-class.): judicium, Tert. adv. Marc. 4, 29 .

Pācātŭla.opening: dim. pacata , a female proper name , Hier. Ep. 128 , n. 4.

pācātus.opening: Part. and P. a. , from 2. paco.

Pācensis.opening: adj. Pax Julia . Of or belonging to the city of Pax Julia (in Lusitania), the modern Beja; hence, , , , the inhabitants of that city. Inscr. Grut. 199, 4 .— Pacensis colonia, the city of Forum Julii, the mod. Frejus ,…

Păchȳnum.opening: , and ( ), (Păchўnus, Avien. Perieg. 645 ; Prisc. Perieg. 482 ), and , = Πάχυνος , the south-eastern promontory of Sicily , looking towards Greece , now Capo Passaro : ipsius promuntorium Pelorus vocatur vergens in…

Pācĭdĭānus.opening: a famous gladiator , whose combat with Æserninus , the Samnite , mentioned by Lucilius , became proverbial , Lucil. ap. Non. 393, 30 ; Cic. Opt. Gen. Or. 6, 17 ; id. Tusc. 4, 21, 48 ; id. Q. Fr. 3, 4, 2 ; Hor. S. 2, 7,…

pācĭfer.opening: adj. pax-fero , peace-bringing , that makes or announces peace , peaceful , pacific ( poet. and postclass.): sermo, Luc. 3, 305 : oliva, Verg. A. 8, 116 : laurus, Plin. 15, 30, 40, § 133 ; of the same: virga, Val. Fl.…

pācĭfĕro.opening: id. , to keep peace : pacifero, εἰρήνην ἄγω , Gloss. Gr. Lat.

pācĭfĭcātĭo.opening: pacifico , a peacemaking , pacification (class.): spes pacificationis, Cic. Att. 7, 8, 4 : opem et gratiam alicujus ad pacificationem quaerere, id. ib. 9, 11, 2 ; id. Fam. 10, 27, 2 : ubi ista pacificatio perpetrari…

pācĭfĭcātor.opening: id. , a peacemaker , pacificator (class.; cf. pacator): Allobrogum, Cic. Att. 1, 13, 2 : Servius pacificator, id. ib. 15, 7, 1 ; Liv. 27, 30, 4 ; Quint. 11, 3, 119 : Karthaginiensium, Just. 18, 2, 4 .

pācĭfĭcātōrĭus.opening: adj. pacificator , peace-making , pacificatory : legatio, Cic. Phil. 12, 1, 3 .

pācĭfĭco.opening: v. a. (ante- and post-class.; also, , , v. dep.; v. in the foll. , and cf. Prisc. p. 799 P.) [paxfacio], to make or conclude a peace (not in Cic. or Cæs.). Lit. : quo Metellus initio, Jugurthā pacificante, praesidium…

pācĭfĭcus.opening: adj. id. , peacemaking , pacific , peaceable (class.): persona, * Cic. Att. 8, 12, 4 : secures, the axes in the fasces of the lictors, Luc. 7, 63 : Janus, Mart. 8, 66 .— Plur. as subst. : beati pacifici, Vulg. Matt. 5,…

păcĭo.opening: a contract , covenant (ante-class. for pactio): pacionem antiqui dicebant, quam nunc pactionem dicimus: unde et pacisci adhuc et paco in usu remanet, Fest. p. 250 Müll. (perh. too, ap. Fest. s. v. nuptias, p. 170,…

păcisco.opening: v. n. and a. [collat. form of dep. paciscor, q. v.], to agree , contract , bargain , covenant (class. only in perf. part. pass. ): id quoque paciscunt, Naev. ap. Non. 474, 17 : paciscit, obsides ut reddant, id. ib. 18…

păciscor.opening: v. dep. n. and a. ( act. collat. form, v. supra ) [1. paco], to make a bargain , contract , or agreement with any one; to covenant , agree , stipulate , bargain , contract respecting any thing (cf.: transigo, stipulor,…

păco.opening: , prim. of paciscor and pango, to make or come to an agreement , to agree together respecting any thing: NI CVM EO PACIT TALIO ESTO, Lex XII. Tab.; cf. Dirks, Uebers. p. 516 sq.

pāco.opening: v. a. pax , to bring into a state of peace and quietness , to make peaceful , to quiet , pacify , subdue , soothe (class.; cf.: pacifico, placo). Lit. : pacare Amanum, Cic. Fam. 15, 4, 8 : omnem Galliam, Caes. B. C. 1,…

Pacōnĭus.opening: the name of a Roman gens. So M. Paconius, Cic. Mil. 27, 74 ; another M. Paconius, Suet. Tib. 61 ; Tac. A. 3, 66 .

Păcŏrus.opening: A son of Orodes , king of Parthia , the conqueror of Crassus; he was afterwards conquered by Ventidius Bassus , the legate of Antony , Cic. Att. 5, 18, 1 ; id. Fam. 15, 1, 2 ; Just. 42, 4, 6 ; 16 .— Pacorus II., a king…

pactīcĭus.opening: or , , adj. paciscor , agreed upon , stipulated , Gell. 1, 25, 8 .

pactĭlis.opening: adj. pango , plaited together , wreathed : corona, Plin. 21, 3, 8, § 11 (opp. sutilis).

pactĭo.opening: paciscor . In gen., an agreeing , covenanting; an agreement , covenant , contract , bargain , pact (syn. pactum): est autem pactio duorum plurinmve in idem placitum et consensum, Dig. 2, 14, 1 : in pactionibus faciendis…

pactĭuncŭla.opening: dim. pactio , an agreement : pactio, pactiuncula, Not. Tir.

Pactōlus.opening: , = Πακτωλός , a river in Lydia which was said to bring down golden sands , the mod. Sarabat , Verg. A. 10, 142 ; Plin. 5, 29, 30, § 110 ; Hyg. Fab. 191 ; Ov. M. 11, 142 : Pactolus aureas undas agens, Varr. ap. Non.…

pactor.opening: paciscor , one who makes a contract , a contractor , negotiator : societatis pactores, Cic. Verr. 2, 5, 21, § 55 .

Pactŭmējus.opening: a supposititious son of Canidia , Hor. Epod. 17, 50 .

Pactўē.opening: , and , , , = Πακτύη , a town of Thrace , now Doghan Arslan , Nep. Alc. 7, 4 ; Plin. 4, 11, 18, § 48 .

Pācŭvĭus.opening: ( ), , , the name of a Roman gens. So esp. Pacuvius, a celebrated Roman poet , a native of Brundisium , nephew of Ennius , and contemporary of P. Scipio Africanus , Cic. Opt. Gen. Or. 1, 1 ; id. Brut. 64, 229 ; id. Fin.…

Pădaei.opening: a people of farther India , at the mouth of the Indus. Acc. to Herodotus (3,99) they were cannibals.— Sing. collect. : vicinus Phoebo tenet arva Padaeus, Tib. 15, 1, 145 .

Pădus.opening: the Po , the principal river of Italy , Liv. 5, 33, 10 ; Mel. 2, 4, 4 sq. ; Plin. 3, 16, 20, § 117 : sive Padi ripis, Verg. A. 9, 680 : populiferque Padus, Ov. Am. 2, 17, 32 . —Hence, , , adj. , of or on the Po :…

Pădūsa.opening: a canal running from the Po to Ravenna , now the canal of St. Alberti : piscosove amne Padusae, Verg. A. 11, 457 ; cf. Plin. 3, 16, 20, § 119 .

Paean.opening: , = Παιάν . An appellation of Apollo , as the healing deity : signum Paeanis, Cic. Verr. 2, 4, 57, § 127 : Paeana voca, Ov. M. 14, 720 ; Juv. 6, 172 ; cf. Fest. p. 222 Müll.; Macr. S. 1, 17 .— Transf. A religious hymn ,…

Paeānītis.opening: , and , acc. em or , , a precious stone , now unknown, Plin. 37, 10, 66, § 180 .—Form in -tes, Sol. 9, 22 ; Prisc. Perieg. 440 ; Isid. Orig. 14, 4, 13 .

paeantis.opening: a precious stone , otherwise unknown, Sol. 9 ; Isid. Orig. 14, 4 .

paedăgōga.opening: paedagogus , a governess , Hier. Ep. 128 , n. 4.

paedăgōgātus.opening: id. , education , instruction (post-class.), Tert. adv. Val. 13 .

paedăgōgĭānus.opening: adj. paedagogium , of or belonging to the paedagogium (post-class.): puer, Amm. 26, 6, 15 ; 29, 3, 3 : qui ministeriales et paedagogiani exsistunt, reared to serve at court , Cod. Th. 8, 7, 5.

paedăgōgīum.opening: , = παιδαγωγεῖον , the place where boys of servile birth intended for pages were educated , the pages' hall (not ante-Aug.), Plin. Ep. 7, 27, 13 .— Transf. In gen., the boys in a paedagogium: paedagogium pretiosā veste…

paedăgōgo.opening: v. a. paedagogus , to educate , instruct (ante- and post-class.): depulsum mammā paedagogandum accipit, Pac. ap. Fest. s. v. repotia, p. 281 Müll.; Fulg. Planc. Contin. Virg. fin.

paedăgōgus.opening: , = παιδαγωγός , lit. a slave who took the children to school and had the charge of them at home , a governor , preceptor , pedagogue (cf. praeceptor). Lit. : non paedagogum jam me, sed Ludum vocat, Plaut. Bacch. 1, 2,…

paedĕros.opening: , = παιδέρως . A precious stone. An opal , Plin. 37, 6, 22, § 84 .— An amethyst , Plin. 37, 9, 40, § 123 .— A plant , a kind of bear's-foot , Plin. 22, 22, 34, § 76 .

Paedīa.opening: , = παιδεία (personified), a doctrine , learning , Mart. Cap. 7, 728 ; cf. id. 6, 578 .

paedīcātor.opening: 1. paedico , one given to unnatural vice , Licin. Calv. ap. Suet. Caes. 49 .

paedīco.opening: 1. paedico , one who practises unnatural vice , Mart. 6, 33, 1 ; 12, 86, 1 .

paedĭdus.opening: adj. paedor , nasty , filthy , stinking : paedidos sordidos significant atque obsoletos: tractum vocabulum a Graeco, quia παῖδες , i. e. pueri, talis sint aetatis, ut nesciant a sordibus abstinere, Paul. ex Fest. p. 222…

paedor.opening: root pu-; Sanscr. pūje, to be rotten, stink; Gr. πύθομαι, πύον; cf. pus, puter, etc. , nastiness , filth (syn.: illuvies, sordes). Lit. : barba paedore horrida, Poët. ap. Cic. Tusc. 3, 12, 26 : membra horrida paedore,…

paegnĭārĭus.opening: adj. paegnium , of or belonging to play. Thus the name paegniarii was given to gladiators who fought only in jest, Suet. Calig. 26 : APRILIS PAEGNIAR., Inscr. Orell. 2566 .

paeōnĭa.opening: , = παιωνία , the peony , so named after its discoverer, Pæon, Plin. 25, 4, 10, § 29 .

paeōnĭcus.opening: adj. paeon , of or belonging to the foot pœon , pœonic : metrum, Diom. p. 506 P.

paetŭlus.opening: adj. dim. [paetus], having a slight cast in the eye , slightly blinkeyed : redeo ad deos: ecquos si non tam strabones, at paetulos esse arbitramur? Cic. N. D. 1, 29, 80 ; cf. paetus.

paetus.opening: adj. etym. dub. , having leering eyes , with a cast in the eyes , blinking or winking with the eyes , blinkeyed; esp. as an epithet of Venus, prettily leering , with a pretty cast in her eyes , prettily blinking :…

Pāgānālĭa.opening: pagus , the festival of the pagus, celebrated in January; the country festival , rural festival , Varr. L. L. 6, § 24 ; cf. id. ib. 6, § 26 Müll.; Macr. S. 1, 16 .

pāgātim.opening: adv. pagus , by districts or villages , in every village : templa pagatim sacrata, Liv. 31, 26 ; 31, 30 .

pāgĭna.opening: root pag-(pak-), of pango, πήγνυμι; v. pagus , a written page or leaf : paginae dictae, quod ... in illis versus panguntur, id est figuntur, Fest. p. 221 Müll. Lit. : cum hanc paginam tenerem, Cic. Q. Fr. 1, 2, 3, § 10…

palmĕs.opening: 1. palma, II. E. , a young branch or shoot of a vine , a vinesprig , vine-sprout (syn. pampinus). Lit. : palmites vitium sarmenta appellantur, quod in modum palmarum humanarum virgulas quasi digitos edunt, Fest. p. 222…

palmētum.opening: 1. palma , a palmgrove , Hor. Ep. 2, 2, 184 : Hiericus palmetis consita, Plin. 5, 14, 15, § 70 ; cf. Tac. H. 5, 6 . —In sing. , Just. 36, 3, 4 .

palmĕus.opening: adj. id. . A hand'sbreadth , or palm , in length , width , etc.: orchis herba, caule palmeo, etc., Plin. 26, 10, 62, § 95 .— Of or made of palms , palm- : tabulae, Vitr. 10, 20 : tegetes, Col. 5, 15 : vinum, Plin. 12,…

palmĭcĕus.opening: and , , adj. id. , of or made of palms , palm- : palmicea sporta, Sulp. Sev. Dial. 1, 11 and 14.

palmĭfer.opening: adj. 1. palmafero , palm-bearing , abounding in palms , palmiferous : Memphin palmiferamque Pharon, Ov. Am. 2, 13, 8 : Thebae, Prop. 5, 5, 25 : Idume, Sil. 3, 600 ; cf.: palmiferos Arabas, Ov. M. 10, 478 .

palmĭger.opening: adj. 1. palmagero , palm-bearing , holding a palm-branch : Nemea, Plin. 35, 4, 10, § 27 .

palmĭpĕdālis.opening: adj. palmipes , a foot and a palm in height , breadth , etc.: limen altum palmipedale, Varr. R. R. 2, 4, 14 : malleolus, Col. 3, 19, 1 : cardines, Vitr. 10, 20 .

palmĭpes.opening: adj. palmus-pes , a foot and a palm high : palmipedi intervallo, Plin. 17, 20, 32, § 143 : gradus spectaculorum ne minus alti sint palmipede (al. palmopede), Vitr. 5, 6 fin.

palmo.opening: , no perf. , , v. a. 1. palma . To make the print or mark of the palm of one's hand , Quint. Decl. 1, 12 ; v. in the foll. P. a. —* To tie up a vine : palmare hoc est materias alligare, Col. 11, 2, 96 .—Hence, , , P. a.…

palmōsus.opening: adj. 1. palma , abounding in palm-trees : palmosa Selinūs, Verg. A. 3, 705 .

palmŭla.opening: dim. id. , the palm of the hand. Lit. , Varr. ap. Non.-372, 29: saevientes, App. M. 8, p. 105, 17 ; 3 , p. 138, 27.— Transf. The blade of an oar , an oar : palmulae appellantur remi a similitudine manūs humanae, Fest.…

palmŭlāris.opening: adj. palmula , of or with the palm of the hand : frictus, Mart. Cap. 8, 271, § 805 .

palmus.opening: 1. palma , the palm of the hand. Lit. : manūs palmum, Vitr. 2, 3 : Graeci antiqui doron palmum vocabant: et ideo dora munera, quia manu darentur, Plin. 35, 14, 49, § 171 .— Transf. , as a measure of length, a span , or…

Palmȳra.opening: ( ), , , = Παλμύρα, Παλμιρα , a city of Syria , whose ruins still remain , the seat of the empire of Odenathus and Zenobia , Plin. 5, 25, 21, § 86 ; 6, 28, 32, § 144 .—Hence, ( ), , adj. , of Palmyra : solitudines,…

pālor.opening: ( gen. plur. part. palantūm, Sil. 5, 445 ), , v. dep. ( act. collat. form , , Sulp. Sat. 1, 43 Wernsd.; Poët. Lat. Min. 3, p. 90) [cf. Sanscr. pad, go; Gr. ποῦς, ποδός ; Lat. pes], to wander up and down , to wander ,…

palpābĭlis.opening: adj. 1. palpo , that can be touched , that may be felt , palpable (late Lat.): tenebrae crassitudine palpabiles, Oros. 1, 10 : tenebrae, Hier. in Isa. 10, 32, 14 .

palpāmen.opening: id. , a stroking , caressing (late Lat.), Prud. Ham. 302 .

palpāmentum.opening: id. , a stroking , flattering (post-class.): muliebria palpamenta, Amm. 27, 12, 6 .

palpātĭo.opening: id. . A stroking , flattering , flattery : aufer hinc palpationes, Plaut. Men. 4, 2, 43 .— Trembling , terror (eccl. Lat.): tenebrae et palpatio, Vulg. Isa. 32, 14 .

palpātor.opening: id. , a stroker; trop., a flatterer : perjurus, Plaut. Rud. 1, 2, 38 ; plur. , id. Men. 2, 1, 35 .

palpē^bra.opening: (collat. form , , , Non. 218, 19 ; Cael. Aur. Tard. 2, 1 ), an eyelid (usually in plur. ; cf. cilium). Lit. : palpebrae sunt tegmenta oculorum ... munitaeque sunt palpebrae tamquam vallo pilorum, etc., Cic. N. D. 2, 57,…

palpē^brālis.opening: adj. palpebra , of or on the eyelids : palpebrales setae, Prud. Ham. 880 .

palpē^brāris.opening: adj. id. , of or for the eyelids : collyria palpebraria, Cael. Aur. Tard. 4, 2 fin.

palpē^brātĭo.opening: palpebro , a blinking with the eyes, Cael. Aur. Acut. 1, 3, 36 ; id. Tard. 1, 5, 148 .

palpē^bro.opening: v. n. palpebra , to wink frequently , to blink , Cael. Aur. Acut. 2, 10, 70 .

palpĭtātĭo.opening: palpito , a frequent and rapid motion , a palpitation : cordis, a palpitation of the heart, Plin. 32, 5, 18, § 49 : oculorum, a blinking, id. 32, 10, 46, § 132 : partium singularum, id. 11, 4, 3, § 10 .

palpĭtātus.opening: (only in the abl. sing. ), id. , a frequent and rapid motion , Plin. 9, 30, 48, § 90 .

palpĭto.opening: v. freq. n. [palpo], to move frequently and quickly , to tremble , throb , pant , palpitate. Lit. : cor palpitat, * Cic. N. D. 2, 9, 24 : radix micat ultima linguae, Utque salire solet mutilatae cauda colubrae,…

palpus.opening: ( nom. not in use) [1. palpo], the soft palm of the hand (Plautin.): timidam palpo percutit, Plaut. Am. 1, 3, 28 : palpo percutis, id. Merc. 1, 2, 42 : mi obtrudere non potes palpum, id. Ps. 4, 1, 35 .

Paltus.opening: ( ), , , = Πάλτος , a city in Syria , Plin. 5, 20, 18, § 79 ; Mel. 1, 12, 5 (as Greek, Cass. ap. Cic. Fam. 12, 13 ).

Pălūda.opening: (dressed in the military cloak), an epithet of Minerva , Enn. ap. Varr. L. L. 7, § 37 Müll. (Ann. v. 510 Vahl.); cf.: paluda a paludamentis, Varr. l. l.

pălūdāmentum.opening: kindred with pallium, q. v. , a military cloak , soldier's cloak. In gen. (very rare; cf.: sagum, trabea): cognito super umeros fratris paludamento sponsi, quod ipsa confecerat, Liv. 1, 26 ; Sall. Fragm. ap. Non. 539, 3…

pălūdātus.opening: adj. , dressed in a military cloak (v. paludamentum). In gen. (very rare): virgines, Fest. p. 329 Müll.—Hence, a soldier : qui invident stipendia paludatis, Sid. Ep. 5, 7 . — In partic., dressed in a general's cloak…

pălūdester.opening: adj. 2. palus , marshy , swampy (late Lat.): illuvies, Cassiod. Var. 2, 32 .

pălūdĭcŏla.opening: 2. palus-colo , a dweller in fens or marshes (post-class.): paludicolae Sicambri, Sid. Ep. 4, 1 fin. : Ravenna, id. ib. 7, 17 .

pălūdĭfer.opening: adj. 2. palusfero , marsh-making , swamp-making : aquae, Auct. Carm. Philom. 42.

pălūdĭgĕna.opening: adj. gen. comm. [2. palus-gigno], marsh-born , that grows in marshes : paludigena papyrus, Poët. in Anth. Lat. 2, p. 462 Burm.

pălūdĭvăgus.opening: adj. 2. palusvagor , wandering about or among morasses ( poet. ): alumni, Avien. Perieg. 312 .

pălūdōsus.opening: adj. 2. palus , fenny , boggy , marshy ( poet. ): humus, Ov. M. 15, 268 ; Prop. 4 (5), 6, 77 . Nilus, Stat. S. 3, 2, 108 : Ravenna, Sil. 8, 602 .

pălumbārĭus.opening: palumbes , a kind of hawk which attacks doves : palumbarius, = φασσοφόνος , Gloss. Philox.

pălumbes.grammar: is is i ae m. f. m. f.
pălumbes.opening: , or , , and (collat. form , , , Cato, R. R. 90 ; Col. 8, 8 ; Mart. 13, 67, 1 : , , , Cels. 6, 6, 39 ) [cf. Sanscr. kadamba, diver; Gr. κόλυμβος , columba], a woodpigeon , ring-dove : macrosque palumbes, Lucil. ap. Non.…

Palumbīnum.opening: a town of the Samnites , Liv. 10, 45 .

pălumbīnus.opening: adj. palumbes , of wood-pigeons : caro, Plin. 30, 12, 36, § 110 : fimum, id. 30, 8, 21, § 67 : ovum, Lampr. Alex. Sev. 13 .

pălumbŭlus.opening: dim. id. , little wood-pigeon , little dove , as a term of endearment (post-class.): teneo te meum palumbulum, meum passerem, App. M. 10, p. 249, 16 ; id. ib. 8 , p. 213, 33.

pālus.opening: ( neutr. collat. form , , Varr. ap. Non. 219, 18 ) [for paglus (cf. dim. paxillus); root pag-; Sanscr. pācas, snare; Gr. πήγνυμι , fasten; Lat. pango; cf.: pignus, pax], a stake , prop , stay , pale. Lit. (very freq.…

pălus.opening: ( nom. sing. pălŭs, Hor. A. P. 65 ; but usually pălūs, Verg. A. 6, 107 ; v. infra ; gen. plur. paludum, Caes. B. G. 4, 38, 2 Oud.; rarely paludium, Liv. 21, 54, 7 Drak.; Plin. 2, 68, 68, § 174 ; Just. 44, 1, 10 ; Eum.…

palusca.opening: a kind of fig , Cloat. ap. Macr. S. 2, 16 dub.

păluster.opening: ( masc. palustris, Col. 8, 14, 2 ), adj. 2. palus , fenny , marshy , swampy. Lit. : locus, Caes. B. G. 7, 20 : ager, Liv. 36, 22 ; 22, 2 : ulva, Verg. G. 3, 175 ; Col. 8, 14, 2 : ranae, Hor. S. 1, 5, 14 ; cf. calami,…

Pămīsus.opening: , = Πάμισος . A river in Messenia , Plin. 4, 3, 7, § 15 ; Mela, 2, 3, 9.— A river in Thrace , Plin. 4, 8, 15, § 30 .

pammăchārĭus.opening: pammachum , the victor in the pammachum , Hier. in Psa. 36, § 5 .

pammachum.opening: ( ), , , = παμμάχιον , an athletic contest , consisting of wrestling , boxing with the naked fists , and boxing with the cestus : in quibus (ludis) contendit pammachum (al. pammacho) quod nos pancratium vocamus, Hyg.…

Pammĕnes.opening: a Greek rhetorician , instructor of Brutus , Cic. Brut. 97, 332 ; id. Or. 30, 105 ; id. Att. 5, 20, 2 .—Hence, , , , of or belonging to Pammenes : Pammenia illa mihi non placent, those views of Pammenes, Cic. Att. 6, 2,…

Pamphăgus.opening: the name of a dog , Ov. M. 3, 210 .

Pamphĭlus.opening: , = Πάμφιλος , a Greek proper name. A disciple of Plato , whom Epicurus heard , Cic. N. D. 1, 26, 72 .— A celebrated painter , a native of Amphipolis , the instructor of Apelles , Plin. 35, 10, 36, § 75 ; 35, 11, 40, §…

Pamphȳlĭa.opening: , = Παμφυλία , a country on the sea-coast of Asia Minor , between Lycia and Cilicia , Mela, 1, 14; Liv. 33, 41, 6 ; Plin. 5, 27, 26, § 96 ; Cic. Div. 1, 1, 2 ; Stat. S. 1, 4, 77 .—Hence, , , adj. , Pamphylian : teilus,…

pampĭnārĭus.opening: adj. pampinus , of or belonging to tendrils , that has tendrils : palmitum duo genera sunt: alterum, quod, quia primo anno plerumque frondem sine fructu affert, pampinarium vocant, etc., Col. 5, 6, 29 : sarmentum, id.…

pampĭnātĭo.opening: pampino , a breaking off of superfluous tendrils and leaves of vines , a lopping or trimming of vines : ut frequenti pampinatione supervacua detrahantur, Col. 4, 6, 1 ; cf. id. 4, 6, 1, § 5 ; 4, 7, 1 ; 4, 28, 1 ; Plin.…

pampĭnātor.opening: id. , one who plucks or lops off the superfluous tendrils and leaves of vines , a vine-trimmer , Col. 4, 10, 2 : industrius, id. 4, 27, 5 .

pampĭnātus.opening: adj. pampinus , having tendrils and leaves. Lit. : lanceam argenteam pampinatam librarum triginta, Gallien. Ep. ap. Treb. Claud. 17, 5 . — Transf. , tendril-shaped , tendril-like , Plin. 16, 42, 82, § 225 .

pampĭnĕus.opening: adj. id. , full of tendrils or vine-leaves , consisting of tendrils : uvae, Ov. P. 3, 1, 13 : vites, id. ib. 3, 8, 13 : umbrae, Verg. E. 7, 58 : auctumnus, id. G. 2, 5 : hastae, wrapped round with vine-leaves, id. A. 7,…

pampĭno.opening: v. a. id. , to pluck or lop off the superfluous tendrils , shoots , and leaves of vines , to trim vines. Lit. : pampinare est ex sarmento coles qui nati sunt, de iis qui plurimum valent, primum ac secundum, nonnumquam…

pampĭnōsus.opening: adj. id. , full of foliage , leafy , branchy : vitis, Col. 5, 5, 14 ; Plin. 23, 1, 16, § 21 .

pampĭnus.opening: and (in fem. : circumflua pampinus, Claud. III. Cons. Stil. 366 : opaca, id. Epith. Pall. et Celer. 5; cf. Donat. p. 1747 P.; Serv. Verg. E. 7, 58 , acc. to whom Varro often used the word as a fem. ) [root pamp-, pap-,…

Pān.opening: ( acc. Pāna), , = Πάν , Pan , the god of the woods and of shepherds , the son of Mercury and Penelope , Cic. N. D. 3, 22, 56 ; Hyg. Fab. 224 : Pan erat armenti custos, Pan numen equarum, Ov. F. 2, 277 : Panos de more…

panăca.opening: a kind of drinking-vessel , Mart. 14, 100 in lemm.

pănăcēa.grammar: ae is ăcis f. n. m.
pănăcēa.opening: , also , , , = πανάκεια, πανακές, πάναξ . An herb to which was ascribed the power of healing all diseases , all-heal , panacea , catholicon; on the different kinds, v. Plin. 25, 4, 11, § 30 sq. : odorifera panacea,…

pănăcĭnus.opening: adj. panacea , made of the panacea : clyster, Cael. Aur. Tard. 4, 7, 95 .

Pănaenus.opening: a famous painter , brother of the sculptor Phidias , Plin. 35, 8, 34, § 54 ; 35, 8, 34, § 57 .

Pănaetĭus.opening: , = Παναίτιος , a celebrated Stoic , a native of Rhodes , the instructor and friend of Scipio Africanus the Younger , Cic. Off. 1, 26, 90 ; id. de Or. 1, 11, 45 ; id. Off. 1, 12 ; 3, 2, 7 ; id. Tusc. 1, 32, 79 : Hor. C.…

Pănaetōlĭcus.opening: adj. , = Παναιτωλικός , of or belonging to the whole of Ætolia , Panœtolian : concilium, Liv. 31, 32, 3 ; 35, 32, 8 .

Pănaetōlĭum.opening: , = Παναιτώλιον , the council of the whole of Ætolia , a general assembly or congress of the Ætolians : concilium Aetolorum quod Panaetolium vocant, Liv. 31, 29, 1 ; Weissenb. ad Liv. 31, 32, 3 .— A very high mountain…

pănāricĭum.opening: corrupted from paronychium , a disease of the finger-nails , App. Herb. 42 .

pānārĭŏlum.opening: dim. panarium , a small bread-basket , Mart. 5, 49, 10 .

pānārĭum.opening: ( ), , panis , a bread-basket : hinc panarium, ubi id (sc. panem) servabant, sicut granarium, ubi granum frumenti condebant, unde id dictum, Varr. L. L. 5, § 105 Müll.; Plin. Ep. 1, 6, 3 ; Suet. Calig. 18 ; Stat. S. 1,…

pānārĭus.opening: id. , a bread-seller : panarius, ἀρτοπώλης , Vet. Gloss.

pănăthēnāĭcon.opening: , = παναθηναϊκόν , an ointment made in Athens , Plin. 13, 1, 2, § 6 .

Pănăthēnāĭcus.opening: adj. , = Παναθηναικός , of or belonging to the Panathenœa (a popular festival of the Athenians); hence, subst. , , (sc. solemnia), the Panathenœa , Varr. ap. Serv. Verg. G. 3, 113 .— , , (sc. liber), a holiday oration…

pancarpĭnĕus.opening: adj. pancarpus , composed of all kinds of fruits : cibus, Varr. ap. Non. 264, 27 .

pancarpĭus.opening: and , , adj. , = παγκάρπιος and πάγκαρπος , consisting or composed of all kinds of fruits. Lit. : pancarpiae dicuntur coronae ex vario genere florum factae, Fest. p. 220 Müll.: Jesum cognominant Soterem et Christum ...…

Panchāĭa.opening: , = Παγχαία , a fabulous island in the Erythrœan Sea , east of Arabia , rich in precious stones , incense , myrrh , etc.: totaque turiferis Panchaia pinguis arenis, Verg. G. 2, 139 : (phoenicem) deferre nidum prope…

panchrestārĭus.opening: panchrestus , a confectioner : coquos, panchrestarios, Arn. 2, 70 .

panchrestus.opening: ( ), , adj. , = πάγχρηστος , good or useful for every thing : medicamenta, Plin. 36, 20, 38, § 146 ; 23, 7, 71, § 136 .— Transf. , ironically: cum omnes ejus comites iste sibi suo illo panchresto medicamento amicos…

panchrōmos.opening: , = πάγχρωμος (all-colored), a plant , called also verbenaca, App. Herb. 3 .

panchrus.opening: , = πάγχρους (of all colors), a variegated precious stone , Plin. 37, 10, 66, § 178 .

Panchrȳsos.opening: adj. , = πάγχρυσος , all golden : Berenice urbs, quae Panchrysos cognominata est, Plin. 6, 29, 34, § 170 .

pancrătĭas.opening: , for pancratiastes, a pancratiast , v. l. ap. Gell. 13, 27, 3 (al. pancratiastae).

pancrătĭastes.opening: , = παγκρατιαστής , a combatant in the pancratium, a pancratiast : Diagoras tres filios adulescentes habuit, unum pugilem, alterum pancratiasten, tertium luctatorem, Gell. 3, 15, 3 ; Plin. 34, 8, 19 , §§ 57, 59; Quint.…

pancrătĭcē.opening: adv. , after the manner of the pancratiasts : pancratice atque athletice valere, i. e. heartily, finely, Plaut. Bacch. 2, 3, 14 .

pancrătĭum.opening: ( ), , , = παγκράτιον . A complete combat; a gymnastic contest which included both wrestling and boxing; cf. Quint. 2, 8, 13 : et patitur duro volnera pancratio, Prop. 4, 13, 8 ; Sen. Ben. 5, 3, 1 : Autolycos pancratio…

pancrătĭus.opening: adj. , = παγκράτιος , Pancratian : metrum pancratium, a trochaic metre , consisting of a monometer hypercatalectus, Serv. Centimetr. p. 1819 P.

Pandae.opening: a people of India : gens sola Indorum regnata feminis, Plin. 6, 20, 23, § 76 .—Hence, , , adj. , of the Pandœ : gens, Sol. 52 .

Pandāna.opening: 2. pando , one of the oldest gates of Rome , so called because it always stood open: Saturnia porta, quam Junius scribit, ibi, quam nunc vocant Pandanam, Varr. L. L. 5, § 42 Müll.; Sol. 1, 13 : Pandana porta dicta est…

Pandărus.opening: A leader of the Lycians , auxiliary of the Trojans , Verg. A. 5, 496 .— A son of Alcanor , companion of Æneas , slain by Turnus , Verg. A. 9, 672 sq. ; 11, 396 .

Pandātārĭa.opening: ( or ), , , a small island in the Tyrrhenian Sea , a place of exile under the emperors , now the island of Vandolina , Varr. R. R. 1, 8, 5 ; 3, 5, 7 ; Plin. 3, 6, 11, § 82 ; Suet. Tib. 53 ; Tac. A. 1, 53 ; 14, 62 ;…

pandātĭo.opening: 1. pando , a warping of wood, Vitr. 7, 1 .

pandecter.opening: , = πανδεκτήρ (allcontaining), the title of the fourth book of the work of Apicius.

pandectes.opening: or , , , = πανδέκτης , a book that contains every thing , a complete repertory , an encyclopedia , a title frequently given to books; cf. Gell. 13, 9, 4 ; Plin. H. N. praef., § 24. In gen.: novissime Tiro in Pandecte…

pandēmus.opening: adj. , = πάνδημος , affecting all the people , public , general : lues, an epidemic, Amm. 19, 4, 7 .

pandĭcŭlāris.grammar: dicebatur dies idem et communicarius, in quo omnibus diis communiter sacrificabatur

pandĭcŭlor.opening: v. dep. 2. pando , to stretch one's self : ut pandiculans oscitatur, Plaut. Men. 5, 2, 80 ; cf.: pandiculari dicuntur, qui toto corpore oscitantes extenduntur, eo quod pandi fiunt, Fest. p. 220 Müll.

Pandīon.opening: , = Πανδίων . A king of Athens , father of Progne and Philomela , Hyg. Fab. 48 ; Ov. M. 6, 426 ; 676 : Pandionis populus, i. e. the Athenians, Lucr. 6, 1143 : Pandione nata, i. e. Progne, Ov. M. 6, 634 .— Transf. , for…

pando.opening: (acc. to Prisc. p. 891 P.), passum, and less freq. pansum (v. Neue, Formenl. 2, p. 567 sq.), , v. a. , to spread out , extend; to unfold , expand [from the root pat of pateo, cf. πετάννυμι , q. v.] (syn.: explano,…

Pandōra.opening: ( gen. Pandoras, Plin. 36, 5, 4, § 19 ), Πανδώρα, gifted by all , the first woman , made by Vulcan at Jupiter's command , and presented with gifts by all the gods , the wife of Epimetheus and mother of Pyrrha , Hyg.…

pandōrĭus.opening: or , , , i. q. pandura, Isid. Orig. 3, 20, 8 .

Pandōsĭa.opening: , = Πανδωσία . A city in Epirus , on the Acheron , now Kastri , Liv. 8, 24 ; Plin. 4, 1, 1, § 4 .— A city of the Bruttians , near the modern Mendocino , Liv. 8, 24 ; Just. 12, 2, 4 .

Pandrŏsos.opening: , i. , = Πάνδροσος , daughter of Cecrops and sister of Aglauros and Herse , Ov. M. 2, 559 ; 2, 738 .

pandūra.opening: , and , , , = πανδοῦρα , a musical instrument of three strings , invented by Pan , Isid. Orig. 3, 20 : hircipedem (i. e. Pana) pandura ... Faunum tibia decuerunt, Mart. Cap. 9, § 906 ; 9, § 924 .

pandūrizo.opening: v. n. pandura , to play the pandura, Lampr. Elag. 32 .

pandus.opening: adj. 2. pando , bent , crooked , curved (mostly poet. ; syn.: curvus, uncus): carina, Enn. ap. Vet. Schol. in Stat. Achill. 1, 558 (Ann. v. 560 Vahl.); Verg. G 2, 445 : rami, Ov M. 14, 660: juga, id. Am 1, 13, 16 :…

pănēgўrĭcus.opening: adj. , = πανηγυρικός , of or belonging to a public assembly or festival; hence, subst. : , , , the festival oration of Isocrates , in which he eulogized the Athenians , Cic. Or. 11, 37 ; Quint. 10, 4, 4 .— Transf. ,…

pănēgўrista.opening: , = πανηγυριστής , a eulogist , panegyrist , Sid. Ep. 4, 1 .

pănĕros.opening: , or , , = πανέρως , a precious stone , supposed to have the property of making fruitful , Plin. 37, 10, 66, § 178 .— , a Roman surname , Suet. Ner. 30 .—As a slavename , Inscr. Marin. Fr. Arv. p. 631.

Pangaeus.opening: , and , , , = Πάγγαιον ὄρος , a mountain of Thrace , on the borders of Macedonia , near Philippi , now Pilaf Tepeh : Mons Pangaeus, Plin. 4, 11, 18, § 40 : flerunt Rhodopeiae arces Altaque Pangaea, Verg. G. 4, 462 ;…

pango.grammar: nxi, nctum, and pēgi or pĕpĭgi, pactum 3 v. a.
pango.opening: (v. Neue, Formenl. 2, 474 sq.), , v. a. root pac-; Sanscr. pāca, band, fetter; Gr. πήγνυμι, fix; πάχνη, frost; πάσσαλος, peg, etc.; cf.: pagus, pagina, paciscor; old form paco, pago; cf.: rem ubipacunt, XII.Tab. ap.…

pangōnĭus.opening: , or , , = παγγώνιος , a precious stone , otherwise unknown, Plin. 37, 10, 66, § 178 .

pānĭcellus.opening: dim. panis , a little loaf , Plin. Val. 1, 6 .

pānĭcĕus.opening: adj. id. , made of bread : mensae, i. e. huge loaves, Serv. Verg. A. 3, 257 .—As subst. : , , , an inhabitant of Breadville : opus est Paniceis, milites panicei (a comic expression), Plaut. Capt. 1, 2, 59 .

Parthĕnŏpaeus.opening: , = Παρθενοπαῖος , the son of Meleager and Atalante , one of the seven who went against Thebes : inclutus armis Parthenopaeus, Verg. A. 6, 480 ; Stat. Th. 4, 248 ; cf. Hyg. Fab. 99 .

Parthĕnŏpē.opening: , = Παρθενόπη , one of the Sirens , who , on the departure of Ulysses , threw herself , for grief , into the sea , and was cast up on the shore where Naples afterwards stood; on this account that city was in early times…
