păvĭbundus.opening: adj. id. , fearful , anxious (post-class.): trepidationes, Arn. 7, 221 .

păvīcŭla.opening: pavio , a rammer : paviculae, ὁμαλιστῆρες , Gloss. Philox.; Cato, R. R. 91 ; 129 ; Col. 1, 6, 13 ; 12 ; 2, 20, 1 ; 11, 3, 34.

păvīcŭlo.opening: or , , v. a. pavicula , to beat down : paviclat, ποδίζει, ἐδαφίζει , Gloss. Vet.

păvĭdus.opening: adj. paveo , trembling , quaking , fearful , terrified , alarmed , timid , timorous (perhaps not in Cic.). Lit. : timida atque pavida, Plaut. Curc. 5, 2, 49 ; Lucr. 5, 973 : castris se pavidus tenebat, Liv. 3, 26 :…

păvīmentārĭus.opening: pavimentum , a maker of pavements , a pavior , Inscr. Don. cl. 9, n. 35; Inscr. Murat. 527, 6 .

păvĭmento.opening: v. a. id. . To cover with a pavement , to pave : porticus pavimentata, Cic. Q. Fr. 3, 1, 1 ; id. Dom. 44, 116 ; Vitr. 6, 5, 3 .— To make a pavement , Plin. 27, 4, 5, § 15 .

păvīmentum.opening: pavio , a floor composed of small stones, earth, or lime, beaten down with a rammer , a hard floor , a pavement : ibi de testā aridā pavimentum struito: ubi structum erit pavito fricatoque oleo, uti pavimentum bonum…

păvĭo.opening: v. a. kindr. with παιω , to beat , strike. Lit. : pavit aequor harenam, Lucr. 2, 376 : aliquid ex ore pavire terram, Cic. Div. 2, 34, 72 .— Transf. , to beat , ram , or tread down : aream esse oportet solidam, terrā…

păvĭtātĭo.opening: pavito , a trembling , quaking (post-class.), App. de Mundo, p. 65, 31.

păvītensīs.opening: adj. pavio , beaten close : vestis (opp. levidensis), Isid. Orig. 19, 22, 19 .

păvĭto.opening: v. freq. n. and a. [paveo]. In gen., to tremble or quake with fear , to be very fearful , be greatly afraid; to tremble at (ante-class. and poet. ): quae pueri in tenebris pavitant, Lucr. 2, 58 : prosequitur pavitans,…

pāvo.opening: (ante-class. and late collat. form , , Enn. ap. Charis. p. 75 P., or Ann. v. 15 Vahl.; Arn. 7, 215 ; Tert. Pall. 5 ; id. Anim. 33 ; Aus. Epigr. 69 ; id. Ep. 20, 10 ; Vulg. 3 Reg. 10, 22 ; whence fem. pava, q. v.), cf.…

Pāvo.opening: a Roman surname : Fircellius Pavo, Varr. R. R. 3, 2 .

pāvōnācĕus.opening: adj. 1. pavo , of or belonging to a peacock; transf., like a peacock's tail , variegated , Plin. 36, 22, 44, § 159 .

pāvōnīnus.opening: adj. id. , of or belonging to a peacock. Lit. : ova pavonina, Varr. R. R. 3, 9, 10 : pulli, Col. 8, 11 , 13: muscaria, fly-flaps made of peacocks' tails, Mart. 14, 67 in lemm. — Transf. , colored like a peacock's tail ,…

păvor.opening: (old nom. pavos, Naev. ap. Non. 487, 8 ; Fragm. Trag. 45 Rib.; Pac. ap. Cic. Or. 46, 155 ; Fragm. Trag. v. 82 Rib.; B. and K. read pavor), , paveo , a trembling , quaking , throbbing , panting with fear, desire, joy,…

pax.opening: from the root pac, pag, pacisco, pango; whence also pagina, pagus, q. v.: pacem a pactione conditionum putat dictam Sinnius Capito, quae utrique inter se populo sit observanda, Fest. p. 230 Müll.; orig. an agreement,…

Pax.opening: a slave's name , Plaut. Trin. 4, 2, 94 (889 Ritschl).

paxillus.opening: , = πάσσαλος , a small stake , a peg. Lit. , Varr. ap. Non. 153, 9 ; Col. 4, 16, 3 ; 8, 8, 3 : dodrantales paxilli, Plin. 17, 21, 35, § 154 ; Vulg. Isa. 22, 25 et saep.*— Transf. : novam haeresim novo paxillo…

peccāmen.opening: pecco , a fault , sin (late Lat.): omnium peccaminum venia, Hilar. in Matt. 18, 10; 25, 5; Prud. Ap. 979 ; id. Cath. 9, 96 ; Hier. in Job, 30.

peccans.opening: Part. and P. a. , from pecco.

peccanter.opening: adv. , v. pecco, P. a. fin.

peccātĭo.opening: id. , a failing , fault , sin (post-class.), Gell. 13, 20, 19 .

peccātor.opening: id. , a transgressor , sinner (post-class.), Lact. 3, 26 ; Tert. Spect. 3 ; Vulg. Matt. 9, 10 et saep.

peccātōrĭus.opening: adj. peccator , sinful (post-class.), Tert. adv. Marc. 2, 14 ; id. Carn. Chr. 8 .

peccātrix.opening: id. , a female sinner (post-class.), Paul. Nol. Carm. 28, 127 ; Hier. adv. Joann. Jerosol. n. 4; Vulg. Luc. 7, 39 .— Adj. , sinning , sinful : peccatrix anima, Prud. Cath. prooem. 35: gens, Tert. Spect. 3 : generatio,…

peccātum.opening: pecco , a fault , error , mistake , transgression , sin (syn.: delictum, culpa): pro peccatis supplicium sufferre, Ter. And. 5, 3, 17 : corrigere, id. Ad. 4, 3, 2 : peccata remordent, Lucr. 3, 827 : recte facta sola in…

peccātus.opening: id. , a failing , fault , trespass (very rare): in manifesto peccatu teneri, Cic. Verr. 2, 2, 78, § 191 , acc. to Gell. 13, 20, 17 sq. (al. peccato).

pecco.grammar: āvi, ātum, 1 v. n. and a.
pecco.opening: v. n. and a. [often referred to Sanscr. pāpa, pāpaka, wicked; but better to root pik-, to be angry; cf.: piget, pigeo, and Fick, Vergl. Wört. 632], to miss or mistake any thing; to do amiss , to transgress , to commit a…

pĕcŏrālis.opening: adj. pecus , of or belonging to cattle : aestimatio pecoralis multae, Paul. ex Fest. s. v. ovibus, p. 202 Müll.

pĕcŏrārĭus.opening: pecus , a farmer of the public pastures and herds : pecorarius, προβατώδης , Onomast. Vet.

pĕcŏrōsus.opening: adj. id. , rich in cattle ( poet. ): Palatia, Prop. 5, 9, 3 : Phyllos, Stat. Th. 4, 45 : ver, id. ib. 10, 229 .

pecten.opening: pecto , a comb. Prop., for the hair , Plaut. Capt. 2, 2, 18 ; Ov. Am. 1, 14, 15 : deducit pectine crines, id. M. 4, 311 ; 12, 409 ; Petr. 126 ; Spart. Hadr. 26 .— Transf. , of things resembling a comb. The reed or sley…

pectĭnārĭus.opening: adj. pecten , of or belonging to combs , Inscr. Spon. Miscell. Antiq. p. 231, and Inscr. Murat. 982, 7 .— Subst. : , , , a combmaker , Inscr. Alessi, Antich, d'Este, p. 181; Inscr. Grut. 648, 2 , et Fabr. p. 701, n. 221.

pectĭnātim.opening: adv. id. , in the form of a comb , like the teeth of a comb : cuniculatim, pectinatim divisa, Plin. 9, 33, 52, § 103 : digitis pectinatim inter se implexis, id. 28, 6, 17, § 59 (cf.: digitis inter se pectine junctis,…

pectĭnātor.opening: pectino , a comber , carder : pectinator, κτενιστής , Gloss. Philox.

pectĭnātus.opening: Part. and P. a. , v. pectino.

pectĭno.opening: v. a. pecten , to comb , card , heckle. Lit. : caudae setas, App. M. 6, p. 185, 18 .— Transf. , to harrow : segetem, Plin. 18, 21, 50, § 186 .— Hence, , , P. a. , combed , i. e. sloped two ways like a comb : pectenatum…

pectĭo.opening: pecto , a combing of the hair, Cael. Aur. Tard. 1, 4, 98 .

pectis.opening: a plant , called also consolida and symphyton, App. Herb. 59 .

pecto.opening: (pexui, Alcim. Ep. 77 ), pexum and , v. a. Gr. πέκω, πεκτέω, to comb, shear; πόκος, fleece; Lat. pecten , to comb. Lit. : tenues comas, Tib. 1, 9, 68 : longas comas, id. 2, 5, 8 : caesariem, Hor. C. 1, 15, 14 :…

pectŏrālis.opening: adj. pectus , of or belonging to the breast , breast- , pectoral : pectorale os, the breast-bone, Cels. 8, 1 : tunicula, Amm. 14, 9, 7 : cinctum, App. M. 11, p. 261, 36 : fascia, Vulg. Isa. 3, 24 (Hier. in loc., Vulg.…

pectŏrōsus.opening: adj. id. , with a large or high breast , full-breasted , broadbreasted : sint ergo matrices quadratae, pectorosae, magnis capitibus, Col. 8, 2, 8 ; Plin. 14, 22, 28, § 140 : nemo est feroci pectorosior Marte, Auct.…

pectuncŭlus.opening: dim. pecten , a small scallop , Col. 8, 16, 7 ; Plin. 9, 29, 45, § 84 .

pectus.opening: kindred with the Sanscr. vakshas, pectus , the breast , in men and animals. Lit. , the breast , the breastbone : pectus, hoc est ossa praecordiis et vitalibus natura circumdedit, Plin. 11, 37, 82, § 207 ; cf. Cels. 8, 7…

pectuscŭlum.opening: dim. pectus , a little breast (late Lat.), Hier. Ep. 22 , n. 30: pectus, pectusculum, Not. Tir. p. 58 ; Vulg. Exod. 29, 26 ; id. Num. 6, 20 .

Pectuscum Pălāti.opening: a part of Rome : Pectuscum Palati dicta est ea regio Urbis, quam Romulus obversam posuit eā parte, in quā plurimum erat agri Romani ad mare versus, et qui (l. qua) mollissime adibatur Urbs, etc., Fest. p. 213 Müll.…

pĕcu.opening: ( dat. pecui, Lucil. ap. Gell. infra; plur. : pecua, pecuda; gen. pecuum, Cato ap. Gell. 7, 3, 37 : pecubus, Lucr. 6, 1132 ), v. pecus , cattle , esp. the larger kinds (mostly ante-class.): pastor harum dormit, quom…

pĕcŭālis.opening: adj. pecu , of or belonging to cattle (late Lat.): animal pecuale, Sedul. 1, 146 .

pĕcŭārĭus.opening: adj. id. , of or belonging to cattle : res pecuaria, Plaut. Truc. 1, 2, 45 : pecuarii greges, herds of cattle, Varr. R. R. 2, 5, 17 : quaestio, id. ib. 2, 2, 1 : negotiatio, Col. 8, 1, 1 : canis, id. 7, 12, 8 : res, a…

pĕcŭasco.opening: , a false read. for pecus pascere, Minuc. Sentent. de Finib. Genuat. 1, 32, p. 6 Rudorff.

pĕcŭātus.opening: adj. pecu , beastly , brutal , Fulg. Moral. n. 35; cf. pecuatus, θηριώδης , Onomast. Vet.

pĕcŭdālis.opening: adj. pecu , of or belonging to cattle (post-class.), Mart. Cap. 8, § 806 .

Pĕcŭdĭfer.opening: adj. pecufero, cattle-bearing , an epithet of Sylvanus , Inscr. Murat. 70, 6 .

pĕcŭīnus.opening: adj. pecu . Lit. , of cattle (ante- and post-class.): daps, Cato, R. R. 132, 2 : ossa, App. M. 8, p. 215, 49 .— Absol. : pecuina et ferina, App. M. 11 init. — Transf. , beastly , brutal : animus, App. Mag. 281, 11 .

pĕcūlātor.opening: peculor , an embezzler of public money , a peculator , Cic. Off. 3, 18, 73 ; Tac. H. 1, 53 ; Val. Max. 5, 3, 2 ; Salv. Gub. Dei , 7, 21.

pĕcūlātōrĭus.opening: , a corrupt read., Varr. L. L. 5, § 95 ; v. Müll. ad loc.

pĕcūlātus.opening: (PEQVLATVS, Lex Apparit., v. in the foll. ), , peculor . Lit. , an embezzlement of public money , peculation : peculatus furtum publicum a pecore dictum, sicut et pecunia, eo quod antiqui Romani nihil praeter pecora…

pĕcūlĭāris.opening: adj. peculium , of or relating to private property. Lit. : peculiaris causa, concerning property, Dig. 41, 2, 44 : peculiari nomine, on account of property, ib. 14, 12, 16 .— Transf. One's own , belonging to one (cf.…

pĕcūlĭārĭus.opening: adj. id. , of or relating to private property (post-class. for the class. peculiaris): res, Dig. 44, 4, 4 : causa, ib. 15, 1, 4 fin. (al. peculiari); Inscr. Murat. 1640, 7 : peculium peculiarius, Not. Tir.

pĕcūlĭātus.opening: Part. and P. a. , from peculio.

pĕcūlĭo.opening: v. a. peculium , to give one something for one's self , as one's private property; hence, comic. in mal. part., Plaut. Pers. 2, 2, 10 .—Hence, . , P. a. , furnished with property of his own , that has private property.…

pĕcūlĭŏlum.opening: dim. peculium , a little private property , Quint. 1, 5, 46 .

pĕcūlĭōsus.opening: adj. id. , having a large private property , wealthy (ante- and post-class.): servus, Plaut. Rud. 1, 2, 24 ; Sid. Ep. 2, 2 fin. ; Aug. in Psa. 38 .

pĕcūlĭum.opening: pecus , lit., property in cattle; hence, as in early times all property consisted of cattle, in gen., property. Lit. In gen.: peculi sui prodigi (servi), Plaut. Most. 4, 1, 19 : cupiditas peculii, Cic. Par. 5, 2 fin. :…

pĕcūlor.opening: v. dep. n. [peculium], to defraud the public , to embezzle the public money , to peculate : rem publicam, Flor. 3, 17, 3 .—Hence, , , P. a. —As subst. plur. : , , , peculations : vestra, Commod. 70, 13 .

pĕcūnĭa.opening: (on the oldest inscrr., also written PEQVNIA, as PEQVDES, PEQVLIVM), pecus, because the wealth of the ancients consisted in cattle: pecus, a quo pecunia universa, quod in pecore pecunia tum consistebat pastoribus, Varr.…

pĕcūnĭālis.opening: adj. pecunia , of or belonging to money , pecuniary (post-class.): quaestus, Cael. Aur. Tard. 1, 5, 147 .

pĕcūnĭāris.opening: adj. pecunia , of or belonging to money , pecuniary (post-class. and rare for pecuniarius): damnatio, i. e. to pay a fine, Dig. 48, 19, 10 fin. dub. (al. pecuniaria).—Hence, adv. : , relating to money , pecuniarily ,…

pĕcūnĭārĭus.opening: adj. id. , of or belonging to money , pecuniary (class.): rei pecuniariae socius, in a money matter, Cic. Rosc. Am. 40, 117 : res, Tac. A. 6, 5 : praemia rei pecuniariae magna, great rewards in money, Caes. B. C. 3, 59…

Pĕcūnĭŏla.opening: dim. id. , the surname of one P. Aurelius in the first Punic war , Val. Max. 2, 7, 4 .

pĕcūnĭōsus.opening: adj. id. , that has much money , moneyed , rich , wealthy. Lit. (class.): tum erat res in pecore et locorum possessionibus, ex quo pecuniosi et locupletes vocabantur, Cic. Rep. 2, 9, 16 : homines copiis rei familiaris…

pĕcus.opening: , i. q. 1. pecus, Lucil. ap. Gell. 20, 8, 4 .

pĕda.opening: a footstep : peda vestigium humani praecipue pedis, Fest. p. 210 Müll.: peda, pedatura, ἴχνος , Gloss. Philox.

pĕdālĭon.opening: a plant , called also proserpinaca, App. Herb. 18 .

pĕdālis.opening: adj. pes , of or belonging to the foot , foot-. In gen.; hence, subst. : , , (sc. solea), a slipper , Petr 56.— In partic., of the size of a foot , of a foot , as a measure; a foot in length , breadth , thickness ,…

pĕdāmen.opening: , and , , 1. pedo , a stake or prop , with which trees and vines are supported: quibus stat recta vinea, dicuntur pedamenta: quae transversa junguntur, juga ... Pedamentum fere quattuor generum, etc., Varr. R. R. 1, 8,…

pĕdānĕus.opening: adj. pes , of the size of a foot , a foot in length , breadth , etc. Lit. (very rare): pedaneum super rudus inducimus, a foot thick, Pall. 6, 11, 2 : pedanei ramuli, Sol. 2, 42 .— Transf. Pedanei judices, petty judges…

pĕdārĭus.opening: adj. pes , of or belonging to the foot , foot-. —Only transf. pedarii senatores, those senators who had not yet been entered by the censors on the list or roll of senators , and who had no vote of their own , but could…

Pēdăsa.opening: , and , , , = Πήδασα and Πήδασον , a city in Caria , Liv. 33, 30, 3 ; Plin. 5, 29, 29, § 107 .

pĕdātim.opening: adv. pes , foot by foot , one foot after another : leo tantum et camelus (gradiuntur) pedatim, hoc est, ut sinister pes non transeat dextrum sed subsequatur, Plin. 11, 45, 105, § 253 .

pĕdātūra.opening: 1. pedo , a prop of a vine: VINEAE, Inscr. Grut. 215, 2 .

pĕdātus.opening: (collat. form of the abl. sing. pĕdāto, Cato; v. in the foll. ), 1. pedo , an attack , a charge against an enemy (ante-class.): nisi pedatu tertio omnes afflixero, Plaut. Cist. 2, 1, 50 ; for which: igitur tertio pedato…

pĕdĕplāna.opening: (sc. loca) [pesplanus], rooms on the ground-floor (postclass.), Cod. Th. 7, 8, 13.

pĕdē^pressim.opening: adv. pes-premo , cautiously : pedetentim et pedepressim dictum est caute, quasi lenta et tarda itione, Non. 29, 3 .

pĕdes.opening: pes , one that is or goes on foot. In gen.: etiam si pedes incedat, on foot, afoot, Liv. 28, 9, 15 : cum pedes iret in hostem, Verg. A. 6, 881 : silvā pedes errat in altā, Ov. M. 14, 364 .—Esp., apposit.: etiam si pedes…

pĕdester.opening: ( masc. pedestris, Nep. Eum. 4, 3 ; Vop. Prob. 21, 1 ), adj. id. , on foot , that goes , is done , etc., on foot , pedestrian. Lit. : gratior illi videtur statua pedestris futura, quam equestris, Cic. Phil. 9, 6 :…

pĕdĕtemptim.opening: or , adv. pes-tendo; qs. by stretching out the feet; cf. Doed. Syn. 3, p. 98; hence , step by step , slowly (syn.: paulatim, sensim). Lit. : expectando excrucior. Pa. Pedetemptim, Plaut. Mil. 4, 2, 32 : pedetemptim et…

Pĕdĭātĭa.opening: a nickname of the Roman knight J. Pediatius, on account of his effeminacy , Hor. S. 1, 8, 39 .

pĕdĭca.opening: pes , a shackle , fetter , or chain for the feet , a springe , gin , snare (cf.: compes, vinculum tendicula). Lit. , Plaut. Poen. 3, 1, 10 ; Liv. 21, 36 : tunc gruibus pedicas et retia ponere cervis, Verg. G. 1, 307 ;…

pĕdīcellus.opening: dim. pediculus , a little louse , Petr. 57 dub. (al. peduclum).

pĕdĭcĭnus.opening: pes , the foot of a press , Cato, R. R. 18, 3 .

pĕdīcōsus.opening: adj. pedis , full of lice , lousy , Titin. ap. Fest. s. v. pedibus, p. 210 Müll.

pĕdīcŭlāris.opening: adj. pediculus , of or belonging to lice , pedicular : herba pedicularis, lousewort (so called because it kills lice), Col. 6, 30, 8 ; v. 1. pedicularius: morbus, the lousy distemper, phthiriasis, Serv. Verg. G. 3, 564 .

pĕdīcŭlārĭus.opening: , = συντονάριος , one who pressed the scabellum with his foot , qs. a time-marker , Gloss. Philox.

pĕdīcŭlōsus.opening: adj. pediculus , full of lice , lousy , Mart. 12, 59, 8 .

pĕdīcŭlus.opening: ( , ), , dim. pedis , a louse : qui inter pilos palpebrarum pediculi nascuntur: id φθειρίασιν Graeci nominant, Cels. 6, 6, 15 ; Plin. 29, 6, 38, § 121 : ocimi cibus pediculos facit, id. 20, 12, 48, § 120 ; Col. 8, 7 :…

pĕdis.opening: pes , a louse : est pedis unus ingens in naso, Nov. ap. Non. 220, 26 : e capite et e collo eorum crebro eligendi pedes, Varr. R. R. 3, 9 : ubi quamque pedem videbat, Plaut. Vidular. Fragm. ib. 220, 28 : pedes…

pĕdĭsĕquus.opening: , and lesscorrectly , old form , , adj. pes-sequor , that follows on foot : SERVVS PEDISSEQVVS, Inscr. Murat. 928, 6 .—Hence, subst. : , , , a male attendant; a footman , man-servant , page , lackey; and, , , , a female…

pĕdĭtastellus.opening: dim. peditaster, not in use; formed like parasitaster, etc.; cf.: magistellus, cultellus, etc. , a wretched foot-soldier , tramp : at peditastelli quia erant, sivi viverent, Plaut. Mil. 1, 1, 50 Brix ad loc.

pĕdĭtātus.opening: pedes , foot-soldiers , foot , infantry (opp. equitatus, cavalry): aliquem peditatu, equitatu, copiis instruere, Cic. Phil. 5, 2, 6 : equitatum peditatumque cogere, Caes. B. G. 5, 3 .—In plur. : peditatibus et…

pĕdĭto.opening: v. n. id. , to go on foot : pedes, peditat, peditatus, Not. Tir. p. 75 : pedito, πεζεύω , Gloss. Philox.

Pĕdĭus.opening: the name of a Roman gens. —So, Q. Pedius, a joint-heir with Augustus to Cœsar's estate , Cic. Att. 9, 14, 1 ; id. Planc. 7, 17 ; Suet. Caes. 83 ; Vell. 2, 65, 2 .— Q. Pedius, grandson of the former , born dumb , became…

pĕdo.opening: pes , one who has broad feet , a splay-foot : pedo, plancus, πλατύπους , Gloss. Philox.

pēdo.opening: (pēdĭtum), , v. n. for perdo, Sanscr. root pard-; Gr. πέρδω, πορδή; cf. Germ. Furz; Engl. fart , to break wind , Hor. S. 1, 8, 46 ; Mart. 10, 14, 10 .— Part. as subst. : , = crepitus ventris, Cat. 54, 3 .

Pĕdo.opening: a Roman surname. —Esp., M. Juventius Pedo, Cic. Clu. 38, 107 .— C. Pedo Albinovanus, a poet; v. Albinovanus.—Others are mentioned, Juv. 7, 129 ; Mart. 5, 5, 6 ; 10, 19, 10 .

pĕdocucullus.opening: a covering for the feet : pedocucullus, cuculluspedo, Not. Tir. p. 157 .

Pĕdūcaeus.opening: a Roman surname. —So, Sex. Peducaeus, a prœtor in Sicily when Cicero was quœstor there , Cic. Verr. 2, 2, 56, § 138 .—Hence, , , adj. , Peducœan : ??ensus Peducaeanus, Cic. Verr. 2, 2, 56, § 139 .— , , adj. , Peducœan :…

pĕdūcŭlus.opening: a louse; another form for pediculus, v. h. v.

pĕdūlis.opening: adj. pes , of or for the feet : fasciae crurales pedulesque, Dig. 34, 2, 26 . — Subst. : , , , a sole : pedale mensura est pedis: pedule vero sub pedibus praestat utilitatem, Front. Diff. Voc. p. 2194 P.: pes, pedale,…

pĕdum.opening: id. , a shepherd's crook , a sheep-hook , Verg. E. 5, 88 : pedum est baculum incurvum, quo pastores utuntur ad comprehendendas oves, aut capras a pedibus: cujus meminit etiam Vergilius in Bucolicis, Fest. p. 249 Müll.;…

Pĕdum.opening: a town of remote antiquity in Latium , near Rome , prob. the mod. Gallicano , Liv. 2, 39 ; 8, 12 ; 13 .— Hence, , , adj. , of Pedum , Pedan : regio, Hor. Ep. 1, 4, 2 .— Subst. : , , (sc. praedium), an estate near Pedum…

Pēgae.opening: Πηγαί , a fountain in Bithynia , Prop. 1, 20, 33 .

pēgănon.opening: , = πήγανον , gardenrue , App. Herb. 89 .— Peganon orinon = πήγανον ὀρεινόν , wild-rue , App. Herb. 115 .

pēgē.opening: , = πηγή , a fountain , v. l. ap. Prop. 1, 20, 33 , for Pegae, q. v.
