per-cĕlĕbro.opening: v. a. , to practise a thing very frequently. In gen. (post-class.): ut exercerent, ut gererent, ut percelebrarent haec mala, Arn. 2, 43 .— In partic., to pronounce frequently , to have often in one's mouth (class.): de…

per-cĕler.opening: adj. , very quick or swift : interitus, Cic. Cael. 24, 58 .— Adv. : , very quickly , very soon , Cic. Fam. 6, 12, 3 .

per-cello.opening: (perculsi for perculi, Amm. 17, 8, 4 ; 25, 8, 13 ), v. a. cf.: procella, celer , to beat down , throw down; to overturn , upset (class.; syn.: percutio, deicio). Lit. : ventus Cercius plaustrum oneratum percellit, Cato…

per-censĕo.opening: v. a. , to go through or over a thing. Lit. , to count over , reckon up , enumerate : inveniendi locos, Cic. Part. 36, 127 : gentes, Liv. 33, 32 ; 10, 36, 15 : numerum legionum, Tac. A. 4, 4 : res Caesaris, Plin. 7, 26,…

percensĭo.opening: percenseo , a going over , a survey , review , Front. Orat. Ep. 3 Mai.

percepta.opening: plur. , v. percipio, P. a. fin.

perceptī^bĭlis.opening: percipio . Perceptible , Cassiod. Hist. Eccl. 5, 20 .— Participating in any thing, Boëth. Dial. in Porphyr. 1, 20.

perceptĭo.opening: percipio , a taking , receiving; a gathering in , collecting. Lit. , Ambros. in Luc. 4, 15 : frugum fruetuumque reliquorum, Cic. Off. 2, 3, 12 : fructuum, Col. 1, 3, 2 .— Trop. , perception , comprehension (cf.: notio,…

perceptor.opening: id. , a receiver , imbiber (late Lat.): sapientiae, Aug. Soliloq. 1, 1 fin.

perceptus.opening: Part. and P. a. , from percipio.

percernis.opening: adj. per-cerno , easily visible , Inscr. Fabr. p. 615 , n. 127.

per-cīdo.opening: ( perf. percecīdi, Flor. 4, 12, 7 ), , v. a. caedo , to beat or cut to pieces , to smash. In gen.: os alicui, Plaut. Pers. 2, 4, 12 ; id. Cas. 2, 6, 52 ; Sen. Q. N. 4, 4, 1 .— Esp. To cut to pieces , rout utterly ,…

per-cĭĕo.grammar: cīvi and ii, ĭtum, 2 īvi and ĭi, ītum, 4 v. a.
per-cĭĕo.opening: , and , , v. a. , to move or rouse greatly , to stir up , excite. In gen.: irai fax subdita percit, Lucr. 3, 303 ; 3, 184 : crura hercle defringentur nisi istum verbum saepe unum perciet aureis Omnibus, id. 4, 563 .— In…

percingo.opening: , v. l. for praecingere (q. v.), Col. 10, 347 ; Manil. 3, 325 .

percĭpĭbĭlis.opening: adj. percipio , perceptible : aër ictus auditu percipibilis, Mar. Vict. p. 2451 P.

per-cĭpĭo.opening: (old form of the pluperf. percepset for percepisset, Poët. ap. Cic. Off. 3, 26, 98 ; v. Trag. Rel. p. 207 Rib.), v. a. capio , to take wholly , to seize entirely (cf. occupo). Lit. To take possession of , to seize ,…

percis.opening: , a false reading for pegris, Plin. 32, 11, 53, § 150 .

per-cĭto.opening: v. a. , to excite thoroughly , strongly , vehemently (ante-class.), Pac. ap. Fest. s. v. reciprocare, p. 274 Müll.: matronae percitatae tumultu, Att. ap. Non. 467, 27 .

percĭtus.opening: Part. and P. a. , from percieo.

per-cīvīlis.opening: adj. , very courteous , affable , civil : sermo, Suet. Tib. 28 .

per-clāmo.opening: v. a. , a false reading, Plaut. Truc. 1, 1, 8 ; Speng. superba facta.

per-clāresco.opening: v. inch. n. , to become very clear , very well known (postclass.), Symm. Ep. 10, 72 bis.

percnoptĕrus.opening: (= περκνόπτερος , dusky-winged), a mountain-stork , i. q. oripelargus, Plin. 10, 3, 3, § 8 .

percnos.opening: ( ), , (= περκνός , dusky), a kind of eagle , Plin. 10, 3, 3, § 7 .

percognĭtus.opening: Part. and P. a. , from percognosco.

per-cognosco.opening: v. a. , to become perfectly acquainted with : aliquem, Plaut. Truc. 1, 2, 50 (Speng. pergnovi).— Hence, , , P. a. , well known : lex naturae non ignota, etsi nondum percognita, Plin. 2, 45, 45, § 116 : Germania, id. 4,…

per-cŏlăpho.opening: v. a. , to buffet well , Petr. 44 dub.

percōlātĭo.opening: 1. percolo , a straining through , a filtering , Vitr. 8, 7 .

per-cōlo.opening: v. a. , to strain through , to filter , percolate. Lit. : tum vinum percolato, polentam abicito, Cato, R. R. 108 ; Cels. 6, 9 ; Col. 12, 41, 2 ; Plin. 31, 6, 37, § 70 .— Transf. , in gen., to cause to pass through :…

per-cŏlo.opening: v. a. Lit. To cultivate , of the soil; hence, to inhabit : Eleusiniam glebam, App. M. 11, 2, p. 257 .— To perfect , finish : incohata percolui, Plin. Ep. 5, 6, 41 .— Transf. To cleanse : os curā, App. Mag. 8 .— To deck…

percŏlŏpo.opening: v. a. per-colophus , to box the ears of one, to beat : larvas sic istos percolopabant, Petr. 44, 5 .

per-cōmis.opening: adj. , very friendly , very courteous , Cic. Brut. 58, 212 .

per-commŏdus.opening: adj. , very suitable , very convenient , very opportune : alicui rei, Liv. 22, 43, 11 .— Adv. : , very suitably , very conveniently , very well : percommode accidit, quod, etc., Cic. Caecin. 27, 77 : percommode factum…

per-cōnor.opening: v. dep. , to carry out an undertaking, Sen. Ep. 95, 46 .

percontātĭo.opening: ( ), , percontor , an asking , inquiring after any thing; a question , inquiry. In gen. (class.): tempus percontatione consumere, Cic. Univ. 1 : aliquid percontationibus reperire, Caes. B. G. 5, 13 : percontatio quid in…

percontātīvus.opening: ( ), , adj. percontor , universally known (postclass.), Cael. Aur. Tard. 4, 8, 114 .— In gram., interrogative : modus, Diom. p. 328 P.— Adv. : , inquiringly , Charis. p. 161 P.

percontātor.opening: ( ), , id. , an asker , inquirer , Plaut. Men. 5, 5, 31 : percontatorem fugito; nam garrulus idem est, Hor. Ep. 1, 18, 69 .

perconto.opening: ( ), , v. a. and n. (ante- and post-class.) [v. percontor], to question strictly or particularly , to inquire earnestly : docte percontat, Aeneas quo pacto, etc., Naev. ap. Non. 474, 7 : si percontassem, etc., Nov. ib.…

percontor.opening: ( ), ( inf. percontarier, Plaut. Am. 2, 2, 78 ; id. As. 2, 2, 76 ; id. Cas. 3, 3, 8 ; id. Most. 4, 2, 47 al. ), v. dep. a. and per and root cunc-; Sanscr. canc- (canka, hesitation); cf. ὄκνος for κόκνος , to ask…

per-contŭmax.opening: adj. , very obstinate , very contumacious , Ter. Hec. 3, 5, 54 .

per-cŏŏpĕrĭo.opening: v. a. , to cover entirely , Theod. Prisc. 4, 1 al.

per-cōpĭōsus.opening: adj. , very abundantly supplied; hence, very rich in expression, very copious, Plin. Ep. 9, 31, 1 ; Sid. Ep. 1, 1 .— Adv. : , very copiously , Sid. Ep. 4, 7 fin.

per-cŏquo.opening: v. a. , to boil or cook thoroughly , boil soft. Lit. : prandium, Plaut. Merc. 3, 3, 18 : bubulas carnes, Plin. 23, 7, 64, § 127 : lens non bene percocta, id. 22, 25, 70, § 142 .—Prov.: In digitis hodie percoquam quod…

Percōsĭus.opening: adj. , = Περκώσιος , of or belonging to Percosius , king of Cyzicus : Percosia conjux, i. e. Clyte, wife of king Percosius, Val. Fl. 3, 10 .

Percōtē.opening: , = Περκώτη , a Trojan town on the coast of Mysia , now Bourgas , Plin. 5, 32, 40, § 141 ; Val. Fl. 2, 622 .

per-crēbesco.opening: , and , , v. inch. n. , to become very frequent or prevalent , to be spread abroad (class.): cum hoc percrebrescit, Cic. Att. 1, 1, 1 : quae (opinio) apud exteras nationes omnium sermone percrebruit, Cic. Verr. 1, 1, 1…

per-crĕpo.grammar: ŭi, ĭtum, 1 v. a. and n.
per-crĕpo.opening: v. a. and n. Neutr. , to sound very much , to resound , ring : lucum percrepare vocibus, Cic. Verr. 2, 5, 13, § 31 .— Act. , to make resound , to celebrate loudly : pugnam, Lucil. ap. Non. 255, 14 .

per-cresco.opening: v. n. , to grow greatly , Ser. Samm. 36, 679 .

per-crībro.opening: v. a. , to sift thoroughly , Scrib. Comp. 87 : res contusae et percribratae, id. ib. 289 .

per-crŭcĭo.opening: v. a. , to torment or vex greatly : hoc est demum quod percrucior, for which I vex myself, grieve, Plaut. Bacch. 5, 1, 13 .

per-crūdus.opening: adj. Lit. , quite raw : coria, Vitr. 10, 20, 3 .— Transf. , quite unripe or crude : pruna, quite green, Col. 12, 10, 4 .

per-cūdo.opening: v. a. , to strike or break through : an pulli rostellis ova percuderint, Col. 8, 5, 14 (Schneid. pertuderint).

percultor.opening: 2. percolo , an ardent adorer or reverencer : doctorum, Aur. Vict. Caes. 1, 5 .

per-cumbo.opening: v. n. , mentioned as an unused form, Varr. L. L. 9, § 49 Müll.

per-cŭpĭdus.opening: adj. , very partial to , very fond of one.—With gen. : percupidus tui, Cic. Fam. 1, 7, 2 .

per-cŭpĭo.opening: v. a. , to wish greatly , desire earnestly , to long (ante-class.): percupio obsequi gnato meo, Plaut. As. 1, 1, 61 ; Ter. Eun. 5, 2, 57 .

per-cūrĭōsus.opening: adj. , very curious or inquisitive : servolus, percuriosus et minime mendax, Cic. Clu. 62, 175 .

per-cūro.opening: v. a. , to heal thoroughly , cure completely (perh. not anteAug.). Lit. : percurato vulnere, Liv. 21, 57 ; Curt. 4, 6, 21 ; 7, 6, 23 : tarde percurabitur, Col. 6, 12, 2 : donec strumae percurentur, Plin. 32, 8, 28, § 88…

per-curro.grammar: percŭcurri or percurri, percursum, 3 v. a. and n.
per-curro.opening: v. a. and n. Act. , to run through , hasten through; to pass through , traverse , run over , pass over or along class.; syn. peragro). Lit. : percurrere agrum Picenum, Caes. B. C. 1, 15 : labro calamos, Lucr. 4, 588 :…

percursātĭo.opening: percurso , a running or travelling through , a traversing : Italiae, Cic. Phil. 2, 25, 62 .— Absol. , Cic. Phil. 2, 39, 100 .

percursĭo.opening: percurro , a running through or over; trop., A rapid or hasty thinking over a thing: propter animi multarum rerum brevi tempore percursionem, Cic. Tusc. 4, 13, 31 .— Rhet., a rapid or hasty passing over a subject: huic…

percurso.grammar: āre v. freq. a. and n.
percurso.opening: v. freq. a. and n. id. . Act. , to run or range through , ramble over (perh. not ante-Aug.): ripas, Plin. Pan. 12, 11 .— Neutr. , to range or rove about : finibus nostris, Liv. 23, 42, 10 .

percursor.opening: id. , one who runs through : viae, Lact. 6, 7 dub. (al. praecursor).

percussĭbĭlis.opening: adj. percutio , penetrating , pervading (post-class.): odor, Cael. Aur. Acut. 1, 16, 163 : virtus, id. Tard. 2, 13, 164 .

percussĭo.opening: id. , a beating , striking (class.). Lit. : capitis percussiones, beatings on the head, Cic. Tusc. 3, 26, 62 : digitorum, a snapping, id. Off. 3, 19, 75 . — Transf. , in music and rhetoric, a beating time; hence,…

percussĭōnālis.opening: adj. percutio , adapted for striking , played by striking : instrumentum musicum, Cassiod. Mus. 1 .

percussor.opening: id. , a striker , stabber , shooter. In gen. (post-Aug.): leo vulneratus percussorem novit, Plin. 8, 16, 19, § 51 .— In partic., a murderer , assassin , bandit (class.; syn.: sicarius, interfector), Cic. Phil. 2, 29, 74…

percussūra.opening: id. , a blow , stroke , thrust (post-class.): percussura ferro facta, App. Herb. 31 ; Veg. Vet. 2, 20, 1 ; Vulg. Lev. 14 . 54.

percussus.opening: percutio , a beating , striking ( poet. and in post-Aug. prose): caducis Percussu crebro saxa cavantur aquis, Ov. P. 2, 7, 40 ; Sen. Q. N. 2, 6, 3 : venarum, Plin. 7, 51, 52, § 171 : non sentire percussum, not to feel…

per-cŭtĭo.opening: ( perf. contr. percusti for percussisti, Hor. S. 2, 3, 273 ), v. a. quatio . (With the notion of the per predominating.) To strike through and through , to thrust or pierce through (syn.: percello, transfigo). Lit. :…

perdāgātus.opening: Part. (from the obsol. perdāgo, like indago), explored , Claud. Mam. Stat. Anim. 2, 3 init.

per-dēcĭpĭo.opening: v. a. , to deceive utterly (late Lat.): aurum populum ... sic specie perdecepit, ut hoc esse deum crederent, Petr. Chrys. Serm. 29 .

per-dĕcōrus.opening: adj. , very comely , very pretty (post-Aug.), Plin. Ep. 3, 9, 28 .

per-dēfessus.opening: adj. , worn out , utterly wearied : vexationibus, Petr. Chrys. Serm. 112 .

per-dēflĕo.opening: , ēre. , v. a. , to lament : generis humani primordia perdeflenda, Petr. Chrys. Serm. 166 .

per-dēlĕo.opening: v. a. , to destroy utterly , to exterminate (post-class.), Tert. adv. Jud. 11 ; Veg. Vet. 3, 10 .

per-dēlīrus.opening: adj. , very silly or foolish ( poet. ), Lucr. 1, 692 .

per-densus.opening: adj. , very compact , very dense (post-Aug.): humus, Col. 3, 12, 2 .

per-depso.opening: v. a. , to knead over , to work up , in mal. part., Cat. 74, 3 .

perdīcālis.opening: adj. perdix , of or belonging to partridges , partridge- (postclass.): herba, App. Herb. 81 .

Perdiccas.opening: and , , , = Περδίκκας . Perdiccas , a Macedonian general under Alexander the Great , Curt. 3, 9, 7 ; 4, 3, 1 ; 7, 6, 19 ; Cic. Tusc. 5, 12, 34 ; Just. 13, 2, 5 ; 13, 6, 6 ; Nep. Eum. 3, 5 .— The name of three kings of…

perdīcĭum.opening: , = περδίκιον . Pellitory : helxinen vocant, Plin. 22, 17, 19, § 41 .— The plant parthenium, Plin. 21, 30, 104, § 176 .

per-dīco.opening: v. a. , to say out , to finish saying (post-class.), Alcim. 5, 607 ; cf.: dicit, perdicit, perdixit, Not. Tir. p. 10 .

per-diffĭcĭlis.opening: adj. , very difficult (class.), Cic. Part. 24, 84 : quaestio, id. N. D. 1, 1, 1 : navigatio, id. Att. 3, 8, 2 .— Sup. : perdifficillimus aditus, exceedingly difficult, Liv. 40, 21 .— Adv. : , with great difficulty ,…

per-dignus.opening: adj. , very worthy; with abl. : homo perdignus tuā amicitiā, Cic. Fam. 13, 6, 4 .

per-dīlĭgens.opening: adj. , very diligent : homo, Cic. Q. Fr. 3, 5, 6 .— Adv. : , very diligently , Cic. Att. 1, 11, 1 : complecti aliquid, id. Brut. 3, 14 .

per-disco.opening: v. a. , to learn thoroughly or completely , to get by heart (rare but class.): omnia jura belli, Cic. Balb. 20, 47 : locus de moribus est oratori perdiscendus, id. de Or. 1, 15, 69 : hominis speciem pingere, id. ib. 2,…

per-dĭsertus.opening: adj. , very eloquent (late Lat. and rare), Gram. Vat. Praep. 5 (Class. Auct. vol. 5 Mai).—Hence, , adv. , very eloquently , Cic. de Or. 1, 14, 62 .

perdĭtē.opening: adv. , v. perdo, P. a. fin.

perdĭtim.opening: adv. perditus , desperately , to desperation : aliquam amare, Afran. ap. Charis. p. 191 P. (Com. Rel. v. 354 Rib.).

perdĭtĭo.opening: perdo , ruin , perdition (post-class.): perditionis iter, Alcim. 4, 138 ; Lact. 2, 14, 11 ; 4, 18, 32 ; Vulg. Matt. 7, 13 et saep.; cf. perditio, ἀπώλεια , Gloss. Philox.

perdĭtor.opening: id. , a ruiner , destroyer (rare but class.): perditor rei publi cae, Cic. Planc. 36, 89 ; id. Vatin. 3, 7 : vexa tor et perditor, id. Pis. 34, 84 : afflictor et perditor ordinis, id. ib. 27, 64 : hominum, Lact. 2, 14,…

perdĭtrix.opening: perditor , she that ruins or destroys (eccl. Lat.), Tert. Exhort. ad Cast. 13 ; Hier. Ep. 123 , n. 8.

perdĭtus.opening: Part. and P. a. , from perdo.

per-dĭu.opening: adv. , for a great while , very long (rare but class.), Varr. R. R. 1, 58 : perdiu nihil eram auditurus, Cic. Att. 3, 22, 4 ; id. de Or. 1, 2, 8 .

per-dĭus.opening: adj. dies , all day long , the livelong day (post-class.): stare solitus Socrates dicitur, pertinaci statu perdius atque pernox, Gell. 2, 1, 1 ; App. M. 5, p. 161, 11 ; 9 , p. 219, 23.

per-dĭŭturnus.opening: adj. , that lasts a very long time , very lingering or protracted (rare but class.), Cic. N. D. 2, 33, 85 (but Cic. Sest. 27, 58 Halm and B. and K. read diuturnum).

per-dīvĕs.opening: adj. , very rich , Cic. Att. 6, 1, 3 : mulier perdives et nobilis, Cic. Verr. 2, 4, 26, § 59 .

per-dīvīsus.opening: adj. , wholly parted from , quite apart from : marito, Petr. Chrys. Serm, 164.

perdix.opening: , = πέρδιξ , a partridge , Plin. 10, 33, 51, § 100 ; Mart. 3, 37, 15 : perdicas Boeotios, Varr. ap. Non. 218, 18 : picta, Mart. 3, 58, 15 ; Vulg. Jer. 17, 11 .

Perdix.opening: In mythology, the nephew of Dœdalus , Ov. M. 8, 241 sq. ; Hyg. Fab. 274 .

per-do.opening: (old form of the pres. subj. perduim, Plaut. Aul. 4, 6, 6 : perduis, id. Am. 2, 2, 215 ; id. Capt. 3, 5, 70 : perduit, id. Ep. 1, 1, 64 ; id. Poen. 3, 4, 29 ; but esp. freq., perduint, Plaut. As. 2, 4, 61 ; id. Aul. 4,…

per-dŏcĕo.opening: v. a. , to teach or instruct thoroughly (rare but class.; syn. erudio): res difficilis ad perdocendum, Cic. Sest. 44, 96 : aliquem, Plaut. Capt. 3, 5, 59 : quanti istuc unum me coquitare perdoces? id. Ps. 3, 2, 85 : si…

per-dŏlĕo.opening: , ìtum, , v. n. , to pain or grieve greatly (ante-class.): id perdolitum est T. Manlio, Q. Claud. ap. Gell. 9, 13, 13 : tandem perdoluit, Ter. Eun. 1, 2, 74 .

perdŏlesco.opening: or , , v. inch. n. [per-doleo], to feel great pain or grief : nec perdoliscit fligi socios, Att. ap. Non. 110, 31 (Trag. Rel. p. 150 Rib.): suam virtutem irrisui fore perdoluerunt, * Caes. B. C. 2, 15 .

per-dŏlo.opening: v. a. , to hew out , to fashion with hewing (post-Aug.): cum in materiem perdolantur, Vitr. 2, 10, 2 : arbor perdolata, id. 2, 9, 7 : fomes perdolatus, Arn. 6, 209 .

per-dŏmĭnor.opening: v. dep. n. , to rule or reign throughout a period of time: annum, Claud. Fesc. Nupt. Honor. 77 .

perdŏmĭtor.opening: perdomo , a tamer , subduer (eccl. Lat.): mortis, Prud. Cath. 4, 12 .

per-dŏmo.opening: v. a. To tame or subdue thoroughly , to subjugate completely , to conquer , vanquish , overcome , etc. (Aug.; syn. subigo): ad perdomandum Latium exercitum circumducere, Liv. 8, 13 : Hispaniam, id. 28, 12 : Apulia…

per-dormisco.opening: v. n. dormio , to sleep on : perdormiscin' tu usque ad lucem? Plaut. Men. 5, 5, 29 .

per-dūco.opening: ( imper. perduce for perduc, Ser. Samm. 40, 754 ), v. a. , lit., to lead or bring through; hence, To lead , bring , conduct , guide a person or thing to any place. In gen. (class.): filium illuc, Ter. And. 1, 1, 53 :…

perductĭo.opening: perduco, I. A. 2. , a leading , conducting of water (only in Vitr.): aquarum perductiones ad habitationes, Vitr. 8, 6 .

perducto.opening: v. freq. a. perduco , to lead , conduct to or over a place (Plautin. in the double sense of perductor, q. v.): quicquid est, errabo potius, quam perductet quispiam, Plaut. Most. 3, 2, 160 .

perductor.opening: id. , a leader , conductor; in partic., a pimp , pander (cf. perduco, I. B. 1.): lenonum, aleatorum, perductorum nulla mentio fiat, Cic. Verr. 2, 1, 12, § 34 (lenones sunt scortorum: perductores etiam invitarum…

per-dūdum.opening: adv. , a very long time ago : vidi edepol hominem haut perdudum, Plaut. Stich. 4, 1, 69 .

perdŭellĭo.opening: perduellis . Hostile conduct against one's country , treason , whether consisting of an attempt against the state, its institutions, and chief ruler, or of union with a foreign enemy, desertion, etc. (class.): qui…

per-dŭellis.opening: ( gen. plur. perduellūm, Att. ap. Non. 22, 15 , or Trag. Rel. p. 238 Rib.; abl. perdvellibus, Enn. ap. Varr. L. L. 7, § 49 Müll., or p. 146 Vahl.), per-duellum, i. e. bellum , a public enemy , an enemy actually waging…

per-dulcis.opening: adj. , very sweet; sup. † PERDVLCISSIMUS, Inscr. Rein. cl. 20, n. 150.

per-dūro.grammar: āvi, ātum, 1 v. a. and n.
per-dūro.opening: v. a. and n. Act. , to make hard , to harden (late Lat.): teneras plantas, Prud. Psych. 447 .— Neutr. , to last or hold out , to endure ( poet. and in post-Aug. prose; cf.: obduro, perfero), Ter. Hec. 2, 2, 27 :…

Perĕdĭa.opening: peredo , Gobbledom , Eating-land , a comically formed name of a country, analogous to Bibesia,. Plaut. Curc. 3, 74 .

pĕr-ĕdo.opening: v. a. , to eat up , consume ( poet. ). Lit. : cibum, Plaut. Fragm. ap. Prisc. p. 893 P.: quinque panes et gemellos pisces, Prud. Cath. 9, 58 .— Transf. , to consume , devour , etc.: nec peredit Impositam celer ignis…

pĕr-ēdo.opening: v. a. , to give forth , an old poet in Sid. Ep. 9, 14 .

per-efflo.opening: v. a. , to breathe out entirely , breathe away (post-class.): animam, App. M. 8, p. 207, 23 .

per-efflŭo.opening: v. n. , to flow through. — Trop. , to forget , Vulg. Heb. 2, 1 (transl. of the Gr. παραρρυῶμεν ).

pĕrĕger.opening: ( ), per-ager, who has gone through lands, i. e. , who is on a journey , abroad , away from home (postclass.): si pereger factus sit, Ulp. Reg. tit. 17, 1 (dub.; Huschke, peregrinus): nedum me peregrem composita…

pĕr-ēgrĕgĭus.opening: adj. , very excellent (post-class.): tragoedia, App. Mag. p. 298, 6 .

pĕrĕgrīnābundus.opening: adj. peregrinor , travelling about (rare): dux, Liv. 28, 18, 10 ; Fulg. Myth. 3, 7 fin.

pĕrĕgrīnātĭo.opening: peregrinor , a being or living abroad , a sojourning , a travelling in foreign parts , a travelling about , travel , peregrination (class.). Lit. : perpetua, Cic. Tusc. 5, 37, 107 : transmarina, Quint. 7, 3, 31 ; 12,…

pĕrĕgrīnātor.opening: id. , one who travels about , Cic. Fam. 6, 18, 5 .

pĕrĕgrīnĭtas.opening: peregrinus . The condition of a peregrinus or foreigner , opp. to that of a Roman citizen, alienage (post-Aug.): peregrinitatis reus, Suet. Claud. 15 : in peregrinitatem redigere aliquem, id. ib. 16 ; Dig. 2, 4, 10 .—…

pĕrĕgrīnor.opening: v. dep. n. [id.], to be or live in foreign parts , to sojourn abroad , to travel about (class.; cf.: peragro, migro). Lit. : peregrinari totā Asiā, Cic. Brut. 13, 51 : in alienā civitate, id. Rab. Perd. 10, 28 : in…

pĕrĕgrīnŭlus.opening: adj. peregrinus , estranged (late Lat.), Ven. Fort. Vit. Germ. 64.

pĕrĕgrīnus.opening: adj. peregre , that comes from foreign parts , strange , foreign , exotic (cf.: exter, externus). Lit. In gen. Adj. : ad portum mittunt servulos, ancillulas: peregrina navis, etc., Plaut. Men. 2, 2, 65 : facies, id. Ps.…

pĕr-ēlĕgans.opening: adj. , very neat , fine , or elegant (class.): genus, Cic. de Or. 2, 67, 270 : oratio, id. Planc. 24, 58 : ingenium, Vell. 1, 7, 1 .— Adv. : , very finely , very elegantly : pereleganter dicere, Cic. Brut. 52, 197 .

pĕr-ēlixo.opening: v. a. , to boil thoroughly (post-class.): denuo eum perelixabis (al. perlaxabis), Apic. 7, 7, § 289 .

pĕr-ēlŏquens.opening: adj. , very eloquent : Lentulus, Cic. Brut. 70, 247 .

pĕr-ēmensus.opening: adj. , all measured out : permensus, peremensus, Not. Tir. p. 118 .

pĕremnis.opening: adj. per-amnis , of or belonging to crossing a river; only in augural lang., peremne auspicium, and subst. , , , , the auspices taken by magistrates on crossing a river or a spring : peremne dicitur auspicari, qui amnem…

pĕremptālis.opening: adj. peremptus , of or belonging to destruction or abolition , abolishing , cancelling; only in augural lang., fulmina, lightnings that destroy the effect or portent of former lightnings : peremptalia fulgura Gracchus…

pĕremptĭo.opening: ( ), , perimo , a destroying , killing (eccl. Lat.), Aug. Tract. in Joann. 27 fin.

pĕremptor.opening: ( ), , id. , a destroyer , slayer , murderer (postclass.): incluti regis, Sen. Oedip. 221 : mariti mei cruentis, App. M. 8, p. 207, 16 ; cf.: puer ille peremptor meus, i. e. who has playued me almost to death, id. ib. 7…

pĕremptōrĭus.opening: ( ), , adj. id. . Lit. , destructive , deadly , mortal (post-class.): venenum, App. M. 10, p. 243, 30 : spiculum, Tert. Anim. 25 ; Sid. Ep. 8, 11 .— Trop. , qs. that destroys or precludes all debate, i. e. decisive ,…

pĕremptrix.opening: ( ), , peremptor , she that destroys or kills (eccl. Lat.): mors peremptrix sensūs, Tert. Anim. 42 .

pĕrendĭē.opening: adv. Gr. πέραν-dies , on the day after to-morrow (class.): cras agito, perendie agito, Plaut. Merc. 2, 3, 41 ; id. Aul. 2, 1, 34 ; id. Stich. 4, 1, 12 : scies igitur fortasse cras, summum perendie, Cic. Att. 12, 44, 3 ;…

pĕrendĭnātĭo.opening: perendinus , a putting off till the day after to-morrow (post-class.), Mart. Cap. 9, § 897 .

pĕrendĭnus.opening: adj. perendie , after to-morrow (class.): tot homines tam ingeniosos, per tot annos statuere non potuisse, utrum diem tertium, an perendinum dici oporteret, Cic. Mur. 12, 27 : perendino die, Caes. B. G. 5, 30 .— Absol.…

pĕrennis.opening: († , Inscr. Ann. p. Chr. 341 ap. Guattani Monum. Inedit. 1, 5, p. 39), e ( abl. sing. perenne, Ov. H. 8, 64 ; id. F. 3, 654 ), adj. per-annus , that lasts or continues the year through (post-Aug.): aves perennes, that…

pĕrennĭ-servus.opening: perennis , one who is always a slave , Plaut. Pers. 3, 3, 17 .

pĕrennĭtas.opening: id. , lastingness , continuance , perpetual duration , perpetuity (class.): fontium perennitates, Cic. N. D. 2, 39, 98 : cibi, constant food, Plaut. Pers. 3, 1, 2 : perennitatem conditis frumentis afferunt, Col. 1, 6,…

pĕrenno.grammar: āvi, ātum, 1 v. a. and n.
pĕrenno.opening: v. a. and n. id. . Act. , to keep or preserve long (post-Aug.): ea res, etiamsi non in totum perennat, certe usque in alteram vindemiam plerumque vini saporem servat, Col. 12, 20, 8 (dub.; al. perennem); 12, 19, 2.—…

pĕrentĭcīda.opening: , for pericida [pera-caedo], a cutpurse (a word comically formed with allusion to parenticida), Plaut. Ep. 3, 2, 13 .

pĕr-ĕo.opening: (īvi), ĭtum, īre (periet for peribit, Coripp. Johann. 7, 27; perf. perivit, App. M. 4, 21 : perīt, Juv. 8, 85 : perisset, Lact. 3, 20, 17 al. : perisse, Liv. 1, 49, 1 ; Ov. Am. 2, 19, 56 ; fut. periet, Vulg. Sap. 4, 19…

pĕr-ĕquĭto.grammar: āvi, ātum, 1 v. n. and a.
pĕr-ĕquĭto.opening: v. n. and a. , to ride through , ride hither and thither , ride about; to drive about (class. but not in Cic.). Neutr. : inter duas acies perequitans, Caes. B. C. 1, 46 : longe ex viā, Liv. 23, 47 : per omnes partes, to…

pĕr-erro.opening: v. a. , to wander through , to roam or ramble over ( poet. and in post-Aug. prose). Lit. : fallacem circum vespertinumque pererro Saepe forum, Hor. S. 1, 6, 113 : locum, Verg. A. 5, 441 : freta, Ov. H. 14, 103 : saltus…

pĕr-ērŭdītus.opening: adj. , very learned : homo, Cic. Att. 4, 15, 2 .

pĕr-ēvăcŭo.opening: v. a. , to empty quite (late Lat.), Vit. Caes. 1, 4, 39 .

pĕr-excelsus.opening: very high , lofty : Henna, ubi ea gesta esse memorantur, est loco perexcelso, Cic. Verr. 2, 4, 48, § 107 .

pĕr-excrŭcĭo.opening: , a false read. for probe excruciavero, Plaut. Stich. 3, 1, 32 ; v. Ritschl ad h. l.

pĕr-exĕo.opening: v. n. irr. , to go out through , trop., Cassiod. Var. 11, 7 .

pĕr-exĭgŭus.opening: adj. , very small , very little (class.): semen perexiguum, Cic. N. D. 2, 32, 81 : dies, very short, Cic. Verr. 1, 2, 6 : et perminuta bona corporis, id. Tusc. 2, 13, 30 : loci spatium, Caes. B. G. 5, 15 : argentum,…

pĕr-exīlis.opening: adj. , very slender (postAug.): vitis, Col. 11, 2, 60 : perexile bonum est, Boëth. Cons. Phil. 2, pros. 4.

pĕr-exoptātus.opening: adj. , greatly desired , much longed for (post-class.): in tmesi: per, inquit, exoptatus venis, Gell. 18, 4, 2 .

pĕr-expĕdītus.opening: , a false read. for expedita, Cic. Fin. 3, 11, 36 ; v. Madv. ad h. l.

pĕr-explĭcātus.opening: adj. , wholly completed (post-class.): sexto reditu perexplicato, Sid. Carm. 23, 385 .

pĕr-exsiccātus.opening: adj. , quite dried up (eccl. Lat.): proluvies, Arn. 7, 230 .

pĕr-ex-tĭmĕo.grammar: ŭi, 2 timŭi, 3 v. n. v. n.
pĕr-ex-tĭmĕo.opening: v. n. , and † , , v. n. , to fear greatly , Not. Tir. p. 71 .

per-fabrĭco.opening: v. a. , to work or use up; trop., to take in , overreach , cheat (Plautin.): aliquem, Plaut. Pers. 5, 2, 4 .

per-făcētus.opening: adj. , very witty , very facetious (class.).—Of persons, Cic Brut. 27, 105 .—Of words: aliquid perfacetum dicere, Cic. Planc. 14, 35 .— Adv. : , very wittily : perfacete dicta, Cic. Verr. 2, 1, 46, § 121 .

per-făcĭlis.opening: adj. Very easy (class.): perfacilis et expedita defensio, Cic. Fin. 3, 11, 36 Madv. N. cr. : disciplina cognitu perfacilis, id. Tusc. 4, 3, 6 ; id. Leg. 2, 7, 17 : perfacile factu esse conata perficere, Caes. B. G. 1, 3…

per-fācundus.opening: adj. , very eloquent (post-class.): in contionibus perfacundus, Just. 22, 1, 9 ; App. Flor. 4, 18 .

per-fămĭlĭāris.opening: adj. , very intimate , very familiar (class.): perfamiliaris Philisto, Cic. Q. Fr. 2, 11 (13), 4.—In tmesi: Phaedon Socrati per fuit familiaris, Gell. 2, 18, 1 .— Subst. : , , , a very intimate or familiar friend…

per-fătŭus.opening: adj. , very foolish , very silly : togae, Mart. 10, 18, 4 (al. fatuae); Aug. c. Duas Epp. Pelag. 2, 4, 7.

perfectē.opening: adv. , v. perficio, P. a. fin.

perfectĭo.opening: perficio , a finishing , completing , perfecting; perfection (class.): hanc absolutionem perfectionemque in oratore desiderans, Cic. de Or. 1, 28, 130 : perfectio atque absolutio optimi, id. Brut. 36, 137 : ad cumulum…

perfectissĭmātus.opening: perfectus , the rank and station of a perfectissimus under the later emperors (v. , P. a. ), Cod. Th. 8, 4, 3.

perfector.opening: perficio , a finisher , perfecter (rare but class.): mearum voluptatum, Ter. Eun. 5, 8, 4 : dicendi, Cic. de Or. 1, 60, 257 ; Scip. ap. Cic. Att. 8, 11, 1 .

perfectrix.opening: perfector , she that finishes or perfects (very rare): philosophia beatae vitae perfectrix, Nep. ap. Lact. 3, 15, 10 .

perfectus.opening: perficio , a finishing or perfecting; perfection (very rare), Tert. Anim. 20 .— Plur. , effects , Vitr. 10, 3, 1 (in Vitr. 1, 2, 6 , prospectus is the true reading).

perfĕrens.opening: Part. and P. a. , from perfero.

perfĕrentĭa.opening: perfero , a bearing , suffering; endurance (eccl. Lat.): malorum perferentia, Lact. 3, 11, 9 .

per-fĕro.opening: v. a. , to bear or carry through to a certain place or end. Lit. ( poet. and in post-Aug. prose): lapis nec pertulit ictum, did not bring the blow home, did not reach the mark, Verg. A. 12, 907 : hasta perlata sub…

per-fĕrus.opening: adj. , very wild or savage (ante-class.): boves, Varr. R. R. 2, 1, 5 .

per-fervĕfīo.opening: v. n. , to become very hot (ante-class.).—In tmesi: terra sole perferve ita fit, ut, etc., Varr. R. R. 1, 9, 2 dub. (acc. to Gesn. and Schneid. a gloss).

per-fervĕo.opening: v. n. , to be very hot (post-Aug.): perfervet (fons), Mel. 1, 8 .

per-fervĭdus.opening: , a false read. for praefervida, Col. 5, 5 .

per-fĭcĭo.opening: v. a. facio , to achieve , execute , carry out , accomplish , perform , despatch , bring to an end or conclusion , finish , complete (class.; syn.: absolvo, conficio, exsequor). Lit. : comitiis perficiendis undecim dies…

perfĭcus.opening: adj. perficio , completing , perfecting ( poet. ): natura, Lucr. 2, 1116 .— Subst. : , , , the finishing or completing goddess , she that perfects : natura creatrix, Lucr. 2, 1116 .— Of the goddess supposed to preside…

per-fĭdēlis.opening: adj. , very trusty , very faithful : homo, Cic. Att. 2, 19, 5 : perfidelis in amicos, Aur. Vict. Caes. 13, 8 .

per-fīdens.opening: adj. , trusting greatly , confiding strongly (post-class.): pugnandi arte perfidens, Aur. Vict. Caes. 17 .

perfĭdĭa.opening: perfidus , faithlessness , dishonesty , treachery , falsehood , perfidy (class.): perfidiā deceptus, Cic. Rosc. Am. 38, 110 : fraude et perfidiā aliquem fallere, id. ib. 40, 117 ; id. Fam. 1, 2, 3 : admittere perfidiam…

perfĭdĭōsus.opening: adj. perfidia , faithless , dishonest , treacherous , false , perfidious (class.). Of persons: fallax, perfidiosus, Cic. Pis. 27, 66 : perfidiosus et subdolus animo, Tac. A. 16, 32 .— Sup. : omnium perfidiosissimus,…

perfĭdus.opening: adj. per-fides , that breaks his promise , faithless , false , dishonest , treacherous , perfidious. Lit. (class.; syn. infidus): vanum et perfidiosum esse, Cic. Quint. 6, 26 : omnes, aliud agentes, aliud simulantes,…

perfīgo.opening: v. a. , to pierce through , transfix (only in Lucr.): multa perfigit, 6, 350.—Elsewh. only part. perf. , , , transfixed , pierced : telis pavoris, Lucr. 3, 305 : pectus, id. 6, 392 ; cf. id. 2, 360 .

perfingo.opening: v. a. per-fingo , to form , represent : VARIOS AVIVM CANTVS, Inscr. Fabr. p. 685 .

perflābĭlis.opening: adj. perflo . Pass. , that can be blown through. Prop. (rare but class.): deos inducere perlucidos et perflabiles, Cic. Div. 2, 17, 40 : terra, Sol. 27 : lacernae, Amm. 14, 6, 9 : locus, exposed to the wind, airy, App.…

per-flāgĭtĭōsus.opening: adj. , very shameful , very flagitious. —With perturpe, Cic. Cael. 20, 50 (cf. Madv. ad Cic. Fin. p. 410 ).

per-flagrātus.opening: Part. [flagro], blazing greatly (post-class.), Mart. Cap. 6, § 576 Kopp.

perflāmen.opening: perflo , a blowing through , a blast , breath (eccl. Lat.), Prud. Apoth. 760 .

perflātĭlis.opening: adj. id. , that can be blown through , exposed to the wind (postclass.): pator, App. M. 3, p. 137 ; Ambros. Ep. 30, 5 .

perflātĭo.opening: id. , a blowing through , a blast (post-class.), Mart. Cap. 1, § 26 .

perflātus.opening: id. , a blowing through , a draught of air: venti, Vitr. 4, 7, 4 .—Concr., a wind , breeze (post-Aug.): ut perflatus aliquis accedat, Cels. 3, 19 : loca perflatum non habentia, Plin. 18, 17, 44, § 154 : ulmus in…

per-flētus.opening: Part. [fleo], in reflex. sense. having bewailed her case to excess (post-class.): diutius usu perfleta (i. e. quae fleverat ex more), App. M. 2, p. 125 .

per-flo.grammar: āvi, ātum, 1 v. a. and n.
per-flo.opening: v. a. and n. , to blow through or over (not in Cæs.). Act. : cum venti nubila perflant, Lucr. 6, 132 ; cf. id. 6, 136 , and Ov. R. Am. 369 : unde (nubilarium) commodissime perflari possit, Varr. R. R. 1, 13 : venti…

per-fluctŭo.opening: v. a. , to flow through , to swarm over ( poet. ): animantum copia perfluctuat artus, Lucr. 3, 721 .

per-flŭo.opening: v. a. and n. Act. , to flow or run through (post-class.): pluvialibus nimbis perfluuntur, Arn. 6, 191 .— Neutr. Lit. To flow or run through ( poet. and in post-Aug. prose): per colum vina videmus Perfluere, Lucr. 2, 392…

perflŭus.opening: adj. perfluo , flowing , undulating. — Transf. , effeminate , wanton (post-class.): incessus, App. M. 11, p. 260, 36 .

perfōco.opening: v. a. per-fauces , to stifle , suffocate (post-class.): partum, Dig. 25, 3, 4 (al. praefocat).

per-fŏdĭo.opening: (perfodīvi, Plaut. Mil. 2, 1, 64 Ritschl N. cr. ), , v. a. To dig through , to pierce through , transfix (class.): parietes, Plaut. As. 3, 2, 17 : parietem, id. l. l.; Cic. Vatin. 5, 11 ; Vulg. Matt. 24, 43 : montem,…

perfoedĕrātus.opening: Part. [perfoedero], strongly leagued together , Not. Tir. p. 71 .

perfŏrācŭlum.opening: perforo , a borer , an auger or gimlet (post-class.), Arn. 6, 200 ; cf. perforaculum, τρύπανον, τέρετρον , Gloss. Philox.

per-formīdo.opening: , no perf. , , v. a. , to fear greatly , Not. Tir. p. 71 .

per-formīdŏlōsus.opening: adj. , very fearful (post-class.), Aur. Vict. Caes. 4 .

per-formo.opening: v. a. , to form thoroughly , to form (eccl. Lat.): ad malum performantur (al. praeformantur), Tert. Apol. 1 .

per-fŏro.opening: (in tmesi: perque forare, Lucr. 5, 126, 8 ), v. a. , to bore through , pierce through , perforate. Lit. (class.; syn. terebro): navem, Cic. ap. Quint. 8, 6, 47 : perforare ac demergere triremem, Auct. B. Alex. 25:…

per-fortĭter.opening: adv. , very bravely ( poet. ), Ter. Ad. 4, 2, 28 .

perfossĭo.opening: perfodio , a digging through , perforation : perfossio, διορυγή, διορυγμός , Gloss. Philox.

perfosso.opening: v. a. id. , to dig through : perfosso, διορύσσω , Gloss. Gr. Lat.

perfossor.opening: id. , a digger through , breaker through (ante- and post-class.): perfossor parietum, a house-breaker, Plaut. Ps. 4, 2, 23 ; App. Mag. p. 295, 16 .

perfossūra.opening: id. , a digging through : perfossura, διορυγή , Gloss. Gr. Lat.

per-fŏvĕo.opening: v. a. , to warm through (post-class.): perfovet aegros, Sedul. 4, 25 ; cf. Not. Tir. p. 134 .

per-fragrans.opening: adj. , very fragrant (late Lat.), Fulg. Serm. 27 .

per-frĕmo.opening: v. n. , to roar or snort along (ante-class.): perfremunt delphini, Att. ap. Cic. N. D. 2, 35, 89 .

per-frĕquens.opening: adj. , very crowded , much frequented : emporium, Liv. 41, 1 .

perfrĕto.opening: v. n. per-fretum , to sail over (post-class.), Sol. 27 .

per-frĭco.grammar: cui, cātum, and ctum, āre v. a.
per-frĭco.opening: v. a. Lit. , to rub all over , to rub or scratch (class.): caput unguento, Cic. Verr. 2, 3, 25, § 62 : totam faciem fuligine, Petr. 22 ; Cels. 3, 14 : totum corpus, id. 1, 3 ; Plin. 28, 12, 51, § 190 : perfrictis…

perfrictĭo.opening: perfrico , a rubbing , abrasion (post-Aug.), Veg. 1, 35, 1 ; 1, 38, 3 .— Plur. : perfrictionibus cum oleo mederi, Plin. 21, 18, 69, § 116 (but perh. the same word as the preced. in the same meaning).

perfrictĭuncŭla.opening: dim. 1. perfrictio , a slight cold , M. Aur. ap. Front. Ep. ad M. Caes. 4, 6 .

perfrīgĕfăcĭo.opening: v. a. per-frigefacto , to make very cold , to benumb : mihi perfrigefacit cor Surus, strikes a chill to my heart, makes me shudder with fear, Plaut. Ps. 4, 7, 117 .

per-frīgĕo.opening: v. n. , to take cold : perfrigeo, καταψύχω , Gloss. Philox.

per-frīgĕro.opening: , no perf. , , v. a. , to make cold , to cool off , to let grow cold (postclass.), Scrib. Comp. 271 ; Not. Tir. p. 113 .

per-frīgesco.opening: v. inch. n. Lit. , to grow very cold , to catch cold : ne canes perfrigescant, Varr. R. R. 2, 9, 13 ; Plin. 31, 6, 33, § 66 : ei, qui perfrixit, opus est in laconico sedere, donec insudet, Cels. 1, 3 : si perfrixit,…

per-frīgĭdus.opening: adj. , very cold : tempestas, Cic. Verr. 2, 4, 40, § 86 : vinum, Cels. 1, 3 ; 4, 5 .

perfringo.opening: v. a. perfrango , to break through , to break or dash in pieces , to shiver , shatter (class.). Lit. In gen.: elephanto pugno perfregisti bracchium, Plaut. Mil. 1, 1, 26 : jumenta ingredientia nivem ... jactandis…

per-frĭo.opening: v. a. , to rub to pieces , to crumble up (post-Aug.): bacas myrti, Col. 12, 38, 5 .

per-frīvŏlus.opening: adj. , very worthless , very frivolous (post-class.), Vop. Aur. 6 .

per-fructĭo.opening: or , , perfruor , complete enjoyment or fruition (eccl. Lat.): perfructio summi et veri boni, Aug. Quant. Anim. 33 : sine perfruitione, id. Trin. 6, 10 .

per-frŭor.opening: v. dep. Lit. , to enjoy fully or thoroughly (class.). With abl. : his ego rebus pascor, his delector, his perfruor, Cic. Pis. 20, 45 : laetitiā, id. Cat. 1, 10, 25 : salvā re publicā, id. ib. 4, 6, 4 : sapientiae laude,…

perfŭga.opening: perfugio , a deserter to the enemy (class.): perfugam Gallus Aelius ait, qui liber aut servus aut hostis suā voluntate ad hostes transierit: qui idem dicitur transfuga. Quamquam sunt, qui credant, perfugam esse, non tam…

per-fŭgĭo.opening: v. n. , to flee to a place for refuge. Lit. In gen. (rare; ap. Cic. Pis. 36, 89 , profugisti is the correct reading.; cf. confugio): ad aliquem, Liv. 2, 9 : Corinthum, Nep. Dion. 5, 1 : Bactra, Curt. 6, 6, 22 : ad…

perfŭgĭum.opening: perfugio , a place to flee to , a shelter , asylum , refuge (class.): perfugi sibi copiam comparare, Plaut. Cas. 3, 5, 2 : si unum ostium obsideatur, aliud perfugium petat, id. Truc. 4, 4, 17 Bothe: pedibus perfugium…

per-fulcĭo.opening: v. a. , to prop up , to sustain , support (post-class.): eloquio perfulcire senatum (al. permulcire), Auct. Pan. ad Pis. 86: perfulsit, Not. Tir. p. 117 .

per-fulgĕrat.opening: ( ), impers. , it flashes or gleams brightly , Not. Tir. p. 118 .

perfunctĭo.opening: perfungor , a performing , discharging of an office (class.): honorum, Cic. de Or. 3, 2, 7 : laborum, an undergoing , enduring (along with perpessio dolorum), id. Fin. 1, 15, 49 .—Of things: annua fertur ei totius…

perfunctōrĭus.opening: adj. perfunctus; despatched, i. e. , done in a careless or superficial manner , slight , careless , negligent , perfunctory (jurid. Lat.): examinatio, Nov. Val. 3 , Postul. 2, 11, c. l. § 1: genitus, Ambros. in Psa. 37,…

per-fundo.opening: v. a. , to pour over , to wet , moisten , bedew , besprinkle (class.; syn.: umecto, aspergo, imbuo). Lit. : aquā ferventi Philodamus perfunditur, Cic. Verr. 2, 1, 26, § 67 : fluviis pecus, Verg. G. 3, 445 : greges…

per-fungor.opening: v. dep. n. Lit. , to fulfil , perform , discharge (class.). With abl. : munere quodam necessitatis, et gravi opere perfungimur, Cic. Sen. 21, 77 : honoribus amplissimis et laboribus maximis, id. Fam. 1, 8, 3 : rei…

per-fŭro.opening: v. a. and n. , to rage through , run furiously through ( poet. ) Act. : Eoas domos, Stat. Th. 4, 388 .— Neutr. , to rage furiously , to rage on : incensus et ipse Perfurit, Verg. A. 9, 343 : ita perfurit acri Cum…

perfūsē.opening: adv. perfundo , profusely : perfuse atque abunde sparsa vasa, Sisenn. ap. Non. 516, 31 (al. profuse).

per-fūsĭo.opening: id. . In gen., a pouring over or upon , a wetting , moistening (post-Aug.). perfusio corporis ex aquā calidā, Cels. 4, 8 ; Plin. 18, 7, 14, § 74 .—In plur. : alarum perfusiones, Plin. 23, 9, 82, § 164 .— Esp., baptism ,…

perfūsor.opening: id. , one who pours water over another , a bath-servant , who poured water over the bathers (cf. Cels. 6, 24 ; Suet. Aug. 82 ), Inscr. Pompei. ap. Bullet. Napolit. II. 1843, p. 3, and v. Avellino, ib. p. 67 ; cf.:…

perfūsōrĭus.opening: adj. perfundo , merely wetting or moistening; hence, Slight , superficial (post-Aug.): tenuis et perfusoria voluptas, Sen. Ep. 23, 4 .— Disturbing , wrongful (post-Aug.): assertio, Suet. Dom. 8 .— Adv. : , slightly ,…

Pergăma.opening: , or ( ), , , = Πέργαμα or Πέργαμον , the citadel of Troy , poet. for Troy : Pergama, Liv. Andron. ap. Non. 512, 32 (Trag. Rel. v. 2 Rib.); Enn. ap. Macr. S. 6, 2 (Trag. v. 98 Vahl.); Lucr. 1, 476 ; Verg. A. 1, 651 ; 2,…

Pergămĕus.opening: , v. Pergama, II., and 2. Pergamum, B.

Pergămis.opening: a city in Epirus , Varr. R. R. 2, 2 .

Pergămum.opening: a city in Creta , founded by Agamemnon (or acc. to Verg. A. 3, 133 , by Æneas), Vell. 1, 1, 2 .

per-gaudĕo.opening: v. n. , to rejoice greatly : Trebonium meum a te amari pergaudeo, Cic. Q. Fr. 3, 1, 3, § 9 .

per-gĕnĭtus.opening: adj. , engendered , produced (late Lat.), Pelag. Vet. 11.

per-glisco.opening: v. n. , to become quite fat (post-Aug.): gallina pergliscit, Col. 8, 7, 4 .

per-gnārus.opening: adj. , that has a thorough knowledge of , that is very experienced , well versed in any thing (very rare): locorum pergnari, Sall. Fragm. ap. Non. 554, 21 : colendi, App. Mag. p. 290, 34 .

pergo.grammar: perrexi, perrectum, 3 v. a. and n.
pergo.opening: v. a. and n. per-rego . Act. In gen., to go on , continue , proceed with any thing (esp. a motion), to pursue with energy , prosecute vigorously (v. Mütz. ad Curt. 3, 8, 7 ; rare, and in Cic. only with an obj.-clause ).…

per-graecor.opening: v. dep. n. , to live just like the Greeks , to play the Greek , i. e. to revel , carouse (ante-class.): ut cum solo pergraecetur milite, Plaut. Truc. 1, 1, 69 ; id. Most. 1, 1, 21 ; 64 : pergraecari est epulis et…

per-grandesco.opening: v. inch. n. , to grow very large (ante-class.), Att. ap. Non. 115, 9 .

per-grandis.opening: adj. , very large , very great (rare but class.): gemma, Cic. Verr. 2, 4, 27, § 62 : vectigal, id. Agr. 1, 4, 9 : lucrum, Plaut. Pers. 4, 3, 23 : pergrandis natu, very old, very aged, Liv. 29, 29, 6 : lapis, Vulg.…

per-grăphĭcus.opening: adj. , very skilful , very artful (ante-class.): sycophanta, Plaut. Trin. 5, 2, 15 .

per-grātus.opening: adj. , very agreeable , very pleasant (class.): litterae, Cic. Q. Fr. 3, 1, 6, § 23 : id mihi pergratum perque jucundum erit, id. ib. 3, 1, 4 , § 12; id. Att. 10, 4, 1 : pergratum mihi feceris, si, you would do me a…

per-grăvis.opening: adj. , very weighty or grave , very important (class.): pergravia (haec), opp. levia, Ter. Hec. 3, 1, 12 : testes, Cic. Cael. 26, 63 : oratio, id. Sest. 50, 107 .— Adv. : , very gravely , very seriously (class.):…

pergŭla.opening: pergo; cf. tegula, from tego . A projection or shed in front of a house, used as a booth , stall , shop; of an exchanger , Plin. 21, 3, 6, § 8 ; of a paintingroom , studio , Plin. 35, 10, 36, § 84 ; Lucil. ap. Lact. 1,…

pergŭlāna.opening: pergula , a vine trained over an arbor , Col. 3, 2, 28 .

Pergus.opening: a lake in Sicily , near the city of Enna , where Pluto is said to have carried off Proserpine , the mod. Lago Pergusa , Ov. M. 5, 386 ; Claud. Rapt. Pros. 2, 112 .

per-gustus.opening: taste (late Lat.): severi, Epist. Jud. Minor. Conv. p. 830, t. 41 Migne.

pĕr-haurĭo.opening: v. a. Lit. , to drain completely , to drink up : calicem uno haustu, App. M. 10, p. 246, 39 ; Tert. ad Nat. 1, 15 .— Trop. : auribus perhauriendum'st, Plaut. Mil. 1, 1, 34 .

pĕr-hĭbĕo.opening: v. a. habeo , to hold out , extend , present , produce , bestow , grant , give , afford; to attribute , ascribe , assign , etc. In gen. (mostly ante-class. and post-Aug.; cf.: edo, exhibeo): operam rei publicae fortem…

pĕr-hĭĕmo.opening: ( ), , v. n. , to winter , pass the winter; to lie or remain all winter (post-Aug.), Col. 11, 3 .

pĕr-hŏnōrĭfĭcus.opening: adj. That does one much honor , very honorable : con salutatio forensis perhonorifica, Cic. Att. 2 . 18, 1: discessus, id. Prov. Cons. 19, 45 .— That shows much honor to another , very respectful : collega in me…

pĕr-horrĕo.opening: v. a. , to tremble or shudder greatly at , to have a great horror of any thing (post-class.): horum tela perhorrebimus, Jul. Val. Rer. Gest. Alex. M. 2, 9 Mai.

pĕr-horresco.opening: v. inch. n. and a. Neutr. , to tremble or shudder greatly (class.): toto corpore perhorresco, Cic. Div. in Caecil. 13, 41 : recordatione consulatūs vestri, id. Pis. 20, 45 : clamore perhorruit Aetne, trembled, shook,…

pĕr-horrĭdus.opening: adj. , very dreadful or frightful , most horrid : stagna perhorrida situ, Liv. 22, 16, 4 .

pĕr-hūmānus.opening: adj. , very kind , very courteous , very polite (class.): sermo, Cic. Q. Fr. 2, 6, 1 : epistula, id. Att. 16, 12 . — Adv. : , very kindly , very politely : scribere ad aliquem, Cic. Fam. 7, 8, 1 .

Pĕrĭălŏgos.opening: , = περιάλογος , The Very Unreasonable (sc. father), the title of a work by Orbilius , Suet. Gram. 9 dub.

pĕrĭambus.opening: A metrical foot , consisting of two short syllaoles ; usually called a pyrrhichius, Quint. 9, 4, 80 .

Pĕrĭander.opening: , = Περίανδρος , son of Cypselus , a king of Corinth , and one of the seven wise men of Greece , Gell. 16, 19, 4 ; Aus. Lud. Sept. Sapient. fin. ; Hyg. Fab. 221 .

pĕrĭbŏētos.opening: and , = περιβόητος , cried up , i. e. celebrated , famous (post-Aug.), Plin. 34, 8, 19, § 69 .

pĕrĭbŏlus.opening: , = περίβολος , the circuit , enclosure : exterior, Vulg. Ezech. 42, 7 : sanctorum, id. 1 . Macc. 14, 48.

Pĕrĭbōmĭus.opening: the name of a shameless person , Juv. 2, 16 .

pĕrĭcarpum.opening: , = περίκαρπον , a kind of bulbous plant , Plin. 25, 10, 82, § 131 .

pĕrichristārĭon.opening: , = περίχριστος , a kind of eye-salve , Marc. Emp. 8 .

pĕrĭchўtē.opening: , = περιχυτή , a kind of gladiatorial combat , an enclosing , enveloping (post-class.), Cod. Just. 3, 43, 3 .

Pĕrī^cles.opening: , = Περικλῆς , a famous Athenian orator and statesman , Cic. Rep. 1, 16, 25 ; id. Brut. 15, 59 ; id. de Or. 3, 34, 137 et saep.; voc. Pericle, id. Off. 1, 40, 144 .

pĕrīclĭtābundus.opening: adj. periclitor , trying , testing , making a trial or essay (post-class.). With acc. : puncto pollicis extremam aciem (sagittae) periclitabunda, App. M. 5, p. 168, 34 : voluntatem, id. Mag. p. 308, 18 .— With gen. :…

pĕrīclĭtātĭo.opening: id. , a trying , a trial , experiment : aliquid usu et periclitatione percipere, Cic. N. D. 2, 64, 161 .

pĕrīclĭtor.opening: (periclitatus, in pass. signif.; v. infra fin. ), v. dep. a. and periculum . Act. In gen., to try , prove , test any thing, to make a trial of , put to the test (class.; syn.: experior, tento): periclitatus animum sum…

pĕrī^clўmĕnos.opening: or , , , = περικλύμενος , a climbing plant , the woodbine or honeysuckle , also called clymenus, Plin. 27, 12, 94, § 120 .

Pĕrī^clўmĕnus.opening: , = Περικλύμενος , son of Neleus and brother of Nestor , one of the Argonauts , who had received from Neptune the power of changing his shape at pleasure , Ov. M. 12, 556 .

pĕrĭcŏpē.opening: , = περικοπή , a section of a book, etc. (eccl. Lat.), Hier. in Joel, 2,

pĕrīcŭlor.opening: v. dep. periculum , i. q. periclitor, Cato ap. Fest. p. 242 Müll.

pĕrīcŭlōsus.opening: adj. periculum , dangerous , hazardous , perilous (class.): in nosmetipsos periculosi, incurring danger, endangering ourselves, Cic. Att. 13, 27, 1 : consuetudo, id. Ac. 2, 21, 68 : periculosum et grave bellum, id. Imp.…

pĕrīcŭlum.opening: (contr. , very freq. in the poets, e. g. Plaut. Bacch. 4, 7, 29 ; Ter. And. 2, 2, 13 ; 5, 1, 2 ; 5, 2, 26 al. ; Lucr. 1, 580 ; 2, 5 et saep.; Verg. A. 2, 709 ; 751 ; 3, 711 et saep.; Juv. 6, 94 ), , root, Sanscr. par,…

pĕr-ĭdōnĕus.opening: adj. , very fit , suitable , or proper , very well adapted to any thing (class.). With dat. : locus peridoneus castris, Caes. B. C. 2 . 24: visus est peridoneus praeceptor, maxime ad poëticam tendentibus, Suet. Gram. 11…

Pĕrĭēgēsis.opening: , = Περιήγησις , a leading round to exhibit whatever is worth notice; hence, a geographical description. This term is used as the title of a poem by Avienus. —Hence, , , , the writer of travels : Metrodorus, Lact. ad…

pĕrĭleucos.opening: , = περίλευκος (white all round), a precious stone , otherwise unknown, Plin. 37, 10, 66, § 180 .

Pĕrilla.opening: a female proper name , Ov. Tr. 3, 7, 1 ; 2, 437 ; App. Mag. p. 279, 26 .

Pĕrillus.opening: , = Πέριλλος , a famous Athenian worker in metal , who made a brazen bull for the tyrant Phalaris , in which criminals were to be enclosed and roasted to death , and was the first that suffered in this manner , Ov. A.…

pĕr-illustris.opening: adj. Very brilliant , very notable : quod sub ipsā proscriptione perillustre fuit, Nep. Att. 12, 3 .— Greatly distinguished , highly honored , Cic. Att. 5, 20, 1 .

pĕrĭmăchĭa.opening: , = περιμαχία , an attack , hostile assault (post-class.), Sid. Ep. 1, 7 .

pĕr-imbĕcillus.opening: adj. , very weak or feeble : collum anserum, Varr. R. R. 3, 10, 5 : quod quidem est natum perimbecillum est, Cic. Att. 10, 18, 1 : verbum, Sulp. Sev. Chron. 2, 17, 3 .

Pĕrĭmēdēus.opening: adj. , of or belonging to the sorceress Perimede , Perimedean , magical ( poet. ): gramina, Prop. 2, 4, 8 (18).

Pĕrĭmēlē.opening: a nymph , daughter of Hippodamas , who was changed into the island of the same name , Ov. M. 8, 590 .

pĕrĭmĕtros.opening: , = περίμετρος , a circumference , perimeter , Front. Aquaed. 26 ; 40 ; Vitr. 5, 6 .

pĕrĭmo.opening: (orig. form , Cato ap. Fest. p. 217 Müll.), ēmi, emptum (emtum), , v. a. per-emo , to take away entirely , to annihilate , extinguish , destroy; to cut off , hinder , prevent. In gen. (class.; syn.: perdo, deleo):…

pĕr-impĕdītus.opening: adj. , very much obstructed , very difficult to pass : locus, Auct. B. Afr. 58.

pĕrĭnaeon.opening: and , , , = περιναιον, περινεον , the space between the sexual parts and the fundament , the perineum (post-class.), Cael. Aur. Tard. 5, 4, 66 ; 68 ; 5, 3, 59 .

pĕr-incertus.opening: adj. , very uncertain , Sall. Fragm. ap. Gell. 18, 4, 4 .

pĕr-incommŏdus.opening: adj. , very inconvenient , very troublesome or annoying : alicui, Liv. 37, 41, 3 .— Adv. : , very inconveniently , very unfortunately : accidit perincommode, quod, etc., Cic. Att. 1, 17, 2 .

pĕr-inconsĕquens.opening: adj. , very inconsequent , very absurd (post-class.): per tmesin, Gell. 14, 1, 10 .

pĕr-inde.opening: adv. , a particle of comparison. in the same manner , just as , quite as , equally; in like manner , just so (class.; cf. proinde, with which it is frequently confounded in MSS. and edd.). In gen.: vivendi artem tantam…

pĕr-indĭgĕo.opening: v. n. , to need very much , to be in great need (eccl. Lat.), Tert. adv. Gnost. 13 .

pĕr-indignus.opening: adj. , very unworthy , very unbecoming , Sid. Ep. 4, 4 .— Adv. : , very indignantly (post-Aug.): tulit perindigne actum a senatu, ut, etc., Suet. Tib. 50 .

pĕr-indulgens.opening: adj. , very indulgent , very tender : qui perindulgens in patrem, idem acerbe severus in fratrem, Cic. Off. 3, 31, 112 .

pĕr-infāmis.opening: adj. , very infamous (post-Aug.): vir amore libertinae perinfamis, Suet. Vit. 2 .—With gen. denoting on what account, App. M. 3, p. 136, 26 .

pĕr-infirmus.opening: adj. , very weak or feeble : si quis perinfirmus est, Cels. 2, 14 : sunt enim levia et perinfirma, quae dicebantur a te, Cic. Fin. 2, 16, 53 ; Cels. 2, 14 fin.

pĕr-ingĕnĭōsus.opening: adj. , of good natural abilities , very clever : homines, Cic. Brut. 24, 92 .

pĕr-ĭnīquus.opening: adj. Very unfair , very unjust : quare videant, ne sit periniquum et non ferendum, Cic. Imp. Pomp. 22, 63 .— Very unwilling , very discontented : etsi periniquo patiebar animo, te a me digredi, Cic. Fam. 12, 18, 1 .

pĕr-injūrĭus.opening: adj. , very unjust , very wrong (ante-class.), Cato ap. Prisc. p. 694 P.—With subject-clause , Min. Fel. 15, 1 .

pĕr-insignis.opening: adj. , very remarkable , very conspicuous : corporis pravitates, Cic. Leg. 1, 19, 51 .

pĕr-insŏlens.opening: adj. , very unusual , Not. Tir. p. 47 .

pĕr-intĕger.opening: adj. , very honest , very virtuous (post-class.), Gell. 3, 5, 1 .

Pĕrinthus.opening: ( ), , , = Πέρινθος , a city of Thrace , afterwards called Heraclea, the modern Erekli , Mel. 2, 2, 6 ; Plin. 4, 11, 18, § 47 ; Liv. 33, 30 .—Hence, , , adj. , Perinthian ( poet. ): Menander fecit Andriam, et…

pĕr-ĭnundo.opening: v. a. , to overflow or inundate completely ( poet. ), Alcim. 1, 267 .

pĕr-ĭnungo.opening: v. a. , to anoint all over (ante-class.): tonsas recentes eodem die perinungunt vino et oleo (al. perungunt), Varr. R. R. 2, 11, 7 .

pĕr-invīsus.opening: Part. [invideo], much hated , very odious : homo dis ac nobilitati perinvisus, Cic. Cornel. Fragm. fin. ; Sulp. Sev. Chron. 1, 32, 3 .

pĕr-invītus.opening: adj. , very unwilling : ne perinvitus legerem tuas litteras, Cic. Fam. 7, 33, 2 (dub.); Liv. 40, 57, 3 .

Pĕrĭŏcha.opening: , = Περιοχή , a summary , compendium , the title in the MSS. of the epitomes of the books of Livy; the title of a work by Ausonius.

pĕrĭŏdeuta.opening: , = περιοδευτής , one that goes about , a visitor , Cod. Just. 1, 3, 42 .

pĕrĭŏdĭcus.opening: adj. , = περιοδικός , that returns at stated times , periodical (post-Aug.), Plin. 20, 3, 8, § 15 : typi, Cael. Aur. Acut. 1, 14, 110 .

pĕrĭŏdus.opening: ( , Fest. p. 217 Müll.), , , = περίοδος . A complete sentence , a period : in toto circuitu illo orationis, quem Graeci περίοδον , nos tum ambitum, tum circuitum, tum comprehensionem, aut continuationem, aut…

pĕrĭostĕon.opening: , = περιόστεον , the membrane which surrounds the bone , Cael. Aur. Tard. 5, 1, 5 .

Pĕrĭpătētĭcus.opening: adj. , = Περιπατητικός , of or belonging to the Peripatetic ( Aristotelian ) philosophy , Peripatetic : peripatetica secta, Col. 9, 3, 1 : philosophia, Gell. 1, 3, 10 : disciplina, id. 19, 5, 2 .—As subst. : , , , a…

pĕrĭpĕtasmăta.opening: , = περιπετάσματα , coverings , curtains , hangings , carpets (class.; syn.: aulaeum, stragulum, tapes): Attalica peripetasmata, Cic. Verr. 2, 4, 12, § 27 : de peripetasmatis, id. ib. 2, 4, 12 , § 28.

Pĕrĭphas.opening: , = Περίφας . A king of Attica , Ov. M. 7, 400 .— One of the companions of Pyrrhus , Verg. A. 2, 476 . — One of the Lapithœ , Ov. M. 12, 449 .

pĕrĭphĕrēs.opening: , = περιφερής , moving around , surrounding (pure Lat. circumstans), Mart. Cap. 9, § 958 .

pĕrĭphĕrīa.opening: , = περιφέρεια , a circumference , periphery (post-class.), Mart. Cap. 8, § 827 (pure Lat.: linea circumcurrens).

Pĕrĭphŏrētus.opening: , = περιφόρητος (carried about), an epithet of Artemon (who caused himself to be carried about in a litter), Plin. 34, 8, 19, § 56 .

pĕriphrăsis.opening: , = περίφρασις , a circumlocution , periphrase (post-Aug.), Suet. Gram. 4 ; Quint. 8, 3, 53 ; Gell. 3, 1, 6 (pure Lat.: circuitus eloquendi, ambitus verborum, circumlocutio).

pĕrĭplus.opening: , = περίπλους , a sailing round , circumnavigation , Plin. 7, 48, 48, § 155 .

pĕrĭpneumŏnĭa.opening: , = περιπνευμονία , pulmonary consumption , peripneumonia , Cael. Aur. Acut. 2, 25, 140 ; 2, 26, 142 ; 2, 27, 143 ; id. Tard. 3, 1, 4 .—Hence, (in a later corrupt form, , Veg. Vet. 1, 28 ; and , Theod. Prisc. 2, 4 ), ,…

pĕripsēma.opening: , = περίψημα , that which comes off a thing in cleaning it, offscouring , refuse , filth (post-class.), Tert. Pudic. 14 ; Vulg. 1 Cor. 4, 13 .

pĕriptĕros.opening: adj. , = περίπτερος , surrounded with a row of columns on the outside : aedes, Vitr. 3, 1 ; 4, 7 .

pĕr-īrātus.opening: adj. , very angry : alicui, Plaut. Truc. 3, 1, 11 ; Cic. Fam. 9, 6, 3 .

pĕriscĕlis.opening: , = περισκελίς , a leg-band , anklet , worn by females: saepe periscelidem raptam sibi flentis, Hor. Ep. 1, 17, 56 ; v. Orell. ad h. l.; cf. Isid. Orig. 19, 31, 19 ; Hier. Ep. 64, 10 : tortae, Petr. 67, 4 ; Vulg. Num.…

pĕriscĕlĭum.opening: , = περισκέλιον , i. q. periscelis, an anklet , Tert. Cult. Fem. 13 .

pĕrissŏchŏrēgĭa.opening: , = περισσοχορηγία , a present over and above , an extra present , Cod. Th. 14, 26, 2.

pĕrissŏlŏgĭa.opening: , = περισσολογία , redundancy of expression , Serv. Verg. A. 1, 658 ; cf. Quint. 8, 6, 6 .

pĕrisson.opening: , = περισσόν , the name of a plant , also called dorycnion, Plin. 21, 31, 105, § 179 ; App. Herb. 74 .

pĕristĕrĕon.opening: , and , , , = περιστερεών , vervain , peristereon , Plin. 25, 10, 78, § 126 ; 25, 9, 59, § 105 ; App. Herb. 3 ; Cael. Aur. Acut. 3, 17, 160 .

pĕristrōma.opening: , = περίστρωμα , a covering , curtain , carpet : Babylonia peristromata, Plaut. Stich. 2, 2, 54 ; id. Ps. 1, 2, 12 : conchyliata peristromata, Cic. Phil. 2, 27, 67 .

pĕristrŏphē.opening: , = περιστροφή , a turning about , the turning of an opponent's argument against himself (postclass.), Mart. Cap. 5, § 563 .

pĕristȳlĭum.opening: , = περιστύλιον , a place surrounded with columns on the inside , a peristyle , Vitr. 3, 1 ; 5, 11 ; Plin. Ep. 10, 70, 3 ; 10, 71, 1 ; Suet. Aug. 82 ; cf. peristylum.

pĕristȳlum.opening: , = περίστυλον , the part of a building enclosing the court-yard , surrounded by columns on the inside , Varr. R. R. 3, 5 ; Cic. Dom. 44, 116 ; Suet. Aug. 82 ; Aus. Urb. 5 .

pĕrītĭa.opening: peritus , experience , knowledge gained by experience , practical knowledge , skill (not in Cic. or Cæs.). With gen. obj. : locorum et militiae, Sall. J. 46, 8 : legum, Tac. A. 4, 58 : morum, id. ib. 1, 69 : futurorum,…

pĕrĭto.opening: , a false read. for perit and perlit, Plaut. Capt. 3, 5, 32 ; Lucr. 3, 710 .

pĕrĭtŏnaeos.opening: adj. , = περιτόναιος , of or belonging to the peritoneum , peritoneal : membrana, Cael. Aur. Tard. 3, 4, 57 ; 4, 7, 93 .

pĕrĭtŏnaeum.opening: and , , , = περιτόναιον and περιτόνειον , the membrane enclosing the intestines contained in the abdomen , the peritoneum , Cael. Aur. Acut. 3, 17 (in Cels. 4, 1 , and 7, 4, written as Greek).

pĕrītus.opening: adj. prop. Part. of perior (in ex-perior); root par-, per-; Gr. περάω; v. periculum , experienced , practised , practically acquainted , skilled , skilful , expert (cf.: gnarus, consultus). Lit. Absol. : nil iam mihi…

pĕrixўŏmĕnos.opening: adj. , = περιξυόμενος , scraping himself (in the bath), the name of a statue by Antigonus, Plin. 34, 8, 19, § 26 .

pĕrizōma.opening: , = περίζωμα , a girdle , Isid. Orig. 19, 22 ; Vulg. Gen. 3, 7 .

perjĕrātĭuncula.opening: dim. perjero , a petty perjury : parasiticae, Plaut. Stich. 1, 3, 76 .

per-jūcundus.opening: adj. , very agreeable , very pleasing : cui quidem litterae tuae perjucundae fuerunt, Cic. Fam. 1, 7, 3: disputatio, id. de Or. 2, 7, 26 .—In tmesi: id mihi pergratum perque jucundum erit, Cic. Q. Fr. 3, 1, 4 ; so,…

perjūrĭōsus.opening: adj. perjurium , full of perjury , perjured , perfidious , Plaut. Truc. 1, 2, 52 .

perjūrĭum.opening: perjurus , a false oath , perjury. Lit. (class.): perjuri caput, Plaut. Ps. 1, 1, 129 : fons viti et perjuri, id. Truc. 2, 7, 50 : quod ex animi tui sententiā juraris, id non facere perjurium est, Cic. Off. 3, 29, 108 :…

perjūrus.opening: adj. per-jus . Lit. , who breaks his oath , perjured (class.): quid inter perjurum et mendacem? Cic. Rosc. Com. 16, 46 : perjurissimus leno, id. ib. 7, 20 : perjura Troja, Verg. A. 5, 811 : perjuri arte Sinonis, id. ib.…

per-lābor.opening: ( inf. pres. perlabier, Lucr. 5, 766 ), v. dep. n. , to slip or glide through (mostly poet. ; perh. Cic. Tusc. 1, 12, 28 , is also a poet. reminiscence): isque (aër) ita per nostras acies perlabitur omnes, Lucr. 4, 248…

per-laetus.opening: adj. , very joyful or glad , full of joy : supplicatio, Liv. 10, 21 .

per-lātē.opening: adv. , very widely , very extensively : perlate patere, Cic. de Or. 2, 4, 17 .

per-lătĕo.opening: v. n. , to lie completely hid , lie hid always , Ov. A. A. 3, 416 .

perlātĭo.opening: perfero . A bearing away , a conveying , transferring (postclass.), Hyg. Astron. 1 praef. — A bearing , enduring (post-class.): malorum perlatio, Lact. 5, 22, 3 .

perlātor.opening: id. , a bearer , carrier , conveyer (post-class.): litterarum, Symm. Ep. 5, 28 : perlatore capto, Amm. 21, 16, 11 ; August. Ep. 146 et saep.

perlātrix.opening: perlator , she that bears or carries : perlatrices querelarum litterae, Ennod. Ep. 1, 22 .

per-laudābĭlis.opening: adj. , very commendable : forma, Dict. Cret. 6, 14 .

per-lăvo.opening: v. a. , to wash or bathe thoroughly (post-class.): aliquem, Tert. Poen. 4 ; Pelag. Vet. 26.

perlaxo.opening: v. a. , to relax greatly , Apic. 7, 7 .

perlĕcē^bra.opening: ( ), , pellicio , an enticement , allurement (Plautin.): probri perlecebrae, Plaut. Bacch. 5, 2, 47 (ap. Ritschl as one word, probriperlecebrae): pellecebrae, id. As. 1, 2, 7 .
