pērōnātus.opening: adj. 1. pero , having on boots of untanned leather , rough-booted : arator, Pers. 5, 102 .

pĕr-opportūnus.opening: adj. , very seasonable , very convenient or opportune : diversorium, Cic. de Or. 2, 57, 234 : victoria, Cic. Fam. 6, 6, 6 ; Liv. 10, 45, 2 .— Adv. : , very seasonably , very opportunety : venire, Cic. N. D. 1, 6, 15 :…

pĕr-optātō.opening: adv. optatus , very much to one's wish : peroptato nobis datum est, Cic. de Or. 2, 5, 20 .

pĕr-ŏpus.opening: adv. , very necessary : peropus est, hunc cum ipsā colloqui, Ter. And. 1, 5, 30 .

pĕr-ōrātĭo.opening: peroro , the finishing part , the close or winding up of a speech , the peroration : exstat ejus peroratio, qui epilogus dicitur, Cic. Brut. 33, 127 : jubent exordiri ... deinde rem narrare ... post autem dividere…

pĕrōrīga.opening: , a false read. for per origam, i. e. aurigam, Varr. R. R. 2, 7, 8 ; 2, 8, 4 ; v. Schneid. ad Varr. R. R. 2, 7, 8.

pĕr-ornātus.opening: adj. , very ornate : Crassus in dicendo perornatus, Cic. Brut. 43, 158 .

pĕr-orno.opening: v. a. , to adorn greatly or constantly : senatum, Tac. A. 16, 26 .

pĕr-ōro.opening: v. a. , to speak from beginning to end , to plead or argue throughout , to harangue at length (class.). Prop.: QVOM PERORANT AMBO PRAESENTES, Fragm. XII. Tab. ap. Gell. 17, 2, 10 : contra tales oratores tantam causam…

pĕr-oscŭlor.opening: v. dep. , to kiss again and again : hos (uniones) perosculatur, Mart. 8, 81, 5 dub. (al. deosculatur).

per-pāco.opening: v. a. , to quiet completely , reduce to quiet (i. q. perdomare): omnibus perpacatis, Liv. 36, 21 : Brennos perpacavit, Flor. 4, 12, 4 ; Aur. Vict. Vir. Ill. 33 .

per-parcē.opening: adv. , very sparingly or parsimoniously : perparce nimium facere sumptum, altogether too sparing, Ter. And. 2, 6, 24 ; cf. id. ib. 2, 6, 19 .

per-părum.opening: adv. , very little (late Lat.), Veg. Vet. 3, 3 .

per-parvŭlus.opening: adj. dim. , very little , very small : sigilla, Cic. Verr. 2, 4, 43, § 95 : scrupuli, Sol. 53, 25 .

per-parvus.opening: adj. , very little , very small : semina, Lucr. 3, 216 ; 5, 588 : quae et cum assunt perparva sunt, Cic. Leg. 1, 19, 52 : culpa, id. Deiot. 3, 9 : controversia, id. Leg. 1, 20, 54 : perparva et tenuis civitas, Cic.…

per-pasco.opening: v. n. , to graze , pasture. Lit. , Varr. L. L. 5, § 95 Müll.— Transf. : , , v. dep. , to lay waste , devastate : fluvius perpascitur agros, Sev. Aetn. 489.—Hence, , , P. a. , well fed , in good condition : canis,…

per-paucŭlus.opening: adj. dim. , very little , very few : deduxit in Academiam perpauculis passibus, Cic. Leg. 1, 21, 54 ; M. Aur. ap. Front. Ep. ad M. Caes. 1, 3 Mai.

per-paucus.opening: adj. , very little , very few : homines, Ter. Eun. 3, 1, 19 ; cf. in tmesi: per pol quam paucos reperias amatores, id. Hec. 1, 1, 1 : patres, Liv. 43, 11, 11 : si perpauca mutavisset, Cic. Ac. 2, 43, 132 : dicere, id.…

per-paulŭlus.opening: ( ), , adj. dim. , very little indeed; hence, , , , a very little indeed : perpaululum loci, v. l. in Cic. de Or. 2, 35, 150 .

per-paulus.opening: adj. , very little. As subst. : , , , a very little : loci, Cic. de Or. 2, 35, 150 .— Adv. : , a very little indeed : declinare, Cic. Fin. 1, 6, 19 .

per-pauper.opening: adj. , very poor : vicinus, Afran. ap. Non. 280, 25 (Com. Rel. p. 157 Rib.): rex, Cic. Att. 6, 3, 5 .

per-pauxillus.opening: adj. , very little; hence, , , , a very little , Plaut. Capt. 1, 2, 74 .

per-păvĕfăcĭo.opening: v. a. , to frighten very much , to make one afraid , Plaut. Stich. 1, 2, 28 .

per-pĕdĭo.opening: v. a. , to hinder , impede , Att. ap. Non. 238, 10 (Trag. Rel. p. 145 Rib.).

per-pello.opening: v. a. , to strike or push violently. Lit. (rare; perh. not in Cic., for in Cic. Cæl. 15, 36, the true reading is pepulerunt): nixurit, qui niti vult, et in conatu saepius aliquā re perpellitur, Nigid. ap. Non. 144, 21…

perpendĭcŭlāris.opening: , and , , adj. perpendiculum , perpendicular , Front. Exposit. Form. p. 32 Goes.

perpendĭcŭlātor.opening: id. , an artisan who uses a plumb-line , a stonemason , Aur. Vict. Epit. 14 .

perpendĭcŭlum.opening: perpendo , a plummet , plumb-line. Lit. : non egeremus perpendiculis, non normis, non regulis, Cic. Fragm. ap. Non. 163, 3 : ad perpendiculum columnas exigere, to examine by a plumb-line, id. Verr. 2, 1, 51, § 133 : ad…

per-pendo.opening: v. a. , to weigh carefully or exactly. Lit. (very rare): in librili pendere, Gell. 20, 1, 34 .— Trop. , to weigh carefully , examine; to ponder , consider (class.; syn.: delibero, expendo, reputo): aliquid acri judicio,…

perpensātĭo.opening: perpenso , an exact weighing , a careful consideration : honorum atque officiorum, Gell. 2, 2, 8 .

perpenso.opening: v. freq. a. perpendo , to weigh carefully; trop., to ponder , consider (post-class.), Grat. Cyn. 298 ; Amm. 16, 4, 1 ; 19, 11, 9 .

perpĕrĭtūdo.opening: perperus , heedlessness , thoughtlessness (ante-class.), Att. ap. Non. 150, 14 .

Perperna.opening: or , , , a Roman surname. A famous person of this name was M. Perperna, the murderer of Sertorius , who was defeated by Pompey , Liv. 44, 27, 11 ; id. Epit. 96 ; Vell. 2, 30, 1 ; Flor. 2, 20, 6 .—Form Perpenna, Nep.…

perpĕrus.opening: adj. , = πέρπερος (prop. heedless, inconsiderate; hence, in gen.), not properly constituted , faulty , defective , wrong (as adj. only ante- and postclass.): populares, Att. ap. Non. 150, 12 : nihil perperum, Vop. Tac.…

perpes.opening: adj. like perpetuus, from per-peto , lasting throughout , continuous , uninterrupted , continual , perpetual (anteand post-class.): perpetem pro perpetuo dixerunt poëtae, Fest. p. 217 Müll.: luna proprio suo perpeti…

perpessīcĭus.opening: or , , adj. perpetior , that can endure much , that has endured much , patient , enduring (postAug.): etiam a duro et perpessicio confessionem accipit, Sen. Ep. 53, 6 : Socrates perpessicius senex, id. ib. 104, 27 .

perpessĭo.opening: id. , a bearing , suffering , enduring : harum rerum perpessio, Cic. Rab. Perd. 5, 16 : laborum, id. Inv. 2, 54, 163: rerum arduarum ac difficilium, id. ib. : dolorum, id. Fin. 1, 15, 49 : fortitudinis patientia et…

per-pĕtĭor.opening: v. dep. n. and a. [patior], to bear steadfastly , suffer with firmness or patience; to stand out , abide , endure (class.): animus aeger neque pati neque perpeti potis est, Enn. ap. Cic. Tusc. 3, 3, 5 (Trag. v. 260…

perpĕtrābĭlis.opening: adj. perpetro , that may be done , allowable , permissible (postclass.), Tert. ad Ux. 2, 1 .

perpĕtrātĭo.opening: id. , a performing , committing , performance , perpetration (post-class.), Tert. Poen. 3 : mali, Aug. Trin. 13, 6 .

perpĕtrātor.opening: id. , a performer , committer , perpetrator (post-class.): peccati, Aug. Civ. Dei, 20, 1: caedis infaustae, Sid. Ep. 8, 6 .

per-pĕtro.opening: v. a. patro , to carry through , complete , effect , bring about , achieve , execute , perform , accomplish; to commit , perpetrate (mostly ante-class. and post-Aug.; not in Cic. or Cæs.; rare as verb. finit.; syn.:…

perpĕtŭālis.opening: adj. perpetuus , that holds everywhere , universal , general (a word formed by Quint. as a transl. of the Gr. καθολικός , joined with universalis), Quint. 2, 13, 14 .—Hence, adv. : , permanently (opp. temporaliter),…

perpĕtŭārĭus.opening: adj. id. , constant , permanent; always employed , constantly engaged in any business or calling (post-Aug.): mulio, Sen. Apoc. 6, 2 .— Subst. : , , , a fee-farmer , hereditary tenant , Cod. Just. 11, 70, 5 .

perpĕtŭĭtas.opening: perpetuus , uninterrupted or continual duration , uninterrupted progress or succession , continuity , perpetuity (good prose; cf. infinitas): non ex singulis vocibus philosophi spectandi sunt, sed ex perpetuitate atque…

perpĕtŭĭto.opening: , a false read. in Enn.; v. 2. perpetuo.

perpĕtŭo.opening: (old perf. subj. perpetuassint, Enn. Ann. 322 ), , v. a. perpetuus , to cause a thing to continue uninterruptedly , to proceed with continually , to make perpetual , perpetuate (rare but class.): libertatem ut…

per-pĕtŭus.opening: adj. ( comp. perpetuior, Cato ap. Prisc. p. 601 P.; sup. perpetuissimus, id. ib. ) [peto], continuing throughout , continuous , unbroken , uninterrupted; constant , universal , general , entire , whole , perpetual…

per-pexus.opening: adj. pecto , wellcombed (post-class.): barba, Firm. Math. 5, 5.

per-pinguis.opening: adj. , very rich (postclass.): harenae, Auct. Itin. Alex. M. 45 Mai.

per-plăcĕo.opening: v. n. , to please greatly : ecquid placeant, me rogas? immo hercle vero perplacent, Plaut. Most. 3, 3, 4 : servi mei perplacet mihi consilium, id. Merc. 2, 3, 14 : perplacet (as affirm. answer), Ter. Heaut. 5, 5, 22…

per-plānus.opening: adj. , very plain (post-class.): expositio, Diom. p. 431 P.

perplexābĭlis.opening: adj. perplexor , perplexing : verbum, obscure, ambiguous, Plaut. As. 4, 1, 47 ; cf.: quod aliud audiatur, aliud sentiatur, Non. 151, 31 .— Adv. : , in a perplexing manner , perplexingly : perplexabiliter earum hodie…

perplexim.opening: adv. perplexus , intricately , confusedly , perplexedly : utrum ego perplexim lacessam oratione ad hunc modum, an, etc., Plaut. Stich. 1, 2, 19 (76 Ritschl); Cass. Hem. ap. Non. 515, 20 .

perplexĭo.opening: id. , perplexity , ambiguity; in plur. , Porc. Latro, Decl. ap. Cat. 33 .

perplexor.opening: (old inf. perplexarier; v. infra ), v. dep. id. , to make confusion , cause perplexity : scio, quo vos soleatis pacto perplexarier, Plaut. Aul. 2, 2, 81 .

per-plexus.opening: adj. plecto , entangled , involved , intricate , confused (not in Cic. or Cæs.). Lit. : figurae, Lucr. 2, 102 ; cf. id. 2, 459 ; 463 : foramina linguae, id. 4, 621 : corpora terraï, id. 5, 452 : iter silvae, Verg. A. 9,…

per-plĭcātus.opening: Part. [plico], interlaced , entangled. —In tmesi: perque plicatis (elementis), Lucr. 2, 394 .

per-plōro.opening: v. n. , to weep greatly , Inscr. Grut. 928, 11 .

per-plŭo.opening: (old form , Fest. s. v. patera, p. 250 Müll.; v. in the foll. ), , v. n. and a. Neutr. To rain through , rain in : quā possit ex imbribus aqua perpluere, Vitr. 2, 8, 18 .— Impers. : circuire oportet, sicubi perpluat,…

per-pŏlĭo.opening: ( fut. perpolibo, App. M. 6, 28 ), , v. a. , to polish well. Lit. : loco calce arenāque perpolito, Vell. 2, 22, 3 : aurum tritu perpolitum, Plin. 33, 4, 21, § 66 : caudae setas horridas comptā diligentiā perpolibo, App.…

perpŏlītĭo.opening: perpolio , a thorough polishing , elaborating , Auct. Her. 4, 13, 18 .

perpŏlītus.opening: Part. and P. a. , from perpolio.

per-pŏpŭlor.opening: v. dep. a. , to lay quite waste , ravage , devastate; to plunder or pillage completely : agrum Placentinum, Liv. 34, 56 : omnia loca, id. 34, 28 : Italiam, id. 22, 3 ; Tac. A. 14, 26 .— Part. perf. , in a pass. signif.:…

per-porto.opening: v. a. , to carry or transport a thing to a place: praedam Carthaginem, Liv. 28, 46 fin.

perpōtātĭo.opening: perpoto , a continued drinking , a drinking-bout : biduo duabusque noctibus perpotationem continuare, Plin. 14, 22, 28, § 145 : intemperantissimae perpotationes, Cic. Pis. 10, 22 : vomitiones ac rursus perpotationes,…

per-pŏtĭor.opening: v. dep. n. , to get entire possession of , to hold or enjoy completely (jurid. Lat.).—With abl. : privilegiis, Cod. Just. 7, 37, 2 : nomine tribunorum, ib. 12, 7, 2 : beneficiis, ib. 12, 21, 2 .

per-pōto.opening: v. a. and n. To drink or tipple without intermission , to keep up a carouse : postquam ejus hinc pater sit profectus peregre, tum perpotasse adsiduo, Plaut. Most. 4, 2, 60 ; id. Ps. 2, 6, 13 : totos dies, Cic. Verr. 2,…

perpressa.opening: f , a plant , called also bacchar, Plin. 21, 19, 77, § 132 ; 26, 8, 55, § 87 .

per-prĭmo.opening: v. a. premo , to press hard , to press perpetually (Aug.). In gen.: cubilia, to lie upon, Hor. Epod. 16, 38 : umorem perprimit (al. perpremit), Sen. Ep. 99, 18 .— In partic., in mal. part., Ov. A. A. 1, 394 .

per-prŏbābĭlis.opening: adj. , very worthy of belief , highly probable (late Lat.), Aug. Music. 1, 6, 12 .

per-prŏpĕre.opening: , a false read. for praepropere, Plaut. Mil. 2, 4, 10 .

per-prŏpinquus.opening: adj. , very near : commutatio rerum, Att. ap. Cic. Div. 1, 22, 45 (Trag. Rel. v. 36 Rib.).

per-prosper.opening: adj. , very favorable , very prosperous : valetudo, very good, excellent, Suet. Claud. 31 .

per-prūrisco.opening: v. inch. n. , to itch all over : ubi perpruriscamus usque ex unguiculis, Plaut. Stich. 5, 5, 20 ; App. M. 10, p. 209, 12 .

per-pŭdesco.opening: v. n. , to feel great shame , Cornelia ap. Nep. Fragm. 12, 2 Staver.

per-pugnax.opening: adj. , very pugnacious : perpugnax in disputando, Cic. de Or. 1, 20, 93 ; Aug. contr. Acad. 3, 4.

per-pulcher.opening: adj. , very beautiful : dona, Ter. Eun. 3, 2, 15 .

per-pulsus.opening: adj. pello , greatly smitten : me malis perpulsum, Front. Ep. ad Verum, 9 Mai.

per-pungo.opening: v. a. , to pierce through and through (post-class. and only in part. perf. ), Cael. Aur. Acut. 2, 10, 71 ; id. Tard. 3, 8, 128 .

per-purgo.opening: (ante-class. , v. Ritschl, Opusc. 2, 426 sqq.), , v. a. , to cleanse or purge thoroughly , to make quite clean. Lit. : alvum, Cato, R. R. 115 : se, Cic. N. D. 2, 50, 127 : perpurgata ulcera, Cels. 5, 26 , n. 36:…

per-pūrus.opening: adj. , very clean : lana, Varr. R. R. 3, 16, 28 Schneid. N. cr. (al. purpurea).

per-pŭsillus.opening: adj. , very small , very little : pusillus testis processit ... Non accusabis: perpusillum rogabo, in a double sense ( adj. or adv. ), I will ask very little , or, the very little man , Cic. de Or. 2, 60, 245 .

per-pŭto.opening: v. a. , to trim or prune thoroughly. —Hence, trop., to set forth plainly or neatly : argumentum alicui, ut ego argumentum hoc vobis plane perputem, Plaut. Cist. 1, 3, 7 .

per-quadrātus.opening: adj. , perfectly square , Vitr. 5 , praef. 4 Schneid.

per-quam.opening: adv. (also, less correctly, written separately, , v. per fin. ), as much as possible , extremely , exceedingly : illorum mores perquam meditate tenes, Plaut. Bacch. 3, 6, 16 : perquam indignis modis, id. Rud. 3, 3, 9 :…

per-quĭesco.opening: v. n. , to rest all through , to spend in rest : totam noctem, App. M. 8, p. 211, 15 .

perquīrĭtātus.opening: adj. P. a. of unused perquirito, āre , greatly sought after : opusculum usquequaque perquiritatum, Claud. Mam. Stat. Anim. 1 praef.

per-quīro.opening: v. a. quaero . To ask or inquire after diligently , to make diligent search for any thing: perquirunt, quid causae siet, Plaut. Stich. 1, 3, 49 : vasa, Cic. Verr. 2, 4, 18, § 39 ; cf. id. ib. 2, 3, 58 , § 134; id. Cael.…

perquīsītor.opening: perquiro , a seeker out , a hunter after any thing: auctionum, Plaut. Stich. 2, 2, 61 ; Amm. 14, 5 .

per-rārus.opening: adj. , very uncommon , very rare (as an adj. not in Cic.), Liv. 29, 38, 7 : perrarum est, ut, etc., Plin. 31, 3, 23, § 38 .— Adv. : , very seldom , very rarely : si quando id efficit, quod perraro potest. Cic. Rep. 2,…

per-rĕcondĭtus.opening: adj. , very hidden or abstruse , very recondite : ratio consuetudinis, Cic. de Or. 1, 30, 135 .

per-rēpo.grammar: psi, ptum, 3 v. n. and a.
per-rēpo.opening: v. n. and a. Neutr. , to creep or crawl through to a place: ad praesepia, Col. 6, 5 : in aliena jugorum compluvia, id. 4, 24 .— Act. , to crawl through or over any thing: tellurem genibus, Tib. 1, 2, 85 .

perrepto.opening: v. freq. a. perrepo , to creep or crawl through : omnes plateas perreptavi, Plaut. Am. 4, 1, 3 ; so, omnes latebras, id. Rud. 1, 4, 4 : perreptavi usque omne oppidum ad portam, Ter. Ad. 4, 6, 3 .

Perrhaebi.opening: , = Περραιβοί , a people of Thessaly about Tempe and Mount Olympus , the Perrhœbians , Liv. 33, 32 ; 34 ; 42, 53 .—Hence, , , adj. , Perrhœbian , Thessalian : Pindus, Prop. 3, 3 (4, 4), 33, 55: Caeneus, Ov. M. 12, 172 .…

per-rīdĭcŭlus.opening: adj. , very laughable , very ridiculous : doctrina, Cic. de Or. 2, 19, 77 ; Val. Max. 9, 12, 8 .— Adv. : , very laughably , very ridiculously , Cic. de Or. 2, 59, 239 : perridicule homines augurabantur, Cic. Verr. 2, 2,…

per-rīmōsus.opening: , a false read. for paeminosus, Varr. R. R. 1, 51, 1 .

per-rōdo.opening: v. a. , to gnaw or eat through : non plures sinus perroserint, Cels. 5, 28, 12 ; Plin. 30, 16, 53, § 149 .

perrŏgātĭo.opening: perrogo , a decree , Inscr. Maff. Mus. Ver. 288, 4 .— The passage of a law : perrogationem legis Maniliae flagitasti, Cic. Mur. 23, 47 .

per-rŏgĭto.opening: v. freq. a. , to ask through in succession , to ask one after another : defessus perrogitando advenas de gnatis, Pac. ap. Prisc. p. 634 P. (Trag. Rel. v. 315 Rib.).

per-rŏgo.opening: v. a. To ask through in succession , to ask one after another (perh. not ante-Aug.): sententias, Liv. 29, 19 ; Tac. H. 4, 9 ; Suet. Aug. 35 .— Transf. , to carry through , to pass (a law) after proposing it: tribunus…

per-rumpo.grammar: rūpi, ruptum, 3 v. n. and a.
per-rumpo.opening: v. n. and a. , to break through. Neutr. , to break or rush through , to force one's way through : per medios hostes perrumpunt, Caes. B. G. 6, 39 : in vestibulum templi, Liv. 3, 18 : in urbem, id. 10, 41 : in triclinium…

Persa.opening: the name of a little dog , Cic. Div. 1, 46, 103 .

Persae.opening: , = Πέρσαι , the Persians , originally the inhabitants of the country of Persis , afterwards of the great kingdom of Persia , Plaut. Curc. 3, 1, 72 ; Cic. Rep. 3, 9, 15 ; id. Tusc. 1, 45, 108 ; id. Brut. 10, 41 ; id.…

per-saepe.opening: adv. , very often , very frequently : quod persaepe fit, Cic. Lael. 20, 75 : frons, oculi, voltus persaepe mentiuntur, id. Q. Fr. 1, 1, 5, § 15 : persaepe velut qui Junonis sacra ferret, Hor. S. 1, 3, 10 ; id. A. P. 349…

per-saevĭo.opening: v. n. , to be furious : fluctibus hanc propter persaevit Caspius aestus, Prisc. Perieg. 683 .

per-salsus.opening: adj. , very witty , Cic. de Or. 2, 69, 279 .—Hence, adv. : , very wittily : gratias agere, Cic. Q. Fr. 2, 15, 3 .

persălūtātĭo.opening: persaluto , a saluting of all , assiduous salutation , Cic. Mur. 21, 44 .

per-sălūto.opening: v. a. , to salute one after another : omnes, Cic. Fl. 18, 42 : nomenculatores, Sen. Tranq. 12, 6 : deos, Phaedr. 4, 12, 4 ; Curt. 10, 5, 3 .

per-sanctus.opening: adj. , very sacred or holy : CONIVX, Inscr. Afr. ap. Rénier, 4414.—Hence, adv. : , very sacredly or religiously : dejerare, to swear solemnly, Ter. Hec. 5, 2, 5 : jurare, Suet. Tib. 10 ; id. Ner. 35 .

per-sāno.opening: v. a. , to cure completely : vomicas, Plin. 20, 22, 89, § 244 ; 24, 19, 120, § 188 al.

per-sānus.opening: adj. , perfectly sound , Cato, R. R. 157 fin.

per-săpĭens.opening: adj. , very wise , homo, Cic. Prov. Cons. 18, 44 .—Hence, adv. : , very wisely : persapienter dat ipsa lex potestatem defendendi, Cic. Mil. 4, 11 .

per-scĕlĕrātus.opening: adj. , very vicious , Not. Tir. p. 71 .

per-scĭens.opening: Part. [scio], knowing well. —With acc. : animum persciens, Lampr. Commod. 5, 2 .—Hence, adv. : , very knowingly , very discreetly , Cic. Brut. 55, 202 .

per-scindo.opening: v. a. , to rend asunder or in pieces : nubem, Lucr. 6, 138 ; 180 : vestem, Tib. 1, 10, 63 : omnia perscindente vento, Liv. 21, 58, 57 ; Lucr. 6, 111 .— Pass. , Lucr. 4, 599 .

per-scisco.opening: v. a. , to learn thoroughly , become well informed of : causam tumultūs cupidus persciscere, Dict. Cret. 2, 37 .

per-scītus.opening: adj. , very clever , very fine. —In tmesi: quod apud Catonem est ... per mihi scitum videtur, Cic. de Or. 2, 67, 271 : per ecastor scitus puer, Ter. And. 3, 2, 6 .

per-scrībo.opening: v. a. Lit. , to write in full or at length , to write out , to write without abbreviations (cf.: conscribo, compono): verbo non perscripto, not being written in full , Tiro Tullius ap. Gell. 10, 1, 7 : in M. Catonis…

perscriptĭo.opening: perscribo . A writing down , an entry in a book, an official recording : perscriptionum et liturarum adversaria, Cic. Rosc. Com. 2, 5 ; id. de Or. 1, 58, 250 : falsae perscriptiones, id. Phil. 5, 4, 11 ; id. Fam. 5, 2,…

per-scriptĭto.opening: v. freq. a. id. , to write down , Ter. de Syllab. p. 2391 P. (al. praescriptitare).

perscriptor.opening: id. , a drawer up in writing, a writer : fenerationis, Cic. Verr. 2, 3, 72, § 168 .

perscriptūra.opening: id. , a drawing up in writing, a writing (jurid. Lat.): cum testamenti faciunt perscripturam, Dig. 29, 1, 3 (al. cum testamentum faciunt, per scripturam adicere).

perscrūtātĭo.opening: perscrutor , a searching through , an examination , investigation : profundi perscrutatio, Sen. Cons. ad Helv. 9, 12 .

perscrūtātor.opening: id. , a thorough searcher , an examiner , investigator (post-class.): talium rerum, Capitol. Max. 1 (al. persecutor); Veg. Mil. 3, 3 (al. prosecutores); Cassiod. Var. 2, 15 .

perscrūtātrix.opening: perscrutator , an examiner (late Lat.), Jul. ap. Aug. c. Sec. Resp. Jul. 2, 103.

per-scrūtor.opening: v. dep. ( act. collat. form, v. infra fin. ), to search through , examine (class.). Lit. : speculari et perscrutari aliquid, Cic. Tusc. 5, 20, 59 : canes, qui investigabant et perscrutabantur omnia, Cic. Verr. 2, 4, 21,…

per-sculptus.opening: Part. [sculpo], carved , engraved : lapides, Coripp. Laud. Just. 3, 377 .

persĕa.opening: , = περσέα , a sacred tree in Egypt and Persia , Plin. 13, 9, 15, § 63 ; 15, 13, 13, § 45 .

per-sĕco.opening: v. a. , to cut up , exlirpate; to cut out , excise; trop.: vitium, Liv. 40, 19 fin. : rei publicae vomicas, Auct. ap. Quint. 8, 6, 15 : rerum naturas, to dissect, lay bare the secrets of nature, Cic. Ac. 2, 39, 122 .…

persector.opening: v. freq. [persequor], to follow or pursue eagerly , to investigate (ante-class.): persectari hoc volo, Sceledre, nos nostri an alieni simus, Plaut. Mil. 2, 5, 20 ; Lucr. 4, 1010 : nec persectari primordia singula…

persĕcūtĭo.opening: id. , a following after , a chasing , pursuing; a chase , pursuit. Lit. : bestiae, Dig. 41, 1, 44 ; so ib. 41, 1, 4 ; App. M. 4, p. 155, 1 : pluviis persecutionem passi, Vulg. Sap. 16, 16 ; 11, 21 .— Transf. A…

persĕcūtor.opening: id. . A pursuer (post-class.): flagitiorum turpium, Capitol. Alb. 11, 7 .— A persecutor of Christians, Mort. Persec. 1; id. Inst. 5, 23, 1 : Ecclesiae, Hieron. Ep. ad Helv. 3: sub ense persecutoris pati, Prud. στεφ . 1,…

persĕcūtrix.opening: persecutor , she that pursues or persecutes , Aug. Cons. Evang. 1, 25 .

per-sĕdĕo.opening: v. n. , to remain sitting , to sit or stay long anywhere (not in Cic. or Cæs.): at neque quo pacto persederit umor aquai Visumst, Lucr. 1, 307 : totā nocte in speculis, Curt. 9, 9, 23 : in equo dies noctesque…

per-segnis.opening: adj. , very sluggish or inactive : proelium, Liv. 25, 15, 12 .

Persēĭus.opening: , v. 2. Persa, A., and 1. Perseus, B. 2.

per-sĕnesco.opening: v. inch. n. , to grow old anywhere (post-class.): ibi persenuit, Eutr. 1, 11 .

per-sĕnīlis.opening: adj. , very old or aged (late Lat.): aetas, Vulg. Jos. 23, 1 .

per-sentĭo.opening: v. a. , to perceive plainly. Verg. A. 4, 90 ; App. M. 7, p. 193, 6 .— To feel deeply : pectore curas, Verg. A. 4, 448 .

per-sentisco.opening: v. intens. a. To perceive clearly , to detect (ante-class.): nunc ne legio persentiscat, clam illuc redeundum'st mihi, Plaut. Am. 1, 3, 28 ; id. Aul. 1, 1, 24 : ubi possem persentiscere, Ni essem lapis, Ter. Heaut. 5,…

Persĕphŏnē.opening: , = Περσεφόνη , Proserpine , Ov. F. 4, 591 ; Stat. Th. 12, 276 ; Ov. M. 10, 15 ; Prop. 2, 28, 47 sq. ; Luc. 5, 126 ; Inscr. Orell. 4849 .— Transf. , death : at mihi Persephone nigram denunciat horam, Tib. 4, 5, 5 ; Ov.…

Persēpŏlis.opening: ( ), , , = Περσαιπολις , a city of Persia , the ruins of which are now called Istakhr , Plin. 6, 26, 29, § 115 ; Curt. 5, 4, 33 ; 5, 6, 11 sq.; Vulg. 2 Macc. 9, 2 ; Amm. 23, 6, 42 .

per-sĕquax.opening: adj. , eagerly pursuing (post-class.): in reatu pervestigando, Sid. Ep. 4, 9 (but in App. Flor. n. 23, p. 366, 5, or de Deo Soc. prol. p. 108, Hild. reads oculis perspicax).

persĕquens.opening: Part. and P. a. , from persequor.

per-sĕquor.opening: v. dep. a. and ( act. collat. form of the imperat. persece for perseque, Poët. ap. Cic. Att. 13, 23 fin. ). Act. , to follow perseveringly , to follow after , continue to follow , pursue. Lit. In gen.: ille servolum…

per-sĕro.opening: v. a. , to stick or run through (post-class.): resticulas per ficos maturas perserunt, Varr. R. R. 1, 41, 5 .

per-serpo.opening: v. n. , to creep perpetually , to crawl , Lucil. ap. Charis. p. 100, 31 Keil.

per-servĭo.opening: v. n. , to serve throughout : alicui, Vop. Prob. 18 dub.

per-servo.opening: v. a. , to preserve (post-class.): patientiam, Tert. Pat. 5 .

Perses.opening: , = Πέρσης . A Persian; v. Persae.— Son of Perseus and Andromeda , the progenitor of the Persians , Plin. 7, 56, 57, § 201 .— Son of Sol and Persa , brother of Æetes and Circe , Hyg. Fab. praef.— The last king of…

Perseus.opening: ( acc. , Persea, Ov. M. 4, 610 ), , = Περσεύς . Son of Jupiter and Danăē , abandoned by his grandfather Acrisius , but rescued and brought up by Polydectes , king of Seriphus. When grown up , he undertook , at the…

Persēus.opening: v. the preced. art., I. B. 1.

persĕvērābĭlis.opening: adj. persevero , persevering (post-class.): tenacitas, Cael. Aur. Acut. 3, 21, 198 .

persĕvērans.opening: Part. and P. a. , from persevero.

persĕvēranter.opening: adv. , v. persevero, P. a. fin.

persĕvērantĭa.opening: persevero , steadfastness , constancy , perseverance (syn. pertinacia): perseverantia est in ratione bene consideratā stabilis et perpetua permansio, Cic. Inv. 2, 54, 164 ; id. Phil. 7, 5, 14 : disputandum est, aliud an…

persĕvērātĭo.opening: id. , continuance , duration (post-class.), App. Trismeg. p. 101 fin. : operis, Hyg. p. 178 Goes.

persĕvēro.grammar: āvi, ātum, 1 v. n. and a.
persĕvēro.opening: v. n. and a. [perseverus]. Neutr. , to abide by or adhere to strictly; to continue steadfastly , to persist , persevere in any thing (class.; syn.: persisto, permaneo). With in and abl. : perseveras tu quidem et in tuā…

per-sĕvērus.opening: adj. , very strict : imperium, Tac. A. 15, 48 .— Adv. : , very strictly : inquirere, Plin. Ep. 9, 5, 1 .

per-sĭbus.opening: adj. sibus, callidus sive acutus, Fest. p. 336 , very knowing , very acute , Plaut. and Naev. ap. Fest. p. 217 Müll.; cf. Naev. ap. Varr. L. L. 7, § 107 Müll.

per-siccātus.opening: adj. , quite dried , perfectly dry , Apic. 7, 6 .

per-siccus.opening: adj. , very dry : oculi, Cels. 3, 6, 23 : tempus, Fest. s. v. substillum, pp. 306 and 307 Müll.

Persĭcus.opening: , v. Persae, II. B., and Perses, IV. B.

per-sĭdĕo.opening: v. n. per-sedeo , to continue sitting , remain long sitting anywhere, Plin. 17, 24, 36, § 222 ; Curt. 9, 9, 23 .

per-sīdo.opening: v. n. , to sink or settle down , to penetrate anywhere ( poet. ): pestilitas fruges persidit in ipsas, Lucr. 6, 1126 ; 1, 307 : ubi frigidus imber Altius ad vivum persedit, Verg. G. 3, 442 .

per-signo.opening: v. a. (extremely rare; not in Cic. or Cæs.). To note down , record : uni dona, Liv. 25, 7, 5 .— To mark : notis corpus, Mel. 1, 19, 20 ; so Firm. Math. 3, 7, 12.

per-sĭlĭo.opening: v. n. 2. salio , to leap through , Not. Tir. p. 146 .

per-sĭmĭlis.opening: adj. , very like or similar (class.), Cic. Part. Or. 7, 26 : statuam istius persimilem deturbant, id. Pis. 38, 93 : isti tabulae fore librum Persimilem, cujus, etc., Hor A. P 6 sq.

per-simplex.opening: adj. , very plain or simple : victus, Tac. A. 15, 45 fin.

per-sisto.opening: v. n. , to continue steadfastly , to persist (rare): si perstiteris ad corpus ea referre, Cic. Fin. 2, 33, 107 fin. : in impudentiā, Liv. 38, 14, 11 : in luxuriā, Treb. Poll. Gall. 4, 2: in oratione persistens cum…

persītes.opening: a plant , a species of tithymalus, App. Herb. 108 .

Persĭus.opening: a Roman surname. C. Persius, an orator , a contemporary of the Gracchi , Cic. de Or 2, 6, 25 ; id. Brut. 26, 99 ; id. Fin. 1, 3, 7 .— A. Persius Flaccus, a celebrated satirist of Volaterrœ , in Etruria , who died in the…

persōlāta.opening: ( ), , , a plant , the brown mullen : persolata, quam Graeci arcion vocant (al. persollata), Plin. 25, 9, 66, § 113 ; 26, 5, 12, § 24 Sillig (Jan, persollata).

per-sŏlĭdo.opening: v. a. , to make quite solid , Stat. Th. 1, 352 .

per-sŏlĭtus.opening: adj. , very usual , Not. Tir p. 46.

persolla.opening: dim. persona , a little mask; hence, as a term of abuse, you little fright! Plaut. Curc. 1, 3, 36 .

per-sōlus.opening: adj. , quite alone : oculum effodito persolum mihi, si, etc., my only eye, Plaut. Men. 1, 2, 46 .

persŏlūta.opening: , a corrupt read. for pesoluta, Plin. 21, 33, 108, § 184 .

per-solvo.opening: v. a. , to release or discharge completely; acc. to the signif. of the simple verb. To pay , pay out : stipendium militibus, Cic. Att. 5, 14, 1 : pecuniam alicui, Tac. A. 1, 37 : pecuniam ab aliquo, to pay by a draft on…

persōna.opening: f [acc. to Gabius Bassus ap. Gell. 5, 7, 1 sq. , from per-sŏno, to sound through, with the second syllable lengthened]. A mask , esp. that used by players, which covered the whole head, and was varied according to the…

persōnālis.opening: adj. persona , of or belonging to a person , personal (jurid. Lat.): usus, Dig. 8, 3, 37 : tale beneficium personale est, ib. 24, 3, 13 : actiones, ib. 50, 16, 178 .— In gram.: verbum, a personal verb , i.e. a verb…

persōnāta.opening: a kind of large burdock , said to be synonymous with persolata, Col. 6, 17, 1 , App. Herb. 36 ; Plin. 25, 9, 58, § 104 ; v persolata.

persŏnātĭo.opening: persono , resonance (late Lat.), Cassiod. in Psa. 150, 3 .

persōnātīvē.opening: adv. persona , personally , Charis. p. 181, 25 Keil.

persōnātus.opening: adj. id. . Lit. , provided with or wearing a mask , masked : Roscius, Cic. de Or. 3, 59, 221 : pater, i. e. the father in the play, Hor. S. 1, 4, 56 : personata fabula (* the name of a play of Nœvius ), v. Fest. p. 217…

per-sŏno.opening: ( perf. personavit, App. M. 5, p. 164, 24 : personasse, Prud. στεφ . 34 praef.), v. n. and a. Neutr. To sound through and through , to resound : cum domus cantu et cymbalis personaret, Cic. Pis. 10, 22 : ut cotidiano…

per-sŏnus.opening: adj. , resounding , ringing (post-Aug.): Io ovanti persona sistro, Val. Fl. 4, 418 : verno persona cantu virgulta, Petr. 120 ; Mamert. Grat. Act. ad Jul. 10 .

per-sorbĕo.opening: v. a. , to suck or drink up , to absorb : spongiae persorbentes, Plin. 31, 11, 47, § 123 ; cf. Not. Tir. p. 168 .

perspectē.opening: adv. , v. perspicio, P. a. fin.

perspectĭo.opening: perspicio , a seeing into , perception (post-class.): rerum caelestium, Lact. 2, 8 fin. ; id. Ira Dei, 1, 4: veritatis, Aug. Civ. Dei , 8, 4.

perspecto.opening: v. freq. a. id. . * To look at or behold to the end : quinquennale certamen gymnicum perspectavit, Suet. Aug. 98 .— To look through , look all about : otiose perspecta aedis, ut lubet, Plaut. Most. 3, 2, 128 .

perspector.opening: id. , one who understands , a discerner (eccl. Lat.): mentis perspector Jesus, Juvenc. 2, 275 (al. prospector).

perspectus.opening: perspicio , a viewing thoroughly , an inspection , Luc. 8, 484 (al. prospectus).

per-spĕcŭlor.opening: v. dep. , to examine or explore thoroughly , to reconnoitre well : perspeculatus locorum situs, Suet. Caes. 58 : cum de vallo perspecularetur, Auct. B. Afr. 31.

perspergo.opening: v. a. per-spargo , to besprinkle , to wet. Lit. : ligna amureā crudā perspergito, Cato, R. R. 130 : unde haustā aquā templum deae perspersum est, Tac. A. 15, 44 : Prusiadem urbem perspergit Hylas lacus, Sol. 42, 2 .—…

perspĭcābĭlis.opening: adj. perspicio , that may easily be seen , conspicuous (post-class.): urbs, Amm. 14, 8, 3 ; Aug. Ep. 32 ad Paul.

perspĭcācē.opening: adv. id. , sharp-sightedly , acutely : quam perspicace, Afran. ap. Non. 513, 19 , and 515, 31 (Com. Rel. v. 59 Rib.).

perspĭcācĭtas.opening: perspicax , sharp-sightedness , discernment , discrimination : qui nullā perspicacitate, sine innocentium sontiumque differentiā,...damnarunt, Amm. 15, 3, 2 ; cf.: perspicacitas, τὸ συνοπτικόν , Gloss. Lab.

perspĭcax.opening: adj. perspicio , sharp -sighted , penetrating , acute , perspicacious : perspicax prudentia, old poet ap. Cic. Off. 3, 26, 98 : homo (with astutus), Ter. Heaut. 5, 1, 1 : ad aliquam rem, id. ib. 2, 3, 129 : sequemur et…

perspĭcĭbĭlis.opening: adj. id. , that may be clearly seen , bright : solis splendor, Vitr. 9, 1, 11 .

perspĭcĭentĭa.opening: id. , a full perception or knowledge of a thing: veri, Cic. Off. 1, 5, 15 .

perspĭcĭo.opening: v. a. , to look or see through , to look into , look at. Lit. : quo non modo non intrari, sed ne perspici quidem posset, Caes. B. G. 2, 17 : eas (epistulas) ego oportet perspiciam, corrigam: tum denique edentur, to look…

perspĭcŭĭtas.opening: perspicuus , transparency , clearness. Lit. : vitrea perspicuitas, Plin. 37, 10, 54, § 141 ; 37, 5, 20, § 79 .— Trop. , evidentness , clearness , perspicuity : nihil est clarius ἐναργεία , perspicuitatem, aut evidentiam…

perspĭcŭus.opening: adj. perspicio , transparent , clear (syn. tralucidus). Lit. : aquae, Ov. M. 5, 588 : sal, Plin. 31, 7, 39, § 79 : calix, Mart. 4, 86, 2 : gemma, id. 8, 68, 5 : nives, i.e. crystals, Stat. S. 3, 3, 94 .— Trop. , evident…

per-spīro.opening: v. n. To breathe everywhere , Cato, R. R. 157 .— To blow constantly : venti perspirantes, Plin. 2, 45, 45, § 116 .

per-sterno.opening: v. a. , to pave all over , to make quite even or level : viam, Liv 10, 47, 4; Vitr. 7, 1, 7 .

perstillo.opening: v. n. , to leak , drip : tecta jugiter perstillantia, Vulg. Prov. 19, 13 ; 27, 15 : domus, id. Ecclus. 11, 18 .

per-stĭmŭlo.opening: v. a. , to stimulate violently , Tac. A. 4, 12 fin.

per-stīpo.opening: v. a. , to crowd or press together , Cael. Aur. Acut. 3, 8, 93 .

per-sto.opening: ( fut. part. perstaturus, Liv. 8, 34, 4 ), , v. n. , to stand firmly , continue standing. Lit. (rare): frenatis equis equites diem totum perstabant, Liv. 44, 33 fin. : exercitus a mane usque ad horam X. diei…

per-strĕpo.grammar: ŭi, ĭtum, 3 v. n. and a.
per-strĕpo.opening: v. n. and a. , to make much noise ( poet. and in post-Aug. prose). Neutr. , to make a great noise , to resound , echo , ring : abeunt lavatum, perstrepunt, Ter. Eun. 3, 5, 52 : tellus perstrepit, Sil. 8, 430 :…

perstrictĭo.opening: perstringo , a rubbing , friction (post-class.), Veg. Vet. 1, 35 ; so id. ib. 1, 38 .— Trop. , a verbal attack : de perstrictione diversae partis nihil cavetur, Paul. Sent. 5, 4, 15 .

per-strīdo.opening: v. a. , to roar or whistle through : perstridunt caerula (maria) venti, German. Arat. 1, 6 .

per-stringo.opening: v. a. To bind tightly together; to draw together , draw up , contract : vitem, Cato, R. R. 32 : stomachus nimio rigore perstrictus, Veg. Vet. 3, 53 ; Grat. Cyneg. 296 .— To graze , graze against a thing. Lit. : femur,…

per-strŭo.opening: v. a. , to build completely , build up : parietem in altitudinem, Vitr. 7, 4, 1 .— Trop. : falsitatem, Hilar. Op Hist. Fragm. 2, 30.

per-stŭdĭōsus.opening: adj. , very desirous , very fond of any thing: musicorum, Cic. Tusc. 5, 22, 63 : litterarum Graecarum, id. Sen. 1 fin.—Adv. : , very eagerly , very fondly : audire aliquem, Cic. Brut. 56, 207 .

per-suādĕo.opening: v. a. , to bring over by talking , to convince of the truth of any thing, to persuade (cf. convinco). In gen., constr. absol. , with an obj.-clause and dat. , rarely with acc. of the person : oratoris officium est…

persuāsĭbĭlis.opening: adj. persuadeo , convincing , persuasive (post-Aug.): rhetorice est vis inveniendi omnia in oratione persuasibilia, Quint. 2, 15, 13 ; so id. 2, 15, 17 : humanae sapientiae verba, Vulg. 1 Cor. 2, 4 ; Hier. Ep. 65, 9…

persuāsĭo.opening: id. . Lit. , a convincing , persuading , persuasion : dicere apposite ad persuasionem, Cic. Inv. 1, 5, 6 : difficilis, Just. 34, 4, 3 .— Transf. , conviction , persuasion , belief , opinion (postAug.): falsam sibi…

persuāsor.opening: persuadeo , a convincer , one who persuades or prevails upon , Mart. Cap. 5, § 467 .

persuastrix.opening: ( ), , persuasor , she that persuades , a ( female ) persuader. probripellecebrae et persuastrices, Plaut. Bacch. 5, 2, 47 .—Collat. form persuasitrices, Mart. Cap. 5, § 514 .

persuāsus.opening: persuadeo , a persuading , persuasion : persuasu servi, Plaut. Ep. Argum. 1 : hujus persuasu et inductu, Cic. ap. Quint. 5, 10, 69 .

per-suāvis.opening: adj. , very sweet , very pleasant , delightful : polus, Jul. Val. Rer. Gest. Alex. M. 3, 30 Mai.— Adv. : , very pleasantly , Aug. Music. 4, 13 .

per-subtīlis.opening: adj. Lit. , very fine or delicate , very subtle : animus persubtilis atque minutis Perquam corporibus factus, Lucr. 3, 179 .— Trop. , very ingenious : oratio, Cic. Planc. 24, 58 .

per-sulco.opening: , no perf. , , v. a. , to furrow through , to plough up. — Trop. : rugis persulcata genas, Claud. in Ruf. 1, 136 .

persultātor.opening: persulto , one who leaps or skips about (post-class.): litoris, Symm. Ep. 6, 23 (22).

per-sulto.grammar: āvi, ātum, 1 v. a. and n.
per-sulto.opening: v. a. and n. salto , to leap , skip , or prance about in a place (not in Cic. or Cæs.). Lit. Neutr. : in agro, Liv. 34, 20 : solo stabili, id. 44, 9 : ante vallum, Tac. A. 4, 47 : notis vadis, id. H. 5, 15 : super…

per-sŭo.opening: v. a. , to sew through , sew up , Not. Tir. p. 136 : persuo, διαρράπτω , Gloss. Philox.

per-tābesco.opening: v. inch. n. , to be gradually consumed , to waste away , Auct. Aetn. 472 .

pertaedesco.opening: v. inch. n. [pertaedet], to become disgusted or wearied with any thing (ante- and post-class.): ne pertaedescat, Cato, R. R. 156 : cum jam omnes pertaeduissent, Gell. 1, 2, 6 .

per-taedet.opening: (quidam pertisum volunt: quod consuetudo non probavit, Cic. Or. 48, 159 ; cf. Fest. pp. 216 sq.; 273, 8 Müll.; also Paul. ex Fest. p. 72, 18 Müll.), v. impers. and , to be disgusted or wearied with any thing; to feel…

per-tango.opening: v. a. , to touch all over , i. e. to baste well (post-class.): pullum suo sibi jure, Apic. 6, 9 ; 8, 8 .

per-tĕgo.opening: v. a. , to cover all over (ante-class.). Lit. : villam, Plaut. Rud. 1, 2, 35 : Odeum navium malis et antemnis e spoliis Persicis pertexit, Vitr. 5, 9 init. (al. pertexuit): locus pertectus, Cael. Aur. Tard. 1, 1, 18 .—…

per-tĕmĕrārĭus.opening: adj. , very rash; in tmesi: cum perabsurdum perque temerarium sit, Cod. Just. 12, 21, 2 .

per-tendo.grammar: di, sum, and tum, 3 n. v. a.
per-tendo.opening: v. a. , and —Prop., to stretch out, extend hence, transf., * Act. , to carry out , go on with , perform any thing: video non licere ut coeperam hoc pertendere, Ter. Heaut. 5, 5, 9 .— Neutr. Prop., to strive forward , to…

per-tĕnĕo.opening: v. a. , to hold constantly , keep hold of , hold fast (late Lat.): utinam (me) pertinuisset, Hier. Ep. 66 , n. 13.

per-tento.opening: v. a. , to feel all over; hence, To prove , try , test any thing. Lit. (very rare): cum utrumque pugionem pertentasset, Tac. H. 2, 49 : alta bipenni latera, Petr. poët. 89, v. 24.— Trop. (rare but class.): aliquem, Ter.…

per-tĕnŭis.opening: adj. , very thin , very small or fine. Lit. : sabulum pertenue, Plin. 18, 6, 7, § 34 .— Trop. , very slight or slender , very weak : spes salutis, Cic. Fam. 14, 3, 2 : discrimen, id. Agr. 2, 32, 87 : suspicio, id. Clu.…

per-tĕpĭdus.opening: adj. , very lukewarm , very tepid : aqua, Vop. Carin. 17, 5 .

per-tĕrĕbro.opening: v. a. , to bore through : columnam, Cic. Div. 1, 24, 48 : lapis perterebratus, Vitr. 8, 7, 8 ; Arn. 3, 107 .

per-tergĕo.opening: , and , , v. a. , to wipe off , wipe dry. Lit. : gausape purpureo mensam pertersit, Hor. S. 2, 8, 11 : spongia vasa, Col. 12, 9, 2 . —* Transf. , to rub or touch against gently : (aër) quasi perterget pupillas, Lucr. 4,…

per-tĕro.opening: , no perf. , , v. a. , to rub , bruise , or pound to pieces : myrti bacam, Col. 12, 38, 7 : uva pertrita, id. 8, 5, 21 .

perterrĕfăcĭo.opening: v. a. perterreo-facio , to frighten or terrify thoroughly : Davum, Ter. And. 1, 1, 142 .

per-terrĕo.opening: v. a. , to frighten or terrify thoroughly : aliquem, Ter. Eun. 5, 3, 13 : alios magnitudine poenarum, Caes. B. G. 7, 4 ; 50 : metu perterriti, Cic. Caecin. 10, 26 : obstupefactus ac perterritus, id. Cat. 2, 7, 14 :…

perterrĭcrĕpus.opening: adj. perterreo-crepo , that clatters or rattles most terribly (ante-class.); old poët. ap. Cic. Or. 49, 164 : sonitus, Lucr. 6, 129 .

perterrĭto.opening: v. freq. a. perterreo , to frighten or terrify thoroughly (postclass.), Avien. Arat. 1169 .

per-texo.opening: v. a. Lit. To weave throughout , weave entirely : palla bysso tenui pertexta, i. e. byssina, App. M. 11, p. 258, 21 .— To interweave , i. e. to furnish , decorate , adorn with any thing: Odeum, quod Pericles navium…

pertĭca.opening: a pole , a long staff. In gen.: perticam habere ... quī verberarem asinos, Plaut. As. 3, 2, 43 : pertica suspensos portabat longa maniplos, Ov. F. 3, 117 ; cf. id. Nuc. 68 : perticis oleas decutere, Plin. 15, 3, 3, § 11…

pertĭcālis.opening: adj. pertica , that serves for poles or stakes : salix, Col. 4, 31, 2 ; Plin. 17, 20, 32, § 143 .

pertĭcārĭus.opening: adj. id. , of or belonging to poles : negotians perticarius, Inscr. Marang. Delle Cose Gentil. p. 488.

pertĭcātus.opening: adj. id. , furnished with or carrying a staff , Mart. 5, 12, 1 .

pertĭmĕfăcĭo.opening: v. a. pertimeo-facio , to put in great fear , to frighten greatly : pertimefactus maerore animi, Pac. ap. Non. 467, 33 (Trag. Rel. p. 96 Rib.): te pertimefacto, Brut. ap. Cic. Fam. 11, 20, 2 .

per-tĭmĕo.opening: v. n. , to fear greatly , to be very timid , Lact. 6, 17, 17 : non pertimentes ullam perturbationem, Vulg. 1 Pet. 3, 6 (al. praetim).

per-tĭmesco.opening: v. inch. a. and , to become very much frightened , to be greatly afraid of any thing, to fear greatly : si tantam religionem non pertimescebas, etc., Cic. Verr. 2, 4, 35, § 78 : id vero non mediocriter pertimesco, id.…

pertĭnācĭa.opening: pertinax , perseverance , constancy , in a good sense; and (more freq.) in a bad sense, obstinacy , pertinacity (syn.: perseverantia, pervicacia): dicitur quom demonstratur in quo non debet pertendi et pertendit,…

per-tĭnax.opening: adj. tenax , that holds fast , that clings firmly , very tenacious. Lit. (only poet. and in post-Aug. prose): digitus male pertinax, Hor. C. 1, 9, 24 : ales unguibus pertinax, App. Flor. p. 366 : tenaxne pater ejus est?…

per-tĭnĕo.opening: v. n. teneo , to stretch out , reach , extend to a place; to arrive at a place (class., esp. in the trop. signif.); constr. with ad and acc. , or with advv.; very rarely with in or per and acc.; v. infra . Lit. : aspera…

per-tingo.opening: v. a. tango , to stretch out , reach , extend to a certain point (rare; not in Cic.; often confounded in MSS. with pertineo). Lit. : collis in immensum pertingens, Sall. J. 48, 3 Dietsch and Kritz: montis Apennini jugum…

per-tŏlĕro.opening: v. a. , to bear out , endure : tormenta aetatis, Lucr. 5, 316 : pertolerarem vitam, Att. Trag. Rel. v. 91 Rib.

per-tŏno.opening: v. n. and a. , to thunder violently (late Lat.).— Trop. : contra aliquem, to thunder away at any one, Hier. Ep. 53 , n. 8: quando vero vox illa pertonuit, id. adv. Helv. 20 .— Act. , to proclaim aloud , thunder forth ,…

per-torquĕo.opening: v. a. , to twist awry , to distort : ora foedo sapore, Lucr. 2, 401 .— To hurl , vent : quam senticosa verba pertorquet, Afran. ap. Fest. p. 339 Müll. and ap. Paul. ex Fest. p. 333 ib. (Com. Rel. v. 1 Rib.).

pertractātĭo.opening: and , , pertracto, a touching; hence trop. , A handling : partium aegrarum, Gell. 5, 1, 4 .— A handling , i. e. an occupying or busying one's self with any thing, application to any thing: poëtarum, Cic. de Or. 1, 42,…

pertractātor.opening: a handler (late Lat.), Aug. c. Faust. 3, 2.

per-tracto.opening: ( ), , v. a. , to touch , feel , handle any thing (class.). Lit. : papillam, Plaut. As. 1, 3, 71 : mullos, Cic. Par. 5, 2, 38 : bestias manibus, Auct. B. afr. 72: arma, Plin. 25, 6, 30, § 66 : caput dormienti, Just. 1,…

per-trăho.opening: v. a. , to draw or drag , to bring or conduct forcibly to a place (not in Cic. or Cæs.). Lit. : aliquem in castra, Liv. 7, 39 : ratem ad ripam, id. 21, 28 : pertractus ad Vitellium, Tac. H. 2, 72 : mulierem Romam ad…

per-transĕo.opening: v. n. , to go or pass through (post-Aug.). Lit. : cum viridis aspectus (smaragdi), non pertransit, Plin. 37, 5, 18, § 68 : terram, Vulg. Gen. 12, 6 et saep.— Transf. To go or pass by (late Lat.; not in Sen. Ep. 4, 3 ),…

per-trĕmisco.opening: v. inch. a. , to tremble greatly at , to be in great fear of (late Lat.); with acc. : manum domini, Hier. in Isa. 4, 10, 4 ; 3, 7, 2 : similem sententiam, Hier. cont. Pelag. 1, 38.

per-trĕpĭdus.opening: adj. , in great alarm or in great haste : senatus pertrepidus in aedem Concordiae concurrit, Capitol. Maxim. et Balb. 1, 1 dub. (Peter, praetrepidus).

per-trĭbŭo.opening: v. a. , to give : testimonium alicui (al. retribuere), Plin. Ep. 10, 18, 2 (but ap. Plin. Pan. 95 the correct read. is perhibere).

per-trīcōsus.opening: adj. , very confused or perplexed , very strange : res pertricosa, Mart. 3, 63, 14 dub. (al. praetricosa).

per-tristis.opening: adj. , very sad or mournful. Lit. : carmen, Cic. poët. Div. 1, 8, 14.— Transf. , very austere or morose : patruus, Cic. Cael. 11, 25 .

pertrītus.opening: Part. , rubbed to pieces; from pertero.

per-trītus.opening: adj. , quite worn out , very hackneyed or common , very trite (post-Aug.): quaestio, Sen. Contr. 7, 18, 7 : scio pertritum jam hoc esse, Sen. Ep. 63, 10 .

per-trux.opening: adj. , very savage or terrible : bestiae, App. M. 5, p. 166, 22 .

per-tŭmesco.opening: v. inch. n. , to swell up greatly , Not. Tir. p. 115 .

per-tŭmĭdus.opening: adj. , greatly swelled out : luna (Elm. protumida), App. de Deo Socr. init.

per-tŭmultŭōsē.opening: adv. , in a very agitated or tumultuous manner : aliquid nunciare, Cic. Fam. 15, 4, 3 .

Pertunda.opening: pertundo , the goddess that presides over the loss of virginity , Arn. 4, 131 ; Tert. ad Nat. 2, 11 ; Aug. Civ. Dei , 6, 9.

per-tundo.opening: (tussum; pertunsus, Aur. Vict. Epit. 9, 10 ), , v. a. , to beat , push , or thrust through , to make a hole through , to bore through , perforate (mostly ante-class.; not in Cic. or Cæs.): latus pertudit hasta, Enn. ap.…

perturbātē.opening: adv. , v. perturbo, P. a. fin.

perturbātĭo.opening: perturbo , confusion , disorder , disturbance. Lit. : caeli (opp. serenitas), Cic. Div. 2, 45, 94 : hostium, Vulg. 2 Macc. 13, 16 .— Trop. In gen., political disturbance , disorder , revolution : quid est enim aliud…

perturbātor.opening: id. , a disquieter , troubler , disturber (eccl. Lat. for turbator, cf. turbo): ecclesiarum, Sulp. Sev. Hist. Sacr. 2, 49 ; Ambros. Spirit. Sanc. 3, 17, 121 .

perturbātrix.opening: perturbator , she that disquiets or disturbs , Cic. Leg. 1, 13, 39 .

perturbātus.opening: Part. and P. a. , from perturbo.

per-turbĭdus.opening: adj. , very unquiet , full of disturbance : civitas, Vop. Saturn. 7 .

per-turbo.opening: v. a. , to throw into confusion or disorder , to confuse , disturb (cf.: confundo, misceo). Lit. : omnia, Ter. And. 3, 4, 22 : provinciam, Cic. Sull. 20, 56 : aetatum ordinem, id. Brut. 62, 223 : condiciones…

per-turpis.opening: adj. , very shameful , scandalous , abominable , Cic. Cael. 20, 50

pertūsĭo.opening: pertundo , a perforation (late Lat.), Ps. Soran. Quu. Medic. 230.

pertūsūra.opening: id. , a thrusting or boring through , perforation , Cael. Aur. Tard. 5, 1, 18 .

pertūsus.opening: Part. and P. a. , from pertundo.

pērŭla.opening: dim. pera , a little wallet , a pocket. Lit. : Diogenes fregit exemptum e perulā calicem, Sen. Ep. 90, 11 .— Transf. , comic., = uterus intumescens, App. M. 5, p. 165, 18 .

pĕrunctĭo.opening: perungo , a besmearing , anointing , Plin. 24, 15, 80, § 131 al.

pĕr-ungo.opening: or , , v. a. , to besmear , anoint (class.): corpora oleo, Cic. Tusc. 1, 47, 113 : ora manu, Ov. A. A. 3, 756 : vulnera, Plin. 29, 4, 28, § 90 ; id. 28, 9, 37, § 141 : nardo perunctus, Hor. Epod. 5, 59 : faecibus ora…

pĕr-ūnītus.opening: adj. , united (eccl. Lat.), Primas in Ep. ad Cor. 15.

pĕr-urbānus.opening: adj. , very polite , pleasant , or witty. Lit. : L. Torquatus elegans in dicendo, toto genere perurbanus, Cic. Brut. 68, 239 : C. Lucilius et doctus et perurbanus, id. de Or. 1, 16, 72 .— Transf. , with a bad accessory…

pĕr-urgĕo.opening: v. a. To press upon greatly , to oppress , distress : cum Aureolus perurgeret Illyrium, Treb. Gall. 5; Amm. 29, 1, 18 : eum, Vulg. 1 Macc. 9, 7 .— In gen., to press or urge greatly : aliquem ad capessendam rem publicam,…

pĕr-ūro.opening: v. a. , to burn through and through; hence, Lit. To burn up , consume : perussit ignis multa, Lucr. 5, 396 : perusti late agri, Liv. 24, 20 : vas, Plin. 34, 17, 49, § 165 .—Esp., to be burned or scorched by the sun:…

Pĕrŭsĭa.opening: one of the twelve confederate towns of Etruria , the mod. Perugia , Liv. 9, 37, 12 ; Suet. Aug. 14 ; Vell. 2, 74, 3 ; Flor. 4, 5, 3 .—Hence, , , adj. , Perusian : Perusina cohors, Liv. 23, 17 : contentio, i. e. the…

pĕr-ūtĭlis.opening: adj. , very useful : opera, Cic. Att. 9, 17, 2 .

per-vādo.grammar: si, sum, 3 v. a. and n.
per-vādo.opening: v. a. and n. , to go or come through , to pass or press through , to spread through (class.; syn. penetro). Lit. , constr. with acc. alone, or with per , ad , or in , and absol. : pervade polum, Att. ap. Varr. L. L. 7,…

pervăgābĭlis.opening: adj. pervagor , ranging or sweeping through (post-class.): cymbulae, Sid. Ep. 2, 2 .

pervăgātus.opening: Part. and P. a. , from pervagor.

per-văgor.opening: v. dep. n. and a. , to wander or range through , to rove about , overrun (class.). Lit. : hic praedonum naviculae pervagatae sunt, Cic. Verr. 2, 5, 37, § 98 : iis imperat, ut omnibus in locis pervagentur, Caes. B. G. 7,…

per-văgus.opening: adj. , wandering or roaming all about : puer, Ov. A. A. 2, 18 ; Sabin. Ep. 1, 91.

per-vălĕo.opening: , a false read. for pervolat, Lucr. 6, 916 Lachm. ad h. l.)

per-vălĭdus.opening: adj. , very strong. agmina, Amm. 29, 1, 2 : contritio, profound, Vulg. Isa. 30, 14 .

per-văpōro.opening: v. a. , to steam , fill with vapor : solium, Petr. 73, 5 Keller (Bücheler, parabatur).

per-vărĭus.opening: adj. , very various : utilitates, App. de Deo Socrat. p. 42 dub.— Adv. : , very variously : pervarie narrantur, Cic. de Or. 2, 80, 327 .

pervāsĭo.opening: pervado , an invad ing , invasion (late Lat.): rerum alienarum pervasio, Salv. Gub. Dei , 5, 10.

pervāsor.opening: id. , an invader (late Lat.), Cassiod. Var. 4, 20 ; Cod. Th. 2, 4, 5.

per-vasto.opening: v. a. , to lay waste , devastate : fines, Liv. 6, 4 : pervastatis passim agris, id. 8, 19 : pervastata Italia, Tac. A. 15, 45 : Boii Laevos cum pervastassent, Liv. 33, 37, 6 .

pervectĭo.opening: perveho , a conveying , carrying through , Cod. Th. 11, 1, 13.

pervector.opening: id. , a bringer , conveyer (late Lat.): apicum, a letter-carrier, Symm. Ep. 4, 65 .

per-vĕho.opening: v. a. , to bear , carry , or convey through. Lit. : commeatus, Liv 44, 6, 6.—Mid.: pervehi, to pass through , traverse : Oceanum pervehitur, Tac. A. 2, 8 : volucri litora classe, Sil. 4, 51 .— Transf. , to carry , bring…

per-vello.opening: v. a. , to pull or pluck hard; to pull , iwitch any thing. Lit. : nates, Plaut. Pers. 5, 2, 66 : aurem, Phaedr. 5, 5, 32 ; also, prov., aurem, to pull one's ear , i. e. to remind one of a thing, Sen. Ben. 5, 7, 5 ; Val.…

per-vĕnĭo.opening: (old fut. pervenibunt, Pompon. ap. Non. 508, 6 ; pres. subj. pervenat, Plaut. Rud. 3, 2, 12 ; inf. pres. pass. pervenirier, Ter. Phorm. 4, 3, 35 ), v. n. , to come to , arrive at , reach a place. Lit. : quotumo die…

per-vēnor.opening: v. dep. a. , to hunt through; transf., to run through or about : urbem totam pervenarier, Plaut. Merc. 4, 5, 3 (v. 818 Ritschl).

perventĭo.opening: pervenio , an arrival (late Lat.), Mart. Cap. 4, § 406 ; Aug. Conf. 6, 1 .

perventor.opening: id. , a comer , arriver (post-class.), Sid. Ep. 3, 13 ; Aug. Cons. Evang. 2, 20 .

per-vĕnustus.opening: adj. , very comely (post-class.): homo, Sid. Ep. 3, 13 .

perversē.opening: ( ), adv. , v. perverto, P. a. fin.

perversĭo.opening: perverto , a turning about , inversion; a wresting , perversion , Auct. Her. 4, 32, 44 ; Tert. adv. Marc. 4, 5 .

perversĭtas.opening: perversus , frowardness , untowardness , perversity : quae est autem in hominibus tanta perversitas, ut, etc., Cic. Or. 9, 31 : opinionum, id. Tusc. 3, 1, 2 : magna perversitas, id. Off. 1, 40, 145 : alicujus, id. Q.…

perversus.opening: ( ), , Part. and P. a. , from perverto.

per-verto.opening: ( ), , v. a. , to turn around or about , to overturn , overthrow , throw down (class.). Lit. : pinus proceras pervortunt, Enn. ap. Macr. S. 6, 2 (Ann. v. 196 Vahl.): (coqui) aulas pervortunt, Plaut. Cas. 4, 1, 16 :…

per-vespĕrī.opening: adv. , very late in the evening : ad aliquem venire, Cic. Fam. 9, 2, 1 .

pervestīgātĭo.opening: pervestigo , a searching into , examining , investigation : scientiae, Cic. de Or. 1, 3, 9 .

pervestīgātor.opening: id. , a searcher , investigator : divinae bibliothecae, Hier. Vir. Illustr. 81 .

per-vestīgo.opening: v. a. , to trace out , search out. Lit. , of hounds; hence of spies: canes venaticos diceres, ita omnia odorabantur et pervestigabant, ut, etc., Cic. Verr. 2, 4, 13, § 31 .— Trop. , to seek out , examine , investigate :…

per-vĕtus.opening: adj. , very old : signum ligneum, Cic. Verr. 2, 4, 3, § 7 : oppidum, id. ib. 2, 4, 33 , § 72: amicitia, id. Fam. 13, 17 : epistula sed sero allata, id. Q. Fr. 3, 1, 4, § 14 : vinum non pervetus, Cels. 5, 26, 30 .

per-vĕtustus.opening: adj. , very old : verba, Cic. de Or. 3, 52, 201 : vocabulum, Varr. L. L. 6, 7, 59 .

pervĭam.opening: adv. per-via , accessible (cf. pervius; ante-class. and post-Aug.): angulos aedium perviam facitis, i. q. pervios, Plaut. Aul. 3, 2, 24 ; Front. Orat. 1 fin. Mai: divus Augustus reprehendens Ti. Claudium ita loquitur:…

per-vĭātĭcum.opening: money for a journey : perviaticum publice decretum, Front. ad Amic. 2, 6 Mai.

pervĭcācĭa.opening: pervicax , firmness , inflexibility; in a bad sense, stubbornness , obstinacy (syn.: pertinacia, perseverantia): avaritia, ambitio, mulierositas, pervicacia, Cic. Tusc. 4, 11, 26 : haec pervicacia tua et superbia coëgit…

pervĭcax.opening: adj. per and root vicof vinco , firm , determined; esp. in a bad sense, stubborn , obstinate , headstrong , wilful (not in Cic. or Cæs.): tu pertinaciam esse, Antiloche, hanc praedicas: Ego pervicaciam aio et eā me uti…

pervĭcus.opening: adj. pervico for pervinco , stubborn , obstinate (ante-class. collat. form of pervicax): pervico Ajax animo atque evocabili, Att. ap. Non. 487, 15 (Trag. Rel. p. 131 Rib.); Plaut. Fragm. ap. Non. 487, 15 .

pervĭdens.opening: Part. and P. a. , from pervideo.

pervĭdĕo.opening: v. a. , to look over , look on , overlook , survey. Lit. : sol pervidet omnia, Ov. M. 14, 375 .— Transf. , to look at or upon , to view : cunctaque mens oculis pervidet illa suis, Ov. P. 1, 8, 34 : cum tua pervideas…

per-vĭgĕo.opening: v. n. , to continue blooming , to bloom to the last : opibus atque honoribus perviguere, i. e. remained in constant possession of , etc., Tac. A. 4, 34 .

pervĭgĭl.opening: (collat. form : cura, App. M. 11, p. 270, 31 ), adj. , ever watchful ( poet. and in post-Aug. prose; cf. pernox): pervigil in mediae sidera noctis eras, Ov. Am. 1, 6, 44 ; id. M. 10, 369 : pervigilem draconem, id. ib.…

pervĭgĭlātĭo.opening: pervigil , a devotional watching , a vigil : nocturnae pervigilationes, Cic. Leg. 2, 15, 37 .

pervĭgĭlĭa.opening: id. , a watching all night long : pervigiliae malum, Just. 24, 8, 14 ; Mart. Cap. 1, § 37 ; cf. Charis. p. 43 P.

pervĭgĭlĭum.opening: id. , a watching all night , a remaining awake or sitting up all night long. In gen., Plin. 11, 53, 118, § 283 : pervigilio fatigati, Just. 13, 8, 6 : inter cotidiana pervigilia fessus, Sen. Ira, 3, 29, 1 .— In partic.,…

pervĭgĭlo.opening: v. n. , to remain awake or watch all night; to remain awake during , to watch through any period: continuas has tris noctis pervigilavi pessume, Plaut. Am. 1, 1, 158 ; id. Aul. 1, 1, 33 : vigilare leve est, pervigilare…

per-vīlis.opening: adj. , very cheap : annona, Liv. 31, 50 ; Paul. Nol. Carm. 18, 219 .

pervinco.grammar: vīci, victum, 3 v. n. and a.
pervinco.opening: v. n. and a. Lit. Neutr. , to conquer completely , gain a complete victory : pervicit Bardanes, Tac. A. 11, 10 .— Act. , to conquer or defeat completely , gain a complete victory over : ne nos subdolā perfidiā…

Pervincus.opening: , i. e. Achiever , a Roman surname , Inscr. Grut. 16, 7 .

per-vĭo.opening: v. n. , to go on , proceed , Auct. Itin. Alex. M. 104 Mai.

per-vĭrens.opening: Part. [vireo], ever flourishing , ever green (post-class.), Paul. Nol. Carm. 7, 11 .

per-vĭrĭdis.opening: adj. , very green : campus, Mel. 2, 5, 7 : color, Plin. 6, 22, 24, § 87 ; Sol. 53, 21 ; Front. Aquaed. 7 (al. praeviridis).

per-vīso.opening: v. a. , to behold , contemplate : caelum, Manil. 4, 925 .

per-vīvo.opening: v. n. , to live on , survive to a certain time (ante-class.): pervixi usque adhuc, Att. ap. Non. 238, 2 (Trag. Rel. v. 417 Rib.): pervivo usque ad summam aetatem, Plaut. Capt. 3, 5, 84 .

pervĭus.opening: adj. per-via , that has a passage through; hence, Lit. , that may be passed through or crossed , affording a passage through , passable , pervious (class.): aedes, Ter. Ad. 5, 7, 14 : transitiones, thoroughfares,…

per-vŏlātĭcus.opening: adj. , flying about , unstable , volatile (post-class.): vis vaga et pervolatica, Tert. Anim. 46 .

pervŏlĭtantĭa.opening: pervolito , a flying around , circumvolation : mundi circa terram, Vitr. 9, 7 .

pervŏlĭto.opening: v. freq. n. [pervolo], to fly through or around , to flit about ( poet. ): per dissepta domorum, Lucr. 6, 952 ; 2, 346 : omnia loca, Verg. A. 8, 24 : tecta, Val. Fl. 4, 505 .— Transf. : iter, to traverse repeatedly,…

per-vŏlo.opening: v. n. , to wish greatly , to be very desirous (rare but class.): obtunso ore nunc pervelim progredire Senem, Plaut. Cas. 5, 1, 9 : scire ex te pervelim, Cic. Sull. 7, 23 : quem videre pervellem, id. Att. 11, 14, 3 :…

pervŏlūto.opening: v. freq. a. pervolvo , to roll over and over; hence, in partic., to turn over books, to look through , read : libros, Cic. Att. 5, 12, 2 : scriptores, id. de Or. 1, 34, 158 .

per-volvo.opening: v. a. , to roll or tumble about (syn. voluto). Lit. : aliquem in luto, Ter. And. 4, 4, 38 .—Mid., to roll one's self , to roll : in suo pervoluta sanguine, weltering, App. M. 8, p. 207, 22 .— Transf. , to turn over a…

pervulgātē.opening: adv. , v. pervulgo, P. a. fin.

pervulgātus.opening: Part. and P. a. , from pervulgo.

pervulgo.opening: or , , v. a. , to communicate to the people , to make publicly known , to publish , spread abroad (class.; cf. publico). Lit. In gen., Lucr. 5, 1162 : de re illustri et facile etiam in vulgus pervulgatā, Cic. Fin. 2, 5,…

pēs.opening: kindr. with Sanscr. pād, foot, from root pad, ire; Gr. ποδ-, ποῦς; Goth. fōt; old Germ. vuoz; Engl. foot , a foot of man or beast. Lit. : si pes condoluit, Cic. Tusc. 2, 22, 52 : calcei apti ad pedem, id. de Or. 1, 54,…

Pescennĭus.opening: name of a Roman gens. A friend of Cicero , Cic. Fam. 14, 4, 6 .—Esp., Pescennius Niger, a Roman emperor; hence, , , adj. , pertaining to the emperor Pescennius : reliquiae, Spart. Sev. 15, 4 : domus, id. Pesc. Nig. 12,…

pescia.grammar: in Saliari carmine Aelius Stilo dici ait capitia ex pellibus agninis facta, quod Graeci pelles vocent pesce neutro genere pluraliter

pesestas.opening: Fest. p. 210 Müll.; cf.: pesestas dicebatur pestilentia, Paul. ex Fest. p. 211 Müll.

pesnis.opening: , acc. to Fest. p. 205 Müll.; v. penna.

pesoluta.opening: an Egyptian plant used for making garlands , Plin. 21, 33, 108, § 184 .

pessārĭum.opening: 2. pessum , a pessary , Cael. Aur. Acut. 3, 18, 185 ; Theod. Prisc. 3, 5 .

pessĭmo.opening: v. a. pessimus , to make utterly bad , to spoil completely , to ruin (eccl. Lat.): plebem, Vulg. Ecclus. 36, 11 : te ipsum pessimabis, id. ib. 38, 22 .— Pass. : pessimabor, Vulg. Ecclus. 11, 26 .

Pessĭnūs.opening: and , , ( acc. masc. Pessinuntem, Cic. Har. Resp. 13, 28 ), = Πεσσινοῦς and Πεσινοῦς , a very ancient town in Galatia , on the borders of Phrygia Major , celebrated for its worship of Cybele; the modern Bala Hissar ,…

pessŭlus.opening: ( neutr. collat. form in plur. pessula, Paul. Nol. Carm. 18, 412 ) [ πάσσαλος ], a bolt (ante- and post-class.): occlude sis fores ambobus pessulis, Plaut. Aul. 1, 2, 25 : pessuli, heus pessuli, vos saluto, id. Curc. 1,…

pessum.opening: (collat. form , , , Plin. Val. 1, 5 fin. ; Theod. Prisc. 2, 5 ), = πεσσόν, πεσσός , in medic. lang., a pessary , App. Herb. 121 ; Theod. Prisc. 3, 5 (in Cels. 5, 21 , written as Greek).

pestĭbĭlis.opening: adj. pestis , pestilential , destructive , noxious (post-class.): fundus, Cod. Just. 4, 58, 4 .

pestĭfer.opening: (rarely, Cels. 2, 6 ) , , adj. pestis-fero . Bringing pestilence , pestilential : odor, Liv. 25, 26, 11 .— In gen., that brings destruction , destructive , baleful , noxious , pernicious , pestiferous (class.): res…

pestĭlens.opening: adj. pestis , pestilential , infected , unhealthy , unwholesome (class.). Lit. : loci (opp. salubres), Cic. Fat. 4, 7 : pestilens et gravis aspiratio, id. Div. 1, 57, 130 : Africus, Hor. C. 3, 23, 5 : aedes, Cic. Off.…

pestĭlentĭa.opening: pestilens , an infectious or contagious disease , a plague , pest , pestilence. Lit. (class.): Massilienses gravi pestilentiā conflictati, Caes. B. C. 2, 22 ; Cic. Off. 2, 5, 16 : pestilentia gravis incidit in urbem,…

pestĭlentĭārĭus.opening: adj. pestilentia , pestilential (eccl. Lat.): cathedra, Tert. Spect. 27 .

pestĭlentĭōsus.opening: adj. id. , pestilential , unhealthy (post-class.): locus, Dig. 43, 8, 2, § 29 .

pestĭlentus.opening: adj. pestis , pestilential , unhealthy (ante-class. for pestilens): loca, Laevius ap. Gell. 19, 7, 7 .

pestĭlis.opening: adj. id. , pestilential , un wholesome (eccl. Lat.): aurae, Arn. 1, 11 .

pestĭlĭtas.opening: pestilis , plague , pest , pestilence , for pestilentia ( poet. ), Lucr. 6, 1098 ; 1125 ; 1132 (the first verse also quoted by Non. 158, 2 ).

pestĭmus.opening: adj. pestis , plaguebringing , pestilential : λοιμοφόρος , pestimus, Gloss. Gr. Lat.

pestis.opening: perh. for perd-tis, from perdo , a deadly , esp. an infectious or contagious disease , a plague , pest , pestilence; also, a noxious atmosphere , unhealthy weather (class., but rare for pestilentia; cf. contagio, lues).…

plācātē.opening: adv. , v. placo, P. a. fin.

plācātōrĭus.opening: adj. id. , of or belonging to pacifying , appeasing , or propitiating; appeasing , placatory (post-class.): hostia, Tert. Patient. 13 .

plăcentĭa.opening: placeo , suavity , courteousness (post-class.), App. Dogm. Plat. 2, p. 15, 33 .

plăcĭbĭlis.opening: adj. placeo , that can please , pleasing (post-class.), Tert. Resurr. Carn. 43 .

plăcĭdĭtas.opening: placidus , mildness , gentleness of nature or disposition , placidity (very rare): oves assumptas propter placiditatem, Varr. R. R. 2, 1 ; Auct. ap. Gell. 13, 22, 19 .

plăcĭdŭlus.opening: adj. dim. [id.], gentle , quiet , still (post-class.): cinis placidula, Aus. Parent. 27 .

plāga.opening: cf. plango , = πληγή , a blow , stroke , wound , stripe (class.; syn.: ictus, verbera, vulnus). Lit. In gen., Cic. Verr. 2, 5, 51, § 134 : (pueris) dant animos plagae, Verg. A. 7, 382 ; Ov. M. 12, 487 ; 13, 119 ; Gell.…

plăgĭaules.opening: , = πλαγιαύλης , a player on the cross-flute : plagiaules, monaules, axaules, Not. Tir. p. 173 .

planca.opening: root πλακ-; v. 2. plaga , = πλάξ , a board , slab , plank (post-Aug.): plancae tabulae planae, Paul. ex Fest. p. 231 Müll.: roboreae, Pall. 1, 21, 2 .— A slab of marble , slab upon graves, Inscr. Don. 278, 3 ; Inscr.…

plătўphyllon.opening: , = πλατύφυλλον (broad-leaf), a broad-leaved species of the plant tithymalus, Plin. 26, 8, 44, § 70 .
