pŏdēres.opening: or , , , = ποδήρης , a long garment descending to the ankle , worn by the priests , Tert. adv. Jud. 11 ; cf. Isid. Orig. 19, 21 : in veste poderis quam habebat totus erat orbis, Vulg. Sap. 18, 24 .

pōdex.opening: perh. for pordex, from pedo, ere , the fundament , anus , Hor. Epod. 8, 6 : lēvis, Juv. 2, 12 .

pŏdĭa.opening: a rope fastened to one of the lower corners of a sail , for the purpose of setting it to the wind; in Engl. nautical lang., a sheet , Serv. Verg. A. 5, 830 (al. podium).

pŏdĭārĭus.opening: podium , one who performs mimes on the stage , a mime , Not. Tir. p. 174 : podiarius, inter mimos, Gloss. Isid.

pŏdĭcus.opening: adj. ποῦς , of or belonging to a foot (post-class.): sed temporum alia simplicia sunt, quae podica etiam perhibentur. Pes veri est numeri prima progressio, Mart. Cap. 9, § 974 .

pŏdismātus.opening: adj. podismus , measured out by feet (post-class.): ager, Front. Colon. p. 132 Goes.

pŏdismus.opening: , = ποδισμός , a measuring out by feet , foot-measure (post-class.): ad podismum dimetiri loca, Veg. Mil. 2, 7 fin. ; 3, 15 ; Front. Colon. p. 130 Goes.; Inscr. Orell. 4570 .

pŏdĭum.opening: , = πόδιον , an elevated place , a height. In gen. (post-class.): podia ternis alta pedibus fabricantur, Pall. 1, 38 .— In partic. A projection in a building, a jutty , balcony , podium (postAug.), Plin. Ep. 5, 6, 22 ;…

Poeas.opening: ( ), , , = Ποίας , the father of Philoctetes , Ov. M. 9, 233 ; Sen. Herc. Oet. 1603 ; Hyg. Fab. 14 .—Hence, ( ), , , the son of Pœas , i. e. Philoctetes , Ov. M. 13, 313 . — ( ), , adj. , of or belonging to Pœas ,…

Poecĭle.opening: , = Ποικίλη (variegated). The picture-gallery, a celebrated hall or portico in the market-place at Athens : in porticu, quae Poecile vocatur, Nep. Milt. 6, 3 ; cf. Plin. 35, 9, 35, § 59 .— A gallery in the Athenian…

Poeēessa.opening: or , , , = Ποιήεσσα . An ancient name of the island of Rhodes , Plin. 5, 31, 36, § 132 .— An ancient town of Cea , Plin. 4, 12, 20, § 62 .

pŏēma.opening: ( gen. plur. poëmatorum, Afran. ap. Non. 493, 9 ; cf. Charis. p. 114 P.: poëmatum, Suet. Gram. 23 ; Spart. Hadr. 14 ; dat. and abl. plur. usually poëmatis, Cic. Off. 3, 3, 15 ; Plaut. As. 1, 3, 22 ; Auct. Her. 4, 2, 3 ;…

pŏēmătĭum.opening: , = ποιημάτιον , a little or short poem (post-Aug.), Plin. Ep. 4, 14 ; so id. ib. 4, 27 ; Aus. Idyll. 7 .

Poemĕnis.opening: the name of a dog , Ov. M. 3, 215 ; Hyg. Fab. 181 .

poena.opening: Gr. ποινή, ἄποινα, quitmoney, fine; Lat. pūnio, poenitet , indemnification , compensation , satisfaction , expiation , punishment , penalty (cf. mulcta). Lit. : SI INIVRIAM FAXIT ALTERI VIGINTI QVINQVE AERIS POENAE…

poenālis.opening: adj. poena , of or belonging to punishment , penal (post-Aug.; esp. freq. in the jurists): opera, Plin. 18, 11, 29, § 112 : poenalis aquae dirisque genitae, in the infernal regions, id. 4, 8, 15, § 31 : ex lege poenali…

poenārĭus.opening: adj. id. , of or belonging to punishment , penal , criminal (post-Aug.): actiones, Quint. 4, 3, 9 ; 7, 4, 20 .

Poeni.opening: the Phœnicians , i. e. the Carthaginians (descended from the Phœnicians): Poeni stipendia pendunt, Enn. ap. Varr. L. L. 5, § 182 Müll. (Ann. v. 269 Vahl.); id. ap. Fest. p. 249 ib. (Ann. v. 278 Vahl.); Cic. Rep. 2, 4, 9…

poenĭtens.opening: Part. and P. a. , from poeniteo.

poenĭtenter.opening: adv. , v. , P. a. A. fin.

poenŏsus.opening: adj. poena , painful (eccl. Lat.), Ps.-Aug. ad Fratr. Erem. Serm. 48 .

Poenŭlus.opening: dim. Poeni , The Young Carthaginian , the title of a comedy of Plautus.

pŏēsis.opening: (pŏĕsis, Prud. ap. Symm. 2, 52 ), , , = ποίησις . The art of composing poems , poetry , poesy (rarely so used), Quint. 12, 11, 26 .— A poem , poetry (class.): ut pictura, poësis erit: quae, si propius stes, Te capiat…

pŏēta.opening: (POETES, Inscr. Orell. 1163 ), , = ποιητής . In gen., a maker , producer (ante-class.): nec fallaciam Astutiorem ullus fecit poëta, a contriver, trickster, Plaut. Cas. 5, 1, 7 : tu poëta es prorsus ad eam rem unicus,…

Poetelĭus.opening: name of a Roman gens: M. Petelius, a consul, Liv. 9, 24 .

pŏētĭcus.opening: adj. , = ποιητικός , poetic , poetical : verbum, Cic. de Or. 3, 38, 153 : non poëtico sed quodam oratorio numero et modo, id. ib. 1, 33, 151 : di, represented by the poets, id. N. D. 3, 31, 151 : quadrigae, id. Q. Fr.…

pŏētilla.opening: , a false read. for post illum, Plaut. Truc. 2, 6, 4 .

pŏētor.opening: v. dep. poëta , to be a poet , to write poetry , to poetize (ante- and postclass.): numquam poëtor nisi si podager, Enn. ap. Prisc. p. 829 P. (Sat. v. 8 Vahl.): ineptia poëtandi, Aus. Idyll. 6 praef. —In an active…

pŏētrĭa.opening: , = ποιήτρια , a poetess : fabularum poëtria, Cic. Cael. 27, 64 ; Ov. H. 15, 183 ; Mart. Cap. 8, § 809 .

pŏētris.opening: , = ποιητρίς , a poetess , Pers. prol. 13 (al. poëtrias).

pōgōnĭas.opening: , = πωγωνίας (bearded), a kind of comet , Sen. Q. N. 1, 15, 4 ; Plin. 2, 25, 22, § 89 .

Pola.opening: a maritime town of Istria , Mel. 2, 3 ; Plin. 3, 19, 23, § 129 .

pōlĕa.opening: , = πωλίον , the dung of an ass's foal , Plin. 28, 13, 57, § 200 .

Pŏlĕmo.opening: or , , , = Πολέμων . A Grecian philosopher at Athens , a disciple of Xenocrates and teacher of Zeno and Arcesilaus , Cic. Ac. 1, 9, 34 ; id. de Or. 3, 18, 67 ; id. Fin. 4, 6, 14 ; Hor. S. 2, 3, 254 ; Val. Max. 6, 9, 1…

pŏlĕmōnĭa.opening: , = πολεμώνιον , Greek valerian , otherwise called philaeteria, Plin. 25, 6, 28, § 64 .

pŏlenta.opening: (collat. form , , , Cael. Aur. Tard. 3, 2 ; so plur. : , , Macr. S. 7, 15 ) [perh. from πάλη = pollen], peeled barley , pearl-barley : homines, qui polentam pinsitant, Plaut. As. 1, 1, 17 ; Cato, R. R. 168 ; Col. 6, 17,…

pŏlentārĭus.opening: adj. polenta , of or belonging to pearl-barley : crepitus, caused by eating pearl-barley, Plaut. Curc. 2, 3, 16 : damnum, the loss of a mouthful of pearl-barley, App. M. 6, p. 181, 2 .

pŏlĭa.opening: , = πολιά , a precious stone of a gray color , otherwise unknown, Plin. 37, 11, 73, § 191 .

pōlīa.opening: , = πωλεία , a stud of horses , Dig. 21, 1, 38 fin.

pŏlīmen.opening: 1. polio . Polish , brightness (post-class.). baltei polimina, App. de Deo Socr. p. 54, 30 .— , , , the testicles , Arn. 7, 230 .

pŏlīmenta.opening: id. , the testicles : porcina, Plaut. Men. 1, 3, 28 (dub.; Ritschl, sincipitamenta); cf. Fest. p. 234 Müll.

polindrum.opening: , a false read. for cepolindrum, Plaut. Ps. 3, 2, 43 ; v. Ritschl ad h. l.

Pōlio.opening: ( ), , , the name of a music-teacher , Juv. 7, 176 .

pŏlĭon.opening: or , , , = πόλιον , a strong-smelling plant , perh. the poley-germander : Teucrium polium, Linn.; Plin. 21, 7, 21, § 44 ; 21, 20, 84, § 145 ; Scrib. Comp. 83 .

Pŏlĭorcētes.opening: , = Πολιορκητής (the besieger or stormer of cities), a surname of Demetrius , king of Macedonia (cf.: Demetrius expugnator), Plin. 7, 38, 39, § 126 ; Sen. Ep. 9, 15 ; Vitr. 10, 22 ; Amm. 23, 4, 10 ; 24, 2, 18 .

pŏlītē.opening: adv. , v. 1. polio, P. a. fin.

Pŏlītes.opening: , = Πολίτης , a son of Priam , killed by Pyrrhus , Verg. A. 2, 526 ; 5, 564 .

pŏlītīa.opening: , = πολιτεία . The State , the name of one of Plato's works , Cic. Div. 1, 29, 60 ; 2, 27, 59 .— The administration of the Commonwealth (late Lat.), Ambros. Hexaëm. 5, 15, 52; Cassiod. Var. 9, 2 .

pŏlītĭcus.opening: adj. , = πολιτικός , of or belonging to civil polity or to the State , political , civil : libri, Cael. ap. Cic. Fam. 8, 1, 5 : philosophi, Cic. de Or. 3, 28, 109 : virtutes, Macr. Somn. Scip. 1, 8 .

pŏlītĭo.opening: 1. polio , a smoothing , a furbishing , polishing. Lit. (post-Aug.): speculi, Vitr. 7, 3 .—Of smoothing or plastering a wall, Vitr. 7, 4 .— Transf. , an improving , cultivating : agrorum, Cato, R. R. 136 .

pŏlītor.opening: id. , one who furbishes or polishes , a polisher. Lit. : gemmarum, Firm. Math. 4, 7 fin. — Transf. , a cultivator , improver : agri, Cato, R. R. 5, 136 ; Dig. 17, 2, 52 .

Politorĭum.opening: a town of Latium , the modern La Giostra , Liv. 1, 33 ; Plin. 3, 5, 9, § 68 .

pŏlītūra.opening: 1. polio , a furbishing , polishing , smoothing , working at , etc. (postAug.): chartae, Plin. 13, 12, 25, § 81 : marmoris, id. 36, 6, 9, § 53 : gemmarum (of the vine), id. 17, 26, 39, § 246 : laevitas et politura…

pŏlītus.opening: Part. and P. a. , from polio.

Polla.opening: another form for Paulla, Paula , a female proper name. The wife of D. Brutus , Cic. Fam. 11, 8, 1 .— The wife of the poet Lucan , Stat. S. 2, 7, 62 ; 82 ; Mart. 7, 21, 2 ; 7, 23, 3 ; 10, 64, 1 .

pollen.opening: , and , , and f [ πάλη ]. Lit. , fine flour , milldust , Cato, R. R. 156 ; 157 ; Plin. 13, 12, 26, § 82 ; 18, 9, 20, § 87 ; Ter. Ad. 5, 3, 60 .— Transf. , fine dust of other things: piperis, Cels. 4, 4 : turis, Col. 6,…

pollens.opening: Part. and P. a. , from polleo.

pollenter.opening: adv. , v. polleo, P. a. fin.

pollentĭa.opening: polleo , might , power (ante-class.): impiorum, Plaut. Rud. 3, 2, 4 ; id. Cas. 4, 4, 3 .—Personified, the goddess of power or of victory , Liv. 39, 7, 8 .

Pollentĭa.opening: ( ), , A city in Picenum , now Monte Moline , Cic. Phil. 11, 6, 14 ; id. Fam. 11, 13, 3 .—Hence, , , , the Pollentians , Plin. 3, 13, 18, § 111 .— A city in Liguria , now Pollenza , Col. 7, 2, 4 ; Mart. 14, 157 ; Sil.…

pollĕo.opening: (polet, pollet: quia nondum geminabant antiqui consonantes, Fest. p. 205 Müll.), , v. n. potis-valeo . Lit. In gen., to be strong , powerful , or potent , to be able , to prevail , avail (class.; cf.: valeo, possum):…

pollex.opening: polleo; cf.: pollex nomen ab eo, quod pollet, accepit, Atei. Cap'to ap. Macr. S. 7, 13, 11 . Lit. The thumb : hominis digiti articulos habent ternos, pollex binos et digitis adversus universis flectitur, per se vero in…

Pollex.opening: the name of a slave of Cicero , Cic. Fam. 14, 6, 1 ; id. Att. 8, 5, 1 ; 13, 47, 1 .—A lusus verbb. with 1. pollex, Cic. Att. 13, 46, 1 .

Pollĭa trĭbus.opening: one of the Roman tribes , Liv. 8, 37 ; 29, 37 ; Inscr. Grut. 400, 1 .

pollĭcāris.opening: adj. 1. pollex , of or belonging to a thumb (post-Aug.): frutex pollicari crassitudine, of the thickness of a thumb, Plin. 13, 23, 45, § 128 : latitudine, id. 15, 24, 26, § 95 : amplitudine, id. 27, 9, 49, § 73 .

pollĭcĕor.opening: ( act. form polliceres, Varr. Sat. Menip. 8, 5 ), 2, v. dep. a. and from an old prep. por or port (= Gr. πορτί, προτί, or πρός; cf. pro) and liceor . To hold forth , offer , promise any thing (freq. and class.; syn.:…

pollĭcĭtātĭo.opening: pollicitor , a promising , a promise (class. but not in Cic., who uses promissio, promissum; usu. plur. ): vereor ne istaec pollicitatio Te in crimen populo ponat, Plaut. Trin. 3, 3, 10 : hinc pollicitationes aufer,…

pollĭcĭtātor.opening: id. , a promiser (eccl. Lat.), Tert. adv. Jud. 1 .

pollĭcĭtātrix.opening: pollicitator , she that promises (eccl. Lat.), Tert. Apol. 23 .

pollĭcĭtor.grammar: ātus, 1 v. freq. a. and n.
pollĭcĭtor.opening: v. freq. a. and n. polliceor , to promise (mostly ante- and post-class.; not in Cic. or Cæs.): pro capite argentum, Plaut. Rud. 4, 2, 24 : operam suam alicui, id. Mil. 3, 3, 6 ; Dig. 50, 12, 6 . — Absol. : ego te…

pollĭnāris.opening: adj. pollen , of or belonging to fine flour , flour- , meal- : pollinare cribrum, γυριστήριον κόσκινον , Gloss. Cyril.; v. pollinarius.

pollĭnārĭus.opening: adj. id. , of or belonging to fine flour , flour- , meal- : cribrum, a bolting-sieve, Plaut. Poen. 3, 1, 10 ; Plin. 18, 11, 28, § 108 .

pollinctor.opening: (or ), , pollingo , one who washes corpses and prepares them for burning , an undertaker : pollinctores sunt, qui mortuos curant, Non. 157, 20 ; cf.: pollinctores dicti sunt, qui funera morientium accurant, Fulg. p.…

pollingo.opening: v. a. , to wash a corpse , and prepare it for the funeral pile (ante- and post-class.): pollingo, περιστέλλω νεκρόν, σιροπλόκω, ταριχεύω, ἐνταφιάζω , Gloss. Philox.: quia mihi pollinctor dixit, qui eum pollinxerat,…

pollĭo.opening: , īre: pollit, pila ludit, Paul. ex Fest. p. 243 Müll.

Pollĭo.opening: ( , v. Lucr. p. 33 Lachm.), , , a Roman surname. So esp., Asinius Pollio, v. Asinius.— Trebellius Pollio, v. Trebellius.— The name of a bad actor , Plaut. Bacch. 2, 2, 37 . — v. Polio.

pollūbrum.opening: ( ), , polluo , a wash-basin , laver : polubrum pelluvium vas, quod nos pelvem vocamus, Paul. ex Fest. p. 247 Müll.: polubrum quod Graeci χέρνιβα , nos trulleum vocamus. Livius: argenteo polubro (acc. to Hom. Od. 1,…

pollūcĕo.opening: v. a. old prep. port = Gr. προτί, πρός, and liceor; root licof linquo; Gr. λειπω; cf. licet . Lit. , in relig. lang., to place upon the altar as a sacrifice to the deity , to offer , offer up : Jovi dapali culignam vini…

pollūcĭbĭlis.opening: adj. polluceo, bountifully distributed; hence, in gen. , sumptuous , rich , magnificent (post-class.): cena, Macr. S. 2, 13 fin. : victus, Symm. Ep. 6, 71 . — Comp. : obsonandi pollucibilior, Tert. Jejun. 17 .— Adv. : ,…

polluctūra.opening: polluceo , a sumptuous entertainment , a feast , banquet , Plaut. Stich. 5, 4, 6 .

pollŭo.opening: v. a. cf.: adluo, diluo; Gr. λούω, to wash; λῦμα, λύμη, λυμαίνω, to cleanse, ruin , to soil , defile , pollute. Lit. (very rare): ore dapes, Verg. A. 3, 234 : ora cruore, Ov. M. 15, 98 : pollui cuncta sanie, odore,…

pollūtĭo.opening: polluo , defilement , contamination , pollution , Pall. 9, 10 : peccati, Vulg. Judith, 13, 20 .

pollūtrix.opening: id. , a polluter (late Lat.), Jul. ap. Aug. c. Sec. Resp. Jul. 6, 5.

Pollux.opening: (collat. form of nom. , Plaut. Bacch. 4, 8, 53 ; cf. Varr. L. L. 5, § 73 Müll.— Voc. pol, edepol, v. infra ), , = Πολυδεύκης , a famous pugilist , son of Tyndarus and Leda , and brother of Castor , in connection with…

pŏlōsē.opening: adv. polus , going through the poles (post-class.): obliqua decussata polose, Mart. Cap. 1, § 37 (al. oblique decussatos polos).

pōlŭlus.opening: ( ), , adj. a rustic form for paululus , little (only in the two foll. pass.): labellum, Cato, R. R. 10, 2 : sublaminae, id. ib. 21, 3 .

pŏlus.opening: , = πόλος . Lit. , the end of an axis , a pole ( poet. and postAug.): terra a verticibus duobus, quos appellaverunt polos, centrum caeli est, nec non Signiferi oblique inter eos siti, Plin. 2, 15, 13, § 63 ; 2, 70, 71,…

Pŏlus.opening: a celebrated Greek tragic actor , Gell. 7, 5, 2 .

Polusca.opening: a small and very ancient town in Latium , Liv. 2, 33 ; 39 ; cf. Mann. Ital. 1, p. 645.

pŏlўăcanthos.opening: , = πολυάκανθος , a kind of thistle , Plin. 21, 16, 56, § 94 .

Pŏlўaegos.opening: , = Πολύαιγος , an island of the Ægean Sea , Mel. 2, 7 ; Plin. 4, 12, 23, § 70 .

Pŏlўaenus.opening: , = Πολύαινος , a mathematician , a friend and follower of Epicurus , Cic. Fin. 1, 6, 20 ; id. Ac. 2, 33, 106 .

pŏlўandrĭon.opening: , = πολυάνδριον , a common burial-place , graveyard , cemetery , Lact. Epit. 72, 17 ; Arn. 6, p. 194 .

pŏlўanthĕmum.opening: , = πολυάνθεμον (pure Lat. ranunculus), a caustic plant , otherwise called batrachion (perh. Ranunculus polyanthemos, Linn., many-flowered , crowfoot ), Plin. 27, 12, 90, § 112 .

pŏlўarchĭon.opening: ( ), , , = πολυαρχίον , a kind of soothing ointment , Cael. Aur. Acut. 2, 24, 136 .

Polўbē.opening: one of the fifty daughters of Danaüs , Hyg. Fab. 170 .

Pŏlўbĭus.opening: , = Πολύβιος , a celebrated Greek historian from Megalopolis , in Arcadia , the son of Lycortas and friend of the younger Scipio Africanus , Cic. Rep. 1, 21, 34 ; 2, 14, 27 ; 4, 3, 3 ; id. Off. 3, 32, 113 ; Liv. 30, 45 .

Pŏlўbus.opening: , = Πόλυβος . A king of Corinth , at whose court Œdipus was brought up , Stat. Th. 1, 64 ; Hyg. Fab. 66 ; 67 ; Sen. Oedip. 12 .— One of Penelope's suitors , Ov. H. 1, 91 .

pŏlўcarpos.opening: , = πολύκαρπος , a plant , also called polygonus, App. Herb. 18 .

pŏlychrŏnĭus.opening: adj. , = πολυχρόνιος , long-lived (late Lat.), Firm. Math. 8, 28 med.

Pŏlўclītus.opening: ( , ) (ĕ scanned short, Prud. στεφ . 10, 269), , , = Πολύκλειτος , a celebrated Grecian sculptor from Argos or Sicyon , contemporary with Pericles. —Form Polyclitus, Plin. 34, 8, 19 § 55; Cic. Brut. 18, 70 ; 86, 296 ;…

pŏlycnēmon.opening: , = πολύκνημον , a plant , otherwise unknown, Plin. 26, 14, 88, § 148 .

Pŏlycrătes.opening: , = Πολυκράτης , a prince of Samos , and friend of Amasis , celebrated for his good fortune , but at last crucified by the Persian governor Orœtes , Cic. Fin. 5, 30, 92 ; Val. Max. 6, 9, 5 ext. — Gr. acc. in -en, Quint.…

Pŏlycrătĭa.opening: wife of the Achœan chief Aratus , Liv. 27, 31 .

Pŏlўdaemon.opening: a descendant of Semiramis , slain by Perseus , Ov. M. 5, 85 .

Pō^lўdămas.opening: (the o made long by the requirements of the verse), , , = Πολυδάμας . A Trojan , son of Panthous and friend of Hector , Ov. M. 12, 547 ; id. H. 5, 94 .—Hence, , , adj. , of or belonging to Polydamas : arma, Sil. 12, 212…

Pŏlўdectes.opening: or , , , = Πολυδέκτης , a king of Seriphus , who brought up Perseus , Ov. M. 5, 242 ; Hyg. Fab. 273 ; id. Astr. 2, 12 .

Pŏlўdector.opening: one of the fifty sons of Ægyptus , Hyg. Fab. 170 .

Pŏlўdōrus.opening: , = Πολύδωρος , a son of Priam and Hecuba , killed by the Thracian Polymnestor , Cic. poët. de Or. 3, 58, 219; Verg. A. 3, 45 Serv.; Ov. M. 13, 432 sq. —Hence, , , adj. , of Polydorus , Polydorean : sanguis, Ov. M. 13,…

Pŏlygnōtus.opening: , = Πολύγνωτος , a celebrated Grecian painter and statuary of Thasus , contemporary with Socrates , Plin. 35, 6, 25 ; Cic. Brut. 18, 70 .

pŏlўgŏnăton.opening: , = πολυγόνατον . The plant called Solomon's seal : Convallaria polygonatum (Linn.), Plin. 27, 12, 91, § 113 .— Another name for leucacantha, Plin. 22, 17, 18, § 40 .

pŏlygōnĭus.opening: adj. , = πολυγώνιος , having many angles , polygonal : turres, Vitr. 1, 5 .

pŏlўgŏnŏīdes.opening: , = πολυγονοειδής , a species of the plant clematis, Plin. 24, 15, 90, § 141 .

pŏlўgŏnos.opening: or , , , or , ( , , Scrib. Comp. 193 ), , = πολύγονος or -ον , a plant (called in pure Lat. herba sanguinalis or sanguinaria), knotgrass , Plin. 27, 12, 91, § 113 ; 26, 15, 90, § 158 .

pŏlўgōnum.opening: , = πολύγωνον , a polygon , Censor. de Die Nat. 8 med.

pŏlygrammos.opening: , = πολύγραμμος , a sort of jasper , with many white streaks , Plin. 37, 9, 37, § 118 .

pŏlўgўnaecon.grammar: i, a false reading for syngenicon
pŏlўgўnaecon.opening: Plin. 35, 11, 40, § 134 ; v. Sillig ad h. l.

Pŏlўhistor.opening: , = Πολυίστωρ (the much-knowing or learned man). The title of the natural history written by C. Julius Solinus. — A surname of the grammarian Cornelius Alexander , Suet. Gram. 20 ; Plin. 9, 35, 56, § 115 .

Pŏlўhymnĭa.opening: ( , Poët. ap. Anth. Lat. 1, p. 51 Burm.), , , = Πολυμνία (she of many hymns), one of the Muses , Hor. C. 1, 1, 33 ; Ov. F. 5, 9 ; Mart. 4, 31, 7 ; Aus. Idyll. 20 .

Pŏlўĭdus.opening: , = Πολύϊδος , a soothsayer , native of Corinth , Cic. Div. 1, 40, 89 ; id. Leg. 2, 13, 33 .

Pŏlўmăchaerŏplăgĭdes.opening: πολύσ-μάχαιρα-plaga , a fictitious name of a soldier , Plaut. Ps. 4, 2, 31 .

pŏlўmĭtārĭus.opening: polymitus , of damask , highly wrought or finished : opus, Vulg. Exod. 36, 35 .—Hence, subst. : , , , a damask-weaver , Ven. Carm. 5, 6 praef.; Vulg. Exod. 35, 35 ; 38, 23 .

pŏlўmĭtus.opening: adj. , = πολύμιτος , wrought with many treads : alicula, Petr. 40 : ars, the art of weaving, Hier. Ep. 64, 12 : tunica, Vulg. Gen. 37, 3 .— Subst. : , , , damask , Plin. 8, 48, 74, § 198 ; also sing. , , Vulg. Ezech.…

praecantātrix.grammar: īcis, a false reading for praecantrix
praecantātrix.opening: , q. v., Plaut. Mil. 3, 1, 99 ; Aug. in Psa. 127, 11 .

prae-canto.opening: , no perf. , , v. a. To foretell , prophesy (ante-class.), Lucil. ap. Non. 102, 9 .— To enchant , bewitch (postAug.), Petr. 131 (for Cic. Fin. 2, 29, 94 , v. praecento.

praecantor.opening: praecano , an enchanter (late Lat.), Aug. in Psa. 127, 11 .

praecantrix.opening: praecantor , an enchantress , sorceress (ante-class.), Plaut. Mil. 3, 1, 99 (v. Ritschl ad h. l.); Varr. ap. Non. 494, 27 .

prae-cānus.opening: adj. , gray before one's time : corporis exigui, praecanum, Hor. Ep. 1, 20, 24 (ante tempus canum, Schol. Cruqu.).

prae-cătēchīzātus.opening: Part. [catechizo], previously instructed (eccl. Lat.): praecatechizatus a prophetis, Vulg. Interpr. Iren. 4 .

praecautĭo.opening: praecaveo , precaution (post-class.): passionis avertendae praecautio, Cael. Aur. Acut. 1, 15 .

prae-căvĕo.grammar: cāvi, cautum, 2 v. a. and n.
prae-căvĕo.opening: v. a. and n. , to guard against beforehand. Act. , to guard against , seek to avert , obviate , or prevent (class.; syn. provideo): illud praecavendum est mihi, Plaut. Men. 5, 2, 107 : peccata, quae difficillime…

prae-cēdo.grammar: cessi, cessum, 3 v. a. and n.
prae-cēdo.opening: v. a. and n. , to go before , precede (seems not to occur in Cic., Nep., Tac., or Sall.; once in Cæs.; syn.: antecedo, anteverto). Act. , to go before , precede a person or thing. Lit. ( poet. and in post-Aug. prose):…

prae-cĕler.opening: adj. , very swift or quick (post-Aug.): viri cursu praeceleres, Stat. Th. 6, 550 : vis, Plin. 9, 46, 70, § 153 : fuga, id. 8, 23, 35, § 86 .

prae-cĕlĕro.opening: v. a. and n. , to hasten before or in advance ( poet. ). Act. : ducem, Stat. Th. 4, 798 .— Neutr. : calle latenti, Stat. Th. 2, 497 .

prae-cellens.opening: Part. and P. a. , from praecello.

praecellentĭa.opening: praecellens , excellence (eccl. Lat.): praecellentia divinitatis, Tert. Apol. 23 .

prae-cello.opening: (collat. form, acc. to the 2d conj.; pres. praecellet, Plaut. Ps. 2, 3, 13 ; perh. originally written praecellit), v. a. and n. , to rise above others. Act. , to surpass , excel any one (post-Aug.; syn. antecello):…

prae-celsus.opening: adj. , very high or lofty (class.; poet. and late Lat.; cf.: arduus, sublimis, excelsus). Lit. : rupes, Verg. A. 3, 245 ; Sulp. Sev. Chron. 2, 15, 9 .— Trop. : Fortuna, Stat. S. 3, 3, 85 .— Comp. , Ambros. Fid. 4, 1, 7…

praecentĭo.opening: praecino , a singing or playing before a sacrifice, a battle, etc., a prelude , Cic. Har. Resp. 10, 21 : tran quilla, Gell. 1, 11, 4 .

praecento.opening: prae-canto , to sing before , to offer consolation in song : huic Epicurus praecentet, si potest, cum, etc., Cic. Fin. 2, 29, 94 B. and K.; v. Madv. ad loc.

praecentor.opening: praecino , a leader in music, precentor (post-class.): praecentor in choris, App. Mund. p. 74, 3 ; cf.: praecentor qui vocem praemittit (opp. succentor), Aug. Enarr. in Psa. 87 ; cf. Isid. 7, 12, 27 .

praecentōrĭus.opening: adj. praecentor , of or belonging to a prelude (postclass.): harundines, Sol. 5, 19 .

praeceps.opening: (old form , , Plaut. Rud. 3, 3, 8 ; id. et Enn. ap. Prisc. p. 725 P. (Ann. v. 391 Vahl.; abl. praecipiti), adj. prae-caput . Lit. , headforemost , headlong (class.): praecipitem trahi, Plaut. Ps. 1, 5, 79 : aliquem…

praeceptĭo.opening: praecipio . A taking beforehand , a receiving in advance (jurid. Lat.): per praeceptionem legamus, Ulp. Reg. 24, 2 : dotis, Dig. 23, 4, 26 : per praeceptionem legare, Gai. Inst. 2, 192 ; 216 ; Paul. Sent. 3, 6, 1 .— The…

praeceptīvus.opening: adj. praecipio , preceptive , didactic (post-Aug.): pars philosophiae, quam Graeci παραινετικήν vocant, nos praeceptivam dicimus, Sen. Ep. 95, 1 : portemus praeceptivo modo dicens, in the preceptive, hortatory mode,…

praecepto.opening: v. freq. a. id. , to prescribe often : praeceptat, in Saliari carmine est saepe praecipit, Fest. p. 205 Müll.

praeceptor.opening: id. . One who seizes beforehand , an anticipator (postclass.): servilium praeceptor operum (al. praereptor, al. praecerptor), Paul. Nol. Ep. 23 , n. 4.— A commander , ruler (postclass.), Gell. 1, 13, 8 .— A teacher ,…

praeceptrix.opening: praeceptor , a preceptress (class.): sapientiā praeceptrice, Cic. Fin. 1, 13, 43 : praeceptrix et magistra, Vitr. 10, 1 .

prae-cerpo.opening: ( , Oppius ap. Macr. S. 2, 15 ), , v. a. carpo . To pluck , break off , or gather before , or before the time ( poet. and in post-Aug. prose): messes, Ov. H. 20, 143 : germinum tenera, Plin. 18, 19, 49, § 177 : mala…

prae-certātĭo.opening: , a false read. for par certatio, Auct. Her. 4, 30, 41 .

praecessor.opening: praecedo . A predecessor (eccl. Lat.): alicujus, Tert. adv. Prax. 1 ; Hier. in Ruf. 3 , n. 20.— A superior in rank , Vulg. Luc. 22, 26 .

Praecĭānus.opening: adj. : vinum, a celebrated kind of wine, Plin. 14, 6, 8, § 60 (Praetetianus, Jahn): Praecianum pirum, Macr. S. 2, 15 .

praecīdānĕus.opening: adj. praecaedo . Lit. , that is slaughtered or sacrificed before (ante and post-class.): porca praecidanea, the preliminary sacrifice of a sow, Cato, R. R. 134 : quod humatus non sit, heredi porca praecidanea…

praecīdārĭus.opening: adj. , for praecidaneus, Mar. Vict. p. 2470 P.

prae-cīdo.opening: (old form , Quadrig. ap. Gell. 9, 13, 18 ), , v. a. caedo , to cut off in front; hence, in gen., to cut off. Lit. (class.); constr. with acc. alone, or with acc. and dat. or gen. of person. With acc. and dat. : linguam…

praecinctĭo.opening: praecingo , lit., a girding about , a girdle : zonae, Hilar. in Matt. 2, 2.—Hence, Transf. , the broad landing-place or lobby around the amphitheatre , or between each tier of seats , Vitr. 5, 3 ; 2, 8 .

praecinctōrĭum.opening: id. , a girdle , apron (eccl. Lat.): fecerunt praecinctoria de foliis fici, Aug. Genes. cont. Manich. 2, 2.

praecinctūra.opening: id. , a girding , girdle , Macr. S. 2, 3 ; Vitr. 10, 21 Schneid. N. cr.

praecinctus.opening: praecingo , a girding. Lit. (ante-class.): castula est palliolum praecinctui, Varr. ap. Non. 548, 30 .— Transf. , in gen., a dressing , dress (post-class.): in praecinctu ponens omnem decorem, Macr. S. 2, 9 .

prae-cingo.opening: v. a. , to gird about , to gird. Lit. : cincticulo praecinctus in sellā aput magistrum adsidere, Plaut. Bacch. 3, 3, 26 : det tunicam locuples: ego te praecingere possum, Mart. 14, 153, 1 : ilia cultro, Grat. Cyn. 341…

prae-cĭno.grammar: cĭnŭi centum, 3 v. n. and a.
prae-cĭno.opening: (e. g. praecinuit, Plin. 2, 12, 9, § 54 ), , v. n. and a. [cano]. Neutr. , to sing or play before (class.): et deorum pulvinaribus et epulis magistratuum fides praecinunt, Cic. Tusc. 4, 2, 4 : praecinere sibi tibias…

prae-cĭpĭo.opening: v. a. capio , to take or seize beforehand , to get or receive in advance (class., esp. in the trop. sense; syn.: anticipo, praeoccupo). Lit. In gen., Lucr. 6, 1050 : nisi aquam praecepimus ante, id. 6, 804 : a…

praecĭpĭtantĭa.opening: praecipito , a falling headlong , a rapid fall (post-class.), Gell. 6, 2, 11 ; 9, 1, 5 .

praecĭpĭtātĭo.opening: id. , a falling headlong , headlong hurry , inconsiderate haste (post-Aug.), Vitr. 5, 12 ; Sen. Ira, 1, 12, 6 ; App. de Mundo, p. 61, 20; Vulg. Psa. 51, 6 .

praecĭpĭtātor.opening: id. , a destroyer , overthrower (late Lat.), Aug. c. Duas Epp. Pelag. 1, 4.

praecĭpĭtĭum.opening: praecipito . Lit. , a steep place , an abrupt descent , a precipice (post-Aug.): in praecipitium propellere, Suet. Aug. 79 ; Vulg. Judith, 7, 8 .— Trop. : aut per confragosa vexabitur aut per praecipitia labetur, Lact.…

praecĭpĭto.grammar: āvi, ātum, 1 v. a. and n.
praecĭpĭto.opening: v. a. and n. praeceps , to throw or cast down headlong , to precipitate (class.; syn.. deicio, deturbo, proruo). Act. Lit. : pilae in mare praecipitatae, Nep. Alcib. 6 fin. : truncas rupes in tecta domosque, Stat. Th.…

praecĭpŭus.opening: adj. praecipio , that is taken before other things (cf. princeps): excipuum quod excipitur, ut praecipuum, quod ante capitur, Paul. ex Fest. p. 80 Müll.—Hence, Particular , peculiar , especial (class.; opp. communis),…

praecīsē.opening: adv. , v. praecido, P. a. fin.

praecīsĭo.opening: praecido . A cutting off (post - Aug.): genitalium, App. M. 1, p. 106, 12 .— Transf. , concr., the piece cut off , a cut , cutting : tignorum, Vitr. 4, 2 ; absol. , id. 5, 7 .— In rhetoric, a breaking off abruptly , =…

praecīsūra.opening: praecido , a cutting , cut , paring (post - class.): asparagorum, Apic. 4, 2 : agrorum, Front. Colon. p. 102 ; 126 ; 140 Goes.

praecīsus.opening: Part. and P. a. , from praecido.

prae-clāmo.opening: v. n. , to call out beforehand (post-class.), Dig. 48, 8, 7 (al. proclamaverit): proclamat, praeclamat, Not. Tir. p. 93 .

prae-clārĕo.opening: v. n. , to shine forth (late Lat.), Alcim. Avit. ad Soror. 6, 508 .

prae-clārus.opening: adj. , very clear , very bright. Lit. (only poet. and very rare): lux, Lucr. 2, 1032 : sol, id. 5, 120 : iaspis, Juv. 5, 42 .— Transf. , very beautiful (physically or morally), magnificent , honorable , splendid , noble…

praeclāvĭum.opening: prae-clavus , the part of the dress before the purple stripe , Afran. ap. Non. 64, 22 sq.

prae-clūdo.opening: v. a. claudo , to shut in front, hence, in gen., to shut to , to close (class.). Lit. : portas praeclusit, Caes. B. C. 2, 19 fin. : praecludere portas consuli, id. ib. 3, 12 : fores, Prop. 2, 4 (5), 21: portus classi,…

prae-clŭĕo.opening: v. n. , to be very famous or renowned (post-class.): qui in vetustā praecluent comoediā, Ter. Maur. p. 2433 P.: praecluens potestas, Prud. Cath. 4, 37 .—In the collat. form , , v. n. : vos, qui ex ubertate terrae…

praeclŭis.opening: adj. prae-cluo, clueo , very celebrated (post-class.): liberi, Mart. Cap. 1, § 3 ; 1, § 24 : conventus, id. 9, § 906 .

praeclūsĭo.opening: praecludo , a shuting or damming up , a reservoir (postAug.): aquarum, Vitr. 9, 9 med.

praeclūsor.opening: id. , one that shuts up; trop., a hinderer , precluder (postclass.): legis, who impedes an understanding of the law, Tert. adv. Marc. 4, 27 fin.

praeco.opening: (old dat , PRAECONEI, Inscr. Lat. 202, 2, 34), , a crier , herald , in a court of justice, in popular assemblies, at auctions, at public spectacles, games, or processions, etc.: exsurge, praeco, fac populo audientiam,…

prae-coepi.opening: v. a. , to begin before : urbem, Auct. Itin. Alex. M. 84 Mai.

praecōgĭtātĭo.opening: praecogito , a thinking or considering beforehand , forethought , precogitation (post-class.): praecogitationem, Tert. adv. Marc. 4, 39 .

prae-cōgĭto.opening: v. a. , to think upon , ponder , or consider beforehand , to premeditate , precogitate (perh. not anteAug.): plura, Quint. 12, 9, 20 : abscessum, Cod. Th. 8, 4, 20: multo ante praecogitatum facinus, Liv. 40, 4 fin. :…

praecognĭtĭo.opening: praecognosco , foreknowledge , precognition (late Lat.), Boëth. Consol. Phil. 5, 4; Ambros. de Fide, 3, 10, 64.

praecognĭtŏr.opening: id. , he who knows beforehand , Ambros. de Fide, 2, prol. 14.

prae-cognosco.opening: , no perf. , , v. a. , to foreknow , foresee (very rare): praecognito nostro adventu, Planc. ap. Cic. Fam. 10, 15, 4 : mors praecognita est, Suet. Aug. 97 : Christus praecognitus ante mundi constitutionem, Vulg. 1 Pet.…

prae-cŏlo.opening: , no perf. , , v. a. To cultivate beforehand , trop.: animi habitus, ad virtutem quasi praeculti et praeparati, Cic. Part. 23, 80 .— To honor , esteem , revere beforehand : nova et ancipitia (i. e. ante tempus…

prae-commŏdo.opening: v. a. , to advance as a loan , to give as a favor (post-class.): quingentos solidos, Cod. Th. 14, 27, 2: linguam, Coripp. Laud. Just. 1, 7 .

prae-commŏvĕo.opening: v. a. , to move greatly : liberos, Sen. Thyest. 302 .

prae-compŏsĭtus.opening: Part. [compono], composed or prepared beforehand : praecomposito ore, Ov. F. 6, 674 .

prae-concinnātus.opening: Part. [concinno], arranged or prepared beforehand (post-class.): praeconcinnato mendacio fallens maritum, App. M. 5, p. 170, 34 .

prae-condĭo.opening: v. a. , to season beforehand (post-class.): leporem, Apic. 8, 8 med.

prae-condĭtus.opening: Part [condo], prearranged (late Lat.): praeconditis causis, Aug. Gen. ad Lit. 6, 28 .

praecōnĭālis.opening: adj. praeconnius , to be praised or commended , that which ought to be honored : viri, Cassiod. Var. 9, 25 : pietati vestrae praeconiale est diligere, id. ib. 8, 1 .—Hence, adv. : , honorably , Cassiod. in Psa. 17 .

praecōnĭātĭo.opening: praeconium , high commendation (late Lat.), Interpr. Iren. 3, 3.

Praecōnīnus.opening: praeco , a Roman surname , Suet. Gram. 3 ; Plin. 33, 1, 7, § 29 .

praecōnĭus.opening: adj. praeco , of or belonging to a praeco or public crier : quaestus, the office or business of a public crier , Cic. Quint. 31, 95 .— Subst : , , The office of a public crier : facere, to be a public crier, Cic. Fam.…

praecōnor.opening: v. dep. n. [praeco], to perform the office of public crier or herald , to herald , proclaim; to praise (post-class.), Interpr. Iren. 5: fama praeconans, Mart. Cap. 1, § 63 ; Arn. in Psa. 92 and 97.

prae-conspĭcābĭlis.opening: adj. conspicor , very remarkable , wonderful (eccl. Lat.), Cassiod. in Psa. 96, 6 .

prae-consūmo.opening: , no perf. , , v. a. , to waste or spend beforehand (Ovid.): suas vires bello, Ov. M. 7, 489 ; id. Tr. 4, 6, 30 .

prae-con-trecto.opening: v. a. tracto , to feel or handle beforehand , i. e. in thought : praecontrectare videndo, Ov. M. 6, 478 .

prae-cŏquo.opening: v. a. To boil beforehand , Plin. 18, 29, 69, § 288 : rutam, Cael. Aur. Acut. 2, 34, 136 ; id. Tard. 4, 3, 26 .— To ripen fully : praecocta uva (sole), Plin. 14, 9, 11, § 81 .

praecordĭa.opening: ( sing. praecordium, Isid. 10, 102 ), prae - cor . Lit. , the muscle which separates the heart and lungs from the abdomen , the midriff , diaphragm : exta homini ab inferiore viscerum parte separantur membrana, quae…

prae-corrumpo.opening: , no perf. , , v. a. , to corrupt or bribe beforehand (Ovid.): aliquem donis, Ov. M. 14, 134 : illa praecorrupta, id. ib. 9, 295 .

praecox.opening: , also , , and , , adj. praecoquo , ripe before its time , early ripe , rareripe , premature , precocious (syn. praematurus). Lit. : allium praecox, Plin. 19, 6, 34, § 112 : rosa, id. 21, 4, 10, § 19 : germinationes,…

praecrĕpo.opening: v. n. , to sound or resound beforehand : in domo patris praecrepuisse symphoniam, Ambros. in Psa. 118, 11, 26 .

prae-crūdesco.opening: v. inch. n. , to grow very hard , Not. Tir. p. 81 .

prae-culco.opening: v. a. calco , to impress strongly or beforehand (post-class.), Tert. Monog. 10 .

praecultus.opening: Part. and P. a. , from praecolo.

prae-cŭpĭdus.opening: adj. , very desirous or fond of any thing: pretiosae supellectilis praecupidus, Suet. Aug. 70 .

prae-cūro.opening: v. a. , to care for beforehand (post-class.): corpus, Cael. Aur. Acut. 2, 37 : res suas, Tert. adv. Marc. 2, 29 fin.

prae-curro.grammar: cŭcurri cursum, 3 v. n. and a.
prae-curro.opening: (curri, Liv. 8, 30, 13 Weissenb.), , v. n. and a. , to run before , hasten on before , precede (class.; cf.: antecedo, antevenio). Neutr. Lit. : eā ego huc praecucurri gratiā, ne, etc., Plaut. Merc. 1, 2, 110 : propere…

praecursātor.opening: praecurro , an advanced guard (post-class. for praecursor): revocatis praecursatoribus, Amm. 16, 12, 8 .

praecursĭo.opening: id. , a coming or going before. * In gen.: sine praecursione visorum, without a previous occurrence of phenomena, Cic. Fat. 19, 44 .— In partic. * In milit. lang., a preliminary combat , a skirmish , Plin. Ep. 6, 13, 6…

praecursor.opening: id. , one who runs before. A forerunner , precursor , of a servant, Plin. Pan. 76 fin.; one who precedes on the same path , Lact. 6, 7, 3 .— Esp., the forerunner of Christ, John the Baptist, Aug. Tract. in Johan. 4, 6 ;…

praecursōrĭus.opening: adj. praecursor , precursory (post-Aug.): epistula, Plin. Ep. 4, 13, 2 : index, Amm. 15, 1, 2 (al. procursorius).

praecursus.opening: praecurro , a forerunning , coming before , anticipation (post - Aug.): Etesiarum, Plin. 16, 25, 42, § 104 : praecursu quodam gloriosae passionis, Ambros. in Luc. 5, 109 .

prae-cŭtĭo.opening: v. a. quatio , to shake , wave , or brandish before or in front ( poet. ): taedas, Ov. M. 4, 757 (but in Prop. 4, 15, 16 , the true reading is percutit).

praeda.opening: (old abl. sing. PRAEDAD. Inscr. Col. Rostr.), for praehenda, from praehendo, v. prehendo , property taken in war , booty , spoil , plunder , pillage (syn.: exuviae, spolium). Lit. : praedā exercitus undat, Enn. ap.…

praedābundus.opening: adj. praedor , ravaging , pillaging , plundering , Sall. J. 90, 2 : exercitus, Liv. 2, 26 ; Curt. 8, 1, 5 .

praedamnātĭo.opening: praedamno , precondemnation (eccl. Lat.), Tert. Habit. Mul. 4 ; id. Apol. 27 med.

prae-damno.opening: v. a. , to condemn beforehand , to precondemn (not in Cic. or Cæs.). Lit. : praedamnatus collega, Liv. 4, 41 fin. : amicum, Suet. Aug. 56 .— Trop. : spem, i. e. to give it up or renounce beforehand , Liv. 27, 18, 8 : se…

praedātīcĭus.opening: or , , adj. praedor , taken as booty or plunder (postclass.): pecunia, Gell. 13, 24, 28 (in Gell. 4, 18, 12 , the better reading is praedatae).

praedātĭo.opening: id. , a taking of booty , plundering , pillaging (post-Aug.).— In plur. : latrociniis ac praedationibus infestato mari, Vell. 2, 73, 3 ; Tac. A. 12, 29 . —In sing. , Lact. 5, 9 ; Vulg. Isa. 9, 5 .

praedātor.opening: id. , a plunderer , pillager. Lit. (class.): quos ego in eodem genere praedatorum direptorumque pono, Cic. Cat. 2, 9, 20 : exercitus, praedator ex sociis, Sall. J. 44, 1 .— Transf. A hunter ( poet. ): praedator aprorum,…

praedātōrĭus.opening: adj. praeda , plundering , rapacious , predatory : manus (militum), marauders, Sall. J. 20, 7 ; Tac. A. 4, 24 fin. : naves, pirate-ships, Plaut. Men. 2, 2, 69 ; Liv. 34, 36 : classes, id. 29, 28 .

praedātrix.opening: praedator , she that plunders , pillages , robs ( poet. and in post-class. prose): Herculei praedatrix cedat alumni, i. e. the nymph Dryope , who stole away Hylas, Stat. S. 1, 5, 22 .— Adj. : bestia, a beast of prey,…

prae-dătus.opening: Part. [do], given beforehand (post-class.), Cael. Aur. Acut. 2, 37 med. ; 3, 17 ; id. Tard. 1, 1 ; 2, 1 ; 3, 7 fin.

prae-dēcessor.opening: a predecessor (post-class.), Symm. Ep. 10, 47 ; Rutil. Nam. 1, 424 .

prae-dēlasso.opening: v. a. , to weary out or weaken beforehand : quae (moles) incursus praedelassat aquarum, Ov. M. 11, 731 .

prae-dēlēgātĭo.opening: an assignment or delegation before the time (postclass.), Cod. Just. 11, 5, 3 .

prae-dēmonstro.opening: v. a. , to demonstrate beforehand (late Lat.), Rustic. cont. Aceph. p. 1192.

prae-densus.opening: adj. , very thick , very dense (post-Aug.): farrago, Plin. 18, 16, 41, § 142 : grana, id. 18, 7, 10, § 53 : terra, id. 18, 18, 48, § 171 .

prae-dēsignātus.opening: Part. [designo], designated beforehand (post-class.): praedesignatus vobis Christus, Tert. Res. Carn. 22 fin.

praedestĭnātĭo.opening: praedestino , a determining beforehand , predestination (eccl. Lat.), Boëth. Consol. Phil. 4; in the title of a book by Augustin.: De praedestinatione Sanctorum, et saep.

prae-destĭno.opening: v. a. , to determine beforehand , to predestine (not ante-Aug.): triumphos, Liv. 45, 40 fin. : qui praedestinavit nos in adoptionem filiorum, Vulg. Eph. 1, 5 : nuptiarum gaudia sibi, Auct. Paneg. ad Max. et Constant. 7:…

prae-dētermĭno.opening: v. a. , to fix beforehand (late Lat.), Aug. Orat. p. 1126 , t. 47 Migne.

prae-dexter.opening: adj. , very skilful , Grat. Cyn. 67 (acc. to Barth, i. q. ambidexter, aequimanus).

praedĭātor.opening: praedium , a purchaser of mortgaged estates sold at auction , a dealer in landed estates , Cic. Att. 12, 14, 2 ; 12, 17 : qui mercatur a populo praediator appellatur, Gai. Inst. 2, 61 . Persons who followed this…

praedĭātōrĭus.opening: adj. praediator , relating to the sale of estates at auction , prediatory : jus, Cic. Balb. 20, 45 ; Val. Max. 3, 12, 1 : lex, Suet. Claud. 9 .

praedĭātūra.opening: praedium , the purchase of estates at auction , Gai. Inst. 2, 61 .

praedĭātus.opening: adj. id. . Possessing landed properly (post-class.): bene praediatus, App. Flor. p. 349, 40 .— In gen., wealthy : in omnibus praediatus, Mart. Cap. 1, § 46 .— Who pledges his lands to the State : praediatus ὑπὲρ φόρου…

praedĭcābĭlis.opening: adj. 1. praedico , praiseworthy , laudable : aliquid praedicabile, Cic. Tusc. 5, 17, 49 ; Ambros. in Luc. 1, 15 .

praedĭcāmentum.opening: id. , that which is predicated , a quality; in plur. = categoriae, Aug. Conf. 4, 6 ; id. Trin. 5, 8 ; Isid. 2, 16, 1 .

praedĭcātĭo.opening: id. . A public proclaiming , a proclamation , publication (class.) of the praeco, luctuosa et acerba praedicatio, Cic. Agr. 2, 18, 48 : mandata praedicatio, App. M. 6, p. 176, 10 : praedicatio societatis, Cic. Verr. 2,…

praedĭcātīvus.opening: adj. id. , declaring , asserting , predicative (post-class.): propositio, categorical, App. Dogm. Plat. 3, p. 29 fin. : syllogismus, Mart. Cap. 4, § 343 : genus, id. ib.

praedĭcātor.opening: 1. praedico . In gen., one who makes a thing publicly known , a proclaimer , publisher , crier (postclass.), App. M. 6, p. 176, 4 .— In partic. One who publicly commends a thing , a praiser , eulogist (class.):…

praedĭcātōrĭus.opening: adj. praedicator , praising , laudatory (late Lat.): verba, Salv. adv. Avar. 19 fin.

praedĭcātrix.opening: id. , she that makes known (post-class.): summarum potestatum, Tert. Anim. 46 .

prae-dĭco.opening: v. a. To cry in public , make known by crying in public , to publish , proclaim. Lit. , of a public crier: ut praeco praedicat, Plaut. Bacch. 4, 7, 17 : auctionem praedicem, ipse ut venditem, id. Stich. 1, 3, 41 ; cf.:…

prae-dīco.opening: v. a. , to say or mention before or beforehand , to premise. In gen. (mostly post-Aug.; cf. praefor), Ter. And. 4, 4, 54 : hoc primum in hac re praedico tibi, id. ib. 1, 1, 19 : Davus dudum praedixit mihi, id. ib. 5, 1,…

praedictĭo.opening: 2. praedico . A premising , in rhet., Quint. 9, 2, 17 .— A foretelling , prediction. —In sing. : praedictio mali, Cic. Div. 2, 25, 54 ; 2, 42, 87 sq. —In plur. : vatum, Cic. Div. 1, 2, 4 ; id. N. D. 2, 3, 7 ; Suet. Tib.…

praedictīvus.opening: adj. id. , foretelling , predictive; in medicine, prognosticating : item libro praedictivo, quem προρρητικόν appellavit (Hippocrates), Cael. Aur. Acut. 1, 12, 100 .

prae-diffĭcĭlis.opening: adj. , very difficult (post-class.), Tert. Bapt. 2 fin.

prae-dīgestus.opening: adj. digero , that has well digested : corpus, Cael. Aur. Tard. 5, 2, 41 .

praedĭŏlum.opening: dim. praedium , a small farm or estate , Cic. de Or. 3, 27, 108 ; id. Att. 16, 34 ; id. Fam. 2, 15 ; 2, 6, 7 ; Plin. Ep. 1, 24, 4 .

prae-dīrus.opening: adj. , very frightful , detestable (post-class.): facta dictu visuque praedira, Amm. 31, 8 : mulier, Poët. ap. Anth. Lat. 2, p. 329 Burm.

prae-disco.opening: v. a. , to learn beforehand , make one's self acquainted with beforehand (rare but class.): aliquid, Cic. de Or. 1, 32, 147 : ventos et varium caeli praediscere morem, Verg. G. 1, 51 : sic ut praediscere possimus, utrum…

prae-dispŏsĭtus.opening: Part. [dispono], prepared beforehand : nuntii, Liv. 40, 56 fin.

prae-dĭtus.opening: Part. [do]. Endowed , gifted , or provided with , possessed of something (above others) (freq. and class.; syn.: instructus, ornatus); constr. with abl. : legiones pulchris armis praeditas, Plaut. Am. 1, 1, 63 : divino…

praedĭum.opening: for prae-hendium, from praehendo, v. prehendo , a farm , estate , a manor (either in town or country): praedibus et praediis populo cautum est, Cic. Verr. 2, 1, 54, § 142 ; 2, 1, 55, § 143 : urbanum, id. ib. 2, 3, 86 ,…

prae-dīvĕs.opening: adj. , very rich , very plentiful (not in Cic. or Cæs.; opp. inops pecuniae), Liv. 45, 40 : praedives et praepotens, Tac. A. 15, 64 : Senecae praedivitis hortos, Juv. 10, 16 : Licinus, id. 14, 306 : praedivite cornu…

praedīvīnātĭo.opening: praedivino , a divining beforehand , presentiment , Plin. 8, 25, 37, § 89 .

prae-dīvīno.opening: v. a. , to have a presentiment of , to divine beforehand : qui futura praedivinando soleant fari, fatidici dicti, Varr. L. L. 6, § 52 Müll.; Plaut. Truc. 2, 3, 17 : apes praedivinant ventos imbresque, Plin. 11, 10, 10,…

prae-dīvīnus.opening: adj. , presaging , prophetic (post-Aug.): praedivina somnia, Plin. 37, 10, 60, § 167 ; Sol. 27, 46 .

praedo.opening: praeda , one that makes booty , a plunderer , robber (syn.: latro, raptor). Lit. : ita in aedibus sunt fures, praedo in proximo'st, Plaut. Ps. 3, 2, 105 : hostes sunt, quibus bellum publice populus Romanus decrevit, vel…

prae-dŏcĕo.opening: v. a. , to teach , instruct , inform beforehand (very rare): illi praedocti a duce arma mutaverant, Sall. J. 94, 1 : praedoctus esto, Plin. 18, 34, 77, § 334 : myrrheus Pulvis sepulcrum praedocet, points out, shows,…

prae-dŏmo.opening: v. a. , to tame or subdue beforehand : omnes casus praedomuit meditando, mastered or surmounted beforehand , Sen. Ep. 113, 22 .

praedōnŭlus.opening: id. , a little robber , petty robber , Cato ap. Fest. p. 242 Müll.

praedopĭont.opening: , Fest. p. 205 Müll. [praed-opio, ĕre, as the prim. form of opto; v. Fest. p. 204 , a, Müll.].

praedor.opening: (active collat. form, v. infra fin. ), v. n. and a. [2. praedo]. Neutr. , to make booty , to plunder , spoil , rob (in war and otherwise; class.; syn.: spolio, diripio): spes rapiendi atque praedandi, Cic. Phil. 4, 4, 9…

prae-dūco.opening: v. a. , to draw , make , or put before or in front (not in Cic.): fossam et maceriam, Caes. B. G. 7, 69 : fossas transversas viis, id. B. C. 1, 27 ; Tib. 4, 1, 83 : fossas muris, Sil. 10, 411 ; cf. Sen. Ira, 2, 8, 6 :…

praeductal.opening: praeduco , a pencil for drawing lines : praeductal, παράγραφος , Gloss. Philox.

praeductōrĭus.opening: adj. id. , of or for drawing forwards : lora, traces, Cato, R. R. 135, 5 .

prae-dulcis.opening: adj. Lit. , very sweet , luscious (perh. not ante-Aug.): mel, Plin. 13, 4, 9, § 44 : ficus, id. 15, 18, 19, § 72 : vina, id. 14, 6, 8, § 64 : sapor, id. 12, 5, 11, § 23 .—In plur. absol. : , , , over-sweet things ,…

prae-dūro.opening: v. a. Lit. , to make very hard , harden very much (postAug.): sucus praeduratus, Plin. 23, 7, 71, § 139 ; Apic. 6, 9 ; 7, 4 ; 8 .— Trop. , to harden , indurate , Prud. στεφ . 5, 177.

prae-dūrus.opening: adj. , very hard (not in Cic. or Cæs.). Lit. : faba praedura, Plin. 18, 12, 30, § 121 : radices, id. 26, 8, 29, § 46 : caput, id. 9, 29, 46, § 85 ; cf. Quint. 11, 3, 69 : corium, Tac. H. 1, 79 : dens, Mart. 13, 66 (al.…

prae-ēlĭgo.opening: v. a. , to choose rather , to prefer; with object-clause , Sid. Ep. 7, 4 .

prae-ēmĭnentĭa.opening: pre-eminence (post-class.): negotii, Claud. Mam. Stat. Anim. 1 praef.

prae-ēmĭnĕo.opening: ( ), , v. n. and a. , to project forwards , be prominent. Lit. (post-class.), Aug. Conf. 6, 9 ; Sall. H. Fragm. 2, 85 : praeeminentes oculi, Dig. 21, 1, 12 (al. eminentes).— Trop. , to surpass , excel (post-Aug. for…

prae-emptor.opening: emo , one who purchases before others , a pre-emptor : προαγοραστής , praeemptor, Gloss. Gr. Lat.

prae-ĕo.grammar: ĭi, ĭtum, īre v. n. and a.
prae-ĕo.opening: (sometimes written in inscrr. with one e, PRAERAT, etc.), īvi and , v. n. and a. , to go before , lead the way , precede (syn.: praegredior, antecedo). Lit. Neutr. : ut consulibus lictores praeirent, Cic. Rep. 2, 31, 55…

praeēsus.opening: Part. [prae-edo], eaten before , Not. Tir. p. 166 .

prae-exercĭtāmentum.opening: a previous or preparatory exercise (postclass.), as a transl. of the Gr. προγυμνάσματα , Prisc. p. 1329 P.

prae-făcĭlis.opening: adj. , very easy , Not. Tir. p. 51 .

praefandus.opening: P. a. of praefor, q. v.

prae-fătīgātus.opening: Part. , wearied beforehand : fatigatus (late Lat.), Cael. Aur. Tard. 3, 7, 84 .

praefātĭo.opening: praefor , a saying beforehand; concr., That which is said or repeated beforehand , a form of words (esp. relig. or jurid.), formula : praefatio donationis, Cic. Verr. 2, 3, 80, § 186 : sacrorum, Liv. 45, 5, 4 :…

praefātĭuncŭla.opening: dim. praefatio , a short preface or opening (late Lat.), Hier. Ep. 64 , n. 8; 112, n. 20.

praefātus.opening: praefor , a saying beforehand , a prediction (post-class.), Symm. Ep. 10, 22 .

praefectĭānus.opening: adj. praefectus , of or belonging to the prœtorian prefect (post-class.): apparitor, Amm. 17, 3, 6 ; also subst. : , , , Cod. Just. 12, 53, 2 ; 3 .

praefectĭo.opening: praeficio , a setting before : a praefectione praefica dicta, Varr. L. L. 7, § 70 Müll.

praefectōrĭus.opening: adj. praefectus , of or belonging to a prefect : vir, an ex-prefect, Dig. 1, 9, 1 ; also subst. : , , , Sid. Ep. 1, 11 .

praefectūra.opening: ( dat. plur. PRAEFECTVREIS, Inscr. Corp. Lat. 206, 83), id. , the office of a president or overseer , a presidency , superintendence , prefecture. In gen.: villae, Varr. R. R. 1, 17 fin. ; cf. Plaut. Cas. 1, 11 (infra,…

prae-fectus.opening: ( ), , Part. [facio], done beforehand (postclass.), Cael. Aur. Acut. 3, 17, 174 ; id. Tard. 2, 14, 218 ; 5, 4, 71 .

praefĕrĭcŭlum.opening: praefero , a broad brazen dish used at sacrifices : praefericulum vas aëneum sine ansā patens summum, velut pelvis, quo ad sacrificia utebantur, Paul. ex Fest. p. 248 Müll. (whether at the sacrifices in honor of Ops…

prae-fĕro.opening: v. a. , to bear before , to carry in front , to hold forth. Lit. In gen. (class.): dextrā ardentem facem praeferebat, Cic. Verr. 2, 4, 34, § 74 ; cf.: alicui facem ad libidinem, id. Cat. 1, 6, 13 : in fascibus insignia…

prae-fĕrox.opening: adj. , very fierce , bold , violent , impetuous , insolent (perh. not ante-Aug.): praeferoces legatos, Liv. 5, 36 ; Tac. A. 4, 60 : praeferocem ingenio, id. H. 4, 32 ; 4, 23 : multiplici successu praeferocem, Suet.…

prae-ferrātus.opening: adj. , tipped or shod with iron : modius, Cato, R. R. 11 : pilum, pointed with iron, Plin. 18, 10, 23, § 97 . — Transf. : praeferratus apud molas tribunus, i. e. chained, fettered, Plaut. Pers. 1, 1, 22 .

prae-fertĭlis.opening: adj. , very fruitful or fertile (post-class.): germen, Prud. adv Symm. 2, 1025 : terrae ubere, Alcim. 5, 119 .

prae-fervĭdus.opening: adj. , very hot , burning hot , torrid (in prose not anteAug.). Lit. : fulgor, Att. ap. Serv. ad Verg. A. 1, 42 (Trag. Rel. p. 188 Rib.): regio, Col. 3, 1, 3 : balneum, Tac. A. 14, 64 .— Trop. : ira, glowing, burning,…

praefestīnātim.opening: adv. praefestino , very hurriedly , in hot haste , very hastily : praefestinatim et cupide, Sisenn. ap. Non. 161, 29 .

prae-festīno.opening: v. a. To hasten before the time , to hasten too much (rare; not in Cic. or Cæs.): praefestinare praeloqui, Plaut. Rud. 1, 2, 31 : sciscere, quae sit causa, Afran. ap. Charis. p. 186 P. (Com. Rel. p. 182 Rib.): ne…

praefĭca.opening: praeficio , a woman hired to lament at the head of a funeral procession : praefica dicta, ut Aurelius scribit, mulier, ad luctum quae conduceretur, quae ante domum mortui laudes ejus caneret ... Claudius scribit: quae…

prae-fĭcĭo.opening: v. a. facio , to set over any thing (as officer, superintendent, leader, etc.), to place in authority over , place at the head , appoint to the command of. Lit. (freq. and class.; cf.: praepono, praefero): te cum securi…

prae-fīdens.opening: Part. [fido], trusting too much , over-confident (rare but class.): exsultantem te et praefidentem tibi Repriment legum habenae, self-confident , rash , Poët. ap. Cic. de Or. 3, 41, 166 ; so, homines sibi praefidentes,…

prae-fīgo.opening: v. a. , to fix or fasten before , to set up in front , to fix on the end or extremity of. Lit. (class., but not in Cic.): ripa erat acutis sudibus praefixis munita, Caes. B. G. 5, 18 ; so, praefigere aëneos cancellos…

praefĭgūrātĭo.opening: praefiguro , a prefiguration (late Lat.), Aug. Civ. Dei , 16, 2; Hier. Ep. 53, 8 : legis, Hilar. in Psa. 118, 3, 3.

praefĭgūrātor.opening: id. , one who prefigures (eccl. Lat.), Aug. Conj. Adult. 6 .

prae-fĭgūro.opening: v. a. , to prefigure (eccl. Lat.), Lact. 6, 20 ; Cypr. Ep. 2, 3 .

prae-fīnĭo.grammar: īvi and ĭi, ītum, 4 v. a.
prae-fīnĭo.opening: v. a. , to determine , fix , or appoint beforehand , to prescribe (class.; a favorite word with Cic.; syn.: praestituo, praescribo): praefinire non est meum, Cic. Tusc. 5, 8, 21 : aliquid restricte, id. Leg. 2, 18, 45 :…

prae-fīnītĭo.opening: praefinio , a determining or fixing beforehand , appointment , prescription (post-class.), Gai. Inst. 4, 51 ; Dig. 36, 2, 19 ; 20 : saeculorum, Vulg. Eph. 3, 11 ; Tert. Monag. 2 .

praefiscĭnē.opening: , and , adv. adverbial form from prae-fascinum; cf. Non. 153, 12; prop. in security against magic; cf. Corss. Ausspr. 1, 775 sq.; hence , meaning no evil , without offence , without vanity (mostly ante-class.): pol tu…

prae-flōrĕo.opening: v. n. , to flower or blossom before the time (post-Aug.), Plin. 16, 29, 51, § 119 .

prae-flōro.opening: v. a. flos , to deprive of its blossoms beforehand; only trop. To lessen , diminish , tarnish (very rare, and perh. not ante-Aug.): gloriam ejus victoriae praefloratam apud Thermopylas esse, Liv. 37, 58 fin. ; cf.:…

prae-flŭo.opening: v. n. and a. , to flow by or past (rare; perh. not ante-Aug.). Neutr. : infimā valle praefluit Tiberis, Liv. 1, 45, 6 : a latere urbis quod in orientem patet, id. 43, 31, 3 : vado incerto, Tac. A. 12, 33 : ita ut (aquae…

praeflŭus.opening: adj. praefluo , flowing by or past (post-Aug.): amnis, Plin. 19, 4, 20, § 60 .

praefōcābĭlis.opening: adj. praefoco , that has the power of choking , suffocating (postclass.): spiratio, Cael. Aur. Acut. 2, 35 : loca, id. ib. 37 : sensus, id. Tard. 3, 2 .

praefōcātĭo.opening: id. , a choking , suffocation (post-class.), Scrib. Comp. 100 ; Cael. Aur. Acut. 2, 6 .

prae-fōco.opening: v. a. faux , to choke , strangle , suffocate ( poet. and postclass. for suffoco): animae viam, Ov. Ib. 560 : partum, Dig. 25, 3, 4 : Jovem, Arn. 7 , 29: messis praefocata, Calp. Ecl. 4, 115 : ex abundantiā praefocari,…

prae-fŏdĭo.opening: v. a. To dig before or in front of : portas, Verg. A. 11, 473 (id est ante portas fossas faciunt, Serv.). — With respect to time, to dig or bury before : scrobes, to make pits beforehand, Plin. 17, 11, 16, § 79 : aurum,…

prae-fōmento.opening: v. a. , to warm or foment beforehand (post-class.): vulnera aquā gelidā, Theod. Prisc. 1, 19 med.

prae-for.opening: (old imper. praefato, Cato, R. R. 134 . 1: praefamino, id. ib. 141, 2 ; cf. Müll. ad Fest. p. 87, 10 ), v. dep. n. and a. In gen., to say or utter beforehand , to premise , preface : in parte operis mei licet mihi…

praeformātor.opening: praeformo , that forms or arranges beforehand (postclass.), Tert. Praescript. 30 .

prae-formīdo.opening: , no perf. , , v. a. , to fear beforehand (post-Aug.), Quint. 4, 5, 5 Zumpt N. cr. (al. perform-, al. reform-), Sil. 3, 608 .

prae-formo.opening: v. a. , to form or fashion beforehand , to instruct beforehand , to prepare , etc. (post-Aug.): his praeformat dictis, Sil. 7, 385 ; Tert. Apol. 1 fin. : velut praeformata materia, Quint. 2, 6, 5 : praeformatae…

prae-fortis.opening: adj. , very strong (postclass.; opp. infirmus), Tert. Carn. Chr. 5 med.

prae-fōtus.opening: Part. [foveo], warmed or fomented beforehand (postclass.): partes aquā marinā, Cael. Aur. Tard. 4, 2 .

praefractē.opening: adv. , v. praefringo, P. a. fin.

praefractus.opening: Part. and P. a. , from praefringo.

prae-frīgĭdus.opening: adj. , very cold : praefrigidus Auster, Ov. P. 4, 12, 35 : aqua vel tepida vel praefrigida, Cels. 2, 30 : unda, Just. 11, 8, 4 : situs, Plin. 17, 20, 34, § 147 .

prae-fringo.opening: v. a. frango , to break off before or at the end , to break to pieces , shiver (class.): ne caulis praefringatur, Cato, R. R. 33 (cited by Plin. 17, 22, 35, § 20 ): hastas, Liv. 8, 10 ; so, primam aciem telo, to break…

prae-fŭgĭo.opening: v. n. , to flee before (post-class.), Tert. Anim. 33 med.

prae-fulcĭo.opening: v. a. To prop up , support a thing. * Lit. : mollire praefultum torum, Prud. στεφ . 5, 335.— Trop. : primum illud praefulci atque praemuni, quaeso, ut simus annui, secure, Cic. Att. 5, 13, 3 : aliquid multis modis,…

prae-fulgĕo.opening: v. n. , to beam or shine forth , to shine greatly , to glitter before or in front of (rare before the Aug. per.). Lit. : nitor smaragdi collo praefulget tuo (sc. pavonis), Phaedr. 3, 18, 7 : equus praefulgens unguibus…

prae-fulgĭdus.opening: adj. , very bright : nubes caeli, Juvenc. in Matt. 3, 330, 18 .

prae-fulgŭro.opening: v. n. and a. , to flash forth ( poet. ). Neutr. : latus praefulgurat ense, Stat. Th. 7, 502 .— Act. : strictoque vias praefulgurat ense, fills with flashes of light, illuminates, Val. Fl. 3, 119 : aulam augustam cultu,…

prae-fundo.opening: v. a. , to pour out before or in addition to , to add by pouring (post-class.), Simplic. p. 87 Goes.: semine cucuminis praefuso, Cael. Aur. Tard. 5, 10, 124 .— To pour upon , to wet , sprinkle. Lit. : pileus vino Calido…

praefurnĭum.opening: prae-furnus . The opening of a furnace , the door by which fuel is admitted: si uno praefurnio coques, Cato, R. R. 38, 1 .— The heating-room , or hot anteroom of a bath, = προπνιγεῖον , Vitr. 5, 10, 2 ; 7, 10 .

prae-fŭro.opening: v. n. , to rage violently ( poet. ): torvus praefuris, Stat. Th. 2, 420 ; 4, 822 .

prae-fuscus.opening: adj. , very swarthy or black , Manil. 4, 721 dub.

prae-gaudĕo.opening: to rejoice greatly; with inf. : Pelopis sedes adire, Sil. 15, 307 .

prae-gĕlĭdus.opening: adj. , very cold : in locis praegelidis, Liv. 21, 54 : frigora, Col. 4, 8 : hiems, Plin. 9, 16, 24, § 57 : rivi, Sil. 4, 226 .

prae-gĕnĕrātus.opening: Part. [genero], generated before (late Lat.): Prosper Aquit. Epitaph. Haeres. Nestor. et Pelag. init.

prae-germĭno.opening: v. a. , to bud forth early : praeflorent talia et praegerminant, Plin. 16, 29, 51, § 119 .

prae-gĕro.opening: , no perf. , , v. a. To bear or carry before (post-class.): speculum, App. M. 4, p. 157, 5 .— To do before; only subst. : , , , things done before , former things : oblivio praegestorum, Cael. Aur. Tard. 1, 5 , n. 150.

prae-gestio.opening: v. n. , to desire greatly , to delight (rare but class.): videre, Cic. Cael. 28, 67 : apisci, Cat. 64, 145 : ludere, Hor. C. 2, 5, 9 .

prae-gigno.grammar: ĕre, a false reading for progigni

prae-glōrĭōsus.opening: adj. , very famous , very glorious (post-class.); sup ., Inscr. Orell. 1182 .

praegnans.opening: (collateral form , , Plaut. Truc. 1, 2, 95 ; 4, 3, 37 ; M. Aurel. ap. Front. Ep. ad Caes. 4, 6 Mai; Macr. S. 3, 11 fin. ; Plin. 17, 14, 24, § 105 et saep.), adj. prae- and root gna of gnascor (nascor); cf. gigno , with…

praegnātĭo.opening: praegnas , a getting with child or with young , a making pregnant; a being with child or with young , pregnancy (ante- and post-class.). Lit. , App. M. 1, p. 106, 21 .—Of animals, Varr. R. R. 2, 1 .— Transf. , of…

praegnātus.opening: id. , pregnancy (eccl. Lat.): juvenculae, Tert. adv. Jud. 9 ; id. adv. Marc. 3, 13 .

praegnax.opening: adj. praegnas , inclined to pregnancy : divitiae, Fulg. Myth. 2, 3 .

praegno.opening: v. n. , to be pregnant (late Lat.), Dracont. Carm. 10, 577 .—Hence, , Part. , pregnant , Fulg. Rusp. ad Trasim. 2, 1 .

prae-grăcĭlis.opening: adj. , very slender , very lank (post-Aug.): proceritas, Tac. A. 4, 57 .

praegrădo.opening: v. a. prae-gradus , to go before , precede , Pac. ap. Non. 65, 3 (Trag. Rel. p. 68 Rib.).

prae-grandis.opening: adj. , very large , huge , colossal (ante-class. and post-Aug.). Lit. : praegrandi gradu, Pac. ap. Fest. s. v. torvitas, p. 355 Müll. (Trag. Rel. p. 67 Rib.): arbores, Plin. 13, 25, 49, § 138 : aures, id. 4, 13, 27, §…

prae-grăvĭdus.opening: adj. , very heavy , ponderous ( poet. ): moles, Stat. Th. 6, 700 .

prae-grăvis.opening: adj. , very heavy (mostly poet. and in post-Aug. prose). Lit. : praegrave onus, Ov. H. 9, 98 : caput, Plin. 8, 21, 32, § 77 : unda, Mart. 4, 18, 4 : perdix feta praegravem aut delumbem esse simulans, heavy, clumsy,…

prae-grăvo.opening: v. a. , to press heavily upon , to oppress with weight , to encumber (perh. not before the Aug. period). Lit. : exonerare praegravante turbā regnum cupiens, Liv. 5, 34 : praegravata telis scuta, burdened, heavy, id. 7,…

prae-grĕdĭor.opening: v. dep. n. and a. [gradior] (class.; syn.: praeeo, antecedo). Lit. , to go before or in advance , to precede. With dat. : gregi praegreditur equus, Varr. R. R. 2, 7, 6 .— With acc. : praegredi aliquem pedibus, Suet.…

praegressĭo.opening: praegredior , a going before , preceding. Lit. : errantium stellarum cursus, praegressiones, etc., Cic. Tusc. 1, 25, 62 .— Meton. , precedence : causae, Cic. Fat. 19, 44 .

praegressus.opening: praegredior , a going in advance , anticipation (postclass.): anteversio et praegressus, Amm. 21, 5, 13 .

prae-gŭbernans.opening: Part. [guberno], steering or guiding forwards (postclass.), Sid. Ep. 5, 13 .

praegustātor.opening: praegusto , one who tastes the meats and drinks before they are served at the table of a prince, a foretaster , taster , cup-bearer. Lit. , Suet. Claud. 44 : DIVI AVGVSTI, Inscr. Grut. 602, 4 ; so ib. 582 .—With private…

prae-gusto.opening: v. a. To taste beforehand ( poet. and in post-Aug. prose): cibos, Ov. Am. 1, 4, 33 ; Plin. 21, 3, 9, § 12 : pocula, Juv. 6, 633 : potum regis, Just. 12, 14 : caro bestiis praegustata, Vulg. Exod. 22, 31 .— In gen., to…

prae-gypso.opening: v. a. , to cover over with gypsum (post-class.): os vasculi, Cael. Aur. Tard. 3, 2 .

prae-hĭbĕo.opening: (old inf. praehiberier, Plaut. Am. 4, 2, 7 Fleck.), v. a. habeo (for praebeo, which is a contraction of it), to hold forth , offer , furnish , grant , give , supply (Plautinian): vestem, aurum, Plaut. Ps. 1, 2, 49 :…

prae-ĭcĭo.opening: ( or , Fest. s. v. pone, p. 249 Müll.), , v. a. , to cast or throw up in front (post-Aug.). Lit. : moles, Col. 8, 17 .— Trop. , to cast up , object , utter reproachfully : multis in contumeliam Graecorum praejactis…

prae-infundo.opening: v. a. , to pour into beforehand (post-class.), Cael. Aur. Acut. 2, 34 .

prae-innŭo.opening: v. a. , to indicate beforehand , Varr. ap. Non. 91, 4 dub. (al. pertimuerint).

prae-jăcĕo.opening: v. n. , to lie before , be situated in front of any thing (post-Aug.). With dat. : vastum mare praejacens Asiae, Plin. 4, 12, 24, § 75 .— With acc. : campus qui castra praejacet, Tac. A. 12, 36 . — Absol. :…

praejactĭto.opening: v. freq. a. , to boast excessively (late Lat.), Cassiod. in Psa. 36, 14 .

prae-jūdex.opening: one who judges beforehand : praejudex, προδικαστής , Gloss. Philox.

praejūdĭcātus.opening: Part. and P. a. , from praejudico.

praejūdĭcĭālis.opening: adj. Belonging or according to a preceding judgment or decision (post-class.): multam, Cod. Th. 11, 30, 50; Symm. Ep. 10, 51 .— Of or belonging to a preceding examination : actiones ( = praejudicia), Just. Inst. 4, 6,…

prae-jūdĭcĭum.opening: Lit. , a preceding judgment , sentence , or decision , a precedent (class.): praejudiciorum vis omnis tribus in generibus versatur: rebus, quae aliquando ex paribus causis sunt judicatae, quae exempla rectius dicuntur:…

prae-jūdĭco.opening: v. a. , to judge , pass sentence , or decide beforehand , to prejudge (class.). Lit. , in the judicial sphere: praejudicare de aliquo majore maleficio, Cic. Inv. 1, 20, 60 ; Cic. Verr. 2, 3, 65, § 153 .— Transf. , apart…

prae-jūrātĭo.opening: a previous taking of an oath which others then repeat: praejurationes facere dicuntur hi, qui ante alios conceptis verbis jurant: post quos eadem verba jurantes tantummodo dicunt: Idem in me, Fest. p. 224 Müll.

prae-jŭvo.opening: v. a. , to aid before (post-Aug.): affectam ejus fidem praejuvisse, Tac. H. 3, 65 .

prae-lābor.opening: v. dep. n. and a. , to glide onwards , to flow , swim , etc., before or along; to move , glide , etc., quickly by or past (mostly poet. and in post-Aug. prose). Lit. : insula, in quam Germani nando praelabebantur, Tac.…

prae-lambo.opening: v. a. , to lick or taste beforehand or first ( poet. ). Lit. : (mus) praelambens omne, quod affert, Hor. S. 2, 6, 109 .— Transf. , to wash or touch lightly , to bathe gently , of a river that flows by a place: arenas,…

prae-largus.opening: adj. , very copious or abundant ( poet. ): pulmo animae praelargus, Pers. 1, 14 : dapes, Juvenc. 3, 754 .

praelātĭo.opening: praefero , a preferring , a preference (post-class.), Val. Max. 7, 8, 4 : alterius, Tert. Apol. 13 ; id. ad Uxor. 1, 3 ; Ambros. Jacob, 2, 2, 5 .

praelātor.opening: id. , one that prefers , a preferrer (eccl. Lat.): misericordiae praelator quam sacrificii, Tert. Pudic. 2 .

prae-lautus.opening: adj. , very elegant , sumptuous , or luxurious (post-Aug.): homines, Suet. Ner. 30 ; id. Vitell. 2 .

prae-lăvo.opening: v. a. , to wash or rinse beforehand (post-class.): os, App. Mag. p. 278 med. : cinis praelavatus, Theod. Prisc. 1, 27 .

prae-laxātus.opening: Part. [laxo], widened or relieved beforehand (post-class.), Cael. Aur. Tard. 2, 1, 27 .

praelectĭo.opening: 2. praelego , a reading aloud to others , a lecture , prelection (post-Aug.), Quint. 1, 2, 15 ; 2, 5, 4 .

praelector.opening: id. , one who reads an author to others and adds explanations , a prelector (post-class.; cf.: lector, recitator), Gell. 18, 5, 6 .

prae-lēgo.opening: v. a. , to bequeath beforehand , i. e. to bequeath a thing to be given before the inheritance is divided (post-Aug.): eam coronam testamento ei praelegavit, Plin. 33, 2, 11, § 38 : peculia filiis, Dig. 33, 8, 26 :…

prae-lĕgo.opening: v. a. To read any thing to others , as a teacher, to show how it should be read, to set an example in reading , to lecture upon an author (post-Aug.): auctores, Quint. 1, 5, 11 : Vergilium et alios poëtas, Suet. Gram.…

praelībātĭo.opening: praelibo , a tasting or taking away beforehand (post-class.). Lit. , an offering of the first-fruits : praemetium, quod praelibationis causā ante praemetitur, Paul. ex Fest. s. v. praemetium, p. 235 Müll.: labiorum, a…

prae-līber.opening: adj. , very or entirely free (post-class.), Prud. Apoth. 155 .

prae-lībo.opening: v. a. , to taste beforehand , foretaste ( poet. ). Lit. : nectar, Stat. S. 3, 4, 60 .— Trop. : vultus ac pectora Ulysses Praelibat visu, examines, inspects, Stat. Achill. 2, 88 .

prae-lĭcenter.opening: adv. , too freely , too boldly (post-class.): verba finxit, Gell. 16, 7, 1 : disponens, Amm. 16, 5, 3 .

praelĭgāmen.opening: praeligo , something bound on in front or about one , an amulet (post-class.), Marc. Emp. 8 .

praelĭgānĕus.opening: adj. 2. praelego , picked beforehand : vinum, a poor kind of wine made of unripe or bad grapes gathered before the vintage , Cato, R. R. 23, 2 .

prae-lĭgo.opening: v. a. To bind on before , to bind : arida sarmenta praeligantur cornibus boum, Liv. 22, 16 : cauda pecoris quam arctissime praeligata, Plin. 29, 2, 10, § 38 : salice marginem, id. 17, 14, 24, § 109 .— To bind around ,…

prae-lĭno.opening: , no perf. , , v. a. , to smear or daub in front , to plaster over (postclass.): cum fucatur atque praelinitur, Gell. 7, 14, 11 : villas tectorio, id. 13, 23, 1 .

prae-lŏco.opening: v. a. , to set or place before , to put first or foremost (postclass.): si pro trochaeo paenultimo spondeum praelocaveris, Mart. Cap. 5, § 522 ; Aug. Gen. ad Lit. 7, 17 : consonans, Ter. Syll. p. 2390 .

praelŏcūtĭo.opening: praeloquor , a speaking before. Lit. (post-Aug.), Sen. Excerpt. Contr. 3 praef. — Transf. , a preface , preamble , Aug. Doctr. Chr. 4, 2 .

praelongo.opening: v. a. praelongus , to lengthen out very much , to make very long (post-Aug.): pedum crura, Plin. 11, 2, 1, § 3 .

prae-longus.opening: adj. , very long (not in Cic. or Cæs.): homo, i. e. very tall, Quint. 6, 3, 67 : gladii, Liv. 22, 46 : cauda, Plin. 8, 33, 51, § 121 : hasta, Tac. A. 6, 3 : gracilitas, Plin. 13, 4, 9, § 46 .—Of time, very long :…

prae-lŏquor.opening: (quūtus), 3, v. dep. a. and To speak beforehand or first , to speak before another , to forestall in speaking : occupas praeloqui, quae mi'st oratio, Plaut. Rud. 1, 4, 28 ; cf. id. ib. 1, 2, 31 : quod mihi causam…

prae-lūceo.opening: v. n. To shine or give light before; to hold or carry a light before , to light. Lit. Of those who carry a light: servus praelucens, Suet. Aug. 29 : alicui, Stat. S. 1, 2, 89 .— Of the light itself: praeluxere faces,…

prae-lūcĭdus.opening: adj. , shining greatly , very bright (post-Aug.): candor circuli praelucidus, Plin. 37, 6, 23, § 88 .

prae-lūdo.opening: v. a. , to play beforehand , by way of practice or trial; to prelude , rehearse (post - Aug.). Lit. : Nero Pompeiano praeludit, sings beforehand, preludes, Plin. 37, 2, 7, § 19 : tragoediis, Gell. 19, 11, 2 .—With acc.…

praelumbo.opening: v. a. prae - lumbus , to make lame in the loins or hipshot (anteclass.), Nov. ap. Non. 156, 12 .

prae-lūmĭnātus.opening: Part. [lumino], illustrated or explained before (eccl. Lat.), Tert. Res. Carn. 33 .

praelūsĭo.opening: praeludo , a prelude (post-Aug.): praelusio atque praecursio, Plin. Ep. 6, 13, 6 ; Marc. Emp. 20 .

prae-lustris.opening: adj. 1. lustro , very illustrious or magnificent ( poet. ): praelustria vita, shun worldly grandeur, Ov. Tr. 3, 4, 5 .

prae-mācĕro.opening: v. a. , to soak or steep beforehand (post-class.): mala cydonia, Scrib. Comp. 193 .

prae-mălĕdīco.opening: v. a. , to curse beforehand (eccl. Lat.): aliquem, Tert. adv. Marc. 5, 3 .

prae-mando.opening: v. a. , to chew beforehand; trop., to explain accurately and clearly (post-class.): aliquid alicui, Gell. 4, 1, 11 .

prae-mātūrus.opening: adj. Very early , early (syn. praecox): fructus, Col. 11, 3, 51 .— Too early , untimely , premature : denuntiatio, Planc. ap. Cic. Fam. 10, 8 : mors, Plin. 7, 51, 52, § 171 ; so, cineres, Juv. 11, 44 : hiems, Tac. A. 1,…

prae-mĕdĭcātus.opening: Part. [medico], protected by medicines or charms ( poet. , and eccl. Lat.): Aesonides, Ov. H. 12, 15 : antidoto praemedicatus, Tert. Jejun. 12 .

praemĕdĭtātĭo.opening: praemeditor , a considering beforehand , premeditation (used by Cic.): futurorum malorum, Cic. Tusc. 3, 14, 29 : diuturna, id. ib. 3, 15, 31 : futuri regni, Hier. in Matt. 3, 17, v. 9 .

praemĕdĭtātōrĭum.opening: praemeditor , a place for preparation (eccl. Lat.), Tert. Jejun. 6 .

prae-mĕdĭtor.opening: v. dep. a. , to think over , to muse or deliberate upon beforehand , to premeditate (class.). With object - clause : praemeditari id ferendum modice esse, Cic. Phil. 11, 3, 7 .— With relative - clause : praemeditari,…

prae-mercor.opening: v. dep. , to buy before or beforehand (ante - class.): praemercatur ancillam senex, Plaut. Merc. Arg. 2, 10 ; id. Ep. 3, 3, 25 : ni pretio minus parcerent, eaque praemercarentur, should forestall the markets , Cass.…

praemĕtĭum.opening: (al. † ), , prae-metior , the offering of the firstfruits measured out beforehand for Ceres : praemetium quod praelibationis causā ante praemetitur, Paul. ex Fest. p. 235 Müll.; cf.: praemetium de spicis, quas primum…

prae-mētor.opening: v. dep. a. , to measure or measure out beforehand (post-class.), Sol. 40 (dub.; al. metatum).—Hence, in pass. signif.: , , measured or meted out beforehand : praemetata divūm itinera, predestined, Mart. Cap. 8, § 811 .

praemĕtŭens.opening: Part. and P. a. , from praemetuo.

prae-mĕtŭenter.opening: adv. , v. praemetuo, P. a. fin.

prae-mĕtŭo.opening: v. n. and a. Neutr. , to fear or be in fear beforehand (very rare): mens, Lucr. 3, 1019 : Caesar praemetuens suis, fearing for , anxious about his men , * Caes. B. G. 7, 49, 1 .— Act. , to fear something beforehand :…

praemĭālis.opening: adj. praemium , used as a reward (eccl. Lat.): resurrectio, Aug. c. Sec. Resp. Jul. 6, 36.

praemĭātor.opening: praemior . A robber (ante-class.), Naev. ap. Non. 150, 23 (Com. Rel. p. 6 Rib.).— A rewarder , one who gives a reward to : luctantium, Ambros. in Psa. 36, 57 .

praemĭātrix.opening: praemiator , she who rewards (post-class.): bonorum praemiatrix Adrastia, Amm. 14, 11, 25 .

prae-mĭco.opening: v. n. , to gleam or glitter forth , to glitter very much (post-class.): lucerna claro lumine praemicans, App. M. 5, p. 167, 20 : praemicantis lunae candor nimius, id. ib. 11 , p. 257 init. : galea nitore praemicans, id.…

prae-mī^gro.opening: v. n. , to move away beforehand or before (post - Aug.): ruinis imminentibus musculi praemigrant, Plin. 8 28, 42, § 103.

prae-mĭnister.opening: a servant , an attendant (post - class.): deorum ... flaminum, Macr. S. 3, 8 ; Tert. Or. 1 .

prae-mĭnistra.opening: a female attendant or minister (post-class.): lingua mendaciorum et amaritudinum praeministra, App. Mag. p. 278, 6 ; Macr. S. 3, 8 .

prae-mĭnistro.opening: v. n. and a. Neutr. , to wait or attend upon , to minister to any one (post-class.): magistratibus, of the lictors, Gell. 12, 3, 3 ; cf. id. 10, 3, 13 : alicui, App. M. 5, p. 160, 3 .— Act. , to furnish , supply , hand…

prae-mĭnor.opening: v. dep. , to threaten beforehand , to threaten greatly (post-class.); with inf. , Tert. adv. Marc. 5, 19 : aliquid, App. M. 5, p. 167, 8 ; 8 , p. 211, 11: haec illis, Tert. Apol. 21 .

praemĭor.opening: v. dep. praemium , to stipulate for a reward : constabat, in cognitionibus patriis nundinari praemiarique solitum, Suet. Tit. 7 : sequimini me, praemiati, Nov. ap. Fest. p. 464 Müll. (Com. Rel. p. 217 Rib. ex conject.).

praemĭōsus.opening: adj. id. , rich (ante-class.): praemiosam, pecuniosam, dixit Cato, Fest. p. 242 Müll.; cf.: praemiosa, pecuniosa, Paul. ex Fest. p. 243 ib.

praemistus.opening: or , , Part. [misceo], mixed beforehand (postclass.): praemixta olera, Apic. 4, 5 ; Cael. Aur. Tard. 4, 3, 63 .

prae-mītis.opening: adj. , very gentle ( poet. ): asina, Juvenc. 3, 633 ; Ven. Fort. Carm. 3, 12, 37.

prae-mitto.opening: v. a. , to send forward or before , to despatch in advance. Lit. (class.): a portu me praemisisti domum, Plaut. Am. 2, 1, 55 : nuntium, id. Truc. 2, 4, 58 : legiones in Hispaniam, Caes. B. C. 1, 39 : legatum ad flumen,…

praemĭum.opening: prae-emo, what one has got before or better than others (class.). Profit derived from booty , booty ( poet. ; cf. praeda; and: avorti praedam ab hostibus. Pen. Heus, ecqua in istac pars inest praemi mihi? Plaut. Men. 1,…

prae-mŏdĕrans.opening: Part. [moderor], prescribing a measure (post-class.): in proelia ingredi praemoderante citharā gressibus, Gell. 1, 11, 6 .

prae-mŏdŭlātus.opening: Part. [modulor], measured out or modulated beforehand (post-Aug.): cogitationem gestu, to adapt the thoughts beforehand to the gestures, Quint. 11, 3, 109 .

praemŏdum.opening: adv. prae-modus , beyond measure (ante-class.): Livius in Odysseā praemodum dicit, quasi admodum Parcentes, inquit, praemodum: quod significat supra modum: dictumque est quasi praeter modum, Gell. 7, 7, 12 .

prae-mŏlestĭa.opening: trouble beforehand , anxiety , apprehension; another term for metus: alii metum praemolestiam appellabant, quod est quasi dux consequentis molestiae, Cic. Tusc. 4, 30, 64 .

prae-mōlĭor.opening: v. dep. , to prepare or make preparations for beforehand (very rare): res, Liv. 28, 17, 4 .

prae-mollĭo.opening: , no perf. , , v. a. , to soften beforehand (post - Aug.). Lit. : praemollitus sulcus, Quint. 2, 9, 3 ; Cael. Aur. Tard. 4, 3 .— Trop. , to soften or mollify beforehand , Quint. 4, 3, 10 : judicum mentes, id. 6, 5, 9 .

prae-mollis.opening: adj. , very soft (postAug.): ova, Plin. 9, 51, 75, § 165 : involucrum, id. 11, 37, 69, § 181 .

prae-mŏnĕo.opening: v. a. In gen., to forewarn , to advise , or admonish beforehand , to remind beforehand , to premonish (class.); constr. aliquem with ut or ne , with a simple subj. , with quod , with de , aliquid (of a thing): me, ut…

praemŏnĭtĭo.opening: praemoneo , a forewarning , premonition (eccl. Lat.), Tert. adv. Marc. 2, 4 .

praemŏnĭtor.opening: id. , a forewarner , premonitor (post - class.), App. de Deo Socr. p. 51, 12 .

praemŏnĭtōrĭus.opening: adj. praemonitor , that gives previous warning , premonitory (eccl. Lat.): edictum, Tert. Anim. 3 .

praemŏnĭtus.opening: praemoneo , a forewarning , premonition ( poet. ): deūm, Ov. M. 15, 800 .

praemonstrātĭo.opening: praemonstro , a showing or indicating beforehand , a premonstration (eccl. Lat.), Lact. 7, 14, 12 .

praemonstrātor.opening: id. , one who shows or points out beforehand , a guide , director : monitor et praemonstrator, Ter. Heaut. 5, 1, 2 .

prae-monstro.opening: (old form , v. infra ), , v. a. , to show beforehand , to point out the way , to guide , direct. In gen. ( poet. ): praemonstra docte, quid fabuletur, Plaut. Pers. 1, 3, 68 : currenti spatium praemonstra, Lucr. 6, 93 :…

prae-mordĕo.grammar: morsi and mordi, morsum, 2 v. a.
prae-mordĕo.opening: v. a. , to bite in front , to bite at the end; hence, in gen., to bite ( poet. and in post-Aug. prose). Lit. : ni fugissem, medium, credo, praemorsisset, Plaut. Fragm. ap. Gell. 7, 9, 7 : linguam, Luc. 6, 567 :…

praemordĭcus.opening: adj. praemordeo , bitten off in front or at the end (late Lat.): olera praemordica, of which only the tops are eaten (e. g. asparagus), Hier. in Reg. S. Pachom. 52 .

prae-mŏrĭor.opening: v. dep. , to die early or prematurely , to die (mostly poet. and in post-Aug. prose). Lit. : aut ego praemoriar, primoque exstinguar in aevo, Ov. H. 8, 121 : parte corporis velut praemortua, Suet. Gram. 3 .— Trop. , to…

praemortŭus.opening: Part. and P. a. , from praemorior.

prae-mŏvĕo.opening: , no perf. , , v. a. , to move beforehand , to stir greatly (post-class.), Cael. Aur. Tard. 1, 5 : corpus, id. ib. 5, 7 ; 2, 1.

prae-mundātus.opening: Part. [mundo], cleansed beforehand (post-class.): praemundatis oculis, Theod. Prisc. 1, 10 .

prae-mūnĭo.opening: ( , Gell. 13, 27 ; 14, 2 ), , v. a. , to fortify or defend in front (class.). Lit. : aditus magnis operibus, Caes. B. C. 3, 58 : loca necessaria, id. ib. 3, 112 : Isthmum, id. ib. 3, 55 : fossa, Tac. H. 3, 21 .— Trop.…

praemūnītĭo.opening: praemunio, II. B. , a fortifying or strengthening beforehand. In gen., Ambros. de Isaac et Anim. 4, 37.— Trop. , rhet. t. t., = πρὀ παρασκευή , of an orator, who prepares the minds of his hearers for what he has further…

prae-narro.opening: v. a. , to tell or relate beforehand : rem, Ter. Eun. 5, 5, 12 .

prae-năto.opening: v. n. To swim before or in front : praenatans musculus, Plin. 9, 62, 88, § 186 : praenatante pisciculo, id. 9, 45, 68, § 146 .— To swim or flow by : domos praenatat amnis, Verg. A. 6, 705 .

praenāvĭgātĭo.opening: praenavigo , a sailing by or past (post-Aug.): praenavigatio Atlantis, Plin. 6, 31, 36, § 199 ; 4, 12, 19, § 57 .

prae-nāvĭgo.opening: v. a. and n. , to sail by or past any thing, to sail along (post-Aug.). Lit. , absol. : praenavigantes adulterae, Sen. Ep. 51, 12 ; Plin. 6, 23, 26, § 97 .—With acc. : praenavigans litus, loca, Mel. 2, 3, 6 ; Val. Max.…

Praeneste.opening: and , = Πραίνεστος or Πραίνεστε , one of the most ancient and important cities of Latium , famed for the beauty of its roses , for its nuts , and still more for its temple of Fortune and the oracle connected with it ,…

prae-nexus.opening: Part. [necto], tied or bound up in front (post-class.): praenexo obsignatoque ore, Sol. 1, 6 .

prae-nĭmis.opening: adv. , too much , quite too (post-class.): praenimis plebeium est, Gell. 19, 10, 9 .

prae-nĭtĕo.opening: v. n. , to shine or glitter forth ( poet. and in post-Aug. prose). Lit. : vestes praenitent, App. M. 5, p. 162, 37 : luna subito praenitens, Plin. 2, 9, 6, § 42 : juvenis veste niveā praenitens, App. M. 11, p. 261, 21…

prae-nōbĭlis.opening: adj. , very famous or celebrated (post-class.): praenobilis potio, App. M. 10, p. 251, 10 ; Prud. Ham. 700 .— Comp. : praenobilior, App. Flor. 3, p. 355 .

prae-nōmen.opening: Lit. , the name which stood before the name of the gens, the first name , prœnomen , usually abbreviated; thus, in M. Tullius Cicero, Marcus is the prænomen, as A. = Aulus, C. = Caius, Cn. = Cnaeus, etc.: Quintilius cum…

praenōmĭno.opening: , no perf. , , v. a. praenomen , to give one the prœnomen or title of , to name (very rare): Numerios praenominabant, Varr. ap. Non. 352, 29 .— To name in the first place (late Lat.): praenominatur caro, et postea…

prae-nosco.opening: v. a. , to learn or become acquainted with beforehand , to foreknow (class.): futura, Cic. Div. 1, 38, 82 ; Suet. Ner. 56 ; Plin. 18, 24, 56, § 206 : promissum sibi caelum, Ov. F. 3, 159 : venturum caeli laborem, Stat.…
