praenōtĭo.opening: praenosco , a previous notion , preconception , a translation of the Epicurean πρόληψις : sive anticipatio sive praenotio deorum, innate idea, Cic. N. D. 1, 17, 44 : earum rerum, Boëth. Consol. Phil. 5, pros. 4, p. 106,…

prae-nŏto.opening: v. a. (postclass.). To mark or note before or in front : profert quosdam libros litteris ignorabilibus praenotatos, App. M. 11, p. 268, 11 : aureo anulo, to seal , id. ib. 10 , p. 243, 3: psalmum inscriptione, Hilar. in…

prae-nūbĭlus.opening: adj. , very cloudy , very dark or gloomy ( poet. ): densā praenubilus arbore lucus, Ov. Am. 3, 13, 7 .

praenum.opening: Lit. , an implement for combing flax , a hatchel , Gloss. Philox. —Hence, Transf. , an instrument of torture , a rack : tentare praenum, Tert. Apol. 5 .

prae-nuncŭpātus.opening: Part. [nuncupo], named beforehand : Emmanuel prophetico ore, Prud. Cath. 7, 179 .

praenuntĭātĭo.opening: or , , praenuntio , a prediction (eccl. Lat.), Tert. Anim. 46 fin.

praenuntĭātīvus.opening: , a false read. for praenuntios, Plin. 2, 71, 73, § 181 .

praenuntĭātor.opening: praenuntio , one who announces beforehand , a foreteller , predicter (eccl. Lat.), Aug. Conf. 9, 5 ; id. Genes. 8, 4 fin.

praenuntĭātrix.opening: praenuntiator , she that foretells or predicts (eccl. Lat.): gloriae, Prud. στεφ . 2, 29.

prae-nuntĭo.opening: ( ), , v. a. , to announce or publish beforehand , to foretell , foreshow , predict; constr. with acc. , de , or an object-clause (class.). Lit. : futura, Cic. Div. 1, 6, 12 . — Impers. : de eorum adventu esse…

prae-nuntĭus.opening: ( ), , adj. , that foretells or forebodes.—Subst. , , , a foreteller , harbinger , foreboder , an indication , token , omen (class.): Zephyrus Veris praenuntius, Lucr. 5, 737 : lucis praenuntius ales, i. e. the cock,…

prae-obtūrans.opening: Part. [obturo], stopping up in front , Vitr. 10, 12, 1 .

prae-occĭdo.opening: v. n. , to go down or set before; of constellations (post-Aug.); with dat. , Plin. 18, 29, 69, § 285 .

praeoccŭpātĭo.opening: praeoccupo . A seizing beforehand , preoccupation : locorum praeoccupatio, Nep. Eum. 3, 6 .— Rhet. fig., an anticipation of what properly comes afterwards , prolepsis , Beda, Schem. et Tropis init. — A disease that…

prae-occŭpo.opening: v. a. (class., but not in Cic., since praecepit is the true read., Cic. Phil. 10, 1, 2 ). To seize upon , to take possession of or occupy beforehand , to preoccupy. Lit. : hic ne intrare posset saltum, Datames…

prae-ŏlĕo.opening: v. n. , to emit or exhale an odor beforehand (post-Aug.): ut crocus, ita somnus prius quam prope adsit, longe praeolet, Front. Ep. ad M. Caes. 1, 4 Mai.

prae-ŏlo.opening: v. impers. , to perceive before : ut praeolat mihi quod tu velis, Plaut. Mil. 1, 1, 41 ; v. Ritschl ad h. l.

prae-ŏpīmus.opening: adj. , very fat (eccl. Lat.): vitulus, Tert. Poen. 8 .

prae-opto.opening: v. a. , to choose or wish rather , to desire more , to prefer (class.; not in Cic.); constr. aliquid alicui , with an object-clause , or with ut : praeoptantes exsilio modicam domi fortunam, Liv. 29, 30, 12 ; 44, 22, 14…

prae-ordĭno.opening: v. a. , to preordain (eccl. Lat.): Deus praeordinavit te, ut, etc., Vulg. Act. 22, 14 .—Hence, , , Part. , ordered beforehand , preordained (post-class.): causae, Cael. Aur. Acut. 1, 4, 44 ; Vulg. Act. 10, 41 .

prae-ōro.opening: v. a. , to pray before , Not. Tir. p. 106 .

praeostendo.opening: v. a. , to show beforehand , display before , make clear (late. Lat.): hoc monstrare debent, hoc ostendere vel praeostendere, Aug. Civ. Dei , 21, 8, 6.— Absol. : portenta a portendendo, id est, praeostendendo, Aug. Civ.…

prae-palpans.opening: Part. [palpo], stroking or patting before or in front (postclass.), Paul. Nol. Ep. 49 .

prae-pando.opening: v. a. , to open or spread before , to spread out , extend ( poet. and in post-Aug. prose). Lit. , Verg. Cul. 16 : vestibula, Plin. 11, 24, 28, § 80 .— Trop. : lumina menti alicujus, Lucr. 1, 144: hibernos praepandens…

praepărātĭo.opening: praeparo . A getting or making ready , a preparing , preparation (class.): priusquam aggrediare, adhibenda est praeparatio diligens, Cic. Off. 1, 21, 73 : provisio animi et praeparatio ad minuendum dolorem, id. Tusc. 3,…

praepărātō.opening: adv. , v. praeparo, P. a. fin.

praepărātor.opening: praeparo , a preparer (eccl. Lat.): Joannes praeparator viarum Domini, Tert. adv. Marc. 4, 33 .

praepărātūra.opening: praeparo , a preparing , preparation (eccl. Lat.): praeparatura viarum Domini, Tert. adv. Marc. 4, 18 .

prae-părātus.opening: praeparo , a preparation (post - Aug.): praeparatus Caesaris contra Antonium, Vell. 2, 76, 3 dub. (Haase, apparatus; cf. id. 2, 12, 3 ): rei rusticae, Gell. 10, 11, 7 .

prae-parcus.opening: adj. , very sparing , very niggardly (post-Aug.). Lit. : apes praeparcae (opp. prodigae atque edaces), Plin. 11, 19, 21, § 67 .— Trop. : animus, Plin. 22, 24, 51, § 110 .

prae-păro.opening: v. a. , to get or make ready beforehand , to prepare , equip , make preparations for , etc. (class.; cf.: paro, apparo). Lit. : ea quae videntur instare, Cic. Rosc. Am. 8, 22 : praeparaverat ante naves, Liv. 30, 20, 5 :…

prae-pătĭor.opening: v. dep. , to suffer very much (post-class.), Cael. Aur. Acut. 2, 34 al.

praepĕdīmentum.opening: praepedio , a hinderance , impediment (ante-class.), Plaut. Poen. 3, 2, 29 ; Sid. Ep. 7, 6 .

praepĕdĭo.opening: v. a. praepes , to entangle the feet or other parts of the body; to shackle , bind , fetter (mostly poet. and post-Aug.; syn.: impedio, illaqueo, irretio). Lit. : praepeditus latera forti ferro, Plaut. Poen. 4, 2, 5 :…

prae-pendĕo.opening: v. n. , to hang before , to hang down in front (class.): ubi tegumenta praependere possent ad defendendos ictus, Caes. B. C. 2, 9, 3 : storias circum turrim praependentes, id. ib. 2, 9, 5 : praependent demissae in…

praepĕs.opening: adj. prae-peto . Lit. Flying swiftly , swift of flight , nimble , fleet , quick , rapid , etc. ( poet. ; syn.: velox, pernix, levis): praepes Laeva volavit avis, Enn. ap. Cic. Div. 1, 48, 108 (Ann. v. 94 Vahl.):…

prae-pĕto.opening: v. a. , to strive diligently after , Fest. s. v. praepetes, p. 245 Müll. (v. praepes, A. 1).

prae-pĭlātus.opening: Part. [2. pila], furnished in front , i. e. tipped with a ball or button (not before the Aug. per.). Lit. : pila praepilata, Auct. B. Afr. 72: missilia, darts or javelins with a blunt point rounded like a ball , that…

praepĭlo.opening: , no perf. , , v. a. praepilum , to point in front or at the end like a pilum (post-class.): praepilatis missilibus principiis pugnae tentatis, Amm. 24, 6, 10 — To throw forwards , hurl before (postclass.):…

prae-pinguis.opening: adj. , very fat ( poet. and in post-Aug. prose). Lit. : sues, Plin. 8, 51, 77, § 207 : solum, i. e. very rich, very fertile, Verg. A. 3, 698 : ubertas, Plin. 18, 17, 45, § 162 : quod praepinguis fuerit visus, Suet.…

prae-plecto.opening: v. a. , to strike before , Not. Tir. p. 107 .—In part. perf. : praeplexus, Not. Tir. p. 107 .

praepollentĭa.opening: prae-polleo , excellence (late Lat.), Aug. in Psa. 70 , Serm. 1, 15.

prae-pollĕo.opening: v. n. , to exceed or surpass in power , to be very powerful , to be very remarkable or distinguished (perh. not ante-Aug.): quibus additis praepollebat, he had the superiority, Tac. A. 2, 45 ; 51 : Phoenices mari…

prae-pondĕro.opening: v. n. and a. Neutr. , to be of greater weight , to preponderate , incline (post-Aug.; cf. propendeo). Lit. : ne, portionum aequitate turbatā, mundus praeponderet, Sen. Q. N. 3, 10, 3 : quotiens in alterum latus…

prae-pōno.opening: (old perf. praeposivi, Plaut. Rud. 4, 2, 11 .—Sync. form praepostus, Lucr. 6, 999 ), v. a. , to put or set before , to place first (syn.: praefero, praeficio). Lit. In gen.: versus, in primā fronte libelli, Ov. Tr. 1,…

prae-porto.opening: v. a. , to bear or carry before ( poet. ): tela, Lucr. 2, 621 ; Cat. 64, 193 : prae se Scorpius infestus praeportans flebile acumen, Cic. Arat. 430 (682).

praepŏsĭtĭo.opening: praepono . A putting or setting before , a preferring , preference , Cic. Fin. 3, 16, 54 .— A placing or setting over as commander or president , an appointing to command (postclass.): aliquem navi, Dig. 14, 1, 1, § 12…

praepŏsĭtīvus.opening: adj. id. . In gram., that is set before , prepositive : vocales, Prisc. p. 561 P.: conjunctio, Diom. p. 409 P.: praepositiones, Prisc. p. 986 P.

praepŏsĭtūra.opening: id. , the office of a chief or overseer , etc. (post-class.): militares, Lampr. Elag. 6 : horreorum et pagorum, Cod. Just. 10, 70, 2 .

prae-possum.opening: v. n. , to be very powerful or more powerful , to have the superiority , get the upperhand (post-Aug.): postquam Macedones praepotuere, Tac. H. 5, 8 .—Hence, , ( gen. plur. praepotentum, Sen. Ira, 3, 14, 2 ), P. a. ,…

praepostĕrātĭo.opening: praepostero , the reverse order (late Lat.), August. Mus. 3, 9, 20 .

praepostĕrĭtas.opening: praeposterus , a reversed order , inversion (post class.): si Juno est aër, Graeei nominis praeposte ritate repetita, i. e. by transposing the letters of the words ἀὴρ and Ἥρα , Arn. 3, 118 : PARENS AFFLICTVS…

praepostĕro.opening: v. a. praeposterus , to reverse , invert (post-class.): ordinem, Auct. Quint. Decl. 9 : versus, August. Mus. 3, 9, 20 .

prae-postĕrus.opening: adj. , reversed , inverted , perverted , distorted , absurd , preposterous , unseasonable , etc. (class.; syn.: intempestivus, perversus). Of persons, absurd , preposterous : ut erat semper praeposterus atque perversus,…

praepŏtentĭa.opening: praepotens , superior power (eccl. Lat.): praepotentia Dei, Tert. adv. Marc. 2, 7 : horum (regum), App. Mund. 26 .

prae-pōto.opening: v. n. and a. Neutr. , to drink before (post-class.), Cael. Aur. Acut. 3, 17, 159 .— Act. , to give to drink or make drink of before : praepotat absinthio aegrotantes vino sincero, Cael. Aur. Acut. 3, 17, 160 ; id. Tard.…

prae-prŏpĕro.opening: v. n. , to hasten greatly : praeproperat, προπετεύεται , Gloss. Philox.—Hence, * , adv. , very hastily , very rapidly : certare, Lucr. 3, 779 .

prae-prŏpĕrus.opening: adj. , too quick or hasty , over-hasty , sudden , precipitate (class.): praepropera festinatio, Cic. Fam. 7, 8, 1 : prensatio, id. Att. 1, 1, 1 : celeritas, Liv. 31, 42 : ingenium, rash, id. 22, 41 : nisus, Sil. 15, 757…

prae-purgo.opening: v. a. , to purge or cleanse beforehand (post-class.), Cael. Aur. Tard. 1, 4, 128 .

praepūtĭātĭo.opening: praeputio , a retaining of the foreskin , the state of being uncircumcised , uncircumcision (eccl. Lat.; opp. circumcisio), Tert. adv. Marc. 5, 4 ; Hilar. Trin. 1, 13.

praepūtĭo.opening: v. a. praeputium , to draw out the foreskin , Schol. Juv. 10, 206 . —Hence, , , P. a. , having the foreskin , uncircumcised (eccl. Lat.), Tert. adv. Marc. 5, 9 .

prae-pūtĭum.opening: vox hibr., praeπόσθιον , the foreskin , prepuce. —In plur. , Juv. 6, 238 ; 14, 99 ; Sen. Apoc. 8, 1 ; Vulg. Gen. 17, 11 ; 14 .— Trop. : circumcidite praeputium cordis vestri, do away with impurity , Laet. 4, 17, 8;…

prae-questus.opening: Part. [queror], complaining beforehand ( poet. ): multa praequestus, Ov. M. 4, 251 .

prae-rădĭo.opening: v. n. and a. Neutr. , to beam or glitter forth ( poet. ): pilenta praeradiant, Claud. Nupt. Honor. et Mar. 286.— Act. , to outshine : Bacchi conjux Praeradiat stellis signa minora suis, Ov. H. 6, 116 .

prae-rādo.opening: , no perf. , , v. a. To scrape or shave off in front : latus alterum, Cato, R. R. 41 ; Paul. Nol. Ep. 7 , sect. 2. — To shear or shave off before : praerasi capilli, Cael. Aur. Tard. 5, 4, 74 ; id. Acut. 1, 11, 79 .

prae-rancĭdus.opening: adj. , very stale; trop., obsolete : finitiones, Probus ap. Gell. 13, 20, 1 .

prae-răpĭdus.opening: adj. , very swift , very rapid (post-Aug.). Lit. : amnis, Sen. Apoc. 7, 2, v. 11 : celeritas, id. Q. N. 1, 1, 1 : gurges, Liv. 29, 32, 9 : fluminum celeritas, Curt. 9, 4, 15 : fuga, Sil. 16, 563 .— Trop. , very eager ,…

praereptor.opening: praeripio , one who seizes a thing before another , a forestaller (eccl. Lat.): fllius, qui ad benedictionem fratris praereptor adstiterat, Hier. Ep. 36 , n. 15.

prae-rĭgesco.opening: v. inch. n. , to become exceedingly stiff (post - Aug.): ita praeriguisse manus, Tac. A. 13, 35 .

prae-rĭgĭdus.opening: adj. , very stiff , very rigid (late Lat.): mens, Auct. Quint. Decl. 17, 7 .

prae-rīpĭa.opening: ripa , places on the banks of a river (post-class.): praeripia fluminis, App. Mag. p. 278, 17 (dub.; al. praerupia, q. v.).

prae-rĭpĭo.opening: v. a. rapio . In gen., to take away a thing before another , to snatch or tear away , to carry off (class.): quid huc venisti sponsam praereptum meam? Plaut. Cas. 1, 14 : Tun meo patre es prognatus? Men. Immo equidem,…

prae-rōbŏrātus.opening: Part. [roboro], strengthened beforehand (post-class.): praeroboratum corpus, Cael. Aur. Tard. 4, 1 .

prae-rōdo.opening: , no perf. , , v. a. To gnaw in front , to gnaw at the end or tip ( poet. and in post-Aug. prose): digitos suos, Plaut. Ps. 3, 2, 93 : teneros pampinos, Col. Arbor. 15 .— To gnaw , bite , or nibble off : praeroso hamo,…

praerŏgātĭō.opening: praerogo , a distributing beforehand (post-class.): annonae, Fulg. Myth. 1, 2 .

praerŏgativatius.opening: praerogo , one that enjoys certain privileges or prerogatives (late Lat.), Cassiod. Var. 11, 27 ; cf. Symm. Ep. 3, 67 .

praerŏgātīvus.opening: adj. praerogo , that is asked before others for his opinion , that votes before or first , prerogative (class.). Adj. : centuria praerogativa, Cic. Planc. 20, 49 ; cf. Fest. p. 249 Müll.; Becker, Antiq. II. 3, p. 3 sq.,…

prae-rŏgo.opening: v. a. To ask before another, to ask first : sententias, non more atque ordine, sed prout libuisset, praerogabat, Suet. Aug. 35 .— To pay beforehand or in advance : pensionem, Dig. 19, 2, 19 : expensas, Cod. Just. 10,…

prae-rumpo.opening: v. a. , to break or tear off before or in front (class.): retinacula classis, Ov. M. 14, 547 : funes praerumpebantur, were broken off, Caes. B. G. 3, 14 : uncus praerumpitur, Col. 3, 18, 2 . — Trop. , to wrench , tear…

praerupte.opening: , a false read. for praealtus, Plin. 34, 15, 43, § 149 ; v. Sillig ad h. l.

prae-rŭtĭlus.opening: adj. , very red ( poet. ), Auct. Carm. de Judicio Dom. 202.

praes.opening: adv. prae , at hand , now (ante-class.): ibi tibi parata praes est, Plaut. Pers. 2, 4, 17 .

praesaepe.grammar: is is ae ii n. f. f. n.
praesaepe.opening: ( ), , , and or , , ; also, , , , and (each of these forms less correctly written ), , praesaepio , prop. an enclosure of any kind; hence, a stable , stall , fold , pen (syn. stabulum). Lit. : praesaepis bubus hibernas,…

prae-saepĭo.opening: ( ), , v. a. , to fence in front , to block up , barricade (class.): aditus atque itinera trabibus, Caes. B. C. 1, 27 : loca montuosa sublicis, id. ib. 3, 49 : omni aditu praesaepto, id. B. G. 7, 77 .

prae-sāgātus.opening: Part. [sago], perceived beforehand , presaged (eccl. Lat.): scala, Hier. Ep. 3 , n. 4.

prae-sāgĭo.opening: (in the deponent form: animus plus praesagitur mali, presages, Plaut. Bacch. 4, 4, 28 ), v. a. Lit. , to feel or perceive beforehand , to have a presentiment of a thing (class.): sagire, sentire acute est. Is igitur,…

praesāgītĭo.opening: praesagio , a presentiment , foreboding , the faculty of divining or presaging (class.; cf.: praedictio, divinatio, praesagium, praesensio): inest in animis praesagitio extrinsecus injecta, atque inclusa divinitus, Cic.…

praesāgĭum.opening: id. , a presentiment , foreboding , prognostic , presage ( poet. and in post-Aug. prose; cf. praesagitio): vatum praesagia, Ov. M. 15, 879 : mentis, id. ib. 6, 510 : puella praesagio malorum jam vitae exempta, Tac. A.…

praesāgo.opening: v. a. praesagus , to forebode , presage , have a presentiment of (late Lat.): cogitatio praesagantis, Cassiod. Var. 5, 3 : prodigiosa ostenta, App. M. 9, p. 235, 22 : futura rerum, id. Mag. 43, p. 301 fin. ; Hier. Ep.…

prae-sāgus.opening: adj. , foreboding , foretelling , divining , prophetic , presaging ( poet. and in post - Aug. prose): praesaga mali mens, Verg. A. 10, 843 : fulminis ignes, id. ib. 177 : luctus suspiria, Ov. M. 2, 124 : verba, id. ib.…

praesaltor.opening: prae- 2. salio , he who led the dances of the Salii : praesaltor, ὁ ἐν τοῖς ἱεροῖς προορχούμενος , Vet. Gloss.

prae-sānesco.opening: v. incept. , to begin to heal prematurely , to close up too soon : cicatrices, quae praesanuere, aperit, Plin. 24, 10, 43, § 73 .

prae-sāno.opening: v. a. , to heal up prematurely (Plinian): ulcera praesanata, Plin. 26, 41, 87, § 147 (in Plin. 24, 10, 43, § 73 , the true reading is praesanuere, v. praesanesco).

prae-saucĭātus.opening: Part. [saucio], severely wounded (post-class.): vires Cael. Aur. Acut. 1, 3 .

prae-scătens.opening: Part. [scateo], overflowing , abounding , (post-class.): liber doctrinis omnigenis praescatens, Gell. 14, 6, 1 .

praescĭentĭa.opening: praescio , foreknowledge , prescience (eccl. Lat.): Dei bonitas et praescientia, Tert. adv. Marc. 2, 5 : Dei, Aug. Civ. Dei , 5, 9; Mart. Cap. 2, § 159 ; plur. , id. 1, § 32 .

prae-scindo.opening: v. a. , to cut off in front : inferiores sedes praescindantur, Vitr. 5, 7 : vestes, Vulg. 2 Reg. 10, 4 : manus, id. 2 Macc. 7, 4 .

prae-scĭo.opening: v. a. , to know beforehand , to foreknow ( poet. and in postAug. prose): nonne oportuit praescisse me ante? Ter. And. 1, 5, 4 : eum haec praescisse, Suet. Tib. 67 .— Esp. (in eccl. Lat.), of God's foreknowledge :…

prae-scisco.opening: v. inch. a. , to find out , or learn beforehand (not in Cic. or Cæs.): animos volgi, Verg. G. 4, 70 : exploratam fugam, Col. 9, 9, 4 : adversos subitosque motus, Amm. 20, 6, 9 .—With rel.-clause , Liv. 27, 35, 5 .

praescītĭo.opening: praescio , a foreknowing , prognostic (post-class.): numine praescitionum auctore, Amm. 29, 1, 31 .

praescītum.opening: id. , a prognostic , presage , presentiment (Plinian): oraculorum, Plin. 2, 7, 5, § 24 : animi quiescentis, presentiments, id. 10, 75, 98, § 211 : picorum, omens, id. 10, 18, 20, § 41 .

praescītus.opening: id. , a foreknowing , prescience (post-class.): quae sint fortassis regi praescitui, Val. Rer. Gest. Alex. M. 1, 49.

prae-scĭus.opening: adj. , foreknowing , prescient ( poet. and in post-Aug. prose): corda, Verg. A. 12, 452 : lingua, Ov. F. 1, 538 .—With gen. obj. : vates Praescia venturi, Verg. A. 6, 66 : vox sortis, Val. Fl. 5, 529 : facere aliquem…

prae-scrībo.opening: v. a. , to write before , in front , or previously , to prefix in writing (syn.: praefinio, praestituo). Lit. : pagina nomen sibi quae Vari praescripsit, Verg. E. 6, 11 : monimentis consulum nomina, Tac. A. 3, 57 ; cf.:…

praescriptĭo.opening: praescribo . A writing before or in front , a prefixing in writing; hence, meton., a title , inscription , preface , introduction , commencement : praescriptio legis, Cic. Agr. 2, 9, 22 : tribuniciae potestatis, Tac. A.…

praescriptīvus.opening: adj. praescribo, II. B. , of or relating to a legal exception or demurrer (post-class.): praescriptivae quaestiones, Jul. Vict. Art. Rhet. 3, 10: quaestiunculae, id. ib. 4, 1 : praescripti vum praecedens, Sulp. Viet.…

praescriptus.opening: praescribo , a precept (eccl. Lat.), Tert. Exhort. ad Cast. 3 .

praesĕca.opening: or , , a word assumed for the etym. of brassica, Varr. L. L. 5, § 104 Müll.

prae-sĕco.grammar: cŭi, ctum, or cātum, 1 v. a.
prae-sĕco.opening: v. a. , to cut off before or in front , to cut off or out (not in Cic.). Lit. : pars cultello praesecatur, Varr. R. R. 3, 16, 34 : brassica ut praesica, quod ex ejus scapo minutatim praesecatur, id. L. L. 5, § 104…

praesegmen.opening: praeseco , a piece cut off , a paring (ante- and postclass.): tonsor omnia abstulit praesegmina, Plaut. Aul. 2, 4, 33 ; cf.: praesegmina proprie Plautus in Aululariā ea dici voluit, quae unguibus eminulis praesecantur,…

praesēmĭnātĭo.opening: praesemino , a fœtus (only in Vitr.), Vitr. 2, 9, 1 .

prae-sēmĭno.opening: , no perf. , , v. a. , to sow or plant beforehand (post-class.). Lit. : non nati sunt homines tamquam ex draconis dentibus praeseminati, Lact. 6, 10 : vis naturalis, et quasi praeseminata, Aug Gen. ad Lit. 3, 14.— Trop.…

praesensĭo.opening: praesentio . A foreboding , presentiment (class.; syn. praesagium): praesensio et scientia rerum futurarum, Cic. Div. 1, 1, 1 : praedictiones et praesensiones rerum futurarum, id. N. D. 2, 3, 7 .— Absol. : per exta…

praesentālis.opening: adj. praesens , present (post-class.): milites, Cod. Just. 12, 36, 18 : domestici, ib. 17, 4 .

praesentānĕus.opening: adj. praesens . Momentary , instantaneous (late Lat.): commotio, Lact. de Ira Dei, 21, 8.— That operates quickly or immediately (post-Aug.): remedium, Plin. 21, 31, 105, § 180 : venenum, id. 24, 1, 1, § 2 : (remedium)…

praesentārius.opening: adj. id. , that is at hand , ready , quick , present (ante- and post-class. for praesens): id quod mali (haruspices) promittunt, praesentarium est (opp.: pro spisso evenit), happens immediately, Plaut. Poen. 3, 5, 47 :…

praesentātĭo.opening: praesento , a placing before , a showing , representation , exhibition (post-class.): tironis, Cod. Just. 12, 28, 2 (al. praestatio): adhuc in comminatione est (judicium), nondum in praesentatione, Aug. in Psa. 59, 6 ;…

praesentĭa.opening: plur. , v. praesens, s. v. praesum fin.

prae-sentĭo.opening: (collat. form praesentisse for praesensisse, Pac. Pan. Theod. 3 ), v. a. , to feel or perceive beforehand , to have a presentiment of , to presage , divine (class.): ni haec praesensisset canes, Plaut. Trin. 1, 2, 135 :…

praesentisco.opening: v. inch. a. [praesentio], to begin to have a presentiment of , Ter. Heaut. 4, 5, 21 , acc. to Prisc. p. 824 P. (al. persentisceres).

praesento.opening: , no perf. (praesentisse, Pac. ap. Pan. Theod. 3), , v. a. praesens , to place before , exhibit to view , to show , present , hold out (post-Aug.): sarcitis bubulas carnes praesentat, looks like, Plin. 37, 10 , 67, §…

prae-sĕpultus.opening: Part. [sepelio], buried beforehand (post-class.), Quint. Decl. 9 ; Amm. 14, 11, 21 .

prae-sĕro.opening: v. a. , to sow beforehand (post-class.): semina laetitiae, Paul. Nol. Carm. 32, 445 .

praesertim.opening: adv. prae-sero; cf. praecipue, from praecipio, qs. connected beforehand , serves to add an important argument or condition (hence most freq. joined with cum and si), especially , chiefly , principally , particularly ,…

prae-servĭo.opening: v. a. , to serve as a slave (ante- and post-class.). Lit. : alicui, Plaut. Am. prol. 124 .— Trop. : verbum neque numeris, neque generibus praeserviens, Gell. 1, 7, 6 .

prae-servo.opening: v. a. , to observe beforehand (post-class.): aliquid, Cael. Aur. Acut. 3, 8 : liberum se a dominationibus, Hilar. in Psa. 118, 16, 3.

praesĕs.opening: ( gen. plur. praesidium, Flor. 2, 17, 16 ), adj. and subst. [praesideo]. Sitting before a thing, to guard , take care of , or direct it; presiding , protecting , guarding , defending : locus, a place of refuge, Plaut.…

prae-sicco.opening: v. a. , to dry beforehand (post-class.), Cael. Aur. Tard. 2, 14, 217 ; 4, 3, 53 .—Hence, , , dried beforehand (post-class.): succus sole praesiccatus, App. Herb. 124 .

prae-siccus.opening: adj. , very dry (post-class.): vulnera, Prud. στεφ . 5, 141.

praesĭdālis.opening: or , , adj. praeses , of or belonging to the governor of a province , gubernatorial (postclass.): jus, Treb. Poll. XXX. Tyr. 24: jussio, Cod. Just. 4, 24, 11 : judicium, ib. 9, 1, 18 : officium, Amm. 28, 1, 5 :…

praesĭdātus.opening: ( ), , praeses , the office of governor of a province , governorship (post-class.): Dalmatiae, Vop. Carin. 17 : praesidatu regere, Aur. Vict. Caes. 29 ; Dig. 27, 1, 6 .

prae-sĭdĕo.grammar: sēdi ēre v. n. and a.
prae-sĭdĕo.opening: (praesīdi in best MSS., Tac. A. 1, 76 ), , v. n. and a. [sedeo], to sit before or in front of. Lit. (mostly postclass. and rare): pro aede Capitolini Jovis praesidere, Suet. Aug. 26 .— Transf. , in time, to sit…

praesīdĕro.opening: v. n. prae-sidus , to be in advance of the constellations : praesiderare dicitur, cum maturius hiberna tempestas movetur, quasi ante sideris tempus, Paul. ex Fest. p. 223 Müll.; cf. Plin. 18, 25, 57, § 207 .

praesĭdĭārĭus.opening: adj. praesidium . Lit. In gen., that serves for defence or protection (not in Cic. or Cæs.): praesidiarii milites, garrison soldiers, Liv. 29, 8 ; cf.: dicti praesidiarii milites ante alios collocati qui erant, aut in…

praesĭdĭŏlum.opening: dim. praesidium , a small garrison , Not. Tir. p. 56 .

praesĭdĭor.opening: v. dep. id. , to watch , guard : praesidior, φρουρῶ , Gloss. Lat. Gr.

praesĭdĭum.opening: praeses . Lit. , a presiding over; hence, defence , protection , help , aid , assistance; esp. of soldiers who are to serve as a guard , garrison , escort , or convoy : proficisci praesidio suis, Nep. Ages. 3 :…

praesignātĭo.opening: praesigno , a presignifying (eccl. Lat.), Aug. c. Faust. 22, 83.

praesignātor.opening: id. , one who marks out or designates beforehand , Inscr. Fabr. p. 38 , n. 184; Inscr. Murat. 915, 6 .

praesignĭfĭcātĭo.opening: praesignifico , a showing or signifying beforehand , presignification (eccl. Lat.): praesignificatio et figura majoris rei, Lact. 7, 15 .

prae-signĭfĭco.opening: v. a. , to show or signify beforehand , to foreshow , presignify (only in the foll. passages): hominibus quae sint futura, Cic. Div. 1, 38, 82 ; 2, 49, 101 .

prae-signis.opening: adj. signum , distinguished before or above others , remarkable , illustrious , excellent ( poet. ): praesignia tempora cornu, Ov. M. 15, 611 : praesignis facie, id. A. A. 3, 773 ; id. F. 6, 628 : hastā, Stat. S. 4, 8,…

prae-signo.opening: v. a. , to mark before (ante-class. and post-Aug.): ad summum praesignato (al. pertundito), Cato, R. R. 154 : furunculos, Plin. 28, 4, 7, § 36 .

prae-sĭpĭo.opening: v. a. sapio , to feel beforehand , have a presentiment of : praesagire est praedivinare, praesipere, Fest. s. v. praesagire, p. 223 Müll.; cf.: adsipere et praesipere dicebant antiqui a sapiendo, Paul. ex Fest. s. v.…

prae-sŏlĭdus.opening: adj. , very solid (late Lat.). Lit. , Coripp. Laud. Just. 3, 291 .— Trop. , very firm , very constant , or steadfast : praesolidum Simonem dignum cognomine Petri, Juvenc. 1, 436 .

prae-sŏno.opening: v. n. and a. To sound before ( poet. ): praesonuit solemni tibia cantu (al. personuit), Ov. Am. 3, 13, 11 .— To sound louder than , to sound above; with acc. : qui posset avena Praesonuisse chelyn, Calp. Ecl. 4, 65 .

prae-spargo.opening: ( ), , v. a. , to scatter or strew before , Lucr. 5, 738 .

prae-spĕcŭlor.opening: v. dep. , to examine into beforehand (late Lat.), Rustic. c. Aceph. p. 1233; hence, part. in pass. signif.: utilitate praespeculata, Amm. 25, 8, 11 .

prae-spēro.opening: v. a. , to hope beforehand (eccl. Lat.): qui praenunciabatur, ille et praesperabatur, Tert. adv. Marc. 5, 17 .

praespĭcĭo.opening: v. a. prae-specio , to look at before , to regard beforehand , Not. Tir. p. 43 ; Cael. Aur. Tard. 1, 4, 83 .

praestābĭlis.opening: adj. 2. praesto , preeminent , distinguished , excellent (class.; usually only of things concr. and abstr.): res magnitudine praestabiles, Cic. de Or. 2, 85, 347 : praestabilis insignisque virtus, id. Har. Resp. 19, 41…

Praestāna.opening: id. , the goddess of excellence , who was worshipped because Romulus had surpassed all others in throwing javelins: Praestana est, ut perhibetis, dicta, quod Quirinus in jaculi missione cunctorum praestiterit viribus,…

praestans.opening: Part. and P. a. , from 2. praesto.

praestanter.opening: adv. , v. 2. praesto, P. a. fin.

praestantĭa.opening: praestans , preeminence , superiority , excellence (class.): excellentia praestantiaque animantium reliquorum, over other creatures, Cic. Off. 1, 28, 97 : virtutis, ingenii, fortunae, pre-eminence in, id. Lael. 19, 70 :…

praestātĭo.opening: 2. praesto . Lit. , a guaranty , warranty (post-Aug.): ut ad praestationem scribant, if they pledge themselves for the truth of what they write, Sen. Brev. Vit. 13, 9 ; Dig. 45, 1, 2 .— Transf. , in gen., payment of any…

praestātor.opening: 2. praesto , a surety (post - class.): qui advocantur ut praestatores, Front. Col. praef. p. 128 Goes.

praestergus.opening: Plaut. Ps. 1, 2, 30 ; v. Ritschl ad h. l.

prae-sterno.opening: v. a. , to strew or spread beforehand , to prepare (mostly anteand post-class.): eo praesternebant folia farferi (al. prosternebant), Plaut. Poen. 2, 32 : altaria, to prepare, Stat. S. 3, 2, 114 : jubet serta et elysios…

praestĕs.opening: 2. praesto , in relig. lang., an epithet of deities, presiding , protecting; as subst. , a protector , guardian , president , etc. ( poet. and post-class.): praestitem in eādem significatione dicebant antiqui, quā nunc…

praestī^gĭae.opening: (rare in the sing. ; praestigiae, Prud. Peristeph. 2, 86 ), praestinguo , deceptions , illusions , jugglers' tricks , sleights , feats of legerdemain; lit. and trop. (class.; cf. captio): patent praestigiae, Plaut.…

praestigĭātor.opening: praestigiae , a juggler , cheat , impostor , deceiver (anteclass. and post-Aug.): praestigiator hic quidem Poenus probu' est, Plaut. Poen. 5, 3, 6 ; id. Aul. 4, 4, 3 ; Sen. Ep. 45, 8 : pervicaci praestigiator actu, the…

praestigĭātrix.opening: praestigiator , she who plays tricks , juggles , or deceives (Plautin.), Plaut. Am. 2, 2, 150 ; id. Truc. 1, 2, 31 Spengel ad loc.

praestigĭo.opening: v. a. praestigiae , to deceive by juggling tricks : illa tibi numinis praestigiat divinatio, Jul. Val. Rer. Gest. Alex. M. 1, 63 .

praestigĭor.opening: v. dep. id. , to practise sleight of hand : praestigior, ψηφοπαικτῶ , Gloss. Cyrill.

praestigĭōsus.opening: adj. id. , full of deceitful tricks , delusive (post-class.), Gell. 7, 14, 11 : nihil praestigiosum, aut subdolum, Arn. 1, 32 .

praestigĭum.opening: a delusion , illusion , trick : Γοητεία , praestigium, Gloss. ad Prud. Onom. Vet.: praestigiis absolvi, Amm. 14, 11, 23 .

prae-stinguo.opening: , a false read. for praestringo, q. v.

praestĭno.opening: v. a. 1. praes , to buy , purchase (ante- and post-class.): ego eo in macellum, ut piscium quidquid ibi'st, pretio praestinem, Plaut. Ps. 1, 2, 36 : piscis praestinatum abire, id. Capt. 4, 2, 68 ; cf.: praestinare apud…

praestĭtor.opening: 2. praesto , a giver (post-class.): praestitor et tributor, App. Trism. p. 92 .

prae-stĭtŭo.opening: v. a. statuo , to determine or appoint beforehand , to prescribe (class.; syn.: praefinio, praescribo): ei rei dies Haec praestituast proxuma, Plaut. Ps. 1, 1, 59 ; 2, 2, 29 : diem praestituit operi faciundo, Cic. Verr.…

praestō.opening: (old collat. form , acc. to Curtius Valerianus in Cassiod. p. 2289 P.: qui praestu sunt, Inscr. Carina Via Appia, 1, p. 217. In later time as adj. : , , um: bonorum officio praestus fui, Inscr. Grut. 669, 4 ), adv. dat.…

prae-sto.grammar: ĭti ĭtum, 1 v. n. and a.
prae-sto.opening: (post-class. also praestāvi), ātum or , v. n. and a. Neutr. , to stand before or in front. Lit. : dum primae praestant acies, Luc. 4, 30 .— Trop. , to stand out , be superior , to distinguish one's self , to be…

praestōlātio.opening: praestolor , the waiting for , expectation (late Lat.): praestolatio impiorum furor, Vulg. Prov. 11, 23 : praestolatio tua non auferetur, id. ib. 23, 18 ; id. Job, 17, 15.

praestōlor.opening: ( inf. paragog. praestolarier, Plaut. Ep. 2, 2, 33 ; act. collat. form praestolaras, Liv. And. ap. Non. 475, 32 : praestolabo, Turp. ap. ib. 475, 31 ; cf. App. M. 5, 20 ), 1, v. dep. n. and a. [1. praesto], to stand…

prae-strangŭlo.opening: v. a. , to choke , deprive of breath (post-class.): ne anxium oratorem praestrangulet, i. e. ne cogat tacere, Auct. Quint. Decl. 3 .

praestrictĭo.opening: praestringo , a binding fast , binding up (eccl. Lat.): praestrictio sensūs (al. praestructio), Tert. Res. Carn. 49 .

prae-stringo.opening: v. a. , to bind fast or hard , to bind or tie up; to squeeze tight , compress , etc. Lit. ( poet. and in post-Aug. prose): praestrictā fauce, Ov. Ib. 551 : praestricta manus, Sen. Troad. 560 : pollices vincire, nodoque…

praestructim.opening: adv. praestructus , with preparation (eccl. Lat.): ut ad hominem praestructim perveniretur, Tert. Pall. 3 .

praestructĭo.opening: praestruo , a foundation , preparation (eccl. Lat.), Tert. adv. Marc. 4, 14 .

praestructūra.opening: id. , a foundation , preparation (eccl. Lat.): evangelii, Tert. adv. Marc. 4, 2 .

praestructus.opening: Part. and P. a. , from praestruo.

prae-strŭo.opening: v. a. , to build before , as a preparation for other buildings, to lay a foundation : praestructa (opp. ea) quae superposita incumbent, Col. 1, 5, 9 .— Transf. , to build up in front , to block or stop up , to make…

prae-stultus.opening: adj. , extremely foolish : praestultus, πάνυ ἀνόητος , Gloss. Cyrill.

prae-stŭpesco.opening: v. inch. n. , to be greatly astonished : ad quam fortunam ceteris praestupescentibus, Jul. Val. Rer. Gest. Alex. M. 1, 66 .

prae-stŭpĭdus.opening: adj. , very senseless , very stupid (late Lat.): praestupido corde, Juvenc. 4, 200 .

prae-sūdo.opening: v. n. , to sweat before ( poet. ). Lit. : dum matutinis praesudat solibus aër, Claud. Rapt. Pros. 2, 120 .— — Trop. , to exert one's self beforehand , Stat. Th. 6, 4 .

praesul.opening: praesilio , one who leaps or dances before others , a dancer in public , public dancer. Lit. (class.), Cic. Div. 1, 26, 55 ; 2, 66, 136 .— In partic., the leader of the Salii, who annually leaped and danced through the…

praesŭlātus.opening: praesulor , the office of a superintendent (eccl. Lat.), Cassiod. Hist. 2, 3 al.

praesŭlor.opening: v. n. praesul , to be a superintendent (eccl. Lat.), Ps.-Aug. ad Fratr. Erem. Serm. 15 .

prae-sulsus.opening: adj. salsus , salted very much , very salt (post-Aug.): adeps, Col. 6, 2, 7 .

praesultātor.opening: praesulto , one who leaps or dances before others , a public dancer (only in Livy), Liv. 2, 36, 2 ; cf. praesulto.

prae-sulto.opening: v. n. salto , to leap or dance before (only in Livy): praesultare hostium signis, Liv. 7, 10, 3 (cf. praesultator).

praesultor.opening: praesilio , one who leaps or dances before others , a public dancer (post-class. for praesul), Lact. 2, 7, 20 ; Val. Max. 1, 7, 4 .

prae-sum.opening: v. n. , to be before a thing; hence, to be set over , to preside or rule over , to have the charge or command of , to superintend (class.). With dat. : omnibus Druidibus praeest unus, Caes. B. G. 6, 12 : qui oppido…

praesūmenter.opening: adv. praesumo , = praesumpte, confidently , boldly (late Lat.): aliquem defendere, Hilar. Op. Hist. Fragm. 3, 27; Cassiod. Var. 5, 15 .

praesūmo.grammar: mpsi and msi, mptum and mtum, 3 v. a.
praesūmo.opening: v. a. , to take before , take first or beforehand , take to one's self (syn.: praeoccupo). Lit. ( poet. and in post-Aug. prose): neve domi praesume dapes, Ov. A. A. 3, 757 : allium, Plin. 25, 5, 21, § 50 : praesumere…

praesumptĭo.opening: praesumo . A taking beforehand , a using or enjoying in advance , anticipation : rerum, quas assequi cupias, praesumptio ipsa jucunda est, Plin. Ep. 4, 15, 11 : bonae famae praesumptione perfrui, id. ib. 9, 3, 1 .— In…

praesumptĭōsē.opening: ( ), adv. praesumptiosus , boldly , presumptuously (postclass.): praesumptiose arroganterque loqui, Sid. Ep. 7, 6 .

praesumptĭōsus.opening: ( ), , adj. praesumptio , full of boldness , presumptuous (post-class.): juvenis (al. praesumptuosum), Sid. Ep. 1, 11 .— Transf. : vestigia, Sid. Ep. 1, 1 .

praesumptīvē.opening: adv. praesumo , presumptuously (late Lat.), Cassiod. in Psa. 25, 2 ; Aug. c. Faust. 24, 1.

praesumptor.opening: id. . One who takes possession beforehand , a preoccupier (post-class.), Cassiod. Var. 1, 18 .— A bold , confident , reckless , or presumptuous person , Tert. Poen. 6 : Petrus ex egregio praesumptore tam creber negator…

praesumptōrĭus.opening: adj. praesumptor , presumptuous (eccl. Lat.), Aug. Collat. c. Maxim, 13.—Hence, , adv. , boldly , confidently , presumptuously : praesumptorie aliquid elocutus, Tert. adv. Marc. 4, 41 .

praesumptrix.opening: id. , a presumptuous person (eccl. Lat.), Petr. Chrysol. Serm. 109 .

praesumptus.opening: ( ), , Part. and P. a. , from praesumo.

prae-sŭo.opening: v. a. , to sew over , sew up; hence, to cover over ( poet. and in post-Aug. prose): hasta foliis praesuta, Ov. M. 11, 9 : surculos recentibus coriis, Plin. 12, 19, 43, § 96 .

prae-surgo.opening: v. n. , to rise beforehand ( poet. ), Avien. Prognost. Arat. 172 .

prae-suspecto.opening: v. a. , to suspect beforehand , Jul. Val. Rer. Gest. Alex. M. 1, 43 .

prae-taedescit.opening: v. impers. , it disgusts beforehand : praetaedescit, praetaesus, Not. Tir. p. 177 .

prae-taesus.opening: feeling disgust beforehand : praetaedescit, praetaesus, Not. Tir. p. 177 .

prae-tango.opening: , no perf. , , v. a. , to touch beforehand or previously (postclass.). Lit. , Cael. Aur. Tard. 5, 7, 81 : leviter oleo Hispano praetactus, id. ib. 4, 3, 22 .— Transf. , to attack; of violent diseases: praetacta…

praetectĭo.opening: praetego , a covering over : oculorum, Cael. Aur. Acut. 1, 9 ; id. Tard. 3, 8, 131 .

prae-tĕgo.opening: v. a. , to cover over , to shelter , protect ( poet. and in postAug. prose): cavo praetegit aere caput (al. protegit), Prop. 3, 12 (4, 13), 12: quae somnium (tuum) saxa praetexerint, i. e. the rocks that sheltered your…

prae-tendo.opening: ( part. praetensus, Anthol. Lat. 3, 168, 5 ), , v. a. , to stretch forth or forward , to extend (syn. obtendo). Lit. : praetenta Tela, stretched forth, presented, Ov. M. 8, 341 : propagines e vitibus altius praetentos,…

prae-tĕner.opening: adj. , very soft or tender (post-Aug.): capnos, Plin. 25, 13, 99, § 156 .

praetentātus.opening: or , (only in abl. sing. ), praetento , a groping or feeling out one's way (postAug.), Plin. 11, 37, 52, § 140 .

prae-tento.opening: or , , v. a. To feel , search , or grope out beforehand , to examine previously , to estimate beforehand , anticipate (mostly poet. and in post-Aug. prose): praetentare baculo, luminis orbus, iter, Ov. Ib. 262 :…

praetentūra.opening: praetendo , a military guard on the boundaries of a province , a frontier-guard (post-class.): Mesopotamiae tractus praetenturis et stationibus servabantur agrariis, Amm. 14, 3, 2 .— A barricade , Amm. 14, 2, 4 .

prae-tĕnŭis.opening: adj. Very thin or slender (post-Aug.): folium pinūs, Plin. 16, 10, 16, § 38 : fila, id. 16, 31, 56, § 128 ; 19, 6, 34, § 116 : bracteae, id. 33, 6, 32, § 100 : pons, very narrow, id. 8, 50, 76, § 201 .—* Of sound, very…

prae-tĕpĕo.opening: v. n. , to glow before ; trop., of love ( poet. ): si tuus in quāvis praetepuisset amor, Ov. Am. 2, 3, 6 .

praeter.opening: adv. and prep. prae, with the demonstrative suffix ter, as in inter, subter, propter , signifies motion by or past , and hence, also, beyond , or rest outside a thing. Adv. , past , by , beyond (cf. praeterquam), in the…

praeter-ăgo.opening: , no perf. , , v. a. , to drive by or past ( poet. and post-class.): deversoria nota Praeteragendus (est) equus, Hor. Ep. 1, 15, 10 ; Jul. Val. Rer. Gest. Alex. M. 1, 3 .

praeter-bīto.opening: v. n. and a. , to go by , to pass (Plautin.): ne inter vias praeterbitamus, metuo, Plaut. Poen. 5, 3, 43 .—With acc. : cave praeterbitas ullas aedes, quin, etc., Plaut. Ep. 3, 4, 1 .

praeter-curro.opening: , no perf. , , v. n. and a. , to run past or by (post-class.): equis praetercurrentibus, Veg. Mil. 3, 24 : praetercursā Chalcedone, Amm. 22, 9, 3 .

praeter-dūco.opening: v. a. , to lead past or by (Plaut.): pompam, Plaut. Mil. 1, 1, 67 .

praetĕr-ĕā.opening: adv. is . Beyond this or that , besides : si eum reddis mihi, praeterea unum nummum ne duis, Plaut. Capt. 2, 2, 81 : nihilne vobis in mentem venit, quod praeterea Crasso requiratis? Cic. de Or. 1, 35, 60 : haec duo…

praetĕr-ĕo.opening: , and more freq. ĭi, ĭtum, īre ( fut. praeteriet, Vulg. Sap. 1, 8 ; id. Ecclus. 39, 37 ; Juvenc. 4, 159 ), v. n. and a. Neutr. To go by or past , to pass by : si nemo hac praeteriit, Plaut. Cist. 4, 2, 15 : ut arbitri…

praĕter-ĕquĭtans.opening: Part. [equito], riding by (only in Livy), Liv. 3, 61, 9 .

praeter-fĕro.opening: , no perf. , , v. a. , to carry by or past.—Pass. , to come , run , drive , or fly past (rare, not in Cic.): latebras eorum praeterlata acies est, Liv. 21, 55, 9 : pars vocum praeterlata, Lucr. 4, 569 (Lachm.…

praeter-flŭo.opening: v. n. , to flow by or past (class.). Lit. : aqua quae praeterfluat, Varr. R. R. 3, 16 .—With acc. : flumen, quod Valentiam praeterfluit, Sall. Fragm. ap. Prisc. p. 680 P.: amnis praeterfluens moenia, Liv. 41, 11, 3 .—…

praeter-fŭgĭo.opening: v. a. , to hasten by , pass over hastily : propositum exemplum, Ambros. Spirit. Sanc. 3, 11, 78 .

praeter-grĕdĭor.opening: v. dep. n. and a. [gradior], to walk or march by , to go or pass by (class.). Lit. : qui praetergrediebantur. Sall. ap. Non. 556, 19 : ut rapiat praetergredientes, Ambros. Abrah. 1, 5, 32 .—With acc. : castra, to pass…

praetĕr-hāc.opening: adv. hic , beyond this , besides , furthermore , moreover (Plaut.): si praeterhac unum verbum faxis hodie, ego tibi comminuam caput, Plaut. Rud. 4, 4, 73 ; id. Men. 1, 2, 3 : non patiar praeterhac, id. ib. 5, 1, 25 ;…

praetĕr-inquīro.opening: v. a. , to inquire further (post-class.): in negotium, Amm. 15, 5, 12 .

praetĕrĭtĭo.opening: praetereo . A passing over , omission (post-class.), Cod. Just. 6, 29, 4 .— Rhet. t. t., a passing over = παράλειψις , Mart. Cap. 5, § 523 .

praetĕrĭtus.opening: Part. and P. a. , from praetereo.

praeter-lābor.opening: v. dep. n. and a. Lit. , to glide or flow by , to fly or run past : praeterlabentia flumina, Quint. 10, 3, 24 .—With acc. : tumulum, Verg. A. 6, 874 : hanc (tellurem) pelago praeterlabare necesse est, to sail past, id.…

praeter-lambo.opening: v. a. , to lick , bathe , or touch in passing , to flow by (post-class.): oppidum, quod Mosa fluvius praeterlambit, Amm. 17, 2, 4 .

praeter-lŭens.opening: Part. [luo], washing as it flows past (post-class.): fluvius, App. M. 6, p. 177, 40 .

praeter-mĕo.opening: v. n. and a. , to go by or past ( poet. and post-class. prose): saepe salutantum tactu praeterque meantum (in tmesi), Lucr. 1, 317 : amoenitas locorum invitet praetermeantem, Ambros. in Luc. 4, 2 .—With acc. : stellas…

praetermissĭo.opening: praetermitto . A leaving out , omission : sine ullius formae praetermissione, Cic. Top. 7, 31 .— A passing over , neglecting : praetermissio aedilitatis, Cic. Off. 2, 17, 58 .

praeter-mitto.opening: v. a. To allow or permit to go by , to let pass (class.; syn.: omitto, neglego). In gen.: nullum diem, Cic. Att. 9, 14, 2 : nullam occasionem profectionis, Auct. B. Afr. 1: neminem, Cic. Fam. 11, 21, 1 .— In partic. To…

praeter-monstrans.opening: Part. [monstro], pointing out besides , pointing out or showing another (post-class.), Gell. 20, 10, 6 .

praeternāvĭgātĭo.opening: praeternavigo , a sailing by (post-Aug.), Plin. 4, 12, 19, § 57 (al. praenavigatio).

praeter-nāvĭgo.opening: v. n. and a. , to sail by or past (post-Aug.): vitans praeterpavigantium officia, Suet. Tib. 12 ; Flor. 3, 8, 3 .—With acc. : Baianum sinum, Suet. Ner 27 : Seyllam, App. de Deo Socr. 24, p. 55, 30 .

prae-tĕro.opening: v. a. , to rub off or wear down in front (ante-class. and in postAug. prose): anum lima praeterunt, Plaut. Men. 1, 1, 9 ; Plin. 11, 37, 63 .— To rub down beforehand : oleum amygdali amari praetritum, Cael. Aur. Acut. 1,…

praeterpropter.opening: prep. with acc. [praeter-propter], thereabout , more or less (ante-class.), Enn., Cato, and Varr. ap. Gell. 19, 10, 10 (see the whole passage respecting the phrase, and Hand, Turs. 4, 544 sq.).

praeter-quam.opening: (separate, praeter enim quam, Cic. Leg. 3, 19, 45 ; Plaut. Pers. 3, 1, 38 infra), adv. , beyond , besides , except , save (class.): neque, praeterquam quas ipse amor molestias Habet, addas, Ter. Eun. 1, 1, 32 : verbum…

praeterrādo.grammar: ĕre, a false reading for praeterea radit

praeter-sum.opening: v. n. , to be out of , not present at (eccl. Lat.): ipsis rebus praetersumus, Tert. Apol. 38 .

praetervectĭo.opening: praeterveho , a riding , sailing , or passing by : praetervectio omnium, qui, etc., Cic. Verr. 2, 5, 66, § 170 .

praeter-vĕhor.opening: (separate, praeter erant vecti, Ov. M. 13, 713 ), 3, v. dep. n. and a.; prop., to be borne past , to drive , ride , or sail by (class.). Lit. : qui praetervehebantur, Cic. Fin. 5, 18, 49 : praetervehens equo, riding by,…

praeter-verto.opening: v. a. , to go or pass by (post-Aug.): solem, Plin. 2, 71, 73, § 181 .

praeter-vŏlo.opening: v. n. and a. , to fly by or past (class.). Lit. : praetervolans aquila, Suet. Claud. 7 .—With acc. : quem praetervolat Ales, Cic. Arat. 412 .— Transf. , to fly or sail over , fly across : hasta medias praetervolat…

prae-testor.opening: v. dep. a. , to bear witness to beforehand (eccl. Lat.): praetestata viam vitae, Tert. Carm. adv. Marc. 3, 176 .

Praetetĭānus.opening: adj. , of or belonging to the Praetetii: vina, Plin. 14, 6, 8, § 61 .

prae-texo.opening: v. a. , to weave before or in front , to fringe , edge , border. Lit. (mostly poet. ): purpura saepe tuos fulgens praetexit amictus, Ov. P. 3, 8, 7 : glaucas comis praetexere frondes, weave around, Val. Fl. 3, 436 ;…

praetextātus.opening: adj. praetexta, under praetexo fin. B. 1. , clothed with or wearing the toga praetexta (class.): Clodius, qui numquam antea praetextatus fuisset, Cic. Pis. 4, 8 : pupillus, Cic. Verr. 2, 1, 58, § 151 ; id. Phil. 2, 18,…

praetextus.opening: (but found only in abl. sing.; cf. praetextum, s. v. praetexo fin. ), praetexo . Outward appearance , show , ornament , display , splendor , consequence (post-Aug.): majore praetextu, Tac. H. 1, 19 : praetextu senatūs,…

prae-tĭmĕo.opening: v. a. and n. , to fear beforehand , to be in fear , be afraid ( poet. and in post-Aug. prose): sibi praetimet, Plaut. Am. prol. 29 : nil est miserius, quam praetimere, Sen. Ep. 98, 7 : praetimens ne sibi desit…

prae-tĭmĭdus.opening: adj. , very fearful , very timid (late Lat.), Auct. Carm. de Jona et Ninive, 65.

prae-tingo.opening: v. a. , to dip in or moisten beforehand ( poet. and in postclass. prose): semina practincta veneno, Ov. M. 7, 123 : aqua, in quā fuerit candens ferrum praetinctum, Cael. Aur. Tard. 1, 4 .

prae-tondĕo.opening: v. a. , to clip in front (post-class.): cum ejus pinnas praetotonderit, App. M. 5, p. 172, 30 .

praetor.opening: for praeitor, from praeeo . Prop., a leader , head , chief , president : regio imperio duo sunto: iique praeeundo, judicando, consulendo, praetores, judices, consules appellantor, Cic. Leg. 3, 3, 8 .—So, in gen., of the…

praetōrĭānus.opening: adj. praetor , of or belonging to the prœtor , prœtorian (post-class.): tutor, Ulp. Reg. tit. 12: pretia, money earned by the prœtor's administration of justice, Aug. Conf. 6, 10 .

praetōrīcĭus.opening: or , , adj. id. , prœtorian (post-Aug.): praetoricia corona, received at the public games from the prœtor, Mart. 8, 33, 1 .— Subst. , one who has been prœtor , an ex-prœtor , Inscr. Grut. 398, 1 .

praetōrĭŏlum.opening: dim. praetorium , a small country-seat (post-class.), Inscr. Mus. di Mantova, p. 23; Vulg. Ezech. 27, 6 .

praetōrĭum.opening: praetor . A general's tent , Liv. 10, 33 : dictatoris, id. 7, 12 : imperatoris Aequorum, id. 3, 25 ; Caes. B. C. 1, 76 .— Transf. A council of war (because held in the general's tent): praetorio dimisso, Liv. 30, 5 ;…

praetōrĭus.opening: adj. id. . Of or belonging to the prœtor or prœtors , prœtorian : jus, proceeding from the prœtor, consisting of his decisions, Cic. Off. 1, 10, 33 : comitia, the election of prœtor, Liv. 10, 22 : potestas, the office…

prae-torquĕo.opening: , no perf. , , v. a. , to twist forwards , twist round (ante-class. and post-Aug.). Lit. : praetorto capite et recurvato, Col. 3, 18 .— Trop. : praetorquete injuriae collum, Plaut. Rud. 3, 2, 12 .

prae-torrĕo.opening: v. a. , to heat beforehand (late Lat.): igne praetorrenda harena, Cael. Aur. Tard. 3, 8, 112 .

prae-torrĭdus.opening: adj. , very hot , very dry ( poet. ): aestas, Calp. Ecl. 2, 80 .

prae-tractātus.opening: (only in abl. sing. ), a preliminary treatise , an introduction , preface (eccl. Lat.), Tert. Fuga in Persecut. 4 .

prae-trĕpĭdans.opening: Part. [trepido], trembling greatly , very hasty or impatient ( poet. ): mens praetrepidans avet vagari, Cat. 46, 7 .

prae-trĕpĭdus.opening: adj. , trembling very much (post-Aug.). Lit. : cor, palpitating, throbbing, Pers. 2, 52 .— Transf. , trembling greatly , very anxious , disquieted : praetrepidus vixit, Suet. Tib. 63 : Romam praetrepidus rediit, id.…

prae-trunco.opening: v. a. , to cut off before or in front , to cut off , clip (Plautin.): collos (for colla) tergoribus, Plaut. Capt. 4, 3, 2 : linguam alicui, id. Mil. 2, 3, 47 .

prae-tŭmĕo.opening: v. n. , to be puffed up beforehand (late Lat.).— Trop. : eloquii supercilio, Cassiod. Hist. Tripart. 1, 10 ; id. in Psa. 75, 12 .

prae-tŭmĭdus.opening: adj. , much swollen , puffed up ( poet. ): furor, Claud. in Ruf. 1, 225 : praetumidi supplex Orientis, id. II. Cons. Stil. 81 : mens, Juvenc. 584 .

praetūra.opening: praetor , the dignity or office of a prœtor , the prœtorship (class.), Cic. Mur. 26, 53 : praeturae jurisdictio, id. Fl. 3, 6 : praeturā se abdicare, id. Cat. 3, 6, 14 ; Tac. A. 3, 30 .— The term of office of a prœtor :…

praetūrīnus.opening: adj. praetura , of or belonging to the prœtorship , prœtorian , Not. Tir. p. 61 .

Praetūtĭi.opening: a people of Picenum. —Hence, , , adj. , Prœtutian : vina, Plin. 14, 6, 8, § 67 : pubes, Sil. 15, 571 .— , , adj. , Prœtutian : ager, Liv. 22, 9 ; 27, 43 ; Plin. 3, 13, 18, § 110 ; Inscr. Delfico dell' Inter. Pretuz. p.…

prae-ulcĕrātus.opening: Part. [ulcero], caused to ulcerate or made sore beforehand (post-class.): loca praeulcerata, Cael. Aur. Tard. 5, 1 , n. 18.

prae-umbrans.opening: Part. [umbro], casting a shade before. — Trop. , darkening , obscuring (post-Aug.), Tac. A. 14, 47 .

prae-ungo.opening: , no perf. , , v. a. , to smear or anoint before (post-class.): praeungendum est vulnus, Theod. Prisc. 1, 19 : digitus praeunctus adipe anserino, Cael. Aur. Tard. 4, 3, 45 .

prae-ūro.opening: v. a. , to burn before , burn at the end or point (class. but not in Cic.); esp. freq. in part. perf. : hasta praeusta, Liv. 1, 32 : stipites ab summo praeacuti et praeusti, Caes. B. G. 7, 73, 6 ; cf.: multae praeustae…

prae-vādo.opening: v. n. , to pass before. — Transf. , to be discharged from , rid of any thing, with gen. : Quintius dictaturam properat praevadere, Sen. Brev. Vit. 17, 6 .

prae-vălens.opening: Part. and P. a. , from praevaleo.

prae-vălĕo.opening: v. n. In gen., to be very or more able , to have distinguished power or influence; to have greater power or worth; to be superior or distinguished , have the superiority , prevail (not ante-Aug.; cf.: praesto, excello,…

praevălesco.opening: v. inch. n. [praevaleo], to become or grow very strong (postAug.): ante, quam arbor praevalescat, Col. 5, 6, 17 .

praevălĭdus.opening: adj. praevaleo , very strong (not in Cic. or Cæs.). Lit. Of persons: juvenis, Liv. 7, 5 : legiones, Vell. 2, 69, 2 : cohortes, Tac. H. 2, 28 .— Of things: manus, Ov. H. 9, 80 : ramus, Suet. Vesp. 5 .— Trop. , very…

prae-vallo.opening: v. a. , to fortify in front (post-class.): pontem, Auct. B. Alex. 19; Claud. ap. I. Cons. Stil. 2, 188.

prae-văpōro.opening: v. a. , to fumigate or perfume beforehand (post-class.): loca, Cael. Aur. Acut. 1, 3 : praevaporata loca, Theod. Prisc. 1, 2 .

praevārĭcātĭo.opening: praevaricor , a stepping out of the line of duty , a violation of duty; esp. of an advocate who has a secret understanding with the opposite party, the making of a sham accusation or defence , collusion , prevarication…

praevārĭcātor.opening: praevaricor , one who violates his duty; esp. of an advocate who is guilty of collusion with the opposite party, a sham accuser or defender , a prevaricator (class.): praevaricatores a praetergrediendo sunt vocitati,…

prae-vārĭcātrix.opening: praevaricator , she who transgresses or sins (eccl. Lat.), Aug. Ep. 89, 20 ; Hier. in Isa. 5, 12, 3 ; id. in Matt. 22, 7 ; Vulg. Jer. 3, 7 .

prae-vārĭcor.opening: v. dep. , to walk crookedly , not to walk straight. * Lit. : arator praevaricatur, makes a crooked furrow, Plin. 18, 19, 49, § 179 .— Trop. To walk crookedly in the discharge of one's duty , not to act uprightly; esp.…

prae-vārus.opening: adj. , very irregular or unsteady (very rare). Lit. : venarum pulsus praevaros (al. praeclaros, i. e. certos, distinctos), App. Flor. p. 362, 17 .— Trop. , very perverse : quid enim tam praevarum? Cic. Fragm. ap. Isid.…

prae-vĕhor.opening: v. dep. n. and a. To ride , fly , or flow before , in front , or past (not in Cic. or Cæs.): equites Romani praevecti, who had ridden before them, Liv. 9, 35 : praevectus equo, Verg. A. 7, 166 : praevectus ad Germanicum…

prae-vello.opening: v. a. , to tear away before , to tear away (ante- and post-class.), Laber. ap. Diom. p. 369 P.; Tert. adv. Gnost. 13 .

prae-vēlo.opening: v. a. , to veil or cover over; to conceal by placing before (late Lat.): flammea praevelatura pudorem, Claud. Rapt. Pros. 2, 325 : praevelans fronde secures, id. VI. Cons. Honor. 647 : amnem Tiberis domibus amoenis, id.…

prae-vēlox.opening: adj. , very fleet or swift (post-Aug.): praevelocibus camelis fugientes, Plin. 11, 31, 36, § 111 : memoria, Quint. 11, 2, 44 .

prae-vĕnĭo.opening: (in tmesi: praeque diem veniens, Verg. E. 8, 17 ), v. n. and a. , to come before , precede , get the start of , to outstrip , anticipate , to prevent (postAug.; for, in Cic. Off. 3, 7, 33 , the correct reading is…

praeventĭo.opening: praevenio , an anticipating (eccl. Lat.), Aug. c. Gaudent. 1, 14; Primas in Gal. 6.

praeventor.opening: id. , a kind of soldiers , perh. those who began the attack (post-class.), Amm. 18, 9, 3 .

praeventus.opening: (only in abl. sing. ), praevenio , a preventing (eccl. Lat.): mortis, Tert. adv. Marc. 5, 12 .

praeverbĭum.opening: prae-verbum . —In gram., a preposition (ante- and postclass.), Varr. L. L. 6 , §§ 38, 82 Müll.; Gell. 7, 7, 5 .

prae-vernat.opening: v. impers. , to be spring too early or before the time (postAug.): quando praevernat, when spring opens too soon, Plin. 18, 26, 65, § 239 .

prae-verro.opening: v. a. , to sweep or brush before ( poet. ): veste vias, Ov. Am. 3, 13, 24 : praeverrit cauda silices (al. perverrit), Verg. M. 23 .

prae-verto.opening: or , , v. a. , and (only in present tense) or ( inf. pass. paragog. praevortier, Plaut. Am. 3, 2, 39 ), , v. dep. To prefer : ne me uxorem praevertisse dicant prae republicā, Plaut. Am. 1, 3, 29 : si vacas animo, neque…

prae-vexātus.opening: Part. [vexo], ill-treated , abused , or impaired previously or very much (post-class.): aeger viribus praevexatus, Cael. Aur. Tard. 1, 1, 18 : praevexatae vires, id. Acut. 2, 32, 166 .

prae-vĭans.opening: Part. [vio], going before (eccl. Lat.), Ambros. in Luc. 3, 21 .

praevĭātor.opening: id. , a precursor , herald (eccl. Lat.), Ven. Fort., v. Hilar. 2, 9.

prae-vĭdĕo.opening: v. a. , to see first or beforehand , to foresee. Lit. ( poet. ): ictum venientem a vertice, Verg. A. 5, 444 : an, quia praevisos in aquā timet hostia cultros? Ov. F. 1, 327 : cultri in liquidā praevisi undā, Ov. M. 15,…

prae-vincio.opening: v. a. (postclass.). Lit. , to bind before or in front , to fetter : laqueo praevinctus, Gell. 15, 10, 2 . — Trop. : ferinis voluptatibus praevinctus, Gell. 19, 2, 3 .

prae-vĭrĭdans.opening: P. a. virido , being very green or verdant; transf., very blooming or vigorous (ante-class.), Laber. ap. Macr. S. 2, 7 .

prae-vĭrĭdis.opening: adj. , very green : color, Front. Aquaed. 7 dub. (al. perviridis).

praevīsē.opening: adv. praevideo , according to expectation (opp. inopinate), Aug. in Psa. 63, 7 .

prae-vĭtĭo.opening: v. a. , to corrupt or vitiate beforehand ( poet. and in post-class. prose): (gurgitem), Ov. M. 14, 55 : ex alio morbo praevitiati, Cael. Aur. Tard. 2, 1, 15 .

praevĭus.opening: adj. prae-via , going before , leading the way ( poet. ): praevius Aurorae, Solis Noctisque satelles, Cic. Arat. ap. Non. 65, 9 : nunc praevius anteit, Ov. M. 11, 65: praevia luci Pallantias, id. ib. 15, 190 ; Stat. Th.…

prae-vŏlo.opening: v. n. , to fly before or in advance (class.): grues in tergo praevolantium colla et capita reponunt, Cic. N. D. 2, 49, 125 : aquila velut dux viae praevolavit, Tac. H. 1, 62 (but the correct read., Plaut. Mil. 1, 1, 41…

pragma.opening: , = πρᾶγμα , a matter , affair , business (post-class.), Jul. Vict. Art. Rhet. 3, 4.

pragmătĭcārĭus.opening: pragmaticus , one who writes down and prepares imperial edicts , rescripts , and the like (postclass.), Cod. Just. 1, 23, 7 .

pragmătĭcus.opening: adj. , = πραγματικός , prop., skilled in business , esp. experienced in matters of law : pragmatici homines omnibus historiis cavere jubent et vetant credere, Cic. Att. 2, 20, 1 .—Hence, Subst. , , , = πραγματικός , one…

pramnĭon.opening: a precious stone , the darkest kind of rock crystal , Plin. 37, 10, 63, § 173 (al. promnium).

Pramnĭum vīnum.opening: = Πράμνιος οἶνος , a kind of wine in the neighborhood of Smyrna , Plin. 14, 4, 6, § 54 .

prandĕo.grammar: di sum, 2 v. n. and a.
prandĕo.opening: (prandidi, Diom. p. 364 ), , v. n. and a. [prandium]. Neutr. , to take breakfast , to breakfast (v. prandium; class.): hic rex cum aceto pransurus est et sale, Plaut. Rud. 4, 2, 32 : prandi in navi, id. Men. 2, 3, 50 :…

prandĭcŭlum.opening: dim. id. , breakfast : prandicula antiqui dicebant, quae nunc jentacula, Fest. p. 250 Müll.; cf.: prandicula, jentacula, Paul. ex Fest. p. 251 ib.

prandĭŏlum.opening: dim. id. , a small breakfast , Not. Tir. p. 166 .

prandĭum.opening: Sanscr. prep-, pra-, before; Gr. πρῳην; Dor. πράν, early; and Lat. dies; hence, early in the day, sc. that taken or eaten , a late breakfast , luncheon (cf.: jentaculum, cena), usually taken at or soon after noon,…

pransĭto.opening: v. freq. n. and a. [prandeo]. Neutr. , to breakfast , to eat breakfast or luncheon (mostly ante- and postclass.): ad rivum accumbentes viatores pransitare solent, Vitr. 8, 3 : pransitans et cenitans, Lampr. Elag. 27 .—…

pransor.opening: id. , one that eats breakfast , that partakes of a meal in the forenoon , a guest (ante-class.): bonum anteponam prandium pransoribus, Plaut. Men. 2, 2, 2 : cum jam manus pransores lavarent, Veran. ap. Macr. S. 3, 6, 14…

pransōrĭus.opening: adj. pransor , of or belonging to breakfast or luncheon (postAug.): candelabrum pransorium, for humile, fit to breakfast by (when a lamp was not needed), Quint. 6, 3, 99 .

prapĕdīlon.opening: , and , , , the herb lion's-foot , also called leontopo dion, App. Herb. 7 .

Prasĭae.opening: , = Πρασιαί , a township in Attica , Liv. 31, 45 .

Prăsĭānē.opening: an island in the Indus , Plin. 6, 20, 23, § 71 .—Hence, , , adj. , of or belonging to Prasiane : gens, Plin. 6, 22, 24, § 82 .

Prăsĭi.opening: a tribe on the Ganges , Plin. 6, 19, 22, § 70 .

prăsĭnātus.opening: adj. prasinus , having a leek-green garment (post-Aug.): ostiarius prasinatus, Petr. S. 28 .

prăsĭnĭānus.opening: adj. id. , leekgreen , prasinian (post-class.): equus, i. e. of the leek-green party of charioteers in the circus , Capit. Ver. 6: si prasinianus es, Petr. 70 .

prăsĭnus.opening: adj. , = πράσινος , leek-green , prasinous : pila prasina, Petr. 27 : color, Plin. 37, 10, 67, § 181 : de nostrā prasinā est synthesis empta toga, Mart. 10, 29, 4 : flabellum, id. 3, 82, 11 : factio, the party of…

prăsĭon.opening: and , , , = πράσιον , an herb , white horehound , Cels. 5, 11 ; Plin. 20, 17, 67, § 175 .

prăsĭus.opening: , = πράσιος ( λίθος ), prase , a precious stone of a leek-green color , Plin. 37, 8, 34, § 113 .

prăsŏīdes.opening: , = πρασοειδής (leekcolored, leek-green, prasinous), a kind of topaz , perh. a species of jasper , Plin. 37, 8, 32, § 109 .

prăson.opening: , = πράσον , a marine shrub resembling a leek , Plin. 13, 25, 48, § 135 (al. grason).

prātens.opening: adj. pratum , green , meadow-green , grassy : nemus pratentibus viretis amoenum, App. M. 8, p. 209 fin.

prātensis.opening: adj. id. , growing or found in meadows , meadow- : fungi, Hor. S. 2, 4, 20 : faenum, Col. 6, 3 : flores, Plin. 21, 8, 25, § 49 : pastinaca, id. 21, 15, 50, § 86 .

prātŭlum.opening: dim. pratum , a small meadow (class.): in pratulo consedimus, Cic. Brut. 6, 24 : in Siciliae pratulis, Arn. 5, 173 .

prātum.opening: (collat. form , , Gromat. Vet. p. 322, 5) [root prat-; Sanscr. prath, to spread out; cf. Gr. πλατύς, πλάτανος ], a meadow (class.). Lit. : pratum irriguum, aut siccum, Cato, R. R. 8, 1 : stercorare, id. ib. 8, 50 :…

prāvĭ-cordĭus.opening: , and , , adj. pravus-cor , that has a depraved heart (eccl. Lat.), Vulg. Ecclus. 3, 28 ; Aug. in Psa. 124, 2 ; 146, 7 .

prāvĭtas.opening: pravus , crookedness , inequality , irregularity , deformity (class.). Lit. : pravitas membrorum, Cic. Tusc. 4, 13, 29 : corporis pravitates, id. Leg. 1, 19, 51 : oris, a distorting of the mouth in speaking, id. de Or.…

prāvus.opening: adj. cf. Sanscr. prahva, crooked , crooked , not straight , distorted , misshapen , deformed (opp. rectus; class.). Lit. : prava, cubantia, prona, supina atque absona tecta, Lucr. 4, 517 : si quae in membris prava, aut…

Praxăgŏras.opening: , = Πραξαγόρας , a physician of Cos , instructor of Plistonicus , Cels. praef.; Plin. 20, 4, 23, § 52 ; 26, 2, 6, § 10 .

Praxillēus.opening: or , , adj. , of or belonging to the Sicyonian poetess Praxilla : Praxilleum metrum Ionicum majus trimetrum brachycatalectum, Serv. p. 1824 P.: id autem, quod trochaeum recipit, Praxillium dixerunt, ut metrum Praxillae…

Praxĭtĕles.opening: , = Πραξιτέλης , a celebrated Greek sculptor , Prop. 3, 7, 15 (4, 8, 16); cf. Cic. Verr. 2, 4, 2, § 4 ; Plin. 34, 8, 19, § 69 ; 36, 5, 4, § 21 .—Hence, , , adj. , = Πραξιτέλειος , of or belonging to Praxiteles ,…

prĕcābĭlis.opening: adj. precor , entreating , praying : precabile, δεητικόν, εὐκτικόν , Gloss. Lat. Gr.

prĕcābundus.opening: adj. id. , entreating , beseeching (late Lat.), Pac. Pan. 36 .

prĕcāmen.opening: id. , a praying , prayer , entreaty ( poet. ): fundens precamina mille, Poët. ap. Wernsd. Poët. Latin. Min. 6, p. 386, v. 35.

prĕcārĭus.opening: adj. id. , obtained by begging , entreaty , or prayer (opp. debitus and pro imperio; not freq. till the Aug. per.; perh. used by Cic. only adverbially; v. infra ). Lit. : non orare solum precariam opem, sed pro debitā…

prĕcātĭo.opening: precor . Lit. , a praying , prayer (class.): sollemnis comitiorum precatio, Cic. Mur. 1, 1 : precatione uti, id. Tusc. 1, 47, 114 : precationem facere, Liv. 39, 18 ; Plin. 28, 2, 3, § 10 : auguralis, Paul. ex Fest. p.…

prĕcātĭuncŭla.opening: dim. precatio , a slight request : δεησίδιον , precatiuncula, petitiuncula, Gloss. Philox.

prĕcātīvus.opening: adj. precor , prayed for , obtained by entreaty (postclass.): pax, Amm. 17, 5, 1 : precativo modo, by prayer or entreaty , Ulp. Reg. tit. 24.— Adv. : , by request , by entreaty (post-class.), Ulp. Reg. tit. 25, 1 al.

prĕcātor.opening: id. , one who prays or entreats , an intercessor (ante-class.): precator et patronus, Plaut. Ps. 2, 2, 12 ; id. As. 2, 4, 9 ; Ter. Heaut. 5, 2, 23 : ad precatorem adeam, id. Phorm. 1, 2, 90 .

prĕcātōrĭus.opening: adj. precator , of or belonging to petitioning , precatory : ars, Don. Ter. Phorm. 1, 2, 92 .

prĕcātus.opening: precor , a prayer , request (poet, and post-class.), Stat. Th. 10, 71 : concordi precatu tentare aliquid, Amm. 24, 6, 5 : dabitur precatui tuo, Sid. Ep. 8, 15 : precatibus efficacissimis obtinere, id. ib. 9, 3 .

prŏ-auctor.opening: a remote ancestor , founder (post-Aug.): generis sui proauctor, Suet. Claud. 24 .

prŏ-ăvĭa.opening: f , a grandfather's or grandmother's mother , a great-grandmother (post-Aug.), Suet. Calig. 10 ; cf. Dig. 38, 10, 1 ; 10 .

prŏăvītus.opening: adj. proavus , of or belonging to a great-grandfather , or to one's ancestors , ancestral ( poet. ): regna, inherited from his forefathers, Ov. M. 13, 416 : rura, Stat. S. 4, 4, 83 ' potentia, Sil. 16, 254 : medicamina…

prŏ-ăvus.opening: ( gen. plur. proavūm, Stat. Th. 10, 807 ), A grandfather's or grandmother's father , a great-grandfather (class.): pater, avus, proavus, abavus, atavus, tritavus, Plaut. Pers. 1, 2, 5 ; cf. id. Mil. 2, 4, 20: proavus et…

prŏba.opening: probo , a proof (postclass.), Amm. 21, 16, 21 ; Cod. Just. 12, 25, 1 .

prŏbābĭlis.opening: adj. id. . Lit. , that may be assumed , believed , or proved; likely , credible , probable (class.): probabile est id, quod fere fieri solet, aut quod in opinione positum est, aut quod habet in se ad haec quandam…

prŏbābĭlĭtas.opening: probabilis , probability , credibility (class.): magna, Cic. Ac. 2, 24, 75 : captiosa, id. Fin. 3, 21, 72 : quodcumque nostros animos probabilitate percussit, id dicimus, id. Tusc. 5, 11, 33 .

prŏbătĭcus.opening: adj. , = προβατικός , of or belonging to sheep , sheep - (eccl. Lat.): probatica porta Hierosolymis, the sheep-gate , near which the sheep destined for sacrifice were washed in a pool, Hier. de situ et nomine loc. Hebr.…

prŏbātĭo.opening: probo . A trying , proving; a trial , inspection , examination (class.): athletarum probatio, Cic. Off. 1, 40, 144 : futura, Cic. Verr. 2, 1, 54, § 142 ; Varr. R. R. 1, 20, 1 : oesypi, Plin. 29, 2, 10, § 36 : croci…

prŏbătĭon.opening: , = προβάτιον , a plant , also called arnoglossa, App. Herb. 1 .

prŏbātīvus.opening: adj. probo , of or belonging to proof , probative (post-class.): quaestiones, Auct. Quint. Decl. 299 .

prŏbātor.opening: id. , an approver (rare but class.): quid interest inter suasorem facti et probatorem? Cic. Phil. 2, 12, 29 : rationis, id. Caecin. 29, 85 : ingenii, Ov. P. 2, 2, 106 : malorum improbator, bonorum probator, App. de Deo…

prŏbātōrĭa.opening: (sc. epistula) [id.], a letter of recommendation (from the emperor), a certificate of qualification (postclass.): sacra probatoria, Cod. Just. 12, 58, 2 : emissa sacri scrinii probatoria, ib. 12, 60, 6 ; 12, 36, 7 .

prŏbātus.opening: Part. and P. a. , from probo.

prŏbĭtas.opening: 1. probus , goodness , worth , uprightness , honesty , probity; modesty (class.): virtus, probitas, integritas in candidato requiri solet, Cic. Planc. 25, 62 ; id. Fam. 13, 10, 3 : probitatis commendatio, id. de Or. 1,…

prō-bīto.opening: v. a. , to move forward : gradum, Pac. ap. Non. 154, 3 ; v. Trag. Rel. p. 101 Rib.

problēma.opening: ( gen. plur. problematorum, Gell. 3, 6, 1 ; abl. plur. problematis, id. 19, 6, 1 ), , = πρόβλημα , a question proposed for solution , a problem , enigma , riddle , puzzle (post-Aug.), Suet. Gram. 4 : problemata…

prŏbo.opening: v. a. 1. probus . To try , test , examine , inspect , judge of any thing in respect of its goodness, fitness, etc. (rare in class. Lat.; not in Cic. or Cæs.; in eccl. Lat. very freq.). Lit. : militem neque a moribus…

prŏbŏlē.opening: , = προβολή , a putting forth , production (eccl. Lat.), Tert. Praescr. 46 .

prŏboscis.opening: ( , Sol. 24, 14 ; , Cassiod. Var. 10, 30 ), , , = προβοσκίς , a trunk , proboscis , a snout. In gen., Varr. ap. Non. 49, 11 ; Auct. B. Afr. 84, 2.— In partic., the trunk or proboscis of an elephant : proboscidem…

probrăchўs.opening: , = προβραχύς (sc. πούς ), a metrical foot , consisting of one short and four long syllables (e. g. rĕdūndāvērūnt), Diom. p. 478 P.

prŏbrōsĭtas.opening: probrosus , shamefulness , ignominy , infamy (late Lat.), Salv. Gub. D. 3, 9 .

prŏbrōsus.opening: adj. probrum , shameful , ignominious , infamous (class.). Of persons: vitā probrosus, et opertus infamiā, Tac. A. 3, 68 : feminae, Suet. Dom. 8 : sordidissimus, et probrosissimus, Claud. Mamert. Grat. Act. ad Jul. 19…

prŏbrum.opening: cf. Gr. προφέρειν, to reproach; and opprobrium , a shameful or disgraceful act (class.; syn.: dedecus, flagitium). Lit. In gen.: qui, nisi probrum, omnia alia indelicta aestimant, Att. ap. Fest. p. 229 Müll.: flagitium…

probrus.opening: adj. probrum , disgraceful , ignominious , infamous : animalia spurca atque probra, Gell. 9, 2, 9 .

prŏbus.opening: adj. Sanscr. prabhus, prominent, strong, from pra (v. pro) and bhu = fio , good , proper , serviceable , excellent , superior , able; esp. in a moral point of view, upright , honest , honorable , excellent , virtuous ,…

Prŏbus.opening: a Roman surname , Suet. Gram. 24 .— , , adj. , of or named from a Probus: purpura, Lampr. Alex. Sev. 40 .

prŏcācĭa.opening: procax , boldness , shamelessness , impudence (post-class.), Aus. Ep. 22 init.

prŏcācĭtas.opening: id. , boldness , shamelessness , impudence (class.): itaque a petendo petulantia, a procando, id est poscendo, procacitas nominata est, Cic. Rep. 4, 6, 19 (ap. Non. 23, 19 ): procacitatem alicujus coërcere, Nep. Timol.…

procălāre.opening: , provocare ex Graeco καλεῖν , id est voco, Paul. ex Fest. p. 225 Müll.

prŏcăpis.grammar: progenies, quae ab uno capite procedit

Prŏcas.opening: and , , , a king of Alba : Proca Numitorem atque Amulium procreat, Liv. 1, 3, 9 ; Ov M. 14, 622 ; id. F. 4, 52 ; 6, 143 : proximus ille Procas, Verg. A. 6, 767 .

prŏcātĭo.opening: proco , a demanding in marriage , a suing , wooing (post-class.), App. Mag. p. 320, 3 .

prŏcax.opening: adj. id. , bold , shameless , impudent , insolent , forward , pert , wanton (class.; syn.: petulans, protervus). Of persons: leno procax, rapax, trahax, Plaut. Pers. 3, 3, 6 : procaciores estis vos, id. Truc. 1, 2, 52 :…

prō-cēdo.opening: v. n. , to go forth or before , to go forwards , advance , proceed (class.; cf.: progredior, prodeo). Lit. In gen.: procedere ad forum, Plaut. Cas. 3, 3, 2 : illuc procede, id. Capt. 5, 2, 1 : a portu, Cic. Fam. 16, 9,…

prŏcĕleusmătĭcus.opening: , = προκελευσματικὸς ( πούς ), a metrical foot of four short syllables; as, ănĭmŭlă, mĭsĕrŭlă, Diom. 513 P.; cf. Mar. Victorin. p. 2546 P.

prŏcella.opening: f [pro and root kel; Gr. κέλης , runner; cf.: celer, celox], a violent wind (by which things are prostrated), a storm , hurricane , tempest (class.). Lit. : procella distat latitudine a vortice et a turbine disjectā…

prō-cello.opening: v. a. cf.: percello, procella, celer , to throw or cast down (anteclass.): procello, περιτρέπω , Gloss. Philox.: procellunt sese in mensam, i. e. lie down (at table), Plaut. Mil. 3, 1, 167 Ritschl N. cr.; cf.:…

prŏcellōsus.opening: adj. procella , full of storms , stormy , tempestuous , boisterous (perh. not ante - Aug.): ver procellosum, Liv. 40, 2 : status caeli, Col. 9, 4, 1 : mare, Val. Fl. 3, 621 ; cf. in the sup. : procellosissimum pelagus,…

prŏcer.opening: , in sing. only Juv. 8, 26 , and Capitol. Max. 2 ; , (anteclass. collat. form , , in the gen. plur. : procum patricium in descriptione classium quam facit, Serv. Tullius, significat procerum, Fest. p. 249 Müll.; cf.:…

prōcērĭtas.opening: procerus , a high growth , height , tallness. Lit. (good prose): candor hujus te et proceritas, vultus oculique perpulerunt, his tall stature, Cic. Cael. 15, 36 ; so absol. , Tac. A. 12, 44 ; 4, 57 ; Suet. Vit. 17 ;…

prōcērĭtūdo.opening: id. , high stature , height , tallness (late Lat. for proceritas), Sol. 1, 87 ; Auct. Itin. Alex. M. 112 Mai; Jul. Val. Rer. Gest. Alex. 1, 30 .

prōcērŭlus.opening: adj. dim. [id.], rather long , longish (post-class.): manus, App. Flor. 2, p. 351, 8 .

prōcērus.opening: adj. pro and root karof creo; cf. Gr. κράτος, κρατερός , high , tall , long. Lit. (class.; cf. excelsus): procerum collum, Cic. Brut. 91, 313 : boves cornibus proceris, Col. 6, 1, 3 : in procero corpore, Plin. Ep. 4, 9,…

prōcessĭo.opening: procedo , a marching onwards , an advance; in sing. : a militibus nostris reditus magis maturus quam processio longior quaereretur, Cic. Imp. Pomp. 9, 24 ; so in plur. , Veg. Mil. 2, 22 ; of the formal entrance of the…

prōcessus.opening: procedo , a going forwards , advance , course , progression , progress , process. In gen. (class.): processus dicendi, Cic. Brut. 65, 232 : processum vult, the progress of the discourse, id. Or. 62, 210 : in Graecis…

procestrĭa.opening: , quo proceditur in muro. Aelius procestria aedificia dixit esse extra portam, Artorius procestria, quae sunt ante castra, Paul. ex Fest. p. 225, 12 .

prŏchos agrĭos.opening: , = πρόχος ἄγριος , a plant , perh. pure Lat. saxifraga, App. Herb. 97 .

Prŏchўta.opening: , and , , , = Προχύτη , a small Italian island near Campania , the mod. Procida , Mel. 2, 7, 18 ; Plin. 2, 88, 89, § 213 ; 3, 6, 12, § 82 ; Verg. A. 9, 715 ; Ov. M. 14, 89 ; Juv. 3, 5 .

prōcĭdentĭa.opening: 1. procido , a falling down or forwards of a part of the body out of its place, a procidence , prolapse : ani, Cels. 6, 6, 8 fin. : vulvarum, Plin. 23, 9, 81, § 161 : sedis, id. 26, 8, 58, § 90 ; cf. , P. a. — Gram. t.…

prō-cĭdo.opening: v. n. cado , to fall forwards or down , to fall flat , fall prostrate (perh. not ante-Aug.). In gen.: ad pedes alicujus, Hor. Epod. 17, 13 : praeceps procidit ante proram, Liv. 26, 39 : universi prociderunt, id. 45, 25…

procīdo.opening: , no perf. , , v. a. pro-caedo , to strike down , Not. Tir. p. 18 : procisus, praecisus, id. ib.

prōcĭdŭus.opening: adj. 1. procido . Fallen down , prostrate (post-Aug.): salix procidua, Plin. 16, 32, 57, § 133 ; Stat. Th. 3, 127 ; Sid. Carm. 23, 415 .— Of parts of the body, falling down or forwards , prociduous : sedes, Plin. 21,…

prō-cĭĕo.opening: , no perf. , , v. a. , to call forth , demand (post-class.): matrem procitum plurimi venerunt, Liv. Andron. ap. Paul. ex Fest. p. 225 Müll. (a transl. of the Homeric τόσσοι μητέρʼ ἐμὴν μνῶνται , Od. 1, 248).— Procitum…

Procilĭus.opening: An historian contemporary with Cicero , Cic. Att. 2, 2, 2 ; Plin. 8, 2, 2, § 4 .— A quœstor , Cic. Att. 4, 15, 16 ; id. Q. Fr. 2, 6 (8), 1.

Procilla.opening: , or Julia Procilla, the mother of Agricola , Tac. Agr. 1 .

prōcinctŭālis.opening: adj. procinctus . of or belonging to the setting out of an army (late Lat.): ornatus, Cassiod. Var. 6, 22 .

prōcinctus.opening: procingo, prop. a girding up; hence, transf. , milit. t. t., a being prepared or equipped for battle , readiness for action : procinctum, ὅταν εἰς πόλεμον συγκαλέσωνται , Gloss. Philox.: oratorem armatum semper ac velut…

prō-cingo.opening: , no perf. , , v. a. , to gird up , to prepare , equip; only in part. perf. : , , prepared for battle , ready for action , in fighting order : cum procinctae classes erant, Gell. 1, 11, 3 : classis, i. e. an army ready…

procĭtant.opening: , provocitant. Citare enim vocitare est: unde procet et procit et procat dicebant pro poscit, Paul. ex Fest. p. 225 Müll.: procitat, προκαλεῖται , Gloss. Philox.

procitāre.opening: , Paul. ex Fest. p. 226 (perh. more correctly, prolicitare).

proclāmātĭo.opening: f [proclamo]. In gen., a calling out , crying out , outcry (post-class.), Quint. Decl. 8, 21 : trux, id. ib. 18, 16 .— In partic., an appeal to a judge to assert one's liberty, Dig. 40, 12, 25 ; 14 ; 34 ; 23.

proclāmātor.opening: id. , a crier , bawler , vociferator , said of a bad advocate: non enim causidicum nescio quem neque proclamatorem aut rabulam hoc sermone nostro conquirimus, Cic. de Or. 1, 46, 202 Orell. (dub.; B. and K. clamatorem,…

pro-clāmo.opening: v. a. , to call or cry out , to vociferate. In gen. (class.): assunt, defendunt, proclamant, Cic. Verr. 2, 5, 42, § 108 : patre proclamante, se filiam jure caesam judicare, Liv. 1, 26 : magnā proclamat voce Diores,…

Procles.opening: , = Προκλῆς , the twinbrother of Eurysthenes , king of the Lacedœmonians , Cic. Div. 2, 43, 90 ; Nep. Ages. 1, 2 .

prōclīnātĭo.opening: proclino , a bending or inclining forwards : in concreto, a slope , declivity (Vitruvian), Vitr. 5, 12, 4 .— In plur. : ne structurae habeant ullā in parte proclinationes, Vitr. 6, 11 .

prō-clīno.opening: v. a. , to bend or incline forwards , to bend , incline (not in Cic.). Lit. : tum mare in haec magnus proclinet litora Nereus, Ov. Am. 2, 11, 39 ; Vitr. 2, 8, 20 : curvatura montis proclinata ad mare, id. 2, 10, 1 :…

prōclīvis.opening: (ante- and post-class. and poet. ; collat. form , , Plaut. Mil. 4, 2, 27 ; Varr. R. R. 2, 2, 7 ; Cat. 64, 270 ; Front. Strat. 2, 2, 2 ; v. Neue, Formenl. 2, p. 91), adj. proclivus , sloping , steep , going downwards or…

prōclīvĭtas.opening: proclivis . A steep descent , declivity (post-class.): parvulam proclivitatem digressus, Auct. B. Afr. 37.— A tendency , disposition , proneness , propensity , proclivity (class.): ad morbos proclivitas...proclivitas ad…

prōclīvĭum.opening: , a false read. for proclivo, Front. Strat. 2, 2, 2 ; v. proclivis.

prō-clūdo.opening: v. a. , to shut up (post-class.), Pall. 3, 26 (al. praecludat).

prŏco.grammar: āre āri v. a. v. dep.
prŏco.opening: v. a. , and , , v. dep. cf. precor , to ask , demand (very rare): parere mea vos majestas procat, Liv. And. ap. Non. 24, 7 : a procando, id est poscendo, procacitas nominata est, Cic. Rep. 4, 6, 6 (ap. Non. 24, 3 ):…

prŏcoeton.opening: , = προκοιτών , an anteroom , antechamber (post-Aug.), Plin. Ep. 2, 17, 10 and 23 (in Varr. R. R. 2 , prooem. § 2, written as Greek).

procŏmĭon.opening: , = προκόμιον , the hair on the front part of the head , the front hair (pure Lat. antiae), Veg. Vet. 3, 11, 4 Schneid. N. cr. (al. protocomia).

Prŏconnēsus.opening: , = Προκόννησος , an island in the Propontis , abounding in wine and marble , now Marmora , Mel. 2, 7, 4 ; Plin. 5, 32, 44, § 151 .—Hence, , , adj. , of Proconnessus , Proconnessian : marmor, Sol. 37 med. — , , adj. ,…

prō-consul.opening: (also separately, ; v. pro, II. B. 2.; and abbreviated, procos.), , One who at the close of his consulship in Rome became governor of a province , or military commander under a governor; a proconsul , Cic. Div. 2, 36,…

prōconsŭlāris.opening: adj. proconsul , of or belonging to a proconsul , proconsular (not in Cic. or Cæs.): proconsularis vir, i.e. a proconsul, Tac. Agr. 42 : imago, of the military tribuneship , which was in the place of a consulate, Liv.…

prōconsŭlātus.opening: id. . The dignity or office of a proconsul , a proconsulship (post-Aug.), Plin. 14, 22, 28, § 144 ; Tac. A. 16, 23 ; 30 ; Plin. Ep. 3, 9, 2 et mult. al.— A proprœtorship , Suet. Aug. 3 .

prōcrastĭnātĭo.opening: procrastino , a putting off to the morrow or from day to day , procrastination : tarditas et procrastinatio, Cic. Phil. 6, 3, 7 .

prōcrastĭno.opening: v. a. pro crastinus , to put off till the morrow , hence, in gen., to put off , defer , delay , procrastinate (class.; cf. differo): rem differre cotidie ac procrastinare, Cic. Rosc. Am. 9, 26 ; Front. Ep. ad Amic. 2, 6…

prōcrĕābĭlis.opening: adj. procreo , of or belonging to generation (late Lat.): sacramentum, Cassiod. Var. 2, 10 .

prōcrĕātĭo.opening: id. , a begetting , generation , procreation (class.): procreatio liberorum, Cic. Tusc. 1, 14, 31 : hominum procreationes, id. Div. 2, 46, 96 .— Transf. , that which is begotten , Vitr. 2, 9, 1 .

prōcrĕātor.opening: id. , a begetter , producer , creator (class.): ille procreator mundi deus, author, creator, Cic. Univ. 8, 23 : a procreatoribus amari, by one's parents, id. Fin. 4, 7, 17 ; 5, 23, 65 .

prōcrĕātrix.opening: procreator , she that brings forth , a mother (class.): philosophia artium procreatrix quaedam et quasi parens, Cic. de Or. 1, 3, 9 ; Auct. Pervig. Ven. 64.

prō-crĕo.opening: v. a. , to bring forth , beget , generate , procreate , produce (class.). Lit. : procreare liberos lepidum est onus, Plaut. Mil. 3, 1, 88 : multiplices fetus, Cic. N. D. 2, 5, 128 : de matrefamilias duo filios, id. Rep.…

prō-cresco.opening: v. inch. n. To grow forth , spring up , arise , proceed (ante- and post-class.): quattuor ex rebus posse omnia procrescere, Lucr. 1, 715 .— Trop. : vis morbi procrescit, Lucr. 6, 664 .— To continue to grow , to grow up…
