Procris.opening: , = Πρόκρις , a daughter of the Athenian king Erechtheus , wife of Cephalus , who shot her in a wood , mistaking her for a wild beast , Ov. M. 7, 707 sq. , and 795 sq.; id. A. A. 3, 727 ; acc. Procrim, Verg. A. 6, 445 .

Prŏcrustes.opening: , = Προκρούστης , a noted highwayman in Attica. He had a bed upon which he compelled travellers to lie down; when they were longer than the bed he cut off as much of their limbs as would suffice to make the length…

prōcŭbĭtōres.grammar: dicuntur fere velites, qui noctu custodiae causā ante castra excubant, cum castra hostium in propinquo sunt
prōcŭbĭtōres.opening: , ut M. Cato in eo, quem de re militari scripsit, the night-watch , Fest. p. 253 Müll.

prō-cŭbo.opening: v. n. , to lie stretched out , to lie along ( poet. ): ubi saxea procubet umbra, Verg. G. 3, 145 : procubat horrendus Getico Gradivus in Haemo, Claud. Consol. Prob. et Olyb. 119.

prō-cūdo.opening: v. a. , to fashion or make by hammering , to forge a thing. Lit. ( poet. ): in acuta et tenuia posse Mucronum duci fastigia procudendo, Lucr. 5, 1265 : enses, Hor C. 4, 15, 19: vomeris obtusi dentem, Verg. G. 1, 261 .—…

prŏcul.opening: adv. procello, to drive away , in the distance , at a distance , a great way off , far , afar off , from afar. Lit. , of place (class.; cf.: longe, eminus); constr. absol.; with adv. of place; with ab and abl. (not in…

Prŏcŭla.opening: name of a Roman woman , Juv 2, 68; 3, 203.

prōculcātĭo.opening: proculco , a treading down (post-Aug.). Lit. : obturbata proculcatione aqua, Plin. 8, 18, 26, § 68 .— Trop. : ruina et proculcatio, Sen. Tranq. 11, 8 .

prōculcātor.opening: id. , one who treads down obstacles; hence, in plur. : proculcatores, advanced troops , scouts (post-class.), Amm. 27, 10, 10 (al. procursatores).

prōculcātus.opening: Part. and P. a. , from proculco.

prō-culco.opening: v. a. calco , to tread down , trample upon (mostly poet. and in post-Aug. prose). Lit. : turbatus eques sua ipse subsidia territis equis proculcavit, Liv. 10, 36, 5 : crescenti segetes proculcat in herbā, Ov. M. 8, 290…

Prŏcŭlēius.opening: a Roman knight intimate with Augustus , Hor. C. 2, 2, 5 ; Plin. 7, 45, 46, § 148 ; 36, 24, 59, § 183 ; Juv. 7, 94 .

proculĭunt.opening: , ait significare Antistius de jure pontificali L. VIIII., Fest. p. 253 Müll.

Prŏcŭlus.opening: a Roman surname : Proculum inter cognomina eum dicunt, qui natus est patre peregrinante a patriā procul. Proculos sunt qui credant ideo dictos, quia patribus senibus quasi procul progressā aetate nati sunt, Paul. ex…

prō-cumbo.opening: v. n. Lit. , to fall forwards , fall or sink down , to prostrate one's self; of the wounded, the dying, suppliants, etc. (class.; cf.; cado, ruo): procumbunt Gallis omnibus ad pedes Bituriges, ne pulcherrimam urbem…

prō-cŭpīdo.opening: a previous desire (post-class.): amoris, i. e. anteceptus amor, Min. Fel. Octav. 26 .

prōcūrātĭo.opening: procuro . In gen. A caring for , taking care of , having the charge of a thing; a charge , superintendence , administration , management , procuration (class.): dum me rei publicae non solum cura, sed quaedam etiam…

prōcūrātĭuncŭla.opening: dim. procuratio , a small charge or administration (post-Aug.), Sen. Ep. 31, 8 .

prōcūrātor.opening: (the first o short, Ov. A. A. 1, 587 ), , procuro , a manager , overseer , superintendent , agent , administrator , deputy , procurator , keeper. In gen. (class.): procurator peni, Plaut. Ps. 2, 2, 14 : procurator,…

prōcūrātōrĭus.opening: adj. procurator , belonging to an agent or manager , procuratory (post-class.): nomen, Dig. 3, 3, 31 ; 34 : exceptio, ib. 3, 3, 62 .

prōcūrātrix.opening: id. , a governess , protectress : sed cum sapientiam totius hominis custodem et procuratricem esse vellent, Cic. Fin. 4, 7, 17 .

prō-cūro.opening: (the first o scanned short, Tib. 1, 5, 13 ; Ov. A. A. 1, 587 ), , v. a. and n. , to take care of , attend to , look after any thing. In gen. (class.; syn.: curam gero). Act. : nunc tu te interim, quasi pro puerperā, hic…

prō-curro.grammar: cŭcurri and curri, cursum, 3 v. n.
prō-curro.opening: v. n. , to run forth , rush forwards. Lit. (class.), freq. of armies: si Romani ferocius procucurrissent, Liv. 25, 11 : infestis pilis, Caes. B. C. 3, 93 : in proximum tumulum, id. B. G. 6 39: ad repellendum, et…

prōcursātĭo.opening: procurso , in milit. lang., a charge , sally , onset (only in Livy): ubi a velitibus per procursationem commissa pugna esset, Liv. 28, 33 : Numidarum, id. 22, 44 .

prō-cursātor.opening: id. , a forerunner; in military lang., procursatores, skirmishers , sharp-shooters (very rare; not ante-Aug.), Liv. 42, 64, 6 .

prōcursĭo.opening: procurro , a running forward , stepping forth. * Lit. , of an orator: procursio opportuna, brevis, moderata, rara, Quint. 11, 3, 126 .—* Trop. , a digression : necessaria post narrationem, Quint. 4, 3, 9 .

prōcurso.opening: v. freq. n. [id.], to run forth , to sally out , make attacks or onsets. —Of skirmishers: cum ab stationibus procursaretur, Liv. 27, 2 ; Plin. 8, 5, 5, § 15 ; Amm. 27, 10, 9 .— Transf. , to advance : in pulcra facinora,…

prōcursōrĭus.opening: adj. id. , that runs forth or before (late Lat.): index, Amm. 31, 3, 6 (al. praecursorius).

prōcursus.opening: id. . Lit. , a running forth or forwards; esp., in milit. lang., a sallying forth , charge , onset (not in Cic. or Cæs.): procursu militum, Liv. 22, 41 : faciles sternit procursibus herbas, Stat. Th. 4, 787 ; Lucr. 2,…

prō-curvo.opening: v. a. , to bend or curve forwards ( poet. ): aliquem, Stat. Th. 6, 852 : pomiferique simul procurvant bracchia rami, Auct. Carm. de Genesi, 14.

prō-curvus.opening: adj. , curred forwards , crooked , winding ( poet. ): falx, Verg. G. 2, 421 : litora, id. A. 5, 765 .

prŏcus.opening: ( gen. plur. procūm, Cic. Or. 46, 156 ), A wooer , suitor : proci dicuntur, qui poscunt aliquam in matrimonium, Graece μνηστῆρες . Est enim procare poscere, etc., Fest. p. 249 Müll.: me natam nulli veterum sociare…

Prŏcўon.opening: , = Προκύων (Foredog), a constellation that rises before the dog-star (pure Lat. Antecanis), Cic. Arat. 222 ; Hor. C. 3, 29, 18 ; Cic. N. D. 2, 44, 144 ; Col. 11, 2, 52 ; Manil. 5, 197 .

prō-dĕambŭlo.opening: v. n. , to walk abroad , take a walk , Ter. Ad. 5, 1, 4 .

prōdĕo.opening: (lengthened anteclass. form, prodinunt, for prodeunt, Enn. ap. Fest. p. 229 Müll.; post-class., prodient, for prodibunt, Lact. 7, 16 fin. ), v. n. pro-eo , to go or come forth (class.; cf.: proficiscor, progredior).…

prōdīcĭus.opening: or , , adj. prodo , treacherous (eccl. Lat.), Tert. ad Nat. 1, 7 .

prō-dīco.opening: v. a. To say beforehand , to fix or appoint beforehand (very rare): prodictā die, Cic. Dom. 17, 45 (dub.).— To put off , defer (not in Cic. or Cæs.): diem prodicere, to adjourn the time of trial, Liv. 2, 61, 7 ; v.…

prō-dictātor.opening: a vice-dictator (only in Livy): prodictatorem populus creavit Q. Fabium Maximum, Liv. 22, 8, 6 ; instead of which: pro dictatore, id. 22, 31 fin.

prōdictĭo.opening: prodico, II. , a deferring , adjournment , Fest. p. 253 , b fin. Müll.

Prŏdĭcus.opening: , = Πρόδικος , a Grecian sophist of Ceos , contemporary with Socrates , author of the story of The Choice of Hercules , Cic. Brut. 8, 30 ; id. de Or. 3, 32, 128 ; Quint. 3, 1, 12 .—Hence, , , adj. , of or belonging to…

prōdĭgālĭtas.opening: prodigus , wastefulness , prodigality (very rare): summa, Auct. Decl. ap. Cat. 9 .

prōdĭgentĭa.opening: prodigo , extravagance , profusion , prodigality (Tacitean; cf.: luxuria, profusio): prodigentia opum, Tac. A. 6, 14 ; so (opp. avaritia) id. ib. 13, 1 ; 15, 37.

prōdĭgĭālis.opening: adj. prodigium . Unnatural , strange , wonderful , portentous , prodigious (post-class.): res, Amm. 25, 10, 1 : caput, Claud. in Ruf. 2, 434 : signa, Prud. Ham. 467 .—Adverb.: prodigiale canens, Stat. Th. 7, 403 :…

prōdĭgĭātor.opening: id. , an interpreter of prodigies : prodigiatores haruspices, prodigiorum interpretes, Fest. p. 229 Müll.

prōdĭgĭŏlum.opening: dim. id. , a little prodigy , Not. Tir. p. 96 .

prōdĭgĭōsus.opening: adj. prodigium , unnatural , strange , wonderful , marvellous , prodigious ( poet. and in post-Aug. prose): atria Circes, Ov. M. 13, 968 : cura Veneris, id. ib. 9, 727 : mendacia, id. Am. 3, 6, 17 : corpora, Quint. 1,…

prōdĭgĭtas.opening: prodigus , extravagance , prodigality , Lucil ap. Non. 159, 31 .

prōdĭgĭum.opening: ( gen. plur. prodigiūm, Pac. ap. Cic. Or. 46, 155 ), for prodicium, from prodico . Lit. , a prophetic sign , token , omen , portent , prodigy , in a good and (more freq.) in a bad sense (syn.: portentum, ostentum,…

prōdĭgo.opening: v. a. pro-ago , to drive forth , to drive to a place. Lit. (ante-class.): sues in lutosos limites, Varr. R. R. 2, 4 : in pabulum, id. ib. 2, 7 med. : pulli prodigendi in solem, id. ib. 3, 9 med. — Transf. , to get rid…

prōdĭgŭae.opening: , quae consumuntur: unde homines quoque luxuriosi prodigi, Fest. p. 250 Müll. [prodigo].

prōdĭgus.opening: adj. prodigo , wasteful , lavish , prodigal. Lit. (class.; syn.: largus, munificus): omnino duo sunt genera largorum, quorum alteri prodigi, alteri liberales. Prodigi, qui epulis et viscerationibus et gladiatorum…

prōdĭtĭo.opening: prodeo , a going or coming forth , an appearance (post-class.), Sid. Ep. 5, 13 .— Esp., a sally by a besieged garrison: tempestiva, Amm. 15, 5, 33 .

prōdĭtor.opening: prodo , a betrayer , traitor (class.): cum senatus duces nullos ac pro ducibus proditores haberet, Cic. Sest. 15, 35 : proditor patriae, id. Fin. 3, 19, 64 ; id. Fam. 12, 3, 2 : disciplinae, Liv. 2, 59 .— Poet. ,…

prōditrix.opening: proditor , a female betrayer , a traitress (post-class.): patris, Lact. 1, 10, 9 : proditrices numinum, Serv. Verg. E. 8, 30 .— Trop. : Fama proditrix, Prud. στεφ . 1, 11.

prōdĭtus.opening: treachery (late Lat.), Jul. ap. Aug. c. Sec. Resp. Jul. 3, 168.

prōdĭus.opening: adv. prodeo , farther onwards : prodius dictum interius, longius, a prodeundo, quasi porro eundo, Non. 47, 13 sq. ; Varr. ap. Non. l. l.

prō-do.opening: (archaic produit for prodiderit, = porro dederit, porticum sartam tectamque habeto, prodito, Lex Censor. ap. Fest. p. 229, 17 Müll.; pres. part. abl. sing. prodente, Cic. Tusc. 2, 13, 31 ), v. a. To give , put , or…

prō-dŏcĕo.opening: v. a. , to teach before , i. e. to show by teaching , to inculcate (= docere altā voce et palam): haec Janus summus ab imo Prodocet, Hor. Ep. 1, 1, 55 (perh. imitation of the Greek προδιδάσκειν ).

prō-dormĭo.opening: v. n. , to sleep before (post - Aug.): sive prodormias, sive pervigiles, Front. Ep. ad M. Caes. 1, 4 Mai; so id. ib. 4, 6 ; 5, 22.

prodrŏmus.opening: , = πρόδρομος . A certain north-northeast wind that blows eight days before the rising of the dog-star : prodromi nulli, Cic. Att. 16, 6, 1 ; Plin. 2, 47, 47, § 123 .— A kind of early fig , Plin. 16, 26, 49, § 113 .

prōdūcĭbĭlis.opening: adj. , which lengthens out (late Lat.): incus, Hier. Interpr. Orig. in Jer. Hom. 3, 1 .

prō-dūco.opening: (produxe, for produxisse, Ter Ad. 4, 2, 22), v. a. , to lead or bring forth , to lead forward or out. Lit. (class.): fidicinam intus, Plaut. Ep. 3, 4, 40 : aliquem foras ante aedes, id. Capt. 2, 2, 2 : aliquem e…

prōductĭlis.opening: adj. produco . That may be drawn out , ductile , productile : productile, ἐλατόν , Gloss.— Of beaten work , of highly wrought metal : Cherubim aurei et productiles, Vulg. Exod. 25, 18 : tubae, id. Ecclus. 50, 18 .

prōductĭo.opening: id. . A lengthening , prolonging (class.): productio temporis, Cic. Fin. 3, 14, 45 : verbi, id. Top. 8, 36 .— A lengthening in pronunciation: ut aut contractione brevius fieret, aut productione longius, Cic. de Or. 3,…

prōductīvus.opening: adj. id. , fit for prolongation : nomina, Cassiod. Hist. Eccl. 1, 14 .

prōducto.opening: v. freq. a. id. , to draw one thing before another, to interpose : ut huic malo aliquam productem moram, Ter. And. 3, 5, 9 Fleck.

prōductor.opening: id. , a leader away , an enticer (perh. a pander): productor, προαγωγός , Vet. Gloss.

prōductus.opening: Part. and P. a. , from produco.

prōdux.opening: produco , a twig , shoot , layer; trop. (eccl. Lat.), Tert. Carn. Chr. 20 .

prŏēgmĕnon.opening: , = προηγμένον (in pure Lat. productum; v. producta, in produco fin. ), a preferable thing , acc. to the Stoic philosophy, Cic. Fin. 3, 4, 15 (as Greek, id. ib. 3, 15, 51 al.).

proelĭāris.opening: ( ) and , , adj. proelium , of or belonging to a battle (ante- and post-class.): pugnae proeliares, pitched battles, Plaut. Curc. 4, 4, 17 : acies, App. M. 8, p. 208, 40 : proeliares dies appellantur, quibus fas est…

proelĭātĭo.opening: proelior , the battling , fighting : nostra inter nos, Jul. Val. Rer. Gest. Alex. 3, 8, 4 .

proelĭātor.opening: ( ), , id. , a fighter , warrior , combatant (post - Aug.), Tac. A. 2, 73 : proeliator insignis, Just. 15, 4 fin. ; in appos.: proeliator miles, Amm. 19, 7, 8 : vir, Vulg. Isa. 42, 13 .

proelĭo.opening: v. a. (ante-class.; collat. form of proelior): mortales inter sese pugnant, proeliant, Enn. ap. Non. 472, 31 (Trag. v. 26 Vahl.); cf. Prisc. p. 799 P.— Impers. pass. : proeliatum est, Just. 19, 1, 9 .

proelĭor.opening: ( ), , v. dep. n. [proelium], to join battle , to engage in battle , fight (class.). Lit. : legiones in ipsis fluminis ripis proeliabantur, Caes. B. G. 2, 23 : pedibus, id. ib. 4, 2 : ad Syracusas, Cic. Div. 1, 25, 53 :…

proelĭum.opening: ( ), , etym. dub.; perh. for provilium, pro-dvilium; cf. duellum (bellum) , a battle , combat (class.; syn.: pugna, dimicatio). Lit. : induperatores pugnare ac proelia obire, Lucr. 4, 967 : non proeliis, neque acie…

pro-ēmĭnĕo.opening: v. n. , to project : προκύπτω , proemineo, Gloss. Gr. Lat.

Prŏërna.opening: , = Πρόερνα , a town of Thessaly , the mod. Ghynekokastro , Liv. 36, 14 .

Proetus.opening: , = Προῖτος , a king of Tiryns , brother of Acrisius , Ov. M. 5, 238 sq. — , , , = Προιτιδες , his daughters , who being punished with madness by Juno for their pride , imagined themselves to be cows : Proetides…

prŏfānātor.opening: id. , a profaner (eccl. Lat.): profanator Christi, Prud. Apoth. 246 .

prŏfānĭtas.opening: profanus , profaneness , profanity (eccl. Lat.): superiorum profanitas, i. e. the ancient heathen writers, Tert. Pall. 2 .

prōfāno.opening: v. a. pro-fanum , to bring any thing to a god before the temple , i. e. to dedicate , consecrate , offer in sacrifice (ante-class.): daps profanata, Cato, R. R. 50 : profanato sine contagione, id. ib. 132 : decimam…

prŏfāno.opening: v. a. profanus . Lit. , to render unholy , deprive of sanctity , to unhallow , desecrate , profane (perh. not ante - Aug.): dies festos, sacra, sacerdotes, Liv. 31, 44 : sacrum, Ov. Am. 3, 9, 19 : festum, id. M. 4, 390…

prŏfānus.opening: adj. pro - fanum; prop. before the temple, i. e. outside of it; hence, opp. to the temple as a sacred object , unholy , not sacred , common , profane. Lit. : profanum quod non est sacrum, Plautus: Sacrum an profanum…

prŏfātus.opening: (only in abl. sing. ), profor , a speaking out , uttering , saying , pronouncing (post-Aug.): effreno nimbos aequare profatu, Stat. S. 5, 3, 103 : vocis, Sen. Apoc. 7 : voces dictu profatuque ipso tetrae, Gell. 18, 11,…

prŏfectīcĭus.opening: or , , adj. proficiscor , that proceeds from some one (post-class.); profecticia dos est, quae a patre vel parente profecta est, de bonis vel facto ejus, Dig. 23, 3, 5 , §§ 1, 6, 14; Ulp. Fragm. 6, 3 ; 4, 6 .

prŏfectĭo.opening: id. . Lit. , a going away , setting out , departure (class.): profectione laeti, Pac. ap. Cic. Div. 1, 14, 24 : profectio et reversio alicujus, Cic. Phil. 1, 1, 1 : profectionem parare, to prepare for setting out , Caes…

prŏfectō.opening: adv. pro-facto , a particle of affirmation, confirmation, and declaration, actually , indeed , really , truly , surely , assuredly , by all means , certainly , etc. (very freq. and class.): neque di regunt neque…

prŏfector.opening: [proficiscor), a traveller : Ἔκδημος , profector, Gloss. Gr. Lat.

prōfectus.opening: (with the first syllable short, Aus. ldyll. 4, 70), , proficio , advance , progress , effect , increase , growth , profit , success ( poet. and in post-Aug. prose): sine profectu, Ov M. 9, 50: verbaque profectu…

Prōfĕra.opening: prefero , she that presents , makes known , i. e. the goddess of Arithmetic, Mart. Cap. 8, § 803 Kopp ad loc.

prō-fĕro.opening: ( inf. pass. parag. proferrier, Lucr. 1, 207 ; proferis for profers, Firm. Mat. 22, 3 ), v. a. Lit. To carry or bring out , to bring forth (class.; cf.: prodo, produco, adduco): Al. Vin' proferri pateram? Am. Proferri…

prŏfessĭo.opening: profiteor , a public acknowledgment , declaration , expression , profession , promise (mostly post-Aug.). In gen.: professio bonae voluntatis, Planc. ap. Cic. Fam. 10, 8, 2 : Canidius timidius decessit, quam professioni…

prŏfessĭōnārĭus.opening: professio , perh. a registrar of wares , one who fixed the duties on imported goods , Inscr. Marin. Frat. Arv. p. 151.

prŏfessor.opening: profiteor , a public teacher , professor , one who makes instruction in any branch a business (post-Aug.): sapientiae professores, Cels. praef. init. : ceterarum artium, Quint. 12, 11, 20 : Latinae simul Graecaeque…

prŏfessōrĭus.opening: adj. professor , of or belonging to a public teacher , professorial (post-Aug.): professoria lingua, Tac. A. 13, 14 fin.

prŏfessus.opening: Part. and P. a. , from profiteor

prŏ-festus.opening: adj. pro-festus; cf. profanus . Lit. , non-festival , not kept as a holiday , common; of days, workingdays : profestum diem dicebant qui festus non erat, Paul. ex Fest. p. 252 Müll.: profesti dies a festivitate vacui,…

prōfĭcĭo.opening: v. n and a. [pro-facio], to go forward , advance , gain ground , make progress. Lit. (very rare): cum quinqueremis sola non proficeret, Plin. 32, 1, 1, § 4 .— Trop. , to go on , advance , make progress; to profit ,…

prŏfĭciscor.opening: v. dep. n. [profacio, facesso, faciscor; orig., to make, i. e. put one's self forward; hence], to set out , start , go , march , travel , depart , etc. (class.; cf. progredior). Lit. : proficisci ad dormiendum, to go to…

prōfĭcŭus.opening: adj [proficio], beneficial , advantageous , conducive (late Lat): quibus mora potest esse proficua, Cassiod. Var. 1, 39 .

prŏfĭtĕor.opening: v (old form of the inf. PROFITEREI, and of the imper. PROFITEMINO, several times in the Tab. Her, in Haubold, Mon. Leg. p. 99 sq.), v. dep. a. [pro-fateor], to declare publicly , to own freely , to acknowledge , avow ,…

prō-flāmen.opening: a flamen's substitute , proflamen , Inscr. Orell. 2270 .

prō-flātus.opening: pro-flo . Lit. , a blowing , breeze (post-Aug.): aestivo proflatu refrigerari, Col. 5, 9, 7 .— Transf. , a snoring : proflatu terrebat equos, Stat. Th. 10, 320 .

prōflīgātĭo.opening: 1. profligo . Ruin , destruction (post-class.): bonorum profligatio, Aus. Per. Od. 2 .— A settling , collection : debitorum, Cod. Th. 6, 30, 10; Novell. Th. 2, 26 pr.

prōflīgātor.opening: id. , a spendthrift , prodigal (post-Aug.): ganeo et profligator, Tac. A. 16, 18 : justitiae, Ennod. Dict. 18 .

prōflīgātus.opening: Part. and P. a. , from 1, profligo.

prō-flīgo.opening: v. a. , to strike down , ruin , destroy (post-class.): proflictae res, cast down, ruined, Gell. 15, 5, 2 .

prō-flo.opening: v. a. , to blow forth , breathe out. Lit. ( poet. ): leo proflat ferus ore calores, Q. Cic. poët. ap. Aus. Ecl.: flammas, Ov. F. 1, 573 ; Val. Fl. 7, 571 : pectore sanguineos rivos, Stat. Th. 11, 266 .— Transf. , to…

prōflŭens.opening: Part. and P. a. , from profluo.

prōflŭenter.opening: adv. , v. profluo, P. a. fin.

prōflŭentĭa.opening: profluo , a flowing forth (trop.): inanis quaedam profluentia loquendi, a stream of words, fluency, Cic. Part. 23, 81 .

prō-flŭo.opening: v. n. , to flow forth or along (class.). Lit. : Mosa profluit ex monte Vogeso, Caes. B. G. 4, 10 : si lacrimae ab oculis et pituita a naribus profluent, Col. 6, 7, 11 : umor profluit, Verg. G. 4, 25 : sanguis profluens,…

prōflŭus.opening: adj. profluo , flowing forth , flowing , streaming (post-Aug.): recessus, Col. 8, 17, 9 : lacrimae, Sid. Ep. 4, 23 .

prōflŭvĭum.opening: id. , In gen., a flowing forth , a flowing , flow ( poet. and in post-Aug. prose): sanguinis, Lucr. 6, 1205 : sanguinis per nares, Col. 6, 33, 2 : narium, Plin. 32, 10, 42, § 124 : urinae, id. 28, 6, 17, § 61 .— In…

prōflŭvĭus.opening: adj. id. . Flowing; trop., fluctuating , inconstant : profluvia fides, Caecil. ap. Prisc. p. 699 P.— Subst. : , , , for profluvium, a flux , Veg. Vet. 1, 17, 19 ; 1, 38, 4 .

prŏ-for.opening: ( inf. profarier, Prud. στεφ . 10, 939), v. dep. a. , to say or speak out , to say , speak (mostly poet. and in post-Aug. prose). In gen.: veteres Casmenas cascam rem volo profari, tell , relate , Att. ap. Varr. L. L.…

prŏ-fringo.opening: v. a. frango , to break up : inarata, i. e. to plough, Stat. Th. 10, 512 .

prŏfŭga.opening: , collat. form of profugus, II. B., q. v.

prŏ-fŭgĭo.opening: (with first syll. long, Juvenc. 2, 477 ), , v. a. and n. Act. , to flee before or from , to flee , fly from any thing ( poet. and post-Aug.): Phocaeorum Velut profugit execrata civitas Agros, Hor. Epod. 16, 18 :…

prŏfŭgus.opening: adj. profugio , that flees or has fled , fugitive (not in Cic. or Cæs.; cf. fugitivus). In gen.: profugus domo, Liv. 1, 1 : ex urbe, Tac. H. 4, 49 : ex Peloponneso, Liv. 1, 8 : e proelio, Tac. H. 2, 46 : a proelio,…

prŏfundātus.opening: , a false read. for probe fundata, Plaut. Mil. 3, 3, 44 ; v. Ritschl ad h. l.

prŏfundĭtas.opening: profundus , depth (post - class.). Lit. : corporum tres sunt dimensiones, longitudo, latitudo, profunditas, Macr. Somn. Scip. 1, 6, 36 : aquarum, Cassiod. Var. 2, 21 .— Trop. , vastness , immensity , Hadrian. ap. Vop.…

prō^-fundo.opening: v. a. , to pour out or forth , to shed copiously , to cause to flow (class.). Lit. : sanguinem suum profundere omnem cupit, dummodo profusum hujus ante videat, Cic. Clu. 6, 18 : sanguinem pro patriā, id. Fin. 2, 19, 60…

prŏ-fundus.opening: adj. , deep , profound , vast (class.; syn. altus). Lit. : mare profundum et immensum, Cic. Planc. 6, 15 ; Curt. 9, 4, 18 : per inane profundum, Lucr. 1, 1108 : pontus, Verg. A. 5, 614 : Acheron, Lucr. 3, 978 :…

prŏfūsē.opening: adv. , v. profundo, P. a. fin.

prŏfūsĭo.opening: profundo , a pouring out , shedding , effusion (post-Aug.). Lit. : profusio sanguinis, Cels. 2, 7 ; 7, 21 : alvi, looseness, diarrhœa, id. 2, 7 ; 7, 21 .— In partic., a pouring out , libation of wine, milk, water,…

prŏfūsor.opening: id. , a squanderer (eccl. Lat.), Tert. adv. Marc. 1, 24 .

prŏfūsus.opening: Part. and P. a. , from profundo.

prō-gemmans.opening: Part. [gemmo], budding forth , budding (post-Aug.): palmis progemmantibus, Col. 4, 27, 1 .

prō-gĕner.opening: a granddaughter's husband : progenerum appellat avus neptis suae virum, Paul. ex Fest. p. 228 Müll.; cf.: socer dicitur uxoris meae pater: ego illius sum gener: socer magnus dicitur uxoris meae avus: ego sum illius…

prōgĕnĕrātio.opening: progenero , an engendering , procreation (post-class.): mularum, Plin. 8, 43, 68, § 167 ; 18, 28, 67, § 263 : Diomedis, Mart. Cap. 6, § 651 .

prō-gĕnĕro.opening: v. a. , to beget , engender , generate (rare; not in Cic. or Cæs.): nec imbellem feroces Progenerant aquilae columbam, Hor. C. 4, 4, 31 .—Of bees: fetus, Plin. 11, 16, 16, § 46 .—In pass. : qui (vituli) ex his…

prŏgĕnĭcŭlo.opening: pro-geniculum , to fall on the knees , to beg on one's knees : progeniculo, γουνοῦμαι , Gloss. Lat. Gr.: progeniculat, γονυπετεῖ , ib.

prōgĕnĭes.opening: (archaic gen. sing. progenii, Pac. ap. Gell. 9, 14, 13 ; and id. ap. Non. 490, 6 ), progigno , descent , lineage , race , family. Lit. : in abstracto (very rare but class.): progeniem vestram usque ab avo atque atavo…

prōgĕnĭtor.opening: id. , the founder of a family , an ancestor , progenitor (very rare; not in Cic. or Cæs.): si tui veretur te progenitoris, Att. ap. Non. 497, 2 : Eurysthenes progenitor majorum suorum, Nep. Ages. 7, 4 : deūm, Val.…

prōgĕnī^trix.opening: ( ), , progenitor , the foundress or general mother of a tribe or family, Isid. 9, 6, 22 .

prō-germĭno.opening: v. n. , to shoot forth , germinate (post-Aug.): surculus progerminat, Col. 4, 10, 1 ; 4, 15, 3 .

prō-gĕro.opening: v. a. To carry forth or out , to clear out , cast out (post-Aug.): defunctas (apes), Plin. 11, 18, 20, § 63 : formicae ova progerentes, id. 18, 35, 88, § 364 : fimum stabulis, Col. 1, 6, 22 : urcei, quibus oleum…

progesto.opening: v. freq. a. progero , to carry before one (post-class.): nucleos, App. M. 6, p. 185, 23 .

prō-gigno.opening: v. a. , to beget , bear , bring forth , produce (rare but class.): neque natus est neque progignetur, Plaut. True. 4, 1, 1 : in seminibus vis inest earum rerum, quae ex iis progignuntur, Cic. Div. 1, 56, 128 : illam…

prō-gnārē.opening: adv. gnarus , notoriously , openly : invenimus prognare significare aperte, Paul. ex Fest. p. 95 Müll.

prō-gnārĭter.opening: adv. id. , very skilfully , very expertly (ante-class.): prognariter armis Certare, Enn. ap. Non. 150, 6 (Ann. v. 215 Vahl.): age, indica prognariter, decisively, definitely, Plaut. Pers. 4, 4, 39 Ritschl N. cr.; cf.…

prōgnātĭo.opening: prognatus , a birth (post-class.): Diomedis Tydeique prognatio, Mart. Cap. 6, § 651 .

prō-gnātus.opening: Part. [gnatus, natus, from nascor], born , descended , sprung from some one; of children or descendants. Lit. : CORNELIVS LVCIVS SCIPIO BARBATVS GNAIVOD PATRE PROGNATVS, first Epitaph of the Scipios; SO, PROGNATVM…

Prō^gnē.opening: or , , , = Πρόκνη , Daughter of Pandion , king of Athens , sister of Philomela , and wife of Tereus; she was changed into a swallow : natae ex Philomelā atque ex Progne hirundines, Plaut. Rud. 3, 1, 12 ; Ov. M. 6, 440…

prognōsis.opening: , = πρόγνωσις . Foreknowledge , Isid. 12, 7, 19 .— Esp., as med. t. t., prognosis , forecast , in disease, Cael. Aur. Tard. 4, 8, 112 .

prŏgnōstĭcon.opening: or , , , = προγνωστικόν , a sign or token of the future, a prognostic; hence, , , , the signs of the weather , Quint. 5, 9, 15 .— Also as the title of Cicero's translation of the Προγνωστικά of Aratus, Cic. Div. 1, 8,…

prŏgramma.opening: , = πρόγραμμα , a proclamation , an edict , manifesto (postclass.), Vulc. Av id. Cassiod. 6 ; Cod. Just. 1, 14, 3 ; Inscr. Fabr. p. 529 , n. 382.

prō-grĕdĭor.opening: (collat. form, acc. to the fourth conj., inf. progrediri, Plaut. Cas. 5, 1, 9 ; imp. progredimino, id. Ps. 3, 2, 70 ; act. collat. form, v. infra fin. ), v. dep. a. [gradior], to come or go forth , to go or march…

prōgressĭo.opening: progredior , a going forth or forward , progression; trop., advancement , progress , growth , increase (a favorite word with Cicero). In gen.: omnium rerum principia parva sunt, sed suis progressionibus usa augentur,…

prōgressor.opening: id. , one that goes forward , advances (late Lat.), Aug. Mus. 6, 6 .

prōgressus.opening: progredior , a going forward , advance , progress (class.). Lit. : (Antonium) Brutus progressu arcuit, Cic. Phil. 11, 2, 4 .—Of the planets: progressus et regressus constantes, Cic. N. D. 2, 20, 51 : progressum…

prŏgymnastes.opening: , = προγυμναστής , a slave who performs gymnastic exercises before his master , Sen. Ep. 83, 4 .

prŏ-hĭbĕo.opening: (old forms, prohibessis, Cato, R. R. 141, 2 ; Enn. ap. Prob. ad Verg. E. 6, 31 (Trag. v. 323 Vahl.): prohibessit, Plaut. Ps. 1, 1, 11 : prohibessint, Cic. Leg. 3, 3 fin. ), v. a. habeo , to hold in front , i. e., To…

prŏhĭbĭtĭo.opening: prohibeo . In gen., a hindering , preventing (post-class.), Dig. 3, 3, 42, § 1 .— In partic., a legal hindering, i. e. a forbidding , prohibition (very rare, but class.): sceleris, Cic. Fragm. ap. Quint. 9, 2, 18 :…

prŏhĭbĭtor.opening: id. , a withholder , restrainer , preventer (post-class.): valetudinum pessimarum, Arn. 7, 249 ; Amm. 21, 12, 9 ; 24, 4, 23 ; App. de Deo Socr. p. 52 med.

prŏhĭbĭtōrĭus.opening: adj. prohibitor , restraining , prohibitory (post-Aug.): avis, i. e. that restrains from an act by unfavorable omens, Plin. 10, 14, 17, § 37 : interdictum, Dig. 43, 26, 1 ; Gai. Inst. 4, 140 ; Ambros. Par. 1, 5, 26 .

prŏ-hinc.opening: adv. , hence , on this account (post-class.), App. M. 3, p. 133, 3 ; so id. ib. 5 , p. 159, 41; 11, p. 270, 40.

prō-ĭcĭo.opening: ( ), , v. a. jacio . Lit. In gen., to throw forth or before; to fling away , throw down; to throw , thrust , drive , or put out; to stretch out , hold out , extend : projectum odoraris cibum, thrown before or to you ,…

prŏ-indē.opening: (abbrev. , like dein for deinde; usually monosyl., Plaut. Am. 1, 1, 155 ; id. Capt. prol. 63 ; 3, 4, 20 et saep.; Ter. And. 2, 4, 5 ; id. Eun. 1, 1, 11 ; id. Heaut. 1, 2, 3 ; dissyl., Cat. 20, 16 ), adv. Just so , in…

prōjectē.opening: adv. , v. proicio, P. a. fin.

prōjectīcĭus.opening: or , , adj. proicio , cast out , exposed (ante- and postclass.). Lit. : puella, Plaut. Cist. 1, 3, 43 ; cf. Argum. Cist. 8.— Trop. : Palladius projecticius, rejected, despised, Amm. 28, 6, 26 .

prōjectĭo.opening: id. , a throwing forward , a stretching out. Lit. : brachii, i e. extension (opp. contractio), Cic. Or. 18, 59 : projectiones aquae, jets , Fest. s. v. tullios, p. 352 Müll.— Transf. , concr., like projectura, a…

prōjecto.opening: v. freq. a. id. . Lit. , to drive forth , drive out (post-class.): homines in aperta pericula, Amm. 14, 5, 7 .— Trop. , to reproach , accuse (ante-class.): aliquem probris, Plaut. Bacch. 3, 6, 38 : ego projector quod tu…

prōjectōrĭus.opening: adj. id. , ejecting , detergent (in later medicine): vis, Theod. Prisc. Diaet. 5 : herba projectoriae virtutis, Aem. Mac. 4, 1 .

prōjectūra.opening: proicio , a jutty , projecture in buildings, Vitr. 3, 2 ; 3 .

prōjectus.opening: (only in abl. sing. ), proicio , a jutting out , projecting , projection (very rare): corporis, Lucr. 3, 987 : frondis, Plin. 17, 11, 19, § 92 .

prō-lābor.opening: v. n. , to glide forward , to slide or slip along , to fall down (class.; in Cic. most freq. in a trop. sense). Lit. : at Canis ad caudam serpens prolabitur Argo, Cic. poët. N. D. 2, 44, 114; Prop. 1, 20, 47 : ruit…

prōlapsĭo.opening: prolabor . A slipping , falling : ingredi sine casu aut prolapsione, Cic. Cael. 17, 41 .— A falling or tumbling down : aedificiorum prolapsiones, Suet. Aug. 30 .— Trop. , an error , misstep (late Lat.): intempestiva…

prōlapsus.opening: prolabor , a falling (late Lat.), Rufin. Orig. Princip. 2, 1, 1 .

prōlātĭo.opening: profero . A bringing forward , putting forth , adducing , pronouncing , etc.: vocis, utterance, Lact. 4, 8, 12 : verbi intellegibilis, Cael. Aur. Tard. 2, 1, 6 ; cf.: Latinorum nominum prolatione, v. l. for…

prōlātīvus.opening: adj. , uttered (late Lat.): si quis insitum et prolativum verbum Dei filium dicat, anathema sit, Hilar. Synod. 45.

prōlāto.opening: v. freq. a. profero . To lengthen , extend , enlarge (not in Cic.; syn.: distendo, extendo; profero, differo): agros, Tac. H. 2, 78 : villam, Col. 1, 5 : rem rusticam, id. 1 , praef. § 19: effugium, Lucr. 1, 983 :…

prōlātus.opening: profero , a bringing forward (post-class.), Tert. adv. Valent. 33 .

prōlectĭbĭlis.opening: adj. prolicio , alluring , Sid. Ep. 4, 18 dub. (al. plectibilibus).

prōlecto.opening: v. freq. a. id. , to allure or entice forth (cf.: illicio, invito). Lit. (post-class.): lacrimae redeunt, prolectante gaudio, App. M. 5, p. 162, 8 : mox prolectante studio, id. ib. 5 , p. 159; 11, p. 259, 33: aviculae…

prō-lēgātus.opening: a lieutenant-governor's substitute , a prolegate , Inscr. Maff. Mus. Veron. 119, 6 ; Inscr. Don. 137, 1 .

pro-lĕpos.opening: a substitute for agreeableness , Not. Tir. p. 80 .

prŏlepsis.opening: , = πρόληψις , in rhetoric, a mentioning a thing by a name which it has not yet received, anticipation , prolepsis (pure Lat. occupatio), Diom. p. 438 and 439 P.; or an allusion to a thing as having happened before it…

prōles.opening: ( gen. plur. prolum, Mart. Cap. 3, § 301 ), pro and root al- of alo, to nourish, whence olesco in ad-olesco, etc.; cf.: suboles, indoles . Lit. , that which grows forth; esp. of human beings, offspring , progeny , child…

prōlētārĭus.opening: proles . According to a division of the people by Servius Tullius, a citizen of the lowest class , who served the State not with his property , but only with his children (proles), a proletary : qui aut non plus mille…

prō-lĕvo.opening: v. a. , to draw forth , trop.: aliquem peccatorum fluctibus mersum, Tert. Poen. 4 .

pro-lībo.opening: v. a. , to pour out , offer as a libation to the gods (Plinian): vina diis, Plin. 14, 18, 22, § 117 ; 14, 19, 23, § 119 ; 28, 4, 11, § 46 .— Impers. pass. : fictilibus prolibatur simpuviis, Plin. 35, 12, 46, § 158 .

prō-lĭcĕo.opening: v. n. liqueo , to run or flow forth : prolicere, emanare, effluere. Varro: demum ubi prolicuit dulcis unda, Gloss. Isid.

prō-lĭcĭo.opening: ( Not. Tir. p. 149 ), , v. a. lacio , to allure or entice forth , to entice , incite ( poet. and in post - Aug. prose): ejus amos cupidam me huc prolicit per tenebras, Plaut. Curc. 1, 2, 2 : voluptas tardā prolicienda…

prō-līmen.opening: a space before the threshold , Hier. in Ezech. 12, 40, 8

prō-lĭquātus.opening: Part. [liquo], liquefied , liquid , App. Mag. p. 283, 39 .

prōlixĭtas.opening: prolixus . Great length , breadth , or width , great extension (post-class.): terrae, App. de Mundo, p. 60, 21: colubra prolixitatis immensae, Arn. 7, 250 : temporis, length of time, Dig. 36, 1, 22 . — Of speech,…

prōlixo.opening: v. a. id. , to lengthen , extend : aciem ferramenti, Col. 4, 24, 22 .

prō-lixus.opening: adj. laxus , stretched far out , long , broad (syn.: latus, spatiosus). Lit. (not in Cic.): capillus passus prolixus, Ter. Heaut. 2, 3, 49 Umpfenb. (Fleck. prolixe): comae, Ov. Tr. 4, 2, 34 : barba, Verg. E. 8, 34…

prōlŏcūtĭo.opening: ( ), , proloquor , a preamble (late Lat.), Claud. Mam. Stat. Anim 2, 3 ; 2, 10 .

prōlŏcūtor.opening: ( ), , id. , a pleader , advocate , Auct. Quint. Decl. Trib. Marian. 3.

prŏlŏgĭum.opening: , = προλόγιον , a preface , introduction : prologium, principium, proloquium. Pacuvius: quid est? nam me exanimasti prologio tuo, Paul. ex Fest. p 226 Müll.

prolŏgus.opening: , = πρόλογος . Lit. , a preface or introduction to a play , a prologue , Ter. Phorm. prol. 14 : in prologis scribundis operā abutitur, id. And. prol. 5 : in Hydriae (Menandri) prologo, Quint. 11, 3, 91 : in prologo…

prolongo.opening: v. [pro-longus], to lengthen , prolong , extend (late Lat. for prorogo, profero, duco): dies, Vulg. Deut. 6, 2 : iniquitatem suam, id. Psa. 128, 3 ; Hilar. ad loc.; id. in Psa. 119, 13 ; Aug. Serm. 9, 2 : sermonem,…

prōlŏquĭum.opening: proloquor . * An introduction , preamble , Paul. ex Fest. p. 226 Müll.; v. prologium.— An assertion , proposition , axiom (class. Lat. pronunciatum), the Gr. ἀξίωμα , Varr. ap. Gell. 16, 8, 1 ; cf. App. Dogm. Plat. 3,…

prō-lŏquor.opening: (quūtus), 3, v. dep. n. and a. In gen., to speak out , utter , declare , say (mostly ante-class. and poet. ; not found in Cic., Cæs., or Quint.): prolocutum (dicimus), cum animo quod habuit, extulit loquendo, Varr. L.…

prō-lŭbīdo.opening: will , desire , inclination : prolubium (al. prolubiem) et prolubidinem dici ab eo quod lubeat, Varr. ap. Non. 64, 13 .

prō-lŭbĭum.opening: lubet . Subject., will , desire , inclination (ante- and post-class.): muliebre ingenium, prolubium, occasio, Att. ap. Non. 64, 8 ; Novat. and Laber. ib. 10 and 12; Ter. Ad. 5, 9, 28 ; Gell. 16, 19, 12 .— Object.,…

prō-lūcĕo.opening: v. n. , to shine forth , Sen. Ot. Sap. 5, 4 ( id. Vit. Beat. 32 ; Haase, perducens).

prōlūdĭum.opening: proludo , preliminary exercise , training (late Lat.): cum quasi in proludiis negotium spectaretur, Amm. 28, 1, 10 : cotidiana proludia exercitūs, id. 14, 11, 3 : disciplinae castrensis, id. 16, 5, 10 .

prō-lūdo.opening: v. n. , to play or practise beforehand , to prelude. Lit. : et sparsā ad pugnam proludit harenā, Verg. G. 3, 234 .— Absol. : sic ubi prolusit, etc., Ov. A. A. 3, 515 ; Flor. 3, 22, 6 .— Trop. : sententiis, quibus…

prō-lūgĕo.opening: v. n. , to mourn greatly : prolugere dicuntur qui solito diutius lugent, Paul. ex Fest. p. 226 Müll.

prō-lŭo.opening: v. a. , to wash forth or out , to cast out (mostly poet. and in postAug. prose; not found in Cic.; once in Cæs.; v. infra ). Lit. : genus omne natantum Litore in extremo ... fluctus Proluit, Verg. G. 3, 543 ; ventrem,…

prōlūsĭo.opening: proludo , a prelude , transf., a preliminary exercise , trial , essay , Cic. de Or. 2, 80, 325 ; id. Div. in Caecil. 14, 47

prōlŭvĭes.opening: proluo , an overflow , inundation (class.): Romae et maxime Appia ad Martis mira proluvies, Cic. Q. Fr. 3, 7, 1 (Bait.); Lucr. 5, 950 : alvi, i. e. filth cast forth, excrements, id. 6, 1200 ; Col. 6, 7, 1 ; 12, 38, 1 :…

prōlŭvĭo.opening: id. , an inundation , App. de Mundo, p. 73, 33.

prōlŭvĭōsus.opening: adj. proluvio , overflowing : pestis, i. e. spreading in all directions , Auct. ap. Fulg. p. 564, 13 .

prōlŭvĭum.opening: prolus , an overflow; trop., an excess , abundance : castitatis, Ambros. Virg. 1, 4, 18 ; cf.: proluvium, profusio, Non. p. 373 ; Ter. Ad. 5, 9, 28 (Umpfenb. and Fleck. prolubium); id. ap. Serv. ad Verg. A. 3, 217 .

prŏlўtae.opening: , = προλύται , jurists who , after studying five years , were dismissed by their instructors with credit , Dig. praef. § 5.

prō-măgister.opening: one who presides , rules , etc., in the place of another , a vice-president , vicegerent , vice-director (in class. Lat. pro magistro), Inscr. Fabr. p. 442, 49 ; Inscr Grut. 426, 5; 607, 1 al.

prōmăgistĕrĭum.opening: pro-ma gister , the office of a promagister, a vice presidency , lieutenancy , etc., Inscr. Grut. 173, 5 .

prō-măgistrātus.opening: administration by a substitute or deputy , S. C. de Bacchan.; Inscr. Grut. 629 fin. ; Inscr. Murat. 582, 1 .

promenervat.opening: (in Saliari carmine) pro monet, Fest. p. 205 Müll.

prō-mercālis.opening: adj. merx , that is dealt in , that is bought and sold (post-Aug.): res, Col. 1, 8, 13; 11, 1, 34 : vestes, Suet. Gram. 23 : aurum, id. Caes. 54 ; Gell 4, 1, 23.

prō-mercĭum.opening: id. , trade , traffic , merchandise (post-class.), Dig. 48, 8, 3, § 4 ; 30, 1, 41 al.

prō-mĕrĕo.opening: v. a. , and , , v. dep. a. To deserve , be deserving of , merit , in a good or bad sense (class.) In gen.: retineri nequeo, quin dicam ea, quae promeres, Plaut. Trin. 3, 2, 15 ; id. Am. 5, 2, 12 : quid mali sum…

Prŏmētheus.opening: ( ), , , = Προμηθεύς (the Forethinker), a son of Iapetus and Clymene , brother of Epimetheus , and father of Deucalion. He formed men of clay, and animated them by means of fire brought from heaven; for which he was…

prō-mĭco.opening: v. n. and a. Neutr. , to gleam forth; transf., to spring forth , start forth (post-class.): promicant molles plumulae, i. e. grow out, App. M. 3, p. 138, 30 : rosae, id. ib. 10 , p. 253, 9: lacrimae, burst or gush forth…

prōmĭnens.opening: Part. and P. a. , from promineo.

prōmĭnenter.opening: adv. , v. promineo, P. a. fin.

prōmĭnentĭa.opening: prominens , a jutting out , projection , prominence (postAug.): ita uti summam habeant prominentiam (anterides), Vitr. 6, 11 ; praecordiorum, Cael. Aur. Acut. 3, 5, 50 ; in plur. of promontories , Sol. 27, 1 .

prō-mīnĕo.opening: v. n. , to stand or jut out , be prominent , to overhang , project (not in Cic.; cf. Moser ad Cic. Rep. 3, 7, p. 352 ext.; syn.: exsto, emineo). Lit. : Phaselis prominet penitus in altum, Liv. 37, 23 : collis prominens,…

prō-mĭno.opening: v. a. , to drive forward or along : jumenta ad lacum bibendi causā, App. M. 9, p. 229, 24 .

prōmĭnŭlus.opening: adj. promineo , projecting a little , rather prominent (postclass.): venter, Capitol. Pert. 12 : mammae, Sol. 27 fin. : labra, Mart. Cap. 3, § 261 .

prōmiscam.opening: , and , advv. , v. promiscuus fin. , A., B., and C.

prō-miscŭus.opening: (collat. form , Gell. 11, 16, 8 ; 16, 13, 4 ; Liv. 5, 13, 7 ; prob. also ante-class.; v. below the adv. promiscam), , adj. misceo . Lit. , mixed , not separate or distinct , without distinction , in common ,…

prōmissĭo.opening: , ōnis promitto . In gen., a promising , promise (class. only in sing. ; prop. the act of promising; cf. promissum, the thing promised ): provinciae, Cic. Att. 8, 9, 4 : auxilii, id. Fam. 4, 13, 1 : scelerum, id. Phil.…

prōmissīvus.opening: adj. promitto , promising , promissive; in gram.; promissivum tempus, i. e. the future tense , Cons. p. 2061 P.: modus, Diom. p. 328 P.: sententiae, Isid. 2, 21, 18 .— Adv. : , by way of promise , with a promise…

prōmissor.opening: id. , a promiser , esp. who promises great things (very rare), Hor A. P 138; Quint. 1, 5, 6 Zumpt.

prō-mitto.opening: (sync. forms: promisti for promisisti, Ter. Ad. 5, 8, 17 ; Cat. 110, 3 : promisse for promisisse, id. 110, 5 : promissem, Plaut. Bacch. 5, 1, 12 ; archaic inf. pass. promittier, id. ib. 4, 8, 32 ), v. a. Lit. , to let…

prōmo.opening: (msi), mptum (mtum), , v. a. pro-emo , to take , give , or bring out or forth , to produce (freq. and class.; syn.: profero, effero) Lit. : si quid tibi opus erit promptu, promito, Plaut. Cist. 1, 1, 113 : Pa.…

prō-mŏnĕo.opening: v. a. , to warn or admonish further : ibi te igitur videbo et promonebo, Cic. Att. 4, 12 fin. B. and K. (dub.; al. promovebo).

prōmōtĭo.opening: promoveo , advancement , preferment , promotion (post-class.), Lampr Anton. Diadum. 2; Firm. Math. 3, 7, 5; Ascon ad Cic. Verr. 2, 1, 28 .

prōmōtus.opening: promoveo , advancement , promotion (post-class.), Tert. Coron Mil. 3 fin.

prō-mōvĕo.opening: ( pluperf. promorat. Hor Epod. 11, 14: promosset, Ov. Am 2, 9, 17 Jahn), , v. a. , to move forward , cause to advance , push onward , advance. Lit. In gen.: saxa vectibus, Caes B. C. 2, 11: onera, Col. 11, 1, 8 ; Plin.…

promptē.opening: adv. , v. promo, P. a. fin.

promptim.opening: adv. 1. promptus , quickly , suddenly (post-class. for the usual prompte), Tert. Carm. in Gen. 98 .

prompto.opening: v. freq. a. promo , to give forth or out abundantly , to distribute , dispose of a thing (Plautin.): thesauros Jovis, i. e. to be Jupiter's treasurer, Plaut. Ps. 2, 2, 33 : illum meum malum promptare malim quam…

promptŭārĭus.opening: ( ), , adj. promo , of or belonging to distribution (sc. of things stored up), distributing : arca vestiaria, armarium promptuarium, i. e. storehouse, repository, Cato, R. R. 11, 3 : cella, App. Mag. p. 309, 20 ; and,…

promptŭlus.opening: adj. dim. [1. promptus], ready , prompt (late Lat.): ad loquendum promptulus, Hier. in Daniel, praef. fin.

promptus.opening: ( ), , promo, prop. a taking forth; hence , An exposing to view , a being visible , visibility; only in the phrase in promptu (esse, habere, ponere, etc.), public , open , visible , manifest , before the eyes : ut…

promtus.opening: , = promptus, v. promo, Part. and P. a. , and 2. promptus.

promulcum.opening: a tow-rope : promulco agi dicitur navis, cum scaphae ducitur fune, Paul. ex Fest. p. 224 Müll.; v. remulcum.

prōmulgātĭo.opening: promulgo , a making publicly known , a proclaiming , publishing , promulgation : leges nullā promulgatione latae, Cic. Phil. 1, 10, 25 ; 5, 3, 8 ; id. Fam. 1, 5 , a, 2; id. Leg. 3, 19, 43 .

prōmulgātor.opening: id. , one that publishes or proclaims a thing, a promulgator : Numa feriarum promulgator, Front. de Feriis Als. 3 Mai.

prōmulgo.opening: v. a. etym. unknown , in publicist's lang., Lit. , to expose to public view (as a proposed new law, etc.), to make known , publish , promulgate (cf.: edico, pronuntio): promulgari leges dicuntur, cum primum in vulgus…

prōmulsĭdāre.opening: promulsis , a tray on which the promulsis was served : in promulsidari, Petr. 31 .—In plur. : promulsidaria, Dig. 34, 2, 19, § 10 .

prō-mulsis.opening: mulsum . Lit. , a relish of eggs, salt fish, mead, etc., served first at a Roman banquet , a whet , antepast , Cic. Fam. 9, 16, 8 ; 9, 20, 1 .— Transf. A foretaste : libidinis, Petr. 24 fin. — For promulsidare, the tray…

prō-mulsus.opening: Part. [mulceo], stroked forward , smoothed down in front : caproneae, App. Flor. 1, p. 342, 2 .

prōmuntŭrĭum.opening: ( ), , pro-mineo . The highest part of a chain of mountains , a mountain-ridge , Liv. 21, 35, 8 .— A part of a mountain projecting into the sea , a headland , promontory , Cic. Verr. 2, 5, 56, § 145 ; id. Phil. 1, 3, 7…

prōmus.opening: adj. promo . In economic lang., of or belonging to giving out , distributing. cella, a store-room , larder , Tert. Res. Carn. 27 .— Subst. : , , a store-room , Tert. ad Uxor. 2, 4 fin. —Much more freq., Subst. : , , , a…

promuscis.grammar: ĭdis, a corrupt form for proboscis
promuscis.opening: a trunk , proboscis : elephas, promuscis, Not. Tir. p. 174 .

pro-mūtŭor.opening: v. dep. n. , to be loaned beforehand : promutuor, προδανείζομαι , Gloss. Philox.

prō-mūtŭus.opening: adj. , paid over beforehand , advanced , loaned : publicanis (imperabatur) insequentis anni vectigal promutuum, was demanded in advance as a loan, Caes. B. C. 3, 32 fin. (for which before: insequentis anni mutua…

prō-năto.opening: v. n. , to swim forth , swim along (post-class.): delphines e toto mari pronatant ad Arionis cantum, Hyg. Astr. 2, 17 fin.

prō-nātus.opening: sprung forth , born , for prognatus, Tert. Anim. 2 .

prŏnāus.opening: or , , , = πρόναος , the porch , vestibule , portico of a temple , Vitr. 3, 1 fin. ; 4, 4, 1 ; 4, 7, 2 ; 5, 1, 9; Inscr. Grut. 27, 2 ; 214 .

prō-necto.opening: v. a. , to knit or spin out (post-Aug.): seriem aevi, Stat. S. 4, 3, 145 .

prŏ-nĕpos.opening: (scanned prōnĕpos, Sid. Carm. 11 fin. ), , , a great-grandson , Dig. 38, 10, 1 ; 38, 10, 14 ; Cic. Tusc. 3, 12, 26 ; id. Phil. 13, 7, 15 ; id. Att. 16, 14, 4 ; Ov. M. 10, 606 .

prōnĭtas.opening: pronus , inclination , propensity , proneness : naturae ad malum, Sen. Contr. praef., dub. (the phrase is wanting in several MSS.).

prōno.opening: v. a. id. , to bend forward , to bow (post-class.): ipsi latrones ad pavimentum defuncti ora pronaverant, Sid. Ep. 8, 11 fin. ; 5, 17 .

prŏnoea.opening: , = πρόνοια , providence (pure Lat. providentia), Cic. N. D. 2, 64, 160 ( id. ib. 1, 8, 18 ; 2, 22, 58 , written as Greek).

prō-nōmen.opening: in gram., a pronoun, Varr. L. L. 8, § 45 Müll.; Quint. 1, 4, 19 ; 1, 5, 47 ; 26 ; 11, 3, 87 et saep.

prōnōmĭnālis.opening: adj. pronomen , of or belonging to a pronoun , pronominal : constructio, Prisc. p. 1069 P.

prō-nōmĭnātĭo.opening: a figure of speech , by which another epithet is substituted for a proper name (e. g. Africani nepotes, for Gracchi), Auct. Her. 4, 31, 42 .

prōnōmĭno.opening: v. a. pronomen ; in gram., to designate a person by a pronoun, Prisc. p. 1064 P.

prōnŭbans.opening: Part. [pronuba], arranging a marriage : pronubante nobis maestitia, Hier. Vit. Malch. n. 6.

prōnŭbus.opening: adj. pro-nubo , of or belonging to marriage , bridal , promoting marriage : canes, pimps, Tert. ad Nat. 1, 2 : anulus, wedding-ring, id. Apol. 6 : nox, the bridal night, Claud. Cons. Honor. 642 : flamma, a bridal torch,…

prō-nŭmĕro.opening: v. a. , to count up , reckon , enumerate (post-class.): versiculos pro morarum mercede, Sid. Ep. 2, 10 .

prōnuntĭābĭlis.opening: ( ), , adj. pronuncio , declarative , enunciative : oratio, i. e. a complete sentence, a proposition, enunciation, App. Dogm. Plat. 3, p. 29 med.

prōnuntĭātĭo.opening: ( ), , id. . A public declaration , publication , proclamation : quā pronuntiatione factā, Caes. B. C. 2, 25 fin. —Of the decision of a judge, Cic. Clu. 20, 56 ; Petr. 80 ; Dig. 48 .— Of the proclamation of a public…

prōnuntĭātīvus.opening: ( ), , adj. pronuntio , of or belonging to declaration , declarative , enunciative; in gram.: pronuntiativus modus, i. e. the indicative mood, Diom. p. 329 P.— Adv. : , declaratively , affirmatively , Don. ad Ter.…

prōnuntĭātor.opening: ( ), , , id. . One who delivers any thing , a reciter : meae orationi M. Caesar actor contigit et pronuntiator, Front. Ep. ad M. Caes. 1, 6 Mai.— In gen., a relater , narrator : Thucydides rerum gestarum pronuntiator…

prōnuntĭātus.opening: ( ), (only in abl. sing. ), pronuntio , pronunciation (post-class.): ratio in pronuntiatu, Gell. 4, 17, 8 ; 15, 3, 1 .

prō-nuntĭo.grammar: āvi, ātum, 1 v. n. and a.
prō-nuntĭo.opening: ( ), , v. n. and a. , to make publicly known , to publish , proclaim , announce (cf.: edico, promulgo). Lit. In gen.: palam de sellā ac tribunali pronuntiat, sese ejus nomen recepturum, Cic. Verr. 2, 2, 38, § 94 : cum…

prō-nūper.opening: adv. , in a supposititious verse, ap. Plaut. Trin. 2, 4, 26 ; v. parerga, I. p. 528 Ritschl sq.

prō-nŭrus.opening: a grandson's wife , Dig. 38, 10, 4 ; Paul. ex Fest. p. 224 Müll.: pronurus et magni Laomedontis ero, i. e. the wife of Paris, who was grandson of Laomedon, Ov. H. 17, 206 .

prōnus.opening: (archaic form of fem. pronis, Varr. ap. Non. 494 fin. ), adj. [like Gr. πρᾶνής = πρηνής , from root pra-, πρό ; cf. prae). Lit. , turned forward , bent or inclined , leaning or hanging forward , stooping , bending down…

prŏoecŏnŏmĭa.opening: , = προοικονομία , a previous arrangement , Serv. Verg. A. 5, 858 ; 9, 468 .

prŏoemĭor.opening: v. dep. prooemium , to make an introduction or preface (postAug.): prooemiatur apte, Plin. Ep. 2, 3, 3 ; Sid. Ep. 4, 3 .

prŏoemĭum.opening: , = προοίμιον . An introduction , preface , proem (class.; syn.: exordium, principium): quod principium Latine vel exordium dicitur, majore quădam ratione Graeci videntur προοίμιον nominasse: quia a nostris initium modo…

prō^pāgātĭo.opening: 1. propago , a propagating , propagation. Lit. (class.): propagatio vitium, Cic. Sen. 15, 53 : propagationum genera tria sunt in usu maxime, Col. Arb. 7 : propagationes facere, Dig. 19, 2, 24 .— Transf. : quae…

prō^pāgātor.opening: 1. propago , a propagator; trop., an enlarger , extender (class.): provinciae propagator, Cic. Att. 8, 3, 3 (al. prorogator).— An epithet of Jupiter , as the enlarger of boundaries , App. de Mundo, p. 75, 10: ORBIS AC…

prō^pāges.opening: id. A set , layer; for the usual propago: propages progenies a propagando: ut faciunt rustici, eum vitem vetulam supprimunt, ut ex eā unā plures faciant, Paul. ex Fest. p. 227 Müll.— Transf. , offspring , progeny ,…

prō^pāgĭno.opening: , no perf. , , v. a. 1. propago , to propagate (post-class.): populi propaginati, Tert. Pall. 2 fin.

propagmen.opening: id. , propagation; trop., prolongation : vitae, Enn. ap. Non. 64, 32 (Ann. v. 458 Vahl.).

prō^pāgo.opening: (prŏ-, Lucr. 1, 42 ; Verg. A. 6, 870 ; Ov. M. 2, 38 : prō-, Verg. G. 2, 26 ), , ( , Fab. Pict. ap. Gell. 10, 15, 13 ) [1. propago]. Lit. A set , layer of a plant, Cic. Sen. 15, 52 ; Col. Arb. 7, 2 : arbores aut semine…

prō-pălam.opening: adv. , openly , publicly , notoriously , manifestly (class.): minus jam furtificus sum: rapio propalam, Plaut. Ep. 1, 1, 10 : signis propalam collocatis, * Cic. de Or. 1, 35, 161 : dicere, Liv. 34, 33 : obviam ire, id.…

prōpălo.opening: , no perf. , , v. a. propalam , to make public or manifest , to divulge (post-class.), Sid. Ep. 9, 11 : propalata et publica veritas, Oros. 6, 5 : divinitus propalatum, Aug. Ep. 137 : nondum propalatam esse sanctorum…

prō-pansus.opening: and , , Partt. [pando], spread out , extended (postclass.): propansis pinnis, App. M. 6, p. 179, 14 : propassis pennis, id. Flor. p. 365, 35 (or de Deo Socr. p. 109 Hild.).

prō-pătĭor.opening: v. dep. a. , to endure before (post-class.), Schol. Juv. 2, 50 .

prŏpător.opening: , = προπάτωρ , a forefather , ancestor (eccl. Lat.), Tert. Praes. 49 .

prō-pătŭlus.opening: adj. Open in front , not covered up , open , uncovered (class.): in aperto ac propatulo loco, Cic. Verr. 2, 4, 49, § 110 .—More freq., Subst. : , , , an open or uncovered place. In phrase in propatulo (class.): in…

prŏpe.opening: adv. and prep. pro and demonstr suff. -pe (cf.: nempe, quippe), = Sanscr. -pa . Adv. ( comp. propius, and sup. proxime, v. under propior), near , nigh (class.). Lit. , in space: quaenam vox mihi prope hic sonat? Quis…

prŏpĕdĭem.opening: (also separate, ), adv. prope-dies , at an early day , very soon , shortly (class.), Plaut. Pers. 2, 4, 24 ; 5, 2, 56 : prognostica mea propediem exspecta, Cic. Att. 2, 1, 11 : propediem te videbo, id. Div. 1, 23, 47 ;…

prō-pello.opening: (prŏpellat, Lucr. 4, 195 ; 6, 1026 ), , v. a. Lit. , to drive before one's self , to drive , push , or urge forward , to drive forth; to hurl , propel , hurl or cast down , to overthrow (class.; syn.: proturbo,…

prŏpĕ-mŏdŏ.opening: weakened from propemodum; cf. postmodo , nearly , almost : tenes jam? Ca. propemodo, Plaut. Trin. 3, 3, 50 (cf. Ritschl ad loc.); id. Ps. 1, 3, 42 (Ritschl and Fleck. propemodum.)

prŏpĕmŏdum.opening: adv. prope-modus . Nearly , almost (class.): propemodum jam scio, quid siet rei, Plaut. Men. 5, 2, 12 ; id. Ps. 1, 3, 42 Ritschl: quid enim sors est! idem propemodum, quod micare, quod talos jacere, Cic. Div. 2, 41, 85…

prŏpemptĭcon.opening: , = προπεμπτικόν , a farewell poem , in which a prosperous journey is wished: propempticon Metio Celeri, Stat. S. 3, 2 in lemm.; Sid. Carm. 24 in lemm.

prō-pendeo.opening: (in Plaut. As. 2, 2, 39 , the correct reading is propendes), v. n. , to hang forth or forward , hang down. Lit. (class.): ex ramis propendens, Plin. 26, 7, 20, § 36 ; Suet. Galb. 21 : lanx propendet, Cic. Tusc. 5, 17,…

prō-pendŭlus.opening: adj. propendeo , hanging forth or forward , hanging down (post-class.): propenduli crines, App. Flor. 1, p. 342, 2 .

prōpensē.opening: adv. , v. propendeo, P. a. fin.

prōpensĭo.opening: propendeo , inclination , propensity : propensio ad summum bonum adipiscendum, Cic. Fin. 4, 17, 47 .

prōpensus.opening: Part. and P. a. , from propendeo.

prŏpĕrābĭlis.opening: adj. propero , hasty , rapid (eccl. Lat.): calor (opp. rigor tardabilis), Tert. Anim. 43 .

prŏpĕrans.opening: Part. and P. a. , from propero.

prŏpĕranter.opening: adv. , v. , P. a. , A. fin.

prŏpĕrantĭa.opening: propero , a hastening , haste (very rare; not in Cic. or Cæs.): ex tantā properantiā, Sall. J. 36, 3 : periculum ex properantiā, Tac. A. 12, 20 .

prŏpĕrātim.opening: adv. properatus , hastily , quickly , speedily (ante-class.): properatim conficere opus, Caecil. ap. Non. 153, 15 : pergis properatim, Pompon. ib. 155, 3 ; also Sisenn. acc. to Gell. 12, 15, 1 .

prŏpĕrātĭo.opening: propero , a hastening , haste , quickness , speediness (rare but class.), Cic. Fam. 5, 12, 2 ; Q. Cic. ap. Cic. Fam. 16, 27, 1 : properationem explorare, Sall. H. 2, 50 Dietsch; Amm. 31, 5, 9 .

prŏpĕrātō.opening: adv. , v. , P. a. , B. fin.

prŏpĕrātus.opening: Part. and P. a. , from propero.

prŏpĕrē.opening: and , advv. , v. properus fin. , A. and B.

prŏpĕrĭpēs.opening: adj. properus pes , swift of foot : ducem sequuntur Gallae properipedem, Cat. 63, 34 .

prŏpĕro.grammar: āvi, ātum, 1 v. a. and n.
prŏpĕro.opening: v. a. and n. properus . Act. , to hasten , quicken , accelerate; to prepare , make , or do with haste (mostly poet. and in post-Aug. prose): alia quae incepto usui forent properare, Sall. J. 37, 4 : itineris properandi…

Prŏpertĭus.opening: a Roman surname. So, Sex. Aurelius Propertius, a celebrated elegiac poet , an older contemporary of Ovid , Ov. Tr. 4, 10, 53 ; Plin. Ep. 9, 22, 1 ; Quint. 10, 1, 93 .— Gen. Properti, Ov. Tr. 2, 465 al.

prŏpĕrus.opening: adj. root par-, to make; whence parare, parĕre , quick , speedy , hastening (mostly poet. and in postAug. prose): properam pro celeri ac strenuā dixisse antiquos, testimonio est Cato, Fest. p. 253 Müll.: properi…

prŏ-pēs.opening: a rope , the loose part of the sheet with which a sail is trimmed to the wind (ante-class.), Turp. ap. Isid. Orig. 19, 4 .

prōpetrāre.opening: , mandare quod perficiatur; nam impetrare est exorare, et perpetrare perficere, Paul. ex Fest. p. 227 Müll.

prō-pexus.opening: Part. [pecto], combed forward , combed down in front , hanging down ( poet. ): crines, Att. ap. Serv. Verg. A. 12, 605 : propexam in pectore barbam, Verg. A. 10, 838 : propexam ad pectora barbam, Ov. F. 1, 259 : propexa…

prŏphēta.opening: and , , , = προφήτης , a foreteller , soothsayer , prophet (post-class.; cf. vates): prophetas in Adrasto Julius nominat antistites fanorum oraculorumque interpretes, Fest. p. 229 Müll. (Trag. Rel. p. 194 Rib.):…

prŏphētālis.opening: adj. propheta , prophetic , prophetical (eccl. Lat.): os, Hier. Ep. 54 , n. 17: habitus, Hilar. in Matt. 2, 2: scriptura, id. ib. 23, 4 ; Cassiod. in Psa. 16 .

prŏphētātĭo.opening: propheto , a soothsaying , prophesying , Aug. Civ. Dei , 10, 32; 18, 14.

prŏphētīa.opening: , = προφητεία , prediction , prophecy (eccl. Lat.), Tert. Anim. 35 fin. ; Vulg. 1 Tim. 1, 18 .— A body of prophets or singers , Vulg. 1 Par. 15, 27 et saep.

prŏphētĭālis.opening: adj. prophetia , of or belonging to prophecy , prophetic (eccl. Lat.): patrocinium, Tert. adv. Val. 28 .

prŏphētĭcus.opening: adj. , = προφητικός , predicting , prophetic , prophetical (eccl. Lat.): Moyses propheticus, non poëticus pastor, Tert. Cor. Mil. 7 : sermo, Vulg. 2 Pet. 1, 19.— Adv. : , prophetically (eccl. Lat.): prophetice dictum,…

prŏphētis.opening: , = προφῆτις , a prophetess (eccl. Lat.), Tert. Res. Carn. 11 ; Vulg. Judic. 4, 4 .

prŏphētissa.opening: propheta , a prophetess (eccl. Lat.), Tert. Praescr. 51 ; Hier. Ep. 7, 6 ; Vulg. Luc. 2, 36 .

prŏphētīzo.opening: v. a. id. , to prophesy (eccl. Lat.), Vulg. Matt. 26, 68 ; id. Luc. 22, 64 .

prŏphēto.opening: , no perf. , , v. a. id. , to foretell , predict , prophesy (eccl. Lat.; cf.: praedico, vaticinor): docet, instruit, prophetat, Prud. στεφ. 13, 101: servi prophetaturi, Tert. Anim. 47 : mors Christi prophetata, id. adv.…

prŏpīna.opening: , for popina, a cook-shop , acc. to Isid. Orig. 15, 2 fin.

prŏpīnātĭo.opening: propino . A drinking to one's health , a pledging in something (post-Aug.): tralaticiā propinatione dignus, Petr. 113 : propinationem ab aliquo accipere, Sen. Ben. 2, 21, 5 .—In plur. : propinationibus crebris aliquem…

prŏpīno.opening: (the first o scanned long, Mart. 1, 69, 3 ; 3, 82 ; 8, 6 ; Ter. Eun. 5, 9, 57 ; Plaut. Ps. 5, 1, 19 ; id. Stich. 3, 2, 15 ), , v. a. , = προπίνω . To drink to one's health , to pledge one in something (class.): propino…

prŏpinquĭtas.opening: propinquus , nearness , vicinity , proximity , propinquity (class.). Lit. , of place: ex longinquitate, propinquitate, Cic. Inv. 1, 26, 38 : hostium, Caes. B. G. 2, 20 : loci, id. ib. 7, 19 : ex propinquitate pugnare,…

prŏpinquo.grammar: āvi, ātum, 1 v. a. and n.
prŏpinquo.opening: v. a. and n. propinquus . Act. , to bring near , bring on , hasten , accelerate ( poet. ): tu rite propinques Augurium, Verg. A. 10, 254 : mortem, Sil. 2, 281 .— Neutr. , to draw near , come nigh , approach (mostly…

prŏpinquus.opening: adj. prope , near , neighboring (class.). Lit. , of place: rus, Ter. Eun. 5, 5, 1 : loca, Sall. J. 12, 2 ; 48, 4 : nimium propinquus Sol, Hor. C. 1, 22, 21 : propinquum praedium, Cic. Rosc. Am. 46, 133 : provinciae, id.…

prŏpĭo.opening: , no perf. , , v. n. prope , to draw near , approach (post-class.): nec domibus nostris propient mala, Paul. Nol. Carm. 23, 412 ; in pass. , id. ib. 27, 405 .

prŏpĭor.opening: gen. ōris, adj. comp. , and , , adj. sup. (v. below, II.) [from the obsol. propis; whence prope]. Comp. , nearer , nigher. Lit. , of place: portus propior, Verg. A. 3, 530 : tumulus, Liv. 22, 24 : ut propior patriae sit…

prŏpĭtĭābĭlis.opening: adj. propitio , that is easy to be appeased , propitiable (anteand post-class.): animus, Enn. ap. Non. 155, 31 (Com. v. 6 Vahl.); Prud. στεφ . 14, 130.

prŏpĭtĭātĭo.opening: id. , an appeasing , atonement , propitiation (post-class.), Macr. Somn. Scip. 1, 7 : propitiatio placatio est, Isid. Orig. 15, 4 ; Ambros. Cant. 2, 14 ; Vulg. Lev. 23, 28 et saep.— Transf. : ipse est propitiatio pro…

prŏpĭtĭātor.opening: propitio , a propitiator (eccl. Lat.): habentes propitiatorem dominum nostrum Jesum Christum, Hier. Ep. 21 , n. 2; Ambros. in Luc. prol. 7 .

prŏpĭtĭātōrĭus.opening: adj. propitiator , atoning , reconciling (eccl. Lat.): bonitas Dei, Ambros. Fug. Sec. 3, 14 .—Hence, subst. : † , , A means of reconciliation , an atonement , propitiation : propitiatorium, quasi propitiationis…

prŏpĭtĭātrix.opening: id. , a propitiatress (eccl. Lat.): delictorum, Ambros. Laps. Virg. 4 , n. 16.

prŏpĭtĭĕtas.opening: propitius , a state of propitiation , reconciliation , Not. Tir. p. 92 .

prŏpĭtĭo.opening: (prōpĭtĭo, Ven. Fort. S. M. 4, 163; Prud. στεφ . 3, 211), v. a. id. , to render favorable , to appease , propitiate (ante-class. and post-Aug.; cf. placo), Pac. ap. Non. 111, 20 : Venerem, Plaut. Poen. 1, 2, 120 : manes…

prŏpĭtĭus.opening: (prōpĭtĭus, Juvenc. 1, 16, 43 al. ), adj. prope , favorable , well-disposed , gracious , kind , propitious (class.; cf.: faustus, prosperus, secundus). Of persons, esp. of deities: Mars pater, te precor quaesoque, uti…

prŏplasma.opening: , = πρόπλασμα , a pattern , model , after which the artist fashions a thing (post-Aug.), Plin. 35, 12, 45, § 155 (in Cic. Att. 12, 41, 4 , written as Greek).

prŏpnĭgēum.opening: , = προπνίγειον , the place before an oven or furnace , the room where a bath was heated (pure Lat. praefurnium), Vitr. 5, 11 ; Plin. Ep. 2, 17, 11 .

Prōpoetĭdes.opening: , = Πρωποιτιδες , Cyprian girls , who , having denied the divinity of Venus , were turned to stone , Ov. M. 10, 220 ; Lact. Placid. Fab. Ov. 10, 7 .

prŏpōla.opening: (prōpōla, Lucil. v. infra ), , , = προπώλης , a forestaller , a retailer , huckster (class.): sicuti cum primus ficos propola recentes protulit, Lucil. ap. Non. 154, 27 ; Plaut. Aul. 3, 5, 38 : panis et vinum a propolā,…

prŏpŏlis.opening: , = πρόπολις , the third foundation in making honey , a gummy substance with which the bees close the crevices of their hives , bee-glue , propolis : propolin vocant, quod apes faciunt ad foramen introitus protectum in…

prō-pollŭo.opening: v. a. , to defile or pollute , Tac. A. 3, 66 dub.; v. Orell. ad h. l.

prŏpŏma.opening: , = πρόπομα , a drink taken before eating , a whet (postclass.), Pall. 3, 32 in lemm.

prō-pōno.opening: v. a. , to put or set forth , to set or lay out , to place before , expose to view , to display (class.). Lit. : proponere vexillum, Caes. B. G. 2, 20 : pallentesque manus, sanguineumque caput, Ov. Tr. 3, 9, 30 : i puer…

Prŏpontis.opening: (Prōpontis, Manil. 4, 676 ), ĭdos and , , = Προποντίς , the Propontis or Sea of Marmora , between the Hellespont and the Thracian Bosporus , Mel. 1, 1, 5 ; 1, 3, 1 ; Plin. 4, 12, 24, § 76 ; Liv. 38, 16 ; Tac. A. 2, 54 ;…

prō-porro.opening: adv. (Lucretian). Lit. , furthermore , moreover : et, sibi proporro quae sint primordia, quaerunt, Lucr. 2, 979 ; 4, 890 ; 5, 312 ; Lucil. ap. Non. p. 140, 13 .— Transf. , in gen., altogether , utterly , wholly , Lucr.…

prō-portĭo.opening: comparative relation , proportion , symmetry , analogy , likeness (class.): proportio, quod dicunt ἀνάλογον , Varr. L. L. 10, § 2 Müll.; Cic. Univ. 5 : Penatis singulariter Labeo Antistius posse dici putat, quia…

prōportĭōnābĭlĭter.opening: adv. lengthened form of proportionaliter , proportionally , Boëth. 1 Geom. p. 1206.

prōportĭōnālis.opening: adj. proportio , of or belonging to proportion , proportional (post-class.): termini, Front. Colon. p. 111 . —Hence, , adv. , proportionally , Cassiod. Geom. 6 .

prōportĭōnātus.opening: adj. proportio , proportioned , proportionate (postclass.): corpus, Firm. Math. 4, 13.

prōpŏsĭtĭo.opening: propono . A setting forth or proposing , a representation. (Mental; class.) Vitae, Cic. Tusc. 3, 18, 39 : rerum magnarum cum animi amplā quādam propositione cogitatio, Cic. Inv. 2, 54, 163 .— (In words.) Sunt quaedam…

prōpŏsĭtor.opening: id. , a proposer (eccl. Lat.), Aug. Duab. Anim. 8, 10 .

prō-praefectus.opening: a vice-prefect , Inscr. Murat. p. 17 , n. 7.

prō-praetor.opening: (also or , ), a magistrate in the times of the republic , who , after having administered the prœtorship one year in Rome , was sent in the following year as prœtor to a province where there was no army , a proprœtor…

proprĭĕtārĭus.opening: proprietas , an owner , proprietor (post-class.), Dig. 7, 1, 15 et saep.—As adj. : proprietaria res, belonging to one as his property, proprietary, Paul. Sent. 5, 7, 3 .

prō^prĭĕtas.opening: proprius . Lit. , a property , peculiarity , peculiar nature , quality of a thing (class.): singularum rerum singulae proprietates, Cic. Ac. 2, 18 : terrae caelique, Liv. 38, 17 : definitio genere declaratur, et…

prōprĭĭfĭco.opening: v. a. proprius-facio , to appropriate , make one's own (eccl. Lat.), Rustic. c. Aceph. p. 1245.

proprĭo.opening: (archaic form, propriassit, proprium fecerit, Paul. ex Fest. p. 229 Müll.), v. a. id. , to appropriate (ante- and post-class.), Cael. Aur. Tard. 5, 11 ; id. Acut. 1, 15 fin.

proprītim.opening: adv. for propriatim from proprio , properly , Lucr. 2, 975 .

prō^prĭus.opening: adj. etym. dub.; perhaps from root prae; cf. prope , not common with others , one's own , special , particular , proper (class.; cf.: peculiaris, privatus). In gen., opp. communis: nam virtutem propriam mortalibus…

propter.opening: adv. and prep. contr. for propiter, from prope; cf.: inter, subter . Adv. , near , hard by , at hand (syn.: prope, juxta; rare but class.). serito in loco, ubi aqua propter siet, Cato, R. R. 151, 2 : ibi angiportum…

proptĕrĕā.opening: adv. propter-is , therefore , for that cause , on that account (syn.: ideo, idcirco, inde; class.): quia mihi natalis est dies, propterea te vocari ad cenam volo, Plaut. Capt. 1, 2, 71 : propterea ... quia, Cic. Div 1,…

prōpŭdĭānus.opening: adj. propudium , offered on account of infamous deeds : propudianus porcus dictus est, ut ait Capito Atteius, qui in sacrificio gentis Claudiae velut piamentum et exsolutio omnis contractae religionis est, Fest. p. 238…

prō^pŭdĭōsus.opening: adj. id. , shameful , disgraceful , infamous (ante- and postclass.), Plaut. Stich. 2, 2, 10 : uxor, Gell. 2, 7, 20 : ancilla propudiosissima, Sid. Ep. 9, 6 : facinus, Arn. 5, 175 : concubitus, id. 4, 149 : meretrices,…

prō^pŭdĭum.opening: , a dub. reading: moraris tanquam propudium ignores, Petr. 99 ; perh. a signal to set sail (Bücheler), or a vulgar form for propediem.

prōpugnācŭlum.opening: propugno , a bulwark , tower , rampart , fortress , defence (class.). Lit. : pontes et propugnacula jungunt, Verg. A. 9, 170 ; Cic. Verr. 2, 5, 34, § 88 : Siciliae, i. e. the fleet, id. ib. 2, 3, 80 , § 186: solidati…

prōpugnātĭo.opening: id. . A fighting for , defence of a place (post-class.), Val. Max. 5, 1, 4 ect. — A defence , vindication (class.): with the gen. or pro : propugnatio ac defensio dignitatis tuae, Cic. Fam. 1, 7, 2 : propugnatio pro…

prō-pugnātor.opening: propugno , one who fights in defence of a place, a defender , soldier (class.). Lit. : classis inops propter dimissionem propugnatorum, of the marines, Cic. Verr. 2, 5, 33, § 86 : a propugnatoribus relictus locus, Caes.…

prōpugnātrix.opening: propugnator , she that defends , a protectress : PROPVGNATRIX MEORVM PERICVLORVM, Inscr. Marin. Iscriz. Alb. p. 136.

prō-pugno.grammar: āvi, ātum, 1 v. n. and a.
prō-pugno.opening: v. n. and a. To rush out to fight , go forth to fight , to make sallies or sorties : ipsi ex silvis rari propugnabant, Caes. B. G. 5, 9 ; cf. id. ib. 2 . 7; id. B. C. 2, 8 .— To fight or contend for , to defend a thing…

prōpulsātĭo.opening: propulso , a driving back , a keeping or warding off , a repelling , repulse (rare but class.): periculi, Cic. Sull. 1, 2 : criminis, Tiro ap. Gell. 7, 3, 15 .

prōpulsātor.opening: id. , one that drives back , a warder off , averter (postclass.): propulsatorem odio insecutus, Val. Max. 7, 8, 7 : valetudinum pessimarum, Arn. 7, p. 249 .

prōpulso.opening: v. freq. a. propello , to drive back , keep or ward off , to repel , repulse (class.). Lit. : lupos, Varr. R. R. 2, 9 : hostem, Caes. B. G. 1, 49 : populum ab ingressione fori, Cic. Phil. 5, 4, 9 : et aquas hiemis et…

prōpulsor.opening: id. , one that wards off or drives back (post-class.): cornigeri pecudis, Venant. Vit. S. Mart. 3, 301 .

prōpulsus.opening: (only in abl. sing. ), propello , a driving on or forth , propulsion , impulse (post-Aug.): ventum propulsu suo concitare, Sen. Q. N. 5, 14, 3 .

prō-pungo.opening: v. a. , to prick , puncture in front (post-class.): tum partium propungentibus pilis capitis, Cael. Aur. Tard. 1, 1 dub. (al. tum praerasis prominentibus pilis, capiti).

prō-purgo.opening: v. a. , to cleanse beforehand , Not. Tir. p. 120 ; Vulg. Ecclus. 7, 33 .

prŏpўlaeum.opening: ( ), or , , , = προπύλαιον , a gateway , entrance; esp. (in plur. ) of the celebrated entrance to the temple of Pallas in the citadel of Athens, the Propylœum : Phalereus Demetrius Periclem vituperat, quod tantam…

prō-quaestōre.opening: a magistrate , who , after administering the quœstorship at Rome , was associated with a proconsul in the administration of a province , a proquœstor : qui et legatus et pro quaestore fuisset, Cic. Verr. 1, 4, 11 : cum…

prō-quĭrīto.opening: , no perf. , , v. a. , to cry out or exclaim in public , to publish , proclaim (post-class.): epistulam saepe aperiens proquiritabat, App. Mag. p. 326, 8 : lex proquiritata, Sid. Ep. 8, 6 : hoc opusculum, Claud. Mam.…

prōra.opening: (collat. form ; acc. prorim, Att. ap. Non. 200, 33 , or Trag. 575), , = πρώρα . The forepart of a ship , the prow (opp. puppis, the stern; class.): astitit prorae, Plaut. Merc. 1, 2, 65 ; Lucr. 2, 554 : prorae admodum…

prō-rēpo.opening: v. n. , to creep forth , crawl out , come out in a gradual or unobserved manner ( poet. and in post-Aug. prose). Lit. : (formica) non usquam prorepit, Hor. S. 1, 1, 37 : cum prorepserunt primis animalia terris, id. ib.…

prōrēta.opening: , = πρωράτης , the lookout man at the prow , the under-pilot (anteand post-class.): si tu proreta isti navi es, ego gubernator ero, Plaut. Rud. 4, 3, 75 ; Dig. 39, 4, 11 .

prōreus.opening: ( ), , , = πρωρεύς , the lookout man at the prow , under-pilot ( poet. ), Ov. M. 3, 634 .

prōrĭga.opening: prob. pro-rego , a stable-boy , an attendant employed in breeding horses , Plin. 8, 42, 64, § 156 ; Varr. R. R. 2, 7, 9 .

prō-rĭpĭo.opening: v. a. To drag or snatch forth (class.). Lit. : hominem proripi jubet, Cic. Verr. 2, 5, 62, § 161 : nudos pedes, i. e. spring forth, Ov. Am. 3, 7, 82 .—With se , to rush out , to hasten or hurry forth or away : quo illum…

prō-rīto.opening: v. a. like ir-rito, āre; cf. also ira . To provoke , cause , or produce by irritation (post - Aug.), Plin. 26, 8, 58, § 90 .— Transf. , to incite , entice , allure , tempt (post-Aug.): nisi pretium proritat, Col. 2, 10,…

prōrŏgātĭo.opening: prorogo . A prolonging , extension of a term of office: prorogatio imperii, a prolongation of one's command, Liv. 8, 26 fin. — A putting off , deferring of an appointed time: diei, Cic. Att. 13, 43 (in Cic. Mur. 23, 47…

prōrŏgātīvus.opening: adj. id. , admitting of delay , prorogative (post-Aug.): prorogativa fulmina sunt, quorum minae differri possunt, Sen. Q. N. 2, 47 fin.

prōrŏgātor.opening: id. , one that pays or gives out , a dispenser (post-class.): tritici, vini, et olei, Cassiod. Var. 10, 28 .

prō-rŏgo.opening: v. a. To prolong , continue , extend , protract (class.; syn.: propago, produco): ne quinquennii imperium Caesari prorogaretur, should not be prolonged, Cic. Phil. 2, 10, 24 : provinciam, id. Att. 5, 11, 1 ; 5, 2, 1 :…

Prorsa.opening: ( ), , 2. prorsus , sc. dea, i. e. the goddess presiding over births with the head foremost (opp. Postverta), Varr. ap. Gell. 16, 16, 4 ; cf. Hartung, Relig. d. Röm. 2, p. 199.

prorsum.opening: (collat. form , like prosus=prorsus, Plaut. Trin. 5, 2, 6 Ritschl), adv. pro-versum . Forwards ( poet. ): neque prorsum iniit, Plaut. Cist. 4, 2, 32 : cursari rursum prorsum, to and fro, Ter. Hec. 3, 1, 35 .— Straight…

prorsus.opening: (collat. form ; v. II.), , adj. for pro-versus . Straightforwards , right onwards , straight , direct (post-Aug.): prorso tramite siste gradus (al. proso), Avien. 3 : prorsi limites appellantur in agrorum mensuris, qui…

prō-rumpo.grammar: rūpi, ruptum, 3 v. a. and n.
prō-rumpo.opening: v. a. and n. Act. , to thrust or cast forth , to cause to break , burst , or rush forth , to send forth : (Aetna) atram prorumpit ad aethera nubem, Verg. A. 3, 572 : proruptus pons, broken down, Tac. H. 1, 86 (al.…

prō-rŭo.grammar: rŭi, rŭtum, 3 v. a. and n.
prō-rŭo.opening: v. a. and n. Act. , to cast or tear down in front , to pull down , throw down , hurl to the ground , overthrow , overturn , demolish (class.): his (munitionibus) prorutis, Caes. B. G. 3, 26 : vallo proruto, jam in…

prō-ruptĭo.opening: prorumpo , a breaking or rushing forth , an eruption (post-class.): hostium, a sally, sortie, Aur. Vict. Caes. 33 : undarum, Mart. Cap. 6, § 624 .— Absol. , Mart. Cap. 8, § 804 .

prōruptor.opening: id. , one that breaks forth , sallies out from a besieged place (post-class.), Amm. 24, 5 .

prōsăĭcus.opening: adj. 1. prosa . Prosaic , in prose (post-class.): prosaico relatu, Ven. Carm. 7, 11, 1; id. Vit. S. Mart. 1, 13 .— Subst. : , , , a prose writer , prosaist (post-class.), Ven. Vit. S. Mart. 2, 469 .

prōsāpĭa.opening: (collat. form , ēi or ēs), pro and root sa.; cf. sero, satus , a stock , race , family (archaic; v. Quint. 1, 6, 40 ; 8, 3, 26 ; cf.: stirps, genus, progenies, posteritas): prosapia progenies: id est porro sparsis et…

prŏsăpŏdŏsis.opening: a figure of speech , defined by Mart. Cap. § 533 Kopp (al. proapodosis, q. v.).

prōsārĭus.opening: adj. 1. prosa , of or belonging to prose , prosaic (post-class.): opus, Sid. Ep. 3, 14 : loquendi genus, id. ib. 9, 13 .

prōsător.opening: pro-sero , an ancestor (eccl. Lat.), Jul. ap. Aug. c. Sec. Resp. Jul. 1, 90.

proscaenĭum.opening: ( ), , ,= προσκήνιον . The place before the scene where the actors appeared , the proscenium; also, in gen., the stage , Plaut. Am. prol. 91 ; id. Truc. prol. 10 , id. Poen. prol. 17 : veteres ineunt proscaenia ludi,…

proschŏlus.opening: , = πρόσχολος , an under-teacher , under-master (post-class.): tam pauper, ut proscholus esset grammatici, Aug. Serm. Apostol. Serm. 178 , n. 8; Aus. Prof. 22 in lemm.

prō-scindo.opening: v. a. , to tear open in front , to rend , split , cleave , cut up , cut in pieces ( poet. and in post-Aug. prose). Lit. In gen.: ferro proscindere quercum, Luc. 3, 434 : piscem, App. Mag. p. 300, 18 and 20: spumanti…

prōscissĭo.opening: proscindo, I. B. . In agriculture, the first ploughing , a breaking up , Col. 2, 13, 6 ; 6, 2, 8 .

prō-scrībo.opening: v. a. , to write before or in front of , to write over or upon , to inscribe. In gen. (post-Aug.): vultus voluntariā poenarum lege proscripti, written over, inscribed, Petr. 107 .— In partic. To publish any thing by…

prōscriptĭo.opening: proscribo (class.). A written public notice of sale. an advertisement : proscriptio bonorum, Cic. Quint. 18, 56 : quam ad diem proscriptiones venditionesque fiant, id. Rosc. Am. 44, 128 : bonorum, id. Cat. 2, 10, 21 :…

prō-scriptor.opening: id. , one who proscribes or oullaws; adj. , proscriptive (post-Aug.): proscriptor animus, Plin. 7, 12, 10, § 56 ; cf. proscripturio.

prōscriptūra.opening: id. , proscription , outlawry , Not. Tir. p. 11 .

prōscriptŭrĭo.opening: v. desider. n [id], to desire or long to proscribe , (a word formed sarcastically by Cic.): ita sullaturit animus ejus et proscripturit diu, Cic. Att. 9, 10, 6 (cited Quint. 8, 6, 32 ).

prō-sĕco.opening: (old inf. pass. parag. prosecarier, Plaut. Poen. 2, 1, 8 ), , v. a. , to cut off from before , cut away or off. In gen. (post-class.): prosectis naso prius ac mox auribus, App. M. 2, p. 128, 11 .— In partic. In…

prō-sĕcro.opening: v. n. sacro , to sacrifice (eccl. Lat.): daemonibus, Lact. 4, 275 : Aesculapio gallum, id. 3, 20, 16 ; id. Epit. 23, 3 ; 37, 5 .

prōsectĭo.opening: proseco , a cutting off , amputation (post-class.): ferri prosectio, Salv. Gub. D. 6, 16 .

prōsector.opening: id. , one who cuts in pieces , a cutter up , an anatomist (eccl. Lat.), Tert. Anim. 25 .

prōsectus.opening: proseco , a cutting or slashing , a cut , stroke (Appul.): prosectu gladiorum, App. M. 8, p. 214, 32 : dentium, a bite, id. ib. 8 , p. 203, 20.

prōsĕcūtĭo.opening: prosequor . Lit. , a following or accompanying on the way , attendance (post-class.): necessitas prosecutionis, Cod. Th. 8, 5, 47: prosecutio opportuna, Symm. Ep. 7, 59 .— Trop. A following with words , an honorable…

prōsĕcūtor.opening: ( ), , id. , an accompanier , companion , an attendant (post-class.), Dig. 48, 3, 7 ; Cod. Th. 8, 5, 47; 10, 72, 1; 12, 6, 12 et saep.: caterva prosecutorum, Sid. Ep. 4, 8 .

prōsĕcūtōrĭa.opening: (sc. epistula) [prosecutor], a letter relating to taking something in charge , a letter of authorization (post-class.), Cod. Just. 10, 72, 1 .

prō-sĕda.opening: sedeo (she who sits in public), a common prostitute (perh. only Plaut.), Plaut. Poen. 1, 2, 53 ; cf.: prosedas meretrices Plautus appellat, quod ante stabula sedeant. Eaedem et prostibulae, Paul. ex Fest. p. 226 Müll.

prosedămum.opening: Sarmatian , = pigritia equorum in coitu, Plin. 26, 10, 63, § 98 .

Prŏsĕlēnus.opening: , = Προσέληνος , older than the moon , a name by which the Arcadians called themselves, Cic. Fragm. Or. pro Fund. 3 B. and K. ( Serv. Verg. G. 2, 342 ).

prŏsēlўtus.opening: , = προσήλυτος , come from abroad , foreign , strange (late Lat.): numeravit Salomon omnes viros proselytos, Vulg. 2 Par. 2, 17 .—Hence, as subst. , , , A sojourner , a stranger in the land: proselyti et advenae, Vulg.…

prō-sēmĭnātor.opening: prosemino , a sower; trop., a disseminator (eccl. Lat.), Tert. ad Nat. 2, 13 .

prō-sēmĭno.opening: v. a. , to sow or scatter about , to sow (rare but class.). Lit. : ostreas, Cic. Fragm. ap. Non. 216, 13 : tamquam ex draconis alicujus dentibus proseminati, Lact. 6, 10, 19 .— Trop. , to disseminate , propagate :…

prō-sentĭo.opening: v. a. , to perceive beforehand , Plaut. Mil. 4, 4, 16 .

prōsĕquĭum.opening: prosequor , attendance : prosequium a prosequendo, Paul. ex Fest. p. 226 Müll.

prō-sĕquor.opening: (quūtus), 3, v. dep. a. , to follow (in a friendly or hostile manner), to accompany , attend; to follow after , pursue (class.; cf.: comitor, stipo). Lit. : novum maritum volo rus prosequi, Plaut. Cas. 4, 2, 3 : eum…

prō-sĕro.opening: v. a. , to stretch forth , extend (post-class.): aggeribus caput Alpinis proserit in Celtas (Rhodanus), Sil. 3, 447 : proserit hydra caput, Avien. Arat. 1111 : se, id. Perieg. 711, 342 .

Prō^serpĭna.opening: , = Περσεφόνη . Proserpine , daughter of Ceres and Jupiter , and wife of Pluto , who seized her as she was gathering flowers in Sicily , and carried her away to the infernal regions : Cereris Proserpina puer, Naev. 2,…

prōserpĭnāca.opening: a plant , also called polygonon, Plin. 26, 4, 11, § 23 ; 27, 12, 104, § 127 ; App. Herb. 18 .

prōserpĭnālis.opening: adj. , of or belonging to Proserpine : herba, the herb dragonwort, Marc. Emp. 10 .

prō-serpo.opening: v. n. , to creep forwards or forth , to creep or crawl along (ante- and post-class.). Lit. : proserpens bestia, Plaut. Poen. 5, 2, 74 ; cf. id. As. 3, 3, 105 ; id. Pers. 4, 28 ; Varr. L. L. 5, § 68 Müll.: servulus…

prŏseucha.opening: , = προσευχή , a place for prayer , an oratory , Juv. 3, 296 ; Inscr. Grut. 651, 11 .

prōsĭcĭes.opening: proseco, II. B. , the flesh cut off for sacrifice (ante-class. for prosectum): prosiciem extorum in mensam porricere, Varr. ap. Non. 220, 23 .— Collat. form: prosicium, quod prosecatum proicitur, Paul. ex Fest. p. 225…

pro-sĭdens.opening: Part. [sedeo], sitting before , Inscr. Fabr. p. 367 , n. 127.

prō-sĭlĭo.opening: (less freq. īvi or ĭi; īvi, Sen. Ep. 115, 15 ; Just. 11, 5, 10 ; Hyg. Fab. 103 ; ii, Sen. Clem. 1, 3, 3 ; Petr. 106, 1 ), 4 ( fut. prosilibo for prosiliam, Auct. Quint. Decl. 4, 19 ), v. n. salio , to leap or spring…
