prō-sistens.opening: Part. [sisto], standing out , projecting : foliis in modum radiorum prosistentibus, App. M. 11, p. 269, 17 .

proslambănŏmĕnos.opening: ,= προσλαμβανόμενος (taken in addition), the note A in music , Vitr. 5, 4, 5 .

prō-sŏcer.opening: a wife's grandfather : cuique senex Nereus prosocer esse velit, Ov. H. 3, 74 : uxor, et nurus, et pronurus, viro, et socero, et prosocero furtum facere possunt, Dig. 25, 2, 15 : erum cum prosocero meo, Plin. Ep. 5, 14…

prō-sō^crus.opening: a wife's grandmother : prosocrus mihi uxoris meae avia est: ego illius sum progener, Dig. 38, 10, 4, § 6 .

prŏsōdĭa.opening: ,= προσῳδία , the tone or accent of a syllable (ante-class.), Varr. ap. Gell. 18, 12, 8 : accentus quas Graeci προσῳδίας vocant, Quint. 1, 5, 22 .

prŏsōdĭăcus.opening: adj. ,= προσῳδιακός , prosodial , prosodiac (post-class.): metrum, Mar. Vict. p. 2580 P.: numeri, Mart. Cap. 9, § 991 .

prŏsōpis.opening: , and , ,= προσωπίς and προσωπίτης , a plant (pure Lat. personacia), App. Herb. 36 .

Prŏsōpītes.opening: a district of the Delta in Egypt , Plin. 5, 9, 9, § 49 .

prŏsōpon.opening: ,= πρόσωπον , a kind of herb , wild-poppy , App. Herb. 53 .

prŏsōpŏpoeĭa.opening: ,= προσωποποιΐα . Personification , Quint. 6, 1, 25 ; 1, 8, 3 ; 4, 1, 69 ; 11, 1, 41; Isid. 2, 13, 1 ; 2, 21, 45 .— A dramatizing : ad prosopopoeias irrumpunt, Quint. 2, 1, 2 ; 3, 8, 49 .

prŏsōpŏpoeĭcus.opening: adj. prosopopoeia , of or belonging to personification , personifying (post-class.): sermo, Firm. Error. Prof. Relig. 8.

prospectīvus.opening: adj. 2. prospectus , of or belonging to a prospect , furnishing a prospect , prospective (post-class.): fenestrae, Cod. Just. 8, 10, 12 .

prospecto.opening: v. freq. a. prospicio , to look forth upon , look out; to look at , view , behold , see afar off , gaze upon : mare, Cic. Att. 9, 10, 2 . Lit. : pars ex tectis fenestrisque prospectant, Liv. 24, 21 ; cf. Verg. A. 7, 813…

prospector.opening: id. . Lit. , one who looks out : sicut prospector videns casum proximi sui, Vulg. Ecclus. 11, 32 .— Trop. , one that foresees , one that arranges beforehand , a provider (post-class.): deus prospector humanarum…

prospectus.opening: prospicio . Lit. , a lookout , distant view , prospect (class.): sterilis prospectus, Plaut. Mil. 3, 1, 15 : cum saepibus prospectus impediretur, Caes. B. G. 2, 22 ; cf. Sall. J. 53, 1 : non prospectu modo extra vallum…

pro-spĕcŭlor.opening: v. n. and a. Neutr. , to look into the distance , look out (very rare): de vallo, Auct. B. Afr. 31.— Transf. , to explore : L. Siccium prospeculatum ad locum castris capiendum mittunt, Liv. 3, 43, 2 .—* Act. , to look…

prosper.opening: , and more freq. , a. , adj. pro-spero, answering to hope; cf. spes , agreeable to one's wishes , favorable , fortunate , prosperous (freq. and class.; cf.: faustus, propitius): sperem veteres pro spem dixerunt, unde et…

pro-spergo.opening: , no perf. , , v. a. spargo , to besprinkle : haustā aquā templum prospersum est, Tac. A. 15, 44 .

prospĕrĭtas.opening: prosper , desirable condition , good fortune , success , prosperity (rare but good prose): vitae, Cic. N. D. 3, 36, 86 : honestarum rerum, id. Fragm. ap. Amm. 21, 16, 13 : tantā prosperitate usus est valetudinis, ut,…

prospĕro.opening: v. a. prosper . To cause a thing to succeed , to render fortunate or happy , to prosper (syn. secundo; not in Cic.): vos precor, uti populo Romano Quiritium vim victoriamque prosperetis, an old form of prayer in Liv. 8,…

prōspex.opening: prospicio , one foreseeing , a foreseer (post-class.), Tert. Test. Anim. 5 .

prospĭca.opening: id. , she that takes care or provides beforehand , Naev. ap. Non. p. 155, 24 ; cf. Lachm. ad Lucr. 5, 679 .

prōspĭcĭentĭa.opening: prospicio . Foresight , forethought , precaution : vigilia et prospicientia, Cic. Phil. 7, 7, 19 ; Ambros. Off. 1, 21 : Creatoris, id. Hexaëm. 3, 9.—* A view; hence, an appearance , shape , form , Tert. adv. Val. 26 .

prō-spĭcĭo.grammar: exi, ectum, 3 v. n. and a.
prō-spĭcĭo.opening: v. n. and a. [specio]. Neutr. , to look forward or into the distance , to look out , to look , see (class.). In gen.: neque post respiciens, neque ante prospiciens, Varr. ap. Non. 443, 2 : parum prospiciunt oculi, do…

prōspĭcus.opening: adj. prospicio , taking care : hac sibi prospicā, hac despicā, Naev. ap. Non. 155, 25 (Com. Rel. p. 8 Rib.).

prōspĭcŭus.opening: adj. id. . * That may be seen afar off , conspicuous : turris, Stat. Th. 12, 15 .— Looking forward , looking into the future : turris illa prospicua vaticinationis munus explicuit, App. M. 6, p. 181, 20 .— Adv. : ,…

prō-spīro.opening: v. n. , to breathe forth , exhale , App. Mag. p. 306, 12 .

prō-sterno.opening: v. a. , to strew in front of , to strew before one; also, to throw to the ground , throw down , overthrow , prostrate (syn.: fundo, profligo, provolvo). Lit. : eo prosternebant folia farferi, Plaut. Poen. 2, 31 (al.…

prosthĕsis.opening: , = πρόσθεσις , and , , , = πρόθεσις , a grammatical figure consisting in the prefixing of a letter or syllable to a word , prosthesis; as gnatus for natus, tetuli for tuli, Charis. 4 ; Diom. 2 .

prōstĭbĭlis.opening: prosto , a harlot , prostitute , Plaut. Pers. 5, 2, 56 .

prōstĭbŭla.opening: id. , a prostitute , Plaut. ap. Non. 423, 18 ; Tert. Apol. 6 .

prōstĭbŭlum.opening: id. . A prostitute , Plaut. Aul. 2, 4, 6 ; Vulg. Lev. 21, 7 .— Transf. , a male who prostitutes himself , Arn. 6, 199 .— A brothel , Isid. Orig. 18, 42, 2 ; Vulg. Ezech. 16, 24 ; also, in transf. signif., id. Joel, 3, 3.

prō-stĭtŭo.opening: v. a. statuo . To place before or in front , Arn. 5, 177 . — To expose publicly to prostitution , to prostitute : cras populo prostituam vos, Plaut. Ps. 1, 2, 45 ; Sen. Contr. 1, 2 : quae (meretrix) sese toto corpore…

prōstĭtūtĭo.opening: prostituo . Prostitution , Arn. 2, 53 ; Tert. Pudic. 6 ; Aug. in Psa. 128, 6 .— Plur. : mulierum, Lact. 5, 8, 7 .— In gen., a dishonoring , profaning : imaginum, Tert. Apol. 27 .

prōstĭtūtor.opening: id. . A prostitutor , pander , Tert. Cult. Fem. 9 .— In gen., one who dishonors , a violator : Christiani sacramenti, Tert. Pudic. 10 ; id. Cult. Fem. 2, 10 .

prōstĭtūtus.opening: Part. and P. a. , from prostituo.

prō-sto.opening: v. n. * To stand forth , stand out , project : angellis prostantibus, Lucr. 2, 428 .— To stand in a public place. Of a seller, to offer one's wares for sale , carry on one's business (cf. propono): hi (lenones) saltem…

prostŏmis.opening: , = προστομίς , an instrument to hold a horse by the nose , a barnacle , twitch , beak; trop., a drinkingvessel , Lucil. ap. Non. 1 , n. 84 (others read postomis, q. v.).

prostrātĭo.opening: prosterno , an overthrowing , subverting , prostration (postclass.): disciplinae, Tert. Praescr. 41 .

prōstrātor.opening: id. , an overthrower , prostrator (late Lat.): hostium, Jul. Firm. Err. Prof. Relig. 21 fin.

prostȳlos.opening: adj. , = πρόστυλος , having pillars in front : aedes, Vitr. 3, 1 ; 7 praef. fin.

prostўpum.opening: , = πρόστυπον , a pattern , model , Plin. 35, 12, 43, § 152 ; v. Sillig N. cr.

prō-sŭbĭgo.opening: v. a. * To dig up , cast up : terram, Verg. G. 3, 256 .—* To fashion beforehand , prepare : fulmina Cyclops Prosubigit, Val. Fl. 4, 288 .—* To tear down , trample on : molam pede, Prud. στεφ . 3, 130.

prō-sum.opening: v. n. , to be useful or of use , to do good , benefit , profit. In gen., constr. with dat. , a subjectclause , or absol. , rarely with ad or in and acc. : sibi prodesse, Enn. ap. Cic. Fam. 7, 6, 2 (Trag. v. 310 Vahl.);…

prōsūmĭa.opening: a small kind of vessel for reconnoitring , a spy - boat , Caecil. ap. Non. 536, 11 sq. (Com. Rel. pp. 29 and 45 Rib.); cf.: prosumia genus navigii speculatorium parvum, Paul. ex Fest. p. 226 Müll.

Prosumnus.opening: the name of a lewd favorite of Bacchus , who showed the latter the way to the infernal regions , Arn. 5, 176 .

pro-sūmo.opening: , a false read. for praesumpserit, Plaut. Trin. 5, 2, 6 ; v. Ritschl ad h. l.

prosurgo.opening: v. n. , to rise up (late Lat.), Fulg. Serm. 11 .

Prŏsymna.opening: , or , , , = Προσυμνα , a country or town of Argolis , Stat. Th. 1, 383 ; 3, 325 .

prōtăgĭon.opening: a good kind of wine , Plin. 14, 7, 9, § 76 .

pulvillus.opening: dim. contr. from pulvinulus, from pulvinus , a little cushion , small pillow , Hor. Epod. 8, 16 ; Front. Ep. ad Ver. 1 Mai; App. M. 10, p. 248, 25 .

pulvīnar.opening: ( ), , pulvinus , a couch made of cushions , and spread over with a splendid covering , for the gods and persons who received divine honors; a couch or cushioned seat of the gods (in the lectisternium, placed for the…

pulvīnāris.opening: adj. id. , of or belonging to a cushion or pillow : pica, sitting on a cushion, Petr. 37 .

pulvīnārĭum.opening: * A cushioned seat or couch of the gods (for the usual pulvinar), Liv. 21, 62 .—* An anchorage , Plaut. Cas. 3, 2, 27 .

pulvīnārĭus.opening: adj. pulvinar , of or belonging to the couches of the gods : macellum pingue pulvinarium, i. e. provision of beasts for sacrifice , Prud. στεφ 10, 1056 (yet pulvinarium is perh. gen. plur. of pulvinar).

pulvīnātus.opening: adj. pulvinus , cushion-shaped , having a swelling or elevation , swelling , elevated : pulvinatus calyx (juglandis), Plin. 15, 22, 24, § 86 : fissura (seminis palmae), id. 13, 4, 7, § 32 : labrum scrobis, id. 17, 22,…

pulvīnŭlus.opening: dim. pulvinus , a little bank or bed of earth , Col. Arb. 10, 4 .

pulvīnus.opening: , prop. an elevation. A cushion , bolster , squab , pillow to sit or lie upon: mane pulvinum, Plaut. Stich. 1, 2, 38 : Crassum pulvinus poposcisse, Cic. de Or. 1, 7, 29 ; Cic. Verr. 2, 5, 11, § 27 ; id. Fam. 9, 18, 4 :…

pulviscŭlus.opening: ( neutr. collat. form , , Vigilant. ap. Hier. adv. Vigil. 4 ), dim. pulvis . Lit. , small dust , fine powder (ante- and post-class.), Sol. 15 fin. ; App. M. 9, p. 222, 23 ; id. Mag. p. 277, 7 : si abaco et pulvisculo te…

pūmex.opening: ( fem. , Cat. 1, 2 ). Lit. , a pumice-stone , Plin. 36, 21, 42, § 154 ; used for smoothing books, Cat. 1, 2 ; 22, 6 ; Hor. Ep. 1, 20, 2 ; Ov. Tr. 1, 1, 11 ; Mart. 8, 72, 2 ; hence poet. , of verses carefully smoothed,…

pūmĭcātus.opening: Part. and P. a. , from pumico.

pūmĭcĕus.opening: adj. pumex , of pumice-stone , or of soft stone; in gen. (very rare): molae, Ov. F. 6, 318 : sedes, Sil. 7, 419 : antra, Stat. S. 3, 1, 144 ; cf. fontes, flowing from pumice-stone, Mart. 4, 57, 2 . — Trop. : oculi, not…

pūmĭlĭo.opening: (collat. form , Stat. S. 1, 6, 57 ), , pumilus , a dwarf , pigmy : necari a non armato pumilione, Mart. 1, 43, 10 : scutum pumilionis erit, id. 14, 213, 2 .—Of women: parvula, pumilio (est) Χαρίτων μία , tota merum sal,…

pŭtātōrĭus.opening: adj. putator , of or for pruning or lopping (post-class.): falx, a pruning-knife, Pall. 1, 43 .

pŭtĕal.opening: (collat. form † , Inscr. Ann. 16, p. Chr. n. ap. Orell. 4517), , puteus . A stone curb round the mouth of a well : puteal, περιστόμιον φρέατος , Gloss. Philox.: putealia sigillata duo, Cic. Att. 1, 10, 3 ; Dig. 19, 1,…

pŭtĕālis.opening: adj. id. , of or belonging to a well , well- : undae, well-water, Ov. Ib. 391 ; so, lymphae, Lucr. 6, 1178 : aquae, Dig. 43, 1, 20, § 6 : fons, Col. 11, 3, 8 : unda, id. 1, 5, 1 : pocula, of spring-water, Juvenc. 2, 259…

pŭtĕānus.opening: adj. id. , of or belonging to a well , well- : aqua, well-water, Col. 12, 26, 1 ; Plin. 14, 9, 11, § 82 .

pūtĕo.opening: (no perf. or sup. ), , v. n. Sanscr. root pu-, to stink; cf. pus; Gr. πῦον . To stink (cf. putesco), Cic. Fragm. ap. Non. 545, 16 : putet aper, Hor. S. 2, 2, 42 : putere diurno mero, id. Ep. 1, 19, 11 ; Pers. 3, 73 .—…

pūtesco.opening: and , , v. inch. n. [puteo], to rot , putrefy , Cato, R. R. 3, 4 : quod si minus idoneae tempestates sint consecutae, putescere semina soleant, Varr. R. R. 1, 34, 1 ; Cic. Fin. 5, 13, 38 ; id. N. D. 2, 64, 160 ; id.…

pŭtĕus.opening: ( neutr. collat. form of the plur. , , Varr. ap. Non. 217, 4 ) [root pu-, to cleanse; whence also purus, putus, purgo], a well : puteum fodere, Plaut. Most. 2, 1, 32 : ex puteis jugibus aquam calidam trahi, Cic. N. D.…

pūtĭdĭuscŭlus.opening: adj. dim. [putidior], somewhat more disgusting; of discourse, rather more tedious or troublesome , Cic. Fam. 7, 5, 3 .

pūtĭdŭlus.opening: adj. dim. [putidus], disgusting in behavior or speech; offensive , affected (post-Aug.), Mart. 4, 20, 4 ; Capitol. Macr. 14 .

pūtĭdus.opening: adj. puteo , rotten , decaying , stinking , fetid (syn. foetidus). Lit. : caro, Cic. Pis. 9, 19 : aper, Mart. 3, 50, 8 : fungus, Plaut. Bacch. 4, 7, 23 : frons, Cato ap. Plin. 17, 9, 6, § 55 : uvae, Varr. ap. Non. 152,…

pŭtillus.opening: , or , , dim. 2. putus , a little boy; a little girl; a child; a word of endearment Plaut. As. 3, 3, 104 .

pŭto.opening: v. a. root pu, to cleanse; whence putus, puteus, purus, etc. , to clean , cleanse (in the lit. sense very rare; in the trop. very freq.). Lit. In gen.: vellus lavare ac putare, Varr. R. R. 2, 2, 18 : pensa lana putata,…

pūtor.opening: puteo , a foul smell , a stench , rottenness , putridity (ante- and postclass.), Cato, R. R. 157 ; Varr. L. L. 5, § 25 Müll.; Lucr. 2, 872 ; 6, 1101 ; Stat. S. 4, 3, 86 ; Arn. 7, 222 al. ; App. M. 4, p. 144, 4 .

pū^trāmen.opening: puter , rottenness , putridity (late Lat.), Cypr. Laps. 12 .

pū^trēdŭlus.opening: ( ), , adj. putredo , corrupt , foul (late Lat.): voces, Amm. 22, 16, 16 .

pū^trĕfăcĭo.opening: v. a. , and in pass. , (collat. form of the part. pass. putefactus, Prud. στεφ . 10, 1035) [putreo-facio]. To make rotten , to cause to putrefy; and pass. , to become rotten , to putrefy : umor putrefacit deposita…

pū^trĭbĭlis.opening: adj. id. , corruptible , perishable (post-class.): tabulae, Paul. Nol. Ep. 8, 6 : ligna, Aug. Civ. Dei , 21, 7.

pū^trĭdus.opening: adj. putreo . Rotten , corrupt , decayed : dentes, Cic. Pis. 1, 1 : nimis jam putrida membra, Luc. 2, 141 : si quid in nucleo putridi fuerit, Plin. 23, 4, 45, § 88 : cadaver, Vulg. Isa. 14, 19 .— Withered : pectora,…

pŭtus.opening: , another form of pusus, a boy , Verg. Cat. 9, 2 Wagn.

pycnītis.opening: , = πυκνῖτις , a plant , mullein , wool-blade (pure Lat. verbascum), App. Herb. 71 .

pycnŏcŏmon.opening: , = πυκνόκομον , a plant , devil's-bit : Scabiosa succisa, Linn.; or, acc. to Sprengel, small-flowered motherwort : Leonurus Marrubiastrum, Linn.; Plin. 26, 8, 36, § 57 .

pycta.opening: or , , , = πύκτης . Lit. , a boxer , pugilist (pure Lat. pugil), Plin. 7, 47, 48, § 152 ; Sen. Contr. 1, 3 ; Phaedr. 4, 24, 5 ; Tert. Anim. 46 ; id. adv. Gnost. 6 .— When occurring with pugil, pyctes denotes a boxer who…

Pydna.opening: , = Πύδνα , a city in Macedonia , on the Thermaic Gulf (the modern Kitro ), celebrated for the battle in which Perseus was defeated by Æmilius Paulus , Liv. 44, 6, 3 ; 44, 42, 2 sqq.; Nep. Them. 8, 5 .— , , , the…

Pȳlēnē.opening: , = Πυλήνη , a town of Ætolia , Stat. Th. 4, 102 .

pўlōrus.opening: , = πυλωρός , the lower orifice of the stomach , the pylorus , Cael. Aur. Tard. 4, 6 al.

pўrălis.opening: ( ), , , = πυραλίς , a winged insect that was supposed to live in fire , called also pyrausta = πυραύστης , or pyrota, Plin. 11, 36, 42, § 119 ; 10, 74, 95, § 204 .

pȳrēn.opening: , = πυρήν, a precious stone , otherwise unknown, Plin. 37, 11, 73, § 188 .

pȳrēum.opening: , = πυρεῖον, the sanctuary of Vesta , Cassiod. H. E. 30 .

pўrītis.opening: , = πυρῖτις, a precious stone of a black color , otherwise unknown, Plin. 37, 11, 73, § 189 .

Pyrrhĭas.opening: , = Πυρρίας, commander of the Ætolians , Liv. 27, 30 .

Pyrrhĭăs.opening: adj. f. , = Πυρριάς, of the city of Pyrrha in Lesbos , Pyrrhian : puellae, Ov. H. 15, 15 .

pyrrhĭcha.opening: , and , , , = πυρριχη, a dance in armor , the Pyrrhic dance , Plin. 7, 56, 57, § 204 : elephas lasciviente pyrrhiche conludere, id. 8, 2, 2, § 5 ; Suet. Caes. 39 ; id. Ner. 12 ; Spart. Hadr 19 ; App. M. 10, p. 253, 18…

pyrrhĭchārĭus.opening: ( ), , pyrrhicha , one who performs the Pyrrhic dance , a Pyrrhichist , Dig. 48, 19, 8 fin.

pyrrhĭchĭus.opening: adj. , = πυρρίχιος; in prosody, pes, or simply pyrrhichius, a poetical foot consisting of two short syllables , a pyrrhic , Quint. 9, 4, 80 ; 106 ; 101 ; 140 al.; Mart. Cap. 9, § 975 .

pysma.opening: , = πύσμα; in rhet., a question , Aquila Rom. p. 152 Ruhnk.

pȳthaules.opening: , = πυθαύλης. One who plays upon the flute the song of the combat between the Pythian Apollo and the dragon Python , Hyg. Fab. 273 .— Transf. , in gen., one who plays upon the flute an accompaniment to the canticum (…

Pythĕas.opening: a geographer , a native of Marseilles , contemporary with Ptolemy Philadelphus , Plin. 2, 75, 77, § 187 ; 2, 97, 99, § 217 .

Pȳthĭa.opening: , v. Pythius, sub Python, II. B. 1. and 2.

pȳthĭon.opening: , = πυθίων, a kind of bulbous plant , otherwise unknown, Plin 19, 5, 30, § 95 (the correct reading is opitiona).

Pythĭum.opening: , = Πύθιον, a town of Thessaly , Liv. 42, 53 ; 44, 2 .

pyxăgăthus.opening: or , , , = πυξἀγαθός, a skilful boxer , Mart. 7, 57, 2 .

quā^dra.opening: a square. In gen.: qui locus gradibus in quadram formatus est, Fest. s. v. Romanam, p. 262 Müll.— In partic. In arch. The lowest and largest member of the base of a pedestal , the foundation-stone , socle , plinth ,…

Quā^dra.opening: a Roman surname , e. g. Hostius Quadratus, Sen. Q. N. 1, 16, 1 .

quā^drāgēnārĭus.opening: adj. quadrageni , of or belonging to the number forty , consisting of forty , of forty : dolium, perh. holding forty congii, Cato, R. R. 105, 1 : fistula, a forty-inch pipe , i. e. made of a plate forty inches in width…

quā^drāgēni.opening: ( gen. quadragenūm, Caes. B. G. 4, 17 ; Liv. 38, 38 ), num. distrib. adj. [quadraginta]. Forty each : columnae singulae sestertiis quadragenis milibus locatae, Cic. Verr. 2, 1, 56, § 147 ; id. Att. 4, 18, 2 : octoginta…

quā^drāgēsĭmus.opening: (old form † , Num. ap. Eckh. D. N. 6, p. 296), , adj. quadraginta . The fortieth : pars quadragesima, Cato, R. R. 23, 2 : nono et quadragesimo die, Varr. ap. Gell. 3, 10, 7 : anno fere centesimo et quadragesimo, Cic.…

quā^drāgĭes.opening: (old orthogr. QVA DRAGIENS, Monum. Ancyr. ap. Grut. 230), adv. num. id. , forty times : quadragies quater accusatus, Aur. Vict. Vir. Illustr. 47 : sestertium ter et quadragies, the 4,300,000 sesterces , Cic. Fl. 13, 30…

quā^drāgintā.opening: num. adj. quattuor , forty : quattuor quadraginta minae, Plaut. Most. 3, 1, 102 : annos natus, Cic. Rosc. Am. 14, 39 ; id. Rep. 2, 30, 52 : jugera arvi, Cat. 115, 2 ; Col. 5, 2, 10 ; 5, 1, 13 .

quā^drangŭlātus.opening: adj. quadrangulus , quadrangular (eccl. Lat.): quadrangulata turris, Tert. Anim. 17 : ligna, Vulg. 3 Reg. 7, 5 .

quā^drangŭlum.opening: quattuor-angulus , a quadrangle : quadrangulum, τετράγωνον, Gloss. Lat. Gr.; Mart. Cap. 7, § 754 (dub.; al. quadriangulo).

quā^drans.opening: ( gen. plur. quadrantūm, Front. Aquaed. 24 ), quattuor . A fourth part , a fourth , a quarter : operae, Col. 2, 4, 8 : diei noctisque, Plin. 18, 25, 57, § 207 . — In partic. A fourth part , a fourth of a whole:…

quā^drantal.opening: quadrantalis . A liquid measure containing eight congii, a quadrantal , Cato ap. Fest. p. 258, 20 Müll.; id. R. R. 57, 2 ; Plaut. Curc. 1, 2, 15 ; Plin. 14, 14, 16, § 95 .— A die , cube , Gell. 1, 20, 3 .

quā^drantālis.opening: adj. quadrans , containing the fourth part of a measure (postAug.): mensa crassitudine quadrantali, of a quarter of a foot, Plin. 13, 15, 29, § 93 .

quā^drantārĭus.opening: adj. id. . Prop., of or belonging to a quarter , relating to a fourth part : in tabulis quadrantariis, quas ait ab Hirtuleio institutas, i. e. new accounts reducing all debts to one fourth, Cic. Font. 1, 2 .— In…

quā^drātārĭus.opening: adj. quadratus , of or belonging to work with the square , i. e. to the work of the stone-cutter : OPVS, perh. a stone monument , Inscr. Murat. 2012, 2 .— As subst. : , , , a stonecutter (post-class.), interchanged with…

quā^drātē.opening: adv. , v. quadro, P. a. fin.

Quā^drātilla.opening: a Roman female name , e. g. Ummilia, Plin. Ep. 7, 24, 7 ; cf. Inscr Murat. 3, 27, 5.

quā^drātim.opening: adv. quadratus , fourfold , acc. to Charis. p. 168 P.

quā^drātĭo.opening: id. , a square , quadrate : agatur linea rotundationis, quae quadrationis angulos tangat, Vitr. 4, 3, 9 .

quā^drātor.opening: quadro , a stonecutter : marmorum, Cassiod. Ep. 2, 7 .

quā^drātūra.opening: quadro . A making square , squaring , quadrature (postclass.): circuli quadratura, the squaring or quadrature of the circle , App. Dogm. Plat. 3, p. 37, 11 .— Transf. , a square : vitreae, Vop. Firm. 3 .

Quadrātus.opening: a Roman surname , e. g. Ummilius Quadratus, Plin. Ep. 6, 11, 1 ; 7, 24, 6 .

quā^drĭangŭlus.opening: adj. quattuor-angulus , four-cornered , quadrangular (post-Aug.); figura, Plin. 13, 22, 38, § 118 : herba quadriangulo caule, id. 25, 6, 27, § 63 : membrum, Aus. Epigr. 128 . — As subst. : , , , a quadrilateral figure ,…

quā^drĭbaccĭum.opening: and † , , quattuor-bacca , fourbeads , four-pearls , an ornament composed of four pearls, Inscr. Murat. 139, 1 .

Quā^drĭburgĭum.opening: a fortified town in Gallia Belgica , Amm. 18, 2, 4 ; Inscr. Orell. 2090 .

quā^drĭdens.opening: adj. quattuordens , four - toothed , having four teeth (ante - class.): rastri quadridentes, Cato, R. R. 10, 3 ; 11, 4 .

quā^drĭdŭānus.opening: ( ), , adj. quadriduum , of four days , for the space of four days : Lazarus mortuus, Hier. Ep. 108 , n. 24; Vulg. Joan. 11, 39 .

quā^drĭdŭum.opening: ( ), , quattuor-dies , a space of four days , four days (class.): in hoc triduo aut quadriduo, Plaut. Pers. 1, 1, 37 ; so Cato, R. R. 65, 2 ; 113, 2 ; Cic. Verr. 2, 4, 3, § 6 ; id. Tusc. 5, 4, 11 ; 4, 38, 82 ; Liv. 3, 3…

quā^drĭennis.opening: adj. quattuor-annus , of four years , four years old (post-class.): homo, Aur. Vict. Epit. 45 .

quā^drĭennĭum.opening: quadriennis , a space or period of four years (class.), Cic. Caecin. 7, 19 ; id. Opt. Gen. 7, 22 ; id. Sen. 4, 10 ; Cic. Verr. 2, 3, 18, § 47 ; Flor. 2, 6 .

quā^drĭēris.opening: ( ), , vox hibr. from quattuor and ἄρω, analog. to τριήρης , a vessel having four banks of oars , a quadrireme (post-class.): EX CLASS. PR. MIS. QVADRIERE FIDE, Inscr. Murat. 876, 3 : quatrieris, Not. Tir. p. 177 .

quā^drĭfārĭam.opening: adv. quattuor . Fourfold , into four parts (class.; not in Cic. or Cæs.): quadrifariam aliquid dispertire, Varr. ap. Non. 92, 15 : conjurati quadrifariam se diviserunt, Liv. 38, 1 : quadrifariam diviso exercitu, id. 4,…

quā^drĭfārĭter.opening: adv. , in a fourfold manner , in four ways (post-class.), Dig. 38, 10, 10, § 14 ; cf. quadrifariam.

quā^drĭfārĭus.opening: adj. quattuor , fourfold (post-class.): divisio, Cassiod. Var. 3, 51 ; 1, 45 ; Arn. in Psa. 108 .

quā^drĭfĭdus.opening: adj. quattuorfindo , four-cleft , split into four parts , quadrifid ( poet. ). Lit. : quadrifidas sudes, Verg. G. 2, 25 : quadrifidam quercum Scindebat, was cleaving in four, id. A. 7, 509 : quadrifidā trabe fingere…

quā^drĭfīnālis.opening: adj. quadrifinium , bordering on four places , or marking four boundaries (post-class.): arca, Innocent. de Casis Litterar. p. 222 Goes.

quā^drĭfīnĭum.opening: quattuor-finis , a place where four boundaries meet (postclass.), Innocent. p. 221 and 227 Goes.; Isid. 15, 14, 5 .

quā^drĭflŭus.opening: adj. quattuorfluo , having four streams , flowing into four parts (eccl. Lat.): amnis, Prud. Cath. 3, 103 .

quā^drĭflŭvĭum.opening: quattuor-fluvius , a flowing into four parts , in four directions : ima abietis pars, cum excisa quadrifluviis disparatur, i. e. into four parts, according to the course of the veins, Vitr. 2, 9, 7 .

quā^drĭfŏris.opening: adj. quattuor-fores , four-doored , i.e. having four doors or four doorways ( openings ) (post-Aug.): nidi, Plin. 11, 21, 24, § 74 : januae, having four leaves, divided crosswise, Vitr. 4, 6, 5 .

quā^drĭformis.opening: adj. quattuor-forma , four-formed , quadriform , Macr. S. 1, 9, 13 ; Not. Tir. p. 110 .

quā^drĭfrons.opening: adj. quattuor-frons , four-fronted , having four foreheads , or four faces : Janus, Aug. Civ. Dei , 7, 4; Serv. ad Verg. A. 7, 607 .

quā^drīgae.opening: (collat. form in the sing. v. infra ), contr. from quadrijugae , a set or team of four , a four-abreast , fourin-hand , four together (class.). Lit. Of horses, applied to the animals with or without the car or vehicle,…

quā^drīgālis.opening: adj. quadrigae , of or belonging to a team of four : equi, Paul. ex Fest. s. v. curules, p. 49 Müll.

quā^drĭgămus.opening: vox hibr. from quattuor-γάμος , one who has married four times , a husband for the fourth time (eccl. Lat.), Hier. adv. Jovin. 1 , n. 15.

quā^drīgārĭus.opening: adj. quadrigae , of or belonging to a four-horse ( racing ) chariot (post-Aug.): quadrigario habitu, in the dress of the driver of a quadriga, Suet. Calig. 17 : pulvis, for the race-horses , Veg. Vet. 1, 56 ; 2, 28, 19…

Quā^drīgārĭus.opening: a Roman surname. Thus, Q. Claudius Quadrigarius, an old Roman historian , Vell. 2, 9, 6 ; Gell. 1, 7, 9 ; called simply Claudius, Liv. 8, 19, 13 .

quā^drīgātus.opening: adj. quadrigae , marked or stamped with the figure of a quadriga (a coin), Liv. 22, 58, 4 ; cf.: nota argenti fuere bigae, atque quadrigae, et inde bigati et quadrigati dicti, Plin. 33, 3, 13, § 46 ; Paul. ex Fest. p.…

quā^drĭgĕmĭnus.opening: adj. quattuor-geminus , fourfold , four (post-Aug.): cornicula, four, Plin. 8, 23, 35, § 85 ; cf. Sol. 27, 28 .

quā^drĭgōnus.opening: adj. quadrus, γῶνος , having four angles : figura, Claud. Mam. Ep. 1 med.

quā^drīgŭlae.opening: f dim. [quadrigae], a little four-horse team (class.), Cic. Fat. 3, 5 .—In sing. , Plin. 34, 8, 19, § 83 .

quā^drīgŭlārĭus.opening: adj. quadrigulae , of or belonging to a little fourhorse team (post-class.): PICTOR, who painted little four-horse teams, Inscr. Don. 317, 6 ; Inscr. Orell. 4262 .

quā^drĭjŭgis.opening: adj. quattuor-jugum , of or belonging to a team of four ( poet. and post-Aug.): equi, Verg. A. 10, 571 : currus, App. Flor. 3, p. 356, 14 .

quā^drĭjŭgus.opening: adj. id. , of or belonging to a team of four ( poet. ): curru, Enn. ap. Cic. Tusc. 1, 44, 105 (Trag. v. 129 Vahl.); Verg. A. 12, 162 ; id. G. 3, 18 ; Plin. Pan. 22, 1 : equi, Ov. Am. 3, 2, 66 ; id. Tr. 4, 2, 54 :…

quā^drĭlătĕrus.opening: adj. quattuorlatus , four-sided , quadrilateral , Front. p. 35 Goes.; Boëth. Art. Geom. p. 375, 16 (Friedl.): figura, Isid. Orig. 3, 3, 12 .

quā^drĭlībris.opening: adj. quattuor-libra , that weighs four pounds (ante-class.), Plaut. Aul. 5, 2 .

quā^drĭmănus.opening: , and , , adj. quattuor-manus , fourhanded , having four hands (post-class.): puella biceps, quadripes, quadrimana, Jul. Obseq. Prodig. 111 : pueri quadrupedes et quadrimanes, id. ib. 73 .

quā^drīmātus.opening: quadrimus , the age of four years (post-Aug.): extra quadrimatum, Plin. 19, 11, 58, § 181 : ante quadrimatum, id. 8, 45, 70, § 176 : dum quadrimatum agant, Col. 7, 9, 2 ; 9, 1, 7 .

quā^drĭmembris.opening: adj. quattuormembrum , four-limbed or four-footed, going on all fours (post-class.), Mart. Cap. poët. 8, § 805 dub. (al. hiantimembrem).

quā^drĭmenstrŭus.opening: adj. quattuor-mensis , of four months (late Lat.), Cod. Just. 1, 32, 1 ; Cod. Th. 12, 6, 27, § 1.

quā^drĭmestris.opening: adj. id. , of four months (ante-class. and post-Aug.): agni, Varr. R. R. 2, 2, 17 : consulatus, Suet. Ner. 14 : indutiae, Cod. 7, 54, 3, pr. § 1.

quā^drīmŭlus.opening: adj. dim. [quadrimus], of four years , four years old (Plautin.): parvulus, Plaut. Capt. 5, 3, 4 : altera, id. Poen. prol. 85 .

quā^drīmus.opening: adj. quattuor and root ghim-, him-, of Sanscr. himas, snow; cf. Gr. χιών, χεῖμα; Lat. hiems, hibernus; hence, of four winters , of four years , four years old (class.): de quadrimo Catone, of Cato of Utica, when four…

quā^dringēnārĭus.opening: adj. quadringeni , of four hundred each (class.): cohortes, each consisting of four hundred men, Cic. Att. 6, 1, 14 : quadringenariae cohortes (al. quadringentariae), Liv. 7, 7, 4 : IVDEX, who possessed an equestrian…

quā^dringēni.opening: ( , Varr. R. R. 2, 8, 3 ), num. distrib. adj. [quadringenti], four hundred each , Liv. 8, 11 fin. ; 45, 16, 3 : milia nummūm, Suet. Vit. 13 .

quā^dringentēni.opening: , a false read. for quadringenti, q. v.

quā^dringentēsĭmus.opening: adj. quadringenti , the four hundredth : annus, Liv. 5, 45, 4 ; so Plin. 8, 6, 6, § 16 .

quā^dringenti.opening: adj. quattuorcentum , four hundred : anni, Cic. Rep. 1, 37, 58 ; so id. Pis. 5, 10 : talis quadringentis jactis, id. Div. 2, 21, 48 : (sestertia), Juv. 1, 105 ; Vitr. 10, 9, 4 : pantheres, Plin. 8, 17, 24, § 64 .

quā^dringentĭes.opening: adv. quadringenti , four hundred times : HS quadringenties, forty millions of sesterces, Cic. Verr. 2, 2, 10, § 26 ; id. Phil. 2, 37, 93 ; id. Rab. Post. 8, 21 .

quā^drīni.opening: num. distrib. adj. [quattuor], four each , four (ante-class. and postAug.): ab uno uni, a tribus trini, a quattuor quadrini, Varr. L. L. 8, § 55 Müll.: si haberem quadrinas molas, Pompon. ap. Non. 483, 24 : dies, Plin.…

quā^drĭnoctĭum.opening: quattuornox , a space or period of four nights , acc. to Prisc. p. 1357 P.

quā^drĭ-partĭo.opening: , no perf. , , v. a. , and , , v. dep. quattuor-partio , to divide into four parts (in the verb. finit. post-class.): quadripartitur exercitus, Dict. Cret. 1, 19 .— Dep. : quadripartiretur, Not. Tir. p. 109 .— Hence, (…

quā^drĭ-partītĭo.opening: quadripartio , a division into four parts , quadripartition (only in Varro), Varr. L. L. 5, § 1 , and 7, § 5 Müll.

quā^drĭpartītō.opening: adv. , v. quadripartio, P. a. fin.

quā^drĭplātōres.opening: , qui eo quaestu se tuebantur, ut eas res persequerentur, quarum ex legibus quadrupli erat actio, Fest. p. 259, 3 Müll.; v. quadruplator.

quā^drĭ-rēmĭs.opening: ( , Not. Tir. p. 177 ), adj. quattuor-remus , having four banks of oars : machina, Paul. Nol. Carm. 21, 73 .— Hence, subst. : , , , a vessel having four banks of oars , a quadrireme (class.): egreditur Centuripinā…

quā^drĭ-sēmus.opening: adj. vox hibr. from quattuor-σῆμα, sign , quadrisyllabic , containing four morae or prosodial times (gram. term): numerus, Mart. Cap. 9, § 981 .

quā^drĭ-sōmus.opening: adj. vox hibr. from quadrus, σῶμα , containing four bodies : SEPVLCRVM, Inscr. Rein. col. 2, 40; 43 al.

quā^drĭvĭum.opening: quattuor-via . Lit. , a place where four ways meet , a crossway , cross-road : in quadriviis et angiportis, Cat. 58, 4 ; so Juv. 1, 63 : DII, the tutelar gods of cross-roads, Inscr. Grut. 84, 5 ; 1015, 1 ; Inscr. Rein.…

quā^drĭvĭus.opening: adj. quadrusvia , of the cross-roads , only in the phrase DIS or LARIBVS QVADRIVIIS (sometimes QVADRIBIS), Inscr. Orell. 389 ; 1664 ; 2103 sqq.

quā^dro.grammar: āvi, ātum, 1 v. a. and n.
quā^dro.opening: v. a. and n. quadrus . Act. , to make four-cornered , to square , make square : abies atque populus ad unguem quadrantur, Col. 11, 2, 13 : lapides, Vulg. 3 Reg. 5, 17 .— Transf. , to put in proper order , to join…

quā^drŭla.opening: dim. quadra , a little square (post-class.), Sol. 37 .

quā^drum.opening: quattuor , something square , a square , quadrate (class.). Lit. : perticae dolantur in quadrum, Col. 8, 3, 7 : per quadrum singulos habens cubitos, Vulg. Exod. 37, 25 . — Transf. , a being squared or fitted together ,…

quā^drŭ-pĕdans.opening: Part. , from the obsol. quadrupedo [quadrupes]. Going on four feet , galloping ( poet. and postAug.): canterius, Plaut. Capt. 4, 2, 34 : equo juxta quadrupedante, galloping close by on horseback, Plin. 8, 45, 70, § 182…

quā^drŭpĕdātim.opening: adv. quattuorpes , in the manner of a quadruped , acc. to Charis. p. 163 P.

quā^drŭpĕdĭus.opening: adj. id. , fourfooted , quadruped , Jul. Val. Rer. Gest. Alex. M. 3, 36 .

quā^drŭpĕdus.opening: ( , Front. ad M. Anton. Or. 1 ), , adj. quadrupes , going on four feet , galloping (postAug.): quadrupedo gradu repentes, on all fours, Amm. 14, 2, 2 : quadripedo cursu, on a gallop, Front. 1, 1 .— Absol. : quadrupedo…

quā^drŭpēs.opening: ( ), ( gen. plur. quadrupedium, Capitol. Ver. 5, 2 ), adj. quattuor-pes , having four feet , going on four feet; esp., Galloping (post-Aug.): ecus, Enn. ap. Gell. 18, 5, 4 ; cf. Macr. S. 6, 9, 10 : equestri celeritate,…

quā^drŭplāris.opening: adj. quadruplus , fourfold , quadruple (post-class.): numerus duplaris, triplaris, quadruplaris (al. quadruplus), Macr. Somn. Scip. 1, 19, 21 .

quā^drŭplātor.opening: ( , Fest. p. 259 Müll. v. h. v.: , Plaut. Pers. 1, 2, 18 ), , quadruplo . One who multiplies by four , a quadrupler , App. Mag. p. 330, 20 . — Transf. , a multiplier , magnifier , exaggerator : beneficiorum suorum, Sen.…

quā^drū^plātor.opening: ( ), , quadruplor , a public informer , who received a fourth part of the thing informed against (acc. to others, against one who committed an offence punishable with a fourfold penalty; cf. sector); also, in gen., a…

quā^drŭplex.opening: adj. quattuor-plico . Fourfold , quadruple : pecunia, Plaut. Curc. 5, 2, 21 : ordo, Liv. 30, 10 : quadruplici radice, Plin. 27, 8, 38, § 60 .—* Poet. , in gen., four : stellae, Cic. Arat. 92 .— As subst. : , , , a…

quā^drŭ-plĭcātĭo.opening: quadruplico , a making fourfold , quadruplication (post-class.): numeri, Mart. Cap. 7, § 750 ; so Dig. 44, 1, 2 .

quā^drŭplĭco.opening: v. a. quadruplex , to multiply by four , make fourfold , quadruplicate : rem suam, one ' s property , Plaut. Stich. 3, 1, 4 : numerum, Dig. 38, 10, 10 .— , adv. : , four times as much , quadruply (postAug.), Plin. 2,…

quā^drŭplo.opening: , no perf. , , v. a. quadruplus , to multiply by four , make fourfold , quadruple (post-class.), Dig. 4, 2, 14 , §§ 1, 7: numerus quadruplatus, ib. 38, 10, 10, § 17 ; 47, 2, 50 pr.; Ambros. Apol. Dav. 5, 22 .

quā^drŭplor.opening: v. dep. id. , to be an informer , cheater , trickster , chicaner : neque quadruplari me volo, Plaut. Pers. 1, 2, 10 (al. quadrupulari).

quā^drŭplus.opening: ( , Plaut. Truc. 4, 2, 49 Fleck.), , adj. quattuor , fourfold , quadruple (rare as adj. ): strena, Suet. Tib. 34 : numerus, Macr. Somn. Scip. 1, 19, 21 ; 2, 1, 19 .— Subst. : , , , a fourfold amount , four times as much…

quadrurbem.grammar: Athenas Attius appellavit, quod scilicet ex quattuor urbibus in unam domicilia contulerunt, Braurone, Eleusine, Piraeeo, Sunio

quā^drus.opening: adj. for quatrus, from quattuor , square (post-class.): quadrus terminus, Auct. Limit. p. 281 Goes.: cella, Pall. 1, 40 : lapides, Vulg. Isa. 9, 10 .

quā^drŭus.opening: adj. quattuor , fourcornered or fourfold (post-class.): errabam riguis per quadrua compita in hortis, i. e. laid out in squares, Aus. Idyll. 14, 5 : vis, fourfold, Prud. Psych. 842 .

quaerĭto.opening: v. freq. a. quaero , to seek , search , or look for earnestly (ante-class.). In gen.: hominem inter vivos quaeritamus mortuum, Plaut. Men. 2, 1, 15 : defessus sum quaeritando, id. Am. 4, 1, 4 ; id. Cist. 4, 2, 19 :…

quaero.opening: (old orthogr. QVAIRO, Epitaphs of the Scipios, 6; for the original form and etym. , , v. quaeso), sīvi or , v. a. , to seek. Lit. In gen.: aliquem, Enn. ap. Cic. Div. 1, 20, 40 (Ann. v. 43 Vahl.); Plaut. Mil. 2, 3, 3 :…

quaesītĭo.opening: quaero , a seeking or searching after (post-Aug.). In gen.: Psyche quaesitioni Cupidinis intenta, populos circuibat, App. M. 5, p. 171, 8 .— In partic., a questioning by torture , the question , inquisition : cum…

quaesītor.opening: id. , a seeker , searcher (post-class.). In gen., as for gold, connected with scrutator, Pacat. Pan. Th. 28 .— In partic., an investigator. In judicial (esp. in criminal) matters, an examiner , inquisitor : quid mihi…

quaesītūra.opening: , a false read. for quaestura, Tac. A. 3, 29 .

quaesītus.opening: (only in abl. sing. ), quaero . A seeking , searching (postAug.), Plin. 5, 9, 10, § 51 (al. quae situs).— Investigation : (rem) semper quaesitu dignam putavi, Macr. S. 7, 8, 9 .

quaeso.opening: v. a. old form of quaero; root kis-; Sanscr. cish-, to hunt out . To seek , to seek to obtain any thing (ante-class.): quaeso, ut significat idem, quod rogo, ita quaesere ponitur ab antiquis pro quaerere, Fest. p. 258…

quaestĭcŭlus.opening: dim. quaestus , a small profit , slight gain (class.), Cic. Div. 2, 15, 34 ; id. Fam. 9, 16, 7 ; App. M. 11, p. 272, 1 .

quaestĭo.opening: quaero , a seeking. In gen. (Plautin.): cave, fuas mi in quaestione, lest you suffer yourself to be to seek, lest I have to look after you, Plaut. Pers. 1, 1, 52 : tibi ne in quaestione essemus, id. Capt. 2, 2, 3 ; id.…

quaestĭōnālĭter.opening: adv. quaestio , by way of question , in the form of a question (post-class.): propositio quaestionaliter posita, Fulg. Prisc. Serm. 16 .

quaestĭōnārĭus.opening: id. , a torturer , executioner (post-class.), Cod. Th. 16, 12, 3; Hier. in Joel. 2, 21 ; Schol. Juv. 6, 480 ; Inscr. Grut. 545, 6 .

quaestĭōno.opening: v. a. id. , put to the question , i. e. put to the torture , put to the rack (eccl. Lat. and rare): omnes quaestionari, Fragm. Jur. Civ. Ante-Just. p. 109 Mai: tot confessores quaestionati et torti, Cypr. Ep. 69 , n. 6.

quaestĭuncŭla.opening: dim. id. , a little or trifling question (class.): quaestiunculam alicui ponere, Cic. de Or. 1, 22, 102 ; Sen. Ep. 117, 1 : multae, Cic. Leg. 2, 20, 51 ; Quint. 1, 3, 11 ; Suet. Gram. 24 fin.
