querquedŭla.opening: from the Gr. κερκουρίς, Varr. L. L. 5, § 79, acc. to O. Müller's conjecture , a kind of duck , perh. the teal , Varr. R. R. 3, 3, 3 ; 3, 11, 4 ; Col. 8, 15, 1 : aquatiles querquedulae, Varr. ap. Non. 91, 4 .

querquĕrus.opening: or , , adj. cf. Gr. καρκαίρω, to tremble , cold to trembling , shivering (ante- and post-class.): querqueram frigidam cum tremore a Graeco κάρκαρα certum est dici, unde et carcer. Lucilius: Jactans me ut febris…

querquētŭlānus.opening: adj. from querquetum, for quercetum , of or belonging to an oak-forest , named from an oakwood : querquetulanae virae (i. e. virgines) putantur significari nymphae praesidentes querqueto virescenti: quod genus silvae…

quĕrŭlōsus.opening: ( ), , adj. querulus , full of complaints , querulous (late Lat.): murmuratores, Vulg. Ep. Jud. v. 16 ; Cassiod. Var. 9, 14 .

quĕrŭlus.opening: adj. queror . Lit. , full of complaints , complaining , querulous (mostly poet. ; not in Cic.): (senex) difficilis, querulus, laudator temporis acti, Hor. A. P. 173 : ululatus, Ov. H. 5, 73 : dolor, id. Tr. 3, 8, 32 :…

questĭo.opening: queror , a complaining , complaint : habebat enim flebile quiddam in questionibus aptumque ad misericordiam commovendam, Cic. Brut. 38, 142 Orell. (B. and K. ex conj. Lambin.: conquestionibus).

questus.opening: queror , a complaining , complaint , plaint (class.). Lit. In gen., Cic. Quint. 30, 94 : caelum questibus implet, Verg. A. 9, 480 : tantos illa suo rumpebat pectore questus, id. ib. 4, 553 : tales effundit in aëra…

qui.opening: (old forms: nom. ; gen. quojus; dat. quoi, and in inscrr. QVOEI, QVOIEI, and QVEI; abl. qui; plur. ques or queis; fem. QVAI; neutr. qua; dat. and abl. queis and quĭs.—Joined with cum : quocum, quācum, quicum, quibuscum;…

quī.opening: adv. interrog. , rel. and indef. [old abl. of 1. qui]. Interrog. , in what manner? how? whereby? by what means? why? In direct questions: quī minus eadem histrioni sit lex quae summo viro? Plaut. Am. prol. 76 : Quī,…

quĭă.opening: conj. [for quiam, from abl. quī and jam, whereby now; hence], because (usually, like quod, of the determining reason; while quonĭam introduces any casual circumstance). In gen., constr. with indic. in asserting a fact;…

quīcumque.opening: (or ), (also separately: cum quibus erat cumque una, Ter. And. 1, 1, 36 ; quam se cumque in partem, Cic. de Or. 3, 16, 59 . — Old form of the plur. quescumque, Cato ap. Charis. p. 70 P., and ap. Prisc. p. 960 P.), pron.…

quīdam.opening: , and subst. quiddam, pron. indef. , a certain , a certain one , somebody , something (v. aliquis init. ): quidam ex advocatis, Cic. Clu. 63, 177 : quidam de collegis nostris, id. Fam. 11, 21, 5 : quaedam certa vox, id.…

quĭdem.opening: adv. Indeed : sibi quidem persuaderi, eum, etc., Caes. B. C. 1, 40 : tantum doleo, ac mirifice quidem, Cic. Att. 2, 19, 1 : in his locis post solstitium Canicula oritur, et quidem aliquot diebus, id. Div. 2, 44, 93 .—…

quĭes.opening: adj. , for quietus, a, um (cf. inquies), quiet , peaceful (ante-class.): mens, Naev. ap. Prisc. p. 704 P.: milites quietes, Licin. Macer. ib.

quĭescentĭa.opening: quiesco , rest , quiet (post-class. for quies), Firm. Math. 1, 3.

quĭescĭtus.opening: Part. , from quiesco; v. quiesco init.

quĭesco.grammar: ēvi, ētum, 3 v. n. and a.
quĭesco.opening: (the uncontr. Part. , QVIESCITA, Inscr. Don. cl. 10, n. 11), v. n. and a. [quies], to rest , repose , keep quiet. Lit. : placida compostus pace quiescit, Verg. A. 1, 249 : felicius ossa quiescant, Ov. Ib. 305 : patrono…

quĭētē.opening: adv. , v. quiesco, P. a. fin.

quĭētūdo.opening: quies , rest , calmness , quietude : quietudo, ἠρεμία, ἡσυχία, Gloss. Cyrill.

quĭētus.opening: Part. and P. a. , v. quiesco.

quī-lĭbet.opening: ( ), , and subst. quidlibet, pron. indef. , any one who will , any one without distinction , whom you will , no matter who , the first that comes , any , all (class.): quem ament igitur? Sy. Alium quemlibet, any body…

quilon.opening: ( ), , , jelly (postclass.): si cylon feceris, etc., Veg. Vet. 3, 38 : ut quilon fiat, id. ib. 3, 66 .

quĭmātus.opening: , a false read. for quinquennatus, Plin. 8, 45, 70, § 178 .

quīn.opening: conj. [ abl. quī and ne]. As an interrog. particle , why not? wherefore not? (only in exhortation or remonstrance; not in inquiring for a fact; cf.: quidni, cur non). Usu. with indic. pres. : quid stas, lapis? Quin…

quī-nam.opening: pron. interrog. , who , which , what , pray (anteclass.): quinam homo hic ante aedes ejulans conqueritur? Plaut. Aul. 4, 9, 17 : quinam Tantalidarum internecioni modus sit? Att. ap. Charis. p. 70 P.: quodnam ob facinus?…

quīnārĭus.opening: adj. quini , containing five (mostly post-Aug.): quinaria (fistula) dicta a diametro quinque quadrantum, a pipe which was five quarter-digits in diameter, Front. Aquaed. 25 ; so, fistulae, Plin. 31, 6, 31, § 58 :…

quincuncĭālis.opening: adj. quincunx . Containing five twelfths of a whole (of a foot, etc.): quincuncialis magnitudo, the size of five twelfths of a foot, Plin. 9 . 48, 72, § 155: herba, five twelfths of a foot high, id. 27, 11, 74, § 98 .—…

quincunx.opening: . , quinque-uncia , fire twelfths of a whole (of an as, a jugerum, a pound, a sextarius, etc.). Lit. : si de quincunce remota est Uncia, quid superat? from five twelfths of an as, Hor. A. P. 327 ; so five twelfths of a…

quincŭpĕdal.opening: quinque-pes , a measuring-rod of five feet , a five-foot rod , Mart. 14, 92 in lemm.

quincū^plex.opening: adj. quinque-plico , fivefold ( poet. ): cera, a writing-tablet consisting of five waxed leaves, Mart. 14, 4 : quincuplex Tolosa, consisting of five wards or quarters , Aus. Ep. 24, 83 ; Vop. Fl. 3 .

quindĕcĭes.opening: ( ), adv. quindecim , fifteen times : quindeciens sestertium ( neutr. sing. ), fifteen hundred thousand sesterces , Cic. Verr. 2, 2 . 25, § 61; Mart. 7, 10, 15 .

quindĕcim.opening: num. adj. quinque-decem , fifteen : QVINDECIM PONDO, Lex XII. Tab.: quindecim miles minas dederat, Plaut. Ps. 1, 1, 51 ; 1, 3, 112 ; Hor. C. S. 70 : dies circiter quindecim, Caes. B. G. 1, 15 ; App. Mag. p. 304, 33 .

quindĕcim-prīmi.opening: the board of fifteen chief magistrates in the municipia, in MSS. abbrev. XV. primi: evocat ad se Caesar Massiliensium XV. primos, Caes. B. C. 1, 35, 1 ; so perh. also Inscr. Murat. 626, 1 .

quindĕcĭmus.opening: adj. quindecim , the fifteenth (late Lat. for the class. quintus decimus), Marc. Emp. 36 .

quindĕcimvir.opening: ( plur. in inscrr. usually X¯V̄. VIRI, but also written in full, QVINDECIM VIRO SACRIS FACIVNDIS, Inscr. Grut. 476, 7 , of A. D. 346), vĭri (separated, quindecim Diana preces virorum, Hor. C. S. 70 ), quindecim-vir , a…

quindĕcimvĭrālis.opening: (in inscrr. abbrev. X¯V¯. VIRALIS), adj. id. , of or belonging to the quindecimvirs or council of fifteen (post-Aug.): sacerdotium quindecimviraie, Tac. A. 11, 11 : SACERDOS ( fem. ), Inscr. Orell. 2198 ; 2199 ; 2328 .

quindĕcimvĭrātus.opening: id. , the dignity of a quindecimvir , the quindecimvirate , Lampr. Alex. Sev. 49 .

quindēnārĭus.opening: quindeni , containing fifteen : numerus, Ambros. Cant. Cantic. 3, 25 fin.

quingēnārĭus.opening: adj. quingeni . Consisting of five hundred each (post-Aug.): cohortes, Curt. 5, 2, 3 .— Consisting of five hundred : thorax, i. e. of five hundred pounds weight, Plin. 7, 20, 19, § 83 : lanx, id. 33, 11, 52, § 145 :…

quingēni.opening: num. distr. adj. [quingenti]. Five hundred each (class.): quingenos denarios dat, Cic. Att. 16, 8, 1 ; 4, 16, 7 ; Suet. Aug. 101 ; id. Caes. 38 ; id. Ner. 10 ; Dig. 38, 1, 15 .— In gen., five hundred , Col. 5, 2, 6 .

quingentārĭus.opening: adj. id. , consisting of five hundred (post-class.): cohors, Veg. Mil. 2, 6 .

quingentēni.opening: num. distr. adj. [id.], = quingeni, Vulg. 2 Macc. 8, 22 .

quingentēsĭmus.opening: adj. id. , the five hundredth (class.): annus, Cic. Fl. 1, 1 ; so Plin. 15, 1, 1, § 2 .

quingenti.opening: (old orthogr. quincenti, acc. to Fest. p. 254 Müll.), ae, a ( gen. plur. quingentum, Liv. 10, 37, 5 , etc.: quingentorum, Tac. A. 6, 34 ; Just. 2, 11 ), num. adj. quinque-centum . Five hundred : quingentos uno ictu…

quingentĭes.opening: ( ), adv. quingenti , five hundred times : quingentiens mille, Vitr. 1, 6 .—Of money: quingentiens HS., fifty millions of sesterces, Cic. Verr. 2, 2, 38, § 93 : miliens et quingentiens, Suet. Aug. 101 ; id. Galb. 5 .

quīni.opening: ( gen. plur. quinum, Col. 4, 30 ; Pandect. 40, 9, 5: quinorum not found), num. distr. adj. [quinque]. Five each : quini in lectulis, Cic. Pis. 27, 67 : pedes, Caes. B. G. 3, 73 : ordines, id. ib. 7, 23 : versus, Nep.…

quīnī-dēni.opening: or , , num. distr. adj. Fifteen each : quina dena jugera agri data in singulos pedites sunt, Liv. 35, 40 : quini deni pedes, Quint. 1, 10, 43 : quindeni pedes, Vitr. 6, 9 : anni, Plin. 10, 63, 83, § 178 : HS., Suet.…

quīnĭo.opening: quini , the number five , a pentad (post-class.): quinionem filiorum eniti, Tert. Anim. 6 : voluminum, id. ib. 46 . —Esp. at dice, a five , a cinque , Isid. Orig. 18, 65 .

quīnī-vīcēni.opening: ( ), , num. distr. adj. , twenty-five each (only in Liv.): militibus quini viceni denarii dati, Liv. 37, 59 fin.

quinquāgēnārĭus.opening: adj. quinquageni . Consisting of fifty , containing fifty : grex equarum, Varr. R. R. 2, 10, 11 : dolium, Cato, R. R. 69, 2 : urna, id. ib. 10, 2 : fistula, the plate of which, before being bent, was fifty inches in…

quinquāgēni.opening: ( gen. plur. quinquagenūm, Plin. 15, 24, 28, § 99 al. : quinquagenorum not found), num. distr. adj. [quinquaginta]. Fifty each : in singulos HS. quinquagenis milibus damnari mavultis? Cic. Verr. 2, 3, 28, § 69 :…

quinquāgensĭens.opening: adv. id. , fifty times (for the usual quinquagiens), Plaut. Men. 5, 9, 99 Ritschl N. cr.

quinquāgēsĭmus.opening: num. adj. [quinquaginta]. The fiftieth : anno trecentesimo et quinquagesimo fere post Romam conditam, Cic. Rep. 1, 16, 25 ; 2, 35, 60 : quinquagesimo uno raptus anno, Plin. 7, 8, 6, § 46 : liba, Mart. 10, 24, 4 .—…

quinquāgĭens.opening: adv. id. , fifty times : dimicare, Plin. 7, 25, 25, § 92 : centena milia, id. 6, 9, 10, § 27 : perfricare, Cels. 2, 14 .

quinquāginta.opening: num. adj. , fifty : quinquaginta et quattuor, Plaut. Mil. 3, 1, 35 : famulae, Verg. A. 1, 703 : milia, Cic. Att. 4, 2, 5 ; Pomp. ap. Non. p. 280, 18 ; Col. 12, 23, 1 .

quinquangŭlus.opening: adj. quinque-angulus , five-cornered , quinquangular , Prisc. Pond. p. 1358 P.; Boëth. Geom. p. 398, 8 and 10.

Quinquātrūs.grammar: ŭum ōrum and ĭum f. n.
Quinquātrūs.opening: , and , , quinque, as falling on the fifth day after the ides; cf. Varr. L. L. 6, § 14 Müll.; Fest. p. 254 sq. ib.; Gell. 2, 21, 7 , a festival celebrated in honor of Minerva , the festival of Minerva (of these there…

quinquĕfŏlĭus.opening: adj. quinquefolium . Five-leaved : rosae, Plin. 21, 4, 10, § 24 .— Subst. : , , , a plant , cinque-foil , Cels. 2, 33 fin. ; Plin. 25, 9, 62, § 109 .

Quinquĕgentĭāni.opening: quinque-gens , a people in Cyrenaica (Latinized for Pentapolitani), Eutr. 9, 22 .— As adj. : Quinquegentianae nationes, Aur. Vict. Caes. 39 .

quinquĕgĕnus.opening: adj. quinquegenus , of five kinds (post-class.): nux, Aus. ldyll. 12 in Monosyll. de Cibis, 10.

quinquĕjŭgus.opening: adj. quinquejugum , having five summits , five-peaked (post-class.): vertex, Jul. Val. Rer. Gest. Alex. M. 1, 18 .

quinquĕlibrālis.opening: adj. quinque-libra , of five pounds (post-Aug.): pondus, Col. 3, 15, 3 .

quinquĕ-libris.opening: adj. id. , of five pounds weight (post-class.): patera, Vop. Prob. 5, 1 .

quinquĕmestris.opening: adj. quinquemensis , of five months , five months old (anteclass. and post-Aug.): pulli, Varr. R. R. 2, 7 : agni, Plin. 8, 48, 75, § 198 .

quinquennālīcĭus.opening: adj. quinquennalis , who has been a quinquennal , Inscr. Orell. 3720 ; 3721 ; 3890 .

quinquennālis.opening: adj. quinquennis . That takes place every fifth year , quinquennial : quinquennalis celebritas ludorum, Cic. de Or. 3, 32, 127 : certamen, Suet. Ner. 12 : ludicrum, Tac. A. 14, 20 : vota, Liv. 31, 9 : agon, Vulg. 2…

quinquennālĭtas.opening: quinquennalis, II. B. , the office and dignity of a quinquennal (post-class.), Inscr. Orell. 4075 ; cf. ib. 82 ; 6029 .

quinquennātus.opening: quinqueannus , the age of five years : robur in quinquennatu, Plin. 8, 45, 70, § 178 Sillig N. cr.

quinquennis.opening: adj. id. , of five years or five years old : filia, Plaut. Poen. prol. 85 : Olympias, celebrated every fifth year, quinquennial, Ov. P. 4, 6, 5 : vinum, Hor. S. 2, 8, 47 : oleae, id. ib. 2, 2, 57 : juvenis, Col. 7, 3, 6…

quinquennĭum.opening: quinquennis , a period of five years , five years (class.): CENSORES MAGISTRATVM QVINQVENNIVM HABENTO, Cic. Leg. 3, 3, 7 : tria quinquennia, i. e. fifteen years, Ov. M. 4, 292 : duo, id. ib. 12, 584 .

quinquĕ-partītus.opening: ( ), , adj. partio , divided into five parts , fivefold , quinquepartite (rare but class.): argumentatio (al. quinquepertita), Cic. Inv. 1, 34, 59 .— Adv. : , in a fivefold manner , fivefold (post-Aug.), Plin. 25, 6,…

quinquĕpĕdal.opening: quinquepedalis , a five-foot measure , a rod five feet long , Mart. 14, 92 in lemm.

quinquĕ-pĕdālis.opening: adj. , of five feet (post-class.): terminus, Hyg. Limit. p. 212 Goes.

quinqueplex.opening: adj. quinqueplico , for quincuplex, fivefold : quinqueplex, πεντάπλους, Gloss. Vet.

quinquĕ-prīmi.opening: (and separated, ), , , the five principal men in a city , after the magistracy in the colonies and municipia; transl. of πεντάπρωτοι : magistratus et quinqueprimi evocantur, Cic. Verr. 2, 3, 28, § 68 .

quinquĕrēmis.opening: adj. quinque-remus : decem quinqueremes naves, having five banks of oars, Liv. 41, 9, 1 .—As subst. : , , , a ship or galley having five banks of oars , a quinquereme (class.): in quinqueremi, Cic. Verr. 2, 4, 46, § 103…

quinquēres.opening: vox hibr., from quinque-ἐρέσσω , a vessel having five banks of oars , a quinquereme : bieris, trieris, quatrieris, quinqueris, hexeris, hepteris, penteris, Not. Tir. p. 177 .

quinquertĭum.opening: quinque-ars , the five sorts of bodily exercises for youth (discus, cursus, saltus, lucta, jaculatio): quinquertium vocabant antiqui, quem Graeci πένταθλον . . . Livius quoque (Andron.) ipsos athletas sic nominat:…

quinquessis.opening: quinque-as , five asses (post-class.): sed tum quinarius quinquessis valebat, App. ap. Prisc. p. 708 P.

quinquĕ-vertex.opening: adj. , having five summits , five-peaked (post-class.): urbs, Jul. Val. Rer. Gest. Alex. M. 1, 29 .

quinquĕvir.opening: ( .), , , usu. in plur. : , , vir , board of five , the quinquevirs , a board or commission of five men for any official function. Thus, five commissioners , For the apportionment of lands, Cic. Agr. 2, 7, 7 :…

quinquĕvĭrālīcĭus.opening: adj. quinqueviri , of or belonging to the quinquevirs , Inscr. Grut. 395 .

quinquĕvĭrālis.opening: ( .), , adj. id. , belonging to the quinquevirs , Cod. Th. 9, 1, 13; Cassiod. Var. 4, 23 .

quinquĕvĭrātus.opening: ( .), , id. , the office or dignity of a quinquevir , the quinquevirate : quinqueviratum accipere, Cic. Prov. Cons. 17, 41 .

quinquĭens.opening: adv. quinque , five times : quinquiens quinque numerare, Cato, R. R. 156 : absolutus est, Cic. Phil. 11, 5, 11 : quinquiens miliens, five thousand, Plin. 2, 23, 21, § 85 .

quinquĭfĭdus.opening: adj. quinquefindo , five-cleft , quinquifid (post-class.): tela, Ven. 5, 6 praef.

quinquĭplĭco.opening: v. a. quinqueplico , to make fivefold , to quintuplicate : magistratus, Tac. A. 2, 36 fin. † * , , v. a. , to expiate , purify by religious rites : quinquatrus a quinquando, id est lustrando, Charis. p. 62 P. dub.

quintădĕcĭmāni.opening: quintusdecimus , the soldiers of the fifteenth legion , the men of the fifteenth , Tac. H. 4, 36 ; id. A. 1, 23 .

quintānus.opening: adj. quintus , of or belonging to the fifth , viz., Of or belonging to the fifth rank or order , the fifth in order : nonae quintanae dicuntur, quae quinto mensis die veniunt: sicut septimanae, quae septimo, that fall…

quintārĭus.opening: adj. id. , of or belonging to five , containing five : quintarius numerus, i. e. five sixths , taking the number six as a whole, Vitr. 3, 1 : limes, that encloses five centuriae, Hyg. Limit. p. 158 Goes.

quintĭceps.opening: adj. , having five peaks , five-peaked : Cespius mons quinticeps, an ancient formula in Varr. L. L. 5 , §§ 50, 52, and 54 Müll.

Quintīlis.opening: ( ), , , with and without mensis [quintus], the fifth month (counting from March), afterwards, in honor of Julius Cæsar, called Julius, July , Suet. Caes. 76 ; Varr. L. L. 6, § 34 Müll.: mense Quintili, Cic. Att. 14, 7,…

Quintĭlĭus.opening: ( ), , , ( ), , , the name of a Roman gens. Thus, Quintilius Varus, proconsul of Syria , afterwards commander of the Romans in Germany , defeated by Arminius , Vell. 2, 117, 2 ; Suet. Tib. 17 ; Tac. A. 1, 3 ; Flor. 4,…

Quintĭpor.opening: Quintus-puer , a name for slaves , of frequent occurrence, Varr. ap. Non. 448, 15 ; cf. Marcipor and Fest. p. 257 Müll.

Quintĭus.opening: ( ), , , the name of a Roman gens. Thus, L. Quintius Cincinnatus, Liv. 3, 26, 8 sq. — T. Quintius Flaminius, Liv. 32, 10, 7 .— Hence, ( ), , adj. , of or belonging to a Quintius , Quintian : in Quintiā gente, Liv. 3, 12…

quintuplex.opening: adj. quintus-plico , fivefold , quintuple (post-class.): salarium, Vop. Prob. 7 .

quintus.opening: (old form , Plaut. Trin. 2, 4, 123 ), , num. adj. quinque , the fifth : quarta invidia, quinta ambitio, Plaut. Pers. 4, 4, 8 : locus, Cic. Inv. 1, 53, 102 ; 1, 55, 107 : natura, id. Tusc. 1, 17, 41 : quinta pars,…

Quintus.opening: , and , , , Roman prænomen; the former usually abbreviated Q.: Quintus Arrius, Cic. Mil. 17, 46 : Q. Scaevola, id. Phil. 8, 10, 31 .—Quinta, Cic. Cael. 14, 34 ; id. Har. Resp. 13, 27 ; Liv. 29, 14, 12 .

quintus-dĕcĭmus.opening: num. adj. , the fifteenth (class.): locus, Cic. Inv. 1, 54, 105 : quintisdecimis castris, Liv. 45, 33 fin. : in libro quintodecimo, Gell. 1, 16, 11 ; often separately: quinto decimo Kal. Dec., Col. 11, 2, 88 ; and…

quippe.opening: adv. and conj. [quī-pe], a particle of corroboration, similar to nempe (from nam-pe), surely , certainly , to be sure , by all means , indeed , in fact. Recte igitur diceres te restituisse? Quippe: quid enim facilius…

quippĭ-ni.opening: ( ), adv. quippeni , why not? or, affirmatively, certainly , to be sure , by all means (ante- and post-class.), Plaut. Men. 5, 9, 50 ; id. Poen. 3, 4, 21 ; 28 ; 30 ; App. M. 9, p. 229, 15 : Chr. Quid? illam meretricemne…

quī-qui.opening: pron. indef. , for quisquis, whosoever (very rare): quiqui est, Plaut. Aul. 4, 10, 45 .

Quĭrīna.opening: a Roman tribe : Quirina tribus a Curensibus Sabinis appellationem videtur traxisse, Fest. p. 254 Müll.; Cic. Quint. 6, 24 ; id. Fam. 8, 8, 5 and 6; Inscr. Grut. 56, 11 et saep.

Quĭrīnālis.opening: ( abl. QVIRINALE, Kalend. in lnscr. Orell. 2, p. 396), adj. Quirinus . Of or belonging to Quirinus ( Romulus ), Quirinal : Quirinalis flamen, priest of Romulus, Varr. L. L. 7, § 45 Müll.: lituus, such as Romulus bore…

Quĭrīnĭāna.opening: and , a kind of apple , Cato, R. R. 7 ; Varr. R. R. 1, 59 ; Plin. 15, 14, 15, § 50 ; Macr. S. 2, 15, 2 .

Quĭrīnus.opening: adj. 1. Quirinus, I. , of or belonging to Quirinus , i. e. Romulus , Quirinal ( poet. ): spolia ex umeris Quirinis (al. Quirini), Prop. 4 (5), 10, 11. collis, i. e. the Quirinal, Ov. M. 14, 836 .—Hence, as subst. : , q.…

quĭris.opening: or Sabine , a spear : sive quod hasta curis (al. quiris) est dicta Sabinis, Ov. F. 2, 477 .

Quĭrīs.opening: , and mostly plur. , , (or tum, Aus. Prof. 22, 9 ), Cures . Originally, the inhabitants of the Sabine town Cures, the Quirites (very rare): prisci Quirites, Verg. A. 7, 710 Serv.: veteres illi Sabini Quirites, Col.…

quĭrītātĭo.opening: quirito , a plaintive cry , a scream , shriek : quiritatio facta, Liv. 33, 28 .

quĭrītātus.opening: id. , a plaintive cry , a wail , scream , shriek (post - Aug.): ululatus feminarum, infantium quiritatus, Plin. Ep. 6, 20, 14 : lamentabiles, Val. Max. 9, 2, 1 ; 6, 2, 8 .

quĭrīto.opening: (in a dep. form: de Fenestellā quiritatur, Varr. ap. Diom. p. 377 P.), v. n. and a. [Quirites, i. e. to cry : pro fidem, Quirites!], orig., to implore the aid of the Quirites or Roman citizens; hence, in gen. Neutr. ,…

quirrīto.opening: v. n. , to utter the natural sound of the boar, to grunt : quirritant verres, Auct Carm. Philom. 55.

quis.opening: pron. indef. As subst. Alone, any one , any body , any thing; some one , somebody , something : aperite, heus! Simoni me adesse, quis nunciate, Plaut. Ps. 5, 1, 37 : simplicior quis, et est, etc., Hor. S. 1, 3, 63 :…

quisnam.opening: pron. interrog. [quis-nam], who , which , what pray (class.). In direct interrogation: quisnam igitur tuebitur P. Scipionis memoriam mortui? Cic. Verr. 2, 4, 36, § 80 : sed earum artificem quem? Quemnam? id. ib. 2, 4, 3…

quispĭam.opening: , and subst. quidpiam or quippiam, pron. indef. , any one , any body , any thing , any; some one , something , some : quispiam quin significet aliquis, et quaepiam aliquae, similiterque alia ejusdem generis, ut dubium…

quis-quam.opening: (old form QVIQVAM, S. C. Bacch.), quaequam, quicquam or quidquam ( abl. masc. quoquam, very rare, Liv. 3, 57, 6 Weissenb. ad loc., and 34, 35, 9; Suet. Caes. 59 ), pron. indef. , any , any one , any body , any thing ,…

quis-que.opening: , and subst. quicque (quidque), pron. indef. , whoever or whatever it be , each , every , every body , every one , every thing (prop. of more than two persons or things; cf. uterque): non tute incommodam rem, ut quaeque…

quisquĭlĭae.opening: ( neutr. collat. form , , Petr. 75 ; cf.: quisquilia, σκύβαλα, Gloss. Philox.) [prob. from quisque, all sorts of things, odds and ends]. Lit. , the waste or refuse of any thing, the droppings of trees , sweepings ,…

quis-quis.opening: , and subst. quicquid, quidquid, pron. rel. , whoever , whosoever , whatever , whatsoever , every one who , each , every , all : hostem qui feriet, mihi erit Carthaginiensis, Quisquis erit, Enn. ap. Cic. Balb. 22, 51…

quisquis-lĭbet.opening: , quidquid-libet, pron. indef. , whoever it may be , whatever it may be (late Lat.): quidquidlibet dederis pro te, vile est, Salv. Avar. 3, 18 .

quī-vīs.opening: ( abl. quīvis, Ter. Ad. 2, 3, 1 ), and subst. quidvis, pron. indef. (separated: quod genus vis propagabis, Cato, R. R. 52 ), who or what you please , any whatever , any one , any thing : Juppiter non minus, quam vostrum…

quīvis-cumque.opening: pron. indef. , who or what you please , any whatsoever you will , each , every ( poet. ): nec repentis itum cujusviscumque animantis Sentimus, Lucr. 3, 388 : quoviscumque loco potes, at whatever place you please, Mart.…

Quiza.opening: a town or fortress of Mauritania , near the present Giza , in Oran , Plin. 5, 2, 1, § 19 ; Mel. 1, 6 .

quō.opening: adv. prop. dat. or abl. of qui . Where (rare but class.): respondit, se nescire, quo loci esset, Cic. Att. 8, 10 : quo loci illa nasceretur, id. Div. 2, 66, 135 : mitte sectari rosa quo locorum Sera moretur, Hor. C. 1,…

quŏ-ad.opening: (monosyl., Lucr. 2, 849 ; Hor. S. 2, 3, 91 ; collat. form , Varr. R. R. 1, 1, 2 ; Inscr. Fabr. p. 641, 357 ; cf. Cardin. Dipl. p. 22, 30, and n. 337, and Cavedon. Marm. Moden. p. 243), adv. orig. quod-ad = ad quod , how…

quŏăd-usque.opening: until that (post-class.), Aug. Civ. Dei , 1, 1; Lact. 4, 12, 17 ; Vulg. Cant. 2, 7 ; id. Act. 7, 18 (but in Varr. L. L. 5, 2 ; Suet. Caes. 14 ; Tac. A. 14, 58 , a false read.).

quō-circā.opening: (separated: quo, bone, circa, Hor. S. 2, 6, 95 ; old form ; v. the letter Q ), conj. , for which reason , wherefore (rare but class.), Varr. L. L. 9, 59 : quocirca bene apud majores nostros senatus decrevit, ut, etc.,…

quō-cumque.opening: (in tmesi: quo nos cumque feret, Hor. C. 1, 7, 25 : quo res cumque cadent, Verg. A. 2, 709 : quo ea me cumque ducet, Cic. Tusc. 2, 5, 15 ), adv. , to whatever place , whithersoever (class): quocumque venerint, Cic.…

quod.opening: , another orthogr. for quot, v. h. v.

quōdam-mŏdo.opening: (in tmesi: quodam tamen modo, Quint. 1, 12, 5 ), adv. quidam-modus , in a certain manner , in a measure (class.): quodammodo latebat, Nep. Eum. 7, 3 : voce, motu, formā etiam magnifica et generosa quodammodo, Cic. Brut.…

Quod-sĕmĕl-arrĭpĭdes.opening: quod-semel-arripio , That-snatches-onceides , a comically formed proper name, Plaut. Pers. 4, 6, 22 .

quoi.opening: , i. q. cui, v. 1. qui init.

quōjas.opening: or , , i. q. cujas or cujatis, Plaut. Poen. prol. 109 ; 5, 2, 33 et saep.

quō-lĭbet.opening: adv. quilibet , whither it pleases , to any place whatever ( poet. ): gubernaculum contorquet quolibet, Lucr. 4, 902 : quolibet ire, Ov. Tr. 3, 8, 22 .

quō-mĭnus.opening: conj. , that not , from , after verbs of hindering, preventing, etc.; v. minus under parvus.

quō-mŏdŏ.opening: , or (in tmesi: quo tu me modo voles esse, Plaut. Cist. 1, 1, 48 ; Curt. 6, 4, 14 ), adv. , in what manner , in what way , how. Interrog. : Quomodo? Quantum poposcerit Apronius? Cic. Verr. 2, 3, 10, § 25 : Maecenas…

quōmŏdŏ-cumquĕ.opening: ( ), adv. Lit. , in what manner soever , howsoever (class.): quomodocumque dicitur, intellegi tamen potest, Cic. Fin. 5, 11, 30 .— Transf. , be it as it may , in any way whatever : sed tamen quomodocumque, quamquam…

quōmŏdŏ-lĭbet.opening: adv. , howsoever (eccl. Lat.): qui quomodolibet vixerint, Aug. Civ. Dei , 21, 19.

quōmŏdŏ-nam.opening: adv. , in what manner pray? how? (class.): quomodonam, mi frater, de nostris versibus Caesar? Cic. Q. Fr. 2, 16, 5 .

quō-nam.opening: adv. Whither pray? (class.): quo tu te agis? Char. Quonam, nisi domum? Plaut. Trin. 4, 3, 71 ; id. Merc. 5, 2, 16 : eam si nunc sequor, quonam? Cic. Att. 8, 3, 5 : quonam haec omnia, nisi ad suam perniciem pertinere?…

quondam.opening: (CONDAM, Inscr. Rein. p. 543 ), adv. quom = cum, with the demonstr. part. dam . At a certain time , at one time , once , heretofore , formerly : verum tempestas, memini, quondam fuit, cum, etc., Plaut. Truc. 2, 4, 29 :…

quŏn-ĭam.opening: adv. quom = cum, and jam , since now , since then , since , seeing that , because , whereas (quoniam gives a ground or reason, quod and quia give the determining cause or reason). With indic. , stating a fact: quoniam…

quō-pĭam.opening: adv. quo , to any place , whithersoever ( poet. ): quopiam devorti, Plaut. Most. 4, 2, 50 : iturane, Thais, quopiam es? Ter. Eun. 3, 2, 9 .

quō-quam.opening: adv. To any place , whithersoever (rare but class.): ut hanc ne quoquam mitteret, nisi ad se, Plaut. As. 3, 3, 45 ; Ter. Ad. 2, 1, 16 ; id. Hec. 4, 1, 50 : meare diversa, Lucr. 1, 428 Lachm.: neque se quoquam movit ex…

quŏque.opening: conj. , also , too (subjoined to the emphatic word in a clause) [etym. dub.; perh. for quomque; v. Rib. Lat. Part. p. 23 sq. ]: quă de causa Helvetii quoque reliquos Gallos virtute praecedunt, Caes. B. G. 1, 1 : me…

quō-quō.opening: adv. quisquis , to whatever place , whithersoever (class.): quoquo ibo, Plaut. Aul. 3, 3, 1 : quoquo venias, id. ib. 3, 5, 31 ; id. Curc. 5, 3, 22 : quoquo hic spectabit, eo tu spectato simul, id. Ps. 3, 2, 69 : quoquo…

quōquō-mŏdo.opening: adv. quisquis-modus , in what way soever , howsoever : quoquomodo se res habeat, Cic. Fam. 1, 5, 2 : tu quoquomodo hominem investiges velim, in every possible way, id. Q. Fr. 1, 2, 4 : tu cum esses praetor renuntiatus…

quōquō-versus.opening: ( ) or (QVOQVEVERSVS, Inscr. Grut. 207 , lin. 19; 21; 26; 801, 12) [quoquo-versus], in every direction , every way (class.): legatos quoquoversus dimittere, Caes. B. G. 3, 23, 2 ; 7, 4 ; 14 ; Cic. Phil. 9, 7, 17 : pedes…

quorsum.opening: and , adv. quovorsus or -um , to what place , whitherward , whither , Lit. : nescio hercle, neque unde eam, neque quorsum eam, Ter. Eun. 2, 3, 14 : quaerit quorsus potissimum in praedam superne sese ruat, App. Flor. 1,…

quŏt.opening: (in MSS. often ), adj. plur. indecl. [kindr. with Sanscr. kati, quot, like tot, Sanscr. tati]. Lit. , how many , as many , as : quot sunt? Sce. Totidem, quot ego et tu sumus, Plaut. Rud. 2, 7, 6 ; id. Most. 3, 1, 114 :…

quot-cumque.opening: adv. , how many soever , as many as (rare): quotcumque senatus creverit, tot sunto, Cic. Leg. 3, 3, 8 : tot ... quotcumque, Manil. 4, 315 .

quŏtēni.opening: num. distrib. adj. [quot], how many (class.): is ita partes fecit, nescio quotenorum jugerum, Cic. Att. 12, 33, 1 : quotenos suae aetatis annos Christus absolverit, Ven. Carm. 6, 5.

quŏtennis.opening: adj. quot-annus , of how many years , how many years old (eccl. Lat.): quotenne vinum sit, Aug. Quantit. Anim. 19 .

quŏtīdĭō.opening: ( ), adv. for cottidie, daily , Q. Caepio ap. Charis. p. 174 P.

quŏtĭens.opening: or , adv. quot , how often , how many times , as often as (class.): o quotiens et quae nobis Galatea locuta est! Verg. E. 3, 72 : quotiens et quot nominibus a Syracusanis statuas auferes? Cic. Verr. 2, 2, 59, § 145 ;…

quŏtĭens-cumquĕ.opening: adv. , how often soever , as often soever as (class.): quotienscumque dico, totiens mihi videor in judicium venire, etc., Cic. Clu. 18, 51 ; id. Tusc. 3, 34, 84 ; id. Rosc. Com. 6, 18 ; Nep. Eum. 5, 7 : hoc facite…

quŏtĭens-quĕ.opening: ( ), adv. for quotienscumque, how often soever , as often soever as (post-Aug.): quotiensque mel remediis adhibetur, Col. 6, 17, 8 .

quot-lĭbet.opening: adv. , as many as pleases , as many as one will , Hyg. Astron. 1, 6 .

quot-quŏt.opening: adj. indecl. [quot]. Lit. , how many soever , as many soever as (class.): si leges duae aut si plures aut quotquot erunt conservari non possint, Cic. Inv. 2, 49, 145 ; Cat. 42, 1 : quotquot eunt dies, i. e. daily, Hor.…

quŏtŭmus.opening: adj. quotus , of what number (Plautin.): quotumas aedes dixerit, ego incerto scio, Plaut. Ps. 4, 2, 7 : quotumo die, on what day (by number)? id. ib. 4, 7, 77 .† * , , adj. quotus-plico , how many fold , how many times…

quŏtus.opening: adj. quot , which or what in number , order , etc.; of what number , how many (class.): quotus erit iste denarius, qui non sit ferendus? Cic. Verr. 2, 3, 94, § 220 : scire velim, chartis pretium quotus arroget annus,…

quŏtus-cumque.opening: adj. , whatsoever in number , order , etc.; how great or small soever ( poet. ): moverit e votis pars quotacumque deos, Tib. 2, 6, 54 (in Ov. H. 13, 60 , the true reading is quota quemque).

quŏtus-lĭbet.opening: adj. , of what number : pars, Claud. Mam. Stat. Anim. 1, 18 .

quŏ-usquē.opening: (also separated, quo enim usque, Cic. Phil. 3, 1, 3 : quo te spectabimus usque, Mart. 2, 64, 9 ), adv. Of time, until what time , till when , how long (class.): De. Quousque? Li. Usque ad mortem volo, Plaut. As. 1, 1,…

quō-vīs.opening: adv. quivis , to any place whatever ( poet. ): cibo perduci poteris quovis. Plaut. Most. 4, 2, 7 : quovis admittunt aves, id. As. 2, 1, 11 .—With gentium : immo abeat quovis gentium, let him go anywhere in the world,…

R.opening: or (sc. littera) The seventeenth letter of the Latin alphabet, which derives its form from the Greek P, but is not, like that, aspirated. Thus Burrus, arrabo, were originally written for Πύρρος, ἀρραβών. In words…

răbĭdus.opening: adj. 1. rabo , raving , furious , enraged , savage , fierce , mad , rabid (as adj. mostly poet. and in post-Aug. prose; cf.: furens, furiosus, insanus): canes, Lucr. 5, 892 ; Plin. 29, 5, 32, § 98 ; Sen. Ira, 1, 1, 6 ;…

răbĭes.opening: ( gen. rabies, Lucr. 4, 1083 ; the other cases do not occur), rabio . Lit. , rage , madness (cf.: furor, insania). Of dogs, Col. 7, 12, 14 ; Plin. 7, 15, 13, § 64 ; 29, 5, 32, § 99 .— Of other animals, Col. 6, 35 ;…

răbĭo.opening: v. n. etym. dub. , to rave , be mad ( poet. and in post-Aug. prose), Varr. and Caecil. ap. Non. 40, 2 sq. : oculis rabere visa es ardentibus, Poëta ap. Cic. Div. 1, 31, 66 ; id. Imp. Pomp. 5, 207 ; 5, 222 ; Sen. Ep. 29,…

răbĭōsŭlus.opening: adj. dim. [rabiosus], a little rabid : litterae, Cic. Fam. 7, 16 .

răbĭōsus.opening: adj. rabies , raving , fierce , mad , rabid (rare but class.; syn.: furiosus, furibundus): canis, Hor. Ep. 2, 2, 75 ; Plin. 29, 5, 32, § 98 : homo, Plaut. Capt. 3, 4, 15 : fortitudo, * Cic. Tusc. 4, 22, 50 : rabiosa…

Răbīrĭus.opening: the name of a Roman gens. Thus, C. Rabirius, a tribune of the people; and, C. Rabirius Postumus, a knight; both of them defended by Cicero in orations still extant.— An indifferent philosophical writer , Cic. Ac. 1, 2,…

Rabocentus.opening: a Bessic prince , put to death by L. Piso , Cic. Pis. 34 .

răbŭla.opening: 1. rabo , a brawling , wrangling advocate , a pettifogger (cf.: clamator, declamator): non declamatorem aliquem de ludo aut rabulam de foro ... quaerimus, Cic. Or. 15, 47 ; with causidicus and proclamator , id. de Or.…

răbŭlāna.opening: an unknown kind of pitch [perh. ravus, grayish], Plin. 14, 19, 24, § 120 .

răbŭlātus.opening: rabula , a brawling , wrangling , pettifogging , Mart. Cap. 2, 46 Graev. dub. (Kopp, § 213, reboatu).

răbuscŭla.opening: an unknown species of vine [perh. ravus, grayish], Plin. 14, 3, 4, § 42 .

racco.opening: v. n. , to utter the natural cry of the tiger , Auct. Carm. Philom. 49 (al. rancant).

răcēmārĭus.opening: adj. racemus , of or belonging to grape-stalks , stalky : pampini, that bear nothing but stalks, unfruitful, Col. 3, 18, 4 .

răcēmātĭo.opening: f [id.], the gleaning of a vineyard , a grape-gleaning (cf. spicilegium), Tert. Apol. 35 .

răcēmātus.opening: adj. id. , having clusters or berries , Plin. 18, 7, 10, § 54 .

răcēmĭfer.opening: adj. racemusfero , cluster-bearing , clustering; a poet. epithet: uvae, Ov M. 3, 666; and in a broader sense: racemifer Bacchus, crowned with clusters, id. ib. 15, 413 ; cf.: capilli (Bacchi), id. F. 6, 483 .

răcēmor.opening: v. dep. a. [racemus], to glean; trop., to treat of in a supplementary manner , Varr. R. R. 3, 9, 1 .

răcēmōsus.opening: adj. id. , full of clusters , clustering (Plin.): pomum, Plin. 13, 4, 7, § 30: flos, id. 13, 6, 12, § 54 .— Sup. : uvae, Plin. 14, 3, 4, § 40 .

răcēmus.opening: ῥάξ, ῥαγός . Lit. , the stalk of a cluster of grapes and similar plants: alia (poma) racemis dependent, ut uvae, palmae, Plin. 15, 28, 34, § 115 ; cf. id. 16, 26, 48, § 112 ; 14, 3, 4, § 43 : sunt et mora cruenta, et…

Racilius.opening: the name of a Roman gens; e. g. L. Racilius, a tribune of the people, Cic. Q. Fr. 2, 6, 5 ; Cic. Verr. 2, 2, 12, § 31 ; id. Fam. 1, 7, 2 . — Racilia, wife of Cincinnatus , Liv. 3, 26, 9 .

rădĭātĭlis.opening: adj. radio , emitting rays , radiant : umbra, Ven. Fort. 2, 286.

rădĭātĭo.opening: id. , a glittering , shining , a beamy lustre , radiation (postAug.): marmoris, Plin. 36, 5, 4, § 32 : stellarum, Jul. Firm. Math. 1, 4. — Plur. , Arn. 6, 208 .

rādīcālis.opening: adj. radix , having roots (post-class.), Aug. c. Faust. 13, 12.

rādīcesco.opening: v. inch. [radix], to take root , Sen. Ep. 86 fin.

rādīcĭtus.opening: adv. id. , with the roots , by the roots (class.). Lit. : effodere herbas malas, Cato, R. R. 50 : concidere rosetum, Varr. R. R. 1, 35, 1 ; Cat. 64, 288 : evellere arborem, Suet. Vesp. 5 : eximere, Col. 4, 33, 4 :…

rādīco.opening: v. n. , and , , v. dep. n. [id.], to strike root , take root (post-Aug.). Lit. Form radico, Cassiod. H. E. 2, 6 . — Form radicor: mergi facile radicantur, Col. 4, 2, 2 ; Plin. 13, 4, 8, § 36 ; 18, 7, 10, § 51 al.…

rādīcōsus.opening: adj. id. , full of roots , having many roots : bracchia hederarum, Plin. 16, 34, 62, § 151 .

rādīcŭla.opening: dim. id. . In gen., a small root , rootlet , Cic. Div. 2, 66, 136 ; Col. 5, 5, 5 .— In partic. Fuller ' sweed , soapwort , Plin. 19, 3, 18, § 48 . — A small kind of radish , Col. 4, 8, 1 ; 11, 2, 19 ; Cels. 2, 18 ; 21 ;…

rădĭo.opening: radius . * (Acc. to radius, I. B. 1.) V. a. , to furnish with spokes : rota radiata, Varr. R. R. 3, 5, 15 .— (Acc. to radius, II.) V. a. and (mostly poet. and in post-Aug. prose). Act. , to furnish with beams , make…

rădĭŏlus.opening: dim. radius . * A small , feeble sunbeam , Amm. 28, 4, 18 .— A kind of long olive , Col. 12, 49, 2 .— A plant resembling fern , App. Herb. 83 .

rădĭōsus.opening: adj. id. , emitting many beams , radiant : sol, Plaut. Stich. 2, 2, 41 .

rădĭus.opening: cf.: radix, ramus , a staff , rod. In gen.: acuti radii immissi, stakes, Liv. 33, 5, 11 : ferreus, Plin. 10, 42, 58, § 117 .— In partic. A spoke of a wheel, Plin. 16, 40, 76, § 206 ; Verg. G. 2, 444 ; id. A. 6, 616 ;…

rādix.opening: ( gen. plur. radicium, Cassiod. H. E. 1, 1 ; Jul. Val. Itin. Alex. 32 (75)), Gr. ῥίζα, a root; ῥάδιξ, a shoot or twig; cf. ramus , a root of a plant (cf. stirps). Lit. In gen. (mostly in plur. ): radices agere, to…

rādo.opening: v. a. , to scrape , scratch , shave , rub , or smooth; of the hair, to shave off with a razor (while tondere is to cut off with shears; mostly poet. and in post-Aug. prose; cf. scabo). Lit. : MVLIERES GENAS NE RADVNTO,…

raeda.opening: or (falsely written ), , prob. Celtic: plurima Gallica valuerunt ut raeda ac petorritum, Quint. 1, 5, 57; cf. id. 1, 5, 68 , a travelling-carriage or wagon with four wheels , Varr. ap. Non. 167, 25 ; 451, 17 ; Caes. B.…

raedārĭus.opening: ( ), , adj. raeda , of or belonging to a four-wheeled carriage : mulae, Varr. R. R. 3, 17, 7 .— Hence, subst. : , , A coachman , the driver of a ræda : raedarium occidunt, Cic. Mil. 10, 29 .— A wagon-builder ,…

Raeti.opening: ( ), , , the Rætians , a mountain people north of the Po , between the Danube , the Rhine , and the Lech , Plin. 3, 20, 24, § 133 ; 3, 19, 23, § 130 ; Liv. 5, 33 fin. ; Just. 20, 5, 9 ; Tac. H. 1, 68 ; 3, 5 ; 53 ; Hor.…

Ralla.opening: a Roman surname in the Marcian gens. M. Marcius Ralla, Liv. 29, 11 .— Q. Marcius Ralla, Liv. 34, 52 .

rallum.opening: rado , an instrument for scraping off the earth from the ploughshare , Plin. 18, 19, 49, § 179 .

rallus.opening: adj. dim. [for rarulus, from rarus], thin : tunica, a thin tunic, Plaut. Ep. 2, 2, 46 ; cf. Non. 539, 15 .

rāmāle.opening: ramus , twigs , shoots , sticks , brushwood; very rare in sing. : ut ramale vetus, Pers. 1, 97 .— Usually plur. : , , Ov. M. 8, 644 ; Pers. 5, 59 ; Sen. Ep. 90, 10 ; Tac. A. 13, 58 .

rāmenta.grammar: ōrum i ae n. n. f.
rāmenta.opening: ; less freq. in sing. , , , (collat. form , , , Plaut. Bacch. 3, 4, 15 ; 3, 4, 23 ; id. Rud. 4, 3, 77 ) [rado]. Lit. , what is grated , shaved , or rubbed off; scrapings , shavings , chips , etc. (larger than scobes),…

rāmentōsus.opening: adj. ramentum , full of little bits , full of small pieces (late Lat.), Cael. Aur. Tard. 4, 3 .

rāmĕus.opening: adj. ramus , of or belonging to boughs or branches : fragmenta, i. e. sticks , = ramalia, Verg. G. 4, 303 .

rāmex.opening: id. . (In plur. ) The blood-vessels of the lungs , Plaut. Merc. 1, 27 ; id. Poen. 3, 1, 37 ; Varr. ap. Non. 166, 12 .— ( Sing. and plur. ) A rupture , hernia , varicocele , Cels. 7, 18 ; Plin. 22, 25, 57, § 121 ; 30,…

rāmĭcōsus.opening: adj. ramex , afflicted with hernia , ruptured , Plin. 30, 15, 47, § 136 .

Ramises.opening: (also or ), an ancient king of Egypt , Plin. 36, 8, 14, § 65 ; Tac. A. 2, 60 .

Ramnes.opening: and , , The Latin stock or tribe from whose union with the Taties ( Sabines ) and Luceres ( Etruscans ) sprang the most ancient Roman State; form Ramnes, usually applied to the tribe , Varr. L. L. 5, § 81 Müll.; Liv.…

rāmōsus.opening: adj. ramus , full of boughs , having many branches , branching , branchy. Lit. : arbor, Lucr. 5, 1096 : ilex, Ov. M. 8, 237 ; cf.: domus Silvani, Prop. 4 (5), 4, 5. stipes, Ov. F. 3, 751 . — Comp. : lappago, Plin. 26,…

rāmŭla.opening: ramus , the hoof : equorum, Veg. Vet. 1, 56, 31 (al. ungulae); 2, 58, 4.

rāmŭlōsus.opening: adj. ramulus , full of branching veins : folia, Plin. 16, 24, 38, § 92 .

rāmŭlus.opening: dim. ramus , a little branch or bough , a twig , sprig , Cato, R. R. 101 ; Cic. Div. 1, 54, 123 ; Plin. 24, 15, 81, § 132 ; 27, 12, 88, § 111 al.

rāmus.opening: for rad-mus; Sanscr. root vardh, crescere; cf.: radix, radius , a branch , bough , twig (cf.: surculus, termes). Lit. : in quibus (arboribus) non truncus, non rami, non folia sunt denique, nisi, etc., Cic. de Or. 3, 46,…

rāmuscŭlus.opening: dim. ramus , a little branch or bough , a twig (late Lat. for ramulus), Hier. Ep. 133, 3 ; Vulg. Isa. 18, 5 .

rāna.opening: for racna; cf.: ranco, racco, to roar, cry out; Germ. röcheln; Gr. λακεῖν; v. Cors. Ausspr. 1, p. 636 sq. . A frog , Plin. 11, 37, 65, § 172 ; Ov. M. 6, 381 ; 15, 375 ; Verg. G. 1, 378 ; 3, 431 ; Hor. S. 1, 5, 14 :…

rancens.opening: Part. , stinking , putrid , rancid (ante- and post-class.), Lucr. 3, 719 : axungia, Ser. Samm. 978 .

rancesco.opening: v. inch. n. , to become stinking , grow rancid , Arn. 1, 12 .

rancĭdŭlus.opening: adj. dim. [rancidus] (post-Aug.). Lit. , stinking , rank , rancid : opsonia, Juv. 11, 135 .— Trop. , disgusting , loathsome , offensive : rancidulum quiddam locutus, Pers. 1, 33 ; cf. Mart. 7, 34, 7 .

rancĭdus.opening: adj. ranceo, rancens , stinking , rank , rancid. Lit. : cadavera, Lucr. 6, 1155 : aper, Hor. S. 2, 2, 89 .— Trop. , disgusting , loathsome , offensive : aspectus, Plin. 22, 22, 46, § 92 .— Comp. : quid rancidius, quam,…

rancor.opening: ranceo, rancens . Lit. , a stinking smell or flavor , rankness , rancidity (late Lat.), Pall. 1, 20, 2 ; 11, 10, 2 . — Trop. , an old grudge , rancor , Hier. Ep. 13, 1 .

rānŭla.opening: dim. rana . Lit. , a little frog , a tadpole , App. M. 9, p. 233, 11 . — Transf. , a little swelling on the tongue of cattle , Veg. 4, 5, 1 al.

rānuncŭlus.opening: dim. rana . Lit. , a little frog , a tadpole , porwigle , Cic. Div. 1, 9, 15 .— Transf. , jocosely, of the inhabitants of Ulubrae (as residing in the neighborhood of marshes), Cic. Fam. 7, 18, 3 .— A medicinal plant ,…

rāpācĭa.opening: rapum , turnip tops , Plin. 18, 13, 34, § 127 ; v. rapicius.

răpācĭda.opening: rapax , robber , a comically formed patronymic, Plaut. Aul. 2, 7, 8 .

răpācĭtas.opening: id. , greediness , rapacity : quis in rapacitate avarior, Cic. Cael. 6, 13 ; Suet. Tit. 7 ; Just. 38, 7, 8 ; Mart. 6, 72, 1 : dirae filius es rapacitatis, id. 12, 53, 7 .

răpax.opening: adj. rapio , grasping , greedy of plunder , rapacious. Lit. (class.; syn. furax): vos rapaces, vos praedones, Plaut. Men. 5, 7, 26 ; id. Pers. 3, 3, 6 : olim furunculus, nunc vero etiam rapax, Cic. Pis. 27, 66 ; so with…

răphănīnus.opening: adj. , = ῥαφάνινος, of radishes , made from radishes : oleum, Plin. 23, 4, 49, § 94 .

răphănos agrĭa.opening: , = ῥάφανος ἀγρία, a sort of wild - radish , Plin. 26, 8, 46, § 72 .

rāpīcĭus.opening: adj. rapum , of or belonging to rapes or turnips , rape- , turnip- : coles, Cato, R. R. 35, 2 : semen, rape-seed, id. ib. 134, 1 .— As subst. : , , (sc. caules), turnip-shoots , young turnipplants , Plin. 18, 13, 34, §…

răpĭdĭtas.opening: rapidus , swiftness of a stream that carries all before it; velocity , rapidity (only in the foll. passages): fluminis, Caes. B. C. 1, 62, 2 ; id. B. G. 4, 17, 2 ; Front. Strat. 1, 6, 2 .

răpĭdŭlus.opening: adj. dim. [id.], swift , rapid : sonitus, Mart. Cap. 8, § 804 .

răpĭdus.opening: adj. rapio , tearing away , seizing. Lit. (very rare, and only poet. ): ferae, Ov. H. 10, 96 ; 11, 111 (but in Lucr. 4, 712 , the correct read. is rabidi leones).—Of hunting-dogs: agmen, a tearing, fierce pack, Ov. M.…

răpīna.opening: rapio . Robbery , plundering , pillage , rapine (class.; in anteAug. prose, as also in Tac., Suet., Verg., and Hor., only in plur. ; syn. praeda): nihil cogitant, nisi caedes, nisi incendia, nisi rapinas, Cic. Cat. 2,…

rāpīna.opening: rapum . A turnip-field , Col. 11, 2, 71 .— Transf. , a turnip , rape , Cato, R. R. 5, 8 ; 35, 2 ; Inscr. Fratr. Arv. 41, 30 (2270 ap. Orell.).

răpīnātĭo.opening: 1. rapina , plundering , rapine , pillage : rapinationes facere, M. Aur. ap. Front. 2, 15 .

răpīnātor.opening: id. , a robber , only Lucil. and Varr. ap. Non. 129, 29 , and 167, 20 sq.

răpĭo.opening: (old perf. subj. rapsit, Cic. Leg. 2, 9, 22 ; part. perf. fem. ex raptabus, Gell. ap. Charis. p. 39 P.), v. a. root ἁρπ; Gr. ἅρπη, a bird of prey, ἁρπαγή, ἁρπάζω; Lat. rapidus, rapax, rapina, etc.; cf. Sanscr. lup-,…

răpo.opening: rapio , a robber (anteclass.; v. raptor), Varr. ap. Non. 26, 32 .

rapso.opening: , i. q. rapto, to snatch or hurry away : RAPSATA, Inscr. Orell. 4859 .

raptim.opening: adv. raptus, from rapio , by snatching or hurrying away , i. e., Violently , greedily , rapaciously (very rare): ludunt raptim pila, Nov. ap. Non. 96, 20 : semine raptim avium fame devorato, Plin. 17, 14, 22, § 99 .—Far…

raptĭo.opening: rapio , a carrying off , abduction , ravishing , rape (ante- and postclass.): in raptione affuisse, * Ter. Ad. 3, 3, 2 : Proserpinae, Arn. 5, 183 : Helenae, Aus. Per. Iliad. prooem. § 4.

raptĭto.opening: v. freq. [id.], acc. to Gell. 9, 6 fin.

rapto.opening: ( inf. pass. paragog. raptarier, Enn. Trag. 192 ), , v. freq. a. id. , to seize and carry off , to snatch , drag , or hurry away (mostly poet. ). Lit. In gen.: vidi Hectorem curru quadrijugo raptarier, dragged along ,…

raptor.opening: rapio , one who seizes by force , a robber , plunderer , abductor , ravisher (only poet. and in post-Aug. prose; syn.: praedo, direptor, praedator). Lit. With gen. : (fluvius) rapidus raptori pueri subduxit pedem,…

raptōrĭus.opening: adj. id. , that serves for dragging away : machinamentum, Cael. Aur. Tard. 3, 6 fin.

raptrix.opening: raptor , she that carries off , ravishes : aquila (that carried off Ganymede), Hier. Chron.

raptum.opening: robbery , rapine , plunder , etc., v. rapio, I. O. 1. fin.

raptus.opening: rapio , a carrying off by force. In gen. (very rare): Inoo lacerata est altera raptu, violent rending, Ov. M. 3, 722 : runcinarum, Plin. 16, 42, 82, § 225 : lenes cucurbitarum, Cael. Aur. Acut. 1, 11 .—Esp. a jerking ,…

rāpŭlum.opening: dim. rapum , a little turnip or rape , Hor. S. 2, 2, 43 ; 2, 8, 8 .

rāpum.opening: akin to Gr. ῥάφη, ῥαφάνη (collat. form , , , Col. 11, 3, 16 ; Scrib. Comp. 176 ; 177 ), a turnip , rape : Brassica rapa, Linn.; Varr. R. R. 1, 59, 4 ; Col. 2, 10, 22 sq. ; Plin. 18, 13, 33, § 125 ; flung at one as an…

rārē-făcĭo.opening: (written also separately ), , v. a. rarus , to make thin or rare , to rarefy (Lucret.): rarefieri, Lucr. 1, 648 : rarefacta, id. 2, 1139 ; 3, 442 : rareque facit, id. 6, 233 ; 870 .

rāresco.opening: v. inch. n. [rarus], to grow thin , lose its density , to become rare , be rarefied ( poet. and in post-Aug. prose). Lit. : fulgit item cum rarescunt quoque nubila caeli, Lucr. 6, 214 ; cf. id. 6, 513 ; Stat. S. 1, 2,…

rārĭ-pĭlus.opening: adj. rarus , thinhaired : caprinum pecus, Col. 1 , praef. § 26.

rārĭtas.opening: id. , the state of being loose or not dense , looseness of texture , distance apart (good prose). Lit. : in pulmonibus inest raritas quaedam et assimilis spongiis mollitudo ad hauriendum spiritum aptissima, Cic. N. D.…

rārĭtūdo.opening: id. , looseness (rare form for raritas): rete a raritudine (dictum), Varr. L. L. 5, § 130 Müll.: mediocri raritudine terra, Col. Arb. 3, 7 .

rārus.opening: adj. etym. dub.; cf. Sanscr. root rah-, to abandon , having wide interstices between its parts , of a loose texture , not thick or dense , thin (opp. densus; freq. and class.). Lit. : denseri poterunt ignes, rarique…

rāsāmen.opening: rado , that which is scraped or shaved off , a scraping , shaving , Marc. Emp. 1 med.

rāsĭlis.opening: adj. id. , scraped , shaved , smoothed , polished , smooth , = levigatus (mostly poet. ): torno rasile buxum, Verg. G. 2, 449 : foris, Cat. 61, 168 : fibula, Ov. M. 8, 318 ; Stat. Th. 7, 658 : calathi, Ov. H. 9, 76 :…

rāsĭo.opening: id. , a shaving , scraping : capitis, Cael. Aur. Tard. 1, 4 : strigilis rasio est adhibenda corporibus, id. ib. 4, 7 .

rāsis.opening: a kind of raw pitch , Col. 12, 20, 6 .

rāsĭto.opening: v. freq. a. , to shave often , to shave (post-Aug. and very rare): faciem cotidie, Suet. Oth. 12 : barbam, Gell. 3, 4, 3 .

rāsōres.grammar: fidicines dicti, quia videntur chordas ictu radere
rāsōres.opening: (qs. scrapers of the strings ), Paul. ex Fest. p. 275, 2 Müll.; cf. Fest. p. 274, 13 ib.

rasta.opening: Germ.; O. H. Germ. rasta or rast, rest; Goth. rasta, a mile; cf. the Slav. werst , a German measure of a mile (late Lat.), Hier. in Joel, 3, 18.

rastellus.opening: dim. rastrum , a hoe , rake , mattock , Varr. L. L. 5, 31, 38 ; id. R. R. 1, 49, 1 ; Col. 2, 12, 6 (for which, id. 2, 10, 27 , rastra), Suet. Ner. 19 .

rastrārĭus.opening: adj. rastrum , of or belonging to the hoe , i. e. to husbandry or a country life : Hypobolimaea, the title of a comedy of Cæcilius, Non. 16, 19 ; 40, 4 ; 89, 16 al.

rastrum.opening: , usually in plur. , , , (so nom. rastri, Varr. L. L. 5, § 136 Müll.; Verg. G. 1, 164 ; Ov. M. 11, 36 ; acc. rastros, Cato, R. R. 10, 3 ; 11, 4 ; Plaut. Merc. 2, 2, 6 ; Ter. Heaut. 1, 1, 36 ; 5, 1, 58 al. ; but rastra,…

rāsūra.opening: id. . Lit. , a scraping , a shaving (post-Aug.): calami, Col. 4, 29, 9 : barbae capitisque, Hier. in Isa. 5, 15, 2 .— Concr., what is scraped or shaved off; a scraping , shaving : eboris, Veg. 1, 10, 6 ; 6 (4), 8, 8.—…

rāsus.opening: rado , a scraping , shaving : ab rasu rastelli dicti, Varr. L. L. 5, § 136 Müll.

rătārĭae.opening: ratis , small vessels made of logs fastened together , rafts , acc. to Gell. 10, 25 fin. ; also called ratiariae in Serv. ad Verg. A. 1, 43 ; cf. ratiarius.

rătĭārĭus.opening: id. a raftsman , lighterman , Dig. 13, 7, 30 ; Inscr. Murat. 67, 7 .

rătĭhăbĭtĭo.opening: ratum-habeo , an approval , ratification (jurid.), Dig. 3, 5, 6, § 6 ; 50, 17, 152 al.

rătĭo.opening: ( abl. rationi, Lucr. 6, 66 ), reor, ratus , a reckoning , account , calculation , computation. Lit. Sing.: Les. Nequaquam argenti ratio conparet tamen. Sta. Ratio quidem hercle adparet: argentum οἴχεται, Plaut. Trin.…

rătĭōcĭnābĭlĭter.opening: adv. ratiocinor , according to correct computation , Macr. Somn. Scip. 2, 11 fin.

rătĭōcĭnātĭo.opening: id. , a rhet. and archit. t. t. In rhet. An exercise of the reasoning powers , calm reasoning , ratiocination (opp. impulsio, a passionate feeling, impulse; cf. argumentatio): ratiocinatio est diligens et considerata…

rătĭōcĭnātīvus.opening: adj. id. . In rhet., of or belonging to reasoning , syllogistic , ratiocinative : genus, Cic. Inv. 1, 13, 17 : quaestio, Quint. 7, 1, 60 : status, id. 7, 8, 3 ; cf. id. 3, 6, 46 ; 61 ; 5, 10, 6 .— In gram.:…

rătĭōcĭnātor.opening: id. , a reckoner , computant , accountant , i. q. calculator. Lit. , Cic. Att. 1, 12, 2 ; Col. 3, 3, 7 ; Dig. 14, 4, 5, § 16 .— Trop. : ut boni ratiocinatores esse possimus et addendo deducendoque videre, quae reliqui…

rătĭōcĭnĭum.opening: id. , a reckoning , computation , Col. 5, 1 fin. ; 5, 2, 6 ; 5, 11, 13 ; Cod. Th. 8, 1, 6: publica, ib. 9, 16, 2 .— The obligation to render an account : imponere, Cod. 2, 7, 6 al.

rătĭōcĭnor.opening: v. dep. n. and a. [ratio] (rare, but good prose). Lit. , to reckon , compute , calculate : in summo apud illos (sc. Graecos) honore geometria fuit: itaque nihil mathematicis illustrius; at nos metiendi ratiocinandique…

rătĭōnābĭlis.opening: adj. ratio (post-Aug.; = rationalis, which is in better use), reasonable , rational : natura, Sen. Vit. Beat. 14, 1 : virtutes quae ad rationabilem animum pertinent, App. Dogm. Plat. 2, p. 17, 18 ; cf.: virtutes…

rătĭōnābĭlĭtas.opening: rationabilis , reasonableness , rationality , App. Dogm. Plat. 1, p. 9, 5 .

rătĭōnālis.opening: adj. ratio . Of or belonging to accounts (post-Aug.): LITTERAE, Inscr. (a. p. Chr. 193) Orell. 39.—Hence, subst. , , , an accountant , receiver of revenue , treasurer , Lampr. Alex. Sev. 45 ; 46 ; Capitol. Gord. 7 ;…

rătĭōnālĭtas.opening: rationalis , reasonableness , rationality : habet anima rationalitatem, Tert. Anim. 38 fin.

rătĭōnārĭum.opening: ratio , a statistical table , schedule , book of accounts : imperii, Suet. Aug. 28 (for which: breviarium imperii, id. ib. 101 ; cf. Tac. A. 1, 11 ).

rătis.opening: ( , acc. to Prob. p. 1473 fin. ; yet perh. we should here read vates; acc. ratim, Hyg. Fab. 175 ), , Sanscr. ar-i-tras that which propels, an oar; Gr. ἐρέτης, rower; ἐρέσσω, to row; Lat.: remus, remigium, triremis, etc.…

rătītus.opening: adj. ratis , marked with the figure of a raft : ratitum quadrantem dictum putant, quod in eo et triente ratis fuerit effigies, ut navis in asse, Paul. ex Fest. p. 275 Müll.; so, quadrantes, Lucil. ap. Varr. L. L. 5, §…

rătĭuncula.opening: dim. ratio . A small reckoning , a little account : subduxi ratiunculam, Quantum aeris mihi sit, quantumque alieni siet, Plaut. Curc. 3, 1 ; id. Capt. 1, 2, 89 ; Ter. Phorm. 1, 1, 2 .— A slight ground or reason : leves,…

rătō.opening: adv. ratus , certainly , surely (postclass.), Tert. Anim. 35 ; id. ad Uxor. 2, 9 .

Ratumēna Porta.opening: ( ). a gate at Rome , which, acc. to Festus, derived its name from an Etruscan youth, Paul. ex Fest. p. 275 Müll.; cf. Plin. 8, 42, 65, § 161 ; Sol. 45, 15 (in Plut. Public. 13, written Ῥατουμένα ).

rătus.opening: Part. and P. a. , v. reor fin.

rauca.opening: a species of worm that breeds in oak-roots , Plin. 17, 18, 30, § 130 ; Dig. 19, 2, 15, § 2 .

raucēdo.opening: raucus , hoarseness : raucedo amputatio vocis. Haec et arteriasis vocatur, eo quod raucam vocem et clausam reddat ab arteriarum injuriā, Isid. Orig. 4, 7, 14 .

raucesco.opening: v. n. id. , to grow hoarse , become hoarse : quomodo raucescit vox (gallinae), Aug. in Psa. 58 ; Isid. 12, 7, 15 .

raucĭdŭlus.opening: adj. dim. [id.], a little hoarse : cornix, Hier. Ep. 40, 2 .

raucio.opening: , no perf. , , v. n. id. , to be hoarse : rausuro tragicus qui carmina perdit Oreste, Lucil. ap. Prisc. p. 907 P.

raucĭ-sŏnus.opening: adj. id. , hoarsesounding (only in the foll. passages): cantus cornicum, Lucr. 5, 1084 : bombi, Cat. 64, 263 .

raucĭtas.opening: id. . Hoarseness , raucity (not ante-Aug.), Cels. 2, 1 med. ; Scrib. Comp. 184 ; Plin. 20, 6, 23, § 53 ; and in plur. , id. 22, 23, 49, § 104 .— Transf. A snoring , Mart. Cap. 8, § 804 .— Of the hoarse sound of the…

raucus.opening: adj. from root ru-, to make a loud noise, ravus , hoarse. Lit. (freq. and class.): rogitando sum raucus factus, Plaut. Ep. 2, 1, 16 : expurigabo ad raucam ravim omnia, id. Fragm. ap. Non. 164, 19 : nos raucos saepe…

Raudii campi.opening: a broad plain near Verona , where Marius defeated the Cimbri , Vell. 2, 12, 5 .— Called also, in sing. , , Flor. 3, 3, 14 ; Aur. Vict. Vir. Ill. c. 67.

raudus.opening: (also and ), , kindr. with rudis; cf.: crudus, crudelis , a rude mass; hence, in partic., a piece of brass used as a coin (an old word): rodus vel raudus significat rem rudem et imperfectam. Nam saxum quoque raudus…

Rauduscŭla.opening: or , a gate at Rome , according to the ancient division of Servius Tullius , between the P. Naevia and Lavernalis, Varr. L. L. 5, § 163 Müll.; Fest. s. h. v. p. 274 ib.; Val. Max. 5, 6, 3 .

rauduscŭlum.opening: ( and ), , dim. raudus . A little piece of brass used as a coin (an old word): in mancipando cum dicitur: Rudusculo libram ferito, asse tangitur libra, Fest. s. v. rodus, p. 265 Müll.; v. raudus.— Hence, Transf. , a…

Raunōnĭa.opening: an island north of Germany , Plin. 3, 13, 27, § 94 .

Raurăci.opening: ( , Plin. 4, 17, 31, § 106 ), , , a people of Gaul , on the Rhine , neighbors of the Helvetians , near Basle , Caes. B. G. 1, 5 ; 6, 25 ; 7, 75 .—Hence, , , , the city of the Rauraci , now Augst , near Basle , Amm. 14,…

Răvenna.opening: ( , Coripp. Laud. Just. 2, 123 ), , , a celebrated seaport in Gallia Cispadana, still bearing the same name , Plin. 3, 15, 20, § 115 ; Caes. B. C. 1, 5 fin. ; Cic. Att. 7, 1, 4 ; id. Fam. 1, 9, 9 ; Tac. A. 4, 5 :…

rāvĭdus.opening: adj. 2. ravus , grayish , dark-colored : ravidi vel nigrantes oculi, Col. 8, 2, 9 .

Rāvilla.opening: id. , an appellation of L. Cassius Longinus (Cons. 626 A.U.C.), Front. Aquaed. 8 ; cf.: Ravillae a ravis oculis, quemadmodum a caesiis Caesullae, Fest. p. 274 Müll.; cf. Paul. ex Fest. p. 275 ib.

rāvĭo.opening: v. n. ravis , to talk one ' s self hoarse , Plaut. Poen. 3, 5, 33 ; cf. Paul. ex Fest. s. v. ravim, p. 275 Müll.

rāvis.opening: acc. , kindr. with ravus, q. v. , hoarseness (ante- and post-class., and only occurring in the acc. sing. ): usque ad ravim poscam, Plaut. Aul. 2, 5, 10 : expurigabo hercle omnia ad raucam ravim, id. Fragm. ap. Non.…

rāvŭlus.opening: adj. dim. [1. ravus], a little hoarse : dat ravulos choraulas, Sid. 9, 13 in carm.

rāvus.opening: adj. for hravus, ghrav-us; root in Sanscr. gar-an; Gr. γέρων, senex; cf.: γῆρας, γραῦς; O. H. Germ. grā; Engl. gray , gray-yellow , gray , tawny (rare but class.): ravi coloris appellantur, qui sunt inter flavos et…

rĕ.opening: , or with d demonstrative (see the letter D), (so, too, before vowels and h; also in red-do, and with the union-vowel i in rĕdĭ-vivus. In reicio and often in later Latin re is found before vowels and h; e. g.…

rĕ-accendo.opening: v. a. , to kindle anew , Hier. in Isa. 9, 30, v. 12 .

rĕ-adūnātĭo.opening: a reuniting , reunion : ossium (at the resurrection), Tert. Res. 30 .

rĕ-aedĭfĭco.opening: v. a. , to build again , rebuild (late Lat.): reaedifico quae destruxit, Tert. adv. Marc. 5, 3 ; so id. Pud. 20 fin. ; Hier. Ep. 108, 9 ; Vulg. Marc. 15, 29 .

rĕagnosco.opening: v. n. , to recall to mind (late Lat.), Fulg. Serm. 29 .

rēapse.opening: adv. contr. from re and eapse, an old form for ipsā; hence in tmesi: reque eapse, Scip. Afr. ap. Fest. p. 286, 3; cf. ipse init. , in fact , in reality , actually , really (an old word, which does not occur after Cic.):…

Rĕāte.opening: (of the same form in the nom. , acc. , and abl. ), a very ancient town of the Sabines , now Rieti , Plin. 3, 12, 17, § 109 ; Varr. R. R. 3, 1, 6 ; Liv. 25, 7 ; 26, 11 ; 23 ; Plin. 3, 12, 17, § 109 ; Sil. 8, 417 .—Hence,…

rĕātus.opening: reus . Lit. , the condition of an accused person , a state of impeachment (a word first used by Messala, acc. to Quint. 8, 3, 34 ): revocato ad reatum Alcibiade, Just. 4, 4, 4 : si diutino tempore aliquis in reatu…

rĕ-baptīzo.opening: v. a. , to baptize again , rebaptize (late Lat.), Cod. Just. 1, 6, 2 ; Aug. Ep. 203 fin. al.

rĕbellātĭo.opening: rebello , a renewal of hostilities , revolt , rebellion (post-Aug. for the class. rebellio), * Tac. A. 14, 31 ; Val. Max. 7, 3, 9 ext.; 7, 4, 1; Serv. Verg. A. 12, 186 .

rĕbellātrix.opening: id. , she that revolts or rebels (very rare): Germania, Ov. Tr. 3, 12, 47 : provincia, Liv. 40, 35 fin. ; Amm. 14, 8, 2 .

rĕbellĭo.opening: id. , one who revolts , an insurgent , rebel (late Lat.), Treb. Poll. Salon. 1; Faustina ap. Vulc. Gall. Avid. Cass. 9 ; Vop. Prob. 9 ; cf. rebellis.

rĕbellis.opening: adj. id. , that makes war afresh , insurgent , rebellious ( poet. and in post-Aug. prose). Lit. : rebelles Aeneadae, Verg. A. 12, 185 : Gallus, id. ib. 6, 858 : Numidae, Ov. M. 15, 754 : regio rebellis et indomita,…

rĕbellĭum.opening: id. , a renewal of war , revolt , rebellion (a collat. form for rebellio, like consortium for consortio, contagium for contagio, etc.): qui pacatos ad rebellium incitasset, Liv. 42, 21, 3 Gronov. (dub.; Weissenb.…

rĕ-bello.opening: v. n. , to wage war again (said of the conquered), to make an insurrection , to revolt , rebel (mostly postAug.; not in Cic. or Cæs.; syn.: descisco). Lit. : Volsci rebellarunt, Liv. 2, 42 ; 4, 31 ; 40, 35 ; 8, 14, 5:…

Rebilus.opening: surname of the legate C. Caninius, v. h. v.

rĕ-bīto.opening: v. n. bēto , to turn back , return (ante-class.): si non rebitas huc, Plaut. Capt. 2, 3, 20 ; cf. id. ib. 2, 3, 49 ; 3, 5, 89.

rĕbŏātus.opening: reboo , a shouting back : qui quidem omnes inter Musarum carmina concinentium audiri, licet perstreperent, nullo potuere reboatu, Mart. Cap. 2, § 213 (al. rabalatu).

rĕ-bŏo.opening: v. n. and a. Neutr. , to bellow back , resound , re-echo ( poet. ): reboant silvaeque et longus Olympus, * Verg. G. 3, 223 ; so, rupti poli, Sil. 17. 252 : et reboat raucum regio cita barbara bombum, Lucr. 4, 546 :…

rĕ-bullĭo.grammar: īvi or ii v. n. and a.
rĕ-bullĭo.opening: v. n. and a. (Appuleian). Neutr. , to bubble up : vinum, App. M. 9, p. 233, 8 .— Act. , to cause to bubble forth , to cast forth with a bubbling noise : oleum, App. M. 5, p. 170, 26 : spiritum, to breathe out, id. ib. 1…

rĕburrus.opening: with bristling hair (Fr. rebours ), Aug. c. Faust. 6, 1; Not. Tir.; ἀνάσιλλος, Thom. Thes.

rĕ-calcĭtro.opening: v. n. , to kick back (of horses); transf. ( Poet. ) To deny access , Hor. S. 2, 1, 20 .— (Late Lat.) To be petulant , disobedient : incrassatus est dilectus, et recalcitravit, Vulg. Deut. 32, 15 ; cf.: majestati…
