rĕcorpŏrātĭo.opening: recorporo , a furnishing again with a body or flesh; the restoration of the body to its former state (post-class.), Tert. Res. Carn. 30 ; Cael. Aur. Tard. 1 prooem.; 1, 4, 112.

rĕcorpŏrātīvus.opening: adj. id. , that serves to restore the body to its former condition , restorative (a late medic. word): cucurbitae, Cael. Aur. Tard. 2, 1 ; 7 : adjutoria, id. Acut. 3, 16 : virtus, id. ib. 2, 38 .

rĕ-corpŏro.opening: v. a. , to furnish again with a body , to restore the body to (animam) its former condition (post-class.), Tert. Anim. 33 med. : argillam in materiam robustiorem, id. Res. Carn. 7 ; Cael. Aur. Acut. 3, 4 fin.

rĕ-corrĭgo.opening: v. a. Lit. , to mend or correct again (post-Aug. and very rare): costas, i. e. to set right again, Petr. 43, 4 .— Trop. , to amend , reform : animum, Sen. Ep. 50, 6 : aliquem ad regulam, Tert. adv. Marc. 4, 5 .

rĕ-crastĭno.opening: v. a. crastinus , to put off from day to day , to procrastinate (post-Aug. and rare), Col. 2, 20, 2 ; Plin. 17, 14, 24, § 113 .

rē^crĕābĭlis.opening: adj. recreo , refreshing : delectatio, Cassiod. Var. 11, 16 .

rĕcrĕātĭo.opening: id. , a restoration : ab aegritudine, recovery, convalescence, Plin. 22, 23, 49, § 102 .

rĕcrĕātor.opening: id. , a restorer , reviver (post-class.): corporum somnus, Tert. Anim. 43 : OMNIVM MVNERVM, Inscr. Grut. 1095, 7 .

rĕ-crēmentum.opening: cerno , refuse , filth , dross , slag , recrement (post-Aug.): plumbi, Cels. 6, 8 : farris, i. e. chaff, Plin. 18, 16, 41, § 142 ; Prud. Apoth. 65 .— Of human excrements , Gell. 17, 11, 2 .

rē^-crĕmo.opening: v. a. cremo , to burn again , burn utterly : nec recremanda foris, sed recreanda polis, Ven. Fort. Carm. 9, 2, 114.

rĕ-crĕo.opening: v. a. , to make or create anew , to remake , reproduce , restore , renew (very rare; syn.: reficio, reparo): lumen, Lucr. 5, 759 ; 5, 277 ; cf. id. 5, 323 : carnes, Plin. 34, 15, 46, § 155 . — Poet. : Athenae…

rĕ-crĕpo.opening: v. n. and a. , to sound back , resound , ring , echo ( poet. ; perh. only in the foll. passages): cava cymbala recrepant, Cat. 63, 29 : saepe lapis recrepat Cyllenia murmura (i. e. lyram) pulsus, Verg. Cir. 108 .

rĕ-cresco.opening: v. n. , to grow again , to grow up or increase again (mostly poet. and post-Aug.): ergo terra tibi libatur et aucta recrescit, Lucr. 5, 260 : favete nomini Scipionum, suboli imperatorum vestrorum, velut accisis…

rĕcrŭcĭfīgo.opening: v. a. re-, crux, and figo , to crucify anew , Hier. in Ep. ad Gal. 3, 5, 14 .

rĕ-crūdesco.opening: v. inch. n. , to become raw again. * Lit. , of wounds, to break open afresh : nunc autem hoc tam gravi vulnere etiam illa, quae consanuisse videbantur, recrudescunt, * Cic. Fam. 4, 6, 2 . — Trop. : recrudescente…

rectā.opening: and , advv. , v. rego, P. a. fin.

rectĭfĭcātĭo.opening: rectus-facio , the harmonizing , reconciling (late Lat.): contrariorum, Junii Part ib. Div. Leg. 2, 29 .

rectĭo.opening: rego , a leading , guiding , government , direction (Ciceronian): rerum publicarum, Cic. Fin. 5, 4, 11 .— Plur. : rerum publicarum, Cic. Fin. 4, 22, 61 (Madv. conj. rerum publicarum rectionis genera).

rectĭtātor.opening: rectito, v. rego , a leader , director : ratis rectitator, Poët. ap. Mar. Vict. p. 2551 P.

rectĭtūdo.opening: rectus (post-class.). Straightness , directness. Lit. , Aggen. ap. Front. p. 46 Goes.— Trop. , uprightness , rectitude (class. aequitas), Hier. in Isa. 8, 10 ; 26, 7 : hominum, Just. Nov. 13 praef.

rectō.opening: adv. , v. rego, P. a. fin.

rector.opening: rego , a guider , leader , director , ruler , master (cf.: moderator, gubernator). Lit. (mostly post-Aug.), of a helmsman : navium rectores, Cic. Div. 1, 14, 24 ; so Verg. A. 5, 161 ; 176 ; Ov. M. 2 . 186; 6, 232; 11,…

rectrix.opening: rector , she that leads or guides; a directress , governess , mistress (post-Aug.): animam velut aurigam rectricemque membrorum, Col. 3, 10, 9 : sapientia domina rectrixque est, Sen. Ep. 85, 32 : Italia rectrix…

rectūra.opening: rego . Uprightness , Front. Colon. p. 131 Goes. — Control , government : decuriarum, Cassiod. Var. 5, 21 .

rectus.opening: Part. and P. a. , from rego.

rĕcŭbĭtus.opening: recumbo , a falling down; reclining at table , Plin. 24, 13, 72, § 116 ; Hier. in Cantic. Hom. 1, 1 .— Plur. , Vulg. Matt. 23, 6 .

rĕ-cŭbo.opening: v. n. , to lie upon the back; to lie back , recline (rare but class.): hunc tu, diva, tuo recubantem corpore sancto Circumfusa super, Lucr. 1, 38 ; * Cic. de Or. 3, 17, 63 : Tyrio recubare toro, Tib. 1, 2, 75 : sus…

rēcŭla.opening: (also written ), , dim. res . A small matter , a trifle , Plaut. Fragm. ap. Prisc. p. 613 P.; in plur. , App. M. 4, p. 148 : resculae (al. reculae), Salv. c. Avar. 4, p. 166.— In partic., a small estate , Don. Vit.…

rĕ-cumbo.opening: v. n. cumbo, cubo , to lay one ' s self back , lie down again; to lie down. Of persons. In gen. (class.): eum primo perterritum somno surrexisse, dein, cum se collegisset ... recubuisse, etc., Cic. Div. 1, 27, 57 : in…

rĕ-cūro.opening: v. a. , * to restore by taking care of; to refresh , invigorate , make whole , cure , = recreare; also, to take care of; to prepare with care : me otio et urticā, Cat. 44, 15 : chartam, to prepare carefully, Plin. 13,…

rĕ-curro.opening: (recucurrit, only Paul. Nol. Carm. 27, 99 ), , v. n. , to run back , hasten back (class.). Lit. : ego ad anum recurro rursum, Plaut. Cist. 2, 3, 50 ; cf.: recurrit rursus ad Hispalim Caesar, Auct. B. Hisp. 40 fin. : ad…

rĕcursĭo.opening: recurro , a running back , backward course , return , Mart. Cap. 9, § 911 .

rĕcursĭtans.opening: Part. [recurso], running back repeatedly , frequently returning , Mart. Cap. 1, § 25 .

rĕcurso.opening: v. freq. n. [recurro], to run or hasten back; to come back , return ( poet. and in post-Aug. prose). Lit. : quid ego huc recursem? * Plaut. Most. 3, 1, 34 : (corpora) dissiliunt longe, longeque recursant, * Lucr. 2, 106…

rĕcursus.opening: id. . Lit. , a running back , going back , return , retreat , etc. (not ante-Aug.; and in the poets mostly in the plur. ; in the sing. , Ov. M. 11, 454 ): inde alios ineunt cursus aliosque recursus, Verg. A. 5, 583 : ut…

rĕ-curvo.opening: , no perf. , , v. a. , to bend or curve backwards , to turn back (not ante-Aug.): equi colla, Ov. H. 4, 79 : radicem, Col. 5, 10, 13 : palmam, Gell. 3, 6, 2 : in caput aquas, Ov. Am. 1, 8, 6 : gladios in vulnera, Stat.…

rĕ-curvus.opening: adj. , turned back , bent , crooked , or curved back (a poet. word of the Aug. per.; also in post-Aug. prose; syn.: reduncus, repandus): cornu, * Verg. A. 7, 513 ; Ov. M. 5, 327 ; id. F. 5, 119 : puppis, id. M. 8, 141 ;…

rĕcūsābĭlis.opening: adj. recuso , that should be rejected (post-class.): revelatio, Tert. adv. Marc. 4, 35 fin.

rĕcūsātĭo.opening: id. . In gen., a declining , refusal. Lit. (good prose): disputationis, Cic. de Or. 2, 7, 26 : cotidiana mea recusatio, Hirt. B. G. prooem. § 1: sine ullā recusatione, Cic. Phil. 7, 4, 13 : sine recusatione, id. Cat. 3,…

rĕcūsātīvus.opening: adj. id. , prohibitory (late Lat.), Cael. Aur. Salut. Praecc. 22 .

rĕ-cūso.opening: ( gen. plur. of the part. pres. recusantūm, Verg. A. 7, 16 ), v. a. causa . In gen., to make an objection against , in statement or reply; to decline , reject , refuse , be reluctant or unwilling to do a thing, etc.…

rĕcussābĭlis.opening: adj. recutio , that can be struck back and forth : sphaera, Cael. Aur. Tard. 3, 6 fin.

rĕcussus.opening: recutio , a striking back , a recoil , rebound (only in abl. sing. ), Plin. 8, 53, 79, § 214 ; Fulg. Myth. praef. 1.

rĕ-cŭtĭo.opening: , no perf. , , v. a. quatio , to strike back or backwards , to cause to rebound ( poet. and in post-Aug. prose): aequor penitus, Val. Fl. 5, 167 ; jugum Christi, Aug. Civ. Dei, 2, 40: horrorem, id. Conf. 8, 11 :…

rĕ-cŭtītus.opening: adj. cutis , circumcised : Judaei, Mart. 7, 30, 5 ; Petr. 68, 8 ; cf. poet. transf.: sabbata, Pers. 5, 184 : colla, skinned, galled, Mart. 9, 57, 4 .

rĕd-accendo.opening: , no perf. , , v. a. , to kindle again , rekindle (eccl. Lat.), Tert. Anim. 30 fin. ; id. Res. Carn. 12 ; Hier. Ep. 5, 1 .

rĕdactus.opening: redigo , proceeds , produce : fructuum holeris, Dig. 7, 1, 58 : venditionis, ib. 46, 3, 89 .

rĕd-ădopto.opening: v. a. , to adopt anew , to readopt : filium denuo, Dig. 1, 7, 41 .

rĕd-ambŭlo.opening: v. n. , to come back , return : bene ambula et redambula, Plaut. Capt. 4, 2, 120 .

rĕd-ămo.opening: v. a. , to love back , love in return , return love for love (formed by Cic. after the Gr. ἀντιφιλεῖν ): qui vel amare vel, ut ita dicam, redamare possit, Cic. Lae). 14, 49; also in late Lat., Macr. S. 6, 9, 6 ; Symm.…

rĕd-amtrŭo.opening: v. n. , to dance opposite in the Salian religious festivals: praesul ut amtruet, inde vulgus redamtruat, Lucil. ap. Fest. p. 273 Müll.

rĕdănĭmātĭo.opening: redanimo , a restoring to life , reanimation (eccl. Lat.), Tert. Res. Carn. 38 .

rĕd-ănĭmo.opening: v. a. , to quicken again , restore to life , reanimate (eccl. Lat.), Tert. Res. Carn. 13 ; 19 ; 31 al.

rĕd-ardesco.opening: v. n. , to blaze up anew : flamma redardescet, quae modo nulla fuit, Ov. R. Am. 734 .

rĕd-argŭo.opening: v. a. , to disprove , refute , confute , contradict (class.; syn.: refello, refuto). With acc. : nosque ipsos redargui refellique patiamur, Cic. Tusc. 2, 2, 5 ; so, aliquem, id. Clu. 23, 62 ; Quint. 6, 3, 73 al. ; opp.…

rĕdargūtĭo.opening: redarguo , a refutation , reproof , defence : non habens in ore suo refutationes, Vulg. Psa. 37, 15 : in redargutionem venire, to fall into contempt, be mocked at, id. Act. 19, 27 ; id. Psa. 37, 15 ; Boëth. Arist.…

rĕd-armātus.opening: Part. [armo], armed again , rearmed : manus novis jaculis, Dict. Cret. 2, 40 .

rĕd-auspĭco.opening: v. n. , to take the auspices anew or again : exauspicavi ex vinclis: nunc intellego Redauspicandum esse in catenas denuo, comically for, to go back again, return, Plaut. Capt. 3, 5, 108 Brix ad loc.

reddĭtĭo.opening: reddo , a giving back , returning. Jucunditatis, Vulg. Ecclus. 1, 29 : rationis, i. e. rendering a reason , Aug. Civ. Dei , 21, 7.— A repetition , recurrence : orationis, Mart. Cap. 5, § 533 .— Rhet. t. t., Gr.…

reddĭtīvus.opening: adj. redditio, III. , of or belonging to the apodosis , consequential , redditive : pars, the apodosis, Diom. p. 432 P.: particulae, e. g. talis, ita, Prisc. p. 1052 P.

reddĭtor.opening: reddo , one who pays , a payer : debitorum, Aug. Ep. 5 ; Vulg. Ecclus. 5, 4 .

red-do.opening: (old fut. reddibo = reddam, Plaut. Cas. 1, 41 ; id. Men. 5, 7, 49 , acc. to Non. 476, 27 ; id. Fragm. ap. Non. 508, 9 ; pass. reddibitur, id. Ep. 1, 1, 22 ), v. a. Lit. , to give back , return , restore (freq. and…

rĕdemptĭo.opening: redimo . A buying back , buying off; a releasing , ransoming , redemption : cum captivis redemptio negabatur, Liv. 25, 6 : ducis (capti), Quint. 7, 1, 29 : puellae, Val. Max. 4, 3, 1 : sacramenti, i. e. the purchase of…

rĕdemptĭto.opening: v. freq. a. redempto , to buy up , redeem : malefacta benefactis, to compensate , make amends for , Cato ap. Fest. p. 286 Müll.

rĕdempto.opening: v. freq. a. redimo , to buy back , ransom , redeem : (captivi) a propinquis redemptabantur, Tac. H. 3, 36 .

rĕdemptor.opening: id. . In all periods of the lang., one who undertakes a thing by way of contract; a contractor , undertaker , purveyor , farmer (syn. conductor); absol. : redemptor qui columnam illam de Cottā et de Torquato conduxerat…

rĕdemptrix.opening: redemptor, II. , she that redeems , a redemptress , Prud. στεφ. 10, 77, 3; Coripp. Laud. Just. 4, 297 ; Am. bros. de Caïn et Abel, 2, 4, 13; id. de Vid. 6, 36 .

rĕdemptūra.opening: redimo , an undertaking of public deliverings by contract , a contracting , farming (very rare): qui redempturis auxissent patrimonia, Liv. 23, 48 fin. : redempturis faciendis, Dig. 14, 3, 5 ; cf. Becker, Antiq. 2, 1,…

rĕd-ĕo.opening: (lengthened form of the pres. redīnunt, Enn. ap. Fest. p. 286 Müll.; cf.: obinunt, ferinunt, nequinunt, solinunt, for obeunt, feriunt, nequeunt, solent; and danit, danunt, for dat, dant; rare fut. redies, App. M. 6, 19…

rĕd-hālo.opening: v. a. , to breathe forth again , exhale , Lucr. 6, 523 .

rĕd-hĭbĕo.opening: ( ), no perf. , , v. a. habeo , mercant. t. t., to take back a defective article purchased; hence, of the buyer, to carry , give back; of the seller, to receive back : redhibere est facere, ut rursus habeat venditor,…

rĕdhĭbĭtĭo.opening: ( ), , redhibeo , a taking back , a giving or receiving back a damaged article sold, Dig. 21, 1, 21 sq. ; 44, 2, 25 : esse in causā redhibitionis, Gell. 4, 2, 10 ; Quint. 8, 3, 14 : quoniam retroacta venditio esset…

rĕdhĭbĭtor.opening: Aug. in Psa. 58 , Serm. 2, 1: ἀνάδοχος, Gloss. Philox.

rĕdhĭbĭtōrĭus.opening: adj. redhibeo , in jurid. Lat., of or relating to taking back a thing sold: actio, Dig. 21, 1, 54 : judicium, ib. 21, 1, 18 : exceptio, ib. 21, 1, 48 .

rĕd-hostĭo.opening: v. a. , to recompense , requite , Nov. and Att. ap. Fest. p. 270 Müll.; Non. 165, 20 sq.

rĕ-dīco.opening: v. a. , to say again , say over , repeat : haec, Sid. Ep. 9, 13 .

Rĕdĭcŭlŭs.opening: redeo , the name of a Roman divinity , worshipped in a chapel at Rome , before the porta Capena, whence Hannibal set out upon his retreat , Fest. p. 282, 23 Müll.; cf. Paul. ex Fest. p. 283, 4 ib.: Campus Rediculi,…

rĕd-ĭgo.opening: v. a. ago . To drive , lead , or bring back (syn. reduco). Lit. : (Sol) Disjectos redegit equos, Lucr. 5, 403 : si materiem nostram collegerit aetas Post obitum, rursumque redegerit, ut sita nunc est, bring it back,…

rĕdĭmīcŭlum.opening: (collat. form , , , late Lat., Fulg. Serm. 5 ), redimio , a band. Lit. A fillet , necklace , chaplet , frontlet , etc., Cic. Verr. 2, 3, 33, § 76 : habent redimicula mitrae, Verg. A. 9, 616 ; Ov. M. 10, 265 ; id. F. 4,…

rĕdĭmĭo.opening: ( imperf. redimibat, Verg. A. 10, 538 ; Aus. Epigr. 94 ), v. a. etym. dub. , to bind round , wreathe round , encircle , gird , crown , etc. (mostly poet. ; syn.: cingo, circumdo). In the verb finit. : caput atque umeros…

rĕdĭmītus.opening: redimio , a binding or wreathing round , a crowning , Sol. 33 .

rĕd-ĭmo.opening: v. a. emo . To buy back , repurchase (freq. and class.; syn.: recupero, reparo). In gen.: eam (domum) non minoris, quam emit Antonius, redimet, Cic. Phil. 13, 5, 10 : neque adeo hasce emi mihi — illi redemi rursum,…

rĕd-indūtus.opening: Part. [induo], that has put on again , i. e. clothed again , reclothed with any thing: redindutus carnem, Tert. Res. Carn. 42 fin.

rĕdintegrātĭo.opening: redintegro , a renewal , restoration , repetition (mostly post-class.), Macr. S. 1, 11, 5 : terrae, App. Mund. p. 68, 3 : corporis et virium, Arn. 7, 249 : ejusdem verbi, Auct. Her. 4, 28, 38 : membrorum, Tert. adv.…

rĕdintegrātor.opening: id. , a renewer , restorer : OPERVM PVBLICORVM, Inscr. Orell. 3766 : virium (somnus), Tert. Anim. 43 : carnis, id. Res. Carn. 57 .

rĕd-intĕgro.opening: v. a. , to make whole again; to restore , renew; to recruit , refresh (good prose; syn.: renovo, restauro, recreo): vide, quantis imbribus repente dejectis (di) solum molliant venasque fontium arentes redintegrent, Sen.…

rĕd-invĕnĭo.opening: v. a. , to find again : coronam auream, Tert. Anim. 46 .

rĕd-ĭpiscor.opening: v. dep. a. [apiscor], to get again , to regain , recover : condalium, Plaut. Trin. 4, 3, 15 .

rĕ-disco.opening: v. a. , to learn again : Ven. Vit. S. Mart. 1, 122 .

rĕ-discussio.opening: repeated examination (late Lat.), Hier. in Naum. 2, 10 .

rĕdĭtĭo.opening: redeo , a going or coming back; a returning , return (very rare; more freq. reditus): quid illi reditio etiam huc fuit? * Plaut. Most. 2, 1, 30 ; so, huc, * Ter. Eun. 4, 4, 4 : spe domum reditionis sublatā, * Caes. B.…

rĕdĭtus.opening: redeo . A returning , return (freq. and class.). Lit. : noster itus, reditus, Cic. Att. 15, 5, 3 : reditu ( returning ) vel potius reversione ( turning back ) meā laetatus, id. ib. 16, 7, 5 : inter profectionem…

rĕdĭ-vīvus.opening: adj. v. re init. . That lives again (late Lat.; cf. recidivus): Christus, Prud. Cath. 3, 204 .— Renewed , renovated , of old building-materials used as new: redivivus rudus (opp. novum), Vitr. 7, 1 : unam columnam…

rēdo.opening: a kind of fish without bones , Aus. Idyll. 10, 89 .

rĕd-ŏlĕo.grammar: ŭi, ēre v. a. and n.
rĕd-ŏlĕo.opening: v. a. and n. , to emit a scent , diffuse an odor; to smell of or like , be redolent of any thing. Act. Lit. : vinum redolens, smelling of wine, Cic. Phil. 2, 25, 63 : unguenta, Plin. 11, 18, 19, § 61 : thymum, Quint.…

rĕ-dŏmĭtus.opening: Part. [domo], retamed , broken in again : cives redomiti atque victi, Cic. Sull. 1, 1 , v. Halm ad h. 1.

rĕdōnātor.opening: redono , one who gives back again , restorer , Inscr. Orell. 6 .

Rēdŏnes.opening: ( ), , , a people in Gallia Lugdunensis near the modern Rennes in Brittany , Caes. B. G. 2, 34, 1 ; 7, 75, 4 .

rĕ-dōno.opening: v. a. , to give back again , restore , return (only in Hor.). * In gen.: quis te redonavit dis patriis, Hor. C. 2, 7, 3 .— * To give up , resign : graves Iras et invisum nepotem Marti redonabo, Hor. C. 3, 3, 33 .

rĕd-ŏpĕrio.opening: v. a. , to wrap up or cover again , Ambros. de Noë et Arcā, 20, 72.

rĕd-opto.opening: v. a. , to wish for again : mortem, Tert. Res. Carn. 4 fin.

rĕd-ordior.opening: v. dep. a. , to take apart , unweave , unravel (Plinian): redordiri fila, rursusque texere, Plin. 6, 17, 20, § 54 ; 11, 22, 26, § 76 .

rĕ-dormio.opening: v. n. , to sleep again , Cels. 1, 2 ; Plin. Ep. 9, 36, 3 .

rĕdormītĭo.opening: dormito , a repeated sleeping , a falling asleep again : in redormitione vana esse visa, etc., Plin. 10, 75, 98, § 211 .

rĕd-orno.opening: v. a. , to adorn again , to readorn : specula, Tert. Res. Carn. 12 .

rĕ-dūco.opening: (rēduco or redduco, Lucr. 1, 228 ; 4, 992 ; 5, 133 ; old imp. redduce, Ter. Hec. 4, 2, 29 ), v. a. To lead or bring back , to conduct back (very freq. and class.; syn. redigo). Lit. In gen. Of living objects: reducam te…

rĕductĭo.opening: reduco , a leading or bringing back; a restoring , restoration (very rare): quoniam senatūs consultum nullum exstat, quo reductio regis Alexandrini tibi adempta sit, * Cic. Fam. 1, 7, 4 (shortly afterwards: ut per te…

rĕducto.opening: v. freq. a. reduco ; in milit. lang., to withdraw , draw back : exercitum, Aur. Vict. Caes. 38 fin.

rĕductor.opening: id. , one who leads or brings back (very rare). Lit. : plebis Romanae in urbem, * Liv. 2, 33 fin. — Trop. : litterarum jam senescentium reductor ac reformator, i.e. restorer, Plin. Ep. 8, 12, 1 .

rĕductus.opening: Part. and P. a. , from reduco.

rĕd-ulcĕro.opening: , no perf. , , v. a. , to make sore again , to scratch open again. Lit. : scabram partem pumice, Col. 7, 5, 8 . — Trop. : redulceratus dolor, i. e. renewed, App. M. 5, p. 163, 37 .

rĕd-uncus.opening: adj. , curved or bent backwards (very rare; syn.: recurvus, repandus): jamque aliis adunca, aliis redunca (cornua dedit), Plin. 11, 37, 45, § 125 .— Poet. , in gen., curved , bent : pennis rostroque redunco, Ov. M. 12,…

rĕdundans.opening: Part. and P. a. , from redundo.

rĕdundanter.opening: adv. , v. redundo, P. a. fin.

rĕdundantĭa.opening: redundans , an overflowing , superfluity , excess. * Lit. : aër crassus, qui non habet crebras redundantias, Vitr. 1, 6 med. — Trop. , redundancy , excess , of language, feeling, etc.: illa pro Roscio juvenilis…

rĕdundātĭo.opening: redundo , an overflowing; hence, transf.: stomachi, a rising, Plin. 7, 6, 5, § 41 ; 11, 37, 55, § 149 : astrorum, the flowing back , i. e. revolution , Vitr. 9, 1 fin. — Transf. , the over-abundance , multitude :…

red-undo.opening: v. n. ; of water, from being over full, to run back or over , to pour over , stream over , overflow (freq. and class.; a favorite word of Cic., esp. in trop. senses; not in Cæs., Verg., or Hor.; cf.: refluo, recurro).…

rĕdŭplĭcātĭo.opening: re-duplico , rhet. t. t., = ἀναδίπλωσις, repetition , Mart. Cap. 5, § 533 ; Boëth. Aristot. Anal. 1, 38.

rĕ-duplĭcātus.opening: Part. [duplico], doubled again , redoubled , reduplicated , Tert. Pat. 14 fin.

rĕ-dūresco.opening: v. inch. n. , to grow hard again : ferrum, Vitr. 1, 4 .

rĕdŭvĭa.opening: ( ), , A hangnail on the finger: rediviam quidam, alii reluvium appellant, cum circa ungues cutis se resolvit, Fest. p. 270, 17 Müll.; cf. Paul. ex Fest. p. 271, 11 ib.; so, redivia, Titin. ib.: reduviae, Plin. 30, 12,…

rĕdŭvĭōsus.opening: ( ), , adj. reduvia , full of hangnails , Laev. ap. Fest. p. 270 Müll.

rĕmĭniscentĭae.opening: reminiscor , recollections , remembrances , reminiscences , a transl. of the Platonic ἀναμνήσεις, Tert. Anim. 23 sq. ; Arn. 2, 57 .

rĕ-mĭniscor.opening: v. dep. n. and a. [root men; whence mens, memini; v. comminiscor]. To recall to mind , recollect , remember (syn. recordor): reminisci, quom ea quae tenuit mens ac memoria, cogitando repetuntur, Varr. L. L. 6, § 44…

rēmĭ-pēs.opening: adj. remus , oar-footed , i. e. which has oars for feet (Auson.): anates, Aus. Ep. 3, 13 : ratis, id. ib. 5, 34 : lembi, id. Idyll. 10, 201 .

rĕ-miscĕo.opening: , no perf. , mixtum or , v. a. , to mix or mingle again , to mix up , intermingle (perh. only in the foll. passages). Lit. : venenum remixtum cibo, Sen. Const. 7, 4 .— Trop. : sic veris falsa remiscet, Hor. A. P. 151 :…

rĕmissa.opening: f [remitto], a pardon , remission (eccl. Lat., for remissio): peccatorum, Tert. adv. Marc. 4, 18 fin. ; Cypr. Ep. 59 fin.

rĕmissārĭus.opening: adj. id. , that can be easily shoved back : vectes, a sliding bolt, Cato, R. R. 19 fin.

rĕmissē.opening: adv. , v. remitto, P. a. fin.

rĕmissĭbĭlis.opening: , e. adj. remitto (postclass). Pardonable , remissible : delicta, Tert. Pudic. 2 .— Easy , light : digestio, Cael. Aur. Tard. 2, 13, 164 .

rĕmissĭo.opening: id. (acc. to remitto, I. A. and B.), a sending back or away , releasing Lit. (rare). A sending back , returning; of persons: obsidum captivorumque, Liv. 27, 17, 1 .—Of things, a throwing back , reflecting : splendoris,…

rĕmissīvus.opening: adj. id. (late Lat.). In medicine, relaxing , laxative : relaxare tumentia rebus congruis et remissivis, Cael. Aur. Acut. 3, 4 .— In gram.: adverbia, formed to express the idea in a weakened or moderated sense ,…

rĕmissor.opening: remitto , he who remits or forgives : injuriae, Ambros. Off. Min. 1, 17, 66 : peccati, Hilar. Psa. 121, 8: peccatorum, Ambros. Psa. 39, 10 .

rĕmissus.opening: Part. and P. a. , from remitto.

rĕ-mitto.grammar: mīsi, missum, 3 v. a. and n.
rĕ-mitto.opening: v. a. and n. Act. , to let go back , send back , despatch back , drive back , cause to return (class. and very freq.; cf. reddo). Lit. In gen.: Al. Redde mihi illam (filiam) ... Non remissura es mihi illam? ... non…

rēmĭ-văgus.opening: adj. remus , oar-wafted , impelled by oars : celox, Varr. ap. Non. 533, 8 .

Remmĭus.opening: Name of a Roman gens, e. g., Tac. A. 2, 68 ; Suet. Gram. 23 .—Hence, Lex Remmia de calumniatoribus, of Remmius , Remmian , Cic. Rosc. Am. 19, 55 ; Dig. 48, 16, 1 ; 22, 5, 13 : quā, qui calumniabatur, damnabatur, si…

rĕ-mōlĭor.opening: v. dep. a. , to press , push , or move back or away ( poet. and in post-Aug. prose): saepe remoliri luctatur pondera terrae (Typhoëus), Ov. M. 5, 354 ; so, ferrea claustra, Stat. Th. 10, 527 ; Sen. Q. N. 6, 13 fin. — To…

rĕ-mollesco.opening: v. inch. n. , to become soft again , to become or grow soft (class.). Lit. : ut Hymettia sole Cera remollescit, softens, Ov. M. 10, 285 : sole remollescit quae frigore constitit unda, i. e. melts, id. ib. 9, 661 .—…

rĕ-mollio.opening: , no perf. , , v. a. , to make soft again , to make soft , soften ( poet. and in post-Aug. prose). Lit. : terram, Col. 2, 11, 9 : grana umore remollita, App. Herb. 3, 9 : quare ... Salmacis enervet tactosque remolliat…

rĕ-mŏnĕo.opening: v. a. , to warn again , remind : haec benevole remonebam, App. M. 5, p. 169, 23 .

rĕ-mŏra.opening: delay , hinderance , passive resistance (ante- and post-class.): quae Remoram faciunt rei privatae et publicae, Plaut. Trin. 1, 1, 16 ; cf. Lucil. ap. Paul. ex Fest. p. 276, 8 Müll.: remora si sit, if I delay, Plaut.…

Rĕmŏra.opening: the name given to Rome by Remus : certabant urbem Romam Remoramne vocarent, Enn. ap. Cic. Div. 1, 48, 107 (Ann. v. 85 Vahl.).

rĕmŏrāmen.opening: remoror , a delay , hinderance; in plur. , Ov. M. 3, 567 ; cf.: Remoramina impedimenta, Gloss. in Auct. Class. Vatic. tom. 8, p. 507, a, Mai.

rĕmŏrātĭo.opening: id. , slowness , delaying (late Lat.), Aug. Don. Persev. 17, 3 .

rĕmŏrātor.opening: id. , a delayer , hinderer , Mart. Cap. 1, § 70 .

rĕmŏrātrix.opening: remorator , she that delays , hinders , Gloss. Cyril.

rĕ-morbesco.opening: v. inch. n. [morbus], to become sick again , suffer a relapse , Enn. ap. Fest. p. 277 Müll. (cf. Enn. p. 178 Vahl.).

rĕ-mordeo.opening: , no perf. , , v. a. , to bite again; mostly poet. , and only in the trop. sense; to vex , torment , disturb : me remorsurum petis, Hor. Epod. 6, 4 : praeteritis male admissis peccata remordent, Lucr. 3, 827 : animus se…

rĕmŏres.grammar: aves in auspicio dicuntur, quae acturum aliquid remorari compellunt
rĕmŏres.opening: Fest. p. 276 Müll.: Remum dictum a tarditate, quippe talis naturae homines ab antiquis remores dicti, Aur. Vict. Orig. Gent. Rom. 21 fin.

rĕ-mŏror.opening: v. dep. n. and a. Neutr. , to stay , tarry , linger , loiter , delay (so rarely): nam quid illaec nunc tam diu intus remorantur remeligines? Plaut. Cas. 4, 3, 7 : ibi corpora, Lucr. 2, 75 : res nulla foris, id. 2, 158 :…

rĕmorsus.opening: mordeo , a biting back or in return (late Lat.), Primas. in Gal. ad c. s.

rĕmōtē.opening: adv. , v. removeo, P. a. fin.

rĕmōtĭo.opening: removeo , a putting back , withdrawing : bracchii, Auct. Her. 4, 19, 26 .— A putting away , removing , removal. Lit. : tutoris, Dig. 26, 10, 4 .— Trop. : remotio criminis est cum ejus intentio facti, quod ab adversario…

rĕmōtus.opening: Part. and P. a. , from removeo.

rĕ-mŏvĕo.opening: (sync. pluperf. remorant, Hor. S. 2, 1, 71 ; Sil. 11, 175 ; inf. remosse, Lucr. 3, 69 ; perf. remorunt, Ov. Ib. 240 ), v. a. , to move back , draw back; to take away , set aside , withdraw , remove (freq. and class.;…

rĕ-mūgĭo.opening: v. n. , to bellow back; to resound , re-echo ( poet. ): ad mea verba remugis, Ov. M. 1, 657 : Sibylla antro remugit, Verg. A. 6, 99 : totus remugit Mons, id. ib. 12, 928 : Ionius remugiens sinus Noto, Hor. Epod. 10, 19…

rĕ-mulcĕo.opening: v. a. , to stroke back ( poet. and rare). Lit. : caudam, i. e. to droop, Verg. A. 11, 812 : aures, to stroke gently, App. M. 1, p. 103, 8 : crines, id. Flor. 2, p. 350, 39 .— Trop. , to soothe : minas stimulataque corda…

rĕmulcum.opening: ( , acc. to the Gr., Amm. 18, 5, 6 ), i (for the most part only in abl. ), ῥυμουλκέω , nautical t. t., a tow-rope , or any other contrivance for towing : remulcum funis, quo deligata navis magnā trahitur vice remi,…

rēmŭlus.opening: dim. 1. remus , a small oar , Turp. ap. Non. 533, 6 .

Rĕmŭlus.opening: a proper name. Remulus Silvius, a king of Alba , Ov. M. 14, 616 ; id. F. 4, 49 sq. (called Romulus Silvius, Liv. 1, 3 ).— For Remus , Sulp. Sat. 19 ; cf. 2. Remus.— A name of fictitious heroes , Verg. A. 9, 360 ; 593 ;…

rĕ-mundo.opening: v. a. , to cleanse again , Inscr. Maff. Mus. Veron. 146 .

rĕmūnĕrātĭo.opening: remuneror , a repaying , recompense , reward , remuneration (Ciceron.): expeditior et celerior remuneratio, Cic. Off. 2, 20, 69 : benevolentiae, id. Lael. 14, 49 : officiorum, id. Inv. 2, 22, 66 : RAT. S. R., i. e.…

rĕmūnĕrātor.opening: id. , one that repays or recompenses , a rewarder , recompenser (post-class.): Deus, Tert. Apol. 36 ; Aug. Civ. Dei , 14, 26; Vulg. Heb. 11, 6 : VIRTVTVM, Inscr. Orell. 1140 .

rĕmūnĕrātrix.opening: remunerator , she that repays or avenges , Ambros. Psa. 118, 14, 31 fin. ; id. Cant. Cantic. 2, 33 fin.

rĕ-mūnĕror.opening: v. dep. a. , to repay , reward , recompense , remunerate (class.; syn. retribuo). Aliquem, Varr. R. R. 2, 1, 2 ; Cic. Att. 8, 1, 7 ; id. Fam. 3, 9, 3 : aliquem munere, id. ib. 9, 8, 1 ; id. Brut. 4, 15 : aliquem magno…

remurīnus.grammar: ager dictus, qui possessus est a Remo
remurīnus.opening: , et habitatio Remi Remorima. Sed et locus in summo Aventino Remoria dicitur, ubi Remus de urbe condendā fuerat auspicatus, Fest. p. 276 and 277 Müll.; Paul. ex Fest. p. 226 ib.; cf. Müll. p. 402: eundem locum (Remus)…

rĕmurmŭrātĭo.opening: re-murmuro , a murmuring back or against (late Lat.), Cassiod. in Psa. 37, 14 .

rĕ-murmŭro.opening: v. a. and n. , to murmur back , remurmur ( poet. ). Lit. Neutr. : remurmurat unda, Verg. A. 10, 291 : pinus remurmurat, Stat. S. 5, 1, 153 . — Act. : carmina remurmurat echo, Calp. Ecl. 4, 28 . — Trop. , to murmur back…

rēmus.opening: ἐρετμός , an oar. Lit. , Plaut. As. 3, 1, 16 : ut retinet navis cursum, intermisso impetu pulsuque remorum, Cic. de Or. 1, 33, 153 ; Caes. B. G. 3, 13 : remis navem incitare, id. ib. 3, 14 ; 4, 25: remis contendere, id.…

Rĕmus.opening: the brother of Romulus , Liv. 1, 5 ; 1, 7 ; Cic. Rep. 2, 2, 4 ; id. Div. 2, 38, 80 ; Verg. G. 2, 533 ; Ov. F. 3, 41 ; 4, 56 ; 5, 464 .—In the poets, as the ancestor of the Romans, instead of the more usual Romulus:…

rēn.opening: , only in plur. renes, q. v.

rēnālis.opening: adj. renes , of or belonging to the kidneys or reins , renal : passio, Cael. Aur. Tard. 5, 3 .

renancĭtur.opening: significat reprehendit. Unde adhuc nos dicimus nanciscitur et nactus id est adeptus, Paul. ex Fest. p. 276 , and Fest. p. 277 Müll.

rĕ-narro.opening: v. a. , to tell over again; to tell of , relate ( poet. ): fata divom, Verg. A. 3, 717 : facta, Ov. M. 5, 635 Bach.: priora, id. ib. 6, 316 : Thebas Argosque, Stat. Th. 12, 390 .

rĕnascĭbĭlĭtas.opening: renascor , a regeneration , new birth (eccl. Lat.), Inc. Qu. ex Nov. Test. 50 .

rĕ-nascor.opening: v. dep. n. , to be born again; to grow , rise , or spring up again (class.; cf. regeneror). Lit. : res quaeque ... De niloque renata forent, Lucr. 1, 542 : de nilo, id. 1, 674 ; 757 ; cf.: corpore de patrio parvus…

rĕnātus.opening: , um. Part. , from reno. ; Part. , from renascor.

rĕ-nāvĭgo.opening: v. n. and a. , to sail back. Neutr. : post in haec Puteolana et Cumana regna renavigaro, Cic. Att. 14, 16, 1 : ab Asturā Antium, Plin. 32, 1, 1, § 4 : ex Indiā, id. 6, 23, 26, § 106 .— Act. : Acheron invius Renavigari,…

rĕ-necto.opening: v. a. , to connect : ali. quem, Avien. Arat. 474 .

rĕ-nĕo.opening: v. a. , to unspin , i. e. to undo , unravel what had been spun ( poet. ): at Clymenus Clothoque dolent, haec fila reneri, i. e. that the destiny is reversed, Ov. F. 6, 757 : Parcarum fila, Stat. S. 3, 1, 171 (dub.);…

rēnes.opening: (renium, Plin. 21, 29, 103, § 175 ; 28, 8, 27 , §§ 98 and 102; Scrib. Comp. 125 ; 143 . — Sing. , not used. — Collat. form , Plaut. ap. Fest. p. 276 Müll.; cf. Charis. p. 24 P.; Prisc. p. 645 P.), φρένες; cf. Lid. and…

rēnĭcŭlus.opening: dim. ren, renes , a little kidney , Marc. Emp. 26 fin.

rĕnīdentĭa.opening: renideo , a smiling , a smile : infantum, Tert. Anim. 49 .

rĕ-nīdĕo.opening: ( perf. reniduit, ἐμειδίασεν, Gloss. Philox.), , v. n. perh. kindr. with νίζω , to shine again , shine back; to glitter , glisten , be bright or resplendent ( poet. and not freq. till after the Aug. period). Lit. : nec…

rĕnīdesco.opening: v. inch. n. [renideo], to grow bright , to shine : tota circum Aere (i. e. armis) renidescit tellus, Lucr. 2, 326 .

rĕnīsus.opening: renitor , resistance (post-Aug. and very rare), Cels. 5, 28, 12 ; Aug. Civ. Dei , 21, 16.

rĕnītenter.opening: adv. id. , unwillingly (late Lat.), Aug. Lib. Arbit. 3, 69 .

rĕ-nĭtĕo.opening: v. n. , to shine back , flash (eccl. Lat.), Ambros. de Fide, 2, 14 al.

rĕ-nītor.opening: v. dep. n. , to strive or struggle against , to withstand , resist (rare and not ante-Aug.; syn.: resisto, adversor, reluctor). Lit. : quoniam alter motus alteri renititur, Plin. 2, 82, 84, § 198 ; 16, 42, 81, § 222 ;…

rĕ-no.grammar: āvi, ātum, 1 v. n. and a.
rĕ-no.opening: v. n. and a. , to swim back (very rare): per Stygias aquas, Albin. 1, 432 : simul imis saxa renarint Vadis levata, i. e. shall float back to the surface, Hor. Epod. 16, 25 : eodem renato stagno, Aug. Civ. Dei , 18, 17.†…

rēno.opening: or , , Celtic , a reindeer-skin , as a garment of the ancient Germans, a fur pelisse : renones sunt velamina umerorum et pectoris usque ad umbilicum atque intortis villis adeo hispida, ut imbrem respuant, Isid. Orig.…

rĕ-nōdis.opening: adj. nodus , unbound , loose : capillus, Capitol. Albin. 13 .

rĕ-nōdo.opening: , no perf. , , v. a. * (Like religo, I.) To bind back or behind ( = in nodum colligere): longam comam, Hor. Epod. 11, 28 ; v. Dillenb. and Orell. ad h. l. — To untie , unbind , loosen : teque (Dianam) renodatam…

rĕ-normātus.opening: Part. [normo], arranged or laid out anew : ager, Front. Col. p. 104 and 137 Goes.

rĕ-nosco.opening: v. a. , to recognize , Paul. Nol. Carm. 15, 342 .

rĕnŏvāmen.opening: renovo , a renewing , renewal : quorum Forma ... in hoc renovamine mansit, in that new condition, Ov. M. 8, 731 .

rĕnŏvātĭo.opening: id. . In gen., a renewing , renewal (Ciceron.): mundi, Cic. N. D. 2, 46, 118 : doctrinae, id. Brut. 71, 250 : timoris, id. Fam. 11, 18, 3 ; Vulg. Tit. 3, 5 .— In partic., in business lang., a renewing of interest ,…

rĕnŏvātīvum.grammar: fulgur vocatur, cum ex aliquo fulgure functio fieri coepit, si factum est simile fulgur, quod idem significet

rĕnŏvātor.opening: renovo , a renovator , restorer : OPERVM PVBLICORVM, Inscr. Fabr. p. 101 .

rĕ-nŏvello.opening: v. a. , to renew : vineam, i. e. to plant or set anew , Col. Arb. 6 .

rĕ-nŏvo.opening: v. a. , to renew , restore (class., esp. in the trop. sense; syn.: instauro, redintegro). Lit. : marc fontes assidue renovant, Lucr. 2, 591 ; cf.: quibus (vaporibus) altae renovataeque stellae atque omnis aether…

rĕ-nūbo.opening: v. n. , to marry again , Tert. ad Uxor. 1, 7 .

rĕ-nūdo.opening: v. a. , to uncover , make naked; to bare , strip (post-class.): bracchia umero tenus, App. M. 8, p. 214, 10 : puellam laciniis cunctis, id. ib. 2 , p. 122, 9; 8, p. 215, 37: tectum, parietes, januas, to uncover, open,…

rĕ-nūdus.opening: adj. , bare , Tert. Virg. Vel. 17 (others, nudae).

rĕ-nŭmĕro.opening: v. a. (anteand post-class.). Lit. , to count over , count up. — Hence, transf., to pay back , repay : aurum alicui, Plaut. Bacch. 1, 1, 12 ; 3, 4, 18 : omnem pecuniam patri, id. ib. 4, 2, 26 ; cf.: dotem huc, Ter. Hec.…

rēnuncŭlus.opening: dim. ren , a little kidney (only in plur. and late Lat.), Marc. Emp. 26 ; Vulg. Lev. 3, 4 ; 9, 10 .

rĕnuntĭātĭo.opening: ( ), , renuntio . Publicists' and jurid. t. t., a report , declaration , proclamation , notice , announcement (class.), Cic. Verr. 2, 1, 34, § 88 : Caesio renuntiat, se dedisse: cognoscite renuntiationem ex litteris…

rĕnuntĭātor.opening: ( ), , id. , a reporter , relater , proclaimer (late Lat.): consiliorum nostrorum renuntiatores, Dig. 48, 19, 38 : dispositionis infernae, Tert. Anim. 57 fin. : erroris tui, id. Pall. 4 , fin.

rĕ-nuntĭo.opening: ( ), , v. a. To bring or carry back word , to report , give notice , declare , announce. In gen. (rare and mostly ante-class.; syn. refero): quid nunc renuntiem abs te responsum, Chreme? Ter. Heaut. 4, 8, 18 : hoc alii…

rĕnuntĭus.opening: renuntio , one who brings back intelligence , a reporter (anteand post-class.), Plaut. Trin. 2, 1, 22 ; Cod. Th. 3, 7, 1.

rĕ-nŭo.grammar: ŭi, ĕre v. n. and a.
rĕ-nŭo.opening: v. n. and a. [nuo, whence nutum; abnuo], to nod back the head , to deny by a motion of the head; to deny , oppose , disapprove , reject , decline , refuse , = recusare (rare before the Aug. per.; syn.: abnuo, abnego).…

rĕnūto.opening: v. freq. n. [renuo], to decline , refuse (ante- and post-class.), Lucr. 4, 600 ; Prud. Ham. 774 .

rĕ-nutrĭo.opening: v. a. , to nourish again : aliquem, Paul. Nol. Ep. 23, 9 .

rĕnūtus.opening: renuo , a denying , refusal; a word formed by Pliny the Younger, for the Homeric ἀνένευσεν (Il. 16, 250): ego quoque simili nutu ac renutu respondere voto tuo possum, Plin. Ep. 1, 7, 2 .

rĕor.opening: (2 pers. pres. rere, Plaut. As. 3, 1, 22 ; id. Ep. 3, 4, 45 ; id. Trin. 2, 4, 13 ; Verg. A. 3, 381 ; 7, 437 ; Hor. S. 1, 9, 49 : reris, Plaut. Bacch. 5, 2, 9 ; Verg. A. 6, 97 ; Hor. S. 2, 3, 134 ), v. dep. a. [etym.…

rĕpāges.opening: poet. , = repagula, acc. to Paul. ex Fest. p. 280 , and Fest. p. 281 Müll.

rĕ-pāgŭla.opening: pag, pango, that which is thrust back again , bolts or bars of a door. Lit. : occludite aedes pessulis, repagulis, Plaut. Cist. 3, 18 : valvae clausae repagulis, Cic. Div. 1, 34, 74 : convulsis repagulis (templi)…

rĕpandĭ-rostrus.opening: adj. repandus-rostrum , with a turned-up snout : pecus Nerei, the dolphins or sea-calves , Pac. ap. Quint. 1, 5, 67 .

rĕ-pando.opening: v. n. , to open again , throw open : fores, App. M. 3, p. 150, 37 ; 9 , p. 226, 20.

rĕ-pandus.opening: adj. , bent backwards , turned up (syn.: recurvus, reduncus): lascivire pecus . . . rostrique repandum, with turned-up snouts (dolphins, seacalves), Lucil. ap. Non. 159, 1 (cf. repandirostrus): dorsum (delphini), Plin.…

rĕ-pango.opening: v. a. , to set in , plant : semen ferulae, Col. 5, 10, 14 ; id. Arb. 22 fin.

rĕpărābĭlis.opening: adj. reparo , that may be repaired , restored , or regained; retrievable , reparable (mostly poet. ; not anteAug.): damnum, Ov. M. 1, 379 ; id. Am. 1, 14, 55 : laesa pudicitia, id. H. 5, 103 : caelum, Val. Fl. 6, 562 :…

rĕpărātĭo.opening: reparo , a restoration , renewal : THERMARVM, Inscr. Orell. 1147 : vitae, Prud. Cath. 10, 128 .

rĕpărātor.opening: id. , a restorer , renovator : aevi, Stat. S. 4, 1, 11 : ORBIS, Inscr. Orell. 1103 .

rĕ-parco.opening: ( ), , v. n. , to be sparing with any thing; to spare , to refrain or abstain from (ante- and post-class.): utinam a principio rei pepercisses meae, Ut nunc repercis saviis, Plaut. Truc. 2, 4, 25 (where Speng.…

rĕ-păro.opening: v. a. , to get , acquire , or procure again; to recover , retrieve; to restore , repair , renew (not freq. till after the Aug. per.; not in Cæs.; cf.: recupero, redimo, reficio). Lit. : id perdere videbatur, quod alio…

rĕ-pasco.opening: v. n. , to feed or nourish again (late Lat.): divitem impendiis, Paul. Nol. Ep. 44, 1 fin. : parentes, id. Carm. 21, 853 .

rĕpastĭnātĭo.opening: repastino . Lit. , agricult. t. t., a digging up again : quid fossiones agri repastinationesque proferam? Cic. Sen. 15, 53 ; Col. 2, 2, 13 .— * Trop. , a revising , pruning , Tert. Exhort. ad Cast. 6 fin.

rĕ-pastĭno.opening: (old inf. repastinassere, Afran. Com. 288 ), , v. a. Lit. , agricult. t. t., to dig again , to dig or delve anew; to dig around , trench , grub , Varr. R. R. 1, 18, 8 ; 1, 37, 4 ; Col. 3, 18 ; 4, 32, 3 ; Plin. 13, 13,…

rĕ-patrĭo.opening: v. n. , to return to one ' s country , go home again (late Lat.): cum multi captivorum intacti repatriaverint, Sol. 27 : hinc ad Pelusium, id. 33 : ad Romanum imperium, Cassiod. Var. 3, 18 .

rĕ-pecto.opening: , no perf. , , v. a. , to comb again , to comb ( poet. ): jubas, Stat. Th. 6, 418 : in liquidos fontes se barba repectit, Claud. Cons. Prob. et Olybr. 222: coma repexa, Ov. A. A. 3, 154 : crinis, Claud. Cons. Prob. et…

rĕpĕdābĭlis.opening: adj. repedo , giving way , yielding : arbor, Ven. Vit. S. Mart. 1, 266 .

rĕ-pĕdo.opening: v. n. pes , to go or step back , to turn back , retreat , recoil (anteand post-class.): repedare, recedere, Fest. pp. 280 and 281 Müll.: redisse ac repedasse, Lucil. ap. Non. 165, 13 : Romam, id. 165, 13 : ad signa…

rĕ-pello.opening: (less correctly repuli), , v. a. , to drive , crowd , or thrust back; to reject , repulse , repel , etc., = reicere (freq. and class.; syn.: reicio, repono, removeo). Lit. : eum ego meis Dictis malis his foribus atque…

rĕ-pendo.opening: v. a. , to weigh back (syn. compenso). Lit. (rare): aequaque formosae pensa rependis erae, you weigh back, return by weight, the wool weighed out, Ov. H. 9, 78 : pensa, Prop. 4 (5), 7, 41. Ravenna ternos (asparagos)…

rĕpensātĭo.opening: repenso , a recompense : vicissitudinis, Salv in Avar. 4, 3.

rĕpensātrix.opening: repensator , she who recompenses , Mart. Cap. 9, 304 .

rĕpenso.opening: v. freq. a. rependo, II. B. . Lit. , to weigh against : illud sacrosanctum caput Tribuni plebis percussoribus auro repensatum est, Flor. 8, 15, 6 (dub.).— Transf. , to make up for , counterbalance , recompense…

rĕpentīnālĭter.opening: adv. repentinus , suddenly (late Lat.), Fulg. Myth. 3, 2 .

rĕpentīnus.opening: adj. repens , sudden , hasty , unlooked for , unexpected (freq. and class.): adventus hostium (opp. exspectatus), Cic. Rep. 2, 3, 6 ; so (opp. meditata et praeparata) id. Off. 1, 8, 27 : unde iste amor tam improvisus ac…

rĕpercussĭbĭlis.opening: adj. repercutio , that can be struck back , that can rebound , Cael. Aur. Tard. 1, 1, 45 ; 3, 6 fin.

rĕpercussĭo.opening: id. , a rebounding , repercussion : vicinorum siderum, i. e. reflection, Sen. Q. N. 7, 19 .

rĕpercussus.opening: repercutio , a rebounding , reverberation , repercussion , of light, sound, wind, etc.; reflection , echo , counter-pressure : solis, Plin. 5, 5, 5, § 35 ; Plin. Ep. 2, 17, 17 : Etesiarum, Plin. 5, 9, 10, § 55 :…

rĕ-percŭtĭo.opening: v. a. , to strike , push , or drive back , cause to rebound; to reflect , reverberate , re-echo , resound (not ante-Aug.; cf.: repello, reflecto). Lit. , of light, sound, etc.: gemmae Clara repercusso reddebant lumina…

rĕ-pĕrĭo.opening: (less correctly reperi), rĕpertum, 4 (old fut. reperibit, Caecil. ap. Non. 508, 16 : reperibitur, Plaut. Ep. 1, 2, 48 ; Pompon. ap. Non. 1 . 1.; inf. reperirier, Plaut. Truc. 4, 1, 1 ; Lucr. 4, 480 ), v. a. pario…

rĕpertīcĭus.opening: adj. reperio , accidentally met or found , random : quasi unus reliquus ex familiā Scipionis, ac non reperticius civis, Sal. ap. Cic. Decl. 1, 1 .

rĕpertĭo.opening: id. , an invention , device : rhetoricae, App. Flor, 4, p. 360, 12 Hild. (dub.; al. repertoribus).

rĕpertor.opening: id. II. B. 2. , a discoverer , inventor , deviser , author (not in Cic. or Cæs.; cf. inventor): vitis, i. e. Bacchus, Varr. R. R. 1, 2, 19 ; Ov. Am. 1, 3, 11 : mellis, id. F. 3, 762 : carminis et medicae opis, Phoebus,…

rĕpertōrĭum.opening: reperio , an inventory , catalogue , repertory (post-class.), Dig. 26, 7, 7 .

rĕpertrix.opening: repertor , she that finds out , an inventress : artium (Minerva), Hier. Ep. 46, 1 : omnium artium paupertas, App. Mag. p. 285, 35 ; absol. : Ecclesia, Tert. Pudic. 7 fin.

rĕpertus.opening: reperio (Appuleian). A finding again : filiae, App. M. 11, p. 257 .— A discovery , invention , App. M. 11, p. 262, 22 ; id. Flor. p. 341, 15 .

rĕpĕtentĭa.opening: repeto , memory , remembrance , Arn. 2 , pp. 61 and 62 (but in Lucr. 3, 851 , the correct read. is retinentia).

rĕpĕtītĭo.opening: id. . A demanding back , reclamation , Dig. 50, 17, 41 ; App. Mag. p. 332, 4 ; hence, repetitionem habere, i.e. jus repetendi, Dig. 3, 6, 3 .— A repetition , in speaking or writing: repetitio frequentior ejusdem…

rĕpĕtītor.opening: repeto , one that demands back , a reclaimer : nuptae ademptae, Ov. H. 8, 19 .

rĕ-pĕto.grammar: īvi or ĭi, ītum, 3 v. a.
rĕ-pĕto.opening: v. a. , to fall upon or attack again or anew , to strike again (syn. repercutio). Lit. (in gen. not till after the Aug. per.): regem repetitum saepius cuspide ad terram affixit, after he had repeatedly attacked him,…

rĕ-pignĕro.opening: ( ), , v. n. , to redeem a pledge , Dig. 13, 6, 5, § 12 ; Paul. ex Fest. s. v. reluere, p. 280, and Fest. p. 281 Müll.

rĕ-pigro.opening: , no perf. , , v. a. To make slothful : uxoris Cyllenius fotibus repigratus, Mart. Cap. 1, § 35 .— Trop. , to check , keep back , retard (post-class.): dirarum bestiarum impetum, App. M. 8, p. 208, 19 ; p. 175 Bip.:…

rĕ-pingo.opening: v. a. , to paint or form again (late Lat.): oculos, Ven. Vit. S. Mart. 1, 172 : arma crucis digitis, id. ib. 1, 246 .

rĕ-plaudo.opening: v. a. , to strike on or against (Appuleian): frontem replaudens, App. M. 1, p. 105, 15 ; 6 , p. 185, 7.

rē^-plĕo.opening: (contr. form replesti, Stat. S. 3, 1, 92 : replerat, Lucr. 6, 1270 ), , v. a. To fill again , refill; to fill up , replenish , complete , etc. Lit. (class.): exhaustas domos, Cic. Prov. Cons. 2, 4 : exhaustum aerarium,…

rĕplētĭo.opening: repleo, I. , a filling up , complement , Isid. 4, 6, 11 ; Cod. Just. 6, 28, 4 ; 7, 2, 15, § 4 .

rē^plētus.opening: Part. and P. a. , from repleo.

rē^-plexus.opening: Part. [plecto], bent or turned back : cauda, Plin. 20, 1, 3, § 7 (Jahn, reflexa).

rĕplĭcābĭlis.opening: adj. replico , worth repeating (late Lat.): nomen, Ven. Carm. 7, 8, 33; Serv. Verg. A. 1, 161 .

rĕplĭcātĭo.opening: id. . * A folding or rolling back again (of a book). Transf. : ut replicatione quādam mundi motum regat atque tueatur, qs. by winding it up again , Cic. N. D. 1, 13, 33 .— In jurid. Lat., a reply , replication , Just.…

rĕ-plĭco.opening: (e. g. Vulg. Gen. 4, 27 ; id. Jos. 8, 35 al. ), ātum (collat. form, replictae tunicae, Stat. S. 4, 9, 29 ), , v. a. , to fold or roll back , to bend or turn back (cf.: revolvo, reflecto). Lit. : vel Euhemero replicato,…

replum.opening: a bolt for covering the commissure of the folding-door , Vitr. 4, 6 ; 10, 17 .

rĕ-plumbo.opening: , no perf. , , v. a. , to free from lead , to unsolder (post-Aug.), Dig. 34, 2, 19 ; 34, 2, 32 ; Sen. Q. N. 4, 2, 18 .

rĕ-plūmis.opening: adj. pluma , covered again with feathers , fledged anew : corpus (aquilae), Paul. Nol. Carm. 21, 857 .

rĕ-plŭo.opening: v. n. , to rain down again : caelo, Musa ap. Sen. Contr. 5 praef. med.

rēpo.opening: v. n. Gr. ἕρπω; Sanscr. root sarp-, creep; cf. Lat. serpo, serpens , to creep , crawl (cf. serpo). Lit. Of animals: repens animans, Lucr. 3, 388 : cochleae inter saxa, Sall. J. 93, 2 : millipeda, Plin. 29, 6, 39, § 136…

rĕ-pŏlĭo.opening: v. a. , to clean again : frumenta (with repurgare), Col. 2, 20 fin.

rĕ-pondĕro.opening: v. a. , to weigh in return; trop., to repay , return (late Lat.): studii vicissitudinem tibi, Sid. Ep. 1, 4 fin. : gloriam tibi, id. ib. 5, 1 : pro falsitate alicui veritatem, Claud. Mam. Stat. An. 3, 15 .

rĕ-pōno.opening: ( perf. reposivi, Plaut. As. 3, 1, 16 ; part. sync. repostus, a, um, on account of the metre, Lucr. 1, 35 ; 3, 346 ; Verg. G. 3, 527 ; id. A. 1, 26 ; 6, 59 ; 655 ; 11, 149; Hor. Epod. 9, 1 ; Sil. 7, 507 al. ), v. a. ,…

rĕ-porrĭgo.opening: v. a. , to reach forth or hand again : phialam, Petr. 51, 2 .

rĕ-porto.opening: v. a. , to bear , carry , or bring back (class.; syn. refero). Lit. In gen.: alii vini amphoras, quas plenas tulerunt, eas argento repletas domum reportaverunt, C. Gracch. ap. Gell. 15, 12, 4 ; so, aurum ab Theotimo…

rĕ-posco.opening: v. a. , to demand back , to ask for again , as something belonging to one (class.); constr. aliquid; aliquid ab aliquo; more freq., aliquem aliquid , and absol. Lit. : dedisti eam dono mihi: Eandem nunc reposcis, Plaut.…

rĕposco.opening: 1. reposco , one who makes a demand , who urges a claim , a dun : acerrimi, Amm. 22, 16, 23 .

rĕpŏsĭtĭo.opening: repono, I. C. , a laying up , storing up (late Lat.): faeni, palearum, etc., Pall. 1, 32 .

rĕpŏsĭtōrĭum.opening: ( , Capitol. M. Aur. 17 ), , repono , that on or in which any thing is placed or laid. A stand , tray , or waiter on which the dishes were brought to the table, Petr. 33 sq. ; Sen. Ep. 78, 23 ; Plin. 33, 11, 49, § 140 ;…

rĕpŏsĭtus.opening: Part. and P. a. of repono, q. v. fin.

rĕpostor.opening: repono, I. A. , a restorer : templorum, Ov. F. 2, 63 .

rĕpostus.opening: Part. and P. a. of repono.

rĕpōtātĭo.opening: , a false read. for repotia, Varr. L. L. 6, § 84 Müll.; cf. id. ib. 5, § 122 .

rĕ-pōtĭa.opening: poto , an after-drinking, i. e., A drinking or carousing on the day after an entertainment , at a wedding, a birth, or other festive occasion. Hor. S. 2, 2, 60 Acro; Gell. 2, 24, 14 ; Aus. Ep. 9 fin. ; Fest. s. h. v.…

rĕpraesentātĭo.opening: repraesento . A bringing before one; a showing , exhibiting , manifesting; a representation (post-Aug.): plus est evidentia, vel ut alii dicunt, repraesentatio, quam perspicuitas, Quint. 8, 3, 61 ; cf. Plin. 9, 6, 5, §…

rĕpraesentātor.opening: id. , a representative : patris (filius), Tert. adv. Prax. 24 .

rĕ-praesento.opening: v. a. To bring before one , to bring back; to show , exhibit , display , manifest , represent (class.): per quas (visiones) imagines rerum absentium ita repraesentantur animo, ut eas cernere oculis ac praesentes habere…

rĕ-prĕhendo.opening: ( , , or ; cf. prehendo. Examples of the contracted form among the poets are, Lucil. ap. Non. 427, 31 ; Ov. H. 11, 53 ; Hor. Ep. 1, 18, 39 ; id. S. 1, 10, 55 al. ), , v. a. , to hold back , hold fast , take hold of ,…

rĕ-prĕhensĭbĭlis.opening: adj. reprehendo , blamable , reprehensible (late Lat.): ebrietas, Salv. Gub. Dei , 4, 14; Lact. 4, 28, 8 ; Vulg. Gal. 2, 11 .

rĕprĕhensĭo.opening: id. , a holding back , trop. * A checking , check , in speaking: (orationem) concinnam ... festivam, sine intermissione, sine reprehensione, sine varietate, Cic. de Or. 3, 25, 100 .— Blame , censure , reprimand ,…

rĕprĕhenso.opening: v. freq. a. id. , to hold back continually , detain from time to time (very rare, perh. ἅπ. εἰρ ): reprehensans singulos, Liv. 2, 10, 3 Weissenb. ad loc.

rĕprĕhensor.opening: id. , a blamer , censurer , reprehender : restat unum genus reprehensorum, etc., Cic. Ac. 2, 3, 7 ; id. Opt. Gen. 6, 18 : comitiorum, id. Planc. 3, 8 : delicti, Ov. H. 17, 219 : id factum non accusatore tantum, sed…

rĕpressor.opening: reprimo , a restrainer , represser; a limiter (very rare): caedis cottidianae, * Cic. Sest. 69, 144 : tributorum, Eutr. 10, 8 .

rĕ-prĭmo.opening: v. a. , to press back , keep back; to check , curb , restrain (class., partic. in the trop. sense; cf.: repello, refuto). Lit. : illa praedicta Veientium, si lacus Albanus redundasset, Romam periturum; si repressus…

rĕprŏbātĭo.opening: reprobo , rejection , reprobation (eccl. Lat.), Tert. Apol. 13 ; id. adv. Marc. 4, 35 fin. : Vulg. Heb. 7, 18 .

rĕprŏbātrix.opening: reprobator , she that condemns or reprobates (eccl. Lat.): superbiae (disciplina), Tert. adv. Marc. 4, 36 .

rĕ-prŏbo.opening: , no perf. , , v. a. , to disapprove , reject , condemn (post-Aug.; not in Cicero, for in Fin. 1, 7, 23, the correct reading is: et probet, v. Madv. ad h. l.; and in Quint. 6, prooem. § 3 , Halm reads: dis…

rĕ-prŏbus.opening: adj. , false , spurious (late Lat.): nummi, pecunia, Dig. 13, 7, 24 : homines circa fidem, Vulg. 2 Tim. 3, 8 .

rĕprōmissĭo.opening: repromitto , in business lang., a counter-promise (syn. restipulatio), Cic. Rosc. Com. 13, 39 , and 18, 56; Vulg. Ecclus. 29, 24 ; id. Rom. 4, 20 .

rĕprōmissŏr.opening: id. , one who answers or promises in return; a surety , bail , Vulg. Ecclus. 29, 21 sq. : vitae aeternae, Ambros. Fid. 4, 11, 154 .

rĕ-prōmitto.opening: v. a. Lit. , mercant. t. t., to promise in return , to engage or bind one ' s self : repromittam istoc tibi nomine solutam rem futuram, Plaut. As. 2, 4, 48 ; id. Curc. 5, 2, 67 ; Cic. Rosc. Com. 13, 39 ; Suet. Claud. 20…

rĕ-prŏpĭtĭo.opening: v. a. , to propitiate again , make propitiation for (late Lat.): imagines Caesarum, Tert. ad Nat. 1, 17 ; Vulg. Lev. 19, 22 : tu repropitiaberis, id. 3 Reg. 8, 39 ; id. Heb. 2, 17 .

reptābundus.opening: adj. repto , creeping , crawling (post-Aug.): effusus in voluptates, reptabundus (al. vagabundus) semper atque ebrius, Sen. Vit. Beat. 12 .— Trop. : (virtutem) ex intervallo ingenti reptabundus sequar, Sen. Vit. Beat.…

reptātĭo.opening: id. , a creeping , crawling : infantium per manus et genua, Quint. 1, 12, 10 .

reptātus.opening: id. , a creeping , crawling (post-Aug., and only in abl. sing. ). Lit. : spumans limacum, Tert. Anim. 10 med. — Transf. , of plants: vitium, Plin. 14, 1, 3, § 13 .

reptĭlis.opening: adj. repo , creeping , reptile : cochleae, Sid. Ep. 3, 12 .— Neutr. as subst. : , , a reptile , Vulg. Gen. 1, 24 ; id. Deut. 4, 18 .

repto.opening: v. freq. n. and a. [id.], to creep , crawl (mostly poet. and postAug.; a favorite word with Claud.). Neutr. Lit. , of animals and men, Plin. 9, 30, 50, § 95 : chamaeleon humi reptans, Gell. 10, 12, 2 : anguis reptans,…

rĕ-pūbesco.opening: v. inch. n. , to grow young again; trop., with revirescere, Col. 2, 1, 4 .

rĕpŭdĭātĭo.opening: repudio , a rejection , refusal , disdaining (rare, but good prose): supplicum, Cic. Mur. 4, 9 : fideicommissi, Cod. Just. 6, 42, 26 .— Absol. : mihi simulatio pro repudiatione fuerit, Cic. Att. 12, 51, 2 .

rĕpŭdĭātor.opening: id. , a rejecter , contemner : Creatoris, Tert. adv. Marc. 1, 14 .

rĕpŭdĭo.opening: v. a. repudium , t. t. Of persons married or betrothed, to cast off , put away , divorce , repudiate (cf. reicio): sponsas admodum adulescens duas habuit ... priorem ... virginem adhuc repudiavit, Suet. Claud. 26 :…

rĕpŭdĭōsus.opening: adj. repudium , that ought to be rejected or disdained : nuptiae, scandalous, offensive, Plaut. Pers. 3, 1, 56 Ritschl.

rĕ-pŭdĭum.opening: pudet , t. t., of married or betrothed parties, a casting off , putting away of the opposite party; a dissolution of the marriage contract , a separation , divorce , repudiation : inter divortium et repudium hoc…

rĕ-pŭĕrasco.opening: v. inch. n. , to become a boy again. Lit. : quia repuerascis, Novat. ap. Non. 165, 25 (Com. Rel. p. 215 Rib.): si quis mihi deus largiatur, ut ex hac aetate repuerascam et in cunis vagiam, Cic. Sen. 23, 83 .— Trop. , to…

rĕpugnans.opening: Part. and P. a. , v. repugno.

rĕpugnanter.opening: adv. , v. repugno, P. a. fin.

rĕpugnātĭo.opening: repugno , a resistance , opposition , App. Dogm. Plat. 1, p. 9 .

rĕpugnātōrĭus.opening: adj. id. , of or pertaining to resistance , defensive : res, means of defence, Vitr. 10, 22 .

rĕ-pugno.opening: v. n. , to fight against , oppose; to make resistance , resist , defend one ' s self (class.; syn.: adversor, resisto, renitor). Lit. : nostri primo integris viribus fortiter repugnare, Caes. B. G. 3, 4 ; so in milit.…

rĕ-pullesco.opening: v. inch. n. [pullus], to bud or sprout forth again , Col. 4, 22, 5 ; 4, 24, 4 .

rĕ-pullŭlo.opening: v. n. , to sprout forth again , Plin. 16, 10, 19, § 46 ; 16, 44, 90, § 241 ; Isid. 17, 6 , n. 10.

rĕpulsa.opening: repello; prop. Part., sc. petitio ; publicists' t. t., a refusal , denial , repulse in soliciting for an office: Catonem veteres inimicitiae Caesaris incitant et dolor repulsae, Caes. B. C. 1, 4 : omnes magistratus sine…

rĕpulsĭo.opening: repello . Lit. , a repelling , resistance : violentiae per vim, Isid. 5, 4, 2 . — Transf. , a refutation (late Lat.), Cael. Aur. Tard. 2, 7 fin.

rĕ-pulso.opening: v. freq. [id.], to drive back or beat back again , to repel again and again. Lit. : civitas eloquiis caelestibus magis quam corporis voluptatibus hostiles impetus repulsare consueta, Ambros. in Psa. 118 , Serm. 22, § 37…

rĕpulsor.opening: id. , he who repels or drives back , Ambros. in Job, 4, 11, 29; id. in Psa. 118 , Serm. 2, § 22.

rĕpulsōrĭus.opening: adj. id. , driving or forcing back , repulsory : cohortes, Amm. 24, 4, 7 .—As subst. : , , , a means of driving back , Ambros. in Psa. 118 , Serm. 4, § 15 fin.

rĕpulsus.opening: repello , a driving back , repulsion , rebounding , reflection , reverberation (of light, sound, etc.; poet. ; usually in abl. sing. ): (effigies) assiduo crebroque repulsu Rejectae, Lucr. 4, 106 : lucis, Claud. Cons.…

rĕ-pūmĭcātĭo.opening: f [pumico], a making smooth again; a smoothing , polishing : repumicatio et quaedam politura gemmarum, i. e. a trimming off of the buds, Plin. 17, 26, 39, § 246 .

rĕpungo.opening: v. a. , to prick or goad again; trop.: leviter illorum animos, Cic. Fam. 1, 9, 19 .

rĕpurgĭum.opening: repurgo , a cleansing again , a cleaning out (late Lat.): formarum (aquaeductuum), Cod. Th. 15, 2, 1; Cod. Just. 11, 42, 1 .

rĕ-purgo.opening: v. a. Lit. , to clean , cleanse , or clear again (not anteAug.): iter, Liv. 44, 4 fin. : alveum Tiberis, Suet. Aug. 30 : ergastula, id. Tib. 8 : os, mox dentes, Plin. 8, 25, 37, § 90 : nomas, id. 23, 4, 38, § 78 :…

rĕpŭtātĭo.opening: reputo (post-Aug.). A reckoning , computation , Dig. 46, 3, 48 . —In plur. , Dig. 10, 2, 19 ; 27, 2, 2 .— A thinking over , pondering , considering , consideration (cf.: cogitatio, consideratio): sed me veterum…

rĕ-pūtesco.opening: v. inch. n. , to become stinking again , Tert. Anim. 32 .

rĕ-pŭto.opening: v. a. , to count over , reckon , calculate , compute (syn.: numero, expendo). Lit. (mostly post-Aug.): solis defectiones, Cic. Rep. 1, 16, 25 : tempora, Tac. H. 2, 50 : annos infantiae, Plin. 7, 50, 51, § 167 :…

rĕ-quĭes.opening: ( gen. requieï, Ambros. Parad. 3, 19 ; cf. Prisc. p. 704 P., and Val. Prob. II. p. 1460 ib.: requie, Sall. Fragm. ap. Prisc. p. 781 ib., or id. H. 1, 97 Dietsch), , qs. after-rest , i. e. rest , repose from labor,…

rĕ-quĭesco.opening: (sync. requierant, Cat. 84, 7 : requierunt, Verg. E. 8, 4 : requiesset, Cat. 64, 176 : requiesse, Liv. 26, 22 ), v. n. and a. Neutr. , to rest one ' s self , to rest , repose (very freq. and class.). Lit. , Plaut. Ep.…

rĕquĭētĭo.opening: requiesco , rest (late Lat.): septimo requietionis anno, i. e. in the Sabbatical year , Jov. ap. Hier. in Jov. 2, 18 : sabbatum enim requietionis est, Vulg. Lev. 16, 31 ; id. Act. 7, 49 .

rĕquĭētōrĭum.opening: id. I. A. 2 , a resting-place , sepulchre , requietory , Inscr. Oreli. 4533.

rĕquĭētus.opening: Part. and P. a. of requiesco.

rĕquīrĭto.opening: v. freq. a. , to ask after , inquire for any thing: res novas, Plaut. Most. 4, 3, 11 .

rĕ-quīro.grammar: sīvi or sii, sītum, 3 v. a.
rĕ-quīro.opening: v. a. quaero , to seek again; to look after , to seek or search for; to seek to know , to ask or inquire after (class.; cf.: repeto, reposco, exploro). In gen.: Ph. Quid quaeritas? Ha. Vestigium hic requiro, Qua, etc.,…

rĕquīsītĭo.opening: requiro , a searching , examination : historiae antiquioris, Gell. 18, 2, 6 .

rēs.opening: (rēi with e long; gen. , Lucr. 2, 112 ; 548 ; 6, 918 ; dat. , id. 1, 688 ; 2, 236 ; rei, gen. , monosyl. at the end of the verse, Lucr. 3, 918 ; and in the middle of the verse, id. 4, 885 , and Poët. ap. Lact. 6, 6 ),…

rĕ-saevĭo.opening: v. n. , to rage again , Ov. Tr. 1, 1, 103 .

rĕsălūtātĭo.opening: resaluto , a greeting or salutation in return , Suet. Ner. 37 fin.

rĕ-sălūto.opening: v. a. , to greet or salute in return , return a salutation , Cic. Phil. 2, 41, 106 ; Mart. 5, 21, 3 ; 5, 57, 2 ; 10, 70, 5 ; Petr. 44, 10 ; Sen. Tranq. 12 ; Vulg. Gen. 43, 27 .

rĕ-salvāre.opening: v. a. , to save again , redeem : animam suam, Hier. Ep. 98, 21 fin. : resalvati ex monte Zion, Aug. Civ. Dei , 18, 31, 1.

rĕ-sānesco.opening: v. inch. n. , to grow sound again , to heal again; trop.: error animi, Ov. Am. 1, 10, 9 ; Lact. 5, 2, 6 .

rĕ-sāno.opening: v. a. , to make sound again , to heal again (post-class.); trop.: impios, Lact. 4, 20, 1 ; cf. id. 5, 22 fin. : phreneticos symphonia, Mart. Cap. 9, § 926 ; 3, § 224 .

rĕ-sarcĭo.opening: , no perf. , , v. a. , to patch or mend again; to repair , restore (rare; not in Cic.; cf. sarcio). Lit. : discidit vestem? resarcietur, Ter. Ad. 1, 2, 41 ; Tib. 1, 10, 61 : fracta juga vitium, Col. 11, 2, 38 : tecta,…

rĕ-sarrĭo.opening: v. a. , to hoe again : campos, Plin. 18, 20, 49, § 183 (Jahn, reseverunt).

rē-scindo.opening: v. a. , to cut off , cut loose , cut or break down; to cut or tear open (freq. and class.). Lit. : pontem, i. e. to break down, Caes. B. G. 1, 7 ; 4, 19 fin. ; 6, 29; 7, 35; 7, 58 fin. ; Nep. Milt. 3, 4 ; Liv. 2, 10 ;…
