rĕ-sulco.opening: v. a. , to furrow or plough again ( poet. ): vulnera, to scratch open , Prud. στεφ. 5, 141.

rĕsultātĭo.opening: resulto , a reverberation , echo : grata et consona, Ambros. Hexaëm. 3, 5, 11: laetitiae, id. in Psa. praef. § 9: blanda, Cassiod. Var. 2, 40 .— Trop. , a resistance , refusal , Cassiod. Var. 2, 24 .

rĕsultātor.opening: id. , one who resists or denies (late Lat.), Cassiod. in Psa. 9, 27 .

rĕsulto.opening: , no perf. , ātum, 1, v. freq. n. and a. [resilio], to spring or leap back , to rebound ( poet. and in post-Aug. prose; only of inanimate or abstract subjects). Lit. : (corpora) conflicta resultant, etc., Lucr. 2, 98…

rĕ-sum.opening: = resideo, assumed as pres. for the var. l. l. resit, Cic. Scaur. 8, 14 , where B. and K. read residet; and reesset, Cic. Verr. 2, 2, 58, § 143 , B. and K. esset.

rĕ-sūmo.opening: v. a. , to take up again , take back , resume ( poet. and in post-Aug. prose). Lit. (terra) gentes omnis peperit et resumit denuo, Enn. ap. Varr. L. L. 5, § 64 Müll. (Epich. v. 4 Vahl. p. 168): positas (tabellas)…

rĕsumptĭo.opening: resumo , a restoration , recovery of a sick person, Cael. Aur. Acut. 2, 37 fin.

rĕsumptīvus.opening: adj. id. , restorative : odoramenta, Cael. Aur. Tard. 4, 3, 75 : cyclus, id. ib. 2, 1, 47 .

rĕsumptōrĭus.opening: adj. id. , restorative : adjutoria, Cael. Aur. Acut. 3, 8 fin.

rĕ-sŭpīno.opening: , no perf. , , v. a. , to bend or turn back (rare; not in Cic.). Lit. : puer ad me accurrit, Pone apprehendit pallio, resupinat, Ter. Phorm. 5, 6, 23 : assurgentem ibi regem umbone resupinat, Liv. 4, 19 : hominem, Cels.…

rĕ-sŭpīnus.opening: adj. , bent back or backwards , lying on one ' s back or with the face upwards , supine (not in Cic.). Lit. : resupinum in caelo contueri, i. e. lying on one ' s back , face upwards , supine , Att. ap. Cic. Div. 1, 22,…

rĕ-surgo.opening: v. n. , to rise or raise one ' s self again , to appear again ( poet. and post-Aug.; once in Liv. with velut; v. infra ). Lit. : pugnat resurgere saepe, Ov. M. 5, 349 : si resurgat centimanus Gyges, Hor. C. 2, 17, 14 ;…

rĕsurrectĭo.opening: resurgo , in eccl. Lat., a rising again from the dead , resurrection , Tert. Res. Carn. 1 ; Aug. Civ. Dei , 22, 28; Vulg. Matt. 22, 23 ; id. Rom. 3, 4 ; Lact. 4, 19, 9 ; 4, 20, 4 : dominica (i. e. Domini), Sulp. Sev.…

rĕsuscĭtātĭo.opening: resuscito , in eccl. Lat., a raising again from the dead , resuscitation , Tert. Res. Carn. 30 .

rĕsuscĭtātor.opening: id. , in eccl. Lat., one who raises again from the dead , a resuscitator , Tert. Res. Carn. 12 .

rĕ-suscĭto.opening: v. a. , to raise up again , rebuild : templum, Lact. 4, 18, 5 .— To rouse again , revive , resuscitate , freq. in the Christian writers, of the resurrection of the dead, Hier. in Psa. 33, 5 ; id. Ep. 103 ; Tert. Res.…

rĕ-sūtus.opening: Part. [suo], ripped open : tunica ex utrāque parte, Suet. Aug. 94 .

rētae.opening: trees standing on the bank or in the bed of a stream , acc. to Gabius ap. Gell. 11, 17, 4 .— From this is said to come the verb retare, to clear , free from obstructions , in an old edict: flumina retanda; v. Gell. l. l.

rĕ-tālĭo.opening: v. a. , to retaliate : quod imprudentiā factum est, retaliari per imprudentiam debet, Gell. 20, 1, 16 .

rĕ-tango.opening: v. a. , to touch again or repeatedly : faciem spongiā, Cael. Aur. Tard. 2, 13, 156 .

rĕtardātĭo.opening: retardo , a hindering , delaying , retarding , Cic. Phil. 5, 11, 30 (with mora).— In plur. , Vitr. 9, 1, 6 .

rĕ-tardo.grammar: āvi, ātum, 1 v. a. and n.
rĕ-tardo.opening: v. a. and n. Act. , to keep back , hinder , delay , detain , impede , retard (class.; a favorite word with Cic., esp. in the trop. signif.; syn. moror). Lit. : quarum (stellarum vagarum) motus tum incitantur, tum…

rĕ-taxo.opening: v. a. , to censure , reprove , Suet. Vesp. 13 .

rĕ-tĕgo.opening: v. a. To uncover , bare , open (not freq. till after the Aug. period; syn.: nudo, exuo). Lit. : thecam nummariam, Cic. Att. 4, 7, 2 : (area) retecta, unroofed, Varr. R. R. 1, 51, 2 : vultus scisso velamine, Luc. 8, 669…

rĕ-tendo.grammar: di, tum, or sum, 3 v. a.
rĕ-tendo.opening: v. a. , to release from tension , to unbend , slacken , relax (very rare; syn.: relaxo, resolvo). Lit. : lentos arcus, to unbend, Ov. M. 2, 419 ; Stat. S. 4, 4, 30 ; in the part. perf. : arcus retentus, Ov. M. 3, 166 :…

rĕtentātor.opening: 1. retento , a detainer , retainer , Cassiod. Var. 2, 10 .

rĕtentātrix.opening: retentator , she that retains , Macr. S. 7, 4 .

rĕtentĭo.opening: retineo , a keeping back , i. e., A holding back , holding in : aurigae, Cic. Att. 13, 21, 3 ; 13, 25, 1 .— Trop. , a withholding : assensionis (as a transl. of the Gr. ἐποχή ), Cic. Ac. 2, 18, 59 , and 2, 24, 78.— A…

rĕtento.opening: v. freq. a. id. , to hold back firmly , to keep back , to hold fast (rare; not in Cic.). Lit. : cur me retentas? Plaut. As. 3, 3, 1 ; id. Rud. 3, 6, 39 ; cf. agmen, Liv. 10, 5 : legiones, Tac. H. 4, 13 : fugientes, id.…

rĕ-tento.opening: ( ), , v. a. , to try or attempt again , to reattempt (a poet. word of the Aug. per.): timide verba intermissa retentat, Ov. M. 1, 746 : preces, id. ib. 14, 382 : fila lyrae, id. ib. 5, 117 : referoque manus iterumque…

rĕtentor.opening: retineo , one that holds back; a detainer , retainer (post-class.), App. Flor. p. 343, 10 .

rĕtentōrĭus.opening: adj. retentor , fitted to hold back , checking , restraining (late Lat.): virtus animae, Cassiod. Anim. 6 .

rĕtentus.opening: retineo , a holding fast , grasping : vivosque imitata retentus (manūus), Claud. in Rufin. 2, 438 .

rĕ-tergeo.opening: v. a. , to wipe out , cleanse , clear (late Lat.). Lit. : vulnera, Cael. Aur. Tard. 2, 14, 107 .— Transf. : fossas ruderibus obrutas, Amm. 29, 6, 11 .

rĕ-texo.opening: (retexi, Manil. 4, 214 dub.), , v. a. To unweave , unravel what has been woven (class.). Lit. : quasi Penelope telam retexens, Cic. Ac. 2, 29, 95 : tela retexta dolo, Ov. Am. 3, 9, 30 : telas, Stat. S. 3, 5, 9 .— Poet.…

rētĭārĭus.opening: rete , one who fights with a net , a net-fighter (a kind of gladiator, who endeavored to hold his adversary by throwing a net over his head), Quint. 6, 3, 61 ; Suet. Calig. 30 ; id. Claud. 34 ; Val. Max. 1, 7, 8 ;…

rĕtĭcentĭa.opening: reticeo , a keeping silent , silence (rare but good prose): quid taces? enicas me miserum tuā reticentiā, Plaut. Merc. 5, 2, 52 ; Pac. ap. Non. 1, 31 (Trag. Rel. p. 94 Rib.): posterorum, Cic. Phil. 14, 12, 33 : a…

rĕ-tĭcĕo.opening: v. n. and a. Neutr. , to be silent , keep silence (class.; syn.: sileo, obmutesco): cum Sulpicius reticuisset, etc., Cic. de Or. 2, 57, 232 : de Chelidone reticuit, quoad potuit, Cic. Verr. 2, 1, 53, § 139 : de…

rētĭcŭlātus.opening: adj. reticulum , made like a net , net-like , reticulated : fenestra, Varr. R. R. 3, 7, 3 : structura parietum, Vitr. 2, 8 ; Plin. 36, 22, 51, § 172 : distinctio concharum, id. 9, 33, 52, § 103 .

rētĭcŭlum.opening: (collat. form , , , Varr. R. R. 3, 5, 13 ; Fenest. ap. Non. 221, 33 ; Petr. 67, 6 ; Plin. 12, 14 , 32, § 59; also , , Vulg. Exod. 38, 5 et saep.), dim. rete , a little net , a cloth made like a net , a net-work bag for…

rētĭfex.opening: rete-facio , a netmaker (late Lat.), Alcim. Homil. Fragm. 3 .

rĕtĭnācŭlum.opening: (sync. retinaclum, Prud. ap. Symm. 2, 147 ), , retineo, I. , that which holds back or binds; a holdfast , band , tether , halter , halser , rope , cable (only in plur. ; but the sing. occurs as v. l. Amm. 30, 4, 4 ).…

rĕtĭnax.opening: adj. id. , holding back : arbor, Symm. Ep. 1, 41 .

rĕtĭnens.opening: Part. and P. a. of retineo.

rĕtĭnentĭa.opening: retineo, II. , a retaining in the memory , recollection : actarum rerum, Lucr. 3, 675 : nostri, id. 3, 851 .

rĕ-tĭnĕo.opening: v. a. teneo . (With the signif. of the re predominating.) To hold or keep back , not let go; to detain , retain; to restrain (class.; cf. restringo). Lit. : Ep. Asta, abire hinc non sinam. Th. Quid nunc me retines?…

rĕ-tinnĭo.opening: v. n. , to ring again , resound , Varr. R. R. 2 , praef. § 2: in vocibus nostrorum oratorum retinnit quiddam et resonat urbanius, Cic. Brut. 46, 171 .

rētĭŏlum.opening: dim. rete , a little net (post-class.), App. M. 8, p. 202, 33 ; Aug. Ep. 109, 10 ; Serv. Verg. A. 4, 138 .

rĕ-tollo.opening: v. a. , to take away again : triumphos, Coripp. Johan. 2, 329: signa, id. ib. 4, 1154 .

rĕ-tŏno.opening: v. n. , to thunder back , resound : loca fremitu, Cat. 63, 82 .

rĕ-tonsus.opening: Part. [tondeo], cut down , mown : segetes, Plin. 18, 17, 45, § 161 .

rĕ-torpesco.opening: v. inch. n. , to become torpid (late Lat.): pristini sensus, Tert. adv. Gnost. 1 med.

rĕ-torquĕo.opening: v. a. , to twist or bend back; to turn or cast back (class.; cf. reflecto). Lit. : caput in sua terga (anguis), Ov. M. 3, 68 : ora, id. ib. 4, 715 : ora ad os Phoebi, id. ib. 11, 163 : oculos saepe ad hanc urbem, * Cic.…

rĕ-torresco.opening: v. inch. n. , to parch or dry up , to wither : sata, Col. 3, 3, 4 ; 3, 5, 1 ; 3, 17, 4 .

rĕ-torrĭdus.opening: adj. , parched up , burned up , dried up (mostly post-Aug.; not in Cic.). Lit. : rami platani, Sen. Ep. 12, 2 ; 86, 18 : manus Mucii, id. ib. 66, 51 : retorrida et muscosa prata, Varr. R. R. 1, 9, 5 : plantae, Col. 3,…

rē^tractātĭo.opening: retracto . A taking in hand again; a retouching , revision , correction; so only Retractationes, the title of a work of Augustine.— Reconsideration , remembrance : eorum qui fuerunt retractatio non sine acerbitate…

rē^tractātor.opening: id. , a refuser : officii, Tert. Jejun. 15 dub.

rē^tractātus.opening: retracto , Tertullian; v. retractatio. A repetition , Tert. Praescr. 7 . — Hesitation , doubt : sine retractatu, Tert. Apol. 4 ; id. adv. Marc. 1, 1 fin. ; in plur. , id. Spect. 3 .

rē^tractĭo.opening: retraho . A drawing back , retreating : graduum, i. e. the breadth, Vitr. 3, 4, 4 .— Trop. A diminishing : dierum (opp. auctio), Macr. S. 1, 14 .— Hesitation , refusal : sine ullā retractione, Arn. 5, 162 .

rē^-tracto.opening: (in many MSS. also written ), , v. a. id. . To take hold of or handle again; to take in hand again , undertake anew , etc. (class.; esp. in the trop. sense). Lit. (mostly poet. ): arma, Liv. 2, 30 : ferrum, Verg. A. 7,…

rē^tractus.opening: retraho , a drawing back : machinae bellicae, Tert. adv. Gnost. 1 .

rē^-trādo.opening: v. a. , to deliver up again , restore (jurid. Lat.), Dig. 4, 2, 9 ; 19, 1, 6 ; 24, 3, 58 al.

rē^-trăho.opening: v. a. To draw back , withdraw; to call back (class.). Lit. : me retrahis, Plaut. Rud. 4, 3, 8 ; aliquem, Cic. Sen. 23, 83 ; Liv. 30, 20 ; 21, 63 (in the last two passages with revocare); 10, 25: bos domitus et…

rē^-trĭbŭo.opening: v. a. , to give back , return , restore , repay (class., but freq. only in eccl. Lat.; syn. remuneror). Lit. : corpora retribuat rebus recreetque fluentes, Lucr. 5, 275 : populo pecuniam acceptam, Liv. 2, 41, 8 :…

rē^trĭbūtĭo.opening: retribuo , recompense , repayment , retribution (eccl. Lat.): mali pro bono, Aug. Civ. Dei, 22, 23: vitae aeternae, Tert. Apol. 18 : meritorum, Sid. Ep. 4, 11 : contumeliae, Lact. 6, 18, 27 ; Vulg. Psa. 136, 8 .

rē^trĭbūtor.opening: id. , a recompenser , requiter , retributer (eccl. Lat.), Tert. adv. Marc. 4, 29 ; 5, 16 : gratia retributoris, Paul. Nol. Ep. 2, 4 .

retricibus.grammar: cum ait Cato, aquam eo nomine significat, quā horti irrigantur
retricibus.opening: , Fest. pp. 282 and 283 Müll. ( a canal , aqueduct; perh. kindr. with ῥέεθρον, ῥεῖθρον ).

rē^-trīmentum.opening: tero , the dregs , refuse , sediment of pressed olives, Varr. R. R. 1, 64 ; of metals, dross, Cels. 5, 15 ; 5, 19, 26 ; of food and drink, refuse , waste (i. e. excrement, urine), Varr. ap. Non. 217, 23 ; Macr. S. 7, 4…

rē^-trītūro.opening: v. a. , to thresh over , to thresh (eccl. Lat.), Aug. Ep. ad Macr. 255, 3 .

rē^-trītus.opening: adj. , worn down : rutabulum, Naev. ap. Fest. p. 262 Müll.: retritis pilis, Sen. Ep. 47, 5 .

rē^trō.opening: adv. from re and the pronominal suffix ter, as in citro, ultro, intro, etc. . Lit. , of place, backwards , back; on the back side , behind. Denoting tendency, direction, with verbs or nouns of motion: multa videbis…

rē^trŏ-ăgo.opening: v. a. , to drive back , to turn back , etc. (post - Aug.; esp. freq. in Quint.). Lit. : capillos a fronte contra naturam, to push back, Quint. 11, 3, 160 : vasta flumina, Mel. 3, 1, 1 .— Trop. : honores, Plin. 7, 44,…

rē^trō-cēdo.opening: (or separate, ), , v. n. , to go back , retire , recede , Liv. 8, 8, 9 (Weissenb. retro cedentes); Curt. 3, 8, 17 ; 7, 4, 4 .

rē^trō-cessus.opening: cedo , a going back or backwards , retrocession (opp. processus), App. Dogm. Plat. 1, p. 5 fin.

retrō-dūco.opening: v. a. , to bring or draw back , Vitr. 10, 6 fin. ; Dig. 34, 5, 16 .

rē^trŏ-ĕo.opening: v. n. , to go back or backwards , to recede , retire , Sen. Q. N. 7, 21, 1 ; Plin. 2, 16, 13, § 70 .

rē^trō-flecto.opening: v. a. , to bend or turn back (post-Aug.): capillos, Petr. 126, 15 .

rē^trōgrădātĭo.opening: retrogradior , a going back , retrograding (late Lat.), Mart. Cap. 8, § 881 : stellarum, Isid. Orig. 3, p. 83 .

rē^trō-grădĭor.opening: v. dep. n. (collat. form , , v. n. , Mart. Cap. 8, § 887 ), to go back or backwards , to retrograde , Plin. 8, 15, 16, § 39 ; of the retrograde motion of the stars, id. 2, 15, 12, § 61 ; 2, 17, 14, § 76 ; Mart. Cap. 8,…

rē^trōgrădus.opening: (collat. form , , App. M. 4, p. 151 ), adj. retrogradior , going back or backwards , retrograde; usually of the stars, Sen. Q. N. 7, 25 ; Plin. 2, 17, 15, § 77 ; Sid. Ep. 8, 11 : carmen retrogradum (i. e. reciprocum),…

rē^trōgressus.opening: id. , a retrograde movement , retrogression of the sun (post-class.), Macr. S. 1, 17 .

rē^trō-pendŭlus.opening: adj. , hanging back or backwards : crinium globi (opp. antependuli), App. M. 5, p. 168, 22 .

rē^trō-spĭcĭo.opening: v. a. specio , to look back at : orbem lunae (sol), Vitr. 9, 4 .

rē^trōversim.opening: adv. retroversus , backwards : cedentes radii, Claud. Mam. Stat. An. 1, 7 .

rē^trō-versus.opening: or ( , and sync. , , also , Tert. Apol. 19 ), , adj. verto , turned back or backwards ( adj. very rare, but freq. as adv. ; v. infra ). Form : Medusae Ipse retroversus squalentia prodidit ora, Ov. M. 4, 655 : retroversi…

rē^-trūdo.opening: , no perf. , , v. a. , to thrust back (in the verb. finit. only anteand post-class.): quasi retruderet hominum me vis invitum, Plaut. Ep. 2, 2, 64 : in metallum retrudendus, Cod. Th. 1, 5, 1: in carcerem, Vulg. Gen. 41,…

rĕ-tundo.opening: (also rettŭdi, Phaedr. 4, 22, 21 Orell. N. cr. ), tūsum (retunsus, Plaut. Ps. 1, 2, 27 ; 4, 4, 8 ), , v. a. , to beat or pound back any thing sharp, i. e. to blunt , dull (class.). Lit. : ferrum, Cic. Sull. 30, 83 : in…

rĕtunsus.opening: Part. and P. a. of retundo.

rĕ-tūro.opening: v. a. turo, whence also obturo , to open , unstop (only in the two foll. passages): obscenis verbis novae nuptae aures returare, Varr. ap. Non. 167, 6 : ora coarticulare mutorum, surdorum auriculas returare, Arn. 1, 31 .

rĕtūsus.opening: Part. and P. a. of retundo.

Reudigni.opening: Gothic; root rinds, venerable , a people of northern Germany , on the right bank of the Albis , north of the Longobards , Tac. G. 40 .

rĕ-unctor.opening: ungo , an anointer (a physician's assistant, who rubbed the patient with ointments), Plin. 29, 1, 2, § 4 .

rĕus.opening: , and , , res , jurid. t. t. Originally, a party to an action (res), either plaintiff or defendant; afterwards restricted to the party accused , defendant , prisoner , etc.: reos appello non eos modo, qui arguuntur, sed…

rĕ-vălesco.opening: v. inch. n. , to grow well again; to regain one ' s former strength , state , or condition; to recover ( poet. and post-Aug. for convalesco, reficior). Lit. , Ov. H. 21, 231 : ex capitali morbo, Gell. 16, 13, 5 :…

rĕ-vecto.opening: v. a. , to carry back again : ad Macedoniam corpus alicujus, Jul. Val. Res Gest. Alex. 3, 42 .

rĕ-vĕho.opening: v. a. , to carry or bring back , to convey back (class.; syn.: reporto, refero, reddo). Lit. : Diana Segestam Carthagine revecta, Cic. Verr. 2, 4, 35, § 77 ; so, praedam inde, Liv. 1, 35 : tela ad Graios, Ov. M. 13, 402…

rĕvēlātĭo.opening: revelo , an uncovering , laying bare (eccl. Lat.). Lit. : pudendorum, Arn. 5, 182 . — Trop. : imaginariae revelationes, Aug. Conf. 9, 10 : filii sui, a revelation, Tert. adv. Marc. 5, 4 ; Vulg. 1 Cor. 1, 7 . — Esp., the…

rĕvēlātor.opening: id. , a revealer (eccl. Lat.), Tert. adv. Marc. 4, 25 .

rĕvēlātōrĭus.opening: adj. id. , of or belonging to revelation (eccl. Lat.), Tert. Anim. 47 .

rĕ-vello.grammar: velli, vulsum or volsum, 3 v. a.
rĕ-vello.opening: v. a. , to pluck or pull away , to pull or tear out , to tear off or away (freq. and class.). Lit. : tela de corpore, Cic. Pis. 11, 25 : nascentis equi de fronte revolsus amor, Verg. A. 4, 515 : titulum de fronte, Ov.…

rĕ-vēlo.opening: v. a. , to unveil , uncover , lay bare (not ante-Aug.; syn.: patefacio, aperio, nudo, retego). Lit. : caput (opp. involvere), Suet. Galb. 7 : frontem, Tac. G. 31 : os, Ov. F. 6, 619 : pectus, Flor. 4, 2, 71 : carpenta…

rĕ-vendo.opening: v. a. , to sell again : operas liberto, etc., Dig. 38, 2, 37 .

rĕ-vēnĕo.opening: v. n. , to be sold again : si fundus revenisset, Dig. 18, 3, 5 .

rĕ-vĕnĭo.opening: v. n. , to come again , come back , to return (class.; cf.: redeo, revertor). Lit. , absol. : reveni, ut illum persequar, Plaut. Merc. 4, 1, 3 ; so id. Men. 5, 3, 4 ; Tac. A. 12, 59 : domum, Plaut. Am. 1, 1, 33 ; 2, 2,…

rĕ-ventĭlo.opening: to produce again , = proferre: nihil phantasiarum, Claud. Mam. Stat. An. 1, 24 .

rĕvento.opening: , a false read. for reverto, Lucr. 3, 1061 ; v. Lachm. ad h. l.

rĕventus.opening: revenio , a return , Suevius ap. Macr. S. 2, 14 fin.

rĕ-verbĕro.opening: v. a. , to strike back , repel , cause to rebound (post-Aug.): sic veneficiis corpus induruit, ut saxa reverberet, Sen. Contr. 1, 3, 11 : Indus saxis saepe impeditus quīs crebro reverberatur, Curt. 8, 9, 7 : reverberato…

rĕ-vĕrēcundĭter.opening: adv. , respectfully , Enn. ap. Prisc. p. 1010 P. ( Enn. p. 180 Vahl.); Pompon. ap. Non. 516, 22 (Com. Rel. p. 200 Rib.).

rĕvĕrendus.opening: Part. and P. a. of revereor.

rĕvĕrens.opening: Part. and P. a. of revereor.

rĕvĕrenter.opening: adv. , v. , P. a. A. fin.

rĕvĕrentĭa.opening: revereor , timidity arising from high respect or (more rarely) from fear, respect , regard , fear , awe , reverence (not freq. till after the post-Aug. per.): adhibenda est quaedam reverentia adversus homines, et optimi…

rĕ-vĕrĕor.opening: , ĭtus. 2, v. dep. a. ( act. collat. form , acc. to Prisc. p. 799 P.), to stand in awe or fear of; to regard , respect , honor; to fear , be afraid of; to reverence , revere (ante-class. and post-Aug.; syn. veneror):…

rĕ-vergo.opening: v. n. , to incline towards any thing; trop.: in aliorum commoda, to tend , conduce (late Lat.), Claud. Mam. Ep. ad Sid. 4, 2 .

rĕ-verro.opening: ( ), , v. a. , to sweep back again , to scatter again : revorram hercle hoc, quod convorri modo, Plaut. Stich. 2, 2, 64 (cf. id. ib. 2, 2, 27 and 51).

rĕversĭo.opening: ( ), , reverto . A turning back before reaching one's destination (differing from reditus, a coming back, return): quam valde ille reditu vel potius reversione meă laetatus, Cic. Att. 16, 7, 5 : exponam vobis breviter…

rĕverso.opening: v. freq. a. id. , to turn round (late Lat.): versa et reversa in tergum et in latera, Aug. Conf. 6 fin. : panis qui non reversatur, Vulg. Os. 7, 8 : subcinericius panis est cinere coctus et reversatus, Isid. 20, 2, 15…

rĕvertĭcŭlum.opening: reverto , a return : annua solis, App. M. 3, p. 134 ; id. Flor. 4, p. 361, 9 .

rĕ-verto.opening: ( ) and ( ), (-vors-) ( inf. paragog. revertier, Phaedr. 4, 18, 14 ), 3 (the authors of the ante-Aug. per. make the perfect forms, with the exception of the part. reversus, only from the active root, reverti,…

rĕ-vestĭo.grammar: īvi or ĭi, ītum, 4 v. a.
rĕ-vestĭo.opening: v. a. , to clothe again (late Lat.), Tert. adv. Marc. 5, 129 ; id. Res. Carn. 42 fin. ; trop., Dracont. Hexaëm. 1, 629.

rĕvī^brātĭo.opening: revibro , a reflection of light (late Lat.), Hyg. Astr. 4, 14 .

rĕvī^brātus.opening: id. (only in abl. sing. ), a reflection of light, Mart. Cap. 2, § 110 .

rĕ-vī^bro.opening: v. a. and n. Act. , to cast back , reflect : radios, Mart. Cap. 2, § 169 .— Neutr. , to send back a reflection : ipsa caeli contextio lucis fulgoribus revibravit, Mart. Cap. 8, § 810 .

rĕvictĭo.opening: revinco , a refuting , refutation (post-class.), App. Dogm Plat. 3, p. 31, 39 .

rĕ-vĭdĕo.opening: v. n. , to see again , go to see again : nunc ad eram revidebo, Plaut. Truc. 2, 2, 65 : aspectus alicujus, Cassiod. Complex. Act. Apos. 51 .

rĕ-vĭgesco.opening: v. inch. n. , to begin to flourish again , Juvenc. 2, 204 .

rĕ-vīlesco.opening: v. inch. n. , to become vile or contemptible : virtus admota oculis, Sen. Tranq. 17, 2 .

rĕ-vīmentum.opening: vieo , a lappet; an edging , fringe (syn. lacinia): (in oratione) omnia, ut in tenui veste, oris detexta et revimentis sint vincta, Fronto Laud. fumi (a little after, laciniam aliquam porrigat).

rĕvincĭbĭlis.opening: adj. revinco , that may be disproved or refuted (eccl. Lat.): materiae iisdem litteris, Tert. Res. Carn. 13 fin.

rĕ-vincĭo.opening: v. a. To bind back or backwards; to bind around , bind fast , fasten (class.; not in Cic.). Lit. : nisi esset (terra) caelo revincta, Lucr. 5, 553 : ancorae pro funibus ferreis catenis revinctae, Caes. B. G. 3, 13 :…

rĕ-vinco.opening: v. a. , to conquer , subdue. Lit. (only poet. , and in Tac.): victrices catervae Consiliis juvenis revictae, Hor. C. 4, 4, 24 ; cf.: revicta conjuratio, repressed, checked, Tac. A. 15, 73 : primordia rerum aliquā…

rĕ-vindĭco.opening: v. a. , to exact retribution from (late Lat.), Primas in Gal. Ad. c. 5.

rĕ-vĭrĕo.opening: v. n. , to be green again , be covered again with verdure : arbores, Albin. 2, 113 .

rĕ-vĭresco.opening: v. inch. n. , to become or grow green again; to recover its verdure. Lit. (rare): laesae silvae, Ov. M. 2, 408 : arbor Ruminalis in novos fetus, Tac. A. 13, 58 : caepe revirescit decedente lunā, contra autem inarescit…

rĕ-viscĕrātĭo.opening: a restoring of the flesh (eccl. Lat.): revisceratio et respiratio ossium, Tert. Res. Carn. 30 .

rĕvīsĭo.opening: revideo , a seeing again , Claud. Mam. Ep. ad Sid. 4, 2 .

rĕ-vīsĭto.opening: v. a. , to visit again , revisit : urbem nundinis, Plin. 18, 3, 3, § 13 .

rĕ-vīso.opening: v. n. and a. Neutr. , to look back on a thing, come back or again to see (cf. respicio); to pay a visit again (ante- and post-class.): ut ad me revisas, Plaut. Truc. 2, 4, 79 : ad me, Gell. 13, 30, 10 : ad stabulum,…

rĕ-vīvĭfĭcātus.opening: Part. [vivifico], restored to life (eccl. Lat.), Tert. Res. Carn. 19 .

rĕ-vīvisco.opening: ( ; v. Orell. Cic. Fam. 6, 10, 5 ), vixi, 3, v. inch. n. , to come to life again , to be restored to life , to revive (class.; a favorite word with Cic., esp. in the trop. signif.). Lit. : reviviscat M'. Curius aut…

rĕ-vīvo.opening: , no perf. , , v. n. , to live again (post-class.), Sen. Med. 477 ; Paul. Nol. Carm. 35, 563 .

rĕvŏcābĭlis.opening: adj. revoco , that may be recalled or revoked , revocable (mostly poet. ): poenae leves et revocabiles, Sen. Ira, 1, 5, 6 .—Hence, with a negative, for irrevocable : colus Parcarum, Sen. Herc. Fur. 559 : telum, Ov. M.…

rĕvŏcāmen.opening: id. , a calling back or away , a recall (Ovidian), Ov. F. 1, 561 .— Plur. , Ov. M. 2, 596 .

rĕvŏcātĭo.opening: id. , a calling back or away , a recalling (rare but good prose). Lit. : a bello (with receptui signum), Cic. Phil. 13, 7, 15 .— Transf. , in plur. : revocationes lunae a sole, Vitr. 9, 4 fin. — Trop. : revocatio ad…

rĕvŏcātor.opening: revoco , a recaller : animarum (magus), one who restores to life, Quint. Decl. 10, 19 .

rĕvŏcātōrĭus.opening: adj. id. , for calling or drawing back , revocatory (postclass.): emplastrum, Theod. Prisc. 2, 32 .— Subst. : , , (sc. epistula), a letter of recall , Cod. Just. 12, 1, 18 .

rĕ-vŏco.opening: v. a. To call back , recall (class. and freq., esp. in the trop. sense). Lit. In gen.: quotiens foras ire volo, me retines, revocas, Plaut. Men. 1, 2, 5 ; cf. Suet. Claud. 15 fin. : de meo cursu rei publicae sum voce…

rĕ-vŏlo.opening: v. n. , to fly back (rare but class.). Lit. : turdi quotannis in Italiam trans mare advolant et eodem revolant, Varr. R. R. 3, 5, 7 : grus, Cic. N. D. 2, 49, 125 : mergi, Verg. G. 1, 361 : Daedalus ceratis alis, Ov. M.…

rĕvŏlūbĭlis.opening: adj. revolvo , that may be rolled back ( poet. ): pondus (i. e. saxum), Ov. Ib. 193 : unda, Sil. 15, 237 : orbita, Aus. Ecl. Nomin. Sept. Dier. 12 .—Fig.: juro ego Fatorum nulli revolubile carmen, Prop. 4 (5), 7, 51.…

rĕvŏlūtĭo.opening: id. , a revolving , revolution (late Lat. for conversio), Aug. Civ. Dei , 22, 12; id. Trin. 12, 24 ; Mart. Cap. 9, § 922 .

rĕ-volvo.opening: v. a. , to roll back; to unroll , unwind; to revolve , return (class.; esp. freq. since the Aug. per.). Lit. In gen.: Draco revolvens Sese, Cic. poët. N. D. 2, 42, 106: (pelagus) gelidum ab imo fluctum revolvit in…

rĕ-vŏmo.opening: v. a. , to spew or vomit forth again; to vomit up , disgorge ( poet. and in post-Aug. prose). Lit. : salsos pectore fluctus, Verg. A. 5, 182 : plumam avibus devoratis (dracones), Plin. 10, 72, 92, § 197 : haustum mare…

rĕvulsĭo.opening: ( ), , revello , a tearing off or away (post-Aug.): unius schedae, Plin. 13, 12, 24, § 80 .

rex.opening: ( gen. plur regerum, Gell. ap. Charis p. 40 P.), rego , a ruler of a country, a king. Lit. : omnis res publica, quae ut dixi populi res est, consilio quodam regenda est, ut diuturna sit. Id autem consilium aut uni…

Rex.opening: a surname in the gens Marcia, e. g. Q. Marcius Rex, consul A. U. C. 686, Sall. C. 30, 3 : Q. (Marcius) Rex, brotherin-law of Clodius, Cic. Att. 1, 16, 10 (in a lusus verbb. with rex, a tyrant , despot ); cf. Hor. S. 1,…

Rha.opening: , = Ῥᾶ, the Wolga , on whose banks grew the radix pontica, Rha ponticum, rhubarb (Rheum Rhaponticum, Linn.), which thence received its name, Amm. 22, 8, 28 (cf. Cels. 5, 23 fin. ).

rhabdŏs.opening: , = ῥάβδος (a rod), a sort of meteor , App. de Mundo, p. 64, 14.

rhacŏma.opening: or , , , a root , perh. i. q. rha, rhubarb , Plin. 27, 12, 105, § 128 .

Rhacōtes.opening: , or , , , an ancient name of the site of Alexandria in Egypt , form Rhacotes, Plin. 5, 10, 11, § 62 ; form Rhacotis, Tac. H. 4, 84 .

Rhădămanthus.opening: , = Ῥαδάμανθος, a son of Jupiter and Europa , brother of Minos , a judge in the infernal regions , Cic. Tusc. 1, 5, 10 ; 1, 41, 98 ; Ov. M. 9, 435 ; 439 ; Verg. A. 6, 566 ; Claud. in Rufin. 2, 480 .

Rhădămas.opening: a fictitious name in Plaut. Trin. 4, 2, 83 .

rhăgădes.opening: , and , , , = ῥαγάδες and ῥαγάδια, a kind of sores or chaps on various parts of the body, Plin. 23, 4, 44, § 87 ; 23 7 64. § 129; 24, 7, 23, § 39; 28. 6, 18, § 66 (in Cels. 6, 18, 7 , written as Greek).

rhamnos.opening: , = ῥάμνος, buckthorn, Christ ' s-thorn : Rhamnus, Linn.; Plin. 24, 14, 76, § 124 , Veg. 5, 74 .

Rhamnūs.opening: , = Ῥαμνοῦς, the northernmost town of Attica , famed for an ancient temple of Themis , and in later times for a statue of Nemesis , the mod. Ovriokastro , Plin. 4, 7, 11, § 24 ; 36, 5, 4, § 17 ; Luc. 5, 233 .— Hence, ,…

Rhamses.opening: (or ae), , an ancient and powerful king of Egypt , Tac. A. 2, 60 , Plin. 36, 8, 14, § 65 (al. Ramises).

Rhănis.opening: , ĭdis. , a nymph in the train of Diana , Ov. M. 3, 171 .

Rhēa.opening: an old Italian name. Thus, Rhea Silvia, daughter of Numitor and mother of Romulus and Remus , Liv. 1, 3 ; Flor. 1, 1, 1 ; Prud. adv. Symm. 1, 174 (cf. Verg. A. 1, 276 ).—Hence comes the name of the fabled priestess Rhea…

Rhĕa.opening: , = Ῥέα, another name for Cybele , Ov. F. 4, 201 : Rhea, quae Latiis Ops, Aus. Idyll. 12 de Deis, 2.

Rhēdŏnes.opening: ( ), , , a people in Gallia Lugdunensis, in the neighborhood of the modern Rennes , in Bretagne , Caes. B. G. 2, 34 ; 7, 75 ; Plin. 4, 18, 32, § 107 .

Rhēgĭum.grammar: incorrect spelling for Regium and Reginus

Rhēnē.opening: , = Ῥήνη, an island in the Ægean Sea , one of the Cyclades , Plin. 4, 12, 22, § 67 ; Mel. 2, 7 .

Rhēnus.opening: The Rhine , the river which divided Gaul from Germany , Caes. B. G. 1, 1 ; 4, 10 ; 4, 17 ; 6, 9; Tac. G. 1 ; id. A. 1, 63 ; 2, 6 ; Mel. 3, 2 sq. ; Plin. 4, 14, 28, § 100 ; Cic. Pis. 33, 81 ; Verg. A. 8, 727 ; id. E. 10,…

Rhēsus.opening: , = Ῥῆσος, the son of a Muse , a king in Thrace , who was robbed of his horses and killed by Diomede and Ulysses before Troy , Cic. N. D. 3, 18, 45 ; Verg. A. 1, 469 ; Ov. M. 13, 249 sq. al.

Rhētēnor.opening: a companion of Diomede , Ov. M. 14, 504 .

Rhetĭco.opening: a mountain range in Germany , now the Siebengebirge , near Bonn , Mel. 3, 3, 3 .

rhētor.opening: , = ῥήτωρ, a teacher of oratory or rhetoric , a rhetorician : eos, qui rhetores nominarentur et qui dicendi praecepta traderent, nihil plane tenere, Cic. de Or. 1, 18, 84 ; cf. Quint. 2, 2, 1 : in rhetorum scholis, id.…

rhētŏrĭco.opening: (ante-class.), and , , v. dep. (post-class.) [rhetoricus], to speak rhetorically or like an orator , Novat. ap. Non. 476, 6 (Com. Rel. p. 216 Rib.); act. form, Tert. Res. Carn. 5 .

rhētŏrĭcōtĕros.opening: adj. , = ῥητορικώτερος, more oratorical , Lucil. ap. Cic. de Or. 3, 43, 171 .

rhētŏrĭcus.opening: adj. , = ῥητορικός, of or belonging to a rhetorician , rhetorical. Adj. : nostro more aliquando, non rhetorico loquamur, Cic. de Or. 1, 29, 133 : ars, i. e. a treatise on rhetoric, id. Fin. 4, 3, 7 : rhetorici doctores,…

rhētŏriscus.opening: dim. rhetor , a little rhetorician , Gell. 17, 20, 4 .

rhētŏrisso.opening: v. n. , = ῥητορίζω, to speak rhetorically , Pompon. ap. Non. 166, 3 (Com. Rel. p. 201 Rib.).

rhētra.opening: , = ῥήτρα, a saying , maxim , law : quas (leges) ex rhetris Lycurgi reparavit Sylla, Amm. 16, 5, 1 .

rheuma.opening: , = ῥεῦμα. A flow , flood : maris (i. e. aestus), Veg. Mil. 5, 12 .— A catarrh , rheum , Hier. Ep. 122, 1 .

rheumătĭcus.opening: , = ῥευματικός, one troubled with rheum , that has a catarrh , Plin. 29, 6, 39, § 142 .

rheumătismus.opening: , = ῥευματισμὀς, rheum , catarrh (pure Lat. fluctio): levis humoris fluor quem Graeci rheumatismum vocant, Cael. Aur. Acut. 2, 27, 146 ; Plin. 22, 18, 21, § 46 ; 23, 2, 32, § 66 ; 24, 3, 3, § 7 et saep.

rheumătīzo.opening: v. n. , = ῥευματίζομαι, to be troubled with rheum , to have a catarrh , Theod. Prisc. 1, 10 .

rhexia.opening: a plant , also called onochilis, Plin. 22, 21, 25, § 51 .

rhīna.opening: , = ῥίνη, a kind of shark , of whose skin arrows were made , Plin. 32, 11, 53, § 150 .

rhīnenchўtes.opening: , = ῥινεγχύτης, an instrument for making injections into the nose , Scrib. Comp. 7 ; also called , , , Cael. Aur. Acut. 2, 4, 82 .

rhīnĭon.opening: , = ῥίνιον, collyrium, an ointment for removing scars , Cels. 6, 6, 30 .

rhīnŏcĕros.opening: , = ῥινόκερως. Lit. , a rhinoceros , Plin. 8, 20, 29, § 71 ; Mart. Spect. 9 ; 22 ; id. Epigr. 14, 53 ; 14, 52, 2 ; Curt. 8, 9, 16 ; 9, 1, 5 ; Suet. Aug. 43 : cornua rhinocerotis, Vulg. Deut. 33, 17 ; Plin. 6, 29, 34, §…

Rhīnŏcŏlūra.opening: a town on the borders of Syria and Egypt on the shore of the Mediterranean , prob. the mod. El-Arish , Plin. 5, 13, 14, § 68 ; Liv. 45, 11 ; Sen. Ira, 3, 20, 2 ; Amm. 22, 16, 3 .

Rhinton.opening: ( ), , , the originator of travestied tragedy , a native of Tarentum , Cic. Att. 1, 20, 3 ; Varr. R. R. 3, 3, 9 (cited also Col. 8, 16, 4 ).

Rhĭon.opening: or , , A strait between the Ionian Sea and the Corinthian Gulf , Liv. 27, 29 ; 28, 7 ; Mel. 2, 3 . — A promontory of Achaia near this strait , now Kastro Morea , Plin. 4, 2, 3, § 6 .— A town near the same strait , Liv.…

Rhīpaei.opening: or ( ), , a range of mountains in the most northern part of Scythia , where are the sources of the Tanais , Mel. 1, 19, 13 ; 2, 1, 1 ; 3, 5, 1 ; Plin. 4, 12, 24, § 78 ; 6, 5, 5, § 15 ; Enn. Ann. 4, 5 al. — Less freq. in…

rhīzĭas.opening: , = ῥιζίας, juice extracted from a root (opp. caulias), Plin. 19, 3, 15, § 43 .

Rhīzinĭum.opening: a town of Dalmatia , upon the Gulf of Cattaro , Plin. 3, 22, 26, § 144 ; called also , , now Risano , Liv. 45, 26 .—Hence, , , , the inhabitants of this town , Liv. 45, 26, 15 .

rhīzŏtŏmos.opening: a plant , a kind of iris , Plin. 21, 7, 19, § 41 .

rhīzŏtŏmūmĕna.opening: , = ῥιζοτομούμενα, descriptions of or instructions about medicines prepared from roots cut up (the name of a book written by Micion), Plin. 20, 23, 96, § 258 .

rho.opening: , = ῥῶ, the Greek name of the letter r, Cic. Div. 2, 46, 96 ; Aus. Epigr. 128 .

Rhŏda.opening: A town of Hispania Tarraconensis , now Rosas , Liv. 34, 8 fin. ; Mel. 2, 6, 5 . — A town on the Rhone , Plin. 3, 4, 5, § 33 .

Rhŏdănus.opening: The Rhone , a river in Gaul , Mel. 2, 5, 4 sq. ; Plin. 3, 4, 5, § 33 ; Sil. 3, 446 sq. ; Varr. ap. Gell. 10, 7, 2 ; Caes. B. G. 1, 1 ; Planc. ap. Cic. Fam. 10, 9, 3 ; 10, 11, 2 ; Ov. M. 2, 258 ; Liv. 21, 26 : Rhodani…

rhŏdĭnus.opening: adj. , = ῥόδινος, prepared from roses : unguentum, rose-salve, Plin. 13, 1, 2, § 9 : oleum, oil of roses, id. 15, 7, 7, § 30 .

rhŏdītis.opening: a precious stone , unknown to us, Plin. 37, 11, 73, § 191 .

Rhodo.opening: a friend of Q. Minucius Thermus , Cic. Fam. 2, 18, 1 .

rhŏdŏdaphnē.opening: , = ῥοδοδάφνη, the rose-bay , oleander , Plin. 16, 20, 33, § 79 ; 24, 11, 53, § 90 ; Pall. 1, 35, 9 .

rhŏdŏdendros.opening: , and , , , = ῥοδόδενδρον, the rosebay , oleander , Plin. 16, 20, 33, § 79 ; 21, 13, 45, § 77 ; 24, 11, 53, § 90 .

rhŏdŏmĕli.opening: , = ῥοδόμελι, honey of roses , Pall. 16 Maist.

Rhŏdŏpē.opening: , = Ῥοδόπη. A mountain range in Thrace , a part of the Hæmus , now Despoto Dagh , Mel. 2, 2, 2 ; Verg. G. 3, 351 ; Ov. M. 2, 222 ; 10, 77 .— Acc. to the myth, originally a man, Ov. M. 6, 87 sq. — Meton. , Thrace , Verg.…

rhodōra.opening: (Gallic), name of a plant : Spiraea ulmaria, Linn.; Plin. 24, 19, 112, § 172 (al. rodarum).

Rhŏdos.opening: (rarely ), , , = Ῥόδος. An island on the coast of Asia Minor , celebrated for its pure air , for its Colossus , its school of rhetoric , and the skill of its people in navigation; now Rhodes , Mel. 2, 7, 4 ; Plin. 5,…

Rhoduntĭa.opening: one of the three summits of Mount Œta , Liv. 36, 16 .

Rhoetēum.opening: , = Ῥοίτειον, a city built on a promontory of the same name in Troas , on the Hellespont (now Cape Barbieri ), Mel. 1, 18, 5 ; Liv. 37, 9 ; 37, 38 sq.

Rhoetēus.opening: adj. , = Ῥοιτειος, of or belonging to the promontory of Rhœteum , Rhœtean : profundum, the sea that washes it, Ov. M. 11, 197 ; cf. litora, Plin. 5, 30, 33, § 125 ; and subst. : Rhoeteum rapax, Ov. F. 4, 279 .— Hence…

Rhoeteus.opening: ( ), , , the name of a Rutulian , Verg. A. 10, 399 ; 402 .

Rhoetus.opening: ( ), , A giant , Hor. C. 2, 19, 23 ; 3, 4, 55 .— A centaur , Ov. M. 12, 271 sq. ; Verg. G. 2, 456 ; id. Cul. 27 ; Val. Fl. 1, 140 .—Form Rhoecus, Luc. 6, 390 .— A companion of Phineus , Ov. M. 5, 38 . — A king of the…

rhŏĭcus.opening: adj. , = ῥοϊκός, of or belonging to the sumach (rhus), sumach- : folia, Plin. 24, 11, 54, § 92 .

rhombŏīdes.opening: , = ῥομβοειδές, in mathematics, a four-sided figure , whose opposite sides and angles are equal , a rhomboid , Front. Expos. Form. p. 36 Goes.; Mart. Cap. 6, § 712 .

rhombus.opening: , = ῥόμβος. A magician ' s circle , Prop. 2, 28, 35 (3, 25, 1); 3, 6, 26 (4, 5, 26); Ov. Am. 1, 8, 7 ; Mart. 9, 30, 9 ; 12, 57, 17 .— A kind of fish , flatfish , turbot , Plin. 9, 54, 79, § 169 ; Hor. S. 1, 2, 116 ; 2,…

rhomphaea.opening: (pure Latin form, , Gell. 10, 25, 2 ; with i short, rumpĭa, Val. Fl. 6, 98 ), , = ῥομφαία, a long missile weapon of barbarous nations: rumpia genus teli est Thracae nationis, Gell. 10, 25, 4 ; Liv. 31, 39, 11 : bis…

rhonchĭ-sŏnus.opening: adj. rhonchus , snorting : rhinoceros, Sid. Carm. 3, 8 .

rhoncho.opening: v. n. id. , to snore , to snort , Sid. Ep. 1, 6 .

Rhōsos.opening: , = Ῥῶσος, a town in Cilicia , where highly prized utensils were made , Mel. 1, 12 fin. —Hence, , , adj. , of or belonging to Rhosos : vasa, Cic. Att. 6, 1, 13 .— , , adj. , of Rhosos : montes, Plin. 5, 22, 18, § 80 .

Rhoxŏlāni.opening: ( ), , , a Scythian tribe in Eastern Europe , Plin. 4, 12, 25, § 80 ; Tac. H. 1, 79 ; Amm. 22, 8, 31 .

rhūs.opening: (also corrupted into roris, Col. 12, 42, 3 ; abl. rore, id. 9, 13, 5 ; Pall. Mart. 15, 1 ), ( , Scrib. 142 ), = ῥοῦς, a bushy shrub , sumach , Plin. 24, 11, 54, § 91 ; 13, 6, 13, § 55 ; Cels. 6, 11 ; Col. 12, 42, 3 ;…

rhūsĕlīnon.opening: , = ῥουσέλινον, a plant , also called apium rusticum, App. Herb. 8 .

Rhyndăcus.opening: , = Ῥύνδακος, a river between Mysia and Bithynia , now the Mualitsch , Plin. 5, 32, 40, § 142 ; 6, 34, 39, § 217 ; Mel. 1, 19, 3 .

rhўpărogrăphos.opening: , = ῥυπαρογράφος, a painter of low or mean subjects , a surname of Pyreicus, Plin. 35, 10, 37, § 112 .

rhўpōdes.opening: adj. , = ῥυπώδης, dirty , smeared : emplastrum, a drawing plaster, Cels. 6, 18, 7 ( id. 5, 19, 15 , written as Greek).

Rhysaddir.opening: a town and harbor of Mauretania Tingitana , now Melilla , Plin. 5, 1, 2, § 18 ; also called , Mel. 1, 5, 5 .

rhythmĭcē.opening: , = ῥυθμική, sc. τέχνη, the art of observing rhythm : rhythmice est ars omnis in numeris, Mart. Cap. 9, § 969 .

rhythmĭcus.opening: , = ῥυθμικός, one who pays attention to rhythm , or who teaches the art of preserving rhythm in composition , Cic. de Or. 3, 49, 190 ; Quint. 9, 4, 68 : melo favente rhythmico, Mart. Cap. 2, § 121 .

rhythmizŏmĕnon.opening: , = ῥυθμιζόμενον, that which is reduced to measure or rhythm , Mart. Cap. 9, § 967 sq.

rhythmŏīdes.opening: adj. , = ῥυθμοειδής, like rhythm , rhythmical , Mart. Cap. 9, § 970 .

rhythmos.opening: or , , , = ῥυθμός, symmetry , harmony , rhythm in music or speech, Mart. Cap. 9, § 967 sqq.; Varr. ap. Diom. p. 512 P.; Quint. 9, 4, 45 sq. ; 51 sq. ; 78; 109 (Cicero constantly has numerus instead of this word, which…

rhўtĭum.opening: , = ῥύτιον, a hornshaped drinking-vessel , a drinking-horn , Mart. 2, 35, 2 .

rīca.opening: a veil to be thrown over the head , worn by the Roman women when sacrificing, Varr. L. L. 5, § 130 Müll.; Plaut. Ep. 2, 2, 48; Lucil., Novius, and Serenus ap. Non. 539, 18 sq. ; Massur. Sabin. ap. Gell. 10, 15, 28 ;…

rīcīnĭātus.opening: adj. ricinium , wearing a ricinium: mimi, Auct. ap. Fest. s. v. recinium, p. 277 Müll.

rīcīnĭum.opening: rica , a small veil thrown over the head by the early Romans , esp. by women and mourners, Varr. L. L. 5, § 132 Müll.; id. ap. Non. 549, 32 ; Cic. Leg. 2, 23, 59 ; 2, 25, 64 ; cf. Fest. s. v. recinium, p. 274 Müll.;…

rīcīnus.opening: adj. id. , veiled : mitra, Varr. ap. Non. 539, 26 .

rĭcĭnus.opening: A large kind of vermin that infests sheep , dogs , etc., a tick , tike , Cato, R. R. 96, 2 ; Varr. R. R. 2, 9, 14 ; Col. 7, 13, 1 ; 6, 2, 6 ; Plin. 22, 18, 21, § 47 ; Petr. 57 ; Ser. Samm. 36, 699 .— A plant , called…

ricto.opening: v. n. ringor , to make the natural cry of a leopard , Spart. Get. 5 .

rŏsŭlentus.opening: adj. id. . * Abounding in roses : prata, Prud. στεφ. 3, 199.—* Rose-colored , rosy : splendor, Mart. Cap. 1, § 73 .

rŏta.opening: kindred with Sanscr. ratha, chariot, and Germ. Rad (cf.rotundus), wheel , a wheel. Lit. : pro rotā me uti licet, Plaut. Capt. 2, 3, 9 ; cf.: vorsutior es quam rota figularis, id. Ep. 3, 2, 35 : orbes rotarum, Lucr. 6,…

rŏtābĭlis.opening: adj. rota . Whirling , rotary (late Lat.): flexus, Amm. 23, 4, 2 .— Transf. , of a road, practicable : VIAM INVIAM ROTAB. REDD., Inscr. Grut. 149, 1 .

rŏtālis.opening: adj. id. , having wheels , wheeled (late Lat.): carpentum, Capitol. Macr. 12 : machina, Sulp. Sev. Dial. 1, 13, 2 .

rŏtātĭlis.opening: adj. roto , wheel-like , revolving (post-class.): gyri, Sid. Ep. 2, 9 : trochaei, Prud. στεφ. praef. 8.

rŏtātim.opening: adv. id. , like a wheel , in a circle , around (post-class.): in orbem saltantes, App. M. 10, p. 253, 19 (al. rotarum).

rŏtātĭo.opening: id. , a wheeling or turning about in a circle , rotation : circini, Vitr. 10, 3 init. et fin.

rŏtātor.opening: id. , one who turns a thing round in a circle , a whirler round : Bassaridum (Evan), Stat. S. 2, 7, 7 ; Cassiod. Var. 7, 5 .

rŏtātus.opening: id. , a turning or whirling round , Stat. Achill. 2, 417 ; Aus. Idyll. 10, 362 .

rŏto.grammar: āvi, ātum, 1 v. a. and n.
rŏto.opening: v. a. and n. rota . Act. , to turn a thing round like a wheel; to swing round , whirl about ( poet. and in post-Aug. prose; cf. torqueo). Lit. : Learchum bis terque per auras More rotat fundae, Ov. M. 4, 517 ; cf. id.…

Rotomăgi.opening: a city in Gallia Lugdunensis , now Rouen , Amm. 15, 11, 12 .

rŏtŭla.opening: (collat. form , , , Calp. Ecl. 7, 50 ), dim. rota , a little wheel , Plaut. Pers. 3, 3, 38 ; Col. 11, 3, 52 ; Plin. 18, 18, 48, § 172 ; Pall. 1, 20 .

rŏtundātĭo.opening: rotundo , a making round , a rounding : linea rotundationis, i. e. the circumference, Vitr. 1, 6 fin. ; 3, 1 ; 10, 11 .

rŏtundĭfŏlĭus.opening: adj. rotundusfolium , round-leaved , rotundifolious : herbae, App. Herb. 71 .

rŏtundĭtas.opening: rotundus , a round shape , roundness , rotundity (post-Aug.). Lit. : gemma rotunditatis absolutae, Plin. 37, 11, 73, § 190 ; so id. 18, 13, 34, § 130 ; 16, 23, 35, § 86 ; 19, 5, 25, § 76 al. — Trop. : verborum, a…

rŏtundo.opening: v. a. rotundus , to make round , to round off , round (syn. torno). Lit. (class.): cum similem universitatis naturae efficere vellet, ad volubilitatem rotundavit, Cic. Univ. 10 : tignum ad circinum, Vitr. 10, 11, 1 :…

rŏtundŭla.opening: dim. id. , a little round mass , a little ball , pellet , App. Herb. 13 .

rŏtundus.opening: ( ), , adj. rota , wheel-shaped , i. e. round , circular , spherical , rotund (very freq. and class.; cf. teres). Lit. : cur ea, quae fuerint juxtim quadrata, procul sint Visa rotunda, Lucr. 4, 502 ; cf. Cic. Fin. 2,…

Rōxānē.opening: , = Ῥωξάνη, a daughter of the Persian Oxyartes , wife of Alexander the Great , Curt. 8, 4, 23 ; 10, 6, 9 ; 10, 6, 13 ; Just. 12, 15, 9 ; 15, 2, 4 al.

Roxolāni.opening: ( ), , , a people upon the rivers Don and Dnieper , Spart. Hadr. 6 ; Inscr. Murat. 2099, 7 ; Inscr. Grut. 453 .

rŭbĕ-făcĭo.opening: v. a. id. , to make red or ruddy , to redden ( poet. ): sanguine setas, Ov. M. 8, 383 : rubefactaque sanguine tellus, id. ib. 13, 394 : cornua multo cruore, id. ib. 12, 382 : ora sororum (Aurora), Sil. 16, 137 .

rŭbellĭo.opening: id. , a fish of a reddish color , Plin. 32, 10, 49, § 138 ; Apic. 10, 7 .

rŭbellŭlus.opening: adj. dim. [id.], a little reddish : umbilicus (voluminis), Mart. Cap. poët. 5, § 566: rhamnos, Veg. 5, 74 .

rŭbellus.opening: adj. dim. [ruber], reddish : Veientanum (vinum), Mart. 1, 104, 9 , Pers. 5, 147 ; cf. vineae, Plin. 14, 2, 4, § 23 : calvitium, Mart. Cap. 8, § 804 .

rŭbens.opening: Part. and P. a. of rubeo.

rŭbĕo.opening: v. n. v. ruber , to be red or ruddy (class.). In gen.: ulceribus quasi inustis omne rubere Corpus, Lucr. 6 , 1166: per herbas Matutina rubent radiati lumina solis, id. 5, 462 ; cf. id. 6, 210 : oculi luce, id. 6, 1146 :…

rŭber.opening: (collat. form, nom. , Sol. 40, 23 ), adj. Sanscr. rudhira, blood; Gr. ἐρυθρός, red; ef. rufus . Red , ruddy (cf.: rufus, russus): umor, Lucr. 4, 1051 : sanguis, Hor. C. 3, 13, 7 : cruore pannus, id. Epod. 17, 51 :…

rŭbesco.opening: v. inch. n. [rubeo], to grow red , turn red , to redden ( poet. and in post-Aug. prose): Aurora, Verg. A. 3, 521 ; Ov. M. 3, 600 : mare radiis, Verg. A. 7, 25 : matutina tempora, Ov. M. 13, 581 : terrae mundusque, id.…

rŭbēta.opening: id. , bramblethickets , Ov. M. 1, 105 ; id. F. 4, 509 ; Calp. Ecl. 3, 5 .

rŭbĕus.opening: adj. rubus , of or belonging to the bramble-bush , bramble- : virga, a bramble-twig, Verg. G. 1, 266 .

Rŭbi.opening: a town in Apulia , now Ruvo , Hor. S. 1, 5, 94 .—Hence, , , , the inhabitants of Rubi , Plin. 3, 11, 16, § 105 ; Front. Colon. p. 127 Goes.

rŭbĭa.opening: 1. rubeus , madder , Plin. 19, 3, 17, § 47 : quam aliqui ereuthodanum vocant, id. 24, 11, 56, § 94 ; 35, 6, 26, § 45 ; Vitr. 7, 14 .

Rŭbĭco.opening: ( nom. Rubicon, Luc. 1, 214 Cort. N. cr. ), , , a small river on the east coast of Italy , which formed the boundary between Italy and Cisalpine Gaul; celebrated for having been crossed by Cœsar at the breaking out of…

rŭbĭcundŭlus.opening: adj. dim. [rubicundus], somewhat ruddy : illa, Juv. 6, 424 .

rŭbĭcundus.opening: adj. rubeo , red , ruddy : rufus quidam, ore rubicundo, Plaut. Ps. 4, 7, 121 ; cf. id. Rud. 2, 2, 8 ; Ter. Hec. 3, 4, 26 : corna, Hor. Ep. 1, 16, 8 : pluma, Col. 8, 2, 7 : luna, Plin. 18, 35, 79, § 347 : Priapus,…

rŭbĭdus.opening: adj. id. , red , reddish , dark-red (rare), cf. Gell. 2, 26, 8 sq. ; 14 : ampulla, Plaut. Stich. 1, 3, 77 : panis, id. Cas 2, 5, 2 ; cf. Fest. pp. 262 and 263 Müll.: facies ex vinolentiā, Suet. Vit. 17 .

rŭbor.opening: rubeo , redness of all shades, cf. Gell. 2, 26, 5 (class.). In gen.: candore mixtus rubor, Cic. N. D. 1, 27, 75 : medicamenta ruboris, id. Or. 23, 79 ; cf. Ov. M. 3, 491 ; id. Am. 3, 3, 5 sq. : cui plurimus ignem…

Rŭbrensis.opening: a lake of Gallia Narbonensis , near Narbonne , now L ' Etang de Sigoan , Plin. 3, 4, 5, § 32 ; called also , Mel. 2, 5, 6 .

rŭ_brīca.opening: from ruberica, from ruber (sc. terra), red earth of any kind. In gen., Vitr. 2, 3 ; Col. 3, 11 fin. ; Plin. 18, 14, 36, § 135 .— In partic., red earth for coloring , ruddle , red-ochre , red-chalk : buccas rubrica, cera…

Rŭ_brĭcātus.opening: , and , , , a river of Spain , which falls into the Mediterranean Sea. —Form Rubricatus, Mel. 2, 6 .—Form Rubricatum, Plin. 3, 3, 4, § 21 .

rŭbrīco.opening: , no perf. , , v. a. rubrica , to color red (very rare): furi rubricato minare, Auct. Priap. 73, 2 ; Ven. Vit. S. Mart. 2 fin. ; Petr. 46, 7 ; Vulg. Exod. 25, 5 ; 39, 33 .

rŭbrīcōsus.opening: adj. id. , full of ruddle or red-ochre : ager, Cato, R. R. 34, 2 : terra, id. ib. 34, 128 : solum, Col. 4, 33, 1 ; Plin. 18, 17, 46, § 163 .

Rŭ_brĭus.opening: the name of a Roman gens; masc. Rubrius, Cic. Verr. 2, 1, 25, § 64 ; id. Phil. 2, 16, 40 ; id. Brut. 45, 168 ; Caes. B. C. 1, 23 .— Fem. Rubria, Cic. Fam. 9, 21, 3 .— Adj. : Lex Rubria (or lex Galliae Cisalpinae), of…

rŭbus.opening: ( fem. , Prud. Cath. 5, 31 ; id. Apoth. 123 ) [kindr. with ruber]. A bramble-bush , blackberry-bush , Plin. 16, 37, 71, § 180 ; 17, 13, 21, § 96 ; 24, 13, 73, § 117 al. ; Verg. E. 3, 89 ; id. G. 3, 315 ; Hor. C. 1, 23,…

ructābundus.opening: adj. ructo , belching again and again , Sen. Vit. Beat. 12, 3 .

ructāmen.opening: id. , a belching , eructation , Prud. Ham. 467 .

ructātĭo.opening: id. , a belching , Cael. Aur. Tard. 5, 3, 56 .

ructātrix.opening: ructator , she that belches : mentha, i. e. that produces belching, Mart. 10, 48, 10 .

ructo.grammar: āvi, ātum, 1 v. n. and a.
ructo.opening: v. n. and a. ( dep. collat. form, , Varr. R. R. 3, 2, 3 : ructatur, Hor. A. P. 457 : ructaretur, Cic. ap. Paul. ex Fest. p. 263 Müll.) [rugo, whence ructus, erugo, eructo], to belch , eructate (class). Lit. Neutr. :…

ructŭo.opening: v. a. ructus , to belch forth (late Lat. for the usual ructare); trop.: laudes, Aug. Serm. Temp. 135 .

ructŭōsus.opening: adj. id. , full of belches : spiritus, Cael. ap. Quint. 4, 2, 123 .

ructus.opening: rugo, whence also ructo and erugo , a belching , eructation , rising of the stomach (class. in sing. and plur. ): exhalas acidos ex pectore ructus, Lucil. ap. Non. 164, 33 : suavis ructus mihist, Plaut. Ps. 5, 2, 9 ;…

rūdectus.opening: adj. rudus , full of rubbish , i. e. (of soil) poor , dry : terra, Cato, R. R. 34, 2 : locus, id. ib. 35, 1 .

rūdĕrārĭus.opening: adj. rudus , of or belonging to rubbish : cribrum, App. M. 8, p. 212, 19 .

rūdĕrātĭo.opening: rudero , a paving with rubbish , ruderation , Vitr. 7, 1 .— Transf. , a mass of broken stone , Vitr. 5, 12, 6 .

rūdĕro.opening: v. a. rudus , to cover or pave with broken stone or rubbish , Plin. 21, 4, 10, § 20 ; Vitr. 7, 1 .

Rŭdĭae.opening: a town in Calabria , the birthplace of Ennius , Mel. 2, 4, 7 ; Plin. 3, 11, 16, § 102 ; Sil. 12, 397 .—Hence, , , adj. , of Rudiœ , the Rudian , an appellation of Ennius, Enn. ap. Cic. de Or. 3, 42, 168 (Ann. v. 440…

rŭdĭārĭi.opening: (sc. Cincio) dicuntur, qui saga nova poliunt, Fest. p. 265 Müll. [1. rudis].

rŭdĭārĭus.opening: 2. rudis , a gladiator who is presented with a rudis, i. e. who receives his discharge , Suet. Tib. 7 .

rŭdĭcŭla.opening: dim. id. , a wooden spoon , a spatula , Cato, R. R. 95, 1 : rudiculā ligneā peragitare, Col. 12, 46, 3 ; Plin. 34, 18, 54, § 176 .

rŭdīmentum.opening: 1. rudis , a first attempt , trial , or essay; a beginning , commencement in any thing (not ante-Aug.; cf. tirocinium). Most usual as milit. t. t.: militare, Liv. 21, 3 ; plur. : rudimentis militiae imbutus, the…

rŭdis.opening: ( abl. sing. rudi, Capitol. Opil. Macr. 4, 5 ), a slender stick or rod. To stir with in cooking; a stirring-stick , spatula : versato crebro duabus rudibus, Cato, R. R. 79 ; so, ferreae, Plin. 34, 18, 50, § 170 ; cf.…

rŭdĭtas.opening: 1. rudis , ignorance : litteratoris, App. Flor. 4, p. 363, 6 .

rŭdītus.opening: rudo , a roaring or braying , App. M. 8, p. 215, 24 .

rŭdo.opening: (rūdo, Pers. 3, 9 ), īvi, ītum ( gen. plur. part. rudentūm, Verg. A. 7, 16 ), , v. n. and a. [Sanscr. root ru-, to howl; Gr. ὠρύω ; cf. Lat.: ravis, ravus, raucus], to roar , bellow , bray. Lit. , of animals; e. g. of…

rŭdor.opening: rudo , a roaring (Appul.), App. Flor. 3, p. 357, 38 ; id. Mund. p. 65 .

rufius.opening: the Gallic name for chama, a lynx , Plin. 8, 19, 28, § 70 .

rūfo.opening: v. a. rufus , to make or color reddish : capillum, Plin. 15, 22, 24, § 87 ; 23, 2, 32, § 67 ; 23, 4, 46, § 91 .

Rŭfrae.opening: a town of the Samnites , on the borders of Campania , now Ruvo , Verg. A. 7, 739 ; Sil. 8, 568 ; prob. the same called Rufrium , Liv. 8, 25, 4 .

rūfŭlus.opening: adj. dim. [rufus], reddish , rather red. In gen.: macilentis malis rufulus, red-haired, red-headed, Plaut. As. 2, 3, 20 (cf. rufus): radices mandragorae, Plin. 25, 13, 94, § 147 .— In partic.: , , , the military…

rūfus.opening: adj. kindr. with ruber , red , reddish , of all shades, acc. to Gell. 2, 26, 5 .—In gen.: rufus quidam, redhaired, red-headed, Plaut. Ps. 4, 7, 119 : virgo, Ter. Heaut. 5, 5, 17 ; id. Phorm. 1, 2, 1 (cf. rufulus):…

Rūfus.opening: 1. rufus , a common Roman surname (like the German Roth, Rother), Quint, 1, 4, 25; Cic. Fam. 5, 19 tit.; 14, 14, 2 al.

rūga.opening: a crease in the face , a wrinkle. In gen. (class.; usu. in plur. ). Plur. : non cani non rugae repente auctoritatem arripere possunt, Cic. Sen. 18, 62 : vos populumque Romanum non consilio neque eloquentiā, sed rugis…

Rūga.opening: 1. ruga , a Roman surname , e. g. of Sp. Carvilius, whose divorce is said to have been the first in Rome, Gell. 4, 3, 2 ; 17, 21, 44 ; Val. Max. 2, 1, 4 .

rūgātĭo.opening: rugo , a wrinkling , Cael. Aur. Tard. 2, 1 .

Rugĭi.opening: a German people who have given their name to the island of Rügen , Tac. G. 43 fin.

rūgīnōsus.opening: adj. 1. ruga , wrinkled : cutis, Cael. Aur. Acut. 1, 11 .

rŭgĭo.opening: v. n. , to roar , as a lion, Spart. Get. 5 ; Vulg. Psa. 21, 13 ; Auct. Carm. Philom. 49; to bray , as an ass, Amm. 27, 3, 1 : onager, Vulg. Job, 6, 5 : quasi ursi, id. Isa. 59, 11 .— Transf. , to rumble : rugientem…

rŭgītus.opening: rugio . A roaring of lions, Vop. Prob. 19 : leonis, Vulg. Job, 4, 10 .— Transf. , a rumbling in the bowels, Cael. Aur. Tard. 3, 2 ; 4, 7 ; Hier. Ep. 22, 11 .

rūgo.grammar: āvi, ātum, 1 v. n. and a.
rūgo.opening: v. n. and a. [1. ruga]. Neutr. , to crease , wrinkle; transf., of the dress (cf. 1. ruga, B.), to become wrinkled or rumpled : vide palliolum ut rugat, Plaut. Cas. 2, 3, 30 : pallium, id. Fragm. ap. Gell. 18, 12, 3 .—…

rūgōsĭtas.opening: rugosus , the state of being wrinkled , rugosity (late Lat.): moeroris aut irae, Tert. Patient. 15 .

rūgōsus.opening: adj. 1. ruga , wrinkled , shrivelled. Lit. : rugosiorem cum geras stola frontem, Mart. 3, 93, 4 : spadones, Hor. Epod. 9, 14 : genae, Ov. Am. 1, 8, 112 .— Poet. : senecta, Tib. 3, 5, 25 : frigore pagus (i. e. the…

rŭĭdus.opening: adj. , perh. rough : pilum (in pisturā), Plin. 18, 10, 23, § 97 .

rŭīna.opening: ruo , a rushing or tumbling down; a falling down , fall (syn.: casus, lapsus). In abstracto. Lit. In gen. (rare). grandinis, Lucr. 6, 156 : aquarum, Cael. Aur. Tard. 2, 1 med. : nostra (sc. nucum), Mart. 13, 25, 2 :…

rŭīnōsus.opening: adj. ruina , of buildings. Tumbling down , going to ruin , ruinous (rare but class.): aedes, * Cic. Off. 3, 13, 54 : parietes, Sen. Ira, 3, 35 fin. (better rimosos).—* Poet. , transf., that has already fallen , ruined ,…

Rullus.opening: a Roman surname (cf. Cic. Phil. 5, 17, 48 ). So, P. Servilius Rullus, a tribune of the people in the consulate of Cicero , who directed against him three orations on the Agrarian law , Cic. Fam. 8, 6, 5 . † , , , v.…

rūmen.opening: (collat. form , , , Arn. 7, 230 dub.; Serv. Verg. E. 6, 54 ), the throat , gullet : rumen est pars colli, quā esca devoratur, unde rumare dicebatur, quod nunc ruminare, Fest. p. 270 Müll.; cf. Paul. ex Fest. s. v.…

rūmĭfĭco.opening: v. a. rumor-facio , to make report; to report , proclaim , rumor : quam (sc. Alcumenam) cives Thebani vero rumificant probam, Plaut. Am. 2, 2, 46 .

rūmĭgĕrātĭo.opening: rumigeror , a spreading of reports , a proclaiming , rumoring (late Lat.), Lampr. Heliog. 10 .

rūmĭgĕror.opening: v. dep. a. [rumor-gero], to spread reports , to spread or noise abroad , Fest. s. v. rumitant, p. 270 Müll.; Paul. ex Fest. p. 271, 3 ib.: rumigerantium sermones, Schol. Bob. ad Cic. Or. de Aere Alien, 2 Fragm. 7, p.…

rūmĭgĕrŭlus.opening: adj. rumigeror , that spreads reports or rumors; subst. , a newsmonger (late Lat.), Amm. 14, 1, 2 ; Hier. Ep. 117, 10 ; 50, 1 .

rūmĭgo.opening: v. a. rumen-ago , to chew over again , to ruminate : jam tertium qualum, App. M. 4, p. 153, 2 : bos si non rumigat, Gargil. Mart. Cur. Boum. § 15.

Rūmīna.opening: (in some MSS. ), , rumis, qs. she that offers her breast , a Roman goddess of nursing mothers , who was worshipped in a separate temple near the fig-tree under which Romulus and Remus had sucked the breast (rumis) of…

rūmĭnālis.opening: adj. rumen , chewing again , ruminating : hostiae, Plin. 8, 51, 77, § 206 .

rūmĭnātĭo.opening: ruminor , a chewing over again , chewing the cud , rumination. Lit. : animalium, Plin. 11, 37, 79, § 201 ; Serv. Verg. E. 6, 54 .— Transf. , a doubling; a repetition , return : corticis, Plin. 15, 23, 25, § 94 : hiemis,…

rūmĭnātor.opening: id. , one that chews again or ruminates (late Lat.), Arn. 7, 230 .

rūmĭnor.opening: v. dep. a. , and (after the Aug. period) , , v. n. and a. [rumen], to chew over again , chew the cud , to ruminate. Lit. Neutr. : bos ruminat, Col. 6, 6, 1 ; Plin. 11, 37, 61, § 160 ; 9, 17, 29, § 62 al. ; Vulg. Lev.…

Rūmīnus.opening: rumis, analog. to 1. Rumina , an epithet of Jupiter , as the nourisher of all things , Aug. Civ. Dei , 7, 11.

rumis.opening: (collat. form † , , v. infra ), , a breast that gives suck; a teat , pap , dug : si parum habet lactis mater, ut subiciat sub alterius mammam, qui appellantur subrumi, id est sub mammā: antiquo enim vocabulo mamma…

rūmĭto.opening: v. freq. n. [rumo, rumor], to spread reports , to rumor : rumitant, rumigerantur. Naevius: simul alius aliunde rumitant inter sese, Fest. p. 270 Müll.

rūmor.opening: cf. Gr. ὠρύω, to howl; ὀρυμαγδός, din; Sanscr. root ru-, roar; ravas, uproar; Lat.: raucus, rudo . Lit. , the talk of the many , whether relating facts or expressing opinions. Common talk , unauthenticated report ,…

rumpo.opening: ( inf. paragog. rumpier, Afran. Com. 127 ), , v. a. root rup , to break , burst , tear , rend , rive , rupture; to break asunder , burst in pieces , force open , etc. (very freq. and class.; a favorite word of the Aug.…

rumpōtĭnētum.opening: rumpotinus , a place planted with low trees to support the vines , Col. 5, 7, 2 .

rumpōtĭnus.opening: adj. rumpus-teneo . That serves to support the running vines : genus arbusti Gallici, Col. 5, 7, 1 ; also arbores, id. 5, 7, 1, § 3 .— Subst. : , , , a kind of maple (opulus), Plin. 14, 1, 3, § 12 ; 24, 19, 112, § 172 .

rumpus.opening: a vine branch or runner (syn. tradux), Varr. R. R. 1, 8, 4 .

rūmuscŭlus.opening: dim. rumor , idle talk , common gossip (perh. only in the two foll. passages): qui imperitorum hominum rumusculos aucupati, Cic. Clu. 38, 105 : L. Cassio omnes rumusculos populari ratione aucupante, id. Leg. 3, 16, 35 .

rūna.opening: a kind of weapon , a javelin or dart. Lit. : runa genus teli significat. Ennius: runata recedit, id est pilata, Fest. p. 263 Müll.: C. Gracchus runis et iis sicis, quas, etc.... nonne omnem rei publicae statum…

runcātĭo.opening: runco . A weeding , weeding out , Col. 2, 9, 18 ; 2, 11, 19 ; Plin. 18, 21, 50, § 185 .— Concr., weeds to be pulled out, Col. 2, 11, 6 .

runcīna.opening: ῥυκάνη, acc. to Varr. L. L. 6, § 96 Müll. , a plane , Plin. 16, 42, 82, § 225 ; Arn. 6, 200 ; Tert. Apol. 12 ; Vulg. Isa. 44, 13 .

Runcīna.opening: 1. runco , a rural goddess presiding over weeding , Aug. Civ. Dei , 4, 8 med.

runcīno.opening: v. a. 1. runcina , to plane off , Varr. L. L. 6, § 96 Müll.; Arn. 5, 177 .— Trop. , com.: ego illum probe jam oneratum runcinabo, i. e. will take in, cheat, Plaut. Mil. 3, 3, 61 .

runco.opening: 1. runco , a weedinghook , grubbing-hoe , Pall. 1, 43, 3 ; cf. Isid. Orig. 20, 14, 5 .

rŭo.opening: (ruiturus, a, um, Ov. M. 4, 459 ; Luc. 7, 404 ; Mart. 1, 88, 4 ; Plin. Ep. 7, 19, 8 ; gen. plur. part. ruentum, Verg. A. 11, 886 ), , v. n. and a. , to fall with violence , rush down; to fall down , tumble down , go to…

rūpes.opening: (collat. form , , App. M. 6, p. 72 Hildebr. min.; cf. Gloss. Isid. p. 693 ), rumpo , a rock : ex magnis rupibus nactus planitiem, Caes. B. C. 1, 70 : cum (oppidum) ex omnibus in circuitu partibus altissimas rupes…

rŭpex.opening: a rough , uncultivated man; a boor , rustic , clown (ante- and postclass., and mostly in the plur. ), Lucil. ap. Fest. s. v. squarrosi, pp. 328 and 329 Müll.; Gell. 13, 9, 5 ; Tert. Apol. 21 fin. ; id. Anim. 6 fin. ; in…

rŭpĭco.opening: rupex , for rupex, a boorish man , rustic , App. Flor. 1, p. 344, 34 .

Rŭpĭlĭus.opening: the name of a Roman gens. So, P. Rupilius, consul with Popillius Laenas, A. U. C. 622, Cic. Lael. 11, 37 ; from him proceed the Leges Rupiliae, of Rupilius, Cic. Verr. 2, 2, 16, § 39 ; 18, § 44 ; 24, § 59 ; 50, § 125;…

rūpīna.opening: rupes , a cleft of a rock , a rocky chasm (Appuleian), App. M. 6, p. 184, 16 ; 7 , p. 193 fin. ; id. Flor. 2, p. 348 med.

ruptĭo.opening: rumpo , a breaking , fracture; an injuring , damage; in plur. , Dig. 9, 2, 27, § 17 .

ruptor.opening: id. , a breaker (not ante-Aug.); trop.: foederis, a violator, Liv. 4, 19 (with violator juris); 1, 28; 21, 40 fin. : 25, 31; Tac. H. 4, 57 ; Flor. 1, 3, 8 : indutiarum, Liv. 8, 39 : pacis, Tac. A. 2, 13 .

ruptūra.opening: id. , a fracture , breach , of a limb or vein, Gell. 20, 1, 33 ; Veg. 3, 65, 11 .

rūrālis.opening: adj. rus , of or belonging to the country , rural , rustic (post-class.): negotia, Amm. 30, 2, 10 : opus (Hesiodi), Macr. S. 5, 2 : Apollo, Nemes. Ecl. 1, 65 .— Adv. : , rurally , Cassiod. Var. 3, 51 .

rūrātĭo.opening: ruro , a country life (Appuleian), App. Mag. p. 310, 32 ; id. Flor. 2, p. 350, 25 .

rūrestris.opening: adj. rus , of or belonging to the country , rustic , rural (post-class.): opus, Dig. 32, 1, 99 ; Cod. Just. 4, 65, 31 : arva, App. M. 8, p. 203 : campi, id. ib. 7 , p. 194: vocabulum, id. ib. 4 , p. 143: tibia, Mart.…

rūrĭcŏla.opening: adj. gen. omn. [rus-colo], that tills the ground; that lives in or belongs to the country , rural , rustic ( poet. ); masc. : boves, Ov. M. 5, 479 ; id. F. 1, 384 : Phryges, id. M. 11, 91 : Fauni, id. ib. 6, 392 : deus,…

rūrĭcŏlārĭs.opening: adj. ruricola , of or belonging to tillage , rustic , rural : cultor, Ven. Vit. S. Mart. 1, 325 .

rūrĭgĕna.opening: rus-gigno , one born in the country; a countryman , rustic , Ov. M. 7, 765 .

Rūrīna.opening: (or, in the old orthog., ; v. the letter S ), , rus , a goddess that presided over agriculture , Aug. Civ. Dei , 4, 8.

rūro.opening: v. n. , or , , v. dep. n. [id.], to live in the country (perh. only in the two foll. passages): dum ruri rurant homines, Plaut. Capt. 1, 1, 16 : dum in agro ruror, Varr. ap. Non. 164, 23 .

rursus.opening: , and arch. or (rursum and rusum are the most usual forms in the ante-class., and rursus in the class. per.), adv. contr. from revorsus or revorsum, from reverto; cf. prorsus and sursum , turned back or backwards , back…

rūs.opening: (used in the plur. only in nom. and acc. ), etym. dub.; cf. Zend. ravanh, broad, free; ravan, a plain; Germ. Raum, space , the country (opp. to the city), lands , fields; a country-seat , farm , estate , etc. (cf.:…

Rusca.opening: a surname in the Pinarian family : M. Rusca, a tribune of the people , A.U.C. 622, Cic. de Or. 2, 65, 261 .

ruscārĭus.opening: ( ), , adj. ruscum , of or for butcher ' s-broom : falculae, for weeding out butcher ' s-broom , Cato, R. R. 11, 4 ; Varr. R. R. 1, 22, 5 .

Ruscĭno.opening: a town of Gallia Narbonensis , on the Pyrenees , now Perpignan , Liv. 21, 24 ; Mel. 2, 5, 8 ; Plin. 3, 4, 5, § 32 .

rusco.opening: a disease of cattle , Gargil. Mart. de Cur. Boum.

ruscŭlum.opening: dim. rus , a little country-seat or farm , Gell. 19, 9, 1 .

ruscum.opening: ( ), , , butcher ' sbroom : Ruscus aculeatus, Linn.; Plin. 21, 15, 50, § 86 ; 27, 100, § 173 ; 23, 9, 83, § 166 ; Verg. E. 7, 42 ; id. G. 2, 413 ; Col. 10, 374 ; cf. Fest. p. 262 Müll.

Rūsellae.opening: ( ), , , a town of Etruria , now Rosello. —Hence, ( ), , adj. , of or belonging to Rusellœ : ager, Liv. 10, 4 ; 37 : colonia, Plin. 3, 5, 8, § 51 .— Subst. : , , , the inhabitants of Rusellœ , Liv. 28, 45 fin.

Rūsĭccādē.opening: a town in Numidia , Plin. 5, 3, 2, § 22 ; cf. Mel. 1, 7 .

Rūsor.opening: rusus for rursus; cf. susum , a divinity that provides for the regular return of all productions : quod rursus cuncta eodem revolvuntur, Varr. ap. Aug. Civ. Dei , 7, 23.

Ruspĭna.opening: a town of Zeugitana , Plin. 5, 4, 3, § 25 ; 15, 19, 21, § 82 ; Auct. B. Afr. 6 fin. ; 10, 53; Sil. 3, 260 .

ruspor.opening: v. dep. n. , to search through , examine , explore : crebro quaerere, Fest. p. 264 Müll.: scrutari, Non. 166, 19 (anteclass.): ut latebras ruspans rimarem, Poët. ap. Fest. p. 265 Müll. (Trag. Rel. p. 209 Rib.); cf.:…

russātus.opening: adj. russus , clothed in red , a designation of one of the parties of charioteers in the circus. Lit. : factio, v. factio: auriga, Plin. 7, 53, 54, § 186 (al. russei).—* Transf. : sanguine suo russatus, red, reddened,…

russĕŏlus.opening: adj. dim. [russeus], somewhat red , reddish : sanies, Prud. στεφ. 11, 130.

russesco.opening: v. inch. n. [russus], to become red : russescunt frundes, Enn. ap. Charis. p. 105 P. (Ann. v. 266 Vahl.).

russĕus.opening: adj. id. , reddish (postAug. and very rare): tunica, Petr. 27, 1 : fasciola, App. M. 2, 117 : color, Pall. Mart. 13, 4 : pannus, Plin. 21, 23, 94, § 166 ; 29, 4, 17, § 64 ; 30, 11, 30, § 99 .

russŭlus.opening: adj. dim. [id.], reddish : fasciolae, Capitol. Albin. 5 fin. : tunicae, Val. Imp. ap. Vop. Prob. 4 .

russus.opening: adj. , red (very rare): vela, Lucr. 4, 75 : gingiva, Cat. 39, 19 : tunicae, Val. Imp. ap. Treb. Claud. 14 ; and Vop. Aur. 13 ; cf. Gell. 2, 26, 6 .

rustĭcānus.opening: adj. rusticus , of or pertaining to the country , rustic , country- (Ciceron.): homines ex municipiis rusticanis ... rusticana relegatio, Cic. Rosc. Am. 15, 43 sq. ; cf.: homines rusticani ex municipiis, Cic. Verr. 2,…

rustĭcātim.opening: adv. rusticor , rustically , awkwardly : rustice, Non.: ego rusticatim tangam, urbanatim nescio, Pomp. ap. Non. 166, 31 .

rustĭcātĭo.opening: id. . A living in the country , country life : neque militia solum, sed etiam peregrinationes rusticationesque communes, Cic. Lael. 27, 103 .— Agriculture , husbandry , Col. praef. § 13; 1, 1, 6; 11, 1, 6: creata ab…

rustĭcellus.opening: adj. dim. [rusticulus], somewhat rustic or clownish , Varr. ap. Plin. 7, 20, 19, § 83 .

rustĭcĭtas.opening: rusticus (not anteAug.). Lit. Country life and occupations , i. e. tillage , husbandry , Pall. Insit. 11 .— Concr., country people , Pall. 1, 31 ; Cod. Just. 1, 55, 3 .— Transf. , the manners of the country or of…

rustĭcŏla.opening: and rus-colo , an inhabitant of the country (late Lat.), Ven. Fort. Misc. 5, 5, 107.

rustĭcor.opening: v. dep. n. [rusticus]. Lit. , to live in the country , to rusticate. In gen. (class.): socerum suum Laelium semper fere cum Scipione solitum rusticari, Cic. de Or. 2, 6, 22 : sin rusticatur, id Att. 12, 1, 1 : dies ad…

rustĭcŭlus.opening: adj. dim. [rusticus], rather rustic , somewhat coarse. Libellus, Mart. 10, 19 : nomen (Bissula), Aus. Idyll. Carm. 7, 3 .— As substt. * , , , a little countryman , a little rustic , Cic. Sest. 38, 82 .— , , , a little…

rustĭcus.opening: adj. rus , of or belonging to the country , rural , rustic , country- (very freq. and class.; syn. agrestis; opp. urbanus). Lit. : vita, Varr. R. R. 3, 1, 1 ; cf.: vita haec rustica, quam tu agrestem vocas, Cic. Rosc.…

rŭtābŭlum.opening: ruo , an instrument for raking or stirring up. Lit. For fire, a fire-shovel , oven-rake , Cato, R. R. 10, 3 ; 11, 5 ; Novat. ap. Fest. p. 262 Müll. (Com. Rel. p. 226 Rib.); Suet. Aug. 75 .— For cookery, a wooden shovel…

rūtācĕus.opening: adj. 2. ruta , of rue , made from rue : oleum, Plin. Val. 2, 28 .

rūtātus.opening: adj. id. , flavored or garnished with rue : lacerti, Mart. 10, 48, 11 : mulsum, Plin. 19, 8, 45, § 156 .

rūtellum.opening: dim. rutrum , a little shovel , Lucil. ap. Non. 18, 22 .

Rŭtēni.opening: ( ), , , a people of Aquitanian Gaul , in the vicinity of the Cadurci , dwelling partly in the province now called Rhodez , Départ. Aveyron, Caes. B. G. 1, 45 ; 7, 7 ; 75 ; Plin. 4, 19, 33, § 109 ; Luc. 1, 402 .

rŭtĭlesco.opening: v. inch. n. [rutilus], to grow reddish , Plin. 8, 55, 81, § 217 ; Mart. Cap. 2, § 123 .

Rŭtĭ_lĭus.opening: rutilus, cf. Fest. p. 264 and 265 Müll. , name of a Roman gens. P. Rutilius Rufus, consul A. U. C. 649, an orator , jurist , and historian , Cic. Brut. 29 sq. Ellendt; Suet. Aug. 89 ; Quint. 5, 2, 4 ; 11, 1, 12 .— P.…

rŭtĭlo.grammar: āvi, ātum, 1 v. a. and n.
rŭtĭlo.opening: v. a. and n. 1. rutilus . Act. , to make or color reddish : comas, Liv. 38, 17 : capillos, Plin. 28, 12, 51, § 191 ; Suet. Calig. 47 ; Tac. H. 4, 61 al. — Neutr. , to be reddish; transf., to have a reddish glow ( poet.…

rŭtĭlus.opening: adj. Sanscr. rudhiras, red, bloody; cf. Gr. ἐρυθρός; Lat. ruber, rufus . Lit. , red (inclining to golden yellow): aurei rutili et inde etiam mulieres valde rufae rutilae dictae, Varr. L. L. 7, 5, § 83 Müll.; cf. Fest.…

Rŭtĭlus.opening: 1. rutilus , a Roman surname , e. g. of the augur T. Virginius, Liv. 3, 7 .

rūtrum.opening: ruo, cf. Varr. L. L. 5, § 134 Müll. . An implement for digging, a spade , shovel , Cato, R. R. 10, 3 ; 11, 4 ; Varr. and Pompon. ap. Non. 18, 22 sq. ; Liv. 28, 45 ; Ov. F. 4, 843 .— For mixing mortar, a trowel , Cato,…

rŭtŭba.opening: , perturbatio: nunc sumus in rutubā, Varr. ap. Non. 167, 9 .

Rŭtŭba.opening: A river in Liguria , now the Roya , Plin. 3, 5, 7, § 48 ; Luc. 2, 422 .— The name of a gladiator , Hor. S. 2, 7, 96 .

rūtŭla.opening: dim. 2. ruta , a little piece of rue , acc. to Cic. Fam. 9, 22, 3 ; cf. Hier. in Isa. 13, 47, 2 .

Rŭtŭli.opening: An ancient people of Latium , whose capital was Ardea, Plin. 3, 5, 9, § 56 ; Cic. Rep. 2, 3, 5 ; Liv. 1, 2 ; 1, 57 ; Verg. A. 1, 266 ; 7, 472 ; 795 et saep. —In sing. : , , , a Rutulian : audax, Verg. A. 7, 409 ; 8, 474…

Rŭtŭpĭae.opening: a town and haven of the Cantii , in Britain , now Richborough , in Kent. —Hence, , , adj. , of or belonging to Rutupiœ : ager, Aus. Parent. 18, 8 : litora, Luc. 6, 67 : fundus, Juv. 4, 141 .

S.opening: or (agreeing with littera) The eighteenth letter of the Latin alphabet, corresponding in form to the old Greek S for Σ (Etruscan in a reversed form, ); in its nature a sibilant semi-vowel, whose peculiarities were much…

Săba.opening: , = Σάβα. The largest town in Arabia Felix , especially celebrated for its myrrh , frankincense , etc.: turifera, Plin. 12, 14, 30, § 52 .—Hence, , , adj. , = Σαβαῖος, Sabœan : tus, Verg. A. 1, 416 : odor, Col. poët.…

sabaia.opening: a drink of the poor people in Illyria , prepared from barley , Amm. 26, 8, 2 ; Hier. in Isa. 6, 19 .

sabaiārĭus.opening: sabaia , one who makes , sells , or drinks sabaia, a term of reproach: et injuriose compellabatur ut sabaiarius, Amm. 26, 8, 2 .

sabănum.opening: , = σάβανον (cf. Isid. Orig. 19, 26, 7 ), a linen cloth for wiping, wrapping up in, etc.; a towel , napkin , Pall. Jun. 7, 3 ; Veg. 5, 46, 11 ; Apic. 6, 2 ; Marc. Emp. 26 med.

Săbă_oth.opening: plur. , = Σαβαώθ [Heb. ], the heavenly hosts (eccl. Lat.), Prud. Apoth. 901 : Dominus or Deus Sabaoth, the Lord (or God ) of hosts , Tert. adv. Jud. 13 ; Prud. Cath. 4, 7 .

Săbārĭa.opening: ( ), , , a city in Pannonia , a colony of the emperor Claudius , hence called Sabaria Claudia , now Szombathely , Aur. Vict. Epit. 19, 2 : Colonia divi Claudii Sabaria, Plin. 3, 24, 27, § 146 .

sabatēnum.opening: , = diabathrum, a kind of slipper (late Lat.), Plin. Val. 2, 17 .

Sabatīni.opening: the inhabitants of a town in Campania , otherwise unknown, Liv. 26, 33 fin.

Sābātīnus.opening: ( poet. ), , adj. , of or belonging to Sabate (a town of Etruria): lacus, the Lake of Sabate , now Lago di Bracciano , Front. Aquaed. 71 ; Col. 8, 16, 2 ; called lacus Sabate, Fest. p. 343 Müll.: Sabatina tribus, Liv.…

Săbāzĭus.opening: (collat. form , or , Macr. S. 1, 18 ; App. M. 8, p. 213 ), , , = Σαβάζιος, a surname. Of Bacchus , Cic. Leg. 2, 15, 37 ; Arn. 5, p. 101 ; Macr. l. l.—Hence, , , , a festival in honor of Sabazius or Bacchus , Cic. N. D.…

sabbătārĭus.opening: adj. sabbata , of or belonging to the Sabbath , Sabbatical : luxus, Sid. Ep. 1, 2 med.—Subst. : , , , Sabbath-keepers , poet. for Jews , Mart. 4, 4, 7 .

sabbătismus.opening: , = σαββατισμός, a keeping of the Sabbath , Aug. Civ. Dei , 22, 30 fin. ; Hier. Ep. 140, 8 ; id. in Isa. 16, 58, 13 .

sabbătīzo.opening: v. n. , = σαββατίζω, to observe the Sabbath , Tert. adv. Jud. 2 fin. ; Hier. Ephes. 2, 12 ; Vulg. Exod. 16, 30 ; id. Lev. 25, 2 .

sabbătum.opening: , and, more freq., , , , = σάββατα (orig. Heb. ). Lit. In gen., the day of rest among the Jews, the Sabbath; considered by the Romans to have been ordained as a fast-day. Plur. form, Just. 36, 2, 14 ; August. ap. Suet.…

Săbelli.opening: prob. contr. from Sabinuli, from Sabini , the more ancient and, for the most part, poetical name for the Sabines , Varr. ap. Philarg. Verg. G. 2, 167 : duri, Col. poët. 10, 137; Plin. 3, 12, 17, § 107 ; Hor. S. 2, 1, 36…

Săbellĭus.opening: an elder of the Christian Church at Rome , and afterwards at Ptolemais , in the third century , the founder of the heretical sect of Sabellians , Prud. Apoth. 178 .—Hence, , , , the followers of Sabellius , Sabellians ,…

Săbīni.opening: the Sabines , an ancient Italian people adjoining the Latins , a part of whom, as early as the time of Romulus, were united with the Romans as one people, under the name of Quirites, Plin. 3, 12, 17, § 108 ; Cato ap.…

Sabis.opening: A river in Gallia Belgica , now the Sambre , Caes. B. G. 2, 16 ; 2, 18 .— A river in Carmania , Mel. 3, 8, 4 ; Plin. 6, 23, 27, § 107 .— A deity of the Sabœans , Plin. 12, 14, 32, § 63 .

Sabota.opening: a city in Arabia Felix , Plin. 6, 28, 32, § 155 ; 12, 13, 30, § 52 al.

Sābrăta.opening: ( ), , , a town of Africa , near the Lesser Syrtis , now Sabart , Plin. 5, 4, 3, § 25 ; Sol. 27 .—Hence, , , adj. , of or belonging to Sabrata , Suet. Vesp. 3 ; Cypr. Conc. Carth. p. 120 .

Sabrīna.opening: a river of Britain , now the Severn , Tac. A. 12, 31 .

săbŭlōsus.opening: adj. sabulo , full of sand , sandy , gravelly : loca, Col. 2, 15, 4 : arva, id. 2, 10, 23 : terra, Plin. 13, 4, 7, § 28 : solum, id. 35, 14, 49, § 170 : aprica, id. 21, 29, 103, § 175 : lutum, Vitr. 2, 3 .

săburra.opening: kindr. with sabulo , sand , esp. in ships as ballast: onerarias multā saburrā gravatas, Liv. 37, 14 fin. : fluctu jactante saburram, Verg. G. 4, 195 ; Plin. 16, 40, 76, § 201 ; 10, 23, 30, § 60 .

Săburra.opening: ( ), , , a lieutenant of King Juba , Caes. B. C. 2, 38, 1 ; 40, 1 ; 41, 2 ; Hirt. B. Afr. 95, 1 .—Form Sabbŭra, Sil. 15, 441 ; Luc. 4, 723 .

săburrālis.opening: adj. saburra , consisting of sand , sand- : sacoma, Vitr. 9, 9 med.

săburrārĭus.opening: id. , one who carries ballast to ships : CORPVS SABVRRARIORVM, Inscr. Orell. 4116 .

săburro.opening: , no perf. , , v. a. id. , to fill or lade with ballast , to ballast (rare). Lit. : sese harenā (echini), Plin. 18, 35, 87, § 361 .—Mid., to ballast one ' s self : grues sublatis lapillis ad moderatam gravitatem…

Sabus.opening: A king of India , Curt. 9, 8, 11 .— The progenitor and god of the Sabines , Sil. 8, 423 .

Săcae.opening: ( ), , , = Σάκαι, a people of Northern Asia , a part of the Scythians , Mel. 3, 7, 1 ; Plin. 6, 17, 19, § 50 ; Curt. 5, 9, 5 ; 7, 4, 6 ; Cat. 11, 6 .—In sing. : ( Σάκης ), Claud. Laud. Stil. 1, 157 .

saccārĭus.opening: adj. saccus , of or belonging to sacks , sack- (post-Aug.). Adj. : navis, perh. laden with sacks , Auct. ap. Quint. 8, 2, 13 .— Substt. , , , one who carries sacks , Dig. 18, 1, 40, § 3 ; Inscr. Orell. 4176 .—* , , ,…

saccellātĭo.opening: saccellus ; in the later medic. lang., the applying of a little bag, a dry poultice, Veg. 3, 11, 3 ; 5, 23, 9 .

saccellus.opening: dim. saccus , a little bag : sonantes aere, Petr. 140 fin. : calidi, i.e. dry poultices for the sick, Cels. 4, 4 med. ; so Veg. 2, 24, 5 ; 3, 28, 3 al. ; Vulg. Mich. 6, 11 .

saccĕus.opening: adj. id. , of or belonging to a sack , sack- (late Lat.): cingulum, tunica, i. e. of coarse sackcloth, Hier. Ep. 22, 27 ; id. Vit. Hilar. 44 .

sacchăron.opening: , = σάκχαρον, a sweet juice distilling from the joints of the bamboo , a kind of sugar , Plin. 12, 8, 17, § 32 ; cf. Luc. 3, 237 .

saccīnus.opening: saccus, II. , made of hair-cloth : pallium, Vulg. Zach. 13, 4 .

saccĭpērĭum.opening: saccus-pera , a pocket for carrying a purse , Plaut. Rud. 2, 6, 64 .

sacco.opening: , no perf. , , v. a. saccus , to strain through a bag , to strain , filter. Lit. : saccata aqua (opp. turbida), Sen. Ep. 86, 11 ; Plin. 18, 7, 17, § 77 ; 29, 2, 10, § 35 ; 33, 6, 34, § 104 al. : Caecuba, to filter,…

saccŭlārĭus.opening: sacculus , one who by juggling tricks, etc., steals money from the pocket; a cut-purse , pick-pocket , swindler , Dig. 47, 11, 7 ; 18, 1 ; Ascon. ad Cic. Tog. Cand. p. 90 .

saccŭlus.opening: dim. saccus , a little sack or bag (not in Cic.); for filtering wine, Lucil. ap. Cic. Fin. 2, 8, 23 ; for grain, App. M. 9, p. 232 et saep.; esp. for money, a purse, Plin. 2, 51, 52, § 137 : pleno cum turget sacculus…

saccus.opening: , = σάκκος, a sack , bag. Cum iste civitatibus frumentum, coria, cilicia, saccos imperaret, Cic. Verr. 2, 1, 38, § 95 : (mulus ferebat) tumentes multo saccos hordeo, Phaedr. 2, 7, 3 .—Esp., a moneybag : mensam poni…

săcellum.opening: dim. sacrum , a little sanctuary , i. e. a small uncovered place consecrated to a divinity; a chapel : sacellum est locus parvus deo sacratus cum āra, Trebatius ap. Gell. 6, 12, 5 : sacella dicuntur loca diis sacrata…

săcer.opening: (ante-class. collat. form sacer, sacris, sacre; plur. : sacres porci, Plaut. Men. 2, 2, 16 ; id. Rud. 4, 6, 4 ; Varr. R. R. 2, 1, 20 ; 4, 16 ; sing. acc. : sacrem porcum, Fest. s. h. v. p. 318 Müll.), adj. root sa-; Gr.…

Săcerdos.opening: 1. sacerdos , a surname of frequent occurrence , esp. in the gens Licinia: C. Sacerdos, a prœtor in Sicily before Verres, Cic. Verr. 1, 10, 27 ; id. Planc. 11, 27 .

săcerdōtālis.opening: (collat. form SACERDOTIALIS, Inscr. Orell. 2469 ), , adj. id. , of or belonging to priests , priestly , sacerdotal (post-Aug.). Adj. : ludi, given by the priests on entering upon their office, Plin. Ep. 7, 24, 6 :…

săcerdōtĭum.opening: 1. sacerdos , the priesthood , the office or dignity of priests , the sacerdotal office (good prose; used equally in sing. and plur. ) Sing. : amplissimum sacerdotium, Cic. Verr. 2, 2, 51, § 127 : amplissimi sacerdotii…

săcerdōtŭla.opening: dim. 1. sacerdos , a young or inferior priestess (very rare), Varr. L. L. 5, § 130 Müll.; Veran. ap. Paul. ex Fest. s. v. oletum, p. 203 Müll.; Fest. s. v. flaminia, p. 93 ib.

săcersanctus.opening: , a false read. for sacer sanctusque, Tert. Cor. Mil. 13 ).

sacondios.opening: or , , Indian , a hyacinth-colored amethyst in India, Plin. 37, 9, 40, § 122 ; v. sacos, or socos.

săcŏpēnĭum.opening: , = σαγάπηνον, the gum-like juice of an umbelliferous plant , Plin. 19, 8, 52, § 167 ; 20, 18, 75, § 197 ; called also, from the Greek, , id. 12, 25, 56, § 126 ; 19, 3, 15, § 40 (Jahn, sacopenium in both passages).

sacos.opening: or Indian , hyacinthcolor , so called by the Indians, Plin. 37, 9, 40, § 122 .

să_crābĭlĭter.opening: adv. sacra; sc. passio , like an epileptic , as if in a fit of epilepsy : spumare, Theod. Prisc. 2, 2 .

să_crāmentālis.opening: adj. sacramentum , sacramental (late Lat.), Cassiod. in Ps. 8, 11 .

să_crārĭum.opening: sacer . A place for the keeping of holy things (sometimes, also, a place for prayer); a shrine , sacristy , sanctuary (cf.: fanum, sacellum, delubrum); an oratory , chapel : notandum est aliud esse sacrum locum, aliud…
