schīnus.opening: , = σχῖνος, the mastic-tree (pure Lat. lentiscus), Vulg. Dan. 13, 54 .

schisma.opening: , = σχίσμα, a split , separation , disunion , schism (eccl. Lat.), Tert. Praescr. 5 ; Prud. στεφ. 11, 19; 11, 30; Vulg. Johan. 9, 16 .

schismătĭcus.opening: , = σχισματικός, a separatist , seceder , schismatic (eccl. Lat.): schismaticos non fides diversa facit, sed communionis disrupta societas, Aug. Quaest. in Matt. 11 .

schistos.opening: adj. , = σχιστός, split , cleft , divided; a t. t. in Pliny the Elder: lapis, that easily cleaves or cracks , fissile , schistose , a name given to a kind of red oxide of iron , Plin. 29, 6, 38, § 124 ; 33, 4, 25, § 84…

Schoeneus.opening: , = Σχοινεύς, a king of Bœotia , father of Atalanta , Hyg. Fab. 244 ; 246 .—Hence, , , , the daughter of Schœneus , Atalanta , Ov. H. (15) 16, 263; id. Am. 1, 7, 13 .— , , adj. , of or pertaining to Schœneus : virgo, i.…

schoenĭcŭlae.opening: schoenum , prostitutes anointed with schoenum, Plaut. ap. Varr. L. L. 7, § 64 Müll.; id. ap. Fest. pp. 328 and 329 ib.

schoenus.opening: ( neutr. collat. form , Col. 12, 20, 2 and 5, somewhat dub.), = σχοῖνος, ὁ. A rush , of an aromatic kind (pure Lat. juncus), used by the Romans to season wine, Cato, R. R. 105, 2 ; 113, 1 ; Col. 12, 20, 2 ; 12, 20, 5 ;…

schŏla.opening: ( ), , , = σχολή (spare time, leisure; hence, in partic.), Leisure given to learning , a learned conversation or debate , a disputation , lecture , dissertation , etc.: in quam exercitationem (disputandi) ita nos…

schŏlāris.opening: adj. schola . Of or belonging to a school (late Lat.): incohamenta, Mart. Cap. 3, § 326 : murmur, Prud. στεφ. 9, 16: declamatio, Hier. Ep. 36, 14 .— (Acc. to schola, I. B. 2. b.) Subst. : , , , the imperial guard , Cod.…

schŏlastĭcus.opening: , um. Adj. = σχολαστικός, of or belonging to a school , scholastic (post-Aug., and in gen. referring to the schools of rhetoric): controversiae, Quint. 4, 2, 92 ; 4, 2, 97 ; Tac. Or. 14 fin. : materia, Quint. 11, 1, 82…

schŏlĭcus.opening: adj. , = σχολικός, of or belonging to a school , school - (anteand post-class.): dape, Varr. ap. Non. 452, 1 : quaedam nugalia, Gell. 4, 1, 1 : axioma, Mart. Cap. 4, § 327 .

scĭădeus.opening: , and , , , = σκιαδεύς and σκίαινα, the male and female of a sea-fish; perh. a kind of grayling or ombre : Salmo thymallus, Linn.; Plin. 32, 11, 53, § 151 .

Sciāpŏdes.opening: ( ), , , = Σκιάποσες, a fabulous people in Libya , with monstrously large soles to their feet , which they were said to turn up and use as umbrellas , Plin. 7, 2, 2, § 23 ; Tert. Apol. 8 ; Aug. Civ. Dei , 16, 8.

Scĭăthos.opening: ( ), , , = Σκίαθος, a small island in the Sinus Thermaicus , with a town of the same name , now still Skiatho , Mel. 2, 7 ; Plin. 4, 12, 23, § 72 ; Liv. 31, 28 ; 31, 45 ; 44, 13 ; Val. Fl. 2, 8 .

scībĭlis.opening: adj. scio , that can be known , knowable , discernible (post-class.): Deus non omnibus scibilis, Tert. adv. Marc. 5, 16 : scientia rei, Mart. Cap. 4, § 375 .

scĭda.opening: or , , , = σχίδν, σχέδη, a strip of papyrus bark , Plin. 13, 12, 23, § 77 .—Form scheda, a leaf or sheet of paper , Cic. Att. 1, 20, 7 ; id. Fam. 15, 16, 1 ; Quint. 1, 8, 19 ; Mart. 4, 89, 4 (form scheda; al. scida).

scĭens.opening: Part. and P. a. , from scio.

scĭenter.opening: adv. , v. scio, P. a. fin.

scĭentĭa.opening: ( plur. only Vitr. 1, 1, 18 ; 3 , praef. 1) [sciens], a knowing or being skilled in any thing, knowledge , science , skill, expertness , = cognitio, eruditio (freq. and class.). Absol. : aut scire istarum rerum nihil,…

scĭentĭŏla.opening: dim. scientia , a little knowledge , a smattering , Aug. Civ. Dei , 11, 31: parvas concinnavit scientiolas artium, Arn. 2, 56 .

scīlĭcet.opening: adv. contr. from sci- (root of scire) licet; cf. vide-licet, i-licet , or , as it is freq. written in Lucr. and in archaic lang. in Liv., and sometimes in Cels.; prop., you may understand or know, = Gr. δηλονότι, and…

scĭlla.opening: ( ), , , = σκίλλα. A sea-onion , sea-leek , squill : Scilla maritima, Linn.; Plin. 19, 5, 30, § 93 ; 20, 9, 39, § 97 ; 21, 17, 66, § 106 ; Varr. R. R. 2, 7, 8 ; Col. 12, 33 ; 12, 34 ; Pall. Febr. 29, 2 ; id. Mart. 10, 4…

scillĭnus.opening: adj. , = σκίλλινος, of sea-onions or squills : acetum, vinegar flavored with squills, Plin. 23, 2, 28, § 59 ; also called acetum scilliticum ( σκιλλιτικόν ), Cels. 5, 19, 19 ; Col. 12, 34 ; Plin. 32, 10, 47, § 135 ;…

scillītes.opening: , = σκιλλίτης ( οἶνος ), wine seasoned with squills , Col. 12, 33 ; Pall. Jul. 6 .—Hence, also, acetum scillites, Plin. 26, 8, 48, § 77 ; Aus. Ep. 4, 69 .

scimpŏdĭon.opening: , = σκιμπόδιον, a small bed or couch (syn. grabatus): Graeciense, Gell. 19, 10, 1 .

scincos.opening: or , , , = σκίγκος, a kind of lizard common in Asia and Africa, Plin. 8, 25, 38, § 91 ; 28, 8, 30, § 119 ; 32, 5, 16, § 43 .

scindo.opening: (old perf. redupl. scicidi, Enn., Naev., Att, and Afran. ap. Prisc. p. 890 P.; or Enn. p. 133 Vanl.; Com. Rel. pp. 19 and 164 Rib.; cf. also, sciciderat. Gell 6, 9, 16), v. a. akin to Gr. σχίζω, to split; cf. Germ.…

scindŭla.opening: scindo , a split piece of wood , a shingle; later form of scandula, q. v.

scintilla.opening: dim. kindr. with σπινθήρ , a spark (class.). Lit. ; sing. : videmus Accedere ex unā scintillā incendia passim, Lucr. 5, 609 ; 4, 606 ; Verg. A. 1, 174 ; Ov. M. 7, 80 ; Liv. 38, 7 al. : parva saepe scintilla contempta…

scintillātĭo.opening: scintillo , a sparkling : oculorum, as a disease, Plin. 20, 9, 33, § 80 .

scintillo.opening: v. n. scintilla , to sparkle , glitter , glow , gleam , flash ( poet. and in post-Aug. prose; cf. fulguro). Lit. : templa caeli, Lucr. 6, 644 : fulgetra, Plin. 2, 43, 43, § 113 : clipeus ardens, id. 2, 34, 34, § 100 :…

scintillŭla.opening: dim. id. , a little spark , sparklet (rare): eas in pueris virtutum quasi scintillulas videmus, e quibus accendi philosophi ratio debet, Cic. Fin. 5, 15, 43 : vitae, Tert. Anim. 23 : animae, Plaut. Trin. 2, 4, 91 Fleck.

scĭo.opening: (old imperf. scibam, Plaut. As. 2, 2, 34 ; 2, 4, 89 ; id. Ps. 1, 5, 84 ; 1, 5, 86 ; Ter. Heaut. 2, 3, 68 ; id. Phorm. 4, 1, 16 : scibas, Plaut. Aul. 4, 10, 24 ; id. Ps. 1, 5, 85 : scibat, id. Am. prol. 22 ; Lucr. 5, 934…

scĭŏlus.opening: scius , a smatterer , sciolist , Arn. 2, 86 dub.; Hier. Ep. 48, 18 ; 58, 5 ; 125, 16 .

scĭŏthērĭcon.opening: , = σκιοθηρικόν , a sun-dial , Plin. 2, 76, 78, § 187 .—Also called ( σκιόθηρον ), Hyg. Limit. p. 175 Goes.

scīpĭo.opening: root skap-; Gr. σκήπτω, to support, σκίπων, = σκῆπτρον, a staff; cf.: scāpus, scopio, scamnum , a staff (carried by persons of wealth, rank, high official station, etc.): unde ornatu hoc advenis? quid fecisti scipione?…

Scīpĭo.opening: 1. scipio , the name of a celebrated family in the gens Cornelia, the most famous members of which were the two conquerors of the Carthaginians, P. Cornelius Scipio Africanus major, in the second, and P. Cornelius…

scīrĕrўtis.opening: a sort of silver dross , Plin. 33, 6, 35, § 108 .

Scīron.opening: an Epicurean philosopher in Cicero's time : omnia meminit Sciron Epicuri dogmata, Cic. Ac. 2, 33, 106 .

scirpĕus.opening: ( ), scirpus . Adj. , of rushes , rush- : ratis, Plaut. Aul. 4, 1, 9 : clava, Nov. ap. Fest. s. v. scirpus, p. 330 Müll.: simulacra, i. e. images of men made of rushes , which were thrown into the Tiber annually, Ov. F.…

scirpĭcŭlus.opening: ( and ), id. . Adj. , of or made of rushes. So with falces (their use is unknown), Cato, R. R. 11, 4 ; Varr. R. R. 1, 22, 5 ; id. L. L. 5, § 137 Müll.: fiscella, Vulg. Exod. 2, 3 .—More freq., Subst. : ( , ), , , a…

scirpo.opening: ( ), no perf. , , v. a. id. , to plait of rushes , Varr. L. L. 5, § 137 sq. ; id. ap. Non. 83, 24 .

scirpŭla.opening: a kind of vine , otherwise unknown, Plin. 14, 3, 4, § 41 ; so, uva, Col. 3, 2, 27 ; Plin. 14, 9, 11, § 81 .

scirpus.opening: (sometimes ), , A rush , bulrush , Plin. 16, 37, 70, § 178 ; 7, 56, 57, § 206 ; Fest. p. 330 Müll.; Plaut. Rud. 2, 6, 39 ; Vulg. Job, 8, 11 . — Prov.: nodum in scirpo quaerere, to seek a knot in a bulrush , to find a…

scirros.opening: , = σκίρρος , a hard swelling or tumor , Plin. 7, 15, 13, § 63 .

scirrōsis.opening: , = σκίρρωσις , a hardening in the flesh , = saxitas, Cael. Aur. Tard. 3, 4, 49 .

sciscĭtātĭo.opening: sciscitor , an asking , inquiry : diligentissima sciscitatio, Petr. 24, 5 .

sciscĭtātor.opening: id. , an inquirer , examiner , investigator (post-Aug.): urinae, Mart. 3, 82, 16 ; Prud. Cath. 7, 193 : minutissimus artium, Amm. 22, 16, 16 .

sciscĭtor.opening: v. dep. a. [scisco], to inform one's self; to ask , inquire , question , examine , interrogate , etc. (class.; syn.: percontor, interrogo); constr. regularly, ex ( ab ) aliquo aliquid , de aliquā re , with a rel.clause…

scisco.opening: ( dep. collat. form , acc. to Prisc. p. 799 P.), v. inch. a. [scio], to seek to know; to search , inquire. Lit. (ante-class. and very rare; cf., on the other hand, the deriv. sciscitor): praefestinamus, quae sit causa,…

scissĭlis.opening: adj. scindo . That may easily be split , cleft , or rent : alumen, Cels. 5, 2 ; 6, 11 : lapis, id. 6, 6, 30 .— (Postclass.) , , rent , torn : palliastrum, App. M. 1, p. 104, 27 ; cf. centunculus, id. 9, p. 222, 27 :…

scissim.opening: adv. id. , by rending , cleaving , or dividing (late Lat.), Prud. Enchir. Vet. Test. 9 .

scissĭo.opening: id. , a cleaving , dividing , scission of a number (late Lat.), Macr. Somn. Scip. 1, 6 ; Vulg. Amos, 6, 12 .

Scissis.opening: a town of Hispania Tarraconensis, probably in the territory of the Lacetani , Liv. 21, 60 fin.

scissor.opening: scinde . One who cleaves or divides , a carver , Petr. 36, 6 .— A kind of gladiator , Inscr. Orell. 2569 .

scissūra.opening: id. , a tearing , rending , dividing; a rent , cleft , scissure (postAug.). Lit. , Sen. Q. N. 6, 2 : ad scissuram Nili, Plin. 5, 9, 9, § 50 ; 11, 28, 34, § 100 : sal rectis scissuris, id. 31, 7, 39, § 79 ; Pall. Mai, 12…

scissus.opening: = σχίσμα, a rent , cleft , Gloss. Philox.

scītāmenta.opening: 1. scitus, A. 2. . Delicate food , dainties (ante- and postclass.), Plaut. Men. 1, 3, 26 : Matius ap. Gell. 20, 9, 3 ; Macr. S. 7, 14 ; App. M. 10, p. 245 . —* Trop. , of figures of speech, niceties , prettinesses : '…

scītātĭo.opening: scitor , an asking , inquiring : indefessa scitatio, Amm. 18, 5, 1 .

scītē.opening: adv. , v. scisco, P. a. fin.

scītor.opening: (old inf. scitarier, Ov. M. 2, 741 ), v. freq. dep. a. [scio], to seek to know; to ask , inquire ( poet. and late Lat.; in Cic. Or. 16, 52 , read sciscitari; cf.: interrogo, percunctor): scitari et quaerere causas,…

scītŭlus.opening: adj. dim. [1. scitus, A. 2.], handsome , pretty , neat , trim , elegant (ante- and post-class.): facies, Plaut. Rud. 2, 7, 7 : forma atque aetatula, id. ib. 4, 1, 3 ; App. M. 2, 113, 19 : juvenem formulae scitulae, id.…

scītum.opening: , v. , P. a. , A. 1. and B.

scītus.opening: scisco , with plebi, for the more usual plebiscitum, a decree or ordinance of the people : neque populi jussu neque plebi scitu, Vet. Decr. ap. Cic. Att. 4, 2, 3 : comitia deinde de senatūs sententiā plebique scitu sunt…

scĭus.opening: adj. scio , knowing , having knowledge of a thing (mostly ante- and post-class., and rare for sciens, gnarus, peritus). Absol. : neque quemquam invenit scium, Pac. ap. Prisc. p. 634 : mulieres plus sciae, Petr. 63, 9 :…

scŏbīna.opening: scobis , a rasp , Varr. L. L. 7, § 68 ; Plaut. Fragm. ib.; Plin. 11, 37, 68, § 180 ; Tert. Apol. 12 .

scŏbis.opening: (collat. form , only acc. to Prisc. p. 751 P.; but scobis is found in Cels. 5, 5 ; 8, 2 ; Col. 4, 29, 15 ; 7, 10, 4 ; cf. scrobis init. ), , ( , Vitr. 8, 3 ; Pall. Febr. 17, 6 ) [scabo], powder or dust produced by…

Scodra.opening: a town of Dalmatia , now Scutari , on Lake Labeatis , Liv. 44, 31 ; 44, 32 ; 45, 26 ; Plin. 3, 22, 26, § 144 .—Hence, , , , the inhabitants of Scodra , Liv. 45, 26 .

scōlēcĭon.opening: , = σκωλήκιον, a kind of scarlet berry (which is apt to be wormeaten), Plin. 24, 4, 4, § 8 .

scōlex.opening: , = σκώληξ, a kind of copper rust with the appearance of being worm-eaten , Plin. 34, 12, 28, § 116 .

scŏlĭbrŏchon.opening: , = σκολίβροχον, a plant , also called callitrichos, scolopendrion, and Capillus Veneris, App. Herb. 47 .

scŏlōpax.opening: , = σκολώπαξ, a snipe , woodcock , Nemes. Fragm. Aucup. 2, 3 .

scŏlŏpendra.opening: , = σκολόπενδρα. A kind of multipede , a scolopendra , Plin. 8, 29, 43, § 104 .— A kind of sea-fish , Plin. 9, 43, 67, § 143 .

scŏlŏpendrĭon.opening: , = σκολοπένδριον , a plant , also called callitrochon and scolibrochon, App. Herb. 57 .

Scōlos.opening: , = Σκῶλος, a city of Bœotia , Plin. 4, 7, 12, § 26 ; Stat. Th. 7, 266 .

scŏlўmos.opening: , = σκόλυμος , an edible kind of thistle , carāoon : Cynara cardunculus, Linn.; Plin. 20, 23, 99, § 262 ; 21, 16, 56, § 94 ; 22, 22, 43, § 86 .

scomber.opening: , = σκόμβρος, a kind of tunny , a mackerel : Scomber scomber, Linn.; Plin. 9, 15, 19, § 49 ; 31, 8, 43, § 94 ; 32, 11, 53, § 151 ; Col. 8, 17, 12 ; Plaut. Capt. 4, 2, 71 ; Cat. 95, 8 ; Pers. 1, 43 ; Mart. 3, 50, 9 ; 4,…

scomma.opening: , = σκῶμμα , a teasing , taunting expression; a taunt , jeer , scoff , cavil (late Lat. for convicium, maledictum), Macr. S. 7, 3 .

scōpa.opening: , and plur. : , (cf. on plur. , Varr. L. L. 8, § 7 Müll.; 10, § 24 ib.; Quint. 1, 5, 16 ; Charis. p. 20 P.; 72 ib.; Diom. p. 315 ib.; sing. , v. infra , B.), root skap-, to support; cf.: scipio, scamnum . Lit. , thin…

scŏpa.opening: , = σκοπή, a speculation , theory , Mart. Cap. 8, § 812 .

scōpārĭus.opening: scopa, II. , a sweeper (late Lat.), Dig. 33, 7, 8 .

Scŏpas.opening: , = Σκόπας. A famous Grecian sculptor of Paros , who flourished between the 97 th and 105 th Olympiads , Plin. 34, 8, 19, § 49 ; Cic. Div. 1, 13, 23 ; Hor. C. 4, 8, 6 ; Mart. 4, 39, 3 .— A very rich Thessalian in the…

scŏpĕlismos.opening: , also written as Gr. σκοπελισμός, a crime said to be practised in Arabia , where a man places stones in his enemy's field , as a threat that whoever shall dare cultivate it shall be slain : quae res tantum timorem…

scōpes.opening: , = σκῶπες, a kind of owl , Plin. 10, 49, 70, § 138 ; from Hom. Od. 5, 66.

scŏpĭo.opening: root skap-; cf.: scamnum, scipio , the stalk or pedicle of grapes , Cato, R. R. 112, 3 ; Col. 11, 3, 46 ; 12, 39, 3 ; 12, 43, 10 .—Also called , Varr. R. R. 1, 54, 2 ; 2, 4, 17 .

scŏpo.opening: σκοπέω , to investigate , test , search : spiritum suum, Vulg. Psa. 76, 7 .

scōpo.opening: v. a. 1. scopa, II. , to brush or sweep away , Vulg. Isa. 14, 23 .

scŏpos.opening: , = σκοπός, a mark , aim at which one shoots, Suet. Dom. 19 .

scōpŭlae.opening: 1. scopa, II. , a little broom , Cato, R. R. 26 ; Col. 12, 38, 4 ; also in sing. : , a broom-twig , id. 12, 18, 5 .

scŏpŭlōsus.opening: adj. scopulus , full of rocks , rocky , shelvy , craggy (rare but class.): locus, Cic. Div. in Caecil. 11, 35 : mare, id. de Or. 3, 19, 69 : colles, Sil. 7, 274 : rupes, Luc. 2, 619 : Pylene, Stat. Th. 4, 102 : cete,…

scŏpŭlus.opening: , = σκόπελος, a projecting point of rock; a rock , cliff , crag , esp. a rock , shelf , ledge in the sea. Lit. (mostly poet. ; not in Cic., but v. infra , II.; cf.: rupes, cautes), in the sea: ut pars (remigum) ad…

scŏpus.opening: , = σκοπός, a goal , target : in pueri procul stantis, praebentisque pro scopo dispansam dextrae manūs palmam, sagittas direxit, Suet. Dom. 19 (dub.; Roth, scopulo; cf. σκοπός, in trop. sense, Cic. Att. 8, 11, 2 ).

scordălus.opening: a quarrelsome fellow , a wrangler , brawler (a low post-Aug. word), Petr. 95, 7 ; Sen. Ep. 83, 12 ; 56, 2 ; id. Suas. 7, 14 .

scordĭon.opening: , = σκόρδιον, a plant that smells like garlic , water - germander , scordium : Teucrium scordium, Linn.; Plin. 25, 6, 27, § 63 .—Also called , Plin. 25, 6, 27, § 63 ; and , App. Herb. 70 .

Scordisci.opening: A people on the borders of Illyria , Liv. 40, 57 ; 41, 19 ; id. Epit. 56 .— A people of Pannonia , Plin. 3, 25, 28, § 148 ; Just. 32, 3, 5 .

Scordus.opening: a mountain of Illyria , Liv. 43, 20, 1 .—Called also , Liv. 44, 31, 4 .

scorpĭăcum.opening: , = σκορπιακόν , a remedy against the sting of a scorpion , Tert. adv. Gnost. 1 fin.

scorpĭnāca.opening: a plant , also called proserpinaca, App. Herb. 17 .

scorpĭo.opening: ( poet. collat. forms and , , corresp. to the Greek), , = σκορπίων, σκορπίος, a scorpion. Lit. , Plin. 11, 37, 62, § 86 ; 28, 2, 5, § 24 ; 29, 4, 29, § 91 ; Vulg. Deut. 8, 15 . —In the form scorpius, Ov. M. 15, 371…

scorpĭoctŏnon.opening: , = σκορπιοκτόνον, the scorpion-killer , the name of a plant , the heliotrope , App. Herb. 49 .

scorpĭon.opening: a plant , also called thelyphonon, Plin. 25, 10, 75, § 122 .

scorpĭōnĭus.opening: adj. scorpio , of or belonging to a scorpion , scorpion- : genus cucumeris, Plin. 20, 1, 3, § 8 .

scorpītis.opening: , = σκορπῖτις, a precious stone , resembling the scorpion in color or shape , Plin. 37, 11, 72, § 187 .

scorpĭūrus.opening: ( , App. Herb. 72 ), , , = σκορπίουρος, scorpion's-tail , a kind of heliotrope , App. Herb. 49 .—Also called , Plin. 22, 21, 29, § 60 .

scortātor.opening: scortor , a whoremonger , fornicator , Plaut. Am. 1, 1, 131 ; Hor. S. 2, 5, 75 ; Hier. ad Ephes. 1, 13 .

scortes.grammar: id est pelles testium arietinorum a pellibus dicti

scortĕus.opening: adj. scortum, I. , made of hides or leather , leathern : etiam nunc dicimus scortea ea, quae ex corio ac pellibus sunt facta, Varr. L. L. 7, § 84 Müll.; cf. Ov. F. 1, 629 ; and Fest. s. v. scorta, p. 330 Müll.:…

scortillum.opening: dim. scortum, II. , a little or young harlot , Cat. 10, 3 ; cf. † scortulum.

scortor.opening: (old inf. scortarier, Plaut. Merc. 5, 4, 58 ), v. dep. n. [id.], to employ or associate with harlots (ante- and post-class.): scortari est saepius meretriculam ducere, Varr. L. L. 7, § 84 Müll.; Plaut. As. 2, 2, 4 ; id.…

scortŭlum.opening: πόρνη, Gloss. Vet. Lat. Gr.; cf. scortillum.

scortum.opening: cf. Gr. χόριον, corium; Lith. skurà, skin . Lit. , a skin , hide (post-class. and rare): pellem antiqui dicebant scortum, Varr. L. L. 7, § 84 Müll.: jam Omphale in Herculis scorto designata descripsit, Tert. Pall. 4…

Scōti.opening: ( ), , , the Scots , a people in the northern part of Britain , in the mod. Scotland , Amm. 27, 8, 5 ; 26, 4, 5 ; Hier. in Jovin. 2, 7 .—In sing. : Scotus, collect., Claud. B. Get. 417 ; id. IV. Cons. Hon. 33 ; id.…

scŏtĭa.opening: , = σκοτία , in architect. A hollow moulding in the base of a column , a scotia , Vitr. 3, 5, 2 .— A gutter at the end of a cornice , Vitr. 4, 3, 6 .

Scŏtīnus.opening: , = Σκοτεινός (the Obscure), an epithet of Heraclitus : legati ad Hannibalem missi Heraclitus, cui Scotino cognomen erat, etc., Liv. 23, 39, 3 (v. Munro ad Lucr. 1, 639 ); cf.: Heraclitus cui cognomen fecit orationis…

scŏtōma.opening: , = σκότωμα , dimness of vision , Isid. Orig. 4, 7, 3 .

scŏtōmătĭcus.opening: adj. , = σκοτωματικός, of or belonging to dimness of vision : passio, Cael. Aur. Tard. 1, 2 .—Hence, subst. : , , , a dim-sighted person , Scrib. Comp. 99 ; Theod. Prisc. 2, 3 .

Scŏtūsa.opening: or , , , = Σκότουσα, Σκοτοῦσσα. A town of Macedonia , near the Strymon , Plin. 4, 11, 18, § 42 .— Hence, , the inhabitants of Scotussa , Plin. 4, 10, 17, § 36 .— A town of Thessaly , near Larissa , Liv. 38, 5 ; 38, 7 ;…

scrapta.opening: or (also and ), , , an epithet of an unchaste woman , Plaut. Fragm. ap. Gell. 3, 3, 6 ; id. ap. Non. 169, 8 ; id. ap. Varr. L. L. 7, § 65 Müll. N. cr.; and Titin. ap. Fest. p. 333 ib. (Com. Rel. p. 124 Rib.).

sĕlīnas.opening: ( acc. Gr. -ada), , , a kind of cabbage resembling parsley , Plin. 20, 9, 33, § 79 .

sĕlīnon.opening: , = σέλινον, pure Lat. apium, parsley , App. Herb. 8 ; 116 ; 118 .

Sĕlīnūs.opening: , = Σελινοῦς. A town on the coast of Sicily , near Lilybœum , now Pileri : palmosa, Verg. A. 3, 705 ; Sil. 14, 201 .—Hence, , , adj. , of or belonging to Selinus , Selinusian : creta, Vitr. 7, 14 ; Plin. 35, 6, 27, § 46…

sēlĭquastrum.opening: a kind of seat or stool : ab sedendo appellatae sedes, sedile, solium, sellae, seliquastrum, Varr. L. L. 5, § 128 Müll.; cf.: seliquastra sedilia antiqui generis appellantur D littera in L conversa, ut etiam in sellā…

sella.opening: (ancient collat. form , acc. to Scaur. p. 2252 P.), , dim. for sedla; root sed-; .sedes , a seat , settle , chair , stool (syn.: sedile, scamnum): viden' ut expalluit! datin' isti sellam, ubi assidat cito, Plaut. Curc.…

sellārĭa.opening: sella , a room furnished with seats or settles; a sitting-room , drawing-room , Plin. 34, 8, 19, § 84 ; 36, 15, 24, § 111 ; used by Tiberius for debauchery, Suet. Tib. 43 ; cf. sellarius.— A public courtesan , Vet.…

sellārĭŏlus.opening: adj. sellaria , of or for sitting : popinae, as a resort for idlers and debauchees, Mart. 5, 70, 3 .

sellāris.opening: adj. sella , of or belonging to a seat (post-class.): gestatio, in a sedan, Cael. Aur. Tard. 1, 4, 92 : jumenta, furnished with saddles, used for riding, Veg. 2, 28, 34 ; 6, 7, 5 .— Subst. : , , , a saddlehorse , Vit.…

sellārĭus.opening: sellaria , one that practises lewdness upon a settle (a word invented by the emperor Tiberius), Tac. A. 6, 1 ; v. sellaria.

Sellasĭa.opening: , = Σελλασία, a town of Laconia , on the river Œnus , now St. Saranda , Liv. 34, 28 .

sellĭsternĭa.opening: sella-sterno; cf. lectisternium , religious banquets offered to female deities (because, at table, the women sat upon sellae, while the men reclined upon lecti, whence lectisternium), Tac. A. 15, 44 ; Fest. s. v. solla,…

sellŭla.opening: dim. sella , a little seat or stool; also, a sedan (post-Aug.; but cf. sellularius), Arn. 2, 23 ; Tac. H. 3, 84 ; Fronto Ep. ad M. Caes. 5, 44 .

sellŭlārĭus.opening: adj. sellula , of or belonging to a chair : quaestus, sedentary occupations or trades , Gell. 3, 1, 10 ; so, artes, App. Flor. p. 346, 34 : artifex, a mechanic, id. ib. p. 351, 21.—As subst. : , , , a mechanic : de…

Sēlymbrĭa.opening: , = Σηλυμβρία, a town of Thrace , on the Propontis , Liv. 33, 39 ; Mel. 2, 3 ; Plin. 4, 11, 18, § 47 .

sēmantĭcus.opening: adj. , = σημαντικός, designating , having an indicative force , Mart. Cap. 9 , §§ 985, 988.

sembella.opening: contr. from semi and libella , a half -libella (a coin): sembella quod libellae dimidium, quod semis assis, Varr. L. L. 5, § 174 Müll.: eandem rationem habere assem ad semissem, quam habet in argento libella ad…

sĕmĕl.opening: adv. num. root sam-, one; Sanscr. sa-, sam-, with, together; Gr. ἅμα, ἅπαξ; cf.: sem-per, sim-ilis, sim-plex, sin-gulus, etc. . Lit. , once , a single time : ter sub armis malim vitam cernere, Quam semel modo parere,…

Sĕmĕlē.opening: ( , , pure Lat. collat. form in the cass. obll.), , = Σεμέλη, a daughter of Cadmus , and mother of Bacchus by Jupiter; nom. Semele, Ov. M. 3, 293 ; id. F. 6, 485 ; id. Tr. 4, 3, 67 ; id. Am. 3, 3, 37 ; Hyg. Fab. 167 and…

sēmen.opening: root sa-, sē-; cf.: sero, sevi; Saturnus, sator, etc. . Seed. Of plants, Cato, R. R. 17 ; 27 ; 31 fin. ; 34; Varr. R. R. 1, 40 sq. : semen manu spargere, Cic. Rosc. Am. 18, 50 : terra semen excepit, id. Sen. 15, 51 ;…

sēmentātĭo.opening: semento , a sowing , the seed sown , Tert. Spect. 8 .

sēmentĭfer.opening: adj. sementis-fero , seed-bearing , fruitful : Seriphus, Verg. Cir. 476 .

sēmentis.opening: ( acc. sementim, Cic. N. D. 3, 30, 75 B. and K.; Cato, R. R. 17, 2 ; 17, 27 ; 17, 30 ; 17, 61 fin. al.; Col. 11, 2, 81 , with the var. lect. sementem, a form which appears also in Plaut. Men. 5, 7, 23 ; Varr. L. L. 5, §…

sēmentīvus.opening: adj. sementis , of or belonging to seed or sowing : feriae, that occur at seed-time, Varr. R. R. 1, 2, 1 ; cf. id. L. L. 6, § 26 Müll.; Macr. S. 1, 16 ; Fest. p. 337 Müll.; called also sementiva dies, Ov. F. 1, 658 :…

sēmento.opening: v. n. id. , to bear seed , to run to seed : herbae sementaturae, Plin. 18, 28, 67, § 259 .

sēmestris.opening: adj. semi-mensis , semi-monthly : luna, i. e. the full moon, App. M. 11, p. 258, 29 : species (lunae), Amm. 20, 3, 1 ; cf. semestrium.

sēmestrĭum.opening: id. , a half month , a fortnight , Col. 11, 2, 6 .

sēmēsus.opening: ( ( ), Verg. A. 3, 244 ; and 8, 297; cf. Wagn. ib. 3, 578 ), , adj. semi-edo , half-eaten , half-devoured , half-consumed (not ante-Aug.): praeda, Verg. A. 3, 244 : ossa, id. ib. 8, 297 : pisces, Hor. S. 1, 3, 81 :…

sē-mĕtra.opening: metrum , irregular , inharmonious : dissona, Prud. Psych. 826 .

sēmi-.opening: (also, before vowels, merely sēm-, and before libra, mestris, from mensis, and modius, sē-), an inseparable particle [Sanscr. sāmi; Gr. ἡμι-, ἥμισυς; cf. semis], half , demi- , semi-; as, semestris, semi-monthly;…

sēmĭ-ăcerbus.opening: adj. , halfsour , half-ripe : uvae, Pall. Aug. 13 .

sēmĭ-ădăpertus.opening: ( ), , adj. adaperio , half-opened : janua, Ov. Am. 1, 6, 4 .

sēmĭ-ăd-ŏpertŭlus.opening: adj. operio , half-shut , half-closed : oculi, App. M. 3, 135, 34 .

sēmĭ-ăgrestis.opening: adj. , half-rustic , somewhat boorish : Maximianus, Aur. Vict. Caes. 39 med.

sēmĭ-ambustus.opening: adj. amburo , half-burned , half-consumed (post-Aug.): cadaver, Suet. Calig. 59 : turba, Sil. 2, 681 : saxa, id. 14, 63 .

sēmĭ-ămictus.opening: adj. amicio , half-clad , half-naked (Appuleian), App. M. 1, p. 104, 28 ; 7 , p. 189, 37.

sēmĭ-ampŭtātus.opening: adj. amputo , half cut off , half-trimmed , lopped , or pruned : ramuli, App. M. 1, p. 104, 5 .

sēmĭ-ănĭmis.opening: (in verse, per synizesin, read as a quadrisyl.; and in some editions also written ), anima , and less freq. , , adj. animus , half-alive , half-dead (mostly poet. and in post-Aug. prose; syn.: semivivus, seminex). Form…

sēmĭ-annŭus.opening: adj. , of or lasting half a year : nox (in insulā Thule), Mart. Cap. 6, § 595 .

sēmĭ-ăpertus.opening: adj. aperio , half-opened , half-open : fores portarum, Liv. 26, 39 fin.

sēmĭ-ătrātus.opening: adj. , clothed in half-black , in half-mourning , Varr. ap. Non. 107, 6 .

sēmĭ-axĭus.opening: axis , an appellation of the early Christians , derived from the manner of their martyrdom : licet nunc sarmentitios et semiaxios appelletis, quia ad stipitem dimidii axis revincti, sarmentorum ambitu uriemur, Tert.…

sēmĭ-barbărus.opening: adj. , semibarbarous (post-Aug.): Galli, Suet. Caes. 76 : homo, Capitol. Max. 2 : urbs Leptis, Hier. adv. Jovin. 1, 48 .

sēmĭ-bōs.opening: a half-ox (Ovidian): vir, i. e. the Minotaur, Ov. A. A. 2, 24 ; id. Tr. 4, 7, 18 .

sēmĭ-cănālĭcŭlus.opening: the halfchannel or groove on the edge of a triglyph , Vitr. 4, 3, 5 .

sēmĭ-cănis.opening: a half-dog : semicanes dei, the Egyptian god Anubis, Luc. 8, 832 Weise.

sēmĭ-cānus.opening: adj. , half-gray , grizzled (Appuleian): comae, App. M. 9, p. 231, 5 : cincinni, id. ib. 8 , p. 212, 27.

sēmĭ-căper.opening: a half-goat (Ovidian), an epithet of Pan, Ov. M. 14, 515 ; of a Faun, id. F. 5, 101 .

sēmĭ-centēsĭma.opening: one-half per cent. , as an impost, Cod. Th. 13, 9, 3.

sēmĭ-cinctĭum.opening: a semi-girdle , a narrow girdle or apron , Mart. 14, 153 in lemm.; Petr. 94, 8 (al. hemicyclo); Isid. Orig. 19, 33 ; Vulg. Act. 19, 12 ; cf. semifunium.

sēmĭ-circŭlus.opening: adj. , semicircular : ager, Col. 5, 2, 8 .—Hence, subst. : , , , a half-circle , semicircle (syn. semiorbis): uncus in semicirculi speciem, Cels. 7, 26, 2 : ager, i. e. semicircular, Col. 5, 2, 8 .

sēmĭ-clausus.opening: ( ), , adj. claudo , half-shut , half-closed : os, App. M. 10, p. 243 : postica, Amm. 18, 6, 11 : SILVANE SEMICLVSE FRAXINO (because only half was visible), Inscr. Orell. 1613 .

sēmĭ-coctus.opening: adj. coquo , halfcooked , half-done , Col. 8, 5, 2 ; Plin. 18, 11, 29, § 116 ; 22, 25, 70, § 145 ; Pall. 1, 27, 1 .

sēmĭ-combustus.opening: adj. comburo , half-burned , half-consumed , Prud. στεΦ. 10, 859; Sid. Ep. 3, 13 .

sēmĭ-confectus.opening: adj. conficio , half-made : caespes, Sid. Ep. 6, 10 .

sēmĭ-conspĭcŭus.opening: adj. conspicio , half-visible : nonnulli per fenestras, App. M. 3, p. 130, 14 .

sēmĭ-corpŏrālis.opening: adj. corpus , half-bodied , having but half its body visible : signum (Aries), Firm. Math. 2, 12; cf. semicorporeus.

sēmĭ-corpŏrĕus.opening: adj. id. , having but half its body visible : signum (Cancer), Firm. Math. 2, 12; cf. semicorporalis.

sēmĭ-corpŏris.opening: adj. id. , having half a body (late Lat.), Cassiod. Hist. Eccl. 8, 1 .

sēmĭ-correctus.opening: adj. corrigo , half-corrected (late Lat.), Aug. c. Mend. 3, 6.

sēmĭ-crĕmātus.opening: adj. cremo , half-burned : membra, Ov. Ib. 636 : tura, Mart. 11, 54, 2 ; cf. semicremus.

sēmĭ-crĕmus.opening: adj. id. , halfburned : stipes, Ov. M. 12, 287 .

sēmĭ-crūdus.opening: adj. Halfraw : caro, Front. Strat. 2, 5, 13 : exta, Suet. Aug. 1 : lupinum, Col. 6, 25 .—* That has but half-digested , Stat. S. 4, 9, 48 .

sēmĭ-cŭbĭtālis.opening: adj. cubitum , a half-cubit long : hastile, Liv. 42, 65, 9 .

sēmĭ-cūpae.opening: cupa , a halftun; as a term of reproach, i. q. pot-belly , fat-paunch , Amm. 28, 4, 28 .

sēmĭ-dĕus.opening: adj. , half-divine : heroes, i. e. the Argonauts, Stat. Th. 5, 373 ; called also, reges, id. ib. 3, 518 ; id. Acnill. 2, 363 : parentes, id. Th. 9, 376 : Manes, Luc. 9, 7 : canes, i. e. Anubis, id. 8, 832 (al. semicanes…

sēmĭ-dĭes.opening: a half-day , Aus. Ecl. Rat. Dier. 5 , and Rat. Solst. 2.

sēmĭ-dĭgĭtālis.opening: adj , of the size of half a finger , half a digit in diameter : foramen, Vitr. 10, 22 .

sēmĭ-dīvīnus.opening: adj. , half-divine , semi-divine : locus ex oratione tuā, M. Aur. ap. Front. Ep ad Caes. 1, 5 .

sēmĭ-doctus.opening: adj. , half-taught , half-learned : discipulus, Plaut. As. 1, 3, 74 : haec ut et properans et apud doctos et semidoctus ipse percurro, Cic. de Or. 2, 42, 178 : grammaticus, Gell. 15, 9, 6 : manus villici, Mart. 10, 92,…

sēmĭ-ermis.opening: ( , v. Liv. 27, 1, 15 Drak.; cf. semesus), e (in Liv.), and ( ), (in Tac.), adj. arma , half-armed , badly or indifferently armed : mille semermes per agros palati sunt, Liv. 39, 31 : multitudo, id. 22, 50 ; 23, 5 :…

sēmĭ-factus.opening: adj. facio , halfmade , half-finished : opera, Tac. A. 15, 7 : portae valli, Auct. B. Afr. 83, 3.

sēmĭ-fer.opening: adj. ferus , halfbestial , half man and half beast. Lit. : semifer interea divinae stirpis alumno Laetus erat, i. e. the Centaur Chiron, Ov. M. 2, 633 ; so of the Centaurs, id. ib. 12, 406 ; Stat. Th. 9, 220 ; Luc. 6,…

sēmĭ-formis.opening: adj. forma , halfformed : pulli, Col. 8, 5, 12 : luna, a halfmoon, id. 4, 25, 1 .

sēmĭ-fūmans.opening: adj. fumo , halfsmoking; trop.: dignitas praefecturae, i. e. still warm or fresh , Sid. Ep. 1, 7 .

sēmĭ-fūnĭum.opening: funis , a halfrope , i. e. a slender line or cord , Cato, R. R. 135, 5 ; cf. semicinctium.

Sēmĭ-gaetūlus.opening: a half-Gœtulian , semi-Gœtulian , App. Mag. p. 289, 11 .

Sēmĭ-germānus.opening: adj. , halfGerman , semi-German : gentes, Liv. 21, 38 fin.

Sēmĭgraecŭlus.opening: dim. semigraecus , a little half-Greek , Hier. Ep. 50, 2 .

Sēmĭ-graecus.opening: adj. , halfGreek , semi-Grecian : pastores, Varr. R. R. 2, 1, 2 : poëtae et oratores, Suet. Gram. 1 : civitas (Tarentum), Flor. 1, 18, 6 .—* Adv. : , half in the Greek manner : quod dicimus, Lucil. ap. Vel. Long. p.…

sēmĭ-grăvis.opening: adj. , half-overcome : vino, i. e. half-drunken, Liv. 25, 24, 2 Weissenb. ad loc.

sē-mĭ_gro.opening: v. n. , to go away , remove from any one: a patre, Cic. Cael. 7, 18 .

sēmĭ-hĭans.opening: adj. hio , halfopened , half-open : labellum, Cat. 61, 220 ; cf. labiae, App. M: 10, p. 252, 32; cf. semihiulcus.

sēmĭ-hĭulcus.opening: adj. , half-opened , half-open : savium, Poët. ap. Gell. 19, 11, 4 ; Macr. S. 2, 2, 17 ; cf. semihians.

sēmĭ-hŏmo.opening: a half-man , i. e. half man and half beast. Lit. : Centauri, Ov. M. 12, 536 (for which, semiferi, id. ib. 12, 406 al.; v. semifer, I.): mandragoras (because formed below like a man), Col. poët. 10, 19.— Trop. ,…

sēmĭ-hōra.opening: a half-hour , half an hour , Cic. Rab. Perd. 2, 6 ; Cels. 3, 21 ; Petr. 69, 4 ; Auct. B. Afr. 38.

sēmĭ-ĭnānis.opening: ( ), , adj. , halfempty , but half-full : orbis (lunae), Plin. 2, 18, 16, § 80 .

Sēmĭ-jūdaeus.opening: a half-Jew , half a Jew , Hier. in Isa. 1, 2, 20 ; 15, 54, 12 .

sēmĭ-līber.opening: adj. , half-free : semiliberi saltem simus, Cic. Att. 13, 31, 3 ; id. ap. Sen. Brev. Vit. 5, 2 .

sēmĭ-lībra.opening: a half-pound , half a pound , App. Herb. 99 .

sēmĭ-lixa.opening: half a sutler , one little better than a sutler , as a term of reproach, Liv. 28, 28, 4 ; 30, 28, 3 .

sēmĭ-lixŭla.opening: a half -lixula, acc. to Varr. L. L. 5, § 107 Müll.

sēmĭ-mădĭdus.opening: adj. , halfwet , moist , damp : ager, Col. 2, 4, 5 .

sēmĭ-mărīnus.opening: adj. , half in the sea : corpora (Seyllarum), Lucr. 5, 892 .

sēmĭ-mās.opening: Lit. , a halfmale , hermaphrodite , Ov. M. 4, 381 ; 12, 506 ; Liv. 31, 12 fin. — Transf. , adj. , unmanned , emasculated : capri, Varr. R. R. 3, 9, 3 : semimares capi (appellantur), cum sint castrati, Col. 8, 2, 3 :…

sēmĭ-mascŭlus.opening: adj. m. , = semimas, II.: Attis, Fulg. Myth. 3, 5 .

sēmĭ-mātūrus.opening: adj. , half-ripe , Pall. Mart. 10, 22 ; id. Jun. 12 .

Sēmĭ-mēdus.opening: a half-Mede , half a Mede , App. Mag. p. 289, 13 .

sēmĭ-mortŭus.opening: adj. , half-dead (cf.: semivivus, seminecis), Cat. 50, 15 ; App. M. 6, p. 184, 23 .

sēmĭnālis.opening: adj [semen], of or belonging to seed , good for seed , seminal (late Lat.): vicia, Col. 11, 2, 76 : membrum, Auct. Priap. 26, 2 ; cf. venae, Lact. Opif. Dei, 12: viae, Cael. Aur. Acut. 3, 18, 180 : vascula, Theod.…

sēmĭnārĭus.opening: , um. Adj. semen , of or belonging to seed : seminarium pilum, for bruising seed, Cato, R. R. 10, 5 .— Subst. : , , , a nursery , nursery-garden , seed-plot , seminary. Lit. , Plin. 18, 27, 71, § 295 ; Cato, R. R. 46 ;…

sēmĭnātĭo.opening: semino , a breeding , propagation , Varr. R. R. 2, 6, 3 ; Ambros. de Noë, 29, 107.

sēmĭnātor.opening: id. , an originator , producer , author (Ciceronian). Lit. : seminator et sator et parens omnium rerum (mundus), Cic. N. D. 2, 34, 86 .— Trop. : omnium malorum, Cic. N. D. 3, 26, 66 : tamquam fallaciae seminatores,…

sēmĭ-nĕcis.opening: ( nom. does not occur), adj. nex , half-dead (not ante-Aug.; syn. semivivus): alicui semineci rapere arma, Verg. A. 10, 462 : seminecem eum ad Cannas in acervo caesorum corporum inventum, Liv. 23, 15 ; so, seminecem,…

sēmĭnĭum.opening: semen , a begetting (of animals), procreation (ante-class.), Plaut. Mil. 4, 2, 68 ; Varr. R. R. 2, 6, 1 .— Transf. , a race , stock , breed (of animals), Varr. R. R. 2, 1, 14 ; 2, 3, 3 ; 3, 9, 6 ; Lucr. 3, 742 ; 3, 746…

sēmĭnĭverbĭus.opening: semino-verbum , scattering words , babbling (for Gr. σπερμολόγος ), Vulg. Act. 17, 18 .

sēmĭno.opening: v. a. semen , to sow (rare; not in Cic.; syn.: sero, planto). Lit. : adoreum, triticum, hordeum, etc., Col. 2, 8, 1 ; 2, 8, 3 ; 2, 9, 15 ; 2, 9, 16: agrum, id. 2, 4 fin. — Transf. To beget , engender , procreate : alter…

sēmĭnōsus.opening: adj. id. , full of seeds : cucurbitae, Auct. Priap. 51, 17 .

sēmĭ-nūdus.opening: adj. , half-naked (not ante-Aug.). Lit. : consules, prope seminudi sub jugum missi, Liv. 9, 6 ; 24, 40 ; Suet. Vit. 17 ; Front. Princ. Hist. p. 318 .—As subst. : ille seminudus, Sen. Ep. 6, 2, 2 .— Transf. ,…

Sēmĭ-nŭmĭda.opening: a half-Numidian , half a Numidian , App. Mag. p. 289, 11 .

sēmĭ-ŏbŏlus.opening: a half-obolus , Rhem. Fan. Pond. 8 ; Isid. 16, 25, 10 .

sēmĭ-obrŭtus.opening: adj. obruo , half-covered : dolium, App. M. 9, p. 219, 18 .

sēmĭ-ŏnustus.opening: adj. , halfladen : naves, Sisenn. ap. Prisc. p. 909 P.

sēmĭ-orbis.opening: a half-circle , semicircle , Sen. Q. N. 1, 8, 4 ; Amm. 20, 3, 10 ; 22, 8, 5 .

sēmĭ-pāgānus.opening: a half-rustic , half a clown , Pers. prol. 6 .

sēmĭ-pătens.opening: adj. pateo , standing half-open , half-open : vestibula, Sid. Ep. 7, 6 .

sēmĭ-pĕdālis.opening: adj. , a half-foot in size , half a foot long , broad , etc.: apertura, Vitr. 10, 19 ; Col. 11, 3, 21 : spatium, id. 12, 52, 4 : altitudo, Plin. 26, 8, 42, § 69 : truncus, id. 13, 4, 8, § 37 : pisciculus, id. 32, 1, 1,…

sēmĭ-pĕdānĕus.opening: adj. , a halffoot in size , half a foot long , broad , etc.: terra, Col. 4, 1, 4 .

sēmĭ-pĕractus.opening: adj. perago , half-finished : homo, Paul. Nol. Carm. 20, 299 .

sēmĭ-pĕremptus.opening: adj. perimo , half-destroyed : jugera, Tert. Carm. Sodom. 133 .

sēmĭ-perfectus.opening: adj. perficio , half-finished. Lit. : opera absolvit, Suet. Calig. 21 ; Ambros. Spirit. Sanc. 3, 14, 18 .— Trop. : virtutes, half-perfect, incomplete, App. Dogm. Plat. 2, p. 17, 24 .

sēmĭ-pĕrītus.opening: adj. , halfskilled (with semidoctus), Front. Ep. ad M. Caes. 4, 3 .

Sēmĭ-persa.opening: a half-Persian , half a Persian , App. Mag. p. 289, 13 .

sēmĭ-pēs.opening: A half-foot , half a foot. As a measure of length, Cato, R. R. 123 ; Varr. R. R. 3, 5, 15 : latum semipede, Vitr. 2, 3 : minimi semipedum mensura, Plin. 9, 5, 4, § 11 : non altiores quino semipede, id. 17, 11, 16, § 80…

sēmĭ-piscīna.opening: a small fishpond , Varr. R. R. 1, 13, 3 .

Sēmĭ-plăcentīnus.opening: a half-Placentine , half a Placentine , Cic. Pis. 6, 14 .

sēmĭ-plēnus.opening: adj. , half-full (class.): naves, Cic. Verr. 2, 5, 25, § 63 : scrobes, Col. 5, 5, 4 : favi, id. 9, 15, 4 : vas, Pall. Febr. 32 : stationes, only half-filled, half-manned, Liv. 25, 30 fin. ; cf. legiones, Vell. 2, 80, 1…

sēmiplotĭa.opening: , Fest. s. v. ploti, p. 238 Müll.

sēmĭ-pŭella.opening: a half-maiden , as a designation of the Sirens, who were half girl and half bird, Aus. Idyll. 11, 21 .

sēmĭ-pullātus.opening: adj. , clothed in half-black : accusatores, Sid. Ep. 1, 7 .

sēpărātē.opening: adv. , v. separo, P a. fin.

sēpărātĭo.opening: id. , a sundering , severing , separation (rare, but good prose): sui facti ab illā definitione separatio, Cic. Inv. 2, 18, 55 : distributione partium ac separatione, id. de Or. 3, 33, 132 : congregatio criminum…

sēpărātīvus.opening: adj. separo , of or belonging to separation , disjunctive , separative (late Lat.): conjunctio, Diom. p. 412 P.; Prisc. 1002 P.

sēpărātor.opening: id. , he that separates , a separator (late Lat.), Tert. Praescr. 30 med. ; Vulg. Zach. 9, 6 .

sēpărātrix.opening: separator , she that separates (late Lat.): voluntas conjunctrix ac separatrix hujuscemodi rerum, Aug. Trin. 11, 10 .

sēpărātus.opening: separo , a parting , separating : parili (crinis), App. Flor. p. 350, 40 .

sē-păro.opening: v. a. 2. paro , to disjoin , sever , part , divide , separate (class. and freq., esp. in the trop. sense; cf.: divido, dirimo, disjungo, secludo). Lit. With ab : senatoria subsellia a populari consessu, Cic. Corn.…

sĕpĕlībĭlis.opening: adj. sepelio , that may be buried; hence, trop., that may be hidden or concealed (a word formed by Plaut.): stultitia, Plaut. Cist. 1, 1, 64 .

sĕpĕlĭo.opening: ( perf. sepeli, Pers. 3, 97 ; part. perf. sepelitus, Cato ap. Prisc. p. 909 P.; fut. sepelibis, Aus. Ep 25, 61 ; perf. sepelisset, Prop. 1, 17, 19 ; Quint. 8, 5, 16 ), v. a. , to bury , inter (class.): sepultus…

sē-pēs.opening: adj. sex , six-footed : populi (formicae), App. M. 6, p. 177, 26 .

sēpĭa.opening: , = σηπία , the cuttle-fish , having a black, inky liquid, Cic. N. D. 2, 50, 127 ; Plin. 9, 29, 45, § 84 ; Plaut. Rud. 3, 2, 45 ; Col. 6, 17, 7 .—This liquid was used for ink, Pers. 3, 13 ; hence, transf., ink : furva,…

Sēpĭăs.opening: , = Σηπιὰς ἄκρα , a promontory of Magnesia , Plin. 4, 9, 16, § 32 ; Mel. 2, 3 ; Val. Fl. 2, 9 .

sēpĭŏla.opening: dim. sepia , a little cuttle-fish , Plaut. Cas. 2, 8, 57 .

Sēplā^sĭa.opening: (ă, Aus. Epigr 123 ; ā, Marcell. Medic. 66), , ( , , , Varr. ap. Non. 226, 16 ), a street in Capua , where unguents were sold : Seplasia platea Capuae, in quā unguentarii negotiari sunt soliti, Ascon. Cic. Pis. 11, 24,…

sē-pōno.opening: ( part. perf. sync. sepostus, Sil. 8, 378 ; 17, 281 ; but, sepositus, Hor. S. 2, 6, 84 ), v. a. , to lay apart or aside; to put by , separate , pick out , select , etc. (class.; not in Cæs.; syn.: sejungo, segrego,…

sēpŏsĭtĭo.opening: sepono , a laying aside , setting apart , hoarding : pecuniae, Veg. Mil. 2, 20 .— A separation (postclass.): si forte qui decimam vovit decesserit ante sepositionem (for which, just before, separata), Dig. 50, 12, 2, §…

sēpŏsĭtus.opening: Part. and P. a. of sepono.

sepse.opening: pron. reflex. fem. [se - ipse], one's self. quae (virtus) omnes magis quam sepse diligit, Cic. Rep. 3, 8 (also cited by Sen. Ep. 108, 32 ).

septăs.opening: ἑπτάς , the number seven , acc. to Macr. Somn. Scip. 1, 6 med.

septĕjŭgis.opening: (sc. currus) [septem-jugum; cf. 1. sejugis], a team of seven, Inscr. Grut. 337, 8 .

septem.opening: num. adj. indecl. [Sanscr. saptan; Gr. ἑπτά ; Goth. sibun; Germ. sieben; Engl. seven], seven : septem menses sunt, quom, etc., Plaut. Most. 2, 2, 39 : septem milia, id. Mil. 1, 1, 46 : dis, quibus septem placuere…

September.opening: septem; as, October, Novem-ber, Decem-ber; cf. Varr. L. L. 6, § 34 Müll. , the seventh month of the Roman year, reckoning from March, i. e. our ninth, September (consisting, as now, of thirty days); usually with mensis:…

septem-chordis.opening: ( ), , adj. chorda , with seven strings : cithara, Isid. Or. 3, 21, 4 .

septem-flŭus.opening: adj. fluo , sevenfold-flowing , an Ovidian epithet of the Nile (as having seven mouths): Nilus, Ov. M. 1, 422 : flumina Nili, id. ib. 15, 753 (cf. the foll. art. and septemplex).

septem-gĕmĭnus.opening: adj. , sevenfold ( poet. ): Nilus (as having seven mouths), Cat. 11, 7 ; Verg. A. 6, 800 (cf. the preced. art. and septemplex): Roma (the city of seven hills), Stat. S. 1, 2, 191 : septemgemino Roma jugo, id. ib. 4, 1,…

septem-mestris.opening: ( ), , adj. mensis , of seven months (late Lat.): infans, Censor. de Die Nat. 8, § 10 : septimestris partus, id. ib. 11 , § 2.

septem-nerva.opening: septem-nervus , an herb , called also plantago, App. Herb. 1 .

septem-pĕdālis.opening: adj. , of seven feet , seven feet high : statua, Plaut. Curc. 3, 71 .

septem-plex.opening: adj. plico , sevenfold ( poet. ): clipeus (consisting of layers of ox-hides, the Homer. ἑπταβόειον σάκος , Il. 7, 220 sq.), Verg. A. 12, 925 ; Ov. M. 13, 2 (cf. id. ib. 12, 95 ): Nilus (as having seven mouths), id. ib.…

septemplĭcĭter.opening: adv. septemplex , in a sevenfold manner , Vulg. Isa. 30, 26 .

septemvĭrālis.opening: adj. septemviri , of or belonging to the septemvirs , septemviral : auctoritas, Cic. Phil. 12, 9, 23 .— Subst. : , , , the septemvirs , Cic. Phil. 13, 12, 26 .

septemvĭrātus.opening: id. , the office of the septemvirs , the septemvirate , Cic. Phil. 2, 38, 99 ; Plin. Ep. 10, 8 .

septem-vĭri.opening: (-virūm, Cic. Phil. 6, 5, 14 ), vir , a board or college of seven men , the septemvirs. Of the epulones (v. epulo, 2.), Tac. A. 3, 64 ; sing. septemvir, Luc. 1, 602 ; Plin. Ep. 2, 11, 12 ; Inscr. Orell. 2365 .— For…

septēnārĭus.opening: adj. septem , containing seven , consisting of seven , septenary : numerus, the number seven, Plin. 11, 36, 43, § 120 ; Gell. 3, 10, 1 sq. ; Macr. Somn. Scip. 1, 6 : versus, consisting of seven feet, Diom. p. 514 P.;…

septendĕcim.opening: (less correctly ; v. the letter M ), num. adj. septem - decem , seventeen : septendecim populi, Cic. Verr. 2, 5, 47, § 124 ; id. Phil. 5, 7, 19 (B. and K. XVII.); Liv. 38, 51 ; Tac. A. 13, 6 al. ; so freq. in Liv., acc.…

septēni.opening: ( gen. plur. only septenūm, Cic. Verr. 2, 2, 49, § 122 ; Col. 12, 28, 1 ), num. distrib. adj. [septem]. Seven each : a summo septenis cyathis committe hos ludos, Plaut. Pers. 5, 1, 19 : duo fasces, candelis involuti,…

septentrĭōnālis.opening: adj. septentriones, II. , of or belonging to the north , northern , north- : pars (terrae), circulus, Varr. R. R. 1 . 2, 4; Vitr. 9, 6 : plaga, Sen. Q. N. 4, 5, 2 : latus, id. ib. 5, 16, 6 ; Plin. 2, 70, 70, § 177 :…

septentrĭōnārĭus.opening: adj. id. , northern , north- : ventus, Gell. 2, 22, 15 .

septentrĭōnes.opening: ( ), ( sing. and tmesis, v. infra ), septemtrio; prop. the seven plough-oxen; hence, as a constellation , Lit. , the seven stars near the north pole ( called also the Wain , and the Great or Little Bear ): neque se…

Septĭcĭānus.opening: ( ), , adj. , of or belonging to a Septicius , Septician : libra, a Septician pound , which, in the second Punic war, was reduced from twelve to eight and a half unciae, Mart. 8, 71, 6 ; so too, argentum, id. 4, 89, 3 .

septĭcollis.opening: adj. septem-collis , seven-hilled , standing on seven hills : arx, i. e. Rome , Prud. στεφ . 10, 412 (cf.: dis, quibus septem placuere colles, Hor. C. S. 7 .

sēptĭcus.opening: adj. , = σηπτικός , producing a putrefaction , putrefying , septic : vis, Plin. 30, 4, 10, § 29 (Jahn, smecticus): dos, id. 34, 18, 55, § 177 .

septĭes.opening: ( ), num. adv. [septem], seven times : septies millies sestertium, seven thousand times a hundred thousand sesterces, Cic. Phil. 2, 37, 93 ; Liv. 28, 6 ; Plin. 16, 40, 79, § 213 ; v. sestertius.

septĭfārĭam.opening: adv. septem-for; cf.: ambifariam, multifariam , sevenfold : septifariam divisum volumen, Santra ap. Non. 170, 21 (al. septemfariam).

septĭfārĭus.opening: adj. , sevenfold (late Lat.), Cassiod. in Psa. 28 .

septĭfŏlĭum.opening: septem-folium , a plant , tormentilla , septfoil , App. Herb. 116 .

septĭfŏris.opening: adj. septem-foris , having seven openings , seven-holed (late-Lat.): fistula, Sid. Ep. 2, 2 med. : vultus, Alcim. 1, 63 .

septĭformis.opening: adj. septem-forma , sevenfold (eccl. Lat.): gratia Spiritus Sancti, Aug. Serm. Domin. 1, 4 ; Ambros. in Luc. 6, 82 al. ; Isid. 7, 3, 13 ; Hilar. in Matt. 12, 23.

septĭgrānĭus.opening: adj. , having seven grains; subst. , a plant , also called lathyris, Dynam. 2, 86.

septĭmānus.opening: adj. septem . Of or belonging to the number seven : Nonae, falling on the seventh day of the month (in March, May, July, and October; opp. quintanae, which fell upon the fifth day), Varr. L. L. 6, § 27 Müll.; Macr. S.…

septĭmātrūs.opening: septimus , a festival celebrated seven days after the ides , acc. to Varr. L. L. 6, § 14 Müll.; and Fest. s. v. quinquatrus, pp. 255 and 257 ib.

Septĭmĭus.opening: the name of a Roman gens. C. Septimius, an augur , Cic. Att. 12, 13, 2 ; 12, 14, 1 .— P. Septimius Scaevola, Cic. Verr. 1, 13, 38 ; id. Clu. 41, 115 sq. — Porcius Septimius, Tac. H. 3, 5 .— Titius Septimius, a poet and…

Septĭmontĭālis.opening: adj. Septimontium, II. , of or belonging to the feast of the Seven Hills : sacrum, Suet. Dom. 4 : satio fabae, Col. 2, 10, 8 .

Septĭmontĭum.opening: septem-mons . The circuit of the Seven Hills , the place upon which the city of Rome afterwards stood, Varr. L. L. 5, § 41 Müll.; Fest. s. v. sacrani, p. 321 ib.; and Becker, Antiq. 1, p. 122 sq.— The feast of the Seven…

Septĭmŭlēius.opening: Lucius, a native of Anagnia and friend of C. Gracchus, Cic. de Or. 2, 67, 269 ; Val. Max. 9, 4, 3 .

septĭmus.opening: ( ), , num. ord. adj. [septem]. In gen., the seventh : mense septumo, Plaut. Am. 1, 2, 20 : septimas esse aedes a portā, id. Ps. 2, 2, 3 ; cf.: isque Septimus a prisci numeratur origine Beli, Ov. M. 4, 213 : Roma…

septingēnārĭus.opening: adj. septingeni , of or belonging to the number seven hundred , consisting of seven hundred each : greges, Varr. R. R. 2, 10 fin.

septingēni.opening: num. distr. adj. [septingenti], seven hundred each : bracteae, Plin. 33, 3, 19, § 61 .

septingentēsĭmus.opening: num. ord. adj. [id.], the seven hundredth : supra annum, Liv. prooem. § 4.

septingenti.opening: num. adj. septemcentum , seven hundred : anni, Enn. ap. Varr. R. R. 3, 1, 2 (Ann. v. 493 Vahl.); cf.: annorum septingentorum memoria, Cic. Or. 34, 120 : nummi, Plaut. Rud. 5, 2, 39 : milia passuum, Cic. Quint. 25, 78 :…

septingentĭes.opening: ( ), adv. septingenti , seven hundred times , Plin. 28, 12, 50, § 183 ; 36, 15, 24, § 104 .

septĭnŭbus.opening: adj. , seven times married , Jul. ap. Aug. c. Sec. Resp. Jul. 6, 30.

septĭ-pēs.opening: adj. septem , sevenfoot; hence, poet. , excessively tall , gigantic (late Lat.): Burgundio, Sid. Ep. 8, 9 in carm.; so id. Carm. 12, 11 .

septĭrēmis.opening: adj. septem-remus . having seven ranges of oar-banks : naves, Curt. 10, 1, 3 (§ 19 Foss.).

Septizōnĭum.opening: ( ), , septem-zona . A large building in Rome in the twelfth region , prob. seven stories in height, Suet. Tit. 2 init. — A monument of the emperor Septimius Severus , in the tenth region , Spart. Sev. 19 ; 35 .— A…

septŭāgēnārĭus.opening: adj. septuageni , of or belonging to the number seventy , containing seventy , septuagenarian : fistula, seventy quarter-digits broad, Front. Aquaed. 56 : homo, a man of seventy, a septuagenarian, Dig. 50, 6, 5, § 7 .

septŭāgēni.opening: ( gen. plur. septuagenarum, Cod. Th. 14, 4, 4, § 1), num. distrib. adj. [septuaginta], seventy each : pyramides in imo latae pedum quinum septuagenum, Plin. 36, 13, 19, § 92 ; for which, in one word, fistula…

septŭāgēsimus.opening: num. ord. adj. [septuaginta], the seventieth : ad annum, Cic. Div. 1, 23, 46 : castra, Liv. 28, 16 .

septŭāgĭes.opening: adv. id. , seventy times , Col. 5, 2, 7 .—Collat. form , Mart. Cap. 7, § 737 Kopp. (dub.); Ps.-Ascon. ap. Cic. Verr. 1, p. 152 .

septŭāginta.opening: num. adj. for septumaginta, septem-decenta , seventy , Col. Arb. 4, 3 : centum septuaginta, a hundred and seventy, Cic. Verr. 2, 3, 52, § 121 : septuaginta et tres, Liv. 35, 1 fin. : septem et septuaginta annos, Nep.…

septŭennis.opening: (collat. form , Capitol. M. Aurel. 21 ), , adj. septem-annus , of seven years , seven years old : nunc priusquam septuennist (puer), Plaut. Bacch. 3, 3, 36 ; so, puer, id. Men. prol. 24 ; 5, 9, 57 ; id. Merc. 2, 2, 21 ;…

septŭennĭum.opening: septuennis , a period of seven years , Fest. p. 347 Müll.— Collat. form , Prud. ap. Tetrast. 6; Vell. 2, 31, 2 Haase.

septunx.opening: septem-uncia; cf. Varr. L. L. 5, § 171 Müll. . Lit. , seven twelfths of a whole (v. as, 1.): jugeri, Col. 5, 1, 11 ; Liv. 5, 24, 4 : auri, seven ounces, id. 23, 19, 16 .— Transf. , seven things of a kind , seven pieces…

septŭplum.opening: ίπτάπλους , a septuple : solet pro toto computari, Aug. Serm. 83 med. ; Vulg. Gen. 4, 15 ; id. Dan. 3, 19 .

sĕpulcrālis.opening: adj. sepulcrum , of or belonging to a tomb , sepulchral (Ovidian): fax, a funeral torch, Ov. H. 2, 120 : area, the funeral pyre (cf. sepulcrum, I. B.), id. M. 8, 480 .

sĕpulcrētum.opening: id. , a burialplace , cemetery : in sepulcretis rapere de rogo cenam, Cat. 59, 2 .

sĕpulcrum.opening: (less correctly ; cf. Charis. p. 56 P.), , sepelio; cf. fulcrum, from fulcio; lavacrum, from lavo, etc. . Lit. , a burial-place , grave , tomb , sepulchre (cf.: monumentum, tumulus): sepulcri appellatione omnem…

sĕpulto.opening: v. freq. a. sepelio , to hold buried : quos cara Ravenna sepultat, Ven. Carm. 8, 6, 167.

sĕpultor.opening: id. , one who buries , a burier (post-class.). Lit. : corporis mortui, Aug. Trin. 4, 3 .— Trop. : civilium turbinum (Augustus), the allayer, pacifier, Tert. Anim. 46 med.

sĕpultūra.opening: id. , a burial , interment , funeral obsequies , sepulture (freq. and class.; syn.: exsequiae, funus, humatio): mos sepulturae, Lucr. 6, 1278 : mihi quidem antiquissimum sepulturae genus illud fuisse videtur, quo apud…

sĕpultūrārĭus.opening: adj. sepultura , of or belonging to burial , funereal : fines, Auct. Limit. p. 296 Goes.

Sepyra.opening: a village in Cilicia , on Mount Amanus , Cic. Fam. 15, 4, 9 .

sĕquācĭtas.opening: f [sequor], a facility in following , a disposilion to follow , sequaciousness , sequacity (late Lat.): saltuosa scribarum, Sid. Ep. 9, 9 med. : pigra, id. ib. 4, 11 .

Sēquăna.opening: one of the principal rivers of Gallia Celtica, the Seine , Caes. B. G. 1, 1 ; 7, 57 ; 7, 58 ; Mel. 3, 2, 4 ; masc. , Plin. 4, 17, 31, § 105 .—Hence, , , , the dwellers on the Sequana, Caes. B. G. 1, 1 ; 1, 2 ; 1, 9 ; 1,…

sĕquax.opening: adj. sequor , following or seeking after , pursuing , sequacious ( poet. ; a favorite word of Vergil). Lit. : Medea, Prop. 4 (5), 5, 41. (Arcadas) Latio dare terga sequaci, pursuing, Verg. A. 10, 365 : cui (frondi)…

sĕquēla.opening: or , , id. (postAug.). Lit. , that which follows , a follower : lixas calonesque et omnis generis sequelas, Front. Strat. 2, 4, 8 : jumenta, quorum sequela erat equuleus, Dig. 47, 2, 4, § 15 : petrae aquatilis sequela,…

sĕquentĭa.opening: sequor , that which follows , the sequence , context , Boëth. Inst. Arith. 1, 10 ; plur. , id. ib. 1, 23 ; Front. Aquaed. 34 (dub.; al. consequentiae).

sĕquester.opening: (orig. form sequester, tri. ante- and post - class., and in the poets), id. , jurid. t. t., a depositary , trustee , into whose hands the thing contested was placed until the dispute was settled: sequester dicitur, apud…

sĕquestrārĭus.opening: adj. sequester, I. , of or belonging to sequestration : actio, i. e. in which the thing contested is deposited in the hands of a third party, Dig. 16, 3, 12 ; 4, 3, 9 .

sĕquestrātĭo.opening: sequestro , a depositing in the hands of a third party , a sequestration , Cod. Th. 2, 28, 1.— In gen., a separation , Cassiod. Var. 9, 24 ; id. Complex. 1 ; Alcim. Ep. 14 .

sĕquestrātor.opening: id. , one that hinders or impedes (late Lat.): officiorum familiarium (dolor), Symm. Ep. 8, 53 .

sĕquestrātōrĭum.opening: id. , a depository , a place where any thing is laid up for safe-keeping (late Lat.): terra seminibus, Tert. Res. Carn. 52 fin.

sĕquestro.opening: v. a. sequester (late Lat. for sequestro do or pono; v. sequester, I.). Lit. , to give up for safekeeping , to surrender : hominis tibi (sc. terrae) membra sequestro, Prud. Cath. 10, 133 : corpora sepulturae, Tert. Res.…

sĕquor.opening: (also written sequutus; gen. plur. part. sync. sequentūm, Verg. G. 3, 111 ), , v. dep. ( act. collat. form , acc. to Gell. 18, 9, 8 sq. ; and Prisc. p. 799 P.) [Sanscr. sak-, to follow; sakis, friend; Gr. ἕπομαι, ἕπω ;…

sĕra.opening: 2. sero , a bar for fastening doors (not fixed to the door, but put on and taken off): sera, μοχλὸς θύρας , Gloss. (mostly poet. ; not in Cic.; cf.: claustrum, obex): quā (serā) remotā fores panduntur, Varr. L. L. 7, §…

Sĕrăphīn.opening: or , plur. indecl. , = , the Seraphim , a higher order of angels among the Hebrews, Vulg. Isa. 6, 2 ; Prud. Cath. 4, 5 ; Isid. Orig. 7, 5, 24 sq.

sĕrăpĭăs.opening: , = σεραπιάς , a plant , also called orchis, Plin. 26, 10, 62, § 95 .— Called also , , , App. Herb. 15 .

Sĕrāpĭo.opening: or , , , = Σεραπίων . The name of an Egyptian ambassador to Rome , Caes. B. C. 3, 109 .— A geographer of Antioch , Cic. Att. 2, 4, 1 ; 2, 6, 1 .— In Rome, as a name for slaves; thus, of a servant of Atticus, Cic. Att.…

Sĕrāpis.opening: (a short, Prud. adv. Symm. 2, 531 ; Mart. Cap. 2, § 191 ; Paul. Nol. Carm. 26, 100 ), is and , , = Σάρᾶπις , a chief divinity of the Egyptians , subsequently worshipped also in Greece and Rome, Varr. L. L. 5, § 57…

sĕrārĭus.opening: adj. serum , living on whey : porcus, Cato, R. R. 150, 2 .

Serdica.opening: a city of Mœsia , Cassiod. Hist. Eccl. 4, 21 .—Hence, , , adj. , Serdican , of Serdica : concilium, Cassiod. Hist. Eccl. 4, 24 .— , , adj. , Serdican , of Serdica , Cassiod. Hist. Eccl. 4, 33 ; 4, 38 .

Sĕrēna.opening: a Roman female name; esp., the wife of Stilicho , eulogized by Claudian , v. Claud. Laud. Ser.

Sĕrēnātor.opening: sereno , he that makes fair weather , the clearer-up , an epithet of Jupiter, App. de Mundo, p. 75, 7; Inscr. Gud. p. 3 , n. 8; p. 3, n. 9; p. 4, n. 1 sq.; cf. serenus.

sĕrēnē.opening: adv. serenus , clearly , brightly; trop., comp. : serenius videre, Aug. Trin. 8, 3 .

sĕrēnĭfer.opening: adj. serenusfero , bringing fair weather , clearing up (late Lat.): aquilo, Avien. Arat. 988 ; id. Prognost. 414 .

sĕrēnĭfĭcus.opening: adj. serenusfacio , cleared up , clear , serene : COELO, Inscr. Orell. 855 (of the time of the emperor Antoninus Pius).

sĕrēnĭtas.opening: serenus , clearness , serenity. Lit. , of the weather, clear , fair , or serene weather; with gen. : cum sit tum serenitas, tum perturbatio caeli, * Cic. Div. 2, 45, 94 : diei solisque, Auct. B. Hisp. 29, 4: auctumni,…

sĕrēno.opening: v. a. id. , to make clear , fair , or serene , to clear up ( poet. ; syn. tranquillo). Lit. : vultu, quo caelum tempestatesque serenat (Juppiter), Verg. A. 1, 255 : axem, Sil. 12, 637 : Olympum, id. 12, 665 : glauca…

sĕrēnus.opening: adj. Sanscr. svar, sky; Gr. Σείριος; cf. σέλας; Lat. sol , clear , fair , bright , serene (class.; esp. freq. in the poets; cf. sudus). Lit. : cum tonuit laevum bene tempestate serenā, Enn. ap. Cic. Div. 2, 39, 82 (Ann.…

Sĕrēnus.opening: 1. serenus , a proper name. Q. Serenus Sammonicus, a physician under Septimius Severus , Spart. Get. 5, 5 ; Macr. 3, 16, 6 .— Q. Serenus Sammonicus, son of the preceding , author of a poem , De Medicina, still extant ,…

Sērĕs.opening: , = Σῆρες , a people of Eastern Asia (the mod. Chinese ), celebrated for their silken fabrics, Mel. 1, 2, 3 ; 3, 7, 1 ; Plin. 6, 17, 20, § 54 ; Amm. 23, 6, 67 sq. ; Verg. G. 2, 121 ; Hor. C. 3, 29, 27 ; 4, 15, 23 ; Ov.…

sĕresco.opening: v. inch. n. [serum], to turn to whey : lac frigore serescit, Plin. 11, 41, 96, § 238 .

Sĕrestus.opening: the name of a Trojan who followed Æneas , Verg. A. 1, 611 ; 4, 288 ; 5, 487 ; 9, 171 al.

Sergestus.opening: a steersman among the followers of Æneas; acc. to Vergil, the ancestor of the Sergian family , Verg. A. 1, 510 ; 5, 121 ; 5, 184 ; 5, 221 et saep.

Sergĭus.opening: the name of a Roman gens. L. Sergius Catilina, the famous conspirator. — C. Sergius Orata, a notorious voluptuary , Varr. R. R. 3, 3, 10 ; Cic. Off. 3, 16, 67 ; id. de Or. 1, 39, 178 ; id. Fin. 2, 22, 70 ; Plin. 9, 54,…

sērĭa.opening: a cylindrical earthen vessel for preserving liquids, fruit, salted provisions, etc., a large jar : relevi omnia dolia, omnes serias, Ter. Heaut. 3, 1, 51 ; Cato, R. R. 12 ; Varr. R. R. 3, 2, 8 ; Col. 12, 52, 14 ; Plaut.…

sērĭcārĭus.opening: adj. Sericus , of or belonging to silks : textor, Firm. Math. 8: NEGOCIATOR, Inscr. Orell. 1368 ; 4252 .—As substt. SERICARII, silk - dealers , Inscr. Fabr. p. 713, 346 .— , , a slave who took care of silk , Inscr.…

sĭdērītis.opening: , = σιδηρῖτις . Ironwort , vervain , Plin. 25, 5, 19, § 42 ; 26, 14, 88, § 148 .— A precious stone , Plin. 37, 10, 67, § 182 . A variety of it, found in Æthiopia, is called , = σιδηροποίκιλος , id. 37, 10, 67, § 182 .—…

sīdĕror.opening: v. dep. n. [sidus, II. E.], to be blasted or palsied by a constellation , to be planet-struck , to be sunstruck , = sidere afflari, ἀστροβολεῖσθαι : fluviatilium silurus Caniculae exortu sideratur, Plin. 9, 16, 25, § 58…

Sĭdĭcīni.opening: a people in Campania , whose chief town was Teanum, on the north-eastern side of Mount Massicus , Liv. 7, 29 ; 8, 1 sq.; 8, 15 sq.; Cic. Phil. 2, 41, 107 .— Sing. : de Egnatii Sidicini nomine, Cic. Att. 6, 1, 23…

sīdo.opening: v. n. cf. sedeo; Gr. ἵζω , to seat one's self , sit down; to settle , alight ( poet. and in post-Aug. prose; usu. of things) In gen.: quaesitisque diu terris, ubi sidere detur, Ov. M. 1, 307 ; cf.: (columbae) super…

Sido.opening: a chief of the Suevi about the middle of the first century , Tac. H. 3, 5 ; 3, 21 ; id. A. 12, 29 sq.

Sīdon.opening: (usu. ō, as in Greek; but in the derivatives common. A later collat. form , , Just. 11, 10, 8 ; cf.: Babylonia, Lacedaemonia, etc.), f , = Σιδών, ῶνος and όνος , Heb. and Phoen. a very ancient and celebrated Phœnician…

Sīdŏnĭus.opening: a proper name; so, C. Sollius Sidonius Apollinaris, a Christian writer in the middle of the fifth century , whose Carmina and Epistolae are still extant; v. Bähr, Röm. Lit. § 291.

sīdus.opening: cf. Sanscr. svid, to sweat, melt; Gr. σίδηρος (molten) iron; Lat. sudo . Stars united in a figure , a group of stars , a constellation (and hence mostly plur. ; only so ap. Cic., Cæs., and Quint.): sunt stellae quidem…

sīfĭlum.opening: , collat. form of sibilum, q. v.

Sīgălĭon.opening: σιγάω, to be silent , the god of Silence among the Egyptians , Aus. Ep. 25, 27 .

Sĭgambri.opening: (also , , and ), , , = Σύγαμβροι , Ptol. Dio Cass.; Σούγαμβροι , Strabo, a powerful people of Germany , between the Sieg and the Ruhr , and as far as the Lippe (the mod. Cleve , Berg , and Recklingshausen ), Caes. B. G.…

Sīgēum.opening: , = Σίγειον , a promontory in Troas , and a town of the same name , where Achilles was buried , now Yenishehr , Mel. 1, 18, 3 ; Plin. 5, 30, 33, § 124 ; Cic. Arch. 10, 24 ; id. Fam. 5, 12, 7 ; Liv. 44, 28, 6 .—Hence,…

sĭgilla.opening: ( sing. : SIGILLVM VOLKANI, Inscr. Marin. Fratr. Arv. p. 357; v. also infra, II.), dim. signum . Little figures or images : apposuit patellam, in quā sigilla erant egregia, Cic. Verr. 2, 4, 22, § 48 : Tyrrhena sigilla,…

Sĭgillārĭa.opening: sigilla . The last days of the Saturnalia , in which people made each other presents , especially of little images; the feast of images , Macr. S. 1, 10 fin. ; 1, 11 ; Tiber. ap. Suet. Claud. 5 ; Spart. Carac. 1 fin.…

sĭgillārĭārĭus.opening: Sigiliaria, II. A. , a maker of images , Inscr. Orell. 4280 . —Also called SIGILLARIVS, Inscr. Orell. 4279 ; and SIGILLATOR FIGVLVS, ib. 4191 .

sĭgillārīcĭus.opening: ( ), , adj. sigilla . * Of or belonging to sealing : anulus, a seal-ring, signet-ring, Vop. Aur. 50 .— Subst. : , , , little images; v. Sigillaria, II. A. 1.

sĭgillātus.opening: adj. sigilla , furnished or adorned with little images or figures : scyphi, Cic. Verr. 2, 4, 14, § 32 : putealia, id. Att. 1, 10, 3 : tentoria, Treb. XXX. Tyr. 16: serica, Cod. Th. 15, 7, 11: sal, the pillar of salt…

sĭgillĭŏla.opening: dim. id. , little figures or images , Arn. 6, 197 ; 6, 204 .

Sigimerus.opening: ( ), , , a prince of the Cherusci, the father of Arminius and brother of Segestes , Vell. 2, 118, 2 .—Segimerus, Tac. A. 1, 71 .

sigla.opening: contr. from sigilla , signs of abbreviation , abbreviations (late Lat.): sigla in libris ponere, Just. Ep. ad Antecess. § 8: leges per siglorum obscuritates conscribere, Cod. Just. 1, 17, 2, § 22 .

sigma.opening: , = σίγμα (the Greek letter sigma; hence, from its more ancient form, C). A semicircular couch for reclining at meals, Mart. 10, 48, 6 ; 14, 87, 2 ; Lampr. Heliog. 25 .— A bathing-tub of the same shape, Sid. Ep. 2, 2…

signācŭlum.opening: signo . In gen., a mark , a sign (post-class.): corporis, i.e. circumcision, Tert. Apol. 21 : frontis inscripta oleo, i.e. the sign of the cross, Prud. Psych. 360 .— In partic., a seal , signet , App. Flor. 2, p. 346 ;…

signārĭus.opening: signum , a sculptor : ARTIFEX, Inscr. Orell. 4282 .

signātē.opening: adv. , v. , P. a. B. fin.

signātĭo.opening: signo , a marking , signing : furtiva (crucis), Tert. ad Uxor. 2, 9 .

signātor.opening: id. . A sealer , signer. One who attests a will by sealing it , a witness to a will (mostly postAug.; not in Cic.): ex illis testes signatoresque falsos commodare, Sall. C. 16, 2 : signator falso, a forger, Juv. 1, 67 ;…

signātōrĭus.opening: adj. id. , of or belonging to sealing : anulus, a seal-ring, Val. Max. 8, 14, 4 ; Dig. 50, 16, 74 ; 34, 2, 25, § 10 .— Subst. : , , , a sealing , Alcim. Ep. 78 .

signātus.opening: Part. and P. a. of signo.

Signĭa.opening: an ancient town in Latium which produced an astringent wine , now Segni , Liv. 1, 56 ; 2, 21 fin. ; 8, 3; 32, 2; Plin. 14, 6 . 8, § 65; Sil. 8, 380 .—Hence, , , adj. , of or belonging to Signia , Signian : vinum, Cels.…

Signĭas.opening: , = Σιγνίας , a mountain in Greater Phrygia , Plin. 5, 29, 29, § 106 .

signĭfer.opening: adj. signumfero . In gen., sign-bearing , imagebearing , i.e. bearing signs , figures , or images ( poet. ): puppis, i.e. adorned or painted with images , Luc. 3, 558 ; so, crater, Val. Fl. 1, 337 : manus, giving…

signĭfex.opening: signum-facio , an image-maker , carver , statuary (post-class.), App. M. 2, p. 116, 13 ; Arn. 6, 199 ; Mart. Cap. 1, § 36 ; Sid. Ep. 6, 12 .

signĭfĭcābĭlis.opening: adj. significo , that has meaning , significative : vox, Varr. L. L. 6, § 52 Müll.

signĭfĭcans.opening: Part. and P. a. of significo.

signĭfĭcanter.opening: adv. , v. significo, P. a. fin.

signĭfĭcantĭa.opening: significo (postAug.). * Force , energy , significancy of words: verborum, Quint. 10, 1, 121 .— In gen., meaning , import , signification , Tert. Res. Carn. 21 ; Arn. 7, 230 ; Lact. 4, 26 .

signĭfĭcātĭo.opening: id. . A pointing out , indicating , denoting , signifying; an expression , indication , mark , sign , token , = indicium, signum, ἐπισημασία , etc. (freq. and class.). Absol. : gestus sententiam non demonstratione sed…

signĭfĭcātīvus.opening: adj. significo , denoting , signifying , significative (jurid. Lat.); with gen. : enuntiatio et quantitatis et aestimationis significativa, Dig. 50, 16, 232 ; 45, 1, 75, § 2 .

signĭfĭcātōrĭus.opening: adj. id. , denoting , signifying , significatory (late Lat.); with gen. (like significativus): verbum factitationis significatorium, Tert. adv. Herm. 32 ; Ambros. Incarn. Dom. Sacr. § 98.

signĭfĭcātus.opening: significo (postAug. for significatio, II. B. and D.). A sign , token , prognostic of coming changes of weather: tempestatum significatus. Vitr. 9, 7 fin. ; Plin. 18, 25, 59, § 221 ; 18, 31, 74, § 310 .— Lit. , meaning ,…

signĭfĭco.opening: ( dep. collat. form , acc. to Gell. 18, 12, 10 , without an example), v. a. signum-facio . In gen., to show by signs; to show , point out , express , publish , make known , indicate; to intimate , notify , signify ,…

signĭtĕnens.opening: Part. [signumteneo], constellation-bearing , starry : bigae, Enn. ap. Varr. L. L. 5, § 19 Müll. (Trag. v. 132 Vahl.); cf. signifer.

signo.opening: v. a. signum , to set a mark upon , to mark , mark out , designate (syn.: noto, designo). Lit. In gen. (mostly poet. and in post-Aug. prose): discrimen non facit neque signat linea alba, Lucil. ap. Non. 405, 17 :…

signum.opening: perh. Sanscr. sag-, to cling to, adhere; cf. sigilla . In gen., a mark , token , sign , indication (very frequent in all styles and periods; cf. insigne): meo patri torulus inerit aureus Sub petaso: id signum…

Sīla.opening: a large forest in the country of the Bruttii, which yielded great quantities of pitch , Cic. Brut. 22, 85 ; Sall. Fragm. ap. Serv. Verg. A. 12, 715 (H. 4, 7 Dietsch); Plin. 3, 5, 10, § 74 ; Verg. G. 3, 219 ; id. A. 12,…

silācĕus.opening: or , , adj. 1. sil , like ochre , of ochre : color, Plin. 35, 7, 32, § 50 : cunei, Vitr. 7, 4 ; 7, 5 .

Silanĭo.opening: or , , , a celebrated statuary , Cic. Verr. 2, 4, 57, § 126 ; Plin. 34, 8, 19, § 51 ; Vitr. 7 , praef.

sīlānus.opening: , = σιληνός , Doric σιλανός , a fountain or jet of water (usually spirting from a head of Silenus). Lucr. 6, 1265 ; Cels. 3, 18 med. ; Fest. s. v. tullios, p. 352 Müll.; Inscr. Orell. 3321 ; Hyg. Fab. 169 .

silaus.opening: a kind of parsley , smallage : Apium graveolens, Linn.; Plin. 26, 8, 56, § 88 .

sĭlens.opening: Part. and P. a. of sileo.

sĭlenter.opening: adv. , v. sileo, P. a. fin.

sĭlentĭārĭus.opening: silentium . A confidential domestic servant (orig. watching for the domestic silence; cf. Sen. Ep. 47, 3 ), Salv. Gub. Dei , 4, 3; Inscr. Orell. 2956 ; 3193 ; cf. Becker, Gallus, 2, p. 99 (2d. ed.).— In the later…

sĭlentĭum.opening: sileo . Lit. In gen., a being still or silent , noiselessness , stillness , silence (freq. and class.; cf. taciturnitas): otium et silentium est, Ter. Hec. prol. alt. 35: et ipse conticuit et ceteris silentium fuit,…

sĭlentus.opening: adj. sileo , silent , quiet : loca, Laev. ap. Gell. 19, 7, 7 .

sīler.opening: a kind of brook-willow , Plin. 16, 18, 31, § 77 ; 24, 10, 44, § 73 ; Verg. G. 2, 12 Serv.

sĭlesco.opening: v. inch. n. [sileo], to become still , silent , calm , or quiet (rare; not in Cic.; syn. obmutesco): dum hae silescunt turbae, Ter. Ad. 5, 2, 10 : deum domus alta silescit, Verg. A. 10, 101 : caeli furor aequinoctialis…

sĭlex.opening: ( poet. and late Lat.; also fem. , Verg. E. 1, 15 ; id. A. 6, 471 ; 6, 602 ; 8, 233 ; Ov. M. 9, 225 ; 9, 304 ; 9, 613 ; Amm. 14, 6, 16 ; cf. Quint. 1, 6, 2 ; gen. plur. silicum, Lucr. 6, 683 ; Luc. 4, 304 ) [root sar-,…

sĭlĭcārĭus.opening: silex , one that paves roads with pebble-stones , a pavior , Front. Aquaed. 117 ; Inscr. Grut. 645 .

sĭlĭcernĭum.opening: A funeral feast , Caecil. ap. Fest. p. 294 Müll.; Varr. ap. Non. 48, 9 ; Mart. Cap. 8, § 805 ; cf. Becker, Gallus, vol. 3, p. 296 (2d ed.).—Hence, a term of abuse applied to an old man: te exercebo hodie, silicernium,…

Silĭces.opening: a mountain-tribe in Asia : montani, Plin. 6, 26, 30, § 118 .

sĭlĭcĕus.opening: adj. silex , of flint or limestone , silicious : saxa, Vitr. 8, 3 fin. : lapides, Cato, R. R. 18, 3 .— Trop. : cor, Laev. ap. Gell. 19, 7, 10 .

sĭlĭcĭa.opening: a plant , also called faenum Graecum, fenugreek , Plin. 18, 16, 39, § 140 ; 24, 19, 120, § 184 ; called also siliqua, Col. 2, 10, 33 ; 11, 2, 71 .

sĭlĭcŭla.opening: dim. siliqua , a little husk or pod , a silicle , Varr. R. R. 1, 23, 3 .

sĭlīgĭnārĭus.opening: siligo , a baker of wheat-flour , Dig. 47, 2, 52, § 11 ; Inscr. Orell. 1810 ; Inscr. Rein. cl. 1, n. 254; Inscr. Don. cl. 9, n. 11.

sĭlīgĭnĕus.opening: (late form , Dynam. 1, 7), adj. id. , of wheat , wheaten : farina, Cato, R. R. 121 ; Plin. 18, 9, 20, § 88 : panis, Varr. ap. Non. 88, 14 ; Sen. Ep. 123, 2 ; Vop. Aurel. 35 : cunni, i. e. wheaten loaves of obscene form,…

sĭlīgo.opening: A kind of very white wheat , winter-wheat : Triticum hibernum, Linn.; Cato, R. R. 35, 1 ?? Varr. R. R. 1, 23, 2 ; Cels. 2, 19 ; Col. 2, 6, 2 ; 2, 9, 5 ; 2, 9, 13 ; Plin. 18, 8, 20, § 85 ; 18, 7, 10, § 61 .— Transf. ,…

sĭlĭquastrum.opening: a plant , also called piperitis, pepperwort , Plin. 19, 12, 62, § 187 ; 20, 17, 66, § 174 .

sĭlĭquor.opening: v. dep. siliqua, I. , to put forth or get pods , Plin. 17, 9, 6, § 54 ; 18, 7, 10, § 59 .

Silis.opening: the name of several rivers. I. q. Jaxartes, Plin. 6, 16, 18, § 49 .— I. q. Tanais, the Don , Plin. 6, 7, 7, § 20 .— A river in the Venetian territories , Plin. 3, 18, 22, § 126 .

Sīlĭus.opening: the name of a Roman gens. P. Silius Nerva, a proprœtor in Bithynia and Pontus , to whom are addressed the letters Cic. Fam. 13, 47 , and 61 sqq.; cf. id. Att. 10, 13, 3 .— T. Silius, a military tribune under Cœsar ,…

sillŏgrăphus.opening: , = σιλλογράφος , a writer of lampoons or satires , Amm. 22, 16, 16 .

sillўbus.opening: , = σίλλυβον , a kind of thistle , Plin. 22, 22, 42, § 85 ; 26, 7, 25, § 40 (but the true reading, Cic. Att. 4, 5, 3 ; 4, 8 , a, 2, is sittybus, q. v.).

silphĭum.opening: , = σίλφιον , a plant , called in pure Latin laserpitium, Cato, R. R. 157, 7 ; Plin. 19, 3, 15, § 38 ; 22, 23, 48, § 100 ( Col. 6, 17, 7 ; 12, 7, 4 , written as Greek).

Silpia.opening: a city of Hispania Baetica, prob. Linares , Liv. 28, 12 .

sĭlūrus.opening: , = σίλουρος , a riverfish , prob. the sheat-fish : Silurus glanis, Linn.; Plin. 9, 15, 17, § 44 ; 32, 9, 33, § 104 ; Lucil. ap. Varr. L. L. 7, § 47 Müll; Juv. 4, 33 ; 14, 132 ; Aus. Mos. 135 .

sĭlus.opening: adj. , having a broad , turned-up nose , pug-nosed , snub-nosed , σιμός (cf. simus): ecquos (deos arbitramur) silos, flaccos, frontones? etc., Cic. N. D. 1, 29, 80 ; ante-class. collat. form , , , Plaut. Rud. 2, 2, 11 ;…

silvestris.opening: ( , Plin. 14, 16 , 19, § 110; Col. 1 , praef. 25; Sen. Hippol. 460 ; also written ), (collat. form, dat. SILVANO SILVESTRO, Inscr. Orell. 4990 ; gen. plur. sync. silvestrum, Att. Trag. Rel. v. 256 Rib.), adj. silva . Of…

silvĭcŏla.opening: ( ), , silvacolo , inhabiting woods , sylvan ( poet. ): silvicolae homones, Naev. B. Pun. 2, 17 : viri, Prop. 3, 13 (4, 12), 34: Faunus, Verg. A. 10, 551 : Pales, Ov. F. 4, 746 .

silvĭ-cultrix.opening: ( ), , adj. f. [silva], living in the woods : cerva, Cat. 63, 72 .

silvĭfrăgus.opening: ( ), , adj. silva-frango , breaking or crushing the forest or trees : flabra venti, Lucr. 1, 275 .

silvĭger.opening: ( ), , adj. silva-gero , bearing woods , wooded , woody (very rare): montes, Plin. 31, 3, 26, § 43 : DEVS, a sylvan deity, Inscr. Orell. 1488 (perhaps spurious).

Silvĭus.opening: the name of several kings of Alba Longa, Liv. 1, 3 ; Verg. A. 6, 769 ; Ov. M. 14, 610 .—Hence the fem. Silvia; v. 1. Rhea.

silvōsus.opening: adj. silva , full of woods or trees , woody : saltus, Liv. 9, 2, 7 : rami emicant silvosā multitudine, forestlike, Plin. 12, 5, 11, § 23 ; so, crebrae arbores et silvosae, Vitr. 8, 1 fin.

silvŭla.opening: dim. id. , a little wood , a copse (very rare), Col. 8, 15, 4 ; Sid. Carm. 9, 229 .

sīma.opening: in architecture, a moulding, the ogee, Vitr. 3, 3 fin. ; Inscr. Grut. 207 , col. 1.

sīmĭa.opening: (rarely ), or , , etym. dub.; perh. akin with similis . An ape , Plin. 8, 54, 80, § 215 ; 11, 44, 100, § 246 ; Enn. ap. Cic. N. D. 1, 35, 97 (Sat. v. 45 Vahl.); Cic. Div. 1, 34, 76 ; 2, 32, 69 ; Plaut. Mil. 2, 2, 7 ; 2,…

sĭmĭlāgĭnĕus.opening: adj. similago , made of fine wheat flour : panis, Vulg. Ecclus. 39, 31 .
