solino.opening: = consulo, acc. to Fest. pp. 350 and 351 Müll. [prob. the lengthened form from solo, the ground form to con-sul and con-sulo; different from solinunt-solent; v. soleo init. ].

Sōlīnus.opening: C. Julius, a Roman writer of the third century of the Christian era , author of a work entitled Polyhistor, mostly taken from Pliny's Historia Naturalis.

sŏlĭpūga.opening: a kind of venomous ant (or, acc. to Solinus, a kind of venomous spider ), Plin. 29, 4, 29, § 92 ; 22, 25, 81, § 163 . —Called also , Luc. 9, 837 ; , acc. to Fest. pp. 300 and 301 Müll.; , Sol. 4, 3 and 6; and , Plin.…

sŏlĭtānĕus.opening: adj. solitus, from soleo , usual , customary , ordinary : dolores, Marc. Emp 20 med.

sōlĭtānĕus.opening: adj. solus , separate , distinct : libellum confeci, Theod. Prisc. 3 praef.

sōlĭtānus.opening: adj. sol , the appellation of a species of African snail , perh. named from the Promunturium Solis ( Plin. 5, 1, 1, § 9 ); Varr. R. R. 3, 14, 4 ; Plin. 9, 56, 82, § 174 .

sōlĭtārĭus.opening: adj. solus , alone , by itself , lonely , solitary (class.; syn. singularis): natura solitarium nihil amat, Cic. Lael. 23, 88 : quoniam solitaria non posset virtus ad ea, quae summa sunt, pervenire, conjuncta et…

sōlĭtas.opening: solus , a being alone , loneliness , solitude (ante- and post-class. for solitudo): tuam solitatem memorans, Att. ap. Non. 173, 28 (Trag. Rel. p. 153 Rib.); App. M. 9, p. 225, 14 ; id. Mag. p. 288, 5 ; Tert. adv. Val.…

sōlĭtātim.opening: adv. solitas , solitarily , Front. Eloqu. p. 235 Mai.

sŏlĭto.opening: v. freq. n. [soleo], to be much accustomed or wont : Scipionem Africanum solitavisse in Capitolium ventitare, Gell. 7, 1, 6 .

sōlĭtūdo.opening: solus , a being alone or solitary , loneliness , solitariness , solitude (of a person or place); a lonely place , desert , wilderness (class. in sing. and plur. ; cf.: secretum, secessus). In gen.: ampla domus dedecori…

sŏlĭtus.opening: Part. and P. a. , from soleo.

sŏlĭum.opening: from the root sol, kindr. with sed, sedeo , a seat. Most usu. of gods, kings, or other distinguished personages. Lit. , a seat , chair of state , throne (cf.: thronus, tribunal): regali in solio sedens, Cic. Fin. 2, 21,…

sōlĭvăgus.opening: adj. solus - vagor (Ciceron.). Lit. , wandering or roving alone; of animals that lead a solitary life: earum (bestiarum) partim solivagas, partim congregatas, Cic. Tusc. 5, 13, 38 .—Of persons: non est enim singulare…

sollemnis.opening: (less correctly , , , ), , adj. sollus, i. e. totus-annus , prop. that takes place every year; in relig. lang. of solemnities, yearly , annual; hence, in gen., Lit. , stated , established , appointed : sollemne, quod…

sollemnĭtas.opening: ( , , and ), , sollemnis (postclass.; cf.: sollemne, celebratio). A solemnity , festival , celebration of a day: dierum variae sollemnitates, Gell. 2, 24, 15 : pristina (ludorum Isthmiorum), Sol. 7 : condendi honoris,…

sollemnĭtus.opening: ( , , ), adv. sollemnis , solemnly , Liv. Andron. ap. Non. 176, 14 .

sollers.opening: ( ), ( abl. regularly sollerti; sollerte, Ov. P. 4, 14, 35 ), adj. sollus, i. e. totus - ars, and therefore qs. all art; hence, in gen. , skilled , skilful , clever , dexterous , adroit , expert (class.; syn.; sagax,…

sollertĭa.opening: ( ), , sollers , skill , shrewdness , quickness of mind , ingenuity , dexterity , adroitness , expertness , etc. (class.; syn.: acumen, subtilitas, scientia): data est quibusdam bestiis machinatio quaedam atque…

sollĭcĭtātĭo.opening: ( ), , sollicito . Vexation , anxiety : nuptiarum, i. e. on account of, Ter. And. 1, 5, 26 .— An inciting , instigating , instigation (good prose): omnium, Planc. ap. Cic. Fam. 10, 24, 2 : Allobrogum, Cic. Cat. 3, 9, 22…

sollĭcĭtātor.opening: ( ), , id. , a tempter , seducer (post - Aug.): alienarum nuptiarum, Dig. 47, 11, 1 ; 11, 3, 14 fin. ; Sen. Contr. 2, 15 med. : servi, Dig. 11, 3, 11 ; 11, 3, 14 .

sollĭcĭto.opening: ( ), , v. a. sollicitus , to disturb , stir , agitate , move; to distress , harass , make uneasy , vex , solicit , tempt , seduce , attract , induce. Lit. , to stir , put in lively motion , move violently , disturb ,…

sollĭcĭtūdo.opening: ( ), , sollicitus, II. , uneasiness of mind , care , disquiet , anxiety , solicitude (class.; used equally in sing. and plur. ; syn.: aegritudo, dolor, anxietas): sollicitudo aegritudo cum cogitatione, Cic. Tusc. 4, 8,…

sollĭcĭtus.opening: ( ), , adj. sollus-cieo; cf. sollicito , thoroughly moved , agitated , disturbed. Of physical motion ( poet. and rare). As attrib. of motus, restless , unceasing : quae sollicito motu carerent, referring to the elements…

sollĭcūrĭa.opening: , Fest. s. v. sollo, p. 298 Müll.

sollĭferreum.opening: ( ), , (sc. telum) [sollus-, i. e. totus-ferrum], a missile weapon made wholly of iron , an iron javelin , Liv. 34, 14 fin. ; Gell. 10, 25, 2 ; cf. Fest. s. v. sollo, p. 298 Müll.; Paul. ex Fest. p. 299 ib.; and s. v.…

sollistĭmus.opening: ( ), , adj. old sup. form of sollus = salvus; v. Corss. Krit. Beitr. p. 313 sq. , most perfect , only in the expression tripudium sollistimum, in augural lang.; the most favorable omen , when the chickens ate so…

sollus.opening: adj. cf. Sanscr. sarva, entire; Gr. ὅλος; Lat. salvus; v. Corss. Krit. Beitr. p. 313 , whole , entire , unbroken : vasa quoque omnino redimit non solla dupundi, Lucil. ap. Fest. p. 298 (Sat. v. 38 Gerl.): sollum Osce…

sōlo.opening: v. a. solus , to make lonely or desolate; to lay waste , desolate (only a few times in the post-Aug. poets): urbes populis, Stat. Th. 4, 36 : domos, id. ib. 5, 149 ; Sen. Oedip. 4 .

sŏloecismus.opening: ( , Aus. Epigr. 138 ), , , = σολοικισμός . Lit. , a grammatical fault in the construction of a sentence , a solecism (cf. stribligo): vitia in sermone, quo minus is Latinus sit, duo possunt esse: soloecismus et…

sŏloecista.opening: , = σολοικιστής , one that speaks faultily , that commits solecisms , Hier. in Ruf. 3, 6 .

sŏloecŏphănĕs.opening: , = σολοικοφανές , that which appears to be a solecism , Cassiod. Or. 6 .

sŏloecum.opening: , = σόλοικον , = soloecismus, Auct. ap. Gell. 5, 20, 6 ; Gell. 17, 2, 11 .

Sŏlon.opening: or (the latter in Cic. Rep. 2, 1, 2 ), , , = Σόλων . A famous legislator of the Athenians , one of the seven sages of Greece , Cic. Brut. 7, 27 ; 10, 39 ; id. de Or. 1, 44, 197 ; id. Leg. 2, 23, 59 ; 2, 25, 64 ; Liv. 3,…

Sŏlōn.opening: , = Σολώνιον , a city of the Allobroges , in Gallia Narbonensis, north-west of the Rhodanus , perh. near the modern Sortie , Liv. Epit. 103 .

Sŏlonātes.opening: a Gallic tribe in Gallia Cisalpina, south-west of Forum Julii , now probably Torre di Sole , Plin. 3, 15, 20, § 116 ; Inscr. Orell. 5124 .

Solonĭum.opening: a district near Lanuvium , on the Via Ostiensis , Cic. Div. 1, 36, 79 ; 2, 31, 66 ; id. Att. 2, 3, 3 .—Called also Solonius ager, Liv. 8, 12 ; Fest. s. v. pomonal, p. 250, b. Müll.

sōlor.opening: v. dep. a. To comfort , console , solace ( poet. and in post-Aug. prose; while consolor is class.): diffidentem verbis solatur suis, Plaut. Ep. 1, 2, 9 : lenire dolentem Solando cupit, Verg. A. 4, 394 : quos bonus…

Solorius.opening: a mountain in Hispania Tarraconensis, Plin. 3, 1, 2, § 6 .

sŏlox.opening: adj. (cf.: salvus, solidus; v. Corss. Ausspr. 1, 486; ante- and post-class.). Lit. , of raw, unwrought wool, of a coarse staple , coarse , harsh , bristly : solox, lana crassa, et pecus, quod passim pascitur non tectum,…

solsequĭum.opening: a plant , also called heliotropium, App. Herb. 49 .

solstĭtĭālis.opening: adj. solstitium . Lit. , of or belonging to the summer solstice , solstitial (opp. brumalis): (sol) Brumales adeat flexus, atque inde revortens Cancri se ut vortat metas ad solstitiales, Lucr. 5, 617 : dies, the day on…

solstĭtĭum.opening: sol-sisto . In gen., the time when the sun seems to stand still , either in Cancer or in Capricorn, the (summer or winter) solstice (so in gen. not till after the Aug. period): solstitium aestivum ... hibernum, Col. 7,…

sŏlūbĭlis.opening: adj. solvo (post-class.). Pass. , that may be loosed or taken apart , dissolvable : pons, Amm. 16, 8, 10 : mundus, Min. Oct. 34: caro, Prud. στεφ . 10, 506. —* Act. , loosening , relaxing : aër, Cael. Aur. Acut. 2, 37,…

sŏlum.opening: , (collat. form , , , acc. to Varr. L. L. 6, 1, 2 ), root sar-, to guard, make whole; Sanscr. Sarva, entire; cf.: solea, solidus, sollus , the lowest part of a thing, the bottom , ground , base , foundation. Lit. , the…

sōlus.opening: ( gen. regular. solius; dat. soli; gen. m. soli, Cato ap. Prisc. p. 694 P.; dat. m. SOLO, Inscr. Orell. 2627 ; solae, Plaut. Mil. 4, 2, 28 ; Ter. Eun. 5, 6, 3 ), adj. orig. the same with sollus, q. v.; cf. salus. By…

Sŏlūs.opening: , = Σολοῦς , a town on the northern coast of Sicily , now Castello di Solanto , Plin. 3, 8, 14, § 90 .—Hence, , , , the inhabitants of Solus , Cic. Verr. 2, 3, 43, § 103 ; sing. , id. ib. 2, 2, 42 , § 102.

sŏlūtē.opening: adv. , v. solvo, P. a. fin.

sŏlūtĭlis.opening: adj. solvo , that is easily loosed or taken apart : navis, Suet. Ner. 34 .

sŏlūtim.opening: adv. id. , loosely , = solute, Tert. Pall. 5 .

sŏlūtĭo.opening: id. , a loosing , unloosing , dissolution (rare but class.). Lit. In gen.: linguae, Cic. de Or. 1, 25, 114 : totius hominis, id. Tusc. 3, 25, 61 .— Plur. : ventris et stomachi solutiones, looseness, weakness, Plin. 23,…

sŏlūtor.opening: id. (post-class.). A looser , an opener : signaculi, Aug. Mor. Manich. 2, 13 fin. — A payer , Tert. adv. Marc. 4, 17 .

sŏlūtrix.opening: solutor , she that looses or sets free : malorum, Diom. p. 484 P.

sŏlūtus.opening: Part. and P. a. of solvo.

Solva.opening: a city of Noricum , Inscr. Grut. 537, 1 .—Hence, , , adj. , of or belonging to Solva : Flavium Solvense (sc. oppidum), Plin. 3, 24, 27, § 146 .

solvo.opening: v. a. ( perf. soluit, trisyll., Cat. 2, 13 : soluisse, Tib. 4, 5, 16 ) [for se-luo; cf. socors for se-cords], to loosen an object from any thing, to release or to loose , remove any thing which binds or restrains…

Sŏlўma.grammar: ōrum and ae ōrum a, um

Sŏlўmus.opening: or ( ), , , a Trojan , the founder of Sulmo , Ov. F. 4, 79 ; Sil. 9, 72 .

somnĭālis.opening: adj. somnium , dreambringing , an epithet of Hercules, Inscr. Fabr. p. 692, 130 ; Inscr. Rein. cl. 10, 4.— , adv. : , in a dream (late Lat.), Fulg. Myth. 2, 17 dub.

somnĭātor.opening: somnio , one who has faith in dreams; a dreamer , Sen. Contr. 3, 22, 15 .—Of Joseph, Tert. adv. Gnost. 2 med. ; Vulg. Gen. 37, 19 ; id. Zech. 10, 2 .

somnĭcŭlōsus.opening: adj. somnus , full of sleep , i. e. Pass. , inclined to sleep , drowsy , dozy , sleepy , sluggish , slothful (rare but class.; cf. sopitus): quae vitia non sunt senectutis, sed inertis, ignavae, somniculosae senectutis,…

somnĭfer.opening: adj. somnus-fero , sleep-bringing , soporific , somniferous ( poet. and in post-Aug. prose): vis papaveris, Plin. 18, 25, 61, § 229 : virga (Mercurii), Ov. M. 1, 672 : aspis, causing torpidity, deadly, Luc. 9, 701 ; so,…

somnĭfĭcus.opening: adj. somnus-facio , causing sleep , narcotic (Plinian): crater, Mart. Cap. 1, § 82 : medicamentum, Plin. 37, 10, 57, § 158 : vis aspidum, id. 24, 4, 17, § 63 .

somnĭger.opening: adj. somnusgero , sleep-bringing (very rare for somnifer): cornua Lunae, Dracont. 1, 212 .

somnĭo.opening: v. a. ( dep. collat. form: hic aedes non somniatur, Petr. 74, 14 ) [somnium], to dream; to dream of or see in a dream (freq. and class.). Lit. : mirum atque inscitum somniavi somnium, Plaut. Rud. 3, 1, 5 ; so, somnium,…

somnĭōsus.opening: adj. somnus , sleepy , overcome by sleep , Cael. Aur. Acut. 3, 5, 51 .

somnĭum.opening: id. . Lit. , a dream , Cic. Div. 1, 20, 39 ; 2, 58, 119 ; Plin. 10, 75, 98, § 211 ; Macr. Somn. Scip. 1, 3 ; Lact. Opif. Dei, 18: rex Priamus somnio perculsus, Enn. ap. Cic. Div. 1, 21, 42 (Trag. v. 59 Vahl.): dum huic…

somnŭlentĭa.opening: ( ), , , somnulentus , sleepiness , drowsiness , somnolence (late Lat.), Sid. Ep. 2, 2 med.

somnŭlentus.opening: ( ), , adj. somnus , full of sleep , i. e. sleepy , drowsy , dozy , somnolent (post-Aug.), App. M. 1 fin. ; 10 , p. 251, 37.—Hence, adv. : , sleepily , Hier. in Psa. 118 ; Sol. 20, 7 .

somnurnus.opening: adj. id.; in analogy with nocturnus, diurnus , of or belonging to sleep : imagines, seen in sleep , Varr. ap. Non. 172, 3 .

somnus.opening: Sanscr. svap-nas; Gr. ὕπνος; som-nus for sop-nus; cf.: sopor, sopio . Lit. , sleep : hostes vino domiti somnoque sepulti, Enn. ap. Macr. S. 6 (Ann. v. 291 Vahl.); Lucr. 1, 133 : vix aegro cum corde meo me somnus…

sŏnābĭlis.opening: adj. sono , sounding , noisy : sistrum, Ov. M. 9, 784 .

sŏnans.opening: Part. and P. a. of sono.

sŏnax.opening: adj. sono , sounding , noisy ( poet. and in post - Aug. prose): concha, App. M. 4, p. 157, 3 : dentium attritus, id. ib. 8 , p. 202, 30.

sonchus.opening: , = σόγχος , the herb sow-thistle : Sonchus oleraceus, Linn.; Plin. 22, 22, 44, § 88 .

sŏnĭ-pēs.opening: ( ), , adj. sonus , with sounding feet , noisy-footed ( poet. ): turba (in Isidis sacris), Grat. Cyn. 43 .—As subst. , noisy-foot , i. e. a horse , a prancer , steed : fremit aequore toto Insultans sonipes et pressis…

sŏnĭto.opening: v. freq. n. [sono], to make a noise : cicadae, Sol. 2, § 40 dub. (al. so nant).

sŏnĭtus.opening: ( gen. soniti, Pac. and Cae cil. ap. Non. 491, 24 sq. ), id. , a noise , sound , din , etc. (class.; in sing. and plur. ): at tuba terribili sonitu taratantara dixit, Enn. ap. Prisc. p. 842 P. (Ann. v. 452 Vahl.); cf.:…

sŏnĭvĭus.opening: adj. sonus , noisy (cf. solistimum), only in the phrase sonivium tripudium, of the rattling of the corn upon the ground as it fell from the mouths of the sacred chickens, Cic. Fam. 6, 6, 7 ; Plin. 15, 22, 24, § 86 ; cf.…

sŏno.opening: (ante-class. collat. form acc. to the 3d conj., sonit, Enn. and Att. ap. Non. 504, 32 sq. ; sonunt, Enn. and Att. ib. 505, 11 sq. ; Enn. ap. Prisc. p. 863 P.; inf. sonĕre, Att. ap. Non. 505 ; Lucr. 3, 156 ; part. fut.…

sŏnor.opening: sono , a noise , sound , din ( poet. and in post-Aug. prose for sonitus and sonus); sing. , Lucr. 1, 644 ; 4, 567 ; 4, 570 ; Verg. G. 3, 199 ; id. A. 7, 462 ; Tac. A. 1, 65 ; 4, 48 ; App. M. 11, p. 258 fin.— Plur. ,…

sŏnōrĭtas.opening: sonorus , = εὐφωνία , fulness of sound , melodiousness , Prisc. 541 ; 1220 P; Sarisb. 1, 16.

sŏnōrus.opening: (collat. form , , Diom. 497 and 498), adj. sonor , noisy , loud , sounding , resounding , sonorous ( poet. and in post-Aug. prose for the class. sonans): cithara, Tib. 3, 4, 69 : aes, Claud. IV. Cons. Hon. 149 : arcus,…

sons.opening: adj. ( nom. sing. , Fest. p. 297 ; Aus. Idyll. 12 ) [ Part. from root as-, es-; Sanscr. as-mi; Gr. εὶμί ; Lat. esum, sum; cf. Gr. ἐτεός, ἐτήτυμος ; prop. he who was it, the real person, the guilty one]. Guilty ,…

Sontĭātes.opening: a powerful tribe in Aquitania , Caes. B. G. 3, 20 sq.

sontĭcus.opening: adj. sons . Lit. , dangerous , serious , critical , in the connection morbus sonticus, of a serious disorder that excuses one from duty, etc., Fragm. XII. Tab. ap. Fest. p. 290 Müll.; cf. Gell. 20, 1, 27 ; Dig. 21, 1,…

Sontĭus.opening: a river in Carinthia , now the Lisonzo , Cassiod. Ep. 1, 18 ; Jornand. Get. 57 .

sŏnus.opening: (collat. form , , in gen. , Amm. 20, 4, 14 ; abl. sonu, Sisenn. ap. Non. p. 491, 27 ; App. M. 8, p. 216, 7 ; nom. plur. , Amm. 22, 9, 15 ), sono , a noise , sound (syn. fragor): et pereunte viro raucum sonus aere…

sōnus.opening: adj. id. , sounding , resounding , Isid. Orig. 1, 4, 4 .

Sōnus.opening: , = Σῶνος , a river of India , a branch of the Ganges , Plin. 6, 18, 22, § 65 .

Sōpăter.opening: , = Σώπατρος , a Greek proper name , e. g. a victim of Verres : Halicyensis, Cic. Verr. 2, 2, 28, § 68 .—Another, a witness against Verres , Cic. Verr. 2, 4, 39, § 85 .

Sōphēnē.opening: , = Σωφηνή , a district in Armenia , Mel. 1, 11 ; Luc. 2, 592 ; Plin. 5, 12, 13, § 66 .

sŏphĭa.opening: (i long, Prud. Sym. 122 ; id. Cath. 1613 ; Fortun. Suppl. 2, 62 ), , , = σοφία , wisdom (pure Lat. sapientia): sophiam, sapientia quae perhibetur, Enn. ap. Fest. p. 325 Müll. (Ann. v. 227 Vahl.); Afran. ap. Gell. 13, 8,…

sŏphisma.opening: , = σόφισμα , a false conclusion , fallacy , sophism (pure Lat. captio), Sen. Ep. 45, 8 ; Gell. 18, 13, 2 (in Cic. Ac. 2, 24, 75 , written as Greek, and explained by fallaces conclusiunculae; cf. also Sen. Ep. 111, 1 ).

sŏphismătĭus.opening: adj. sophisma , sophistical : dialecticus, Gell. 18, 13 in lemm.

sŏphistes.opening: or , , , = σοφιστής , a sophist : quis hic est? num sophistes? sic enim appellabantur hi, qui ostentationis aut quaestus causā philosophabantur, Cic. Ac. 2, 23, 72 ; cf. id. Fin. 2, 1, 1 ; id. Or. 11, 37 : Protagoras,…

sŏphistĭcē.opening: , = σοφιστική ( τέχνη ), false reasoning , sophistry , App. Dogm. Plat. 2, p. 17, 10 .

sŏphistĭcus.opening: adj. , = σοφιστικός , sophistic , sophistical; res admodum insidiosa et sophistica, neque ad veritates magis quam ad captiones reperta, Tiro Tullius ap. Gell. 7, 3, 35 : captio, Gell. 18, 2, 6 : ostentatio, Arn. 1, 36 :…

Sŏphŏcles.opening: , = Σοφοκλῆς , a celebrated Greek tragic poet , Cic. Fin. 5, 1, 3 ; id. Sen. 7, 22 ; 14, 47 ; id. Div. 1, 25, 54 ; id. Off. 1, 40, 144 ; Hor. Ep. 2, 1, 163 ; Quint. 10, 1, 67 sq. ; Sen. Q. N. 4, 2, 17 ; Vell. 1, 16, 3 ;…

Sŏphō^clĭdisca.opening: the name of a woman , Plaut. Pers. 2, 2, 23 .

Sŏphŏnība.opening: wife of Syphax and daughter of Hasdrubal , Liv. 30, 12, 11 ; 30, 15, 4 .

sŏphos.opening: or , , , = σοφός , a wise man , sage : te sophos omnis amat, Mart. 7, 32, 4 .—Adjectively, wise , shrewd : victor sophus, Phaedr. 3, 14, 9 : factus periclo tum gubernator sophus, id. 4, 15, 8 .

sŏphōs.opening: adv. , = σοφῶς , an exclamation of applause, well done! well said! bravo! (not ante-Aug.; Cic. has, instead of it, bene!): at tibi tergeminum mugiet ille sophos, Mart. 3, 46, 8 ; 1, 50, 37 ; 1, 67, 4 ; 1, 77, 10; Petr.…

Sōphron.opening: , = Σώφρων , a Greek composer of mimes , Varr. L. L. 5, § 179 Müll.; Quint. 1, 10, 17 .

Sōphrŏna.opening: the name of a woman , nurse of Pamphila , Ter. Eun. 4, 7, 37 .

Sōphroniscus.opening: , = Σωφρονίσκος , a statuary , the father of Socrates , Val. Max. 3, 4 , ext. 1; Sen. Ben. 3, 32, 2 .

Sŏphus.opening: 1. sophos , a surname of the consul P. Sempronius , Liv. 9, 45, 1 ; 10, 9, 2 .

sōpio.grammar: īvi or ĭi, ītum, 4 v. a.
sōpio.opening: v. a. sopor , to deprive of feeling or sense; esp. by sleep, to put or lull to sleep. Lit. (class.; most freq. in part. perf.; in Cic. only so; cf. sedo): impactus ita est saxo, ut sopiretur, became unconscious or…

Sopolis.opening: a celebrated painter in the time of Cicero , Cic. Att. 4, 16 ; acc. Sopolin, Plin. 35, 11, 40, § 148 .

sŏpor.opening: Sanscr. root svap-, sleep; cf. somnus; Gr. ὕπνος , a deep sleep. Lit. , in gen., sleep (mostly poet. and in post-Aug. prose; not in Cic.; cf. somnus): lucrum praeposivi sopori et quieti, Plaut. Rud. 4, 2, 11 : cum eum…

sŏpōrĭfer.opening: adj. sopor-fero , sleep-bringing , inducing sleep , sleepy , drowsy ( poet. and in post-Aug. prose): papaver, Verg. A. 4, 486 : lac, Plin. 19, 8, 38, § 126 : potio, Spart. Hadr. 26 fin. : vis pinnae, Plin. 9, 13, 15, §…

sŏpōro.opening: , no perf. , , v. a. sopor , to put or lay asleep , cast into sleep; to deprive of sense or feeling , to stupefy (not ante-Aug.; usu. in part. perf. ). Lit. : si saepius expergiscitur aliquis quam assuevit, deinde…

sŏpōrus.opening: adj. id. ( poet. ), of or belonging to sleep , i. e., Sleep-bringing , causing sleep : Nox, Verg. A. 6, 390 ; Luc. 2, 236 ; Stat. Th. 1, 403 : soporae pennae (Somni), Sil. 10, 354 : amnis, i. e. Lethe, id. 13, 856 .—…

Sōra.opening: the northernmost city of the Volsci in Latium , near Arpinum , on the Liris , still called Sora , Plin. 3, 5, 9, § 63 ; Liv. 7, 28 ; 9, 23 sq.; 10, 1; Vell. 1, 14, 5 ; Sil. 8, 396 ; Juv. 3, 223 .—Hence, , , adj. , of or…

Sōracte.opening: ( ), , Sanscr. svar, heaven; cf.: serenus, 2. Soranus , a high mountain in Etruria , on which was a temple of Apollo , now Monte S. Oreste , Varr. R. R. 2, 3, 3 ; Plin. 2, 93, 95, § 207 ; Hor. C. 1, 9, 2 ; Verg. A. 7,…

Soractĭa.opening: a city of Syria , founded by Semiramis , Plin. 6, 28, 32, § 145 .

spectābĭlĭtas.opening: spectabilis, II. B. , the office or dignity of a Spectabilis (late Lat.), Cod. Just. 9, 27, 5 ; 12, 26, 1 al.

spectācŭlum.opening: (contr. , Prop. 4 (5), 8, 21 .and 56), , specto , a show , sight , spectacle (class.). In gen.: lepidum spectaculum, Plaut. Poen. 1, 1, 81 : superarum rerum atque caelestium, Cic. N. D. 2, 56, 140 : bis terque mutatae…

spectāmen.opening: specto . * = specimen, a mark , sign , proof : spectamen bono servo id est, Ut absente ero rem sui eri diligenter Tutetur, Plaut. Men. 5, 6, 1 .— = spectaculum, a sight , scene , spectacle (Appuleian): miserum…

spectātĭo.opening: specto , a looking , beholding , contemplation of a thing, a sight , view (rare but class.). Lit. In gen., absol. : homo ad artificem suum (deum) spectat: quam spectationem Trismegistus θεωρίαν rectissime nominavit,…

spectātīvus.opening: adj. id. , contemplative , speculative : thesin a causā sic distinguunt, ut illa sit spectativae partis, haec activae, Quint. 3, 5, 11 : opp. actualis, Isid. 2, 24, 9 .

spectātor.opening: id. , a looker-on , beholder , observer , spectator (class.). In gen.: sunt homines quasi spectatores superarum rerum atque caelestium, Cic. N. D. 2, 56, 140 : unicus caeli siderumque (Ar chimedes), Liv. 24, 34, 2 :…

spectātrix.opening: spectator . She that looks at or observes a thing, Plaut. Merc. 3, 4, 12 ; 5, 2, 1 ; Sen. Cons. ad Marc. 18 med. ; Ov. Am. 2, 12, 26 : scelerum, Luc. 3, 129 .— She that judges or tries : incorrupta praeteritorum…

spectātus.opening: Part. and P. a. of specto.

spectĭo.opening: specio , in the lang. of augurs, an observing of the auspices; hence, also, the right of observing them (which belonged to the magistrates), Varr. L. L. 6, § 82 Müll.; Cic. Phil. 2, 32, 81 ; Fest. s. h. v. p. 333.

specto.opening: v. freq. a. id. , to look at , behold; to gaze at , watch , observe , etc. (freq. and class.; syn.: adspicio, speculor, conspicor, contueor). Lit. In gen. With acc. : speculum a speciendo, quod ibi se spectant, Varr. L.…

spectrum.opening: specio , an appearance , form , image of a thing; an apparition , spectre , the Gr. εἴδωλον (much less freq. than simulacrum and species): spectra Catiana ... nam quae Democritus εἴδωλα , Catius Insuber Epicureus…

spectus.opening: id. , look , appearance , aspect : spectu sine praepositione Pacuvius in Duloreste usus est, cum ait: spectu protervo ferox, Fest. s. h. v. p. 330 Müll.; Pac. Fragm. Trag. v. 147 Rib.

spĕcŭla.opening: id. . A high place from which to look out, a look-out , watch-tower : specula, de quo prospicimus, Varr. L. L. 6, § 82 Müll.: praedonum adventum significabat ignis e speculā sublatus, Cic. Verr. 2, 5, 35, § 93 : dat…

spēcŭla.opening: dim. spes; cf. recula, from res , a slight hope (rare but class.): estne quid in te speculae? Plaut. Pers. 2, 5, 9 ; id. Cas. 2, 4, 27 : ulla nec specula est, id. Rud. 3, 3, 3 ; Cic. Clu. 26, 72 : oblectabar speculā,…

spĕcŭlābĭlis.opening: adj. speculor , that may be seen , visible : Sunion, Stat. Th. 12, 624 .

spĕcŭlābundus.opening: adj. id. , on the look-out , on the watch; watching for any thing (post-Aug.): Festus Hadrumeto, ubi speculabundus substiterat, etc., Tac. H. 4, 50 : ab ostio speculabunda, Mart. Cap. 2, § 112 .—With acc. :…

spĕcŭlāmen.opening: id. , a looking at , observing : glaucum, Prud. Apoth. 88 .

spĕcŭlāris.opening: adj. speculum . In gen., of or belonging to a mirror , like a mirror (post-Aug.): speculari ratione, in the manner of a mirror, Sen. Q. N. 1, 5, 9 . — In partic.: specularis lapis, a kind of transparent stone,…

spĕcŭlārĭus.opening: (contr. collat. form SPECLARIVS, Inscr. Orell. 4284 ), , id. , a mirror-maker , Dig. 50, 6, 6 ; Cod. Th. 13, 4, 2; Cod. Just. 10, 64, 1 ; Inscr. Orell. 6296 .— Called also † SPECVLARIARIVS (or contr. SPECLARIA), Inscr.…

spĕcŭlātĭo.opening: speculor . A spying out , exploration , observation (late Lat.): speculationibus fidis doctus, Amm. 26, 10, 4 ; 27, 2, 4 : turris speculationis, Greg. Mag. in Job, 31, 85.— A contemplation , speculation , Boëth. Consol.…

spĕcŭlātīvus.opening: adj. id. , speculative (late Lat.): philosophia, Boëth. ap. Porphyr. Dial. 1, p. 2.—Hence, subst. : , , , = contemplativa (sc. philosophia), Cassiod. Var. 1, 45 .

spĕcŭlātor.opening: (also written ), , id. , in milit. lang., a looker-out , spy , scout , explorer , éclaireur (syn. explorator). Lit. : speculator, quem mittimus ante, ut respiciat quae volumus, Varr. L. L. 6, § 82 Müll.: repentinus,…

spĕcŭlātōrĭus.opening: adj. speculator , of or belonging to spies or scouts : navigia, spy-boats, vessels of observation, Caes. B. G. 4, 26 ; also called speculatoriae naves, Liv. 30, 10, 14 ; 35, 26, 9 ; 36, 42, 8 ; and caliga, worn by spies…

spĕcŭlātrīx.opening: speculor , she that spies or watches , a (female) spy , watcher. Lit. : furiae deae sunt speculatrices, credo, et vindices facinorum et scelerum, * Cic. N. D. 3, 18, 46 ; Sen. Contr. 1, 6 med. : mens boni speculatrix…

spĕcŭlātus.opening: adj. speculum , furnished or adorned with mirrors : cubiculum, Gloss. ap. Suet. Vit. Hor.

spĕcŭlor.opening: v. dep. a. [1. specula], to spy out , watch , observe , examine , explore (class.; cf.: specto, conspicio): quo mox furatum veniat, speculatur loca, Plaut. Trin. 4, 2, 22 : St. Quid hic speculare? Pa. Nihil equidem…

spĕcŭlum.opening: specio; hence, that in which one sees himself . Lit. , a looking-glass , mirror (usually made of polished metal): speculum a speciendo, quod ibi se spectant, Varr. L. L. 5, § 129 Müll.; cf.: speculum, quod in eo…

spĕcus.opening: ( abl. plur. specibus, Sen. Cons. ap. Front. Aquaed. 125 ; on the various forms found only in the grammarians, v. Neue, Formenl. 1, 569 sq.), ( and v. infra ) [perh. root spec-; v. specio, and so orig. a hole, aperture;…

spēlaeum.opening: ( ), , , = σπήλαιον , a cave , cavern , den ( poet. and in postclass. prose; syn. antrum): in silvis, inter spelaea ferarum, * Verg. E. 10, 52 ; so, spelaea metuenda ferarum, Claud. B. Get. 354 : emptum millibus (ab…

spelta.opening: spelt : totidem speltas, i. e. grains of spelt , Rhemn. Fann. Pond. 10; Hier. in Ezech. 1, 4, 9 .

spēlunca.opening: , = σπήλυγξ , gen. γγος . A cave , cavern , den (class.; syn. specus): Philocteta jam decimum annum in speluncā jacet, Cic. Fin. 2, 29, 94 ; Cic. Verr. 2, 4, 48, § 107 ; id. Fat. 3, 6 ; id. Fl. 17, 39 ; Verg. G. 2, 469…

spēluncōsus.opening: adj. spelunca , full of caves or caverns : loca, Cael. Aur. Acut. 2, 37, 191 .

spērābĭlis.opening: adj. spero , that may be hoped for : cum nulla vitae meae salus sperabilis't, Plaut. Capt. 3, 3, 3 .

spērātus.opening: Part. and P. a. of spero.

Sperchēos.opening: ( ) or ( , v. Neue, Formenl. 1, 127 sq.), , , = Σπερχεῖος , a river of Thessaly , rising on Mount Pindus , now the Ellada; form -eos, Verg. G. 2, 487 ; Rib., Forb. (al. Sperchius); form -eus, Liv. 36, 14, 15 Weissenb.;…

sperma.opening: , = σπέρμα , seed , semen , sperm , Sulp. Sev. Hist. Sacr. 1, 11 .

spermătĭcus.opening: adj. , = σπερματικός , of or relating to seed , seminal , spermatic : pori, Cael. Aur. Acut. 3, 18, 180 .

spernax.opening: adj. sperno , despising , showing contempt , contemptuous (post-Aug. and very rare): viri spernaces mortis, Sil. 8, 465 : in admittendo consilio spernax, Sid. Ep. 4, 9 .

sperno.opening: ( perf. sync. sprērunt, Prud. Dittoch. 31 ), v. a. root spar-, to part; Sanscr. spar-itar, enemy; cf. Lat. parcus; Germ. sperren , to sever , separate , remove (syn.: segrego, separo; perh. only in the foll. passages):…

spernor.opening: v. dep. a. [sperno; cf. aspernor], to despise : pietatem, Front. Eloq. p. 227 Mail.

spēro.opening: v. a. To hope (something desirable), to look for , trust , expect; to promise or flatter one's self (the predom. signif. of the word; syn.: confido, exspecto). Absol. : spero, si speres quicquam prodesse potes sunt,…

spes.opening: ( gen. spe, Liv. 1, 40, 7 dub.; Weissenb. spei; plur. nom. and acc. speres, Enn. ap. Fest. p. 333 Müll., or Ann. v. 410 and 132 Vahl.; gen. sperum, Eum. Paneg. Const. 15 ; abl. speribus, Varr. ap. Non. 171, 27 and 30:…

spētĭle.grammar: vocatur infra umbilicum suis, quod est carnis, proprii cujusdam habitus, exos
spētĭle.opening: (or ) , quā etiam antiqui per se utebantur. Plautus enumerandis suillis obsoniis in Carbonaria sic: ego pernam, sumen sueris, spectile, etc., Fest. p. 330 Müll.

Speusippus.opening: , = Σπεύσιππος , a nephew of Plato , and his successor in the Academy , Cic. Ac. 1, 4, 17 ; id. N. D. 1, 13, 32 ; id. de Or. 3, 18, 67 al.

speustĭcus.opening: adj. , = σπευστικός . hastily made : panes, a kind of bread, Plin. 18, 11, 27, § 105 .

sphăcos.opening: , = σφάκος . = sphagnos, a kind of fragrant moss , Plin. 24, 6, 17, § 27 .— = elelisphacos, a kind of sage , Plin. 22, 25, 71, § 146 .

sphaera.opening: (post-class. ; once , Prud. Apoth. 278 ), , , = σφαῖρα , a ball , globe , sphere (pure Lat. globus, Cic. N. D. 2, 18, 47 ). In gen.: sphaeras pugnum altas facito, Cato, R. R. 82 ; Cic. Fat. 8, 15 : habent suam sphaeram…

sphaerālis.opening: adj. sphaera , of or belonging to a ball , globular , spherical (postclass.): forma, Macr. S. 7, 16 : motus, id. ib. 7, 9 : extremitas, id. Somn. Scip. 1, 22, 7 .

sphaerĭcus.opening: adj. , = σφαιρικός , of or belonging to a ball , spherical : motus, Macr. Somn. Scip. 2, 14, 31 : numeri, Boëth. Inst. Arith. 2, 4 .—Hence, subst. : , , , spherics , the science of heavenly motions , Boëth. Inst. Arith.…

sphaerĭon.opening: , = σφαιρίον , a little ball , a pill in medicine, Cels. 6, 6, 21 .

sphaerista.opening: , = σφαιριστής , a ball-player , Sid. Ep. 2, 9 med. ; 5, 17 .

sphaeristērĭum.opening: , = σφαιριστήριον . Lit. , a place for playing ball , a ball-court , tennis-court , Plin. Ep. 2, 17, 12 ; 5, 6, 27 ; Suet. Vesp. 20 ; Inscr. Orell. 57 .— Transf. , a game at ball , Lampr. Alex. Sev. 30 ; Sid. Ep. 2, 2…

sphaerŏīdes.opening: adj. , = σφαιροειδής , round , globular , spherical : schema, Vitr. 8, 6 med.

sphaerŏmăchĭa.opening: , = σφαιρομαχία , a kind of boxing in which the combatants had iron balls strapped to their hands , Sen. Ep. 80, 1 ; Stat. S. 4 , praef. fin.

sphaerŭla.opening: dim. sphaera , a small ball or sphere , Vulg. Exod. 37, 17 ; Aug. Gen. Lit. 2, 15 .

Sphaerus.opening: , = Σφαῖρος . A Stoic , a pupil of Zeno , Cic. Tusc. 4, 24, 53 .— A freedman of Augustus , Suet. Aug. 89 .

Sphăgĭae.opening: three rocky islands near Pylos , Plin. 4, 12, 19, § 55 .

sphagnos.opening: , = σφάγνος , a kind of fragrant moss , Plin. 12, 23, 50, § 108 ; 24, 6, 17, § 27 .

sphincter.opening: , = σφιγκτήρ , the sphincter , the muscle of the anus , Cael. Aur. Tard. 2, 1 .

Sphinga.opening: ( ), , , = Sphinx (late Lat.), Aug. Civ. Dei , 18, 13.— Plur. , Hyg. Fab. 67 ; Sid. Ep. 5, 7 ; Isid. 12, 2, 32 .

sphingātus.opening: adj. Sphinga , in the form of a sphinx , Isid. Orig. 20, 11 .

sphingĭon.opening: , = σφιγγίον , a kind of ape , perh. the dog-headed ape : Simia cynocephalus, Linn.; Plin. 6, 29, 34, § 173 ; 10, 72, 93, § 199 .

sphinthrĭa.opening: or , , from σφιγκτήρ, the contractile muscle of the anus , a male prostitute , Tac. A. 6, 1 ; Suet. Tib. 43 ; id. Calig. 16 ; id. Vit. 3 fin. ; cf. Aus. Epigr. 119 .

Sphinx.opening: (Gr. gen. Sphingos, Stat. Th. 1, 66 ), , = Σφίγξ . A fabulous monster near Thebes that used to propose riddles to travellers , and tear in pieces those who could not solve them; usually represented with the head of a…

sphrāgis.opening: , = σφραγίς (a seal). A kind of stone used for seals , Plin. 37, 8, 37, § 117 .— Another name for Lemnian earth , so called because sold in sealed packets, Plin. 35, 6, 14, § 33 .— A little ball of plaster in medicine,…

sphrāgītis.opening: , = σφραγῖτες , the impression of a seal , Prud. στεφ . 10, 1076.

sphȳraena.opening: , = σφύραινα , a kind of sea-fish , otherwise called sudis, Plin. 32, 11, 54, § 154 .

spīca.opening: (vulg. : rustici, ut acceperunt antiquitus, vocant specam, Varr. R. R. 1, 48, 2 .— Neutr. collat. form , Varr. ap. Non. 225, 30 ; Cic. Sen. 15, 51 , acc. to Non. 225, 29 ; Cic. poët. N. D. 2, 42, 110.— Masc. collat.…

spīcĕus.opening: adj. spica , consisting of ears of corn ( poet. and in post-Aug. prose): corona, Tib. 1, 1, 16 (24); Hor. C. S. 30 ; Plin. 18, 2, 2, § 6 ; Sabin. Massur. ap. Gell. 6, 7, 8 ; cf. serta, Tib. 1, 10, 22 ; Ov. M. 2, 28 ;…

spīcĭfer.opening: adj. spica-fero , ear-bearing , a poet. epithet of Ceres, Manil. 2, 442 ; Sen. Herc. Oet. 598 .—Of the Nile, Mart. 10, 74, 9 ; Sil. 3, 403 .

spīcĭlĕgĭum.opening: spica-lego , a gleaning , leasing of ears of corn after gathering (very rare): messi facta spicilegium venire oportet, Varr. R. R. 1, 53 ; id. L. L. 7, § 109 Müll.

spīco.opening: , no perf. , , v. a. spica , to furnish with spikes or ears (post-Aug., and usually in the part. perf. ): grana in stipulā crinito textu spicantur, shoot out or put forth ears , Plin. 18, 7, 10, § 60 : chamaecissos…

spīcŭla.opening: dim. id. , a plant , called also chamaepitys, ground-pine , App. Herb. 26 .

spīcŭlo.opening: v. a. spiculum , to sharpen to a point , to point (post-Aug. and very rare): telum, Plin. 11, 2, 1, § 3 : mantichorae cauda spiculata, Sol. 52, § 37 .

spīcŭlum.opening: (contr. , perh. Mart. Cap. 9, § 903 , or p. 306 Grot., where, however, Kopp and others read spicum; v. spica, II. D.), , dim. spicum , a little sharp point or sting (syn.: mucro, acus, aculeus). Lit. In gen., of bees,…

spīcŭlus.opening: adj. spiculum , pointed : non lucernae spiculo lumine opus est, Tert. Pudic. 7 fin.

spīna.opening: root spī, whence also spicna, spīca, spinus , a thorn. Lit. : cum lubrica serpens Exuit in spinis vestem, Lucr. 4, 61 ; cf. Prop. 4 (5), 5, 1 ; Verg. E. 5, 39 ; Col. 3, 11, 5 ; Plin. 21, 15, 54, § 91 al. : consertum…

spīnālis.opening: adj. spina, I. B. 3. , of or belonging to the spine , spinal (late Lat.): medulla, Macr. S. 7, 9 , §§ 22, 24.

spīnĕa.opening: (another name for spionia), a kind of vine , Plin. 14, 2, 4, § 34 .

spīnĕŏla.opening: dim. spina , a kind of small-leaved rose , Plin. 21, 4, 10, § 16 .

spīnesco.opening: v. n. inch. [id.], to grow thorny , Mart. Cap. 6, § 704 .

spīnētum.opening: id. , a thorn hedge , a thicket of thorns. Lit. , Verg. E. 2, 9 ; Plin. 10, 74, 95, § 204 : spineta sentesque, Sen. Ira, 2, 10, 4 .— Trop. : Aristotelis spineta, Hier. in Helv. 2 .

spīnĕus.opening: adj. id. , of or made of thorns , thorny (very rare): vincula, Ov. M. 2, 789 : frutices, Sol. 7 fin.

Spīnĭensis.opening: id. , a deity that guarded the fields against thorns , Aug. Civ. Dei , 4, 21 fin.

spīnĭfer.opening: adj. spina-fero , thorn-bearing , thorny , prickly : pruni, Pall. Insit. 81 : rubus, Prud. Cath. 5, 31 : cauda Pistricis, Cic. Arat. 178 (al. spinigera).

spīnĭger.opening: adj. spina-gero , thorn-bearing , thorny : stirpes, Prud. στεφ . 11, 119.

Spīno.opening: a small stream near Rome , to which divine honors were paid , Cic. N. D. 3, 20, 52 .

spīnōsĭtas.opening: thorniness (late Lat.), Jul. ap. Aug. c. Sec. Resp. Jul. 6, 29.

spīnōsŭlus.opening: adj. dim. [spinosus], somewhat thorny; hence, trop., in disputation, obscure , confused (late Lat.), Hier. Ep. 69, 2 .

spīnōsus.opening: adj. spina , full of thorns or prickles , thorny , prickly. Lit. : caprae in spinosis locis pascuntur, Varr. R. R. 2, 3, 8 : herbae, Ov. M. 2, 810 : frutecta, Plin. 30, 11, 30, § 101 : caulis, id. 19, 3, 17, § 47 :…

spinter.opening: ( ), , prob. from σφιγκτήρ , a kind of bracelet which kept its place on the arm by its own elasticity: spinter, genus armillae quod mulieres antiquae gerere solebant bracchio summo sinistro, Fest. p. 333 Müll.: jubeas…

Spinthărus.opening: A slave and amanuensis of Cicero , Cic. Att. 13, 25, 3 fin. — An athlete , Plin. 34, 8, 19, § 68 .

Spinther.opening: a Roman surname , e. g. P. Cornelius Spinther, Val. Max. 9, 14, 4 ; Plin. 7, 12, 10, § 54 ; Quint. 6, 3, 57 .

spinturnīcĭum.opening: dim. spinturnix , a little bird of ill-omen , Plaut. Mil. 4, 1, 42 .

spinturnix.opening: σπινθαρίς , an unsightly bird , otherwise unknown, Poët. ap. Fest. p. 330 sq. Müll.; Plin. 10, 13, 17, § 36 .

spīnŭla.opening: dim. spina (post-class.). A little thorn , Arn. 2, 49 .—* (Acc. to spina, I. B. 3.) A little backbone or spine , App. M. 10, p. 255, 2 .

spīnus.opening: ( abl. spinu, Varr. ap. Charis. p. 117 P.), id. , a blackthorn , sloe-tree : Prunus spinosa, Linn.; Verg. G. 4, 145 ; Pall. Febr. 25, 6 ; id. Insit. 63 .

Spīo.opening: , = Σπειώ , a sea - nymph , daughter of Nereus and Doris , Verg. G. 4, 338 ; id. A. 5, 826 .

spĭŏnĭa.opening: a kind of grape-vine , Col. 3, 2, 27 ; 3, 7, 1 ; 3, 21, 3 : vitis, Plin. 14, 2, 4, § 34 .

spĭŏnĭcus.opening: adj. spionia , of or belonging to the spionia: gustus, Col. 3, 21, 10 .

spīra.opening: , = σπεῖρα . That which is wound , wreathed , coiled , or twisted; a coil , fold , twist , spire (cf. orbis); of a serpent, Verg. G. 2, 154 ; id. A. 2, 217 ; Ov. M. 3, 77 .—Of the grain of wood, Plin. 16, 39, 76, § 198…

spīrābĭlis.opening: adj. spiro , that may be breathed , good to breathe , breathable , respirable. Lit. : terra circumfusa undique est hac animali spirabilique naturā, cui nomen est aër, Cic. N. D. 2, 36, 91 ; cf. id. ib. 2, 6, 18 ; id.…

spīrācŭlum.opening: id. , a breathinghole , air - hole , vent , spiracle ( poet. and in post-Aug. prose), Lucr. 6, 493 ; Verg. A. 7, 568 ; Plin. 2, 93, 95, § 208 ; Val. Fl. 3, 553 ; Pall. Jun. 7, 8 ; id. Oct. 14, 16 .—Also breath : vitae,…

spīraea.opening: , = σπειραία , the herb meadowsweet : Spiraea, Linn.; Plin. 21, 9, 29, § 53 .

Spīraeum.opening: a promontory of Argolis , on the Saronic Gulf , Plin. 4, 5, 9, § 18 ; 4, 12, 19, § 57 .

spīrāmen.opening: spiro . A breathing - hole , passage for the breath , air-hole , thrill , vent ( poet. and very rare): spiramina Naris, Enn. ap. Prisc. p. 691 P. (Ann. v. 265 Vahl.); Luc. 2, 183 : sunt qui spiramina terris Esse putant,…

spīrāmentum.opening: id. ( poet. and in post-Aug. prose). A breathing-hole , airhole , vent , pore , spiracle. Lit. : caeca relaxat Spiramenta, Verg. G. 1, 90 : (apes) in tectis certatim tenuia cera Spiramenta linunt, id. ib. 4, 39 :…

spīrātĭo.opening: spiro . Lit. , a breathing (post - class.), Scrib. Comp. 47 ; 180 .— Transf. , the breath : odor spirationis, Scrib. Comp. 185 ; 197 .

Spīrĭdĭon.opening: , = Σπειριδίων , a surname of the rhetorician Glycon , Quint. § 1, 41 Spald.; Sen. Contr. 35 fin.

spīrĭtālis.opening: or (the MSS. vary between the two forms), , adj. spiritus . Of or belonging to breathing , to wind , or to air (post-Aug.): machinarum genus spiritale, quod apud eos (Graecos) πνευματικόν appellatur, a kind of…

spīrĭtālĭtas.opening: ( ), , spiritalis, II. , spirituality (eccl. Lat.), Tert. adv. Marc. 5, 8 med. ; Alcim. Ep. 12 .

spīrĭtus.opening: (scanned spĭrĭtus, Sedul. Hymn. 1 fin.; dat. SPIRITO, Inscr. Orell. 3030 ; gen. , dat. , and abl. plur. only eccl. and late Lat., e. g. spirituum, Vulg. Marc. 6, 7 : spiritibus, Aug. Serm. 216, 11 fin. ; Vulg. Luc. 8, 2…

spīro.grammar: āvi, ātum, 1 v. n. and a.
spīro.opening: v. n. and a. [etym. dub.]. Neutr. , to breathe , blow , etc. (cf. flo). Lit. In gen. (only poet. and in postAug. prose): freta circum Fervescunt graviter spirantibus incita flabris, Lucr. 6, 428 ; Ov. M. 7, 532 :…

spīrŭla.opening: dim. spira, II. B. , a small twisted cake or cracknel (post-class.), Arn. 2, 73 ; Serv. Verg. A. 2, 217 .

spissāmentum.opening: spisso , that which is used to compress or stop up any thing, a stopple , plug (post-Aug.): firmiori (quam cera) spissamento opus est, Sen. Ep. 31, 1 : spissamento facto de harundinum foliis, Col. 12, 49, 4 : faeniculi,…

spissātĭo.opening: id. , condensation , packing : terram calcavit et pressit: negat quicquam esse hac spissatione efficacius, Sen. Ep. 86, 18 .

spissesco.opening: v. inch. n. [spissus], to become thick , to thicken , condense (very rare), * Lucr. 6, 176 ; Cels. 5, 27, 4 .

spissĭgrădus.opening: adj. spissegradior , slow-paced : hos duco homines spissigradissimos, Plaut. Poen. 3, 1, 3 .

spissĭtas.opening: spissus , compactness , density (post-Aug. and very rare): quercus (opp. raritas), Vitr. 2, 9 med. : tritici, Plin. 18, 30, 73, § 304 .

spissĭtūdo.opening: id. , thickness , density , consistency (post-Aug. and very rare): aëris crassi, Sen. Q. N. 2, 30, 4 : mellis, Scrib. Comp. 4 ; 5 : emplastri, id. ib. 81 : non nimis liquida, id. ib. 37 : spissitudinem ejus absolvere,…

spisso.opening: v. a. id. . Lit. , to thicken , make thick , condense ( poet. and in post-Aug. prose; esp. freq. in Pliny the elder; cf. denso): omne lac igne spissatur, Plin. 11, 41, 96, § 238 ; so, spissatum lac, id. 20, 7, 24, § 58…

spissus.opening: adj. root spi-, to press; cf. Lith. spitu . Lit. , thick , crowded , close , compact , dense (mostly poet and in post-Aug. prose; syn.: crassus, densas): durata ac spissa, Lucr. 2, 444 : corpus, id. 6, 127 : liquor, Ov.…

splanchnoptes.opening: , = σπλαγχνόπτης , the roaster of entrails; a bronze statue by Styppax , Plin. 22, 17, 20, § 44 ; 34, 8, 19, § 81 .

splēn.opening: , = σπλήν , the milt or spleen , Plin. 23, 1, 16, § 25 ; 24, 15, 80, § 131 ; 24, 19, 120, § 185 ; Col. 7, 10, 8 ; Vitr. 1, 4 med. al.: sum petulanti splene cachinno, Pers. 1, 12 .

splendĕo.opening: ( perf. splendui, Aug. Conf. 10, 27 ), v. n. , to shine , be bright; to gleam , glitter , glisten (mostly poet. ; in Cic. only once in the trop. sense; syn.: luceo, fulgeo, niteo). Lit. : sparsis hastis longis campus…

splendesco.opening: ( perf. dŭi, Aug. Conf. 10, 27 ), 3, v. inch. n. [splendeo], to become bright or shining , to derive lustre from a thing (rare; in Cic. only in a trop. sense). Lit. : incipiat sulco attritus splendescere vomer, Verg. G.…

splendĭco.opening: v. n. id. , to shine , glitter , sparkle (Appuleian): gemmae, App. M. 5, p. 162, 37 : depiles genae levi pueritiā, id. ib. 7 , p. 191, 12.

splendĭdo.opening: v. a. splendidus , to make shining or bright , to brighten , polish (post-class.): dentes, App. Mag. fin.

splendĭdus.opening: adj. splendeo , bright , shining , glittering , brilliant , etc. (class.; syn.: nitidus, lucidus, coruscus). Lit. In gen.: o magna templa caelitum, commixta stellis splendidis, Enn. ap. Varr. L. L. 7, § 6 Müll. (Trag.…

splendĭfĭcē.opening: adv. splendeo-facio , brightly , splendidly : intermicans, Fulg. Myth. 1 , praef. med.

splendĭfĭco.opening: v. a. id. , to make bright , to brighten , illumine : diem, Mart. Cap. 9, § 912 .

splendĭtĕnens.opening: adj. , resplendent (late Lat.), Aug. c. Faust. 15, 6.

splendor.opening: splendeo , sheen , brightness , brilliance , lustre , splendor. Lit. In gen. (mostly poet. and in post-Aug. prose; syn.: fulgor, nitor): splendor acer adurit saepe oculos, Lucr. 4, 304 : splendor clipeo clarior, Plaut.…

splendōrĭfer.opening: adj. splendor-fero , bringing brightness or splendor (late Lat.): lumen, Tert. Judic. Dom. 131 .

splēnētĭcus.opening: adj. splen , affected with spleen , splenetic , App. Herb. 34 ; Pall. 8, 6, 2 (al. splenici).

splēnĭātus.opening: adj. splenium , plastered , having a plaster or patch on : mentum, Mart. 10, 22, 1 .

splēnĭcus.opening: adj. , = σπληνικός , splenetic; subst. , a person affected with spleen , a splenetic , Plin. 20, 9, 34, § 87 ; 24, 10, 47, § 79 ; 31, 11, 47, § 128 ; Pall. Jul. 6, 2 .

splēnītes.opening: , = σπληνίτης , a splenetic person , Cael. Aur. Tard. 3, 8 .

splēnĭum.opening: , = σπλήνιον . Milt-waste , spleenwort , Plin. 25, 5, 20, § 45 . — (Because of its likeness to the spleen in form and color.) A plaster , patch , Plin. 29, 6, 38, § 126 ; 30, 11, 30, § 104 (Jahn, spleniolum); Mart. 2,…

spŏdĭum.opening: , = σπόδιον . Lit. , the dross of metals , slag , scoria , Plin. 34, 18, 50, § 170 ; 34, 18, 52, § 172 .— Transf. , ashes of vegetable matter, Plin. 23, 4, 38, § 76 .

spŏdos.opening: , = σποδός , dross , slag , scoria , Plin. 34, 13, 33, § 128 sqq.

Spōlētĭum.opening: (afterwards called also ; cf. Prisc. p. 592 P.; but whether so as early as the class. period is doubtful, owing to the uncertainty of the readings in the MSS. of Livy, Suetonius, and Florus; cf. Duk. ad Flor. 3, 21, 27…

spŏlĭābĭlis.opening: adj. spolio , that can be stripped off (late Lat.), Mar. Mercat. Nestor Serm. 12, 2.

spŏlĭārĭum.opening: spolium (postAug.). Lit. , a place in the amphitheatre where the clothes were stripped from the slain gladiators who were dragged thither , Sen. Ep. 93, 10 ; Lampr. Commod. 18, 3 ; 19, 3 .— Transf. , a den of robbers or…

spŏlĭātĭo.opening: spolio , a pillaging , robbing , plundering , spoliation (class.). Lit. : in tantā spoliatione omnium rerum, Cic. Sest. 21, 47 : sacrorum, Liv. 29, 8, 9 .— Plur. : spoliationes fanorum atque oppidorum, Cic. Verr. 2, 4,…

spŏlĭātor.opening: id. , a robber , pillager , plunderer , spoiler (rare but class.): eorum (monumentorum), * Cic. Verr. 2, 4, 36, § 80 : templi, Liv. 29, 18, 15 : pupilli, Juv. 1, 46 .

spŏlĭātrix.opening: spoliator , she that robs , pillages , or spoils : Venus spoliatrix, * Cic. Cael. 21, 52 : amica, Mart. 4, 29, 5 .

spŏlĭātus.opening: Part. and P. a. of spolio.

spŏlĭo.opening: v. a. spolium , to strip , to deprive of covering , rob of clothing. In gen. (rare but class.; syn. exuo): Phalarim vestitu spoliare, Cic. Off. 3, 6, 29 : consules spoliari hominem et virgas expediri jubent, Liv. 2, 55…

spŏlĭum.opening: root spal- (skal-); cf.: populor, calamitas, calvus . Lit. , the spoil of an animal, i. e. the skin or hide of an animal stripped off (so only poet. and very rare): pelles et spolia ferarum, Lucr. 5, 954 : serpentum,…

sponda.opening: Lit. , the frame of a bedstead, sofa, etc., Ov. M. 8, 657 ; Petr. 97, 4 ; 94, 8 .— Transf. A bed , couch , sofa (syn. lectus), Verg. A. 1, 698 ; Hor. Epod. 3, 22 ; Ov. F. 2, 345 ; Mart. 3, 91, 9 ; Suet. Caes. 49 .— A…

spondālĭum.opening: or (the form is uncertain), , , a sacrificial hymn , accompanied by the flute : spondalium canere, Diom. p. 472 fin. P.: spondalia dicens, etc., Cic. de Or. 2, 46, 193 Orell. N. cr.

spondĕo.opening: ( perf. spepondi, Cic., Caes., and Val. Antias ap. Gell. 7, 9, 12 sq. ; Inscr. Orell. 4358 ; without redup. sponderat, Tert. Carm. adv. Mart. 3, 135 ; subj. sponsis = spoponderis, an ancient formula of prayer in Fest.…

spondēus.opening: ( ; sometimes incorrectly written ), , , = σπονδεῖος , of or belonging to libations; hence, substt. , , , a vessel used in making libations , App. M. 11, p. 266, 26 .— (Because of its prolonged, solemn character.) A…

spondīăcus.opening: (less correctly ), , adj. , = σπονδειακός , consisting of spondees , spondaic : versus, Diom. p. 494 P.: tractus, Terentian. ap. Prisc. Metr. p. 1321 P.

spondўlē.opening: ( ), , , = σπονδύλη , an insect that lives in the ground , and gnaws the roots of trees , Plin. 27, 13, 118, § 143 .

spondўlĭon.opening: ( ) or , , , = σπονδύλιον ( σφονδύλιον ), the herb bear's-foot , bear's-wort , spicknel : Heracleum sphondylium, Linn.; Plin. 12, 26, 58, § 128 ; 24, 6, 16, § 25 ; Scrib. Comp. 2 and 5.

spondўlus.opening: ( ), , , = σπόνδυλος ( σφόνδυλος ). A joint of the spine , a vertebra , spondyle , Plin. 29, 4, 20, § 67 ; 32, 10, 38, § 116 ; Veg. Vet. 6, 1, 1 .— The hard white or muscle of an oyster or other bivalve, Plin. 32, 6,…

Spongĭa.opening: a proper name , perh. fictitious, in contempt, Cic. Att. 1, 16, 6 .

spongĭo.opening: v. a. spongia , to wipe off with a sponge , to sponge (late Lat.), perh. only Apic. 1, 26 , and 8, 1.

spongĭŏla.opening: dim. id. . A rosegall , a spongy substance growing upon the wild rose-bush, Plin. 25, 2, 6, § 18 .— The small roots of the asparagus, Col. 11, 3, 44 .

spongĭŏlus.opening: dim. id. , a kind of small fungus or mushroom , Apic. 2, 1 ; 5, 1 ; 3, 20 .

spongĭōsus.opening: or , , adj. id. , spongy , porous (post-Aug.): pulmo, Cels. 4, 1 ; Plin. 11, 37, 72, § 188 : pumices, id. 36, 21, 42, § 155 : panis, id. 18, 11, 27, § 105 .

spongītis.opening: , = σπογγῖτις [id.] (sponge - stone), a kind of precious stone , Plin. 37, 10, 67, § 182 .

spongĭus.opening: adj. id. , spongy (late Lat.): lignum, Cassiod. Var. 11, 38 .

spongīzo.opening: v. a. , = σπογγίζω , to wipe off with a sponge , to sponge , Apic. 7, 16 ; 8, 7 .

sponsālīcĭus.opening: or , , adj. sponsalia , of or belonging to betrothal , spousal (post-class.): arrha, Cod. Just. 5, 1, 5 ; 5, 2, 1 : donatio, Sid. Ep. 7, 2 med.

sponsālis.opening: adj. 3. sponsus . Of or belonging to betrothal or espousal , spousal , sponsal (class.): quo die sponsum erat, sponsalis, Varr. L. L. 6, § 70 Müll.: tabulae, Hier. Ep. 54, 15 : largitas, Cod. Th. 3, 16, 2. — Substt. , (…

spontālis.opening: adj. sponte , voluntary (post-class.): parricidium, App. M. 4, p. 147, 25 : sobrietas, id. ib. 11 , p. 272, 30.—* Adv. : , voluntarily : facere (opp. coactus), Sid. Ep. 8, 9 .

spontānĕus.opening: adj. sponte , of one's free will , voluntary , spontaneous (late Lat.): mors, Macr. Somn. Scip. 2, 22 : voluntas, free will, Cod. Just. 2, 3, 2 : benignitates numinum, Arn. 3, p. 114 .— Adv. : , voluntarily , willingly…

sprētĭo.opening: sperno , a despising , disdain , scorn , contempt : Romanorum, Liv. 40, 5 dub.; Ambros. Enarr. in Psa. 43, § 54 .

spūmĕus.opening: adj. id. , foaming , frothy ( poet. and in post-Aug. prose): Nereus, Verg. A. 2, 419 : amnis, id. ib. 2, 496 : unda, id. ib. 10, 212 : torrens, Ov. M. 3, 571 : aper, Mart. 14, 221, 2 : cumulus undarum, Luc. 9, 798 :…

spūmĭdus.opening: adj. id. , foaming , frothy (Appuleian): umor, App. Mag. p. 306 : tabes, id. ib. p. 306.

spūmĭfer.opening: adj. spuma-fero , foam-bearing , foaming ( poet. ): amnis, Ov. Am. 3, 6, 46 : fons, id. M. 11, 140 : fluctus, Stat. Achill. 1, 59 .

spūmōsus.opening: adj. spuma . Lit. , full of foam , foaming ( poet. and in postAug. prose): unda, Verg. A. 6, 174 : litora, Cat. 64, 121 : undae, Ov. M. 1, 570 : aequor, Luc. 2, 627 : morsus equi, Claud. IV. Cons. Hon. 548 : spumosus…

spurcālĭa.opening: plur. [spurco], pollutions (late Lat.), Aldh. Laud. Virg. 25 .

spurcĭdĭcus.opening: adj. spurcusdico , using filthy language , smutty , obscene : versus, Plaut. Capt. prol. 56 .

spurcĭlŏquĭum.opening: spurcus-loquor , filthy or smutty language , obscenity , Tert. Res. Carn. 4 fin.

spurcĭtĭa.opening: ( nom. collat. form , Lucr. 6, 977 ; abl. spurcitie, App. M. 8, p. 214, 33 ), spurcus , filth , dirt , smut , dung (rare; not in Cic.). Lit. , Col. 1, 5, 8 ; 12, 17, 2 ; Plin. 33, 4, 21, § 69 ; plur. , Varr. R. R. 3,…

spurco.opening: , no perf. , , v. a. id. , to make filthy , to befoul , defile (rare; syn.: polluo, contamino). Lit. : si quis fimo aliquem pertuderit, luto oblinierit, aquā spurcaverit, Dig. 47, 11, 1 : vinum, ib. 9, 2, 27 : ex istoc…

spūtāmen.opening: sputo , spittle (late Lat.), Prud. Apoth. 744 ; Tert. adv. Gnost. 10 ; plur. , Cael. Aur. Tard. 2, 14, 199 .

spūtāmentum.opening: id. , spittle (late Lat.), Jul. Val Rer. Gest. Alex. 1, 2; Tert. Spect. 30 .

spūtātĭlĭcus.opening: adj. id. , that deserves to be spit at , abominable , detestable (a word coined by Sisenna): crimina ejus, Sisenn. ap. Cic. Brut. 75, 260 (= κατάπτυστα ).

spūtātor.opening: id. , one who spits much , a spitter , Plaut. Mil. 3, 1, 52 .

squālĭdĭtas.opening: squalidus , filth , dirt , squalidity; trop., neglect , disorder (late Lat.): omnia confundentes squaliditate, Amm. 26, 5, 15 .

squālĭtūdo.opening: squalidus , dirt , filth , Att. ap. Non. 226, 2 (Trag. Rel. v. 340 Rib.).

squălus.opening: a kind of sea-fish , Varr. R. R. 3, 3, 9 Schneid. N. cr.; Plin. 9, 24, 40, § 78 ; 9, 51, 74, § 162 ; Ov. Hal. 123 .

stercus.opening: Gr. σκώρ; gen. σκατός, dung; Sanscr. cakrt = sakart . Lit. , dung , excrements , ordure (syn.: fimus, merda), Varr. R. R. 1, 38 ; Col. 2, 15 ; Cato, R. R. 29 ; 37 ; Cic. Div. 1, 27, 57 ; Hor. Epod. 12, 11 al. ; Fest. p.…

sterelȳtis.opening: a sort of scum or litharge of silver , Plin. 33, 6, 35, § 108 .

stĕrĕŏbăta.opening: , = στερεοβάτης , a pedestal of a column or row of columns, Vitr. 3, 3 .

stergēthron.opening: , = στέργηθρον , a plant , great houseleek , Plin. 25, 13, 102, § 160 ; App. Herb. 123 .

Stēria.opening: , = Στειρία , a town in Attica , Plin. 4, 7, 11, § 24 .

stērĭcŭla.opening: , ae. dim. , the uterus of a sow that has not yet farrowed , Petr. 35, 3 .

stērigmos.opening: , = στηριγμός , the standing-still of a planet (pure Lat. stativa lux), App. de Mundo, p. 64, 25.

stĕrĭlĕfīo.opening: v. n. sterilis-facio , to become unfruitful , barren , or sterile : leaenae sterilefiunt in aeternum, Sol. 27 med. dub. (al. steriles fiunt).

stĕrĭlesco.opening: v. inch. n. [sterilis], to grow unfruitful , barren , or sterile. Lit. : leaenae, Plin. 8, 16, 17, § 45 : caprae pinguitudine, id. 8, 50, 76, § 200 : amygdalae, id. 17, 10, 11, § 63 : mamma (suis), id. 11, 40, 95, § 234…

stĕrĭlĭcŭla.opening: , = vulva sterilis, the womb of a sow that has never borne young , Petr. 35, 3 .

stĕrĭlis.opening: (collat. form, acc. sing. fem sterilam sterilem, Fest. p. 316 Müll.; neutr. plur. sterila, Lucr. 2, 845 ; abl. sterile, Apic. 7, 1, § 258 ), adj. Gr. στερεός, hard; στερίφη, στεῖρα, barren; Sanscr. starī, vacca sterilis…

stĕrĭlĭtas.opening: sterilis , unfruitfulness , barrenness , sterility (class.). Lit. : quae sit vel sterilitas agrorum vel fertilitas futura, Cic. Div. 1, 57, 131 ; id. Agr. 2, 26, 70 : frugum, Vell. 1, 1 fin. : arborum, Plin. 16, 26, 47,…

sternax.opening: adj. sterno , that throws to the ground ( poet. ): equus, that throws his rider, Verg. A. 12, 364 ; Sil. 1, 261 : cives, that fall prostrate, Sid. Ep. 5, 14 fin. ; so of a suppliant, id. ib. 4, 12 fin.

sterno.opening: ( pluperf. sync. strarat, Manil. 1, 774 : strasset, Varr. ap. Non. 86, 8 ), v. a. Gr. root ΣΤΟΡ, στορέννυμι, to spread; στρατός, camp; Sanscr. star- strnāmi = sterno; cf.: strages, struo, torus, and lātus, adj., old…

sternūmentum.opening: sternuo , a sneezing (class.; but cf. sternutamentum). Lit. , Cic. Div. 2, 40, 84 ; Plin. 2, 7, 5, § 24 ; 21, 22, 93, § 163 ; 25, 5, 21, § 52 ; 28, 6, 15, § 57; Gell. 12, 5, 11 ; Cels. 3, 20 ; 8, 4 ; 8, 9 .— Transf. , a…

sternŭo.opening: v. n. and a. [cf. Gr. πτάρνυσθαι , v. Georg Curtius Griech. Etym. p. 696 ]. Neutr. , to sneeze : adorare aliquem, cum sternuerit, Plin. 2, 40, 40, § 107 ; 28, 6, 15, § 57 ; 19, 3, 15, § 40 (al. sternuto); Col. 7, 5, 18…

sternūtāmentum.opening: sternuto , a sneezing (post-Aug.): sternutamenta erunt observanda, Sen. Ira, 2, 25, 4 ; Scrib. 10 (in Cic. Div. 2, 40, 84 , the better reading is sternumenta).

sternūtātĭo.opening: id. , a sneezing , sternutation (post-class. and rare for sternumentum), App. M. 9, p. 228, 24 ; Scrib. Comp. 10 fin. ; Front. Ep. ad M. Caes. 4, 5 fin.

sternūto.opening: v. freq. n. [sternuo], to sneeze , Petr. 98, 4 ; 102, 10 ; Plin. 19, 3, 15, § 40 .

Stĕrŏpē.opening: , = Στερόπη . One of the Pleiades , Att. ap. Serv. Verg. A. 8, 130 (Trag. Rel. p. 135 Rib.); Ov. F. 4, 172 ; id. Tr. 1, 11, 14 .— One of the horses of the sun , Hyg. Fab. 183 .

Stĕrŏpes.opening: , = Στερόπης , one of the Cyclops in Vulcan's smithy , Verg. A. 8, 425 ; Ov. F. 4, 288 ; Claud. III. Cons. Hon. 195 ; id. Rapt. Pros. 1, 239 ; acc. Steropem, Stat. S. 1, 1, 4 .

sterquĭlīnĭum.opening: (in MSS. also written and , Plaut. Pers. 3, 3, 3 ; Ter. Phorm. 3, 2, 41 ; Dig. 19, 1, 17, § 2 ), , (collat. form , , Phaedr. 3, 12, 1 ) [stercus], a dung-pit , laystall , mixen , Cato, R. R. 2, 3 ; Varr. 1, 13, 4 ; 1,…

Stertĭnĭus.opening: a Stoic philosopher , Hor. S. 2, 3, 33 ; 2, 3, 296 .— Adj. : , , of Stertinius : acumen, Hor. Ep. 1, 12, 20 .

sterto.opening: (acc. to Prisc. p. 903 P.; cf. desterto), , v. n. cf.: δέρθω, δαρθάνω , to snore : noctem totam stertere, Plaut. As. 5, 2, 22 ; id. Mil. 3, 2, 7 : stertit noctes et dies, Ter. Eun. 5, 8, 49 ; Hor. Ep. 2, 2, 27 :…

Stēsĭchŏrus.opening: , = Στησίχορος , a Greek lyric poet of Himera : Stesichori graves Camenae, Hor. C. 4, 9, 8 ; cf. Quint. 10, 1, 62 ; Cic. Sen. 7, 23 ; Cic. Verr. 2, 2, 35, § 87 ; Stat. S. 5, 3, 154 .

Sthĕnĕboea.opening: or , , , = Σθενέβοια, Σθενόβοια , daughter of Iobates , king of Lycia , Juv. 10, 327 ; Hyg. Fab. 57 and 243.—Hence, adj. : , , of or belonging to Sthenebœa : heros, i. e. Bellerophon, whom Sthenebœa loved, Sid. Carm.…

Sthĕnĕlus.opening: , = Σθένελος . King of Mycenœ , son of Perseus , and father of Eurystheus , Hyg. Fab. 244 .— King of the Ligurians , father of Cycnus , who was changed into a swan , and who , from his father , is called proles…

Sthennis.opening: , = Σθένις , a sculptor of Olynthus , Plin. 34, 8, 19, § 90 .

Sthĕno.opening: , = Σθενώ , a daughter of Phorcus and Ceto , sister of Medusa , Hyg. Fab. praef.

stĭbădĭum.opening: , = στιβάδιον , a semicircular seat or couch , Plin. Ep. 5, 6, 36 ; Serv. Verg. A. 1, 698 ; Sid. Ep. 1, 11 med. ; 2, 2 med. ; Mart. 14, 87 in lemm.; Inscr. Orell. 2358 .

stĭbĭnus.opening: adj. stibium , antimonial , of antimony : lapides, Vulg. 1 Par. 29, 2 .

stĭbĭum.opening: ; also called , , and = στίβι, στιμμι , antimony , a sulphuret of antimony , stibium , used by women, in the form of powder, to color their eyebrows and eyelashes black; and in medicine, as an eye-salve, Plin. 33, 6,…

stĭcha.opening: , = στίχη , a kind of vine (pure Lat. apiana), Plin. 14, 9, 11, § 81 .

Stĭchus.opening: the name of a slave , Gai. Inst. 2, 193 ; 2, 199 ; 4, 55 ; Dig. 2, 14, 27, § 7 al. —Hence, Title of a comedy of Plautus.

Stictē.opening: one of Actœon's hounds , Ov. M. 3, 217 ; Hyg. Fab. 181 .

stĭcŭla.opening: dim. , a kind of grape , Col. 3, 2, 27 .

stigma.opening: ( fem. collat. form, acc. stigmam, Petr. 45, 9 ; 69, 1 ), = στίγμα , a prick, puncture (post-Aug.). A mark burned in , a brand impressed upon slaves or others, as a mark of disgrace. Lit. , Petr. 103, 2 ; 105, 11 :…

stigmătĭas.opening: , = στιγματίας . One who is branded , of a slave, Cic. Off. 2, 7, 25 .— Title of a comedy of Nœvius , Varr. L. L. 7, § 107 Müll.; v. Com. Rel. p. 19 Rib.

stigmo.opening: v. a. stigma , to brand , stigmatize (late Lat.), Prud. στεφ . 10, 1079.

stigmōsus.opening: adj. id. , full of brand-marks , branded , Petr. 109, 8 ; Regul. ap. Plin. Ep. 1, 5, 2 .

Stilbon.opening: , = Στίλβων (the shining, glittering), a name of the planet Mercury , Aus. Idyll. 18, 11 ; Mart. Cap. 8, § 851 ; Hyg. Astr. 2, 42 fin. (as Greek, Cic. N. D. 2, 20, 53 ).— One of Actœon's hounds , Hyg. Fab. 181 .

Stilicho.opening: (written STELICHO, Inscr. Orell. 4999 ), , , the famous general and father-in-law of the emperor Honorius , celebrated by Claudian in his poem De laudibus Stilichonis; cf. also Oros. 7, 37 sq. —Hence, adj. : , , of or…

stilla.opening: dim. of stĭria; cf. Fest. s. v. stiricipium, p. 345 Müll.; Corss. 1, p. 518 , a drop (a dense, viscous, gummy, fatty drop; whereas gutta is a natural, liquid drop: gutta imbrium est, stilla olei vel aceti, Suet. Fragm.…

stillanter.opening: adv. stillo , drop by drop , Ambros. Ep. 41, 14 .

stillārĭum.opening: stilla , an added drop , a trifling addition , Sen. Ep. 97, 2 .

stillātīcĭus.opening: adj. stillo , dropping , dripping , stillatitious : resina, Plin. 16, 11, 22, § 54 .

stillātim.opening: adv. stilla , by drops , drop by drop : stillatim cadere, Varr. L. L. 5, § 27 Müll.

stillātĭo.opening: stillo , a dropping down , falling in drops (late Lat.): pluviae, Hier. in Mich. 1, 2, 6 .

stillātīvus.opening: adj. id. , dropping , dripping (late Lat.): mel, Plin. Val. 1, 18 .

stillĭcĭdĭum.opening: (also written ; v. Lachm. ad Lucr. p. 33 ), , stilla-cado , a liquid which falls drop by drop , a dripping moisture , stillicide : stillicidium eo quod stillatim cadat, Varr. L. L. 5, § 27 Müll. In gen. ( poet. and in…

stillo.opening: v. n. and a [stilla]. Neutr. , to drop , drip , trickle , distil (mostly poet. ; syn. roro). Lit. : vas, unde stillet lente aqua, Varr. R. R. 1, 41, 2 : gutta (dulcedinis) in cor, Lucr. 4, 1060 : umorem, quasi igni cera…

stĭlo.opening: v. n. stilus, I. , to get stalks , Col. 4, 33, 3 .

Stĭlo.opening: a surname of L. Aelius Praeconinus, Plin. 33, 1, 7, § 29 ; Suet. Gram. 3 ; cf. v. Hensde, Disquis. de L. Aelio Stilone; and Ritschl, Parerga, p. 239.

Stilpo.opening: or , , , = Στίλπων . A proper name , Ter. ap. Cic. Or. 47, 157 .— Esp., a philosopher of Megara , Cic. Fat. 5, 10 ; id. Ac. 2, 24, 75 ; Sen. Ep. 9, 1 .

stĭlus.opening: (not ), , for stiglus; Gr. στίζω, to stick, puncture; στίγμα, mark, point; Sanscr. tig, to be sharp; tigmas, sharp; cf. Engl. stick, sting; Lat. stimulus; not connected with στῦλος . In gen., a stake , pale : extra…

Stĭmŭla.opening: ( , Liv. 39, 12 ), , stimulus , the goddess who pricks on , excites , stimulates to action or pleasure, Aug. Civ Del, 4, 11; 4, 16; perh. for Semele, Ov. F. 6, 503 ; Schol. Juv. 2, 3 ; cf. Müller, Etrusk. 2, 77.

stĭmŭlātĭo.opening: stimulo , a pricking on , incitement , stimulation (post-Aug.): ingens, Plin. 35, 2, 2, § 7 : privata cuique, Tac. H. 1, 90 fin.

stĭmŭlātor.opening: id. , a pricker-on , instigator , stimulator , Claud. ap. Ruf. 2, 501 ; Mamert. Grat. Act. ad Iul. 5 (in Cic. Dom. 5, 11 , Orell. and B. and K. read instimulator); Vulg. Jer. 46, 20 .

stĭmŭlātrix.opening: stimulator , she that pricks on , instigates , or stimulates , Plaut. Most. 1, 3, 46 ; 1, 3, 62 .

stĭmŭlĕus.opening: adj. stimulus , consisting of prickles or goads : supplicium, Plaut. Mil. 2, 6, 31 .

stĭmŭlo.opening: v. a. id. , to prick with a goad , to prick or goad on , to urge on (syn. pungo). Lit. (post-Aug. and rare): quadrijugos flagello, Sil. 4, 439 : equos calcaribus, Val. Max. 3, 2, 9 ; for which, poet. transf.: turbatos…

stĭmŭlōsus.opening: adj. id. , full of incentives , stimulative (post-class.): desiderium Venereae voluptatis, Cael. Aur. Tard. 5, 9 ; id. Acut. 2, 14 ; 3, 18 .

stĭmŭlus.opening: for stig-mulus, from the root stig; Gr. στίζω; v. stilus . A goad for driving cattle, slaves, etc. (class., esp. in the trop. sense). Lit. : jam lora teneo, jam stimulum in manu: Agite equi, etc., Plaut. Men. 5, 2, 112…

stinguo.opening: v. a. cf. stig; Gr. στίζω; cf. also Germ. ersticken , to quench , extinguish ( poet. and very rare, for the usu. extinguo): ut cernere possis Evanescere paulatim stinguique colorem, Lucr. 2, 828 : ignes stingui, id. 1,…

stīpātio.opening: stipo , a crowd pressing around any one, a suite , retinue , train. Lit. : latrones dicti ab latere, qui circum latera erant regi, quos postea a stipatione stipatores appellarunt, Varr. L. L. 7, § 52 Müll. fin. :…

stīpātor.opening: stipo; prop. one that presses upon, crowds about another; hence , an attendant of a nobleman; in plur. , attendants , train , suite , retinue , bodyguard , etc. (class.; used by the Romans in a bad sense; cf. satelles):…

stipātrix.opening: adj. f. [stipator], attendant upon , thronging in attendance : turmae stipatrices, Ambros. Hexaëm. 5, 16, 53.

stīpātus.opening: Part. and P. a. of stipo.

stī^pendĭālis.opening: adj. stipendium , of or belonging to tribute : foedere stĭpendiali. by which one engages to pay tribute , Sid. Ep. 8, 9 .

stĭ_pendĭārĭus.opening: adj. id. . Of or belonging to tribute , liable to impost or contribution , tributary (of imposts payable in money; whereas vectigalis denotes those payable in kind; the former was held to be the most humiliating; cf.…

stīpendĭor.opening: v. dep. n. [id.], to receive pay , to serve for pay (very rare): regi eorum peditum sexcenta M. stipendiantur, Plin. 6, 19, 22, § 68 .— Transf. : (infantes Pontici) butyro stipendiati, serving for butter , getting…

stīpendĭōsus.opening: adj. id. , belonging to military service : milites (opp. tirones), soldiers in the very service, Veg. 1, 18 .

stīpendĭum.opening: contr. from stipipendium, from stips-pendo . In publicists' lang., a tax , impost , tribute , contribution (payable in money; whereas vectigal in kind; the former being regarded as the more humiliating; v.…

stīpĕs.opening: (collat. form , , Petr. 43, 5 ), root stip-, = Gr. στεφ-; v. stipo; Sanscr. sthapa-jami, to cause to stand, to fix, place; cf. stipula . Lit. , a log , stock , post , trunk of a tree , etc. (class.; syn.: palus, sudes),…

stīpĭdōsus.opening: adj. stipes , woody , ligneous : radix, App. Herb. 67 ; 74 .

stīpo.opening: v. a. στέφω, to surround, crowd upon, στέμμα, στέφανος; cf.: stipator, stipulor , to crowd or press together , to compress (class.; esp. of personal objects, and in part. perf.; cf.: comprimo, compono). Lit. : qui…

stĭpŭla.opening: dim. stipes , a stalk , stem , blade , halm; of grain (syn. culmus): frumenta in viridi stipulā lactentia turgent, Verg. G. 1, 315 ; Plin. 14, 16, 19, § 101 ; 17, 27, 47, § 260 ; 18, 18, 47, § 169 : e segete ad…

stĭpŭlātĭo.opening: stipulor , jurid. t. t., a promise given on demand; an engagement , agreement , bargain , covenant , stipulation , obligation (syn. pactum), Gai. Inst. 2, 31 : stipulatio est verborum conceptio, quibus is qui…

stĭpŭlātĭuncŭla.opening: dim. stipulatio , a little , insignificant promise or stipulation , Cic. de Or. 1, 38, 174 .

stĭpŭlātor.opening: stipulor , jurid. t. t., one who demands a formal promise or covenant (opp. promissor, the one who gives the promise); a bargainer , stipulator , Dig. 2, 10, 3 ; 45, 1, 41 sq.; 45, 38, 5; Suet. Vit. 14 ; Isid. Orig. 10,…

stĭpŭlātus.opening: id. , jurid. t. t., a promise formally demanded; a bargain , stipulation , Quint. Decl. 12, 21 : si quid adversus pactionem fiat, non ex stipulatu agitur, etc., Gai. Inst. 3, 94 ; 4, 116 ; Dig. 45, 1, 1 ; 45, 1, 4 sq.;…

stĭpŭlo.opening: v. a. (collat. form of stipulor), to exact , bargain for , stipulate , Symm. Ep. 1, 11 : ἐπερωτῶ , stipulo, Gloss.; mostly pass. : Suetonius autem passivo protulit in IIII. Pratorum, Laetoria, quae vetat minorem annis…

stĭpŭlor.opening: ( inf. paragog. stipularier, Plaut. Ps. 4, 6, 14 ), v. dep. acc. to Varr. L. L. 5, § 182 Müll., kindr. with stips: qui pecuniam alligat, stipulari et restipulari; cf. also: cum spondetur pecunia, stipulari dicitur,…

stĭpŭlus.opening: adj. (old Lat.), firm : stipulum apud veteres firmum appellabatur, Just. Inst. 3, 15 ; Paul. Sent. 5, 7, § 1 .

stīrĭa.opening: cf. stilla; Engl. tear , a frozen drop; an ice-drop , ice-drop , icicle ( poet. and in post-Aug. prose), Verg. G. 3, 366 ; so too Plin. 34, 12, 32, § 124 ; Mart. 7, 37, 5 ; Claud. B. Get. 327 ; Tert. Pall. 4 .

Stĭrĭa.opening: an island near the coast of Cilicia , Plin. 5, 31, 35, § 129 .

stīrĭăcus.opening: adj. stiria , frozen : gutta, Sol. 27 med.

stīrĭcĭdĭum.opening: stiria-cado , a falling of snow-flakes , a snowing : stiricidium quasi stillicidium, cum stillae concretae frigore cadunt. Stiria enim principale est, stilla deminutivum, Fest. p. 345 Müll.; so Cato ib. p. 344 .

stirpesco.opening: v. inch. n. [stirps], to run to stalk : asparagus, Plin. 19, 8, 42, § 149 .

stirpĭtus.opening: adv. id.; cf. radicitus from radix , by the stalk , by the roots , root and branch , stock and stump (very rare). * Lit. : arborem transferre, Dig. 47, 7, 3, § 4 . —* Transf. : barbam forcipibus evellere, Sid. Ep. 1, 2…

stirps.opening: (collat. form of the nom. or , in the best MSS., Liv. 1, 1 fin. ; 41, 8, 10 ; 26, 13, 16 ; v. Drak. ad locc.), , ( poet. and post-Aug.; also , Enn. ap. Fest. p. 313 Müll., and ap. Non. 226, 32 (Ann. 184); Pac. ap. Non.…

stīva.opening: a plough-handle , Varr. L. L. 5, § 135 Müll.; Verg. G. 1, 174 ; Ov. M. 8, 218 ; id. F. 4, 825 ; Col. 1, 9, 3 ; Amm. 15, 4, 3 .

stīvārĭus.opening: stiva , a ploughman (late Lat.), Aldhel. Laud. Virg. 28.

stlāta.opening: 1. latus, q. v. init. , a kind of ship : stlata genus navigii latum magis quam altum, et a latitudine sic appellatum, sed eā consuetudine, quā stlocum pro locum et stlitem pro litem dicebant, Fest. p. 312 Müll.; cf.…

stlātārĭus.opening: ( ), , adj. stlata , of or belonging to a ship (very rare), Enn. ap. Schol. Juv. 7, 134 (Ann. v. 469 Vahl.). — Poet. , transf.; stlataria purpura, brought by ship , i. e. costly , Juv. 7, 134 Schol. (al. deceitful , cf.…

stlembus.grammar: gravis tardus, sicut Lucilius pedibus stlembum dixit equum pigrum et tardum

stloppus.opening: a slap (the sound produced by striking upon the inflated cheek), Pers. 5, 13 .

sto.opening: (scanned stĕtĕrunt, Verg. A. 2, 774 ; 3, 48 ; Ov. H. 7, 166 ; Prop. 2, 8, 10 ), v. n. root sta-; Sanscr. sthā, sthalam, locus; Gr. στα-, ἵστημι, to set, place; στατήρ, weight; O. H. Germ. stām; Goth. standa; Engl. stand…

Stōbi.opening: an ancient and important city of Paeonia in Northern Macedonia , Liv. 33, 19, 3 Weissenb. ad loc.; 39, 53, 15; 40, 21, 1: oppidum Stobi civium Romanorum, Plin. 4, 10, 17, § 34 .—The inhabitants are called , , , Dig. 50,…

stobrus.opening: a tree in Carmania yielding an odorous gum , Plin. 12, 17, 40, § 79 .

stoebē.opening: , = στοιβή , a plant , called also pheos, Plin. 21, 15, 54, § 91 ; 22, 11, 13, § 28 .

Stoechădĕs.opening: , = Στοιχάδες , a group of islands on the southern coast of Gaul , near Massilia , now Isles d'Hyères , Plin. 3, 5, 11, § 79 ; Schol. Cic. Sest. p. 293 Orell .—Hence, , , (sc. herba), French lavender , sticados :…

Stōĭcĭda.opening: Stoicus , a nickname of a voluptuary who gave himself out for a Stoic , Juv. 2, 65 .

Stōĭcus.opening: adj. , = Στωϊκός , of or belonging to the Stoic philosophy or to the Stoics , Stoic : schola, Cic. Fam. 9, 22 fin. : secta, Sen. Ep. 123, 14 : sententia, id. ib. 22, 7 : libelli, Hor. Epod. 8, 15 : turba, Mart. 7, 69, 4…

Stōĭdis.opening: ( ), , , an island off the Indian coast , famous for pearls : Stoades quaestuosa margaritis, Plin. 6, 25, 28, § 110 : Stoadis, id. 9, 34, 54, § 106 .

stŏla.opening: , = στολή , a long upper garment. Orig., as with the Greeks, worn by any one: squalidā saeptus stolā, Enn. ap. Non. 537, 27 (Trag. v. 373 Vahl.); Ov. F. 6, 654 : saeptus mendici stolā, Enn. ap. Non. 537, 28 (Trag. v.…

stŏlātus.opening: adj. stola . Lit. , dressed in or wearing a stola: mulieres, Vitr. 1, 1 med.—Subst. : , , , = matronae, noble dames , matrons , Petr. 44, 18 .— Transf. : pudor, i.e. befitting a matron, Mart. 1, 36, 8 : Ulixes, Ulysses…

stŏlĭdĭtas.opening: stolidus , dulness , obtuseness , stupidity , stolidity (post-class.), Flor. 3, 3, 12 ; 4, 12, 16 ; Gell. 18, 4, 6 ; Arn. 2, 80 al.

stŏlĭdus.opening: adj. root star-; Gr. στερεός, firm; cf. stultus; v. Corss. Ausspr. 2, 155 sq. . Unmovable; and hence, slow , coarse , uncultivated , rude (class.; cf.: fatuus, insipiens, stupidus, stultus, insulsus).— Lit. : stolidum…

stŏlo.opening: a shoot , branch , twig , or scion springing from the stock or root of a tree , a useless sucker , water-shoot : qui (Licinius Stolo) propter diligentiam culturae Stolonum confirmavit cognomen, quod nullus in ejus fundo…

Stŏlo.opening: a cognomen in the gens Licinia; v. 1. stolo.

stŏmăcăcē.opening: , = στομακάκη , a disease of the gums , scurvy of the mouth , Plin. 25, 3, 6, § 20 .

stŏmăchābundus.opening: adj. stomachor , pettish , angry , stomachy : puer, Gell. 17, 8, 6 .
