sŭb-audĭo.opening: v. n. (postclass.). To understand , supply a word omitted: subaudito jubeo, Dig. 28, 5, 1 ; Aug. Civ. Dei , 15, 7; 17, 11; Greg. M. in Job, 33, 17.— To hear a little : nocturnis subaudiens vocibus, App. M. 5, p. 167, 4 .

sŭbaudītĭo.opening: subaudio , an understanding , supplying a word omitted (post-class.), Serv. Verg. A. 10, 80 ; Hier. Quaest. Hebr. in Reg. 2, 3, 13 .

sŭb-aurātus.opening: adj. , slightly gilt : anulus, Petr. 32, 3 : tabellae, Schol. Juv. 7, 23 : STATVA, Inscr. Orell. 1126 .

sŭb-ausculto.opening: v. a. , to listen secretly , to eavesdrop (rare but class.): subauscultando excipere voces, Cic. de Or. 2, 36, 153 : opprime os: is est, etiam subauscultemus, Plaut. As. 3, 2, 40 : tace, subauscultemus, ecquid de me…

sŭb-austērus.opening: adj. , rather harsh : vinum austerum vel certe subausterum, Cels. 3, 6, § 61 ; 6, 6 . 8, § 68.

sub-balbē.opening: adv. balbus , somewhat stammeringly : canorus, Spart. Get. 5, § 1 .

Sub-ballĭo.opening: Under - Ballio , Sub - Ballio; a comically - formed name: Ha. Tune es Ballio? Ps. Immo vero ego ejus sum Subballio, Plaut. Ps. 2, 2, 13 .

sub-băsĭlĭcānus.opening: basilica , one who lounges around the basilicas , a lounger : quorum odos subbasilicanos omnes abigit, Plaut. Capt. 4, 2, 35 Brix ad loc.

sub-bĭbo.opening: v. a. , to drink a little , to tipple (very rare), * Plaut. Truc. 4, 3, 58 (dub.; Speng. si urnas bibit): si paulum subbibisset, * Suet. Ner. 20 .

sub-blandĭor.opening: ( fut. subblandibitur, Plaut. Bacch. 3, 4, 19 ; inf. subblandirier, id. Cas. 3, 3, 22 ), v. dep. n. , to caress or fondle a little (ante-class.): subblanditur, palpatur, Lucil. ap. Non. 472, 6 ; Plaut. As. 1, 3, 33 :…

sub-bullĭo.opening: v. n. , to foam or bubble slightly , Cassiod. Hist. Eccl. 7, 2 ; Plin. Val. 1, 11 .

sub-dĕalbo.opening: v. a. , to whiten a little , make whilish , Varr. ap. Non. 72, 11 .

sub-dēbĭlis.opening: adj. , somewhat weak or enfeebled : femur, Suet. Vit. 17 .

sub-dēbĭlĭtātus.opening: adj. debilito , somewhat enfeebled or debilitated; trop., somewhat discouraged , rather spiritless , Cic. Att. 11, 5, 1 (dub.; better: subitā re quasi debilitatum, B. and K.).

subdēfectĭo.opening: sub - deficio , a slight failure : fidei, Aug. Quaest. in Heptat. 6, 30 .

sub-dēfĭcĭo.opening: v. n. , to become more and more feeble , to fail somewhat (postAug.), Curt. 7, 7, 10 : in labore, Aug. Serm. 343 fin.

subdēlĭgo.opening: v. a. sub-deligo , to choose (late Lat.), Aug. Categ. 6 .

subdescendo.opening: v. n. sub-descendo , to descend lower (late Lat.), Mar. Merc. Commonit. 4, 6.

sub-dĭăcŏnus.opening: a sub - deacon , Cod. Just. 1, 3, 6 ; Aug. Ep. 53 ; 63 ; Isid. 7, 12, 23 .

sub-dĭālis.opening: ( , Amm. 19, 11, 4 ), , adj. dius , that is in the open air (post-Aug.): inambulationes, Plin. 14, 1, 3, § 11 : petrae, id. 34, 12, 29, § 117 .—As subst. : , , , open galleries or terraces; a transl. of the Gr.…

sub-diffĭcĭlis.opening: adj. , somewhat difficult : quaestio, Cic. Lael. 19, 67 .

sub-diffīdo.opening: v. n. , to be somewhat distrustful , Cic. Att. 15, 20, 2 .

sub-dīmĭdĭus.opening: adj. , of a number, half as much less , less by one half of itself (i. e. that bears to another the ratio of 2 to 3): numerus (opp. superdimidius), Mart. Cap. 7, § 761 .

sub-disjunctĭo.opening: , gram. t. t., a minor stop , colon , Diom. p. 432 P.

sub-disjunctīvus.opening: adj. , subdisjunctive; said of two statements opposed to each other in such a way that neither of them may hold good (postclass.): haec verba: ille aut ille, non solum disjunctiva sed etiam subdisjunctivae orationis…

sub-distinguo.opening: v. a. , to make a smaller interpunction (perh. a colon ), Ascon. ad Cic. Verr. 2, 2, 13 fin.

subdĭtīcĭus.opening: (later ), , adj. subdo , substituted , supposititious , spurious , counterfeit (perh. only ante- and postclass., since the correct read. in Cic. Verr. 2, 5, 27, § 69 , is subditivum; and in Quint. 1, 4, 3 , subditos):…

subdĭtīvus.opening: adj. id. , substituted , supposititious , spurious , counterfeit (rare but class.): de illo subditivo Sosia mirum nimis est, Plaut. Am. 2, 2, 198 ; 1, 2, 35 : archipirata, Cic. Verr. 2, 5, 27, § 69 : fratrem ut…

subdĭto.opening: , a false read., Lucr. 6, 604 ; v. Lachm. ad h. l.

sub-dīvĭdo.opening: v. a. , to subdivide (late Lat.): libros, Aug. Civ. Dei , 6, 3 med. : deinde subdivisimus, id. Trin. 3 prooem.: hebdomades, Tert. adv. Jud. 11 fin.

subdīvīsĭo.opening: subdivido , a subdivision (post-class.), Cod. Just. 3, 28, 37 ; 6, 2, 22 ; Hier. Ep. 58, 5 al.

sub-do.opening: v. a. To put , place , set , or lay under (syn.: suppono, sterno). Lit. (class.). In gen.: ego puerum interead ancillae subdam lactantem meae, Liv. Andron. ap. Non. p. 153, 26 (Trag. Rel. v. 26 Rib.): ignem subdito,…

sub-dŏcĕo.opening: v. a. and n. , to teach as an assistant , to act as an assistant-teacher for a person (very rare): aliquem, Cic. Att. 8, 4, 1 : subdocere grammatico, Aug. Conf. 8, 6 .

sub-dŏlens.opening: adj. sub - doleo , somewhat painful : faucium sensus, Cael. Aur. Acut. 3, 2, 7 .

subdŏlōsĭtas.opening: sub - dolosus , craft , cunning , Isid. 10 , n. 229.

subdŏlōsus.opening: adj. id. , crafty (late Lat.), Cassiod. in Psa. 106, 34 .

sub-dŏlus.opening: adj. , somewhat crafty , cunning , sly , subtle , deceptive , or deceitful (mostly ante - class. and post - Aug.; syn.: fallax, astutus): homo et sycophanta et subdolus, Plaut. Poen. 5, 2, 72 ; id. Mil. 2, 4, 2 ; id.…

sub-dŏmo.opening: v. a. , to subject by taming , to tame , subdue , Plaut. As. 3, 3, 112 .

sub-dŭbĭto.opening: v. n. , to be a little doubtful or undecided , to have some hesitation (Ciceron.): antea subdubitabam, Cic. Att. 14, 15, 2 : significabant tuae litterae, te subdubitare, quā essem erga illum voluntate, id. Fam. 2, 13, 2…

sub-dūco.opening: ( perf. sync. subduxti, Ter. Eun. 4, 7, 25 ; inf. subduxe, Poët. ap. Varr. R. R. 2, 1, 6 ), v. a. , to draw from under or from below. Without the idea of removal. In gen., to draw or pull up; to lift up , raise (rare):…

subductārĭus.opening: adj. subduco, I. , that serves for drawing up : funes, hoisting-ropes, lifts, Cato, R. R. 12 ; 68 ; 135, 3 .

subductĭo.opening: id. . (Acc. to subduco, I. B. 1.) Naut. t. t., a hauling ashore of a ship: ad celeritatem onerandi subductionesque paulo facit humiliores (naves), * Caes. B. G. 5, 1 : navium, Vitr. 10, 2, 10 .—* (Acc. to subduco, II.…

sub-ductus.opening: Part. and P. a. , v. subduco.

sub-dulcis.opening: adj. , somewhat sweet , sweetish (Plinian): radix, Plin. 26, 8, 37, § 58 ; 26, 10, 63, § 98 .

sub-dūrus.opening: adj. , somewhat hard , hardish. * Lit. : (genus verrucae) subdurum, Cels. 5, 28, 14 .—* Trop. , Q. Cic. Petit. Cons. 12, 46 .

sŭb-ĕdo.opening: v. a. , to eat , waste , or wear away below : e scopulo, quem rauca subederat unda, Ov. M. 11, 783 ; Hier. in Jer. 1, 2, 37 .

sŭbēlectĭo.opening: sub-eligo , a further selection (late Lat.): subelectio est quando de bonis electis eliguntur meliores, Ps. Aug. ad Frater. Erem. Serm. 39 .

sŭbēlĭgo.opening: v. a. , to choose further (late Lat.), Ps.-Aug. ad Fratr. Serm. 39 .

sŭb-ēnarro.opening: v. a. , to relate (late Lat.), Anon. [Hilar.] in Job, 2, p. 174.

sŭb-ĕo.opening: ( perf. subīvit, Ov. F. 1, 314 ; Stat. S. 2, 1, 155 : subivimus, Claud. ap. Tac. A. 11, 24 dub.), v. n. and a. , to come or go under any thing; to come or go up to , to approach , draw near , advance or proceed to a…

sūber.opening: the cork-oak , cork-tree : Quercus suber, Linn.; Plin. 16, 8, 13, § 34 ; 16, 25, 41, § 98 ; Col. 4, 26, 1 ; 9, 6, 1 ; Verg. A. 7, 742 .— Transf. , cork : silvestre, Verg. A. 11, 554 ; cf.: ut ramale vetus vegrandi…

sūbĕrĕus.opening: adj. suber , of the cork-tree , cork- : cortex, Ser. Samm. 34, 649 : robur, Col. 9, 1, 3 Schneid. N. cr.

sub-ērĭgo.opening: , no perf. , , v. a. , to raise up from below (post-Aug.): Isthmon curvata sublime suberigit unda, Sil. 15, 155 : effultus in cubitum suberectusque, App. M. 2, p. 123 fin. ; Marc. Emp. 20 .

sūbĕrīnus.opening: adj. suber , of the cork-tree , cork - (syn. subereus): cortices, Sid. Ep. 2, 2 med.

Sūbĕrīnus.opening: 1. suberinus , a Roman surname , Plin. Ep. 6, 33, 6 .

sŭb-erro.opening: v. n. , to wander about under any thing: fluvii Italis suberrant Montibus, Claud. Cons. Prob. et Olybr. 254.

Subertāni.opening: a people of Etruria , the inhabitants of Subertum , the modern Sovretto in Tuscany , Plin. 3, 5, 8, § 52 . —Hence, , , adj. , of or belonging to the Subertani : forum, Liv. 26, 23, 5 .

sŭb-excūso.opening: v. a. , to excuse in part , Salv. Gub. Dei , 4, 3.

sŭb-exhĭbĕo.opening: v. a. , to exhibit under any thing, Arn. 6, 195 .

sŭb-explĭcans.opening: Part. [explico], unfolding below (late Lat.): non pedibus se ferens neque suas subexplicans itiones, Arn. 7, 251 .

sŭb-haerĕo.opening: v. n. , to stick under or behind; to cleave , adhere to a thing, Val. Max. 6, 3, 10 .

sŭbhastārĭus.opening: adj. sub-hasta , that is sold by public auction (jurid. Lat.): possessiones, Cod. Th. 13, 6, 9.

sŭbhastātĭo.opening: subhasto , a sale by public auction (late Lat. for venditio palam habita), Cod. Just. 4, 44, 16 ; Cod. Th. 10, 17, 3.

sŭb-hasto.opening: v. a. sub-hasta , to sell by public auction (jurid. Lat. for hastae subicio, palam vendo): res pignori datas. Cod. Just. 7, 53, 3 ; Sol. 10, 4 .

sŭb-hēres.opening: ( ), , , the next or second heir (syn.: heres secundus), Inscr. Orell. 3612 .

sŭb-horresco.opening: v. inch. n. , to become rough or stormy from below, to boil up : subito mare subhorrescere, Sisenn. ap. Non. 423, 9 .

sŭb-horrĭdus.opening: adj. , somewhat rough , roughish : subhorridus atque incultus, Cic. Sest. 9, 21 .

Subi.opening: a river of Spain , Plin. 3, 3, 4, § 21 .—Called also , , , Mel. 2, 6 .

sŭbĭces.opening: subicio , underlayers , supports : Ennius in tragoediā, quae Achilles inscribitur, pro aëre alto ponit, qui caelo subjectus est, in his versibus: per ego deum sublimas subices umidas, Unde oritur imber, sonitu saevo et…

sūb-ĭcĭo.opening: (less correctly ; post-Aug. sometimes ), , v. a. sub-jacio . Lit. , to throw , lay , place , or bring under or near (cf. subdo); in all senses construed with acc. and dat. , or with acc. and sub and acc.; not with sub…

sŭbĭcŭlum.opening: , a false read., Plaut. Pers. 3, 3, 14 ; v. Ritschl ad h. l.

sŭbĭdus.opening: adj , knowing , sensible , Poët. ap. Gell. 19, 9, 11 (dub.; Hertz, subitus).

sŭbĭgĭtātĭo.opening: ( ), , subigito , illicit intercourse , Plaut. Capt. cat. 2.

sŭbĭgĭtātrix.opening: ( ), , id. , she that indulges in illicit intercourse , a lascivious woman , Plaut. Pers. 2, 2, 45 .

sŭbĭgĭto.opening: ( ), , v. freq. a. sub-agito . Lit. , to lie with illicitly (ante-class.): scortum, Plaut. Mil. 3, 1, 53 (649 Ritschl): aliquam, id. ib. 5, 9 ; id. Cas. 5, 4, 2 (al. subicitare); id. Merc. 1, 2, 91 ; Ter. Heaut. 3, 3, 6…

sŭbĭgo.opening: (sūbĭgĭt, scanned with u long, Cic. poët. Div. 1, 47, 106), v. a. sub-ago , to bring under , get under; bring or get up , or up to any place. Lit. (mostly poet. ): sues antequam aestus incipiat, subigunt in umbrosum…

Sŭbĭgus.opening: subigo, I. , the tutelary god of the wedding-night , Aug. Civ. Dei , 6, 9.

sŭbimplĕo.opening: v. a. sub-impleo , to fill up , Aug. c. Epist. Manich. 22, 24.

sŭb-impŭdens.opening: adj. , somewhat shameless or impudent : saepe, Cic. Fam. 7, 17, 1 .

sŭb-ĭnānis.opening: adj. , somewhat empty or vain : quod est subinane in nobis, Cic. Att. 2, 17, 2 .

sŭb-inde.opening: adv. , a particle of time. In gen., immediately after , just after , presently , forthwith , thereupon (not ante-Aug.): primum gaudere, subinde Praeceptum auriculis hoc instillare memento, Hor. Ep. 1, 8, 15 : ager…

sŭb-indĭco.opening: v. a. , to indicate slightly , to hint at (late Lat.), Mar. Marc. Cyril. Incarn. Unigen. 31.

sŭb-indo.opening: v. a. , to subjoin , add , Aur. Vict. Orig. Rom. 3, § 7 .

sŭb-infĕro.opening: irreg. v. a. , to subjoin , add , Aug. Genes. Litt. 3, 24 ; Rutil. Lup. 1, 1 ; Vulg. 2 Pet. 1, 5.

sŭb-inflo.opening: v. a. , to puff up somewhat; pass. subinflari, Cael. Aur. Tard. 2, 4, 71 .—Rare, except in part. , somewhat puffed up or inflated (late Lat.): vultus, Cael. Aur. Acut. 1, 2 sq. : pulsus, id. ib. 1, 6 : pectus, Arn. 2,…

sŭb-inflŭo.opening: , a false read. for subterfluant, Sen. Q. N. 3, 30, 4 .

sŭb-injectus.opening: Part. [inicio], laid down upon : subinjectā manu, Sen. Contr. 3, 13 init.

sŭb-inscrībo.opening: v. a. , = παρεγγράφω , to subjoin , Rustic. c. Aceph. p. 1208 B.

sŭb-insulsus.opening: adj. , somewhat tasteless or insipid : si quid absurdum ... aut subinsulsum est, Cic. Opt. Gen. 3, 7 .

sŭb-intellĕgo.opening: v. a. , to understand or perceive a little (late Lat.), Tert. adv. Marc. 5, 3 ; Hier. Ep. 145 med. — To supply in thought, understand in addition, Aug. Trin. 6, 4 ; id. Serm. 104, 3 fin. ; Greg. M. in Job, 33, 7 al.

sŭb-intro.opening: v. n. , to go into secretly , to enter by stealth , steal into (late Lat.); trop.: populo bellicoso ludorum scenicorum subintravit insania, Aug. Civ. Dei , 1, 32; so Tert. adv. Marc. 5, 3 al.

sŭb-intrōdūco.opening: v. a. , to introduce in secret (late Lat.): eum, Aug. Ep. 137 : fratres, Vulg. Gal. 2, 4 .

sŭb-intrŏĕo.opening: v. a. , to go into , enter : subintroire speciem alicujus, Arn. 6, 198 ; Vulg. Gal. 2, 4 .

sŭbintrōmitto.opening: v. a. sub-intromitto , introduced temporarily , Facund. Defens. 9, 1 (probably an error for subintermitto).

sŭb-invĭdĕo.opening: , no perf. , , v. a. To envy a little or slightly , to be somewhat envious of (Ciceronian): subinvideo tibi, ultro te etiam arcessitum ab eo, Cic. Fam. 7, 10, 1 .—* Part. perf. , a little disliked , somewhat odious :…

sŭb-invīto.opening: v. a. , to invite slightly : aliquem, ut ad se scriberet, Cic. Fam. 7, 1, 6 .

sŭb-īrascor.opening: v. dep. n. , to be somewhat angry (Ciceronian): interdum soleo subirasci, Cic. Fin. 2, 4, 12 : brevitati litterarum, id. Fam. 11, 24, 1 : in Epirum quod me non invitas, subirascor, id. Att. 9, 7, 7 .—Hence, , , P. a. ,…

subis.opening: a kind of bird that breaks eagles' eggs , otherwise unknown, Nigid. ap. Plin. 10, 14, 17, § 37 .

sŭbĭtānĕus.opening: adj. subitus , sudden : imber, Col. 1, 6, 24 ; 2, 4, 4 ; Sen. Q. N. 7, 22, 1 ; Vulg. Sap. 17, 6 ; 17, 14 ; 19, 16 .

sŭbĭtārĭus.opening: adj. id. , done suddenly or in haste , sudden , hasty : ad eum exercitum explendum Latini Hernicique dare Quintio subitarios milites (ita tum repentina auxilia appellabant) jussi, Liv. 3, 4, 11 ; so, milites (corresp.…

sŭbĭtō.opening: adv. , v. subeo, P. a. fin.

sŭbĭtum.opening: , v. subitus, 2. s. v. subeo fin.

subjăcentia.opening: sub-jaceo , the being a subject (philos. t. t., = τὸ ὑποκεῖσθαι ): omni qualitate remotā ipsum subjacentiae solius punctum contuetur, absolute objectiveness, Rufin. Orig. Princ. 4, 1 .

sub-jăcĕo.opening: v. n. , to lie under or near any thing (post-Aug.). Lit. : feles coeunt mare stante, feminā subjacente, Plin. 10, 63, 83, § 174 : frumentum si tegulis subjaceat, id. 18, 30, 73, § 301 : fenestris subjacet vestibulum…

subjectē.opening: adv. , v. subicio, P. a. fin.

subjectĭo.opening: id. , a laying , putting , or placing under. Lit. In gen.: rerum sub aspectum paene subjectio, Cic. de Or. 3, 53, 202 : totius rei sub oculos subjectio, Gell. 10, 3, 7 ; Quint. 9, 2, 40 .— In partic. A representation ,…

subjectīvus.opening: adj. subjectus , of or belonging to the subject of a proposition, subjective : pars, i. e. the subject, App. Dogm. Plat. 3, p. 30, 30 ; Mart. Cap. 4, § 393 ; Tert. Virg. Vel. 4 fin.—Adv. : , subjectively , Mart. Cap. 4,…

subjecto.opening: (also written , Varr. R. R. 1, 52, 2 ), , v. freq. a. subicio , to lay , place , or put under ; to throw out from below (mostly poet. ; not in Cic.): manus, Ov. M. 4, 359 : acres Subjectat lasso stimulos, Hor. S. 2, 7,…

subjector.opening: id. , one who substitutes , a substitutor , forger : testamentorum, Cic. Cat. 2, 4, 7 .

subjectus.opening: subicio , a laying under (post-Aug. and very rare), Plin. 26, 15, 90, § 154 .

sub-jŭgālis.opening: adj. , accustomed to the yoke : subjugales beluae, Prud. στεφ . 10, 333.— Subst. , a beast of burden , Vulg. Matt. 21, 5 .

subjŭgātor.opening: subjugo , one who brings under the yoke , a conqueror , subjugator (post-Aug.): ORBIS TERRARVM, Inscr. Orell. 838 : malorum, App. Dogm. Plat. 2 , pp. 16, 17.

subjŭgĭus.opening: adj. sub-jugum , of or belonging to the yoke , that is attached to the yoke : lora, Cato, R. R. 135, 5 ; Vitr. 10, 3, 3 Schneid. N. cr.—Subst. : , , plur. (sc. lora), yoke-straps , Cato, R. R. 63 .

subjŭgo.opening: v. a. id. (postclass.) To bring under the yoke : decus publicum, Arn. 4, p. 129 : exercitum, Eutr. 4, 17 .— In gen., to subject , subjugate : ORBEM TERRAE ROMANO NOMINI, Inscr. Grut. 281, 2 : hostes, Claud. VI. Cons.…

subjŭgus.opening: adj. id. * That is attached to the yoke , yoked : molae machinariae subjugum aliquem dare, App. M. 7, p. 194, 29 .— , , , the name of an unknown animal : eïdem auctores subjugum, quod nec quale esset animal, nec ubi…

subjunctīvus.opening: adj. subjungo , of or belonging to binding together , connecting; in the later gram. lang., modus, the subjunctive mood , Diom. p. 331 P.; Prisc. p. 820 ib. al.: conjunctiones, e. g. si, cum, antequam, etc., Charis. p.…

subjunctōrĭum.opening: id. , a carriage drawn by animals , Cod. Th. 8, 5, 10.— = ὑποζύγιον , a beast used for draught , Ambros. Interp. Job et Dav. 2, 5, § 20.

sub-jungo.opening: ( inf. pass. subjungier, Prud. ap. Symm. 2, 586 ), v. a. , to yoke , harness (rare): curru subjungere tigres, Verg. E. 5, 29 : (juvencos) plostro, Col. 6, 2, 8 : carpento suo equas, Plin. 11, 49, 109, § 262 .— Transf. ,…

sublăbĭum.opening: sub-labium , a plant , dog's-tongue , App. Herb. 96 .

sub-lābor.opening: v. dep. n. , to fall , glide , or sink under or down , to sink ( poet. and in post-Aug. prose). Lit. : imperfecta necesse est labent et modo prodeant, modo sublabantur aut succidant, Sen. Ep. 71, § 34 : aedificia…

sub-lăbro.opening: v. a. labrum , to put into the mouth , Nov. ap. Non. 170, 8 .

sub-lăcrĭmans.opening: P. a. lacrimo , weeping a little : oculi, Veg. Vet. 1, 30 .

Sublăquĕum.opening: a little town of the Æqui , in Latium , near which Nero had a country-seat , now Subiaco , Plin. 3, 12, 17, § 109 ; Tac. A. 14, 22 .—Hence, , , adj. , of or belonging to Sublaqueum : villa, that of Nero, near…

sublātē.opening: adv. , v. tollo, P. a. fin.

sublātĭo.opening: [tollo), a lifting up , raising , elevation. Lit. : a sublatione (soni) ad positionem, an upward beat in marking time, Quint. 9, 4, 48 ; so (opp. positio) id. 9, 4, 48, § 55 .— Trop. * In gen., an elevation , exaltation…

sublātus.opening: Part. of tollo; as P. a. , v. tollo fin.

sub-lăvo.opening: v. a. , to wash from beneath (post-Aug. and rare): os vulvae vino, Cels. 6, 18, 10 : se, Capitol. M. Aur. 19 ; App. Herb. 79 .

sublectĭo.opening: sublego , a gleaning , leasing (post-class.), Tert. adv. Marc. 4, 31 med.

sublecto.opening: v. freq. a. sub-lacio , to wheedle , cajole : os, Plaut. Mil. 4, 2, 74 .

sub-lĕgo.opening: v. a. To gather from below , to gather or search for underneath , to gather up : (puer) sublegit quodcumque jaceret inutile quodque Posset cenantes offendere, Hor. S. 2, 8, 12 : baca tempestatibus in terram decidit et…

sublestus.opening: adj. acc. to Döderl. Synon. 2, p. 101 sq., perh. from sublevo; and hence, light , slight , trifling , trivial (ante-class.): sublesta antiqui dicebant infirma et tenuia, Plaut. Pers. 3, 1, 20 : fides sublestior, id est,…

sublĕvātĭo.opening: sublevo, II. B. , a lightening , alleviation ; trop.: sublevatio et medicina, Cic. Rep. 2, 34, 59 .

sub-lĕvo.opening: v. a. , to lift up from beneath , to raise up , hold up , support (class.: esp. freq. in the trop. sense; syn.: extollo, erigo). Lit. : qui nos sibi quondam ad pedes stratos ne sublevabat quidem, Cic. Att. 10, 4, 3 : in…

sublĭca.opening: a stake or pile driven into the ground, a palisade (cf.: palus, sudes, stipes), Caes. B. C. 3, 49 ; Liv. 23, 37 ; Vitr. 3, 3 .—Esp., of the piles for a bridge , Caes. B. G. 4, 17 ; 7, 35 ; Liv. 1, 37 .—In the form…

sublĭcĭus.opening: adj. sublica , consisting of or resting upon piles : Pons Sublicius, the pile-bridge , a wooden bridge across the Tiber, built by Ancus Marcius, Liv. 1, 33 ; 2, 10 ; Sen. Vit. Beat. 25, 1 ; Plin. 36, 15, 23, § 100 ;…

sublīdo.opening: v. a. sub-laedo , to press out : murmur voce, Prud. Apoth. 915 .— To injure by degrees , Vitr. 6, 8 (12), 2 dub.

sublĭgācŭlum.opening: subligo , a waistband , breech - cloth , Cic. Off. 1, 35, 129 ; cf. Non. 19, 21 .—Called subsequently , , , Mart. 3, 87, 4 ; Juv. 6, 70 ; Plin. 12, 14, 32, § 59 ; and , , , Theod. Prisc. 1, 26 .

sublĭgātĭo.opening: id. , a binding or tying below : uvarum, Pall. 1, 6, 10 .

sub-lĭgo.opening: v. a. , to bind or tie below , to bind on (mostly poet. ; not in Cic.; syn. subnecto): vites, Cato, R. R. 33, 4 ; Plin. 17, 22, 35, § 197 : lateri atque umeris ensem, Verg. A. 8, 459 : clipeum sinistrae, id. ib. 11, 11…

sublīmātĭo.opening: sublimo , a lifting up , deliverance , Alcim. Ep. 2 .

sublīmātor.opening: id. , an elevator , exalter (late Lat.): Deus est Abrahami sublimator, Salv. Gub. Dei , 1, 8.

sub-līmen.opening: adv. acc. to Ritschl, Opusc. 2, p. 464, = sublimen superum, referring to the hanging up of slaves for punishment; but acc. to Ussing ad Plaut. As. v. 859 from sublimis , on high , upwards (mostly anteclass.): facite…

sublīmis.opening: (collat. form , , um: ex sublimo vertice, Cic. poët. Tusc. 2, 7, 19; Enn. ap. Non. 169 ; Att. and Sall. ib. 489, 8 sq. ; Lucr. 1, 340 ), adj. etym. dub.; perh. sub-limen, up to the lintel; cf. sublimen (sublimem est in…

sublīmĭtas.opening: sublimis , height , loftiness (post-Aug.; cf. altitudo). Lit. : corporis, Quint. 12, 5, 5 : cellarum, Col. 8, 3, 3 : cucurbitarum, Plin. 19, 5, 24, § 69 .—In plur. : lunae, Plin. 2, 16, 13, § 68 .— Trop. In gen.:…

sublīmĭtus.opening: adv. sublimis , up high , high : pauci militum equum sublimitus insilire, Fronto Ep. ad Ver. 1 med. Mai.

sublīmo.opening: v. a. id. , to lift up on high , to raise , elevate (ante- and postclass.). Lit. : facem (sol), Enn. ap. Non. 170, 11 (Trag. v. 319 Vahl.): se nubium tenus, App. Flor. p. 340, 38 ; cf. mid.: sublimata in altum, id. M.…

sublingĭo.opening: sub-lingo , a lick-dish , under-scullion : coqui, Plaut. Ps. 3, 2, 103 .

sub-lĭno.opening: v. a. , to besmear or anoint beneath , to lay on as a groundcolor , to prime with any thing (ante-class. and post-Aug.). Lit. : chrysocollam atramento, Plin. 33, 5, 27, § 90 : caeruleum, id. 35, 6, 26, § 45 : argentum…

sub-līvĭdus.opening: adj. , somewhat blue , bluish (very rare): pustulae, Cels. 5, 28, 1 and 11 med.

sub-lūcānus.opening: adj. lux , towards day , towards morning : temporibus, Plin. 11, 12, 12, § 30 .

sub-lūcĕo.opening: v. n. , to shine a little , to gleam faintly , to glimmer ( poet. and in post - Aug. prose): aries sublucet corpore totus, Cic. Arat. 289 : crepuscula sublucent, Ov. Am. 1, 5, 5 : si fragmenta (picis), subluceant, Plin.…

sub-lūcĭdus.opening: adj. , somewhat light , lightish : lucus, App. M. 6, p. 174, 24 .

sub-lūco.opening: v. a. lux , to trim , cut away , thin out the branches of a tree, to admit light: sublucare arbores est ramos earum supputare, et veluti subtus lucem mittere, Fest. p. 348 Müll.: arbor ... nisi a domino sublucari non…

sub-lūgĕo.opening: v. n. , to lament a little , Inscr. Cenot. Pis. ap. Orell. 643.

sub-lŭo.opening: , no perf. , , v. a. , to wash or bathe underneath (very rare; not in Cic.). Lit. : aliquid aquā calidā, Cels. 4, 15 ; Col. 6, 32, 1 : inguina, Mart. 6, 81, 2 : subluto podice, id. 2, 42, 1 .— Transf. , of rivers, to…

sublustris.opening: adj. sub-lux , giving some light , having a faint light , glimmering (not ante-Aug., and very rare). Lit. : nox, Hor. C. 3, 27, 31 ; Liv. 5, 47 : umbra (noctis), Verg. A. 9, 373 ; Val. Fl. 3, 141 .— * Trop. :…

sub-lūtĕus.opening: adj. , somewhat yellow , yellowish (post-class.): color, App. Flor. p. 348, 29 : color purpurei luminis suffectione subluteus, Arn. 5, 164 .

sublŭvĭes.opening: subluo, that which is washed off , filth , dirt (post-Aug.). In gen.: via subluvie caenosā lubrica, App. M. 9, p. 221, 2 : limosa, Amm. 15, 4 .— In partic., a disease in the feet of sheep , the foul , Col. 7, 5, 11 ; so…

sub-nascor.opening: v. dep. n. , to grow up under , out of , or after; to follow after , succeed (not ante-Aug.): num vada subnatis imo viridentur ab herbis, Ov. Hal. 90 : qui (cortex) subnascente alio expellitur, Plin. 17, 24, 37, § 234 ;…

sub-năto.opening: v. n. , to swim beneath (post-Aug. and very rare): pars subnatat unda Membrorum, pars exstat aquis, Sil. 14, 482 : currus bijuges alii subnatant, App. M. 4, p. 157, 6 .

sub-nāvĭgo.opening: v. a. , to sail under the lee : Cyprum, Vulg. Act. 27, 4 (transl. of the Gr. ὑπεπλεύσαμεν ).

sub-necto.opening: v. a. , to bind or tie under , bind on beneath ( poet. and in post-Aug. prose; syn. subligo). Lit. : antennis velum, Ov. M. 11, 483 : cingula mammae, Verg. A. 1, 492 : tenui de vimine circlos Cervici, id. G. 3, 167 :…

sub-nĕgo.opening: v. a. , to half deny or refuse : quod praesenti tibi prope subnegāram, Cic. Fam. 7, 19 init.

Subnĕro.opening: sub-Nero , the second Nero , an appellation given to the emperor Domitian, on account of his crimes, Tert. Pall. 4 (cf. of the same: calvus Nero, Juv. 4, 37 ).

subnervo.opening: v. a. sub-nervus, to cut the sinew beneath , to hamstring , hough (post-class.). Taurum, Tert. adv. Jud. 10 med. : equos, Vulg. Jos. 11, 6 : jugales, id. 2 Reg. 8, 4 .—* Trop. , to invalidate , refute : calumnias, App.…

sub-nĭger.opening: adj. , somewhat black , blackish : ventriosus, subniger, Plaut. Ps. 4, 7, 120 : oculis, id. Merc. 3, 4, 55 : labris (canum), Varr. R. R. 2, 9, 3 : color (cutis), Cels. 5, 28, 4 .

sub-nixus.opening: ( ), , Part. [nitor], supported from beneath , under-propped , propped up , supported by , resting or leaning upon any thing, etc. (class., esp. in the trop. sense; cf. suffultus). Lit. : (duos circulos) caeli…

subnŏtātĭo.opening: subnoto , a signing underneath , subscription (post-class.), Cod. Just. 1, 23, 6 ; Cod. Th. 8, 5, 22; Hier. Ep. 123 .

sub-nŏto.opening: v. a. (post-Aug.). To mark , note , or write underneath (cf. subscribo): in inferiori lineā particulares propositiones subnotentur, App. Dogm. Plat. 3, p. 31, 27 : nomina palam, to write down, Suet. Calig. 41 .— Transf.…

subnŭba.opening: sub-nubo , a rival : lecti subnuba nostri, Ov. H. 6, 153 .

sub-nūbĭlus.opening: adj. , somewhat cloudy or overcast , rather gloomy : nox, * Caes. B. C. 3, 54 : limes, Ov. R. Am. 599 .

sŭbo.opening: v. n. , to be in heat. Prop. of sows, Plin. 10, 63, 83, § 181 .— Transf. Of other animals, Lucr. 4, 1199 ; App. Mag. p. 298, 22 .— Of women, Hor. Epod. 12, 11 ; Tert. Apol. 46 ; 14 ; Hier. ap. Jovin. 1, 38; 2, 36.

sŭb-obscēnus.opening: ( ), , adj. , somewhat smutty or obscene : ridiculum, Cic. Or. 26, 88 .

sŭb-obscūrus.opening: adj. , somewhat obscure; trop., of language: breves et ob eam ipsam causam interdum subobscuri, Cic. Brut. 7, 29 : ingressio, id. Or. 3, 11 : cicatrix, Vulg. Lev. 13, 21 .— Adv. : , somewhat obscurely : dixit, Gell. 10,…

sŭb-ŏcŭlāris.opening: adj. , that is beneath the eye , subocular : venae, Veg. Vet. 4, 4 .

sŭb-ŏdĭōsus.opening: adj. , somewhat vexatious or odious , Cic. Att. 1, 5, 4 .

sub-offendo.opening: v. n. , to give some offence : apud faecem populi, Cic. Q. Fr. 2, 6, 5 .

sŭb-ŏlĕo.opening: ( , pres. subj. subolat, Ter. Heaut. 5, 1, 26 ; cf. oleo init. ), , v. n. (prop. to emit a smell; only trop. and in third pers. sing. ): hoc subolet alicui, or impers. subolet (alicui), to smell , scent , perceive any…

sŭbŏles.opening: (less correctly ), , sub- 2. oleo, olesco , a sprout , shoot , offshoot , twig , spray : suboles ab olescendo, id est crescendo, ut adulescentes quoque et adultae et indoles dicitur, Fest. p. 309 Müll. Lit. (very rare;…

sŭb-ŏlesco.opening: v. inch. n. , to grow up (very rare): juventus subolescens, Liv. 29, 3 : subolescere imperio adultos ejus filios, Amm. 14, 11, 3 .

sŭb-olfăcĭo.opening: v. a. , to smell out , perceive by the scent : subolfacio, quod nobis epulum daturus est Mammea, Petr. 45, 10 .

sŭb-ŏrĭor.opening: v. dep. n. , to spring up , arise , proceed (very rare), Lucr. 1, 1036 ; 1, 1049 ; 2, 1138 : metallorum opulentia tot saeculis suboriens, Plin. 2, 93, 95, § 207 ; Arn. 3, 9 .

sŭbornātor.opening: suborno , an instigator , abettor , suborner (post-class.): subornatores ac delatores puniuntur, Paul. Sent. 5, 13 : servorum, Lampr. Commod. 19 fin. : subornatore et conscio praefecto praetorio, Amm. 15, 5 med.

sŭb-orno.opening: v. a. With the idea of the verb predominating, to fit out , furnish , provide , equip , adorn (class.; syn. instruo): aliquem pecuniā, Anton. ap. Cic. Phil. 13, 16, 32 : vigilanter nervoseque nos, qui stamus in acie,…

sŭbortus.opening: suborior , a rising or springing up , Lucr. 5, 303 .

sŭb-ostendo.opening: v. a. , to point out secretly , to show indirectly (post-class.): aliquid, Tert. adv. Marc. 4, 38 med. ; id. adv. Valent. 1 : spes adventus Domini subostensa, id. Bapt. 19 ; id. Anim. 12 .

Subota.opening: an island of the Ægean Sea , Liv. 44, 28, 6 .

sub-quartus.opening: adj. , = ὑποτέταρτος , one fourth less (late Lat.), Mart. Cap. 7, § 761 .

sub-salsus.opening: adj. , somewhat salt , brackish : aqua, Cels. 5, 12 : herba, Plin. 21, 29, 103, § 175 .

sub-sannātĭo.opening: subsanno , mockery by gestures , derision in pantomime , Vulg. Psa. 34, 16 ; 43, 14 .

subsannātor.opening: id. , one who insults or mocks by gestures , Vulg. Ecclus. 33, 6 .

sub-sanno.opening: v. a. sanna , to insult by derisive gestures , to deride , mock (late Lat.): ecce ipsi quasi subsannantes, Tert. adv. Jud. 11 med. ; Hier. Ep. 40, 2 ; Vulg. Psa. 34, 16 ; id. Isa. 37, 22 .

subsarcĭno.opening: v. a. , to repair , heal (late Lat.), Victor Funon. Poenit. 29.

sub-scalpo.opening: v. a. , to scratch or rub underneath , Mart. Cap. 1, § 7 .

sub-scrībendārĭus.opening: scribo , an under-secretary (late Lat.), Cod. Th. 7, 4, 1; 7, 84, 8 al.

sub-scrībo.opening: v. a. To write underneath or below (class.; cf. subnoto). In gen.: statuis inauratis ... subscripsit, Reges ab se in gratiam esse reductos, Cic. Clu. 36, 101 ; cf.: subscripsere quidam L. Bruti statuae: utinam viveres,…

subscriptĭo.opening: subscribo . Any thing written underneath , a subscription (class.). In gen.: Serapionis subscriptio, Cic. Att. 6, 1, 17 .— In partic. Jurid. t. t., a subscription to an accusation: si cui crimen obiciatur, praecedere…

subscriptor.opening: id. . (Acc. to subscribo, I. B. 1.) A signer or joint-signer of an accusation, Cic. Div. in Caecil. 15, 47 ; 16, 51 : venalis scriptor et subscriptor tuus, id. Dom. 19, 49 : accusatore Lentulo subscriptoribusque ejus,…

sub-scrūpōsus.opening: adj. (late Lat.), somewhat sharp or critical : examinator meritorum, Amm. 21, 16, 3 .

subscūs.opening: sub-cudo , the tongue or tenon of a dovetail : subscudes appellantur cuneatae tabellae, quibus tabulae inter se configuntur, quia, quo eae immittuntur, succuditur, Fest. p. 306 Müll.: nec ulla subscus cohibet compagem…

sub-sĕco.opening: v. a. , to cut under , cut away below; to clip , pare (rare; not in Cic.): stramentum et manipulum falce, Varr. R. R. 1, 50, 1 : herbam. id. ib. 1, 49, 1 : legumina, id. ib. 1, 23, 3 : radices, Col. 2, 9, 10 : partes,…

sub-sĕcundārĭus.opening: adj. , that comes afterwards , additional : tempora, spare time , leisure moments (with subseciva), Gell. N. A. praef. § 23.

subsentātor.opening: sub-sentio, formed after the analogy of assentator , a flatterer , fawner : subdoli, Plaut. Fragm. ap. Front. Ep. ad M. Caes. 2, 13, p. 62 Nieb.

sub-sentĭo.opening: v. a. , to notice or perceive secretly , to smell out : etsi subsensi id quoque, Illos ibi esse, Ter. Heaut. 3, 1, 62 .

subsĕquĭum.opening: sub-sequor , the sequel , what follows after (late Lat.), Cassiod. in Psa. 9, 5 .

sub-sĕquor.opening: v. n. and a. , to follow close after or immediately; to follow , succeed , ensue (class.). Lit. With acc. : subsequor te, Plaut. Am. 2, 1, 1 ; cf. id. ib. 1, 3, 52 ; id. Bacch. 4, 4, 72 : has (cohortes) subsidiariae…

subsĕquus.opening: or , , adj. subsequor , following , succeeding (late Lat.); form subsequus: probatio, Oros. 1, 1 ; form subsicuus: metus, Jul. Val. Rer. Gest. Alex. 2, 21 fin.

sub-sērĭcus.opening: adj. , half-silken : vestis, Lampr. Heliog. 26 ; Gall. ap. Treb. Claud. 17 ; Vop. Aur. 15, 4 .

sub-sĕro.opening: , no perf. , , v. a. , to put or insert under (late Lat.). * Lit. : subsertis manibus, App. M. 7, p. 200, 23 .— Trop. : res monuit super Eutherio pauca subserere, to add, subjoin, Amm. 16, 7, 4 ; 14, 11, 3 .

sub-servĭo.opening: v. n. , to be subject to , to serve (ante-class.). Lit. : istaec, quae viros subservire Sibi postulant, Plaut. Men. 5, 2, 14 ; Naev. ap. Front. Ep. 2, 13, p. 62 Nieb. (Com. Rel. p. 22 Rib.).—* Trop. , to comply with ,…

subsessa.opening: subsido , an ambush , ambuscade (post-class.): subsessas occultius collocare, Veg. Mil. 3, 6 med. : in subsessā esse, id. ib. 3, 22 ; cf.: hostium dolos subsessas vocamus, Serv. Verg. A. 11, 268 .

subsessor.opening: id. , a waylayer , lier-in-wait (post-Aug.). Lit. : subsessores vocantur, qui occisuri aliquem delitescunt, Serv. Verg. A. 11, 268 ; cf. id. ib. 5, 498 : subsessores cum venabulis, Petr. 40, 1 .— Trop. : alieni…

subsĭcīvus.opening: , less correctly (also transp. or ), , adj. [sub-seco). Lit. , as t. t. of the agrimensores, that is cut off and left remaining , in surveying lands.— Subst. : , , , a remainder or small patch of land , etc.: subsiciva,…

subsīdentĭa.opening: subsido , a sinking down , subsidence; concr., a settling , sediment : aquarum, Vitr. 8, 3 med.

subsĭdĭālis.opening: adj. subsidium , of or belonging to a reserve , subsidiary (late Lat. for the class. subsidiarius): acies, Amm. 14, 6, 17 : manus, id. 27, 10, 15 .

subsĭdĭārĭus.opening: adj. id. ; in milit. lang., of or belonging to a reserve , reserve- , subsidiary. Lit. Adj. (class.): cohortes, Caes. B. C. 1, 83 ; Liv. 9, 27 ; Tac. A. 1, 63 : acies, Auct. B. Afr. 59, 2: naves, Auct. B. Alex. 14, 3.—…

subsĭdĭor.opening: v. dep. n. [id.], to act as a reserve , stand in reserve , Hirt. B. G. 8, 13, 2 .

subsĭdĭum.opening: subsideo . Milit. t. t. Orig., the troops stationed in reserve in the third line of battle (behind the principes), the line of reserve , reserve-ranks , triarii : subsidium dicebatur, quando milites subsidebant in…

sub-sīdo.grammar: sēdi, sessum, 3 v. n. and a.
sub-sīdo.opening: (collat. form acc. to 2d conj., subsīdent, Luc. 1, 646 ; Amm. 28, 4, 22 ), v. n. and a. Neutr. , to sit down , crouch down , squat; to set one's self down , settle down , sink down (class.). Lit. In gen.: agite nunc,…

subsĭdŭus.opening: adj. subsideo , sinking down , settling : fraces, Grat. Cyn. 474 .

subsignānus.opening: adj. sub-signum , that is or serves under the standard : miles, a kind of legionary soldiers kept in reserve to strengthen the centre, Tac. H. 1, 70 fin. ; 4, 33 ; Amm. 29, 5, 23 .

subsignātĭo.opening: subsigno , a subscription , signature. * Lit. : veteres subsignationis verbo pro subscriptione uti solebant, Dig. 50, 16, 39 .—* Trop. , a firm promise , assurance : poenitentiae, Tert. Poen. 2 med.

sub-signo.opening: v. a. , to mark or write beneath , to undersign , subscribe (mostly post - Aug.; syn. subscribo). Lit. : traditas notas subsignabimus Catonis maxime verbis, Plin. 18, 6, 7, § 33 : Ciceronis sententiam ipsius verbis, id.…

sub-sĭlĭo.opening: v. n. salio , to spring upwards , leap up (mostly poet. ; not in Cic.). Lit. : decido de lecto praeceps, subsilit, Plaut. Cas. 5, 2, 50 ; cf. id. Curc. 1, 2, 64 : non subsilis ac plaudis? Varr. ap. Non. 135, 28 : semper…

subsilles.opening: , Paul. ex Fest. p. 307 Müll.; cf. Fest. p. 306 ib.

sub-sĭmĭlis.opening: adj. , somewhat like , partly similar (very rare): Μελίκηρα melli albo subsimilis, Cels. 5, 26, 20 : subsimile aliquid, Dig. 35, 3, 1 med.

sub-sīmus.opening: adj. , with a nose slightly turned up , somewhat snub-nosed or pug-nosed : boves, Varr. R. R. 2, 5, 7 .

subsistentia.opening: subsisto , = ὑπὀστασις , the substance , reality , Cassiod. Hist. Eccl. 5, 38 ; 9, 3 ; 12, 4 fin. ; Boëth. Duab. Nat. p. 950.

sub-sisto.opening: v. n. and a. Neutr. , to take a stand or position , to stand still , remain standing; to stop , halt. Lit. In gen.: reliqui in itinere substiterant, Caes. B. C. 2, 41 : in locis campestribus, id. ib. 1, 79 : in eodem…

sub-sĭtus.opening: adj. , lying or situated below : convallis, App. M. 6, p. 174, 24 .

subsŏlānĕŭs.opening: adj. sub-solum , underground , from under the earth : subsolaneae res, Fest. p. 306 Müll.

sub-sōlānus.opening: adj. , lying beneath the sun , eastern , oriental (post-Aug.): montes, Plin. 7, 2, 2, § 24 .—As subst. : , , (sc. ventus), the east wind , Sen. Q. N. 5, 16, 4 ; Plin. 2, 47, 46, § 119 ; Gell. 2, 22, 8 ; plur. :…

sub-sŏno.opening: v. a. , to express secretly , to hint , intimate : quanti pretii (dentur), Sisenn. ap. Charis. p. 175 P.

sub-sortĭor.opening: v. a. , jurid. t. t., to choose by lot as a substitute , sc. a judge in place of one rejected by the parties: judicem, Cic. Clu. 35, 96 .— Absol. : subsortiemur etiam in M. Metelli locum, Cic. Verr. 1, 10, 30 .— Part.…

subsortītĭo.opening: subsortior , a choosing of substitutes by lot , sc. of other judges in place of those rejected by the parties, Cic. Verr. 2, 1, 61, § 157 ; id. Clu. 33, 91 ; a selection of citizens to receive corn in place of those who…

sub-spargo.opening: v. n. , to scatter under : semina versutiis haereticorum, Tert. Res. Carn. 63 fin.

subspissus.opening: adj. sub-spissus , thickish , medic. t. t.: pleureticorum pulsus, Ps.-Soran. Puls. p. 279.

sub-stāmen.opening: the woof or weft in weaving (late Lat.), Vet. Schol. Juv. 2, 66 .

substantĭa.opening: substo , that of which a thing consists , the being , essence , contents , material , substance (post - Aug.): hominis, Quint. 7, 2, 5 : rerum, id. 2, 21, 1 : placidae et altae mentis, id. 6, prooem. § 7 : rhetorices,…

substantĭālis.opening: adj. substantia . Lit. , of or belonging to the essence or substance , essential , substantial (post - class.): differentia, Tert. Res. Carn. 45 fin. — Transf. , substantial , substantive : potestates, i. e. spirits,…

substantĭālĭtas.opening: substantialis , the quality of being substantial or essential , Hier. in Didym. Spir. Sanc. 15 ; Cassiod. Hist. Eccl. 7, 14 .

substantĭŏla.opening: dim. substantia , a little substance , a small property (late Lat.): paterna et materna, Hier. Ep. 108, 26 : tenuis, id. ib. 125, 16 .

substantīvālis.opening: adj. substantivus , substantive , substantial : forma, Tert. adv. Val. 27 fin.

substantīvus.opening: adj. substantia , self-existent , substantive (post - class.). In gen.: res, Tert. adv. Prax. 26 ; id. adv. Hermog. 26 .— In gram.: substantivum verbum, the substantive verb , i.e. sum (a transl. of the Gr. ὑπαρκτικόν…

sub-sterno.opening: v. a. , to strew , scatter , spread , or lay under or beneath (class.; cf. subicio). Lit. : segetem ovibus, Cato, R. R. 37, 2 : verbenas, Ter. And. 4, 3, 12 : casias et nardi lenis aristas, Ov. M. 15, 398 ; Plin. 20,…

substillus.opening: adj. sub - stillo (ante- and post - class.), slightly dropping , dribbling. Adj. : lotium, i. e. strangury, Cato, R. R. 156, 6 .— Subst. : , , , a slight dropping , a sprinkling : substillum tempus ante pluviam jam…

sub-stĭtŭo.opening: v. a. statuo . To set , put , place , or lay under , to set or place next to any thing (so rare and mostly post - Aug.). Lit. : lapides plantae, Pall. Mart. 10, 22 : post elephantos armaturas leves, Hirt. B. Afr. 59, 3…

substĭtūtĭo.opening: substituo, II. . In gen., a putting in the place of another , substitution , Arn. 3, p. 104 .— In partic., in jurid. lang., the appointment of a second or alternate heir , Gai. Inst. 2, § 174 sq. ; Dig. 28, tit. 6 .

substĭtūtīvus.opening: adj. substituo , conditional : propositio, App. Dogm. Plat. 3, p. 29, 36 .

sub-sto.opening: v. n. To stand or be under or among , to be present (very rare; not in Cic.): si pure substante non rumpuntur hi tumores, Cels. 6, 10 med. : nullo dolore substante, id. 2, 7 med. ; 2, 12, 2 .— * To stand firm , hold out…

sub-stŏmăchans.opening: Part. [stomachor], somewhat angry or vexed : taedio, Aug. Conf. 3, 12 .

substrāmen.opening: substerno , what is strewn under , litter : molle, Varr. R. R. 3, 10, 4 ; 3, 6, 5 ; 3, 9, 8 .— Transf. , supports : lubrica roboreis aderant substramina plaustris, i. e. rollers, Sil. 12, 444 .

substrāmentum.opening: id. , litter , = substramen, Cato, R. R. 161, 2 (al. sub stramentis).

substrātus.opening: substerno , a spreading or laying under; only in abl. sing. , Plin. 24, 9, 38, § 61 .

sub-strĕpens.opening: Part. [strepo], just sounding , just uttering , gasping : verba, App. M. 5, p. 166 fin.

sub-strictus.opening: Part. and P. a. of substringo.

sub-strīdens.opening: Part. [strido], grating or gnashing somewhat , Amm. 16, 4, 2 .

sub-stringo.opening: v. a. , to bind beneath; to bind , tie , or draw up ( poet. and in post-Aug. prose; syn. subligo). Lit. : crinem nodo, Tac. G. 38 : ligatas auro comas, Luc. 3, 281 : sinus, Sen. Troad. 88 : lintea malo, Sil. 1, 689 :…

substructĭo.opening: substruo , an under - building , foundation , substructure , Vitr. 1, 5 : maxima debet esse cura substructionum, id. 6, 11 : maximae, Caes. B. C. 2, 25 : insanae, Cic. Mil. 20, 53 ; 31, 85 ; Liv. 38, 28 ; Front. Aquaed.…

sub-strŭo.opening: v. a. , to build beneath , to underbuild , lay; lit.: fundamentum, Plaut. Most. 1, 2, 40 : intervalla montium, Vitr. 8, 7 med. ; cf.: intervalla substructis canalibus junguntur, Plin. 33, 4, 21, § 74 : locus…

subsultim.opening: adv. subsilio , with leaps or jumps. decurrere, Suet. Aug. 83 .

subsulto.opening: v. freq. n. [id.], to spring up , to leap , jump , hop (rare; not in Cic.). Lit. , Plaut. Cas. 2, 7, 10 : tu subsultas, ego miser vix asto, id. Capt. 3, 4, 104 .— Trop. : ne sermo subsultet imparibus spatiis, Quint. 11,…

sub-sum.opening: , no perf. , , v. n. , to be under , among , or behind; to be near , close , or at hand (class.): ubi non subest, quo praecipitet ac decidat, there is nothing underneath, Cic. Rep. 1, 45, 69 ; Lucr. 3, 873 ; cf. id. 4,…

sub-summo.opening: v. a. sub-summa , to sum up , to multiply (late Lat.), Primas in Apoc. V. 21.

sub-surdus.opening: adj. , somewhat deaf : vox, indistinct, Quint. 11, 3, 32 Halm. (al. surda).

subsūtūra.opening: sub-suo , the hem of a garment, Edict. Diocl. 7, n. c. 49.

sub-sūtus.opening: Part. [suo], sewn beneath or at the lower part : vestis, trimmed , edged , or fringed at the bottom , Hor. S. 1, 2, 29 .

sub-tābĭdus.opening: adj. , somewhat shrunken : stetit subtabidus, Amm. 26, 6, 15 .

sub-tăcĭtus.opening: adj. , somewhat still , silent : secta, Prud. Ham. 174 .

sub-tālāris.opening: adj. sub-talus , lying under the heel : calcei, Isid. Orig. 19, 34, 7 .

subtectĭo.opening: sub-tego , a covering (late Lat.), Aug. Quaest. in Heptat. 2, 177, 15 .

sub-tĕgo.opening: v. a. , to cover underneath : caelum, Amm. 19, 7, 3 (al. sub-texunt); Vitr. 9, 9 : aëra ipsum subtexisse jaculis, Jul. Val. Rer. Gest. Alex. 2, 4 : sub avis caudā pedes equi sunt subtecti, Vitr. 9, 9 : subtecto nubibus…

sub-tĕgŭlānĕus.opening: adj. tegula , that is under the roof , = in-doors : pavimenta, Plin. 36, 25, 61, § 185 .

subtel.opening: τὸ κοῖλον τοῦ ποδός , the hollow of the foot , Prisc. p. 644 P. [sub-talus].

subtēmen.opening: ( ), , contr. from subteximen, subtecmen, from sub-texo , that which is wrought or woven in , the woof , weft of a web: inseritur medium radiis subtemen acutis, etc., Ov. M. 6, 56 ; Varr. L. L. 5, § 113 Müll.; Verg. A.…

sub-tendo.opening: , no perf. , , v. a. and n. Act. , to stretch underneath : lectos loris, Cato, R. R. 10, 5 ; 10, 25 .—* Neutr. , to extend underneath : linea, Front. Expos. Form. p. 32 Goes.

sub-tĕnĕo.opening: v. a. , to hold underneath : vinaceos lectos cestibus subtento (contr. for subteneto), Cato, R. R. 25 Schneid. N. cr.

sub-tĕnŭis.opening: adj. , rather thin , thinnish : setae, Varr. R. R. 2, 7, 5 .

subter.opening: (also ), adv. and prep. sub . Adv. , below , beneath , underneath : navem in fugam transdunt subter saxa, Att. ap. Non. 155, 8 (Trag. Rel. v. 630 Rib.): terram fac ut esse rearis Subter item, ut supera, Lucr. 6, 537 :…

subtĕr-actus.opening: Part. [ago], driven below or underneath : subteractis quasi radicibus, Cels. 5, 28, 1 .

subter-ănhēlo.opening: v. n. , to pant or gasp beneath , Stat. S. 1, 1, 56 .

subter-căvātus.opening: Part. [cavo], hollowed out underneath , Sol. 2 fin.

subter-currens.opening: Part. , moving underneath : basim Vergiliarum, Vitr. 9, 6 .

subter-cŭtānĕus.opening: adj. cutis , that is beneath the skin , subcutaneous (post-class.): morbus, the dropsy, Aur. Vict. Epit. 14 fin. : umor, Veg. Vet. 3, 2, 18 .

subter-dūco.opening: v. a. , to carry off secretly , to steal away any thing (Plautin.): ne tibi clam se subterducat istinc, Plaut. Mil. 2, 3, 72 : si huic occasioni tempus sese subterduxerit, id. As. 2, 2, 12 .

subter-flŭo.opening: v. n. , to flow beneath (post-Aug. and very rare). Lit. : amnis sub montes subterfluens, Vitr. 8, 2 med. : torrente subterfluente, Plin. 8, 50, 76, § 201 : aquae, Sen. Q. N. 3, 30, 4 , acc. to Fickert and Haase (not…

subter-fŭgĭo.opening: v. n. and a. Neutr. , to flee secretly or by stealth , to get off (so very rare): subterfugisse sic mihi hodie Chrysalum, Plaut. Bacch. 4, 6, 2 ; Dig. 42, 6, 20 .— Act. , to escape , evade , avoid , shun (class.; a…

subterfŭgĭum.opening: subterfugio , a subterfuge : Nestorianorum, Facund. Defens. 1, 3.

subter-fundo.opening: v. a. , to found or establish beneath : terram, Lact. 2, 8, 52 .

subtĕr-insĕro.opening: v. a. , to insert , Aldh. Sept. col. 219, t. 89 med.

subtĕr-intendo.opening: v. a. , to look askance , = ὑποβλέπειν (Appul.), Polem. Physiogn. p. 126.

subtĕrĭor.opening: comp. [subter], that is farther beneath , lower , = inferior (late Lat.): termini, Innoc. Cas. Lit. p. 232 Goes.: per subteriora, Aem. Mac. 2, 13 .—Hence, adv. : , lower , farther down : subterius nigro, superius mineo,…

subter-jăcĕo.opening: v. n. , to lie under any thing: hic gens ardentem caeli subterjacet axem, Alcim. 1, 196 .

subter-jăcĭo.opening: v. a. , to throw under any thing: hordei grana, Pall. Febr. 18, 1 .

subter-lābor.opening: v. dep. n. Lit. , to glide or flow under (mostly poet. ): fluctus Sicanos, Verg. E. 10, 4 : flumina subterlabentia muros, flowing close by, id. G. 2, 157 : subterlabens Mosella, Aus. Idyll. 10, 21 .— Transf. , to slip…

subter-lĭno.opening: v. a. , to anoint underneath : plantas aegri, Plin. 28, 7, 23, § 83 .

subter-lŭo.opening: v. a. , to wash beneath , flow underneath : gurgite sidereo subterluit Oriona, Claud. VI. Cons. Hon. 177 .

subterlŭvĭo.opening: subterluo , a washing beneath , washing away : loca umoris assidui subterluvione cadentia, Claud. Mam. Stat. An. 1, 2 .

subter-mĕo.opening: v. n. , to pass beneath : pontes rapido aestu, Claud. Idyll. 6, 61 .

subter-mitto.opening: v. a. , to place underneath , Aug. Quaest. in Heptat. 2, 177, 14 .

subter-mŏvĕo.opening: v. a. , to push under , Isid. 16, 4, 2 .

subter-nătans.opening: Part. [nato], swimming under any thing, Sol. 32, 26 .

subternus.opening: adj. subter , that is underneath , lower , = infernus (post-class.): antra, Prud. adv. Symm. 1, 392 : nox, id. Hamart. 930 .

sub-tĕro.opening: v. a. , to rub off or wear away underneath; to rub , bruise , or grind to pieces (rare; not in Cic.): boves ne pedes subterant, Cato, R. R. 72 ; so, pedes, Col. 6, 15, 2 ; Plin. 28, 16, 62, § 221 : ungulas, Plaut. As.…

subter-pendens.opening: Part. [pendeo], hanging down : mala, Pall. Mart. 10, 8 .

sub-terrānĕus.opening: adj. terra , underground , subterranean (class.): specus, Cic. Att. 15, 26, 4 ; cf.: supterraneos specus aperire, Tac. G. 16 : ergastulum, Col. 1, 6, 3 : structura, Plin. 36, 22, 50, § 170 : regna, Juv. 2, 149 :…

sub-terrēnus.opening: adj. id. , underground , subterrene , = subterraneus: plagae orbis, App. M. 9, p. 227, 27 .

sub-terrĕus.opening: adj. id. , underground , subterranean , = subterraneus: divi, Arn. 7, 226 .

subter-sĕco.opening: v. a. , to cut , divide , separate underneath : medium Capricornum, Cic. Arat. 273 .

subter-sterno.opening: v. a. , to spread under , strew under : aëra jaculis et sagittis, Jul. Val. Rer. Gest. Alex. 2, 17 .

subter-tĕnŭo.opening: v. a. , to make thin below or at the lower part : anulum, Lucr. 1, 312 (Lachm. subter tenuatur).

sub-tertĭus.opening: adj. , of a number, less by a third of itself (i. e. that bears to another the ratio of 3 to 4), a transl. of the Gr. ὑπότριτος : numerus, Mart. Cap. 7, § 761 .

subter-văcans.opening: Part. [vaco], empty below; locus, Sen. Q. N. 6, 25, 1 .

subter-vŏlo.opening: v. n. , to fly beneath : fragor subtervolat astra, Stat. Th. 3, 669 (al. subter volat).

sub-texo.opening: v. a. , to weave under or below any thing; hence, to join on , fasten , affix (mostly poet. and in post-Aug. prose; not in Cic.). Lit. (very rare): lunam alutae, Juv. 7, 192 .— Poet. : patrio capiti nubes, i. e. soli,…

subtīlĭlŏquentĭa.opening: subtililoquus , fine or elegant language , Tert. adv. Marc. 5, 19 med.

subtīlĭlŏquus.opening: adj. subtilisloquor , speaking finely or elegantly , Tert. adv. Marc. 5, 19 med.

subtīlis.opening: adj. sub-tela; and therefore, prop., woven fine; hence , fine , not thick or coarse , thin , slender , minute (syn. tenuis). Lit. (mostly poet. and in postAug. prose; not in Cic.): quae vulgo volitant subtili praedita…

subtīlĭtas.opening: ( ), , subtilis , fineness , thinness , slenderness , minuteness (syn. tenuitas). Lit. (mostly post-Aug.; not in Cic.): linearum, Plin. 35, 10, 36, § 82 : ferramentorum, the keen edge, sharpness, id. 28, 9, 41, § 148 :…

sub-tĭmĕo.opening: v. n. , to be somewhat afraid , to fear a little : numquid subtimes, ne? etc., Cic. Phil. 2, 14, 36 .

sub-tinnĭo.opening: v. n. , to sound a little , to tinkle , Tert. Pall. 4 med.

sub-tĭtŭbo.opening: v. n. , to stagger , totter , or waver a little (late Lat.). Lit. : pede subtitubo, Ven. Vit. S. Mart. 2, 475 . — Trop. : subtitubante fide, Prud. Apoth. 651 .

subtractĭo.opening: subtraho , a drawing back , Vulg. Ep. ad Hebr. 10, 39 (transl. of the Gr. ὑποστολή ).

sub-trăho.opening: v. a. , to draw away from underneath or by stealth; also, in gen., to draw off , carry off , withdraw , take away , remove , etc. (class.; syn. subduco). Lit. : subtractus Numida mortuo superincubanti Romano vivus, Liv.…

sub-triplus.opening: adj. , contained three times in a larger number, Boëth. Inst. Arith. 1, 23 .

sub-tristis.opening: adj. , somewhat sad or sorrowful (ante- and post-class.): subtristis visus est mihi, Ter. And. 2, 6, 16 ; Hier. Ep. 107, 9 .— Comp. : cera subtristior, Hier. Ep. 60, 1 .

subtŭnĭcālis.opening: sub-tunica , = ὑποδύτης, the under-garment of a Jewish priest , Hier. Ep. 29, 4 .

sub-turpĭcŭlus.opening: adj. , somewhat mean or disgraceful , Cic. Att. 4, 5, 1 .

sub-turpis.opening: adj. , somewhat mean or disgraceful : quae sint, quod ridiculi proprium est, subturpia, Cic. de Or. 2, 66, 264 .

subtus.opening: adv. from sub; like intus, from in , below , beneath , underneath (mostly ante-class.; not in Cic. or Cæs.): subtus ambulare, Cato, R. R. 48, 2 : labra subtus pendula, Varr. R. R. 2, 9, 3 : Romani aggere et vineis et…

sub-tussĭo.opening: v. n. , to cough slightly , Veg. Vet. 3, 25 dub.

sub-tūsus.opening: Part. [tundo], somewhat bruised : flet teneras subtusa genas, Tib. 1, 10, 55 : angulus, an obtuse angle , Boëth. Geom. 1, p. 1180.

sŭbūcŭla.opening: sub - UO; whence exuo . A man ' s under-garment , a shirt : postea quam binas tunicas habere coeperunt, instituerunt vocare subuculam et indusium, Varr. ap. Non. 542, 24 ; id. L. L. 5, § 131 Müll.; Hor. Ep. 1, 1, 95 ;…

sūbŭla.opening: Lit. , an awl , Mart. 3, 16, 2 : aënea, Col. 6, 5, 4 ; Pall. Jun. 14, 3 : perforabit aurem ejus subulā, Vulg. Exod. 21, 6 ; id. Deut. 15, 17 . — Transf. , a very small weapon : subulā armatus, Sen. Ep. 85, 1 ; cf.…

sŭbulcus.opening: from sus; formed in analogy with bubulcus , a swine-herd , Varr. R. R. 2, 4, 14 and 20; Mart. 10, 98, 10 ; Verg. E. 10, 19 Wagn. (al. bubulci).

sūbŭlo.opening: A flute-player , the Tuscan name for tibicen: subulo Tusce tibicen dicitur. Itaque Ennius: Subulo quondam marinas propter astabat plagas, Fest. p. 309 Müll.; cf. Varr. L. L. 7, § 35 ib. (Sat. v. 41 Vahl.).— A kind of…

Sūbŭlo.opening: 1. subulo , a Roman surname; e. g. P. Decius Subulo, Liv. 43, 17 .

sŭb-umbĭlīcus.opening: the parts below the navel , Hier. in Zach. 1 ad 2, 18.

sŭb-unctĭo.opening: a rubbing in : faucium, Cael. Aur. Acut. 3, 3, 22 .

Sŭbur.opening: a town in Spain , on the river Rubricatus , perh. the mod. Villa Nuova, in Castile, Mel. 2, 6 ; Plin. 3, 3, 4, § 21 .—Hence, , , , the inhabitants of Subur , Inscr. Grut. 414, 3 .

Sŭbūra.opening: (abbrev. SVG.; v. infra ), , a quarter in Rome , in the second region , between the Esquiline , Viminal , and Quirinal , where provisions were sold , and where many prostitutes dwelt : Subura Junius scribit ab eo, quod…

sŭburbānĭtas.opening: suburbanus , nearness to the city of Rome : suburbanitas hujusce provinciae (Siciliae), * Cic. Verr. 2, 2, 3, § 7 ; Symm. Ep. 2, 22 ; Sid. Ep. 7, 2 med.

sŭb-urbānus.opening: adj. , situated near the city of Rome , suburban. Adj. : rus suburbanum, Cic. Rosc. Am. 46, 133 : fundus, id. Q. Fr. 3, 1, 3, § 9 : ager, id. Div. 2, 32, 69 : gymnasium, id. de Or. 1, 21, 98 : regio Italiae, Col. 11, 2,…

sŭb-urbĭcārĭus.opening: adj. , late jurid. Lat. for suburbanus, situated near Rome , suburban : regiones, Cod. Th. 11, 1, 9; 11, 28, 12; 11, 16, 12: mare, Schol. Juv. 5, 94 .

sub-urbĭum.opening: urbs , a suburb : in suburbium ire, Cic. Phil. 12, 10, 24 .

sŭb-urgĕo.opening: (also written ), , v. a. , to drive or urge close to : proram ad saxa, Verg. A. 5, 202 .

sŭb-ūro.opening: , no perf. , , v. a. , to burn slightly , to singe , scorch : crura nuce ardenti, Suet. Aug. 68 : subustum corpus, Paul. Nol. Carm. 7, 37 .

sŭbustĭo.opening: suburo , a heating from below : thermarum, Cod. Th. 15, 1, 32.

subvădes.opening: sub-vas , sub-sureties , i. e. those who give surety for the bail , Auct. ap. Gell. 16, 10, 8 .

subvectĭo.opening: subveho , a carrying , transporting , conveying , conveyance : frumenti, Liv. 44, 8 ; Tac. A. 13, 51 fin. — Plur. : durae subvectiones, Caes. B. G. 7, 10 : marinae, Vitr. 1, 5, 1 .

subvecto.opening: v. freq. a. id. , to bring up from below (on the shoulder, by ship, etc.), to bring , carry , convey , transport to a place ( poet. and in post-Aug. prose): asini, qui tibi subvectabant rure huc virgas ulmeas, Plaut.…

subvector.opening: subveho , a bearer , carrier , conveyer : Bosporus Inachiae subvector virginis olim, Avien. Perieg. 199 .

subvectus.opening: subveho , a carrying , conveying , conveyance , Tac. A. 15, 4 ; Cassiod. Hist. Eccl. 5, 17 .

sub-vĕho.opening: v. a. , to bring up from below (on the shoulder, by ship, etc.), to bring , carry , convey , conduct to a place, to bring or carry up stream , etc. (not freq. till after the Aug. per.; not in Cic.): ast alium (aërem…

sub-vello.opening: , no perf. , vulsum (volsum), , v. a. , to pluck up , pull out (only in the two foll. passages): rador, subvellor, desquamor, Lucil. ap. Non. 95, 15 : qui barba volsa feminibusque subvolsis ambulet, Scip. Afric. ap.…

sub-vēlo.opening: v. a. , to overshadow , Aug. Lib. Arb. 2, 38 .

sub-vĕnĭo.opening: (old fut. subvenibo, Plaut. Men. 5, 7, 20 ), v. n. , to come up or advance to one ' s assistance (the figure taken from the advance of a military reserve; v. subsidium), to come to one ' s assistance , to aid , assist ,…

subventĭo.opening: subvenio , a rendering aid , assistance , Cassiod. Var. 12, 28 .

subvento.opening: v. freq. n. [id.], to come with assistance to one: spes bona, opsecro, subventa mihi, Plaut. Rud. 1, 4, 11 .

subventor.opening: id. , one who comes in aid , a helper : CIVIVM, Inscr. Orell. 6 : POPVLI, ib. 3766 .

subventrālis.opening: adj. sub-venter , subventral , med. t. t., Ps. - Soran. Quaest. Med. 235.

sub-ventrīle.opening: id. , the lower belly , the abdomen (late Lat.), Marc. Emp. 28 fin. ; cf.: ὑποκοίλιον, sumen, subventrile, Gloss. Philox.

subverbustus.opening: adj. perhaps contr. from sub verubus ustus , branded under the spear , an epithet of a male or female slave (ante- and post-class.): subverbustam veribus ustam significat Plautus cum ait: ulcerosam, compeditam,…

sub-vĕrĕor.opening: v. dep. n. , to be somewhat fearful or apprehensive : subvereri ne te delectet, etc., Cic. Fam. 4, 10, 1 .

subversĭo.opening: subverto , an overturn , overthrow , ruin , destruction (late Lat.): humani generis, Arn. 1, 7 : urbium, Vulg. Gen. 19, 29 .— Plur. : animorum, Arn. 5, 165 .

subverso.opening: ( ), , v. freq. a. id. , to overturn , overthrow , ruin , Plaut. Curc. 4, 1, 23 .

subversor.opening: id. , an overturner , overthrower , subverter (very rare): legum (opp. auctor), Tac. A. 3, 28 : naturae (diabolus), Alcim. 2, 75 .

sub-verto.opening: ( ), , v. a. , to turn upside down; to upset , overturn , overthrow (not in Cic. or Cæs.). Lit. : lupinum aratro, Col. 11, 2, 44 : mensam, Suet. Ner. 47 : statuas, id. Calig. 34 : tantas operum moles, Ov. F. 6, 645 :…

sub-vestĭo.opening: v. a. , to clothe from beneath , clothe by degrees : et nova subvestit reparatas pluma volucres, Dracont. 1, 642 .

subvexus.opening: adj. subveho , sloping upwards (opp. devexus): omnia fastigio leni subvexa, Liv. 25, 36 .

sub-vĭrĭdis.opening: adj. , somewhat green , greenish : folia, Plin. 25, 9, 65, § 113 : balanitae, id. 37, 10, 55, § 149 : emplastrum, Scrib. Comp. 201 and 202.

sub-vŏlo.opening: v. n. , to fly up or upwards (rare but class.): hae (partes corporum) sursum in caelestem locum subvo lent, Cic. Tusc. 1, 17, 40 : avis, Ov. M. 11, 790 : ex agmine, id. ib. 14, 507 : praepes, id. ib. 14, 577 : ad…

sub-volvo.opening: v. a. , to roll up or along : manibus saxa, Verg. A. 1, 424 .

sub-vultŭrĭus.opening: adj. , somewhat vulture-like , a facetiously formed word: corpus, Plaut. Rud. 2, 4, 9 .

Sucasīni.opening: ( ), , , a surname of the Interamnates on the Liris in Latium , Plin. 3, 5, 9, § 64 .

suc-caelestis.opening: ( ), , adj. , that which is under the heavens , subcelestial , sublunary : hebdomas, Tert. adv. Val. 31 .

suc-caerŭlĕus.opening: ( ), , adj. , somewhat blue , bluish : creta, Cels. 6, 5 fin.

suc-candĭdus.opening: ( ), , adj. , somewhat white , whitish (Plinian): folia, Plin. 27, 8, 39, § 61 ; 27, 12, 94, § 120 .

suc-căvus.opening: ( ), , adj. , hollow below or underneath (ante- and postclass.): areae, Cato, R. R. 151, 3 : loca, Lucr. 6, 557 ; Auct. Limit. pp. 252, 260, 303 Goes.: natura Aetnae, Lucr. 6, 682 .

succēdānĕus.opening: or (on the latter very ancient orthog. cf. Gell. 4, 6, 4 sq. ), , adj. succedo , that follows after or succeeds to something, that supplies the place of something, substituted , succedaneous : hostia, quae ad aras…

suc-cēdo.grammar: cessi, cessum, 3 v. n. and a.
suc-cēdo.opening: v. n. and a. [sub]. To go below or under (so mostly poet. ; syn. subeo). Lit. In gen., to enter , go under , come under : simul ac primum nubes succedere soli Coepere, to go under the sun, Lucr. 5, 286 ; cf. id. 6, 402…

suc-cendo.opening: v. a. sub-candeo; v. accendo , to kindle or set on fire from below (syn. inflammo). Lit. (class.): (sapiens) etiamsi in Phalaridis tauro inclusus succensis ignibus torreatur, Cic. Pis. 18, 42 : aggerem cuniculo hostes…

suc-cēno.opening: ( , ), , v. a. , to eat below , dine underneath : Galba de piscibus, qui cum pridie ex parte adesi et versati postero die appositi essent, Festinemus, alii subscenant, inquit, Quint. 6, 3, 90 Spald. N. cr.

succensĕo.opening: and , , v. n. succensus, from succendo , to be inflamed with anger , to be angry , irritated , enraged (class.; syn.: irascor, indignor). With dat. : hominibus irasci et succensere, Cic. Rosc. Com. 16, 46 : neque illi…

succensĭo.opening: succenseo , anger , irritation , indignation : memoriam succensionis obliterare, Symm. Ep. 5, 35 .

succensus.opening: , um. Part. from succendo.— Part. from succenseo.

succentīvus.opening: adj. succino , sounding to , accompanying : tibia, Varr. R. R. 1, 2, 15 .

succentor.opening: id. , an accompanier in singing, Aug. Enarr. in Psa. 87, 1 ; Isid. 7, 12, 26 .— Trop. , a furtherer , promoter : fabularum, Amm. 19, 12, 13 ; Isid. Orig. 6, 19, 13 .

succentus.opening: succino , an accompanying , accompaniment , Mart. Cap. 1, § 11 .

suc-cerno.opening: ( ), , v. a. , to sift through , to sift. Lit. : vinaceos cottidie recentes succernito, Cato, R. R. 25 ; 10, 5 ; 18, 7 ; 151, 3; Plin. 18, 11, 29, § 115 ; Vitr. 2, 5 .—Comically: iste gradus succretu'st cribro…

successĭo.opening: succedo, II. . A coming into the place of another, a following after , succeeding , succession in office, possession, etc. (mostly post-Aug.): si merces Antonii oppressi poscitur in Antonii locum successio, Brut. ap.…

successīvus.opening: , a false read. for succissiva, Lact. Opif. Dei, 12, 15 Bünem. ad loc.

successor.opening: succedo, II. , a follower , successor in office, possession, time, etc. (class.; cf. vicarius): conjunctissimus, Cic. Fam. 3, 3, 1 ; cf.: successori decessor invidit, id. Scaur. Fragm. 33 ; id. Prov. Cons. 15, 37 ; id.…

successōrĭus.opening: adj. successor , of or belonging to succession , successory (post-class.; esp. freq. in jurid. Lat.): de successorio edicto, Dig. 38, 9, 1 pr.: ex successorio capite, ib. 22, 6, 1, § 3 : successorio jure aliquid tenere,…

successus.opening: succedo . (Acc. to succedo, I.) An advance , approach (very rare). Lit. : successus et incursus hostium, Caes. B. G. 2, 20 : equorum, Verg. A. 12, 616 .— Transf. (post-class.), a place which one goes down into, a cavern…

succīdĭa.opening: 2. succido . A leg or side of meat cut off , esp. of pork; a leg of pork , flitch of bacon , Varr. L.L. 5, § 110 Müll.; id. R. R. 2, 4, 3 : jam hortum ipsi agricolae succidiam alteram appellant, their second flitch,…

suc-cĭdo.opening: v. n. sub-cado , to fall under any thing. * In gen.: lorica quod e loris de corio crudo pectoralia faciebant: postea succidit Gallica e ferro sub id vocabulum, i. e. were comprehended under the word, Varr. L. L. 5, §…

suc-cīdo.opening: v. a. sub-caedo , to cut off or away below , cut from below , to cut through , cut off , cut down , fell (rare but class.; not in Cic.): is pernas succidit iniquā superbiā Poeni, Enn. ap. Fest. pp. 304 and 305 Müll.…

succĭdŭus.opening: adj. 1. succido , sinking down , sinking , failing ( poet. ). Lit. : genu, Ov. H. 13, 24 : poples, id. M. 10, 458 : gradus, Stat. Th. 4, 661 : flammae, id. ib. 10, 116 et saep.— Trop. : benedictio, faltering, trembling,…

succinctē.opening: adv. , v. succingo, P. a. fin.

succinctim.opening: adv. succingo , briefly , succinctly : denotare, Claud. Mam. Stat. Anim. praef.

succinctĭo.opening: id. , a girding about (late Lat.), Aug. c. Jul. 2, 6.

succinctōrĭum.opening: id. , an apron (late Lat.), Aug. Gen. adv. Manich. 2 . 15 fin. ; id. Serm. Verb. Dom. 10 fin. ; id. Civ. Dei, 14, 17 al.

succinctŭlus.opening: adj. dim. [succinctus], girded , girt : fasciola, App. M. 2, p. 117, 34 .

succinctus.opening: Part. and P. a. of succingo.

suc-cĭnĕrārĭus.opening: ( ), , adj. sub-cinis , = succinericius, panis, Hier. in Hos. 2, 8, 7 al.

suc-cinĕrīcius.opening: ( ), , adj. id. , prepared under the ashes (late Lat.): panis, baked under the ashes, Vulg. Gen. 18 , 6; id. Exod. 12, 39 ; id. Osee, 7, 8 al.; cf. Isid. Orig. 20, 21 .

suc-cingo.opening: ( ), , v. a. , to gird below or from below , to tuck up , gird , gird about , girdle (mostly poet. and in postAug. prose; cf. subligo). Lit. : crure tenus medio tunicas, Juv. 6, 455 : astricti succingant ilia ventres,…

succingŭlum.opening: ( ), , succingo , an under-girdle , lower girdle , Plaut. Men. 1, 3, 17 ; cf. Fest. p. 302 Müll.

suc-cĭno.opening: ( ; also , Varr. L. L. 6, § 75 Müll.), , v. a. and n. cano , to sing to , accompany (rare). Lit. : tubicines imitatus est succinente Habinnā, Petr. 69, 4 : cantibus iste tuis alterno succinet ore, Calp. Ecl. 4, 79 .—…

succīsĭo.opening: 2. succido , a cutting off or away : cottidiana pilorum, Sid. Ep. 1, 2 .

succīsor.opening: 2. succido , one who cuts or prunes (late Lat.): quam (silvam) nec si serā succisor falce repurget, Alcim. Ep. 4, 48 .

succlāmātĭo.opening: succlamo , a calling or crying out , a shouting , acclamation after any thing (rare; perh. not anteAug.); only plur. : ultro territuri succlamationibus, Liv. 28, 26, 12 ; 40, 36, 4 ; 42, 28, 2 ; Suet. Ner. 24 .

suc-clāmo.opening: ( ), , v. a. , to call or cry out , to shout , exclaim after or in reply to any thing (not in Cic. or Cæs.); with obj.-clause : haec Virginio vociferanti succlamabat multitudo, nec illius dolori nec suae libertati se…

succlausus.opening: adj. sub-claudo , half-closed [Appul.], Polem. Physiogn. p. 128.

succlīno.opening: v. n. sub-clino , to bend or incline somewhat , Ven. Fort. Ep. Praem. Carm. 5, lib. 6.

suc-collo.opening: ( ), , v. a. collum , to take upon the neck or shoulder , to shoulder (very rare): apes fessum (regem) sublevant, et si nequit volare, succollant, Varr. R. R. 3, 16, 8 (for which: attollunt umeris, Verg. G. 4, 217 ):…

suc-condĭtor.opening: ( ), , , an inferior officer in the Circensian games , Inscr. Grut. 339, 5 , and 340, 3.

suc-contŭmēlĭōsē.opening: ( ), adv. , somewhat insolently or contumeliously : tractari, Cic. Att. 2, 7, 3 .

suc-cŏquo.opening: ( ), , v. a. , to cook a little : omnia igni, Marc. Emp. 36 med.

succŏrĭātĭo.opening: sub-corium ; med. t. t., an operating beneath the skin (late Lat.), Ps.-Soran. Quaest. Medic. 245.

suc-cornĭcŭlārĭus.opening: ( ), , , a sub-adjutant , second adjutant , Inscr. Orell. 3490 .

suc-cortex.opening: ( ), , , the under or inner bark , Veg. 4, 28 .

suc-crassŭlus.opening: ( ), , adj. dim. [crassus], somewhat thick , thickish : corporis qualitate succrassulus, Capitol. Gord. 6 .

suc-crĕpo.opening: ( ), , v. n. , to crackle beneath (late Lat.), Aug. Vit. Beat. 3 .

suc-cresco.opening: ( ), , v. inch. n. , to grow under or from under any thing; to grow up (very rare). Lit. : sub ordine naturali pilorum (in palpebris) alius ordo succrescit, Cels. 7, 7, 8 : succrescit ab imo, Ov. M. 9, 352 : ne…

suc-crispus.opening: ( ), , adj. , somewhat curled , frizzled , or crisped : capillus, Cic. Verr. 2, 2, 44, § 108 : juba equi, Varr. R. R. 2, 7, 5 : pars inferior caudae, id. ib. 2, 5, 8 .

suc-crotillus.opening: ( ), , adj. , thin , slender , delicate (ante-class.): succrotilla vox tenuis et alta. Titinnius: femina fabulare succrotillā voculā. Afranius in epistulā: loquebatur succrotillā voce serio. Plautus in describendis…

suc-crūdus.opening: ( ), , adj. , somewhat raw , half raw : brassica, parboiled, Cato, R. R. 156, 7 : succrudum incidendum ne, etc., not fully ripe, Cels. 6, 13 ; 7, 2 .

suc-crŭentus.opening: ( ), , adj. , somewhat bloody : livor facie contusā, Cels. 5, 18, 24 ; 4, 18 .

succŭba.opening: ( ), , 1. succubo . One who lies under; hence, in mal. part., a lecher or strumpet (post-class.): florulentus, Prud. στεφ. 10, 192; cf. 2. succubo.— Transf. , a supplanter , rival : formae, App. M. 5, p. 171, 31 : tori,…

suc-cŭbo.opening: ( ), , cubo , one who lies under; hence, a lecher , Titin. ap. Non. 224, 22 (but Com. Fragm. v. 92 Rib. reads: quam arbitrer Illarum subcuboneam esse, i. e. succubam).

suc-cultro.opening: ( ), no perf. , , v. a. culter , to cut up with a knife , to chop up , mince (late Lat.): pulpas, Apic. 4, 2 : thymum, id. 8, 8 med.

suc-cumbo.opening: ( ), , v. n. , to lay or put one ' s self under any thing; to fall down , lie , or sink down. Lit. (rare; not in Cic.; cf. subsido). In gen.: ancipiti succumbens victima ferro, Cat. 64, 370 : vidit Cyllenius omnes…

succumbus.opening: ( ), , , a boundary-stone , Auct. Limit. pp. 265 and 302 Goes.

suc-cŭnĕātus.opening: ( ), , Part. [cuneo], wedged underneath , supported with wedges : postes, Vitr. 6, 2 .

suc-curro.opening: ( ), , v. n. , to run under. Lit. In gen.: tempore eodem aliud nequeat succurrere lunae Corpus, * Lucr. 5, 763 ; cf.: pagus Succusanus, quod succurrit Carinis, runs , i. e. lies under or behind , Varr. L. L. 5, § 48…

succursor.opening: ( ), , succurro , perh. a helper , succorer , who comes to the aid of the bestiarius, in the combats with beasts in the circus, Inscr. Orell. 2530 .

succussātor.opening: succusso , a jolter : caballus, a jolting horse , Lucil. ap. Non. 16, 30 ; cf. succussor.

succussātūra.opening: ( ), , id. , the jolting of a hard-going horse, Non. 17, 23 .

succussĭo.opening: ( ), , succutio , a shaking , quaking : succussio est, cum terra quatitur et sursum ac deorsum movetur, Sen. Q. N. 6, 21, 2 .

succusso.opening: ( ), , v. freq. a. id. , to shake or jerk up and down , to jolt (as a hard-going horse does his rider), Att. ap. Non. 16, 29 (Trag. Rel. 568 Rib.).

succussor.opening: ( ), , id. , a jolter , said of a horse: sonipes, Lucil. ap. Non. 16, 31 ; cf. succussator.

succussus.opening: ( ), , succutio , a shaking , jolting , Pac. ap. Cic. Tusc. 2, 21, 48 (Trag. Rel. 257 Rib.): membra tremulo succussu quatit, App. M. 3, p. 138, 29 . — Plur. , Tert. Anim. 49 init.

suc-cŭtĭo.opening: ( ), , v. a. sub-quatio , to fling up from below , fling aloft , toss up ( poet. and in post-Aug. prose). Lit. : orbes rotarum, Lucr. 6, 551 : currus alte, Ov. M. 2, 166 : mare, Sen. Q. N. 5, 1, 1 : vasculum, App. M. 2,…

sucerda.opening: sus and root skar-; Gr. σκώρ; cf. stercus , the dung of swine , Lucil. ap. Non. 175, 14 ; Titin. ap. Fest. p. 302 Müll. (Com. Rel. v. 178 Rib.; cf. excerno, 2).

sūcĭdo.opening: v. a. sucus , to make fresh or juicy : cyminum, Plin. Val. 2, 9 .

sūcĭdus.opening: ( ), , adj. id. , juicy , sappy; fresh (very rare; not in Cic.): solum, App. Mag. p. 289 : tonsurae tempus inter aequinoctium vernum et solstitium, cum sudare inceperunt oves; a quo sudore recens lana tonsa sucida…

sūcĭnĕus.opening: ( ), , adj. id. , of amber : novaculae, with amber handles, Plin. 22, 23, 47, § 99 (al. sucinas).

sūcĭnum.opening: ( ), , sucus , amber , usu. called electrum, Plin. 37, 2, 11, § 30 ; Mart. 3, 65, 5 ; 5, 37, 11 ; Juv. 6, 573 al.

sūcĭnus.opening: ( ), , adj. sucinum , of amber : gutta, Mart. 6, 15, 2 : gemma, id. 4, 59, 2 : novacula, Plin. 22, 23, 47, § 99 .

sūco.opening: ( ), , sugo , a sucker; of a usurer, Att. ap. Cic. Att. 7, 13 , b, § 5.

sūcōsĭtas.opening: sucosus , juici ness , Cael. Aur. Acut. 2, 29, 151 .

sūcōsus.opening: ( ), , adj. sucus , full of juice or moisture , juicy , sappy , succulent. Lit. (post-Aug.): poma, Cels. 2, 18 : solum, Col. 2, 16, 3 : resina, Plin. 24, 6, 22, § 33 : radix, id. 25, 9, 70, § 117 : folia, id. 25, 13,…

Sucro.opening: A river of Hispania Tarraconensis, now the Xucar , Mel. 2, 6 ; Plin. 3, 3, 4, § 20 .— A town at the mouth of this river , now Sueca , Plin. 3, 3, 4, § 20 ; Liv. 28, 24 ; 28, 26 ; 28, 29 ; Sen. Ben. 5, 24, 1 ; Flor. 3,…

sŭcŭla.opening: cf. ὕω, to rain , mostly plur. suculae, the constellation Hyades , a transl. of the Gr. ὑάδες, Tiro ap. Gell. 13, 9, 4 ; Plin. 2, 39, 39, § 106 : nostri a similitudine cognominis Graeci propter sues impositum…

sūcŭlentus.opening: ( ), , adj. sucus , full of juice or sap , sappy , succulent (post-class.). Lit. : gracilitas, App. M. 2, p. 115, 22 : arvina, id. ib. 10, 245 : corpus, Paul. Nol. Carm. 21, 631 . — * Trop. , vigorous : furores, Prud.…

sŭcŭlus.opening: dim. sus , a little boar , Just. Inst. 2, 1, 37 .

sūcus.opening: ( ), (collat. form, gen. sing. sucūs, Isid. 17, 9, 28 ; gen. plur. sucuum, App. M. 10, p. 244, 32 ), sugo , juice , moisture , sap (class.; cf.: liquor, latex). Lit. In gen.: stirpes ex terrā sucum trahunt, Cic. N. D.…

sūdābundus.opening: adj. sudo , sweating : turba, Auct. Carm. ad Pis. 176.

sūdārĭŏlum.opening: dim. sudarium , a little handkerchief , Hier. Ep. 52, 5 ; App. Mag. p. 307, 37 al.

sūdārĭum.opening: sudor , a cloth for wiping off perspiration , a handkerchief , Cat. 12, 14 ; 25, 7 ; Mart. 11, 39, 3 ; Petr. 67 : sudario candido tergere frontem, Quint. 6, 3, 60 ; 11, 3, 148 ; Suet. Ner. 25 ; 48 ; 51 ; Val. Max. 9,…

sūdātĭlis.opening: adj. sudo , flowing like sweat , fluid (late Lat.): metallum, Cassiod. Var. 5, 2 .

sūdātĭo.opening: id. . Lit. , a sweating , perspiration , sudation (post-Aug.): multa, Sen. Ep. 86, 5 .— Plur. , Cels. 3, 2 med. —* Transf. , in concr., a sweatingroom , sudatory : concamerata, Vitr. 5, 11 med.

sūdātor.opening: id. , one that perspires easily or copiously , Plin. 23, 1, 23, § 43 .

sūdātōrĭus.opening: adj. sudo , belonging to or serving for sweating , sudatory. Adj. : unctiones, Plaut. Stich. 1, 3, 73 : qualitas, Cassiod. Var. 2, 39 med. — Subst. : , , , a sweatingbath , sweating-room , a sudatory : circa balinea ac…

sūdātrix.opening: sudator , she that sweats or causes sweating : toga, Mart. 12, 18, 5 .

sūdĭcŭlum.opening: ( ), , sudor, producing sweat , a kind of whip or scourge , Plaut. Pers. 3, 3, 14 ; cf. Fest. p. 336 Müll.

Sudīnes.opening: a writer on precious stones , Plin. 9, 35, 56, § 115 ; 36, 7, 12, § 59 ; 37, 8, 35, § 114 al.

sŭdis.opening: ( nom. sing. only, Plin. 32, 10, 54, § 154 infra), , , a stake , pile (syn.: palus, sublica). Lit. , plur. : sudes stipitesque, Caes. B. C. 1, 27 ; id. B. G. 5, 18 ; 5, 40 ; Verg. A. 7, 524 : quadrifidae, id. G. 2, 25 :…

sūdo.grammar: āvi, ātum, 1 v. n. and a.
sūdo.opening: v. n. and a. [Gr. root ἰδ-; ἶδος, ἱδρός, sweat; Germ. Schweisz]. Neutr. (class.), to sweat , perspire. Lit. Absol. : qui sudat, Plaut. As. 2, 2, 23 : sine causā sudare, Cic. de Or. 2, 55, 223 : sudavit et alsit, Hor. A.…

sūdor.opening: [sudo). Lit. , sweat , perspiration : manat ex omni corpore sudor, Enn. ap. Macr. S. 6, 1 (Ann. v. 399 Vahl.); Lucr. 6, 944 : sudor e corpore, Cic. Div. 2, 27, 58 ; cf.: totum sudor habet corpus, Enn. ap. Macr. S. 6, 3…

sūdōrĭfer.opening: sudor-fero , sudorific : vapores, Cael. Aur. Acut. 3, 21, 206 .

sūdōrus.opening: adj. sudor , dripping with sweat , sweaty : corpus, App. Flor. p. 354, 27 .

sūdŭcŭlum.opening: dim. sudes , a kind of whip , scourge : flagri, Plaut. Pers. 3, 3, 14 Ritschl N. cr. (cf. sudiculum).

sūdus.opening: adj. se-udus; cf.: sudum siccum quasi seudum id est sine udo, Fest. pp. 294 and 295 Müll. , without moisture , dry; and of the weather, cloudless , bright , clear (class.; cf. serenus). Adj. : ventorum flamina suda,…

Suël.opening: a town in Spain , Plin. 3, 1, 3, § 8 ; Mel. 2, 6 .

Suelteri.opening: a people of Gallia Narbonensis, Plin. 3, 4, 5, § 35 .

sŭĕo.opening: assumed as a stem for the form sŭēmus, which is probably a contracted perf., = suevimus from suesco; cf. consuesco and the Gr. εἰώθαμεν , to be wont , used , or accustomed : appellare suemus, Lucr. 1, 60 : cernere…

sŭesco.opening: (dissyl. suēvi, suētum; sync. forms, suesti, suerunt, suesse, etc.; v. in the foll. , and cf. also the preced. art.), 3, v. inch. n. and a. [Sanscr. svadhā, will, might, custom; Gr. ἔθος, ἦθος ]. Neutr. , to become used…

Suessa.opening: , = Σύεσσα. A city of Latium , five miles south of the Liris and eight from the sea , founded B. C. 337 by the Aurunci , and afterwards made their capital. It was often called Suessa Aurunca , now Sessa , Liv. 8, 15 ;…

Suessetāni.opening: a people of Hispania Tarraconensis, Liv. 25, 34 ; 34, 20 ; 39, 42 .—Hence, adj. : , , um: ager, Liv. 28, 24 .

Sŭessĭōnes.opening: ( , trisyl., Luc. 1, 423 ), , , a people in Gaul , in the neighborhood of the modern Soissons , Caes, B. G. 2, 3; 2, 12; 2, 13; Hirt. B. G. 8, 6 ; Plin. 4, 17, 31, § 106 .

Suessŭla.opening: a town of Campania , now Castel di Sessola , Liv. 7, 37 ; 8, 14 ; 23, 14 ; 23, 17; 23, 32; 24, 46.—Hence, , , , the inhabitants of Suessula , Liv. 8, 14 ; Plin. 3, 5, 9, § 64 ; Inscr. Orell. 130 ; 2369 .

Suētōnĭus.opening: the name of a Roman gens. So, C. Suetonius Paulinus (Lenis), father of the foll. , Tac. A. 14, 29 ; id. H. 2, 23 ; 2, 31 ; id. Agr. 5 ; 14, 16 ; Suet. Oth. 10 .— C. Suetonius Tranquillus, a contemporary and friend of…

suētūdo.opening: suesco , custom , habit (late Lat.): blanda, Paul. Pell. Euchar. 179 ; 271 .

Suēvi.opening: or (in inscrr. always; but most MSS. have Suevi), , , the Suevi , a powerful people in the north-eastern part of Germany , Caes. B. G. 4, 1 ; Tac. G. 38 ; Luc. 2, 51 .—Hence, or , , adj. , of or belonging to the Suevi ,…

Suēvĭus.opening: a poet , otherwise unknown, Macr. S. 2, 14 .

sūfes.opening: ( ), , Phoen. , a judge , the chief magistrate of the Carthaginians , corresponding to the Roman consul, a sufet , Liv. 28, 37 ; 30, 7 ; 34, 61 ; Sen. Tranq. 4, 5 ; Inscr. Orell. 3056 sq. — Plur. , Liv. 34, 61 ; cf.…

Sufetŭla.opening: a town in Africa , Aug. c. Donat. 6, 26 .

suf-farcĭno.opening: ( ), , v. a. , to stuff full , to cram (ante- and postclass.). Lit. : incedunt suffarcinati cum libris, Plaut. Curc. 2, 3, 10 : vidi Cantharam Suffarcinatam, stuffed out , i. e. with a bundle under her dress , Ter. And.…

suffarrānĕus.opening: or , a false read. for furnariae, Plin. 7, 43, 44, § 135 Sillig ad h. l.)

suffectĭo.opening: ( ), , sufficio (post-class.). An adding : unguentorum, Arn. 5, 166 : macularum, id. 7, 251 .— A supplying , substituting : animarum alterna mortuorum atque viventium suffectio, Tert. Anim. 28 ; cf. suffectura.

suffectūra.opening: ( ), , id. , a supplying , supplement (post-class.): suffectura est quodammodo spiritus animae, Tert. adv. Marc. 1, 28 med.

Suffēnātes.opening: the inhabitants of Nebula Suffena , a town in the Sabine territory , Plin. 3, 12, 17, § 107 .

Suffēnus.opening: a bad poet , ridiculed by Catullus , Cat. 14, 19 ; 22, 1 sqq.

suffĕrentĭa.opening: ( ), , suffero , a bearing , enduring , toleration , sufferance (post-class.), Tert. adv. Marc. 4, 15 ; id. Or. 4 med. ; Vulg. Jacob. 5, 11 ; id. Ecclus. 16, 14 .

suf-fermentātus.opening: ( ), , Part. [fermento], somewhat fermented (postclass.), Tert. adv. Valent. 17 .

suf-fĕro.opening: ( ), , v. a. To carry under , to put or lay under (very rare; syn. subicio): corium, Plaut. Poen. 4, 2, 33 : tergum, id. Fragm. ap. Non. 397, 1 .— In gen. To offer , proffer : neque mater potest sufferre lac, Varr. R.…

suffertus.opening: ( , Lucil. ap. Gell. 4, 17, 3 ), , adj. sub - farcio , crammed full , full (very rare): subicit suffectus posteriorem, Lucil. l. l.: aliquid se sufferti tinniturum, something full-sounding, sonorous, Suet. Ner. 20 .

suf-fervēfăcĭo.opening: ( ), no perf. , , v. a. , to heat or warm from below (Plinian), Plin. 18, 11, 26, § 104 : affirmant, lapillos, qui sufferveflant, rumpi, id. 27, 9, 51, § 75 : aceti heminis quinque suffervefactis, id. 14, 17, 21, § 114…

suf-fervĕo.opening: ( ), , v. n. , to boil or seethe gently , App. Herb. 115 .

suffībŭlum.opening: sub-fibula , a white four-cornered veil , worn on the head by priests and priestesses, Varr. L. L. 6, § 21 Müll.; cf. Fest. pp. 348 and 349 ib.

suffĭcĭenter.opening: adv. sufficio , sufficiently , enough , Dig. 7, 1, 15 ; Vulg. Nah. 2, 12 ; Plin. Ep. 10, 18 (29), 3 dub.

suffĭcĭentĭa.opening: id. , a sufficiency (post-class.), Tert. ad Uxor. 1, 4 fin. ; Sid. Ep. 6, 12 fin. ; Vulg. 2 Cor. 3, 5 ; 9, 8.

suf-fĭcĭo.grammar: fēci, fectum, 3 v. a. and n.
suf-fĭcĭo.opening: ( ), , v. a. and n. facio . Act. To put under or among. Of a building, to lay the foundation for : opus. Curt. 5, 1, 29 Zumpt. — Esp., to put into , dip in , dye , impregnate , imbue , tinge , lanam medicamentis, to…
