suf-fīgo.opening: ( ), , v. a. , to fasten beneath or below , to fasten or fix on , to affix (rare but class.): ecce aedificat: columnam mento suffigit suo, Plaut. Mil. 2, 2, 54 Ritschl N. cr. : antennae suffixit lintea, Luc. 9, 328 :…

suffīmen.opening: suffio , fumigation , incense ( poet. for suffimentum), Ov. F. 4, 731 sq.

suffīmento.opening: v. a. suffimentum , to fumigate : totum bovem, Veg. 3, 2 fin.

suffīmentum.opening: suffio , fumigation , incense (cf.: odor, fragrantia): in iis sine illius suffimentis expiati sumus, Cic. Leg. 1, 14, 40 : quia suffimentum sit (laurus) caedis hostium et purgatio, Plin. 15, 30, 40, § 135 ; cf. Fest.…

suf-fĭo.grammar: īvi or ĭi, ītum, 4 v. a.
suf-fĭo.opening: ( ), , v. a. fio = θύω , to fumigate , perfume , scent (mostly poet. and in post-Aug. prose; not in Cic.; but cf. suffimentum; cf.: vaporo, fumigo): (testam) suffito sertā et schoeno et palmā, Cato, R. R. 113, 1 :…

suffiscus.grammar: dicebatur folliculus testium arietinorum, quo utebantur pro marsupio, forsitan dictus a fisci similitudine

suffītĭo.opening: suffio , a fumigating , fumigation , perfuming : nimia, Col. 1, 6, 20 : suffitionem doliorum facere, id. 12, 50, 16 : suffitiones commendavere, Plin. 25, 2, 5, § 12 : verbenarum, Arn. 5, 3 : funus prosecuti redeuntes…

suffītor.opening: id. , a fumigator : puerum suffitorem fecit, Plin. 34, 8, 19, § 79 .

suffītus.opening: suffio . A fumigating , fumigation (Plinian): suffitu necare cimices, Plin. 32, 10, 42, § 142 ; 37, 10, 54, § 142 : crebrior, id. 22, 23, 48, § 100 .— Plur. , Plin. 24, 11, 61, § 102 .— In concr., the smoke produced by…

sufflābĭlis.opening: adj. sufflo , that can be breathed , breathable (post-class.): animae, Prud. Apoth. 906 .

sufflāmen.opening: id. , a clog , break , drag-chain , to check the motion of a wheel. Lit. : rotam astringit multo sufflamine, Juv. 8, 148 : tardat sufflamine currum, Prud. Psych. 417 .— Trop. , a clog , hinderance , impediment…

sufflāmĭno.opening: v. a. sufflamen , to hold back by a clog , to clog , check. * Lit. : rotam Ixionis, Sen. Lud. Mort. Claud. (Apocol.) 14, 3.—* Trop. , to stay , check , repress in speaking: tanta illi erat velocitas orationis, ut vitium…

suf-flammo.opening: ( ), , v. a. , to kindle , inflame : calumniam invidiā, Sid. Ep. 5, 6 fin.

sufflātĭo.opening: ( ), , sufflo , a blowing or puffing up , inflation (Plinian): bullantium aquarum, Plin. 9, 7, 6, § 18 : praedurum est sufflatione viventibus, id. 9, 29, 46, § 86 .

sufflātus.opening: Part. and P. a. , v. sufflo.

suf-flāvus.opening: ( ), , adj. , yellowish , light blonde : capillus, Suet. Aug. 79 .

suf-flo.grammar: āvi, ātum, 1 v. a. and n.
suf-flo.opening: ( ), , v. a. and n. (rare; not in Cic. or Cæs.). Act. , to blow forth from below; to blow up , puff out , inflate. Lit. : age, tibicen, refer ad labeas tibias, Suffla celeriter tibi buccas, quasi proserpens bestia,…

suffōcābĭlis.opening: ( ), , adj. suffoco , suffocating : parvus locus, Cael. Aur. Acut. 1, 9 .

suffōcātĭo.opening: ( ), , id. , a choking , stifling , suffocating , Sen. Ep. 54, 2 ; hence, mulierum, suffocation of the womb, hysterical passion, Plin. 20, 5, 15, § 30 ; 26, 15, 90, § 158 ; v. suffoco, I.

suf-fōco.opening: ( ), , v. a. faux , to choke , stifle , strangle , suffocate by compressing the throat (rare but class.; syn.: strangulo, elido). Lit. : patrem, Cic. Mur. 29, 61 : quem crassior saliva suffocat, Sen. Q. N. 6, 2, 4 : in…

suf-fŏdĭo.opening: ( ), , v. a. , to dig or pierce underneath; to pierce or bore through; to dig under , sap , undermine (class.; not in Cic.): ilia equis suffodere, Liv. 42, 59 : inguina, Suet. Dom. 17 : equos, to stab in the belly,…

suffossĭo.opening: ( ), , suffodio , a digging under , undermining , Vulg. Jer. 51, 58 .— Transf. , in plur. , concr., mines , Vitr. 1, 5, 5 (dub.): cum ipsum solum subfossionibus tremeret, Sen. Ep. 49, 8 .

suffrāgātĭo.opening: ( ), , suffragor , a voting for one or in one ' s favor , interest , favor , support , suffrage (class.): suffragationem, observantiam, et gratiam tollere, Cic. Planc. 18, 44 ; cf.: sublata sunt studia, exstinctae…

suffrāgātor.opening: ( ), , id. , one who votes for another , a supporter , partisan , suffragator (class.): suffragatorum comparatio, Cic. Mur. 21, 44 : historicis notior, suffragatoribus obscurior, id. ib. 7, 16 : ex fucosis firmi…

suffrāgātōrĭus.opening: adj. id. , of or belonging to the support of a candidate , recommendatory , suffragatory : non brevis et suffragatoria, sed firma et perpetua amicitia, Q. Cic. Pet. Cons. 7, 26 .

suffrāgātrix.opening: suffragator , a (female) favorer , supporter (late Lat.): nec adfuit (Minerva) suffragatricibus suis, Aug. Civ. Dei , 18, 9 fin. ; 18, 10 fin.

suffrāgĭnōsus.opening: adj. suffrago , diseased in the hough or pastern : mula, Col. 6, 38, 2 .

suffrāgĭum.opening: perh. kindr. with suffrago, and therefore, prop., the pasternbone; cf. Wunder, Var. Lect. p. 169; hence, transf. , publicists' and jurid. t. t., a votingtablet , a ballot (syn. tabella), and in gen., a vote , voice ,…

suffrāgo.opening: v. a. , = suffragor. In gen., to favor , support , vote for , Sisenn. ap. Non. 468, 12 .— Absol. To agree with , Pomp. ap. Non. 468, 7 (Com. Fragm. 106 Rib.).— To proceed favorably : opera, Vulg. 3 Esd. 6, 10.

suffrāgor.opening: v. dep. n. [suffragium], publicists' t. t., to vote for , to support with one ' s vote and interest. Lit. : si nihil erit praeter ipsorum suffragium, tenue est; si, ut suffragantur, nihil valent gratiā, Cic. Mur. 34, 71…

suf-frēnātĭo.opening: ( , also ), , freno , a binding down fast , cementing : lapidis, Plin. 36, 22, 49, § 169 : globus multā suffrenatione devinctus, Isid. Orig. 19, 10 .

suf-frendens.opening: ( ), , Part. [frendo], gnashing a little : uxor inflatā cervice, Amm. 15, 12, 1 .

suf-frĭco.opening: ( ), , v. a. , to rub underneath , to rub down , rub or wipe off , Col. 12, 23, 2 : vasa, id. 12, 25, 4 ; 12, 30, 2 : seriam, id. 12, 38, 4 : palpebras medicamentis, Cels. 6, 6, 26 .

suf-frīgĭdus.opening: ( ), , adj. , rather cold or frigid (post-class. and very rare); trop.: argumentum, Amm. 17, 11, 4 . — Adv. : , rather coldly or frigidly : nimis minute ac prope etiam suffrigide, Gell. 2, 9, 4 .

suf-fringo.opening: ( ), , v. a. frango , to break below , to break (rare but class.): talos alicui, Plaut. Rud. 4, 4, 15 ; id. Truc. 2, 8, 8 : crura alicui, * Cic. Rosc. Am. 20, 56 : ossa ejus, Lact. 4, 26, 32 .

suf-frondĕo.opening: ( ), , v. n. , to put forth leaves (late Lat.), Aug. Serm. Mai, 3.

suf-fŭgĭo.opening: ( ), , v. n. and a. , to flee away (rare; not in Cic.). Neutr. : custodes vigilesque suffugere in tecta coëgit (imber), Liv. 24, 46 .— Act. , to flee from , to shun , avoid , escape a person or thing: manuum tactum et…

suffŭgĭum.opening: ( ), , suffugio , a place beneath which one flies for shelter from rain, etc., a shelter , covert (not anteAug.). Lit. : quid nisi suffugium nimbos vitantibus essem? Ov. de Nuce, 119: subterranei specus suffugium hiemi,…

suf-fulcĭo.opening: ( ), , v. a. , to prop underneath , to underprop , prop up , support (mostly ante- and post-class.; not in Cic.). Lit. : porticus paribus suffulta columnis, Lucr. 4, 427 : maxillas et cervices pulvillis, App. M. 10, p.…

suf-fulgĕo.opening: ( ), , v. n. , to gleam or shine beneath : tum fit ut umor aquae suffulgeat, Poët. in Anthol. Lat. 2, p. 311 Burm.

suffultūra.opening: suffulcio , a propping , support (late Lat.): columnae suffulturae solacio nudatae, Cassiod. Hist. Eccl. 34 .

suf-fūmĭgātĭo.opening: ( ), , suffumigo , a fumigating from below , Veg. Vet. 3, 23 fin.

suf-fūmĭgo.opening: ( ), , v. a. , to fumigate from below , to suffumigate : si ex alvo apes minus frequentes evadunt, suffumigandum, Varr. R. R. 3, 16, 6 : vulvam sulphure, Cels. 4, 20 med. : vulnus, id. 5, 27, 5 : vasa rore marino vel…

suf-fūmo.opening: ( ), , v. n. , to smoke or reek a little; trop., Hier. Ep. 29, 1 .

suf-fundātus.opening: ( ), , Part. [2. fundo], built under , laid as a foundation : lapidibus suffundatis, Varr. ap. Non. 48, 15 .

suf-fundo.opening: ( ), , v. a. , to pour below or underneath; to pour into or among; to pour over or upon; to overspread , suffuse (mostly ante-class. and postAug.). Lit. In gen.: animum esse cordi suffusum sanguinem, Cic. Tusc. 1, 9, 19…

suf-fūror.opening: ( ), , v. dep. n. , to steal secretly , to steal away , filch : suffuror, suppilo, Plaut. Truc. 2, 7, 15 .

suffuscŭlus.opening: ( ), , adj. dim. [suffuscus], somewhat brown , brownish (postclass.): homines Aegyptii, Amm. 22, 16, 23 ; so App. M. 2, p. 120, 18 .

suf-fuscus.opening: ( ), , adj. , somewhat brown , brownish , dusky : margarita, Tac. Agr. 12 fin.

suff-ūsĭo.opening: ( ), , suffundo , a pouring or spreading into or among , a pouring over , a suffusion (post-Aug.). In gen.: vini, an infusion, Apic. 1, 1 ; so, cucumeris, Pall. 1, 35, 9 .— Esp., of diseases. A spreading : fellis, i. e.…

suffūsōrĭum.opening: id. , a vessel for pouring , a pitcher , Hier. in Isa. 2, 4, 1 ; Vulg. Zach. 4, 12 ; cf.: suffusorium ἐπίχυσις, Gloss. Philox.

suffūsus.opening: ( ), , Part. and P. a. , from suffundo.

sug-gĕro.opening: ( ), , v. a. , to carry , bring , put or lay under , etc. (class., esp. in the trop. sense). Lit. : flammam costis aëni, Verg. A. 7, 463 : ignem fornace succensā, Pall. 1, 20, 2 . — To heap up , raise , erect , build :…

suggestĭo.opening: ( ), , suggero . * Lit. , an adding to , addition : potus suggestione auctus, Cael. Aur. Tard. 2, 13, 182 .— Trop. * A rhet. fig., where the orator puts a question and answers it himself, a suggestion : quod schema…

suggestum.opening: id. , a raised place , height , mound : ex suggesto faleris prodeunt anates in stagnum, Varr. R. R. 3, 5, 16 .— Esp., a platform , stage , tribune for a speaker: cum in communibus suggestis consistere non auderet, Cic.…

suggestus.opening: ( ), , , and , , suggero . (Acc. to suggero, I.) An elevated place made of materials poured out; hence, a raised place , a height , elevation (cf. pulpitum). Lit. In gen.: labrum in suggestu inter dolia positum, Cato,…

sug-glūtĭo.opening: ( ), , v. n. , to hiccup a little , Veg. Vet. 3, 60 .

sug-grandis.opening: ( ), , adj. , rather large : cubiculum, Cic. Q. Fr. 3, 1, 1, § 2 .

sug-grĕdĭor.opening: ( ), , v. dep. n. and a. [gradior], to go or come up to , to approach (Tacitean). Neutr. : caesis qui barbarorum propius suggrediebantur, Tac. A. 15, 11 : suggressi propius speculatores, id. ib. 2, 12 ; so, propius, id.…

sug-grunda.opening: ( ), , cf. grando; Sanscr. hrāduni, storm; Gr. χάλαζα, hail , the lower border of a roof , the eaves , Varr. R. R. 3, 3, 5 ; Vitr. 10, 21 ; Dig. 9, 3, 5, § 6 ; 50, 16, 242, § 1 .—Called also , Vitr. 2, 9, 16 ; Plin. 25,…

suggrundārĭum.opening: ( ), , suggrunda , the grave of a child less than forty days old (which was a niche in a wall, covered by a projecting roof or eaves; cf. columbarium, 2. d.): suggrundaria antiqui dicebant sepulcra infantium, qui necdum…

sug-grunnĭo.opening: ( ), , v. n. , to grunt a little : sus, Paul. Nol. Carm. 27, 345 .

sūgillātĭo.opening: sugillo , a blackand-blue mark , a livid spot (made by a blow, bruise, etc.; not ante-Aug.). Lit. : sugillationem rapere, Plin. 32, 7, 24, § 74 .— Trop. , an affronting , insulting : consulum, Liv. 43, 14, 5 : domini,…

sūgillātĭuncŭla.opening: dim. sugillatio , a small livid spot , Claud. Mam. Stat. Anim. 2, 9 dub.

sūgillātus.opening: sugillo , post-class. for sugillatio, Tert. adv. Marc. 4, 34 .

sūgillo.opening: (suggillo, oited ap. Victorin. p. 2465 P.), , v. a. etym. dub.; perh. akin with sugo , to beat black-andblue (mostly post-Aug.). Lit. : oculi ex ictu suffusi cruore et sugillati, Plin. 31, 9, 45, § 100 : athleta, qui…

sūgo.opening: v. a. root svag-; cf. sucus , to suck (class.). Lit. : (animalium) alia sugunt, alia carpunt, Cic. N. D. 2, 47, 122 : (agni) matris sugunt mammam, Varr. R. R. 2, 1, 20 : porca frequentiore numero sucta deficiet,…

sŭi.opening: ( gen. ), dat. sĭbī^, acc. and abl. sē or sēsē, sing. and plur. (old dat. sĭbei, C. I. L. 1, 38; 1, 1056; 1, 1180 et saep.: sibe, ib. 1, 1267 ; 5, 300 ; cf. Quint. 1, 7, 24 ; and v. Neue, Formenl. 2, p. 180 sq.; on the…

sŭĭfĭco.opening: v. a. , to make his own (eccl. Lat.), Rustic. c. Aceph. p. 1245.

sŭillus.opening: adj. sus , of or belonging to swine. Adj. : pecus, Varr. R. R. 2, 4, 1 ; Col. 7, 9, 14 : grex, Liv. 22, 10 : genus, Plin. 8, 52, 78, § 212 : rostrum, id. 8, 33, 51, § 121 : caro, swine ' s flesh , pork , Varr. R. R. 2,…

sŭīnus.opening: adj. id. , of or belonging to swine , swine- , Prisc. 594 P.: caro, Varr. R. R. 2, 4, 8 (MSS.; Gesn. and Schneid. suilla): sevum, Theod. Prisc. 4, 1 .

Suĭŏnes.opening: a northern Germanic people of Scandinavia , in the mod. Sweden , Tac. G. 44 and 45.

Sulca.opening: a Roman surname : Q. Baetius Sulca, Liv. 42, 6 .

sulcāmen.opening: sulco , a furrow , = sulcus, App. M. 6, p. 174, 9 .

sulcātor.opening: id. , one who draws furrows , a furrower , plougher (in postAug. poets). Lit. : Leontini campi, Prud. adv. Symm. 2, 939 : patuli agri, Avien. Perieg. 587 .— Transf. , one who sails over , traverses , etc.: sulcator…

sulcātōrĭus.opening: adj. , sailing over; only in subst. : , , (late Lat.), a ship , a barge , Cassiod. Var. 2, 20 .

Sulci.opening: an ancient maritime city on the southern coast of Sardinia , founded by Carthage , now the ruins of Palma de Solo near Sulci , Mel. 2, 7, 19 .— Hence, , , of Sulci : promuntorium, Plin. 3, 7, 13, § 84 ; Mart. Cap. 6, §…

sulco.opening: v. a. sulcus , to furrow , cut furrows through , to plough (mostly poet. and in post-Aug. prose; not in Cic. or Cæs.). Lit. , in agriculture: agros, Tib. 2, 3, 85 : (rura) sulcata Camilli Vomere, Luc. 1, 168 : vomere…

sulcus.opening: Gr. ὁλκός, from ἕλκω , a furrow made by the plough (cf.: lira, porca): sulci appellantur, quā aratrum ducitur, vel sationis faciendae causā vel urbis condendae, vel fossura rectis lateribus, ubi arbores serantur: quod…

sulfur.opening: (in MSS. also and ), , ( masc. , Tert. adv. Prax. 16 ; Veg. Vet. 1, 38 med. ), brimstone , sulphur. Lit. , Plin. 35, 15, 50, § 174 ; Cato, R. R. 39, 1 ; Col. 8, 5, 11 : vivum, Liv. 39, 13, 12 ; Ov. F. 4, 739 ; Lucr. 6,…

sulfŭrans.opening: ( ), , adj. sulfur; cf. sulfuratus , containing sulphur , sulphurous : aquae, Tert. adv. Val. 15 .

sulfŭrārĭa.opening: ( ), , sulfur , a sulphur pit or mine : in calcariam vel sulfurariam damnari, Dig. 48, 19, 8, § 10 ; 47, 2, 53, § 10 .

sulfŭrātĭo.opening: ( ), , id. , a vein of sulphur in the earth, Sen. Q. N. 3, 15, 5 .

sulfŭrātus.opening: ( ), , adj. id. , impregnated with sulphur , sulphurated. Adj. : fontes, Vitr. 8, 3 : aqua, Plin. 31, 6, 32, § 59 : ramentum, Mart. 10, 3, 3 : merx, id. 12, 57, 14 : lana, Cels. 4, 5 .— Comp. : gehenna, Tert. adv. Marc.…

sulfŭrĕus.opening: ( ), , adj. id. , of or like sulphur , sulphurous , sulphureous : fornaces, Ov. M. 15, 340 : aqua, Verg. A. 7, 517 : lux fulminum, Plin. 35, 15, 50, § 177 : color, id. 35, 6, 25, § 41 : odor, id. 36, 19, 34, § 141 .

sulfŭrōsus.opening: ( ), , adj. id. , full of sulphur , sulphureous : fontes, Vitr. 8, 3 med. : plurima sulfurosa, Cael. Aur. Tard. 2, 7 .

Sŭlĭvĭae.opening: a lengthened form for Silviae , a kind of wood-goddesses , Inscr. Orell. 2051 . — Also in the form SVLEVIAE, Inscr. Orell. 2099 sq.

Sulla.opening: (less correctly ), , , a surname in the gens Cornelia. So, esp., L. Cornelius Sulla Felix, the celebrated Roman dictator , Cic. Div. 1, 33, 72 ; Sall. J. 100, 2 ; Flor. 3, 21, 5 ; Vell. 2, 17, 1 .—Hence, , , adj. , of…

sullātŭrĭo.opening: v. desid. n. [Sulla], to imitate or play the part of Sulla : ita sullaturit animus ejus et proscripturit, Cic. Att. 9, 10, 6 ; cf. Quint. 8, 3, 32 ; 8, 6, 32 .

Sulmo.opening: A town in the territory of the Peligni, near Corfinium, the birthplace of Ovid , now Sulmona : aquosus, Ov. Am. 3, 15, 11 : gelidus, id. F. 4, 81 ; Sil. 9, 76 ; 8, 511 ; Ov. Tr. 4, 10, 3 ; Cic. Att. 8, 4, 3 ; 8, 12 , A,…

Sulpĭcilla.opening: dim. Sulpicia , i. e. the poetess Sulpicia , Fulg. Myth. praef. 1 pr.; v. Sulpicius, VII.

Sulpĭcĭus.opening: the name of a Roman gens; e. g. Ser. Sulpicius Galba, consul 610 A.U.C., and an able orator , Cic. de Or. 1, 10, 39 ; id. Brut. 22, 86 .— C. Sulpicius Gallus, a connoisseur in Greek literature , and a good orator , Cic.…

sum.opening: = eum, Enn. ap. Fest., v. is.

sum-.opening: , for sub before m; v. sub fin.

sūmen.opening: contr. from sugimen, sugmen, from sugo , a breast , of women (syn.: uber, mamma). Lit. In gen.: manus lactanti in sumine sidat, Lucil. ap. Non. 458, 7 .— In partic., a sow ' s udder , the paps of a sow (esteemed a…

sūmĭnātus.opening: adj. sumen , of or belonging to a sow ' s udder , that has the paps on (post-class.): caro, i. e. the paps or udder of a sow , Arn. 2, 73 . sus, i. e. a sow , Lampr. Alex. Sev 22 .

summa.opening: (sc. res; old gen. summai, Lucr. 1, 984 ; 6, 679 ) [summus, v. superus]. Lit. , that which is highest in any thing, the top , summit , surface (postAug. and very rare): testudines evectae in summā pelagi, Plin. 9, 10,…

summālis.opening: adj. summa , containing a sum , whole (post-class.), Tert. adv. Herm. 31 .—Hence, , adv. , wholly , perfectly , Primas. in Coloss. 1.

sum-mānans.opening: ( ), , Part. [mano], flowing beneath : aqua sub terrā, Vitr. 3, 1 med.

Summānes.opening: ( ), , , a kind of inferior deities , Mart. Cap. 2, § 164 .

summāno.opening: ( ), , v. a. and n [sub-mano]. Neutr. , to glide or trickle under , Vitr. 8, 1, 2 .— Act. , to wet somewhat : vestimenta mea, ubi obdormivi ebrius, Summano (with a play on the name Summanus, i. e. Pluto), Plaut. Curc.…

Summānus.opening: ( ), , , a Roman deity to whom nocturnal lightnings were asscribed , but whose precise nature was unknown even to Ovid; acc. to Mart. Cap. i. q. Pluto , Ov. F. 6, 731 ; Mart. Cap. 2, § 161 ; Plaut. Bacch. 4, 8, 54 ; id.…

summārĭum.opening: summa , a summary , epitome , abstract : oratio, quae nunc vulgo breviarium dicitur, olim, cum Latine loqueremur, summarium, vocabatur, Sen. Ep. 39, 1 .

summas.opening: id. , of high or noble birth , high-born , noble , eminent , distinguished (ante- and post-class.): vir, Plaut. Ps. 1, 2, 90 ; id. Stich. 3, 2, 36 ; Amm. 14, 6, 12 ; Sid. Ep. 3, 11 : matronae, Plaut. Cist. 1, 1, 27 :…

summātim.opening: adv. id. , on the surface , on the outside , slightly. Lit. (post-Aug. and very rare): radicem summatim eradere, Col. 12, 48, 1 : eruere radices, id. Arb. 6, 2 : ablaqueare vitem, id. ib. 10, 5 .— Trop. , slightly ,…

summātus.opening: id. , chief rule , supremacy , sovereignty , = principatus: imperium ac summatum petere, Lucr. 5, 1142 .

sum-mĕdĭus.opening: ( ), , adj. , middle , mean positura, Diom. p. 432 P.

sum-mējo.opening: ( ), , v. a. , to make water under a thing, se, Marc. Emp. 8, 5 med.

summējŭlus.opening: ( ), , summejo , one who makes water under himself , who wets his bed , Marc. Emp. 26 fin.

sum-mergo.opening: ( ), , v. a. , to dip or plunge under , to sink , overwhelm , submerge , submerse. Lit. (class.; most freq. pass. ): summersus equus voraginibus, Cic. Div. 1, 33, 73 : genera summersarum beluarum, id. N. D. 2, 39, 100 :…

summersĭo.opening: ( ), , summergo , a sinking , drowning , submersion (late Lat.), Arn. 5, 182 ; Firm. Math. 1, 2 fin.

summerso.opening: v. freq. a. id. , to plunge repeatedly or thoroughly , Jul. Val. Rer. Gest. Alex. 3, 26 .

summersus.opening: ( ), , summergo , a plunging under water , sinking (post-class.), Tert. Anim. 32 med.

sum-mĕrus.opening: ( ), , adj. , rather pure : vinum, Plaut. Stich. 1, 3, 116 .

sum-mī^grātĭo.opening: ( ), , , an emigration (late Lat.): e patriā, Amm. 25, 9, 1 .

summĭnĭa.opening: ( ), , sub-minium , a kind of garment for women , Plaut. Ep. 2, 2, 50 .

summĭnistrātĭo.opening: ( ), , sumministro , a giving , furnishing , supplying , subministration (post-class.): divina incorruptibilitatis, Tert. Apol. 48 fin.

summĭnistrātor.opening: ( ), , id. , one who aids or assists; trop., an abettor , promoter (post- Aug.): libidinum testisque, Sen. Ep. 114, 23 .

summĭnistrātus.opening: ( ), , id. , a furnishing , supplying : exiguus cibi, Macr. S. 7, 12, § 20 .

sum-mĭnistro.opening: ( ), , v. a. , to aid by giving; to give , furnish , afford , supply (class.). Lit. : pecuniam alicui, Cic. Deiot. 9, 25 : tela clam, id. Cael. 9, 20 : tela ad manum, Quint. 5, 7, 8 : tela agentibus, id. 12, 3, 4 :…

summissē.opening: adv. , v. summitto, P. a. fin.

summissim.opening: ( ), adv. summissus , in a low voice , gently , softly (post-Aug. and very rare): fabulantes, Suet. Aug. 74 : ridere (with sensim), Gell. 17, 8, 7 .

summissĭo.opening: ( ), , summitto , a letting down , lowering , dropping , sinking (Ciceron.): ex contentione vocis et summissione, Cic. Off. 1, 41, 146 : (iterationes) erunt ab hac summissione orationis alienae, id. Or. 25, 85 : nec…

summissus.opening: ( ), , summitto , a sending to or in , introduction : ex summissu erroris ulciscitur, Tert. adv. Marc. 5, 16 med.

summĭtas.opening: summus , the highest part , height , top , summit (post-class.): placidioribus locis septem pedibus summitas vitis insurgit, Pall. 1, 6, 10 ; Macr. Somn. Scip. 1, 6 med. : terrae, Censor. de Die Nat. 13 : deum…

sum-mitto.opening: ( ), , v. a. With the force of sub predominating (mostly poet. and in post- Aug. prose; cf. subicio). In gen. To set , put , or place under or below : singuli agni binis nutricibus submittuntur: nec quicquam subtrahi…

Summoenĭum.opening: ( ), , submoenia , a place in Rome , probably near the walls , the resort of vile characters , Mart. 1, 35, 6 .— Hence, , , adj. , of or belonging to Summœnium : uxores, Mart. 3, 82, 2 ; cf. buccae, id. 11, 61, 2 .

sum-mŏlestus.opening: ( ), , adj. , somewhat troublesome or vexatious (very rare): illud est mihi submolestum, quod, etc., Cic. Att. 16, 4, 4 .— Adv. : , with some vexation : aliquid ferre, Cic. Att. 5, 21, 1 .

sum-mŏnĕo.opening: ( ), , v. n. , to remind privily , give a hint (very rare): summonuit me Parmeno, quod, etc., Ter. Eun. 3, 5, 22 : patres salutavit nominatim singulos, nullo summonente, Suet. Aug. 53 .

sum-monstro.opening: ( ), , v. a. , to show privately : responsa, Arn. 3, 143 (al. subministrat).

sum-mōrōsus.opening: ( ), , adj. , somewhat peerish or morose : me illa valde movent stomachosa et quasi summorosa ridicula, Cic. de Or. 2, 69, 279 .

summō-tĕnus.opening: adv. , up to the top : summotenus florescentibus floribus, App. Herb. 75 .

summōtor.opening: ( ), , summoveo , one who puts aside or removes (in order to make room), a clearer of a space: summotor aditūs, praeco, accensus, i. e. the lictor, Liv. 45, 29, 2 .

sum-mŏvĕo.opening: ( ), (sync. form of the pluperf. subj. summosses, Hor. S. 1, 9, 48 ), v. a. , to send or drive off or away , to remove (freq. and class.; cf.: repello, amolior). Lit. In gen.: hostes a portā, Caes. B. G. 7, 50 : hostes…

summŭla.opening: dim. summa , a small sum : summulas minutas distribuit servis, Sen. Ep. 77, 8 ; App. M. 11, p. 271, 32 ; Prud. στεφ. 2, 131.

sum-multĭplex.opening: ( ), , adj. , contained many times in another number , Boëth. Inst. Arithm. 1, 22 .

sum-murmŭro.opening: ( ), , v. a. , to murmur a little or in secrēt (late Lat.), Aug. Conf. 6, 9 ; 8, 11 .

summussi.opening: = murmuratores ( murmurers ). Naevius: odi, inquit, summussos; proinde aperte dice, quid sit, Fest. pp. 298 and 299 Müll. (Trag. Rel. p. 12 Rib.) [submusso].

sum-mūto.opening: ( ), , v. a. , to change , interchange , substitute one thing for another: hanc ὑπαλλαγὴν rhetores, quia quasi summutantur verba pro verbis, μετωνυμίαν grammatici vocant, quod nomina transferuntur, Cic. Or. 27, 93 .

sūmo.opening: (sync. form of the inf. perf. sumpse, Naev. ap. Gell. 2, 19, 6 (Com. Rel. v. 97 Rib.; suremit for sumpsit, surempsit for sumpserit, Paul. Diac. 299, 2 ; Fest. 298, 9 ), v. a. contr. for subimo, from sub-emo , to take ,…

sumptĭ-făcĭo.opening: v. a. 2. sumptus , to lay out , spend , expend : restim, Plaut. Cas. 2, 7, 2 .

sumptio.opening: (collat. form , Cato, R. R. 145, 2 ), , sumo , a taking. Lit. , Vitr. 1, 2, 2 .— Trop. , in logic, a premise taken for granted , an assumption : demus tibi istas duas sumptiones, ea quae λήμματα appellant dialectici;…

sumptĭto.opening: v. freq. a. id. , to take much of or in strong doses : saepius helleborum, Plin. 25, 5, 21, § 51 .

sumptŭārĭus.opening: adj. 2. sumptus , of or relating to expense , sumptuary : rationes nostrae, Cic. Att. 13, 47, 1 : lex, id. ib. 13, 7, 1 ; cf. id. Fam. 7, 26, 2 ; Suet. Caes. 43 ; id. Aug. 34 ; Gell. 2, 24 .

sumptŭātus.opening: Part. , well furnished (late Lat.); cf. Jul. Val. Rer. Gest. Alex. M. 2, 18 .

sumptŭōsĭtas.opening: sumptuosus , great expense , costliness , expensiveness , Sid. Ep. 9, 6 .

sumptŭōsus.opening: adj. 2. sumptus , very expensive or costly. Of things, that costs much , dear , expensive , sumptuous : ager, Cato, R. R. 1, 6 : cenae, Cic. Fam. 9, 23 fin. : hostia, Hor. C. 3, 23, 18 : bellum, Liv. 45, 3 : tutela,…

sumptus.opening: ( gen. sumpti, Cato, R. R. 22, 3 ; Lucil., Turp., Caecil., and Varr. ap. Non. 484, 30 sq. ; Turp. ib. 132, 16 ; Plaut. Trin. 2, 1, 21 ; id. Cas. 2, 7, 2 ), sumo, II. D. , expense , cost , charge (class.; used alike in…

Sūnĭum.opening: or , , , = Σούνιον, a promontory and town of Attica , now Capo Colonna , Mel. 2, 2, 8 ; 2, 3, 6 ; Cic. Att. 13, 10, 3 ; 7, 3, 10 ; Plin. 4, 7, 11, § 24 ; Ter. Phorm. 5, 5, 9 ; id. Eun. 3, 3, 13 ; Liv. 28, 8 ; 31, 22 ;…

Sunuci.opening: a Belgic people , Tac. H. 4, 66 ; Plin. 4, 17, 31, § 106 .

sŭo.opening: v. a. Sanscr. siv-, sivjāmi, sew; Gr. κασσύω, to stitch, cobble , to sew or stitch , to sew , join , or tack together (rare but class.). Lit. : quod (foramen) nisi permagnā vi sui non potest, Cels. 7, 4, 3 : tegumenta…

sŭŏvĕtaurīlĭa.opening: , or , , sus-ovis-taurus; cf. Quint. 1, 5, 67 Spald.; Fest. p. 293 Müll., or sollus-taurus , a sacrifice consisting of a swine , a sheep , and a bull , offered esp. at lustrations: solitaurilia hostiarum trium diversi…

sŭpellectĭcārĭus.opening: adj. supellex , of or relating to household stuff or furniture : servi, that have the care of it, Dig. 33, 7, 12, § 31 .

sŭpellex.opening: ( nom. supellectilis, Eutr. 3, 23 ; Salv. Gub. Dei , 3, 2), lectĭlis ( abl. -li or -le; v. Neue, Formenl. 1, 240), superlego , household utensils , stuff , furniture , or goods (class.; only in sing. ; cf.: vasa,…

sŭper.opening: adv. and prep. Sanscr. upari; Gr. ὑπέρ; Goth. ufar , above , over (often confounded in MSS. and edd. with supra, q. v.). Adv. , above , on top , thereupon , upon , etc. (rare but class.). Lit. , of place: Anien infraque…

sŭpĕrābĭlis.opening: adj. supero , that may be got over or surmounted. * Lit. : murus, Liv. 25, 23, 12 .— Trop. , that may be overcome or subdued , conquerable , superable (very rare): non est per vim superabilis ulli, Ov. Tr. 5, 8, 27 :…

sŭpĕr-ablŭo.opening: v. a. , to wash off above , Avien. Perieg. 881 .

sŭpĕrăbundantĭa.opening: superabundo , superabunaance (late Lat.), Hier. in Ezech. 6, 18, 6 ; Vulg. Lev. 25, 37 .

sŭpĕr-ăbundo.opening: v. n. , to be very abundant , to superabound (post-class.): ubi delictum abundaverit, illic gratiam superabundasse, Tert. Res. Carn. 34 ; 47 ; Macr. Somn. Scip. 1, 14 ; Lact. Ep. 6, 13 ; Dig. 27, 1, 6 .—Hence, , adv. ,…

sŭpĕr-accommŏdo.opening: v. a. , to fit on above , put on : ferulas, Cels. 8, 10, 1 fin.

sŭpĕr-ăcervo.opening: v. a. , to heap on , pile up , Tert. ad Nat. 1, 15 .

sŭpĕr-addo.opening: , no perf. , , v. a. , to add over and above , to superadd ( poet. ; now usu. written separately): tumulo superaddite carmen, Verg. E. 5, 42 : laurus superaddita busto, Prop. 2, 13, 33 (3, 5, 17): vitis, Verg. E. 3, 38 .

sŭpĕr-ādĭcĭo.opening: v. a. , to put in or add besides , to superadd (post-class.): quartam partem vini, Pall. Oct. 14, 15 : piper his, Apic. 7, 4 : decem dies observationi veteri, Macr. S. 1, 14 .

sŭpĕradmīro.opening: v. a. , to admire or wonder at exceedingly (late Lat.), Facund. Defens. 2, 2.

sŭpĕr-ădornātus.opening: Part. [adorno], further adorned , additionally ornamented : materia, Sen. Q. N. 4, 2, 18 .

sŭpĕr-ădultus.opening: Part. [adulesco], fully mature , past the first period of maturity : virgo, Vulg. 1 Cor. 7, 36 .

sŭpĕraedĭfĭcātĭo.opening: superaedifico , a building upon , Tert. adv. Marc. 5, 6 fin.

sŭpĕr-aedĭfĭcĭum.opening: the upper building , Ambros. in Ep. ad Cor. 1, 3 .

sŭpĕr-aedĭfĭco.opening: v. a. , to build upon or over , Vulg. 1 Cor. 3, 12 : operationem, Paul. Nol. Ep. 28 ; Ennod. Dict. 2 ; Aug. Civ. Dei , 21, 21; 21, 26.— Absol. : alius superaedificat, Vulg. 1 Cor. 3, 10 .

sŭpĕr-aggĕro.opening: v. a. , to heap over with any thing: scrobem, Col. 12, 46, 4 .

sŭpĕr-allŭo.opening: ( ), , v. a. , to wash over , flow over , Prisc. Perieg. 881 .

sŭpĕr-ambŭlo.opening: v. a. , to walk upon or over : calcatas undas (Dominus), Sedul. Carm. 3, 226 .

sŭpĕrāmentum.opening: supero , a remainder , remnant : superamenta materiarum, Dig. 32, 1, 55, § 4 .

sŭpĕrans.opening: Part. and P. a. , v. supero.

sŭpĕrantĭa.opening: supero , excess , predominance (late Lat.), Cael. Aur. Signif. Diaet. Pass. 9 .

sŭpĕr-appārĕo.opening: v. n. , to appear above , Fulg. Myth. 2, 16 .

sŭpĕrappārĭtĭo.opening: superappareo , an appearance above , Fulg. Myth. 2, 16 .

sŭpĕr-argūmentans.opening: Part. [argumentor], arguing over and above , proving besides , Tert. adv. Herm. 37 .

sŭpĕr-aspergo.opening: v. a. , to scatter upon or over (late Lat.): farinam, Veg. Vet. 3, 3 med. : piperis pulverem, Apic. 4, 2 ; Cael. Aur. Tard. 5, 1, 14 : pardus albis maculis superadspersus, Isid. 12, 2, 19 .

sŭpĕr-asto.opening: ( ), , v. n. , to stand over : superadstantium manibus adtollitur, Sall. H. Fragm. 1, 74 Dietsch.

sŭpĕrātĭo.opening: supero , an overcoming , conquering , Vitr. 3 praef. med. — An excess : fervoris, Theod. Prisc. 4, 2 .

sŭpĕrātor.opening: supero , an overcomer , conqueror (Ovidian): populi Etrusci, Ov. F. 1, 641 : Gorgonis (Perseus), id. M. 4, 699 .

sŭpĕrātrix.opening: superator , she that conquers : CASTARVM, Inscr. Fabr. p. 383 .

sŭpĕr-augmentum.opening: an additional or further increase , Isid. Orig. 6, 17, 23 .

sŭperbĭa.opening: superbus . In a bad sense, loftiness , haughtiness , pride , arrogance (syn.: arrogantia, insolentia, fastidium, fastus): num sibi aut stultitia accessit aut superat superbia? Plaut. Am. 2, 2, 77 : magnitudinem animi…

sŭper-bĭbo.opening: v. n. , to drink upon or after , Plin. 23, 1, 23, § 42 ; Cael. Aur. Acut. 1, 14, 110 .

sŭperbĭfĭcus.opening: adj. superbusfacio , proud-making , that renders proud : manus, Sen. Herc. Fur. 58 .

sŭperbĭlŏquentĭa.opening: superbusloquor , haughty or proud speaking , Poët. ap. Cic. Tusc. 4, 16, 35 .

sŭperbĭo.opening: v. n. superbus , to be haughty or proud , to take pride in a thing (mostly poet. and in post-Aug. prose). Lit. : si habes quod liqueat, neque respondes, superbis, * Cic. Ac. 2, 29, 94 Orell. (dub.; B. and K. and Halm,…

sŭperbus.opening: adj. super; cf. Gr. ὑπέρβιος . In a bad sense, that thinks himself above others, haughty , proud , arrogant , insolent , discourteous , uncivil , rude , supercilious , domineering (cf.: arrogans, insolens, fastidiosus,…

sŭper-cădo.opening: v. n. , to fall upon or over , Vulg. Psa. 57, 9 ; Cael. Aur. Tard. 2, 3, 70 .

sŭper-caelestis.opening: adj. , that is above the heavens , super-celestial (eccl. Lat.), Tert. Anim. 23 ; id. Res. Carn. 49 .

sŭper-calco.opening: v. a. , to tread or stand upon : tabulatum, Col. 12, 39, 3 .

sŭper-cerno.opening: v. n. , to sift upon or over : terram cribris, Plin. 17, 10, 14, § 74 (better superincerno).

sŭper-certo.opening: v. n. , to fight over , to fight therefor , Vulg. Ep. Jud. 1, 3 .

sŭpercĭlĭōsus.opening: adj. supercilium , haughty , disdainful , supercilious; censorious , severe (post-Aug. and very rare), Sen. Ep. 123, 11 ; Arn. 1, 8 ; Mart. Cap. 8, § 809 .

sŭper-cĭlĭum.opening: super and root kal-; Gr. καλύπτω; Lat. celāre, to hide, cover; cf. Gr. κύλον, ἐπικύλιον, eyelid; cf. also, Ang.-Sax. hlid; Engl. lid; Germ. Augenlid : cilium est folliculus, quo oculus tegitur, unde fit supercilium,…

sŭper-cingo.opening: v. a. , to cover over or in addition (late Lat.), Aug. Quaest. in Heptat. 2, 177, 3 .

sŭper-claudo.opening: v. a. , to cover or close up (late Lat.), Adaman. Locc. Sanct. 1, 15.

sŭper-compōno.opening: v. a. , to place together upon or on the top : pisces, Apic. 4, 2 med.

sŭper-concīdo.opening: v. a. , to cut in pieces over : coliculorum minutias, Apic. 5, 5 fin.

sŭper-contĕgo.opening: v. a. , to cover over : lapsos (herbida pondera), Sil. 16, 42 : renes tunicis, Cels. 4, 1, 19 .

sŭper-corrŭo.opening: v. n. , to fall down thereon , Val. Max. 5, 6, 5 .

sŭper-crĕātus.opening: Part. [creo], grown on , adventitious : infusio umoris, Cael. Aur. Tard. 3, 8, 125 ; Hilar. Trin. 6, 5.

sŭper-cresco.opening: v. n. and a. Neutr. Lit. , To grow up , over , or upon : carcinoma, Cels. 5, 28, 2 fin. : caro, id. 5, 28, 22 init. —With dat. , Serv. Verg. A. 3, 15 .— Trop. : fortuna quod supercresceret caritati, i. e., might join,…

sŭper-cŭbo.opening: v. n. , to lie or sleep upon , Col. 7, 4, 5 ; App. M. 6, p. 185, 34 .

sŭper-curro.opening: v. n. Lit. , to run over or beyond : baltei, Sid. Ep. 4, 20 .— Trop. , to surpass , exceed : large vectigali (ager), Plin. Ep. 7, 18, 3 ; Alcim. Ep. 18 .

sŭper-dēlĭgo.opening: (also separate, ), , v. a. , to bind upon or over : spongiam, Cels. 7, 7, 8 fin.

sŭper-destillo.opening: v. n. , to drop or trickle upon , Cael. Aur. Tard. 5, 1, 18 .

sŭper-dīco.opening: v. n. , to say in addition , Dig. 12, 2, 13 fin.

sŭper-dīmĭdĭus.opening: adj. ; of a number, half as much more (i. e. that bears to another the ratio of 3 to 2), Mart. Cap. 7, § 761 sqq.

sŭper-do.opening: v. a. , to put or lay over (post-Aug.), Cels. 5, 28, 3 fin. ; 5, 8, 7 ; Cael. Aur. Acut. 3, 7 med.

sŭper-dūco.opening: v. a. (postclass.), to lead or draw over : pampinum, Sid. Ep. 5, 17 med. : novercam tot liberis, to bring or put over , Capitol. M. Aur. fin. : novercam filio, Quint. Decl. 38 .— To add , subjoin , Tert. Anim. 36 ; id.…

sŭper-ductĭo.opening: super-duco , a drawing over , erasure , Dig. 28, 4, 1, § 1 .

sŭpĕr-ĕdo.opening: v. a. , to eat besides or after a thing: betae radicem, Plin. 19, 6, 34, § 113 .

sŭpĕr-effĕro.opening: , ef-ferre, v. irreg. a. , to exalt , extol (late Lat.), Aug. in Psa. 49, 30 .

sŭpĕr-efflŭo.opening: v. n. , to superabound , be superfluous (late Lat.), Ambros. in Psa. 118 , Serm. 14, § 9: mensura, Vulg. Luc. 6, 38 : quicquid, Paul. Nol. Carm. 35, 511 : PECVNIA, Inscr. Murat. 1772, 8 .— To be abundantly exalted above…

sŭpĕr-effulgĕo.opening: v. n. , to be more than effulgent (late Lat.), Rustic. c. Aceph. p. 1250.

sŭpĕr-ēgrĕdĭor.opening: v. a. , to surmount (late Lat.): plebeias opiniones, Ambros. Ep. 6 .

sŭpĕr-ēlĕvo.opening: v. a. , to raise above (late Lat.): se (iniquitates), Vulg. Esd. 4, 16, 77 .

sŭpĕr-ēmĭco.opening: v. a. , to spring or burst forth over a thing: terram (unda), Sid. Carm. 15, 75 .

sŭpĕrēmĭnentĭa.opening: super-emineo , supereminence (late Lat.): dei, Aug. Serm. 40 ; id. Gest. Pelag. 30, 55 ; Ambros. Parad. 2, 8 : laudis, Hilar. Trin. 11, 4.

sŭpĕr-ēmĭnĕo.opening: v. a. and n. , to overtop , to appear or be above , to rise above ( poet. and in post-Aug. prose). Act. : victor viros supereminet omnes, Verg. A. 6, 857 : umero undas, id. ib. 10, 765 : fluctus omnes, Ov. Tr. 1, 2, 49…

sŭpĕr-ēmŏrĭor.opening: v. dep. n. , to die upon , Plin. 10, 2, 2, § 4 .

sŭpĕr-ēnăto.opening: v. a. , to swim over : amnem, Luc. 4, 133 Cort.: fluctus omnes, Alcim. Diluv. 4, 240 .

sŭpĕr-ērectus.opening: Part. [erigo], standing overhead : sol, vertical, Amm. 20, 3, 10 dub.

sŭpĕr-ērŏgātĭo.opening: a payment in addition (late Lat.), Ps. Quint. Decl. 3 ; 6 .

sŭpĕr-ērŏgo.opening: v. a. , to spend or pay out over and above : si quid forte supererogasti, Cod. Just. 2, 19, 14 ; Vulg. Luc. 10, 35 .

sŭpĕr-ēvŏlo.opening: v. a. , to fly away over : Alpem, Luc. 3, 299 .

sŭpĕrexactĭo.opening: superexigo , a demanding over and above , an excessive demand , Cod. Just. 10, 20 , De superexactionibus.

sŭpĕr-exalto.opening: v. n. , to exalt above others , Vulg. Jacob. 2, 13 . — Part. : superexaltatus deus, Aug. Conf. 3, 2 .

sŭpĕr-excēdo.opening: v. a. , to surpass (late Lat.), Aug. Specul. 6 .

sŭpĕr-excellens.opening: adj. , very excellent , superexcellent , Salv. adv. Avar. 3, 18 .

sŭpĕr-excurro.opening: v. n. , to run or stretch over , to spread over , Dig. 43, 27, 1, § 2 .

sŭpĕr-exĕo.opening: v. n. , to extend over , Aus. Idyll. 18, 1 .

sŭpĕr-exĭgo.opening: v. a. , to demand or exact over and above , i. e. to excess : damna, Cod. Just. 1, 55, 4 .

sŭpĕr-exsulto.opening: v. n. , to leap up , exult greatly , Symm. Ep. 5, 92 ; Cassiod. Complex. ad Ep. Jacob. 5 .

sŭpĕr-extendo.opening: v. a. , to stretch over , cause to cover : in aliquo cutem, Vulg. Ezek. 37, 6 . — To stretch excessively : nos, Vulg. 2 Cor. 10, 14 .

sŭpĕr-extollo.opening: v. a. , to raise or exalt above others, Tert. Res. Carn. 24 ; Vulg. Psa. 71, 16 .

sŭper-fĕro.opening: v. a. To carry over or beyond , to place or put over (postAug.): pedem parturienti, Plin. 28, 8, 27, § 103 . — Pass. , to go , ride , fly , swim , etc., over : pisces, Plin. 9, 16, 25, § 58 ; App. de Mundo fin. ; Tert.…

sŭper-fēto.opening: v. n. , to conceive anew while still with young , to superfetate , Plin. 10, 63, 83, § 179 ; 7, 11, 9, § 48 ; 8, 55, 81, § 219 .

sŭperfĭcĭālis.opening: adj. superficies , of or belonging to the surface , superficial (late Lat.). Lit. : numerus, denoting the superficial contents, Cassiod. Arithm. p. 555 ; Isid. 3, 7, 4 .— Trop. , superficial : officia, Tert. adv. Marc.…

sŭperfĭcĭārĭus.opening: adj. id. , situated on another man ' s land , superficiary (jurid. Lat.). Adj. : praedia, Dig. 10, 2, 10 : aedes, ib. 43, 18, 2 : mathematice, ut ita dicam, superficiaria est: in alieno aedificat, Sen. Ep. 88, 28 . —…

sŭperfĭcĭes.opening: super-facies , the upper side of a thing, the top , surface. In gen. (post-Aug.): testudinum, the upper shell, Plin. 6, 22, 24, § 91 ; 6, 24, 28, § 109 ; 9, 10, 12, § 35 : sardonychum, id. 37, 6, 23, § 89 : aquae, the…

sŭper-fīgo.opening: v. n. , to fasten up , fasten thereupon : superfixa capita hostium portantes redierunt, Liv. 42, 60, 2 ; Treb. Pol. Claud. 3, 5 .

sŭper-fīo.opening: v. n. , to be over and above , to be left , to remain (very rare; not in Cic.): edepol te vocem (ad cenam) libenter, si superfiat locus, Plaut. Ep. 3, 2, 10 ; id. Mil. 2, 4, 3 ; id. Stich. 4, 2, 12 ; id. Trin. 2, 4, 108…

sŭper-flexus.opening: Part. [flecto], bent over : crates, Sid. Ep. 8, 12 med.

sŭper-flōrescens.opening: Part. [floresco], blossoming all over : sibi cucumis, Plin. 19, 5, 24, § 70 .

sŭper-flŭo.opening: v. n. and a. Neutr. , to run over , overflow (mostly postAug.; only once in Cic.; syn. redundo). Lit. : in aeneo vase leniter coquuntur, ne superfluant, Cels. 6, 18, 2 : fons superfluit, Plin. 31, 4, 28, § 51 :…

sŭperflŭus.opening: adj. superfluo , running over , overflowing (post-Aug.). * Lit. : flumina campis, Plin. Pan. 82, 5 . — Trop. Superfluous , unnecessary : invenissent forsitan necessaria, nisi et superflua quaesissent, Sen. Ep. 45, 4 ;…

sŭperfŏrānĕus.opening: adj. superforum , superfluous , unnecessary (late Lat.): labor, Symm. Ep. 3, 48 (al. supervacaneus): super his plura replicare, superforaneum puto, Sid. Ep. 4, 11 med.

sŭper-fŏro.opening: v. a. , to bore from above (late Lat.), Scrib. Comp. 84 .

sŭper-frŭtĭco.opening: v. n. , to sprout forth again; trop.: talia ingenia, Tert. adv. Valent. 39 .

sŭper-fŭgĭo.opening: v. a. , to flee away over a thing: intactas levis ipse superfugit undas, Val. Fl. 3, 554 .

sŭper-fulgeo.opening: v. a. , to shine over a thing, to shine forth : templa superfulgens, Stat. S. 1, 1, 33 .

sŭper-fundo.opening: , füdi, , v. a. To pour over or upon (mostly poet. and in post-Aug. prose; not in Cic. or Cæs.). Lit. : hanc misturam cum composueris, oleum superfundito, Col. 12, 57, 1 ; 4, 8, 3 : unguentum, Plin. Ep. 9, 33, 9 :…

sŭperfūsĭo.opening: superfundo , a pouring or spreading over or upon (late Lat.): aquarum caelestium, Amm. 17, 7, 12 : pavimenti, Pall. 1, 17, 1 .— An overflowing : haec, Ambros. Hexaëm. 3, 3, 14: aquarum, id. ib. 3, 2, 7 .

sŭper-gaudĕo.opening: v. n. , to rejoice over (late Lat.): alicui, Vulg. Psa. 34, 19 ; Ambros. Ep. 70, 20 fin.

sŭper-gĕnĕro.opening: v. a. , to produce more and more (late Lat.): generatur et supergeneratur usura, increases by compound interest, Ambros. Tob. 13, 43 .

sŭper-gestus.opening: Part. [gero]. * Carried or heaped upon or over : terra, Col. 11, 3, 6 . — * Covered over , covered up : orificium, App. M. 9, p. 237 .

sŭper-grĕdĭor.opening: ( , Plin. 27, 12, 68, § 110 ), gressus, 3, v. dep. a. and gradior , to step , walk , or go over (post-Aug.). Lit. : limen, Col. 7, 9, 13 ; Plin. 32, 10, 46, § 133 : capram alteram decubuisse atque ita alteram…

sŭpergressus.opening: supergredior , a surpassing , exceeding : per supergressum, beyond measure, exceedingly, Tert. Res. Carn. 40 .

sŭpĕr-hăbĕo.opening: v. a. , to have over or upon a thing: superhabendum cataplasma, Cels. 7, 20, § 7 (perhaps it should be written separate, super habendum).

sŭpĕr-illĭgo.opening: v. a. , to bind over or upon , Plin. 29, 3, 11, § 40 ; 30, 6, 17, § 51 .

sŭper-illĭno.opening: ( ), no perf. , lĭtum (collat. form superillinītum, App. Herb. 74 ), , v. a. To smear over , besmear , anoint with a thing: totum corpus bulbis contritis, Cels. 3, 19, 19 .— To smear or spread a thing over another:…

sŭper-immĭnĕo.opening: v. n. , to hang over , overhang (very rare): pastorem Ense sequens nudo superimminet, Verg. A. 12, 306 : terrā superimminente, Sen. Q. N. 5, 15, 1 : virgineusque pudor zonae superimminet artus, Avien. Arat. 962 : mons…

surreptĭo.opening: ( ), , id. , a stealing , purloining , theft : surreptionem factitasse, App. M. 10, p. 245, 32 : per surreptionem elicere, i. e. by deception or subreption , Cod. Just. 1, 14, 2 .

surreptīvus.opening: ( ), , adj. surripio , false , fraudulent : defensio, Cod. Th. 12, 16, 1: impetratio, ib. 10, 20, 11 ; 6, 28, 5 .

surreptus.opening: ( ), , um. Part. of surrepo.— Part. of surripio.

sur-rīdĕo.opening: ( ), , v. n. , to smile (rare but class.): surridet Saturius veterator, * Cic. Rosc. Com. 8, 22 : limis surrisit ocellis, Ov. Am. 3, 1, 33 : surridens Mezentius, Verg. A. 10, 742 : modice, Mart. 6, 82, 7 : molle, Pers.…

sur-rīdĭcŭlē.opening: ( ), adv. ridiculus , somewhat laughably , rather humorously , Cic. de Or. 2, 61, 249 .

sur-ringor.opening: ( ), , v. dep. n. , to make a somewhat wry face , to be a little vexed , Cic. Att. 4, 5, 2 .

sur-rĭpĭo.opening: ( ), (rŭpŭi, Plaut. Trin. 1, 2, 46 ; id. Men. 5, 5, 38 ; v. Ritschl, Proleg. p. xcv.), reptum, 3 (sync. forms: surpite, Hor. S. 2, 3, 283 : surpere, Lucr. 2, 314 : surpuit, Plaut. Capt. prol. 8 ; id. ib. 3, 5, 102 ; 5,…

sur-rŏgo.opening: ( ), , v. a. ; publicists' t. t. Of the presider in the comitia, to cause to be chosen in place of another , to put in another ' s place , to substitute (class.): cum eidem essent (decemviri) nec alios surrogare…

sur-rostrāni.opening: ( ), , rostrum , people who hang about the forum near the rostra , loungers , idlers , Cael. ap. Cic. Fam. 8, 1, 4 .

sur-rŏtātus.opening: ( ), , Part. [roto], mounted on wheels : aries, Vitr. 10, 19 med.

sur-rŏtundus.opening: ( ), , adj. , somewhat round , roundish : radicula, Cels. 5, 28, 14 .

sur-rŭbĕo.opening: ( ), , v. n. , to be somewhat red or reddish , to blush : quale coloratum Tithoni conjuge caelum Subrubet, aut sponso visa puella novo, Ov. Am. 2, 5, 36 : uva purpureo mero, id. A. A. 2, 316 : grossi, Pall. Mart. 10, 31…

sur-rŭber.opening: ( ), , adj. , somewhat red , reddish : caro, Cels. 5, 28, 8 .

sur-rŭbĕus.opening: ( ), , adj. , somewhat red , reddish : color ostri, Non. 549, 9 .

sur-rŭbĭcundus.opening: ( ), , adj. , somewhat red or ruddy , reddish (postAug.): vultus, Sen. Ira, 3, 4, 1 : ulcus, Cels. 5, 28, 4 ; 5, 26, 20 : cauliculi, Plin. 25, 13, 106, § 167 .

sur-rūfus.opening: ( ), , adj. , somewhat reddish : color, Plin. 37, 10, 61, § 170 : surrufus aliquantum, red - haired, Plaut. Capt. 3, 4, 115 .

sur-rūmo.opening: ( ), , v. a. rumis , to put to the udder , to let suck : fetus ovium, Col. 12, 3, 9 : agnos, id. 7, 4, 3 ; cf. Fest. pp. 306 and 307.

sur-rumpo.opening: ( ), , v. a. , to break off below; trop., to destroy : aliorum surrumpant et labefaciant scita, Arn. 2, 82 .

sur-rūmus.opening: ( ), , adj. rumis , under the udder , sucking , suckling : agni, Varr. 2, 1, 20 ; 2, 11, 5 ; cf. Fest. p. 270 Müll. et v. rumis.

sur-runcīvus.opening: ( ), , adj. runco , that is grubbed up : limites, Hyg. Limit. p. 152 ; 177 and 209 Goes.

sur-rŭo.opening: ( ), , v. a. , to tear down below , to undermine , to dig under , dig out; to break down , overthrow , demolish , etc. (class.; perh. not in Cic.). Lit. : arbores a radicibus, Caes. B. G. 6, 27 : robora, Ov. M. 15, 228…

sur-rustĭcus.opening: ( ), , adj. , somewhat clownish or rustic : sonare subagreste quiddam planeque surrusticum, Cic. Brut. 74, 259 ; id. Or. 48, 161 : pudor quidam paene surrusticus, id. Fam. 5, 12, 1 .— * Adv. : , somewhat clownishly ,…

sur-rŭtĭlo.opening: ( ), , v. n. , to glow slightly , to glimmer forth (late Lat.). Lit. : jaspis surrutilans, Hier. in Isa. 15, 54, 12 . — Trop. : surrutilare tibi jam debet, quid sit anima, Claud. Mam. Stat. Anim. 1, 25 .

sur-rŭtĭlus.opening: ( ), , adj. , somewhat reddish or ruddy : color, Plin. 10, 3, 3, § 8 : frutex, id. 24, 11, 54, § 91 : aëtites, id. 36, 21, 39, § 149 .

sursum.opening: (collat. form , Lucr. 2, 188 : , Cato, R. R. 157, 15 ; Aug. Tract. 8, Ep. 1, Joan. 2; Tract. 10, 5; Lact. Mort. Pers. 19, 4 : SVRVORSVM, Inscr. Grut. 204 ), adv. contr. from sub-vorsum , from below , i. e. up , upwards…

sūrus.opening: a branch , a stake , Varr. L. L. 10, § 73 Müll.: surum dicebant, ex quo per deminutionem fit surculus. Ennius: unus surus surum ferret, tamen defendere possent, Fest. p. 299 ib. (cf. Enn. Ann. v. 516 Vahl.); cf.…

Surus.opening: a celebrated elephant in the Carthaginian army , mentioned by Cato, Plin. 8, 5, 5, § 12 (v. Syrus).

sūs.opening: ( nom. suis, Prud. adv. Symm. 2, 813 ; gen. sueris, Plaut. ap. Fest. s. v. spectile, p. 330 Müll.; cf. Varr. L. L. 5, § 110 ib.; dat. plur. subus, Lucr. 5, 969 ; 6, 974 ; 6, 977 ; Plin. 29, 4, 23, § 75 : suibus, Varr.…

Sūsa.opening: , = Σοῦσα, τά, the ancient capital of Persia , now prob. Soos , Plin. 6, 27, 31, § 133 ; Prop. 2, 13 (3, 4), 1; Curt. 5, 1, 7 .—Hence, , , , the province of Susiana or Susiane , in which Susa was situated, now Khuzistan…

susceptĭo.opening: suscipio , a taking in hand , undertaking (good prose): quae proficiscuntur a virtute, susceptione primā, non perfectione, recta sunt judicanda, Cic. Fin. 3, 9, 32 : laborum dolorumque, id. Ac. 1, 6, 23 : causae, id.…

suscepto.opening: v. freq. a. id. , to undertake , App. M. 2, p. 128, 22 .

susceptor.opening: id. (post-class.). One who undertakes any thing , an undertaker , contractor (syn.: conductor, redemptor): susceptores sollicitare, Just. 8, 3, 8 : nemo militantium fiat susceptor defensorve causarum, Cod. Th. 2, 12,…

suscĭpĭo.opening: (sometimes ; cf. Serv. Verg. A. 1, 175 and 144; Vel. Long. p. 2226 P.), , v. a. sus, a contraction of subs, for sub; v. sub fin., and capio , qs. to take hold of in order to support, i. e. to take or catch up , to take…

suscĭtābŭlum.opening: suscito , a stimulant , incitement : vocis, Varr. ap. Non. 176, 31 .

suscĭtātĭo.opening: id. , an awakening , resuscitation from death (eccl. Lat.), Tert. Carn. Chr. 23 ; Ambros. de Bono Mort. 4, 15 .

suscĭtātor.opening: id. , an awakener , resuscitator (late Lat.). Lit. , Tert. adv. Prax. 28 fin. — Trop. : litterarum quodammodo jam sepultarum, Sid. Ep. 8, 2 .

suscĭto.opening: v. a. sub-cito , to lift up , raise , elevate (syn.: erigo, elevo). In gen. (only poet. ): terga (i. e. humum), to throw up, cast up, Verg. G. 1, 97 : undas (Nilus), Luc. 10, 225 : aura lintea Suscitat, swells, fills,…

sūsĭnātus.opening: adj. susinus , of or made from lilies : oleum, Marc. Emp. 7 fin.

sūsĭnus.opening: adj. , = σούσινος, of or made of lilies : unguentum, Plin. 13, 1, 2, § 11 ; Cels. 5, 21, 1 .

suspectĭo.opening: 1. suspicio , a looking up to any one; trop., an esteeming highly (very rare), Arn. 7, p. 221 (7, 13 fin. Orell.).

suspecto.grammar: āvi, ātum, 1 v. freq. a. and n.
suspecto.opening: v. freq. a. and n. id. , to look up at; to look up , to watch , observe , etc. (ante-class. and postAug.). In gen.: tabulam pictam, Ter. Eun. 3, 5, 36 .— Absol. : leo suspectans, Plin. 8, 16, 21, § 57 : sollicitis…

suspectō.opening: adv. suspectus , in a manner to excite suspicion , suspiciously : qui mortem liberorum suspecto decedentium non defenderunt, Dig. 34, 9, 11 .

suspector.opening: 1. suspicio , one who looks up to or respects a thing, a respecter : morum vestrorum suspector admiratorque, Sid. Ep. 3, 5 .

suspectus.opening: 1. suspicio , a looking up or upwards ( poet. and in postAug. prose). Lit. : color nigricans aspectu idemque suspectu refulgens, Plin. 9, 38, 62, § 135 : in suspectu esse, id. 37, 9, 40, § 123 ; 21, 8, 22, § 45 .— Poet.…

suspendĭōsus.opening: adj. suspendium , of or belonging to hanging : fames, suffered while hanging, Plin. 8, 37, 56, § 134 Jan.—Hence, subst. : , , , one that has hanged himself , Varr. ap. Serv. Verg. A. 12, 603 ; Plin. 28, 4, 12, § 49 ;…

suspendĭum.opening: suspendo , a hanging of one ' s self , a hanging (class.), Plaut. Cas. 1, 23 : utinam me Divi adaxint ad suspendium, id. Aul. 1, 1, 11 : injuriae remedium morte ac suspendio quaerere, Cic. Verr. 2, 3, 56, § 129 :…

suspendo.opening: v. a. sus, from subs, for sub; v. sub, III., and pendo , to hang up , hang , suspend (freq. and class.). Lit. In gen.: pernas suspendito in vento biduum ... suspendito in fumo biduum ... suspendito in carnario, Cato, R.…

suspensē.opening: adv. suspensus , hesitatingly , in suspense; comp. : suspensius, Aug. Conf. 10, 34 fin.

suspensĭo.opening: suspendo, I. B. 3. , an arching or vaulting , arched work , Vitr. 5, 10 ; cf. the foll. art.— The imperfect pronunciation of a letter: litterae m, Isid. 1, 31, 6 .

suspensūra.opening: id. , an arching or vaulting , arched work , an arch : balneorum, Sen. Ep. 90, 25 ; cf. caldariorum, Vitr. 5, 10 : cellarum, Pall. 1, 40, 2 .

suspĭcābĭlis.opening: adj. suspicor , conjectural (late Lat.): ars (medicina), Arn. 1, 28 .

suspĭcax.opening: adj. id. , apt to suspect , distrustful , suspicious. Lit. (very rare): populus suspicax ob eamque rem mobilis, Nep. Timoth. 3, 5 : frater, Liv. 40, 14 : animus alicujus, Tac. A. 1, 13 .— Transf. , that excites mistrust…

suspĭcĭo.grammar: spexi, spectum, 3 v. a. and n.
suspĭcĭo.opening: v. a. and n. sub-specio . To look up or upwards , to look up at a thing. Lit. : cum caelum suspeximus, Cic. N. D. 2, 2, 4 ; cf. id. ib. 2, 18, 49 : caelum, Suet. Tit. 10 : summum de gurgite caelum, Ov. M. 11, 506 :…

suspīcĭo.opening: (in good MSS. and edd. also ; v. Brambach s. v.; Fleckeis. in Rhein. Mus. viii. p. 225 sqq.; and so always in Plaut. and Ter. acc. to Fleck., and in Cic. acc. to B. and K.; but cf. contra Corss. Ausspr. 2, 359 sq.),…

suspīcĭōsē.opening: ( , v. suspicio init. ), adv. suspiciosus , in a way to raise mistrust or suspicion , suspiciously : criminose ac suspitiose dicere, Cic. Rosc. Am. 20, 55 ; id. Deiot. 6, 17 ; Quint. 4, 2, 81 ; Sen. Contr. 3 prooem.—…

suspīcĭōsus.opening: ( ), , adj. 2. suspicio , full of suspicion (class.). Mistrustful , ready to suspect , suspicious : omnes quibus res sunt minus secundae, magis sunt nescio quomodo Suspitiosi, Ter. Ad. 4, 3, 15 : an te conscientia…

suspīcĭter.opening: adv. suspicio , mistrustfully , suspiciously : suspiciter circum aspicere, Non. 360, 5 .

suspĭcor.opening: ( inf. suspicarier, Plaut. Ps. 1, 5, 149 ; id. Trin. 1, 2, 49 ), 1, v. dep. a. [1. suspicio, II.], to mistrust , suspect (class.). With acc. (rare): id est, quod suspicabar, Plaut. Men. 5, 2, 24 : quid nunc suspicare…

suspīrātĭo.opening: suspiro , a fetching a deep breath , a sighing , sigh (post-Aug.): suspiratione sollicitudinem fateri, Quint. 11, 3, 158 : inde illa nobilis M. Ciceronis suspiratio: O te felicem, M. Porci, etc., Plin. H. N. praef. § 9.

suspīrātus.opening: id. , a sighing , sigh ( poet. and very rare); in plur. : suspiratibus haustis, * Ov. M. 14, 129 (but in Cic. Att. 1, 18, 3 , the correct read. is suspiritu).

suspīrĭōsus.opening: adj. suspirium , breathing deeply or with difficulty , breathing short , asthmatic : mula, Col. 6, 38, 1 : anhelatores et suspiriosi, Plin. 23, 7, 63, § 121 ; 20, 2, 5, § 9 ; 32, 8, 29, § 91 ; Cael. Aur. Acut. 2, 28,…

suspīrĭtus.opening: suspiro , a breathing deeply or with difficulty , a deep breath , a sigh (rare but class.): enicat suspiritus, Plaut. Merc. 1, 2, 4 (14 Ritschl): quem nemo aspicere sine suspiritu posset, Cic. Att. 1, 18, 3 Orell. N.…

suspīrĭum.opening: id. , a deep breath , a sighing , sigh. Lit. (class.): suspirium alte petere, Plaut. Cist. 1, 1, 58 : traxit ex intimo ventre, id. Truc. 2, 7, 41 : crebrum suspirium, Col. 6, 14, 2 : si quis est in rerum naturā sine…

suspīro.grammar: āvi, ātum, 1 v. n. and a.
suspīro.opening: v. n. and a. [subspiro]. Neutr. , to draw a deep breath , heave a sigh , to sigh (class.): occulte, Cic. Att. 2, 21, 2 : familiariter, id. ib. 1, 13, 1 : suspirat ab imis Pectoribus, Ov. M. 2, 655 : dumque ibi suspirat,…

susque dēque.opening: adv. subs for subque, and de-que , both up and down , to express indifference: susque deque fero aut susque deque habeo (his enim omnibus modis dicitur) ... significat autem susque deque ferre animo aequo esse, et quod…

sustentācŭlum.opening: sustento , a prop , stay , support. Lit. (post-Aug. and very rare): sustentaculum, columen, Tac. H. 2, 28 .— Transf. , sustenance , nourishment : sustentaculum sumptuosum corporis, Aug. Mor. Eccl. Cath. 33 .

sustentātĭo.opening: id. . A deferring , delay; forbearance (very rare). In gen.: habere aliquam moram et sustentationem, Cic. Inv. 2, 49, 146 : quae sustentatio sui recte patientia nominatur, Lact. 6, 18, 32 .— In partic., in rhetoric, a…

sustentātus.opening: id. , a holding up or upright , a sustaining , support (postclass.): levia sustentatui, gravia demersui, App. Mag. p. 287, 34 : cujus ille sustentatu, Aus. Per. 5 .

sustento.opening: v. freq. a. sustineo , to hold up or upriqht , to uphold , support , prop , sustain (syn. sustineo). Lit. (only poet. and in post-Aug. prose): multos per annos Sustentata ruet moles et machina mundi, Lucr. 5, 96 :…

sustĭnentĭa.opening: sustineo , an endurance : malorum, Lact. Epit. 34, 7 : spei, Vulg. 1 Thess. 1, 3.— Absol. , patience , endurance , Vulg. Ecclus. 2, 16 .

sustĭnĕo.opening: v. a. subs for sub, and teneo , to hold up , hold upright , uphold , to bear up , keep up , support , sustain (syn. fulcio). Lit. In gen.: onus alicui, Plaut. As. 3, 3, 68 : quantum hominum terra sustinet, id. Poen.…

sustollo.opening: v. a. [subs for sub (v. sub, III.), and tollo], to lift or take up , to raise up , raise (ante- and post-class.; cf.: erigo, effero). In gen.: amiculum, Plaut. Cist. 1, 1, 117 ; id. Poen. 1, 2, 136 : Graecae sunt hae…

sŭsurrāmen.opening: 1. susurro , a muttering , murmuring (post-class.): magicum, App. M. 1, p. 103, 23 ; Mart. Cap. 7, § 726 .

sŭsurrātim.opening: adv. id. , in a low voice , softly (late Lat.): decenter arrisit, Mart. Cap. 6, § 705 .

sŭsurrātĭo.opening: id. , a whispering , Ambros. Laps. Virg. Cons. 6, 25 ; plur. : crebrae, Cassiod. Var. 9, 18 init. ; Vulg. 2 Cor. 12, 20 .

sŭsurrātor.opening: id. , a mutterer , whisperer , tale-bearer , Cael. ap. Cic. Fam. 8, 1, 4 ; Vulg. Ecclus, 5, 17 .

sŭsurrātrix.opening: susurrator , a whisperer (late Lat.), Petr. Chrysolog. Serm. 118 .

sŭsurro.opening: 1. susurro , a mutterer , whisperer , tale-bearer (post-class.): aures mariti susurronum faece completae, Sid. Ep. 5, 7 fin. ; Vulg. Lev. 19, 16 ; Hier. Ep. 11, 1 .

sŭsurrus.opening: adj. 1. susurrus , muttering , whispering : lingua, Ov. M. 7, 825 .

sūtēla.opening: suo , prop. a sewing together; hence, trop., a cunning device or contrivance , an artifice , trick , wile (Plautin.): sutelae dolosae astutiae a similitudine suentium dictae, Fest. pp. 310 and 311 Müll.: ob sutelas…

Suthul.opening: a fortress in Numidia , Sall. J. 37, 3 ; 38, 2 .

sūtĭlis.opening: adj. suo , sewed together , bound or fastened together ( poet. and in post-Aug. prose). balteus, Verg. A. 12, 273 : cymba, id. ib. 6, 414 : naves, Plin. 24, 9, 40, § 65 : domus, made of skins sewed together, Val. Fl. 6,…

sūtor.opening: id. , a shoemaker , cobbler. Lit. , Plaut. Aul. 1, 1, 34 ; 3, 5, 39 ; Asell. ap. Gell. 13, 21, 8 ; Varr. L. L. 5, § 93 Müll.: crepidarius, Asell. ap. Gell. 13, 21, 8 : SVTORVM COLLEGIVM, Inscr. Donat. 1, 131 ; Mart. 3,…

sūtōrīcĭus.opening: or , , adj. sutor , of or belonging to a shoemaker (for the class. sutorius): atramentum, shoemakers ' blacking , Marc. Emp. 8, 2 med.

sūtōrĭus.opening: adj. id. , of or belonging to a shoemaker or cobbler (class.): atramentum, shoemakers ' blacking , Cic. Fam. 9, 21, 3 ; Plin. 20, 12, 48, § 123 ; 34, 12, 32, § 123 ; Cels. 5, 8 : fistula, a shoemaker ' s punch , Plin.…

sūtrīnus.opening: adj. contr. for sutorinus, from sutor , of or belonging to a shoemaker or cobbler , shoemaker ' s - (mostly post-Aug. for sutorius). Adj. : taberna, Tac. A. 15, 34 : ars, Plin. 7, 56, 57, § 196 ; Varr. L. L. 5, § 93…

Sūtrĭum.opening: an ancient town in Etruria , now Sutri , Liv. 6, 3, 2 ; 6, 9 ; 6, 32 ; Vell. 1, 14 . — Prov.: quasi eant Sutrium, i. e. to set about any thing well prepared (as Camillus, when he marched to the conquest of Sutrium),…

sūtrix.opening: sutor , a sewingwoman , Inscr. Gud. p. 199, 2 ; 220, 1 .

sūtūra.opening: suo , a sewing together , a seam , suture : scutale crebris suturis duratum, Liv. 38, 29, 6 ; Cels. 7, 4, 3 ; 7, 4, 11 fin. ; Petr. 13 : calvariae, a suture of the skull, Cels. 8, 1 and 4.

sŭus.opening: (old form sos, sa, sum; dat. plur. sis, Enn. ap. Fest. p. 301 Müll.; acc. sas. id. ib. p. 325 ib. ; cf. Paul. ex Fest. p. 47 ; Schol. Pers. 1, 108 ; sing. sam for suam, Fest. p. 47 Müll.; so for suo, C. I. L. 5, 2007.…

sўăgrus.opening: , = σύαγρος, a kind of palm-tree , Plin. 13, 4, 9, § 41 .

Sўbăris.opening: , = Σύβαρις. A town in Magna Græcia , noted for the effeminacy and debauchery of its inhabitants , afterwards called Thurii, Varr. R. R. 1, 7, 6 ; Cic. Rep. 2, 15, 28 ; Liv. 26, 39, 7 ; Plin. 7, 22, 22, § 86 ; 3, 11,…

Sўbŏta.opening: , = Σύβοτα, islands between Epirus and Corfu , Plin. 4, 12, 19, § 53 .

sўbōtes.opening: , = συβώτης, a swineherd , Hyg. Fab. 126 ; Manil. 5, 126 .

sȳcămīnus.opening: or , , , = συκάμινος, a mulberry-tree , Cels. 3, 18 med. ; 5, 18, 7 ; cf. Plin. 6, 29, 35, § 184 .—Called , , Dig. 47, 11, 10 ; and , Cels. 5, 18, 7 ; Isid. 17, 7, 20 .

sȳcē.opening: , = συκῆ. A plant , called also peplis, Plin. 27, 12, 93, § 119 .— The resin or rosin of the torch-tree , Plin. 16, 10, 19, § 44 .— A constantly running sore in the corner of the eye , Plin. 20, 6, 21, § 44 .

Sȳ^chaeus.opening: (Sych-, Verg. A. 1, 343 ; also ), , , Sychæus , husband of Dido , Verg. A. 1, 343 ; 1, 720 ; 4, 20 ; 4, 502; 4, 632; 6, 474; Ov. H. 7, 97 sq. —Hence, , , adj. , of Sychæus , Verg. A. 4, 552 .

sȳcĭon agron.opening: a plant , called also cucumis anguinus, App. Herb. 113 .

sȳcītis.opening: , = συκῖτις, a precious stone of the color of figs , Plin. 37, 11, 73, § 191 .

sȳcŏphanta.opening: ( ), , , = συκοφάντης (orig. a fig-informer, i. e. one who informed against those who exported figs from Attica contrary to law; hence, in gen.), an informer , tale-bearer , backbiter , slanderer; a deceiver , trickster…

sȳcŏphantī^a.opening: ( ), , , = συκοφαντια, craft , cunning , deceit; sing. : sucophantia atque doli, Plaut. Ps. 1, 5, 70 ; id. Poen. 3, 3, 41 ; id. Mil. 3, 1, 172 . — Plur. , Plaut. As. 1, 1, 56 ; 3, 2, 2 ; id. Bacch. 4, 4, 88 ; id. Ps. 1,…

sȳcŏphantĭōsē.opening: ( ), adv. sycophanta , craftily , knavishly , deceitfully : agere quicquam (with malefice), Plaut. Ps. 4, 7, 113 .

sȳcŏphantor.opening: ( ), , v. dep. n. [id.], to play the rogue , to deceive , trick , cheat (Plautinian): ego nunc sucophantae huic sucophantari volo, I have a mind to trick this trickster, Plaut. Trin. 4, 2, 116 : hoc me sucophantari…

Sycurium.opening: a town of Thessaly , Liv. 42, 54 ; 42, 56 sq. al.

Sycussa.opening: an island in the Ægean Sea , Plin. 5, 31, 38, § 137 .

Sўēnē.opening: , = Συήνη, a town at the southern extremity of Upper Egypt , now Essouan , Plin. 2, 73, 75, § 183 sqq.; Ov. P. 1, 5, 79 ; Mel. 1, 9, 9 ; Luc. 2, 587 ; 10, 234 ; Mart. 9, 36, 7 .— Meton. , the granite of Syene , Syenite…

Sўlēum.opening: ( ), , , = Σύλειον, a stronghold in Pamphylia , Liv. 38, 14, 10 .

syllăba.opening: ( ), , , = συλλαβή, a syllable. Lit. , Plaut. Bacch. 3, 3, 29 : syllaba brevior aut longior, Cic. Par. 3, 2, 26 : syllabarum numerus, id. de Or. 3, 47, 183 : syllaba longa brevi subjecta, Hor. A. P. 251 : syllaba prima…

syllăbātim.opening: adv. syllaba , syllable by syllable , by syllables (Ciceronian): alicui dictare, Cic. Att. 13, 25, 3 : aliquid alicui dicere, id. Ac. 2, 38, 119 .

syllăbĭcē.opening: adv. id. , in respect to syllables , i. e. in increasing the number of them : praepositiones abundant syllabice, Prisc. 14, p. 983 P.

syllăbus.opening: , = σύλλαβος, a list , register , syllabus , Aug. Conf. 13, 15 .

Tadu.opening: an island near Meroë in Ethiopia , Plin. 6, 29, 33, § 185 Jan. (al. Tado).

taedĭo.opening: v. n. taedium , to feel loathing or disgust , to be weary (postclass.): neque umquam taediavit, Lampr. Alex. Sev. 29 : cor taedians, Tert. adv. Jud. 11 med. : animal taedians, loathing its food, Veg. Vet. 1, 17 ; 3, 2 ;…
